items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 8 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Shaheed reportedly avoided a major injury in the collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone in Week 7, an injury that will claim at least one game from the veteran speedster. There’s not really a ton of fantasy value behind Smith-Njigba in Seattle, although veteran Cooper Kupp could see a target or two trickle his way in Shaheed’s absence.

items.name: Zach Charbonnet
items.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) is expected to be active for Week 8 against the Bears.
items.analysis: The team has yet to activate Charbonnet from injured reserve but removed him from the injury report Saturday, leaving only the procedural step in the way of his season debut. He likely returns to a limited role as the team manages his reps in his first game since tearing his ACL in 2025. Rookie Jadarian price is also expected to play after being removed from the injury report. He, too, will need to be activated from injured reserve.

items.name: Jadarian Price
items.headline: Seahawks removed Jadarian Price (chest) from the injury report Saturday and he is expected to play in Week 8 against the Bears.
items.analysis: The team has yet to activate him from injured reserve, a procedural move that is expected to come before they take the field in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday Night Football. Zach Charbonnet is also expected to be activated from injured reserve, giving the team their top two backs for the first time this season. No word yet on an expected snap count for either, although Price would seem to be in line to serve as the top option in the backfield considering it will be Charbonnet’s season debut.

items.name: RJ Harvey
items.headline: Broncos placed RB RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Whoa, that escalated quickly. Harvey reportedly suffered a knee injury in practice this week that initially caused the Broncos to rule him out for Week 8, with the team then making the procedural move of placing him on injured reserve Saturday. Harvey will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he rehabs the injury, leaving rookie Jonah Coleman and veteran J.K. Dobbins to handle primary backfield duties with Tyler Badie also on injured reserve. Coleman warrants weekly FLEX status, at minimum.

items.name: L'Jarius Sneed
items.headline: Chiefs placed CB L’Jarius Sneed (knee) on inured reserve.
items.analysis: That was somewhat unexpected. Sneed missed Wednesday’s practice for personal reasons and was limited Thursday and Friday. He was moved to injured reserve a day later. The Chiefs are now down their top two corners after Mansoor Delane was ruled out for Week 8, creating a much softer matchup for the Broncos on Sunday.

items.name: Derwin James
items.headline: Chargers placed S Derwin James (hamstring) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Previous reports indicated the team was considering a stint on injured reserve following an aggravation of his hamstring injury, with Saturday’s transaction confirming those suspicions. James will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, as the Chargers look to reverse course on a sinking season.

items.name: Mansoor Delane
items.headline: Chiefs downgraded Mansoor Delane (shoulder) to out for Week 8 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Delane entered the weekend listed as questionable for the team’s divisional showdown against the Broncos, ultimately downgraded to out on Saturday. His absence could influence Steve Spagnuolo’s ability to utilize man coverage at the hefty rates he has through the first six games.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Colston Loveland (neck) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play in Week 8 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Loveland popped on the injury report Friday after being limited with a neck injury. A full session Saturday cleared his path to play against the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, where he’ll likely be leaned on to move the football against the suffocating Seattle defense.

items.name: Tytus Howard
items.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) cleared protocol and will play in Week 8 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Howard gains clearance just in time to be charged with slowing an aggressive Pittsburgh pass rush, likely in line to handle his fair share of T.J. Watt on Sunday. There should be no reason for Howard to see a decline in snaps or performance after suffering a concussion in Week 7.

items.name: T'Vondre Sweat
items.headline: Jets placed NT T’Vondre Sweat (knee) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: The vaunted Jets run defense takes a major blow as Sweat is moved to injured reserve. Defensive end David Bailey is also doubtful to play in Week 8, boosting the matchup for Ashton Jeanty on Sunday. Sweat will be sidelined for four games, at minimum, as the Jets struggle to cling to another lost season.

items.name: P.J. Locke
items.headline: Cowboys activated S P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Locke spent the previous five weeks on injured reserve with a plantar fascia issue and is expected to be active for the team’s Week 8 game against the Cardinals. He brings a veteran presence to a defense that struggled mightily to start the season as the Cowboys continue inching closer to full health.

items.name: Jack Bech
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Raiders are expected to activate WR Jack Bech (forearm) from injured reserve ahead of Week 8.
items.analysis: Bech has been on the shelf since fracturing his arm in Week 3, missing the minimum required four games due to the injury. He returns to a passing offense that has been heavily concentrated amongst Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker, unlikely to be a usable weekly fantasy asset. Fantasy managers can stash the youngster in hopes of a growing role moving forward.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Henderson first popped on the injury report with a missed practice Thursday before maintaining that status to end the week, ultimately unable to play through the ailment while being ruled out Saturday. Rhamondre Stevenson steps into a potential workhorse role against the downtrodden Dolphins, where he will be an upside RB2 in Week 8. Expect the team to elevate another back from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s game to play behind Stevenson and Corey Kiner, the latter of whom is expected to serve as the primary change of pace option with Henderson out.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: This was always thought to be the case after Brown missed Thursday and Friday with a “flare up” of an existing knee injury, the same issue that ultimately saw the Rams back out of trade negotiations this offseason. Brown’s absence comes at a horrible time for a team already without Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs, leaving only DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Fantasy managers in a bind could consider taking a shot on upside through Williams’ downfield role against a Dolphins team bleeding explosive passing through the first seven weeks.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) is out for Week 8 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: No surprise here as Monangai hasn’t practiced since Week 4. He’s set to miss his fourth consecutive game against the Seahawks in Week 8. Roschon Johnson figures to continue to serve as the Bears’ RB2 with Monangai sidelined.

items.name: Daron Payne
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture.
items.analysis: Payne suffered the injury during Friday’s practice. A previous report from Ian Rapport stated the 29-year-old defensive tackle suffered a significant foot injury and would be out for the foreseeable future. Payne will be placed on injured reserve as he’s set to miss the rest of the season. He recorded a sack, a forced fumble and 14 tackles in six games with the Commanders this year.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: NBC 26 Northeast Wisconsin reports “newly released records show additional women contacted the Hobart/Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Josh Jacobs.”
items.analysis: The Wisconsin television station received “heavily redacted” police reports on Friday evening, though they included allegations from three other women. There are multiple extremely disturbing allegations of physical violence. One alleged incident took place in January 2022. The accuser “contacted investigators in June after learning about the May investigation, telling police the allegations sounded similar to her prior experience with Jacobs.” She also said the incident had “never been reported to law enforcement, (and that she) contacted police when she believed her alleged experience with Jacobs could be relevant to the case.” The allegations highlight the folly of the NFL’s apparent wish that the situation would just go away. It has not, and now it is quite possible, if not likely, that Jacobs ends up suspended for the remainder of the 2026 season. Stay tuned.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Micah Parsons (knee) is expected to practice next week.
items.analysis: If Parsons returns to practice next week, the Packers will have a 21-day window where he can practice before activating him to the 53-man roster. Pelissero also reported that Parsons’ most likely return date is in Week 11 against the Rams. Including the playoffs, Green Bay is 5-8 since Parsons tore his ACL last December.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts haven’t discussed benching QB Daniel Jones.
items.analysis: Jones received a vote of confidence from Colts HC Shane Steichen earlier this week and now there’s a report from prominent NFL Insider Pelissero that the organization hasn’t discussed benching him. While that’s all well and good, the Colts still seem like they’re in the early stages of a process that will likely end with benching Jones at some point this year. The fact that Pelissero mentioned Jones’ contract includes a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 is an ominous sign. Once the 2-5 Colts are officially eliminated from playoff contention, Indianapolis won’t have much incentive to risk injury with the oft-injured Jones.

items.name: John Harbaugh
items.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports Giants HC John Harbaugh called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about trading for DT Jeffery Simmons.
items.analysis: With Giants GM Joe Schoen stonewalled, Harbaugh broke with traditional NFL trade-talk norms and called the Titans owner himself. Unfortunately for the Giants, the message was the same, that Simmons was off limits in trade talks. Previous reporting from Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer stated that Bears GM Ryan Poles’ long-standing relationship with Titans GM Mike Borgonzi played a huge role in Simmons ending up in Chicago. Poles and Borgonzi first met in 2007 when Poles was a guard at Boston College and Borgonzi was a recruiting assistant.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports WR Garrett Wilson won’t be traded.
items.analysis: Wilson told reporters this week that he hasn’t requested a trade. Now Schefter reports, citing a “well-placed” source, that there’s “no way” the Jets will trade the 26-year-old wide receiver before the trade deadline. Wilson was held to two catches and 26 yards in Week 7, but remains in the WR2 mix heading into Week 8’s matchup against the Raiders.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts are open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor.
items.analysis: Multiple teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old Taylor and talks are active and ongoing, according to Schefter. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts already turned down an offer for Taylor that included a 2027 second-round pick and another pick. While previous reports stated the Colts weren’t interested in trading Taylor, who signed an extension before the season, Indianapolis appears to be holding out for the best offer they can get. Taylor would see a slight boost in fantasy value if acquired by another team while Seth McGowan would likely take over the Colts’ backfield.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) remained sidelined for Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: Shaheed is now firmly on the wrong side of questionable heading into Monday evening’s game against the Bears. If he was in your third receiver or second FLEX spot in a 14-team league, it is time to start making other plans.

items.name: Zach Charbonnet
items.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to “limited” for Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s not particularly concerning — this is probably part of a pre-established practice plan as Charbonnet completes his injury comeback — but Jadarian Price’s Friday return to full practice certainly has our attention. Now even if Charbonnet does manage to make his 2026 debut on Monday evening against the Bears, he could have even more company in Seattle’s crowded backfield. Both backs returning would make all three of Charbonnet, Price and Emanuel Wilson shaky FLEX plays. We will receive official game designations on Saturday afternoon. Until then, hang tight.

items.name: Jadarian Price
items.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was upgraded to “full” for Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: Price was upgraded to full while Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to limited. That is probably part of a pre-planned process with Charbonnet, but as of Friday evening, we suppose Price is now technically closer to returning than his veteran backfield mate. As it is, both players now seem more likely than not to suit up, which would make for an extremely chaotic fantasy situation with Emanuel Wilson still in the fold. With the Seahawks playing on Monday evening, we will receive official game designations Saturday afternoon.

items.name: Daron Payne
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Daron Payne suffered a “significant foot injury” in practice Friday.
items.analysis: Rapoport adds that the injury is likely to sideline the standout defensive tackle “for the foreseeable future,” with a stint on injured reserve appearing likely. The Commanders continue to be dealt significant injuries, this time on the defensive side of the ball, as they fight to remain in contention in a fragile NFC East division. The team will know more about the extent of the injury when Payne undergoes further testing Saturday.

items.name: KaVontae Turpin
items.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Week 8 will mark the second consecutive absence for the veteran kick returner, with little-to-no impact on the offensive pieces around him considering he has played more than 12 offensive snaps only once all season. Fantasy managers are more interested in the potential status of George Pickens, who is listed as questionable. If Pickens can’t go, Ryan Flournoy could see a slight uptick in opportunities on the perimeter.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) is questionable for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Pickens saw a hamstring designation added to his status this week after playing through a shoulder ailment the previous two games, which was enough for the team to list him as questionable after a week of limited sessions. Although we expect Pickens to continue to play through his injuries, fantasy managers will want to confirm his status when the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick. If active, Pickens is an upside WR2 against the Cardinals.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Allgeier saw a steady progression in practice throughout the week, starting off with a “DNP” before upgrading in each subsequent session, culminating in a full practice Friday. He will be available to form a likely three-headed timeshare with Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight against the Cowboys and likely does not warrant fantasy consideration.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was removed from the injury report and will in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Allgeier saw a steady progression in practice throughout the week, starting off with a “DNP” before upgrading in each subsequent session, culminating in a full practice Friday. He will be available to form a likely three-headed timeshare with Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight against the Cowboys and likely does not warrant fantasy consideration.

items.name: RJ Harvey
items.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday with a knee injury before being unable to practice Friday, ultimately ruled out for the team’s divisional clash against the Chiefs. Expect Jonah Coleman to serve as the primary rusher in addition to the possibility he sees his pass game involvement tick up in the absences of both Harvey and Tyler Badie, the latter of whom is on injured reserve. The increase in opportunity is enough to vault Coleman into viable FLEX territory for Week 8.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is questionable for Denver’s Week 8 game against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Waddle got in two limited sessions after missing practice on Wednesday. It feels like he’s on the optimistic side of questionable given the trend line, though of course you would have preferred to see a full session somewhere in here. It’s also possible he winds up on a snap count, so we’ll see if any insiders dig up anything on that this weekend.

items.name: Jamree Kromah
items.headline: Dolphins claimed EDGE Jamree Kromah off waivers from the Bears.
items.analysis: You thought you could just sneak this guy through waivers, did you? Well the Miami Dolphins are going to claim him. They’ve got to look busy here as they try to find one or two front seven pieces that will still have jobs in two years. The 26-year-old Kromah is their latest attempt to find one of them.

items.name: Malik Washington
items.headline: Malik Washington (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: Washington’s WR4 status will continue aplomb against the Patriots in Week 8, though Caleb Douglas’ return probably has capped his ceiling case for the time being.

items.name: Greg Dulcich
items.headline: Greg Dulcich is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: The fringe TE2 life awaits Dulcich against the Patriots on Sunday.

items.name: Derwin James
items.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Rams.
items.analysis: James reportedly suffered a setback with his hamstring injury, with the team now considering injured reserve. His absence is a big hit to their defense as a primary interior defender against the heavy personnel sets from the Rams, upgrading the matchup for Tyler Higbee and company.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
items.analysis: McConkey’s concussion was always unlikely to hold him out for Week 8 with the team coming off their bye, with Friday’s injury report confirming that notion. The Chargers have under-performed offensive expectations more than any team through their first six games, leaving McConkey in the FLEX range for Week 8, a far cry from the WR2 range he was drafted in this offseason.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is questionable for Washington’s Week 8 game against the Eagles.
items.analysis: The rare limited-DNP-limited injury report shows up here after Burks suffered a late foot injury in Week 6’s Monday night football. Burks probably is best considered truly questionable at this point. If he’s absent, it could help Antonio Williams get into the 80 percent snap range.

items.name: Tre' Harris
items.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Harris returns to the lineup after missing Week 6, with the team’s bye week providing enough time for the veteran receiver to get back to the active game-day roster. That doesn’t mean he should be inserted into fantasy lineups after such a slow start to the season.

items.name: Javon Kinlaw
items.headline: Javon Kinlaw (knee) will not play in Washington’s Week 8 game against the Eagles.
items.analysis: He didn’t practice all week after Dan Quinn acknowledged it would be “tough” for him to play. An IR stint probably is in play on Saturday, if not, Kinlaw will probably start Week 9 on the questionable line.

items.name: Stefon Diggs
items.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) is not on Washington’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: He should be a mid-range WR3 with Terry McLaurin out of the picture in Washington. Diggs practiced in full each of the last two sessions of the week after a Wednesday DNP.

items.name: Carlton Davis
items.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: It’s a bit of a surprise questionable because Davis got in three full practice sessions this week. Still, he is coming off a long-term neck injury that has sidelined him most of the year so we understand the Patriots being cautious here. We’d consider Davis on the optimistic side of questionable.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: Ja’Marr Chase is not on Cincinnati’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: He will play and be on the overall WR1 line against the Titans. Zac Taylor spoke earlier today and said he had no concerns about Chase. Everyone has downplayed concerns about Chase’s ankle for the majority of the week. He will be a smash play against a Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans defense.

items.name: Jihaad Campbell
items.headline: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Campbell didn’t practice all week and his availability for Week 9 is likely in question as well. Campbell has 49 tackles in seven starts this season despite spending a few early October weeks as an injury report fixtures. IDP leaguers will need to make other plans this week.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 8 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Barkley gave a cryptic response when asked if he would play earlier in the day, ultimately ready to gut out multiple injuries as the Eagles continue to trudge forward in an injury-decimated season. The veteran back added that the injuries are both something he will need to manage throughout the game but that he feels as if he can play through them. That leaves fantasy managers in a sticky situation, likely forced to start Barkley if he’s on the roster. Barkley is a middling RB2 in a difficult matchup on the ground against the Commanders.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
items.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and has not practiced since the build up to Week 6. As with colleague DeVonta Smith, Wicks enters next week questionable to play and with the Eagles having a Week 10 bye, we wouldn’t be surprised if Wicks sat that game out as well.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
items.analysis: He has not practiced since Week 6. It’s hard to count on Smith to be up for Week 9, though we obviously can’t say anything beyond him being questionable. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye and it might be preferable for them at this point if Smith sat through that — though that is just our speculation.

items.name: Calvin Ridley
items.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
items.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and would seem to be trending towards playing. With Carnell Tate down this week, Elic Ayomanor is probably the Titans dart throw wideout for the desperate against the Bengals if you’re choosing between him or Ridley.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Spears had three DNPs and has not practiced since last Thursday. Michael Carter filled down as the third-down back last week, though all that actually meant is that Tony Pollard got full-time workload. We expect that to continue in Week 8.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is out for Week 8 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Tate’s game-day designation comes on the heels of three missed practices this week. His absence leaves behind an alpha’s target share to go claimed by the remaining pass catchers, most notable of whom is slot man Wan’Dale Robinson. Robinson also draws the top matchup on paper against he inside-funnel nature of the Cincinnati defense, appearing to have a clear path to leading the team in targets and receiving. Fantasy managers can start Robinson as a viable WR3.

items.name: Jack Bech
items.headline: Jack Bech (forearm) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 8 game against the Jets.
items.analysis: He practiced in full all three days. Klint Kubiak was evasive when asked if he would be activated, but players that practice in full three days in a row while trying to come off injured reserve rarely aren’t activated. Bech will be restored to the roster on Saturday if he’s going to play. He doesn’t need to be proactively rostered outside of the deepest leagues.

items.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) will play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Like teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown, Gibbs started the week off with a missed practice before upgrading to a full participant in both sessions to end the week. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will be ready for a normal workload against the division rival Vikings Sunday. Fantasy managers are clearly starting Gibbs, regardless of matchup.

items.name: Kerby Joseph
items.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) will not play in Detroit’s Week 8 game against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Dan Campbell said Joseph has been used only in individual and group practices so far and that he’s handled that well. Next week he’ll get in on real practice. Joseph probably stands a decent chance of being active for Week 9 assuming he acclimates well to that.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: St. Brown started the week off with an absence before logging consecutive full sessions to end the week or preparations, ultimately removed from the injury report entirely heading into the weekend. He should be good to go for a normal workload against the stingy Minnesota defense, where fantasy managers can start him with confidence as a WR1.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Friday.
items.analysis: We’d be floored if Monangai got on the questionable line on Saturday. He hasn’t played or practiced since Week 4. We’re still waiting for some kind of positive movement here. Roschon Johnson will likely be Chicago’s second-string back again in Week 8.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) did not practice Friday and is questionable to play in Week 8 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Meyers managed back-to-back limited sessions to begin the week of preparation but was downgraded to a “DNP” Friday, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for Week 8 against the Colts. An absence could require additional offensive snaps for two-way player Travis Hunter and a slight uptick in route rate for Brian Thomas Jr and Josh Cameron. This is one to monitor for fantasy managers of all Jacksonville pass catchers.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Colston Loveland (neck) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It was an injury report addition, which is never a great sign. We don’t have a lot of smoke on this one yet, though we imagine Ben Johnson will get some questions about it on Saturday. The MNF timing could make this a tricky fantasy lineup decision if Loveland is questionable; the only reasonable pivots would be AJ Barner or — maybe — Sam Roush.

items.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
items.headline: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is out for Week 8 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Hawkins was unable to practice all week as he tends to a knee injury, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 Friday. It will go down as his second consecutive absence, with his next opportunity to take the field to come in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

items.name: Roquan Smith
items.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Smith upgraded his level of participation with each practice this week, starting with an absence before moving to limited and, finally, a full session. He appears to be ready for a normal workload in the interior of the Baltimore defense, a welcome development for the Ravens as they prepare to face the Bills.

items.name: Vega Ioane
items.headline: Vega Ioane (knee) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
items.analysis: Ioane got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday but was evasive when asked if he’d go at his locker yesterday. In the end, it would have been very impressive for him to play through a sprained MCL one week later. Ioane’s practice augurs well for his chances of playing in Week 10, at the very least. Week 9, on Thursday Night, might be too big of an ask.

items.name: Braelon Allen
items.headline: Braelon Allen (ankkle) will play in Week 8 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Allen ended the week of practice with consecutive full showings after being limited Wednesday, while backfield mate Breece Hall officially drew the questionable tag following a week full of limited sessions. Allen would remain an upside RB2 in a solid matchup should Hall be held out for another week, likely maintaining FLEX status should Hall play.

items.name: Kyle Hamilton
items.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: Hamilton managed a full session to clear the report after a Wednesday DNP. While the Ravens are missing some key players on defense, having their star safety ready to deal with Josh Allen is a big get for them in Week 8.

items.name: Mansoor Delane
items.headline: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is questionable for Kansas City’s Week 8 game against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Delane didn’t practice either of the last two days after popping on to the injury report on Thursday. Andy Reid could only muster a “We’ll see how he does here going forward” when asked about it. We’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable.

items.name: Aaron Jones
items.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Jones departed the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts after aggravating an existing knee issue. He was held out of practice Wednesday before retaking the practice field on consecutive days to end the week, ultimately deemed healthy enough to play against the division rival Lions in Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best off finding a suitable alternative considering Jones is struggling through a sprained MCL and the team got Jordan Mason back a week ago, although managers in a bind can safely expect him to be on the field come Sunday.

items.name: Ed Oliver
items.headline: Ed Oliver (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Oliver has been on the shelf since sustaining a knee injury in Week 4, returning in Week 8 following two missed games plus the team’s Week 7 bye. He played a healthy 81 percent snap rate in his only fully healthy game this season as he continues to struggle through multiple injuries, with his return a welcome sight for a defense that has allowed the second most yards and third most points per game this season.

items.name: Spencer Brown
items.headline: Spencer Brown (back) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against Baltimore.
items.analysis: Brown has a history of not practicing and getting up for the game on Sunday, so we wouldn’t necessarily read too far in to his two DNPs on Wednesday and Thursday. That said, it also wouldn’t be surprising if Brown had to sit against the Ravens on Sunday.

items.name: Elgton Jenkins
items.headline: Elgton Jenkins (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: The interior lineman managed a full session on Friday. Cleveland will have its starting center ready for Pittsburgh’s front in Week 8.

items.name: Jared Verse
items.headline: Jared Verse (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: The star edge player will go after a limited session on Thursday and a full practice on Friday. Cleveland’s in a good place this week on the injury report heading into their matchup with the Steelers.

items.name: Dylan Sampson
items.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 8 injury report.
items.analysis: Sampson got in two full sessions to close out the week and should be a low-end RB3/FLEX play in limited snaps against the Steelers.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
items.analysis: McDuffie has missed the previous two games as he tends to a groin injury suffered ahead of Week 6. He made it back to the practice field this week but was unable to prove healthy enough to avoid the questionable designation.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
items.analysis: Parkinson gutted out an injury to his midsection against the Raiders a week ago when he was in and out of the lineup while clearly dealing with significant discomfort. He was unable to practice through Thursday this week, prompting the questionable designation ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Chargers. Already down multiple primary pass catchers, the Rams could see further concentration of volume should Parkinson miss, a situation that could also pave the way for Davis Allen to see an uptick in opportunities in the 12- and 13-personnel-heavy Rams offense. Fantasy managers likely won’t get further updates on Parkinson’s status before the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick.

items.name: Ben Skowronek
items.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 8 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: He was limited all three days. Skowronek carries no standalone value but could eat into snaps for the other Steelers receivers if active.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is questionable for New York’s Week 8 game against the Raiders.
items.analysis: It’s been a full week of limited practices for Hall, so he profiles as a true game-time decision at this point as we head to the weekend. New York’s franchise running back declined to answer reporter questions in the locker room about whether he’d play or not. Hall would profile as an RB2 if he’s deemed ready to go, presuming no snap count, against the Raiders.

items.name: Rashee Rice
items.headline: Andy Reid said Rashee Rice (hamstring) will play in Week 8.
items.analysis: Rice will make his return to the game-day roster after missing two games due to a hamstring injury sustained in Week 4, returning as the top option through the air for an offense that has struggled with him off the field. The Chiefs scored a combined 25 points against the Chargers and Seahawks without Rice, the latter of which tied the fewest points scored in quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ career. Fantasy managers can comfortably re-insert Rice into rosters as an upside WR2 against the Broncos, against whom Rice caught both targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Week 1.

items.name: Kenny Gainwell
items.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) is questionable for Tampa’s Week 8 game against Atlanta.
items.analysis: His absence would free up more work for Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker. Presumably Gainwell will play after logging a full practice on Friday. Either way, with an injury also nipping at him, he’s an unenviable FLEX option at best against the Falcons.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is questionable for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Henderson missed practice Thursday with an illness, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for the team’s Week 8 divisional clash with the Dolphins. That places fantasy managers in a precarious position considering the team plays in the afternoon portion of the Sunday slate. It would be prudent to make alternate plans at FLEX.

items.name: Michael Wilson
items.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson (ribs) is “good to go” for Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: He’ll get cleared off Arizona’s injury report later today. Wilson is in a nice spot in one of the games with the highest over/under total on the slate against Dallas, but may run into Joey Porter Jr. shadow coverage. Still, even with how things have trended of late, this feels like a spot where Wilson has to be started in the majority of leagues.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Moore has practiced with a non-contact jersey on, in a limited fashion, both of the first two days of the practice week after coming off bye. He got in a third limited session on Friday. This isn’t exactly an exciting run-out after the bye, but Moore probably is on the optimistic side of questionable and any fantasy player that is breathing should be elevated in a game projected to have Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson at quarterback.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (chest) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Kincaid was limited in all three practices this week. We’d imagine he’s on the optimistic side of questionable, though it’s not altogether great news that he wound up on the questionable line after a bye week to heal up. Kincaid will have to be started if active in what projects as a scoring bonanza against the Ravens.

items.name: Jeremiyah Love
items.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: After missing the last two games with an ankle injury, Love will return to the Cardinals in what could be a three-way split after the recent emergence of Bam Knight. Love was averaging 16.2 opportunities per game before being sidelined, with most of that work coming on the ground. With only two top-24 PPR performances to his name so far this season, he shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a boom-or-bust RB2 against the Cowboys.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Baltimore’s Week game against the Bills.
items.analysis: “We do think we will have Lamar this game,” Minter said. Jackson practiced in full on Friday and has missed the last three weeks with his high-ankle sprain. The Ravens will likely clear him from the injury report later today. Jackson told reporters that he feels like “I’m no longer a statue.” Jackson will be “safe” to use as a QB1 against the Bills in what profiles as a fantasy points bonanza.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
items.analysis: “We do think we will have Lamar this game,” Minter said. Jackson practiced in full on Friday and has missed the last three weeks with his high-ankle sprain. He was officially cleared off the injury report. Jackson told reporters that he feels like “I’m no longer a statue.” Jackson will be “safe” to use as a QB1 against the Bills in what profiles as a fantasy points bonanza.

items.name: James Pearce
items.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said James Pearce Jr. (suspension) will be added back to the Falcons 53-man roster next week when eligible.
items.analysis: “He’s done everything that we have asked, everything that he has been allowed to do, he’s done a great job,” Stefanski said while saying that Pearce would play in Madrid against the Bengals. Pearce was suspended after violating the league’s personal conduct policy for three felonies and one misdemeanor for his role in a car chase with ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. Pearce’s felony charges were aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

items.name: Tytus Howard
items.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) is questionable for Week 8 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Howard returned to the practice field Friday after missing both sessions to start the week, keeping the door open for him to clear concussion protocol in time for Sunday’s game against the Steelers. Howard will need to remain asymptomatic and gain clearance from an independent neurologist to play.

items.name: Sauce Gardner
items.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Sauce Gardner (calf) will be active for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Gardner missed last week’s game after suffering a calf strain in Week 6 against the Titans, but will return after getting in a limited session on Wednesday and a full practice on Thursday. We’re assuming that means he’s in line for another full practice today.

items.name: Billy Bowman
items.headline: Billy Bowman (hamstring) is questionable for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
items.analysis: Like teammate Divine Deablo, Bowman returned to the practice field Thursday with a limited showing after missing the Week 7 win over the 49ers. The team gives him the questionable designation for Week 8 against the Buccaneers, keeping the door open for a return following one missed game. We’ll gain further clarity when the team released inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick on Sunday.

items.name: Divine Deablo
items.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) is questionable for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
items.analysis: Deablo returned to the practice field in limited capacity Thursday after missing the team’s Week 7 win over the 49ers, keeping the door open for a return to the active game-day roster. We’ll get our final update when the team announces their inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick on Sunday.

items.name: Brian Robinson
items.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
items.analysis: Robinson will miss a second straight game with his hamstring injury, which positions Khalil Herbert to again serve as the backup to Bijan Robinson. Herbert rushed two times for nine yards in last week’s win over the 49ers while adding one reception for 19 additional yards. He will not be on the streaming radar this week.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said A.J. Brown (knee) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: This feels like a very optimistic questionable after Brown missed the last two practices of the week with a new knee tweak. Brown-reliant managers should be making contingency plans ready for Sunday. “We’ll see when he comes in tomorrow, and we’ll make a decision,” Vrabel said.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Steichen said Taylor will see a full workload despite being the subject of trade rumors for a Colts team that will clearly be sellers at the deadline. Taylor is healthy and not on the injury report, so this is strictly an update to inform fantasy managers they can start him with confidence this week. Taylor remains a high-end RB1 as long as his normal workload remains intact.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Tyler Warren (groin) is “good to go” for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Warren was limited in practice on Thursday and Wednesday and will return to a rough receiver corps against a Jaguars defense coming off bye. Warren remains a startable TE1, but it’s hard to forge much of a ceiling case for him at this point.

items.name: Josh Downs
items.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Josh Downs will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars despite his trade request.
items.analysis: Steichen confirmed that Downs did indeed request a trade, but that won’t stop him from being on the field this week against the Jaguars. The Colts appear to be in full sell mode after trading away OG Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner earlier this week. Downs has been on the practice field this week and profiles as a fringe WR3/WR4 after a string of tough outings.

items.name: Antoine Winfield
items.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Antoine Winfield Jr. will return in Week 8 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Winfield has missed the last three games due to fractured ribs he suffered in Week 4. Winfield has earned a 76.8 defensive grade per PFF this season while racking up 24 tackles. The Panthers’ secondary held up fairly well during his three-game absence, allowing only 235.0 passing yards per game, but his return will be a welcomed one for Bowles and his defense.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Emeka Egbuka (foot) will not play in Week 8 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka did clear concussion protocol, but the foot injury he has been dealing with for the last two weeks will officially sideline him for this week’s game against the Falcons. Hopefully this isn’t any kind of a major setback for Egbuka, who shed his non-contact jersey in Thursday’s practice and was limited in the first two practices to start the week. Ted Hurst will again operate as the Buccaneers’ primary outside target but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a risky WR4.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: After being a DNP in each of the Eagles’ first two practices of the week, it’s far too early to be confident that Barkley will suit up on Sunday night against the Commanders. That said, his return to the field is still an encouraging sign for the Eagles, whose backfield is suddenly among the most banged up in the league. We will check back in when the Eagles announce Barkley’s Week 8 status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this ends up being a game-time decision, which could prove frustrating for fantasy managers. We should know more on his availability in the next few hours.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: Brown has now missed back-to-back practices and is at serious risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Dolphins. Brown’s knee injury was reported as a “flare-up” from a previous knee injury, which is never a good sign for a player. Brown has been dealing with injuries like this for a few years but has always found a way to play through them. While it’s possible he ends up doing so again this week, fantasy managers should begin considering other options in the event he is held out.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: Tate was a DNP all week and is at risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Bengals. The team will announce his official status shortly, but if he is unable to go, Wan’Dale Robinson and Elic Ayomanor would be the early favorites to see an uptick in targets against a Bengals secondary that ranks 18th in points allowed to opposing receivers this season.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: After being limited in back-to-back practices to start the week, and shedding his non-contact jersey on Thursday, Egbuka being a DNP on Friday is a notable setback. Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman speculated that Egbuka will “be ruled out again” for Week 8’s game against the Falcons, but we’ll wait for official word from the team before drawing conclusions. That said, the Bucs could again have Ted Hurst operating as their primary outside threat.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Baker Mayfield was seen without his protective glove during Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: Mayfield wore the protective glove during last week’s game to avoid further damage to the thumb he injured in Week 3. Mayfield attempted only 11 passes in his return against the Panthers last week, but that was all he needed in a game where the Buccaneers totaled over 250 yards on the ground. Hopefully the shedding of his protective glove is a sign that he’s no longer at risk of re-injury heading into Week 8’s game against the Falcons.

items.name: Todd Wash
items.headline: Panthers named DL coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator.
items.analysis: Wash will take over for the now-departed Ejiro Evero, who was dismissed shortly after the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers. Wash, who has been with the Panthers since 2023, spent five seasons as the Jaguars’ defensive coordinator (2016 to 2020), with his defense finishing top five in both yards and points allowed in 2017 and 2018. Wash’s first task will be finding ways to improve a run defense that ranks among the worst in the league through the first half of the season, but given that his fingerprints are all over the defensive line, it’s hard to imagine a noticeable improvement is on the way over the final 10 weeks of the season.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be limited in Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: This will be the third straight limited practice for Hall, which is an encouraging sign as he looks to return to action since last playing in Week 3 against the Lions. If he’s active, Hall will likely find himself in a bit more of a timeshare with Braelon Allen, who has rushed for 357 yards and a touchdown on 72 carries in Hall’s absence while averaging a solid 5.0 YPC. We will provide an update on Hall’s Week 8 availability when the team announces it, but at worst, we would expect him to carry a questionable tag entering the weekend.

items.name: Ejiro Evero
items.headline: Panthers fired DC Ejiro Evero.
items.analysis: Just hours after a 27-19 loss to the Packers that saw the Panthers fall below .500 for the first time this season, the team has decided to part ways with Evero after nearly four full seasons with the team. Evero was a holdover from Frank Reich’s 2023 staff and drew a handful of head coaching interviews during the last hiring cycle after his defense finished 15th in points allowed and 16th in yards allowed. The Panthers’ best defensive performances of the season came in games where Cooper Rush and Tanner McKee made starts, but they’ve allowed 35.2 points per game when facing opposing teams’ QB1s this season. From 2022 to 2023, Evero’s defenses ranked seventh and fourth in yards allowed per game, but his units have struggled in more recent seasons. They have particularly struggled on the ground and rank near the bottom of the league in rushing yards allowed and YPC allowed, while allowing a league-high 12 rushing touchdowns. He’ll likely get another job in a coaching role next offseason, in hopes of earning another coordinator job over the next few seasons.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young’s knee injury may be limiting his mobility.
items.analysis: Young declined to get into details about his knee injury after Thursday night’s loss to the Packers, saying, “Everyone’s dealing with something; it’s no excuse,” when speaking with the media after the game. Canales didn’t seem overly concerned about Young’s injury after the game, but did acknowledge that he didn’t appear to have the “quick, make you miss” aspect to his game against the Packers. Young was listed on the Panthers’ injury report throughout the week, but was also a full participant in practice. Young’s knee could be partly to blame for the six sacks he took in Thursday’s loss, and his health will be one to monitor in the weeks ahead, especially with the team already past its Week 5 bye. Assuming he’s good to go in Week 9, Young will face an uphill battle against a stout Broncos defense.

items.name: Tucker Kraft
items.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-6 targets for 53 yards with a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
items.analysis: Kraft was able to bring in a score between a pair of defenders to give the Pack a 6-0 lead in the first quarter. That’s back-to-back games for the tight end with a score, and three in the first half of 2026. Kraft has seen a similar amount of involvement throughout the campaign, and he’ll likely put up a similar statline — hopefully with a touchdown for fantasy managers who roster him — in Week 9 versus the Patriots.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson caught 8-of-10 targets for 113 yards in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
items.analysis: The fact that Watson was able to even play in the second half was incredible, as the 27-year-old was forced to be examined at the hospital following a chest injury. He didn’t do much after putting up 100 yards in the first half, but again, that’s not really the story here. Watson told reporters after the game that he was coughing up blood and suffered a fractured rib before returning. Assuming no setbacks, he’s a WR1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots, but keep in mind Christian Gonzalez — on top of this injury — can make things difficult.

items.name: Matthew Golden
items.headline: Matthew Golden caught 7-of-13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
items.analysis: Golden is rarely boring, that’s for sure. He dropped two passes, and one of those was a wide-open touchdown in the second quarter. The good news for Golden, Jordan Love and fantasy managers was that he was wide open again on the next play, and he was able to bring that pass in. Golden’s athleticism and ability to get down field is unquestionable, but to say the efficiency isn’t there is an understatement. He’ll be back at it in Week 9 against the Patriots.

items.name: Jalen Coker
items.headline: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers while also losing a fumble.
items.analysis: Coker’s fumble came on the last play of the game as the Panthers played pitchy woo woo in their attempt to tie the game. The 24-year-old didn’t have a catch in the first half, but salvaged his fantasy day — to a point, anyway — with a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young. The 24-year-old has just three catches over the last two games, and he’ll try and get things going against the Broncos in Week 9.

items.name: Jalen Coker
items.headline: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.

items.name: Jalen Coker
items.headline: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers while also losing a fumble.

The 24-year-old didn’t have a catch in the first half, but salvaged his fantasy day — to a point, anyway — with a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young. The 24-year-old has just three catches over the last two games, and he’ll try and get things going against the Broncos in Week 9.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 57 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

items.name: Chuba Hubbard
items.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers, adding seven receptions for 38 yards.
items.analysis: Hubbard was easily the most effective offensive player for the Panthers, but that’s at least partially an insult to everyone else as much as it was compliment to him. The tailback was able to make the most of the limited rushing room, and with Bryce Young having zero time to throw the football, he was a frequent target of Young’s checkdowns. Trevor Etienne received just one carry for one yard, meanwhile. Hubbard’s usage makes him a high-end RB2 for Week 9 against the Broncos, even if it’s more floor than ceiling.

items.name: Chuba Hubbard
items.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers, adding five receptions for 38 yards.
items.analysis: Hubbard was easily the most effective offensive player for the Panthers, but that’s at least partially an insult to everyone else as much as it was compliment to him. The tailback was able to make the most of the limited rushing room, and with Bryce Young having zero time to throw the football, he was a frequent target of Young’s checkdowns. Trevor Etienne received just one carry for one yard, meanwhile. Hubbard’s usage makes him a high-end RB2 for Week 9 against the Broncos, even if it’s more floor than ceiling.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: Josh Jacobs rushed 21 times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers, adding six catches for 13 yards and another score.
items.analysis: Jacobs’ fantasy game was salvaged with two scores, but the tailback didn’t look particularly spry in the process. He had a long gain of just six, and there was almost no burst even against the porous Panthers’ run defense. He was involved in the passing game, but again, outside of his four-yard receiving score, there really wasn’t much there. It’s clear this is Jacobs’ backfield despite the scuffles, as MarShawn Lloyd had just three touches in the contest for seven yards. He’s a volatile low-end RB1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interceptions in the Panthers’ 27-19, Week 8 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: Those who believe that sacks are a quarterback stat might change their mind watching the Panthers block Thursday night. The 25-year-old had no time to throw and couldn’t get out of the pocket while taking six sacks and being pressured on what seemed like every throw. That’s not to say that Young was completely a victim of his circumstance; he struggled with accuracy and couldn’t get the ball downfield in another ugly performance for the 25-year-old sans a 26-yard passing score to Jalen Coker in the middle of the fourth. Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

items.name: Jordan Love
items.headline: Jordan Love completed 30-of-41 passes for 288 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Packers’ 27-19, Week 8 win over the Panthers.
items.analysis: Love completed 17 of his first 20 passes, and two of those incompletions were drops. He threw a seed to Tucker Kraft for his first touchdown between defenders, found Matthew Golden wide open in the end zone for his second score — one play after Golden dropped a touchdown — and connected with Josh Jacobs for his third score of the day. The interception was a heinous decision where he didn’t see the safety, but outside of that, it was an impressive evening for the 27-year-old. Love gets zero, well, love from the run game and doesn’t have a quality offensive line, but he’s still putting up respectable numbers. He’ll look to add to those numbers in Week 9 against the Patriots in what should be a fun matchup.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson (chest) returned to action in Week 8 against the Panthers in the third quarter.
items.analysis: Watson went to the hospital to have his chest injury examined, but obviously checked out well if the Packers were willing to reinsert him into a game where they were leading by two scores. It’s a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, as Watson has been sensational Thursday night with six catches for 100 yards in just one half thus far.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 9 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
items.analysis: Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
items.analysis: Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated and will head to the hospital to be further examined. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

items.name: Jack Bech
items.headline: Jack Bech (forearm) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: That’s back-to-back full practices for Bech after the Raiders opened up the 21-day window for the wideout. He’s worth monitoring in redraft leagues in part because the options ahead of him aren’t exactly elite, but fantasy managers don’t need to consider a stash just yet.

items.name: Jadarian Price
items.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Price gets in the limited session after coach Mike Macdonald said that it was realistic that the tailback could be back Monday night against the Bears in Week 8. Zach Charbonnet was a full participant Thursday, so the Seattle backfield could finally be at full strength — or close to it, anyway — for the stretch. That’s nice for the Seahawks, but creates a lot of confusion from a fantasy perspective.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Rashid Shaheed did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Shaheed received positive news on his knee injury that caused him to leave Sunday’s blowout win over the Chiefs, but there’s a pretty good chance that he’s going to miss at least Week 8’s game against Chicago on Monday. Assuming that’s the case, it will lead to more snaps for Tory Horton both as a receiver and as the primary returner.

items.name: Zach Charbonnet
items.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s obviously a positive development for Charbonnet, who appears to be on track for his season debut against the Bears in Week 8. Fantasy managers just have to keep in mind that the rug was pulled from underneath last week when the Seahawks ruled the tailback out late in the week. Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant, but fantasy managers who want to use a Seattle tailback on Monday night won’t have clarity until Saturday at the earliest.

items.name: Zach Charbonnet
items.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant during Monday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s obviously a positive development for Charbonnet, who appears to be on track for his season debut against the Bears in Week 9. Fantasy managers just have to keep in mind that the rug was pulled from underneath last week when the Seahawks ruled the tailback out late in the week. Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant, but fantasy managers who want to use a Seattle tailback on Monday night won’t have clarity until Saturday at the earliest.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Allgeier was able to get a bump up after a DNP for Wednesday. It appears to just be a case of rest for the 26-year-old, but fantasy managers who will consider Allgeier for Week 8 against the Cowboys if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) can’t go — Love was also limited Thursday — should keep an eye on Friday’s designation.

items.name: Jeremiyah Love
items.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was listed as a limited participate in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: That’s a second straight limited session for Love. The Cardinals are taking this slowly with the 21-year-old ahead of a potential return in Week 8 against the Cowboys, but fantasy managers will obviously need to pay close attention to how much he practices Friday and his injury designation.

items.name: Jeremiyah Love
items.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: That’s a second straight limited session for Love. The Cardinals are taking this slowly with the 21-year-old ahead of a potential return in Week 8 against the Cowboys, but fantasy managers will obviously need to pay close attention to how much he practices Friday and his injury designation.

items.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
items.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, OLB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, G Damien Lewis, G Torricelli Simpkins, and DT Bobby Brown inactive for Week 8 against the Packers.
items.analysis: The Panthers are extremely shorthanded along the offensive line and on the defensive side of the ball, most notably in the secondary and with the pass rush. That could spell trouble against the high-powered Green Bay passing game, particularly with wide receiver Matthew Golden active. The Panthers look to halt their recent skid on the road in hostile territory at Lambeau Field.

items.name: Matthew Golden
items.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is active for Week 8 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Golden got in a lone limited session in preparation for the team’s Week 8 meeting with the Panthers on a short week, ultimately able to go as he looks to continue his recent hot stretch in fantasy production. No limitation in expected role has been passed by the team, meaning Golden should be good to go for a normal workload against the Panthers. Fantasy managers can confidently insert him into Week 8 rosters as an upside WR2. Inactive for the Packers are TE Jonnu Smith, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, G Donovan Jennings, C Sean Rhyan, and G Travis Glover.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

items.name: Tre' Harris
items.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

items.name: RJ Harvey
items.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday after being limited in practice due to a knee injury, something fantasy managers will want to monitor as the weekend approaches. Either way, Harvey now has two healthy backs to compete with for touches with the return of Jonah Coleman in Week 7, keeping him on the fringes of FLEX consideration entering a difficult matchup against the Chiefs.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

items.name: Stefon Diggs
items.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) practiced in full Thursday.
items.analysis: Diggs shook of the absence Wednesday with a full showing Thursday, indicating he is tracking well to suit up when the Commanders face off against the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. The tam previously indicated that Diggs’ modest role would not grow in the absence of Terry McLaurin, potentially paving the way for rookie Antonio Williams to see an increase in role and opportunity in the second half of the season. Fantasy managers will want to confirm Diggs’ status on the final injury report Friday, but it appears as if he will be available in Week 8.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Burks downgraded from a limited showing Wednesday to a “DNP” Thursday, indicating he might be headed toward an absence when the Commanders take on the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Considering the team is already without Terry McLaurin, who was lost for the season in Week 6, this would appear to be setting up for the best chance for rookie Antonio Williams to finally break out in Washington. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the status of Burks on the team’s final injury report Friday.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: It’s the second consecutive limited showing for the co-alpha receiver, who will likely need to upgrade to a full showing on Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend. Pickens has played through the shoulder issue for two weeks, but the hamstring ailment is worth monitoring as the weekend approaches. Pickens is a viable WR2 in a solid matchup against the Cardinals, if active.

items.name: Michael Wilson
items.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: It was the second consecutive day in which Wilson practiced with a yellow non-contact jersey after stating Wednesday that the team was simply being overly cautious. Wilson appears on track to maintain a high-volume role in the pass-heavy Cardinals offense in Week 8 against the Cowboys, where he will be a borderline WR1, if active.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: The consecutive limited showings seems to indicate Moore is on track to return from a two-game absence, something we should get further fidelity on after Friday’s practice. There remains a possibility that Moore carries a questionable designation into the weekend if he is unable to upgrade to a full participant Friday, leaving fantasy managers hopeful yet uncertain as we near the weekend. Moore would return to a WR2 profile when the Bills take on the Ravens, if active.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
items.analysis: Chase quickly puts his fantasy managers’ worries to rest, returning to a full session Thursday after being limited Wednesday. The Bengals will be playing without two tight ends and their WR3 in Andre Iosivas, but their primary contributors remain one of the healthier units as we approach the half way point in the regular season. Chase can be started as a top tier WR1 against the Titans.

items.name: Braelon Allen
items.headline: Braelon Allen (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday limited session. We’re pretty sure Allen will play this week and was just being managed on Wednesday, but how often he’ll be playing will depend on how Breece Hall’s situation shakes out on Friday.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Hall appears more likely than not to play this week if he can get in one more practice on Friday. At the very least, he’s likely headed for an actual questionable tag this week. We’ll see what Aaron Glenn has to say Friday morning. Braelon Allen-reliant managers will want to pay attention to that one.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Monangai has yet to practice after sustaining thumb and toe injuries in Week 4, with the potential that he misses his fourth consecutive game a very real possibility. The Bears held a walkthrough Thursday ahead of a Monday Night Football showdown against the Seahawks, meaning Monangai will have two more opportunities to get on the practice field ahead of Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best making alternate arrangements considering the timing of the team’s game.

items.name: Greg Dulcich
items.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Still, back-to-back practices are a good sign that Dulcich will be ready to go for Week 8’s game against the Patriots. That isn’t necessarily an endorsement of using him in fantasy football — even after last week’s surprise 5/86 against the Jets — but hey, the Dolphins will be glad he’s around.

items.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) practiced in full Thursday.
items.analysis: The return to practice comes on the heels of a missed practice Wednesday for the veteran workhorse, immediately putting fantasy managers at ease for Week 8. Managers will want to confirm his practice status Friday before making final preparations for the weekend, but it certainly appears as if Gibbs will be good to go for a normal, and massive, workload when the Lions take the field against the division rival Vikings.

items.name: Malik Washington
items.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Back-to-back limited sessions probably leave Washington in a good spot for Week 8. He’s more likely than not to be cleared off the injury report on Friday as long as there’s not a sudden downgrade.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Illnesses typically don’t hold back NFL players, so we’d be surprised if Henderson missed time, but it is worth noting that it was a Thursday addition to the report. Because of that, if he missed Friday, it wouldn’t be surprising if he was listed as questionable. We’d still expect him to play either way.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
items.analysis: The upgrade from “DNP” to a full session indicates St. Brown will be fine for a normal workload when the Lions face off against the Vikings Sunday, easing fantasy managers’ collective minds after the star receiver was not present at practice Wednesday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on Friday’s injury report, but it certainly appears as if the team will have their veteran alpha for the divisional tilt.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) and Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) practiced in full Thursday.
items.analysis: The upgrades from “DNP” to full sessions indicates both players will be fine for normal workloads when the Lions face off against the Vikings Sunday, easing fantasy managers’ collective minds after both players were not present at practice Wednesday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm their respective statuses on Friday’s injury report, but it certainly appears as if the team will have their full complement of skill position players for the divisional tilt.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Meyers has put together a pair of limited sessions out of the bye and seems likely to play against the Colts in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr.'s disappearing act has left Meyers capable of putting up WR3 lines, but the Colts may not be opponent enough to force that kind of production out of Meyers this week.

items.name: Adetomiwa Adebawore
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Colts have told teams they won’t move Adetomiwa Adebawore.
items.analysis: Adebawore, a fourth-round pick in 2023, played under 200 snaps in each of his first two seasons and was a pass-rush specialist in 2025. In 2026, he’s taken a step forward, with an 81.8 PFF grade buoyed by an 86.3 pass rush grade. It would be reasonable to expect the Colts to try to extend a player like this, but they sure didn’t seem to have any urgency to do it before the year.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.analysis: It was his second consecutive limited showing following two missed games, with his level of activity Friday likely to be telling as it pertains to a potential return in Week 8. Warren’s absence has been felt hard by a Colts offense that has struggled to move the football consistently. He would likely return to a sizable role over the middle of the field against the pass-funnel Jaguars, if active in Week 8.

items.name: Aaron Jones
items.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
