In an otherwise low-volume day, Allen had another game with a high share of the Colts’ receiving output. He will be in the WR3 ranks ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Jaguars.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Geno Smith completed 23-of-30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Jets’ 28-25, Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Smith posted another impressive box score and was almost perfect in this game, but his few mistakes were extremely impactful. The first was a red zone interception where Dolphins safety Michael Taaffe simply read Smith like a book and jumped the throw for an easy interception. The second catastrophic blunder was a 12-yard sack at the goal line that forced the Jets to settle for a field goal. Smith simply stared down Chop Robinson as the EDGE rusher ran straight at him for an easy sack. Smith isn’t at risk of losing his job anytime soon, but he needs to get back on track against the Raiders next week before taking on the Chiefs and Bills in the following weeks. Smith will be a mid-range QB2 for Week 8.

items.name: Seth McGowan
items.headline: Seth McGowan rushed 11 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding one reception for two yards.
items.analysis: With Jonathan Taylor trade possibilities swirling, McGowan quietly saw an increase in usage against the Vikings. He turned 12 touches into 48 yards, seeing 20 offensive snaps to Taylor’s 41. Though Taylor is still the definitive RB1, it is notable that the rookie 25-year-old is getting more opportunities, including a couple red zone snaps. McGowan has not quite achieved standalone fantasy value but should be added as a bench stash. He would be the Colts’ RB1 should Taylor be traded later this season.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 40 yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
items.analysis: Feel lucky McMillan even reached those marks, as the Panthers simply did not compete in a game where they committed four turnovers and trailed 33-6 at halftime. The first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. McMillan had a better go of it than Jalen Coker, who caught one pass and fell down to create an interception. A shambles, though one the Panthers have to move on from quickly, as they are headed to Green Bay for a potential short-week shootout on Thursday Night Football.

items.name: Jaylin Noel
items.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Jaylin Noel has a turf toe injury.
items.analysis: Noel was spotted in a boot after the game and Ryans confirmed the injury at a post-game scrum. Noel is droppable at this point between the injury and the sudden integration of Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell.

items.name: Jalen Coker
items.headline: Jalen Coker caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
items.analysis: Coker was also the intended target on the first of Bryce Young’s two interceptions. The wideout fell down, leading to the miscue. It was simply a nightmarish day for the Panthers’ offense, who also watched Young cough up a fumble-six. With the Panthers trailing 33-6 at halftime and 43-6 at the 10:21 mark of the fourth, the first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. A disaster for fantasy managers, but likely a short-lived one with the Panthers heading to Green Bay for a short-week Thursday night matchup with the Pack. Coker must still be fired up as a WR2 for that one.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 18 times for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding 2 receptions for 15 yards.
items.analysis: Taylor once again operated as the Colts’ lead back, though rookie Seth McGowan took on more work as the game went on. A first quarter 38-yard touchdown by Taylor was the Colts’ most explosive play of the game; the rest of his rushes averaged just over three yards per carry. It was a tough matchup for the Colts against a high-motor Vikings defense and the offense was not able to sustain drives long enough for Taylor to get opportunities. He saw red zone snaps later in the game but the Colts were unable to move the ball close to the goal line. With another Indy loss, Taylor remains in trade rumors. Regardless of where he plays the rest of the season, Taylor is still a fantasy RB1 moving forward.

items.name: Nico Collins
items.headline: Nico Collins caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: He did draw a defensive pass interference and a defensive holding, so at least he helped in points per penalty leagues. The Giants had defenders draped all over Collins for the majority of the game, and he was punished when he did catch the ball. It was Collins’ worst box score return since his rookie season, and one of only four games in his career where he was targeted and did not return at least 13 yards. The Texans wideout situation is complicated, but we’d still bet on Collins returning from the bye as a low-end WR1.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
items.analysis: To add insult to injury, Mitchell had a two-point conversion catch called back because of a penalty. Omar Cooper Jr. once again stole the show, reeling in several long catches en route to his second 100-yard game in a row. Playing in his first game in over a month, Mitchell did not appear awfully involved in the team’s game plan. The hope will be that he earns more opportunities next week, but Cooper Jr. may have already cemented himself as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Mitchell will be stuck in the WR5 ranks when he takes on the Raiders next week.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Marvin Harrison caught 1-of-4 targets for six yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: Harrison had to come back to the ball in the end zone, one that was placed to his back shoulder by C.J. Stroud to fit it around a zone defender. That was the good. Harrison also added an egregious drop while playing just 13 snaps. Your guess is as good as ours about fantasy value here as we sort through the names. Harrison doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered through his Week 8 bye.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
items.analysis: The Dolphins shut down Wilson, opting to let Omar Cooper Jr. and Mason Taylor beat them through the air. The duo combined for 177 yards and three touchdowns while Wilson was stuck with decoy duties. Wilson was spotted screaming at Geno Smith in the fourth quarter after Smith took a back-breaking sack on third down at the goal line. Wilson downplayed the altercation after the game, saying he was “collaborating” and then noting that he wasn’t even talking to Geno. He was. With several young players taking on larger roles in the Jets’ offense, Wilson’s role as the team’s unquestioned WR1 on the team has taken a hit. Still, he should at least stay in the fantasy WR2 mix for his Week 8 date with the Raiders.

items.name: Xavier Hutchinson
items.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants, adding two carries for 12 yards.
items.analysis: One of the carries came on Houston’s last goal-to-go sequence of the game, where they wound up setting up what looked like a Hutchinson pass only to see him tuck the ball and run. We got nothing. With Tank Dell back and Marvin Harrison Jr. looking for work as well, it would seem that Hutchinson’s days as a FLEX option are over. But we would have said that before this game as well, and Hutchinson wound up with more wideout snaps than anyone but Nico Collins.

items.name: Tank Dell
items.headline: Tank Dell caught his only target for 43 yards in Houston’s Week 7 game against the Giants.
items.analysis: He added a two-yard rush on an end around. While it was good to see him back on the field, it should be noted that it looked like his 43-yard catch glanced off Jaylin Noel’s hands and seemed to immaculately find it’s way into Dell’s as he scampered off for some yards after the catch. Dell further confounded the Houston Wideout Situation, playing just 14 snaps. We have no idea what to trust here beyond Nico Collins. Dell seemed to be running just fine, though it sounded like at times his delay in getting up to speed was about recovery. We’ll all get the Week 8 bye to sort this one out. Dell isn’t a must-roster through it.

items.name: Jacob Cowing
items.headline: Jacob Cowing caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
items.analysis: With Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, De’Zhaun Stribling, and more out with injuries, Cowing was asked to do more as a receiver in this one. He ran the third-most routes of any receiver, but did have more targets and catches than Brandin Cooks, who ran the most routes. Still, with the 49ers on bye next week and likely to be healthier when they return in Week 9, Cowing is not a recommended add on waiver wires.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Hockenson operated as the Vikings’ No. 2 pass-catcher on the day, seeing a lot of Kyler Murray’s targets in the flats. He caught a five-yard touchdown in the second half and finished with 35 receiving yards. Two of his targets came in the end zone, giving him a solid floor as a red zone receiver. Hockenson’s red zone usage is a good sign for his fantasy value; he is in the low-end TE1 range for Week 8 against the Lions.

items.name: Braelon Allen
items.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 17 times for 104 yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins, adding six catches for 30 yards.
items.analysis: Allen almost turned a solid fantasy outing into an RB1 performance in the fourth quarter, but the Dolphins stonewalled him at the goal line. Geno Smith was sacked on the next play and the Jets settled for a field goal. Allen appeared to get banged up late in the game and missed a few snaps on the Jets’ final drive, but he ultimately got back on the field just before the team’s last snap on offense. With Breece Hall expected to return next week, Allen’s days as low-end RB1 might be at an end. Fantasy managers should still hold on to him in case he forces a committee in Week 8 against the Raiders.

items.name: Dalton Schultz
items.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 5-of-6 targets for 45 yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: Nothing groundbreaking here, though this was more like reasonable low-end TE1 work than reasonable low-end TE2 work. Schultz heads into the Week 8 bye with 137 yards in six games against non-Bengals defenses this year and unless you’re in a TE-premium league likely does not need to be on the roster while on bye.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: Christian Kirk was not targeted in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
items.analysis: Kirk was activated off the injured list this week after missing the first six games of the season with a calf injury. He played on just 20 of the team’s 66 snaps and ran a route on 14 of their 43 dropbacks. Kirk was always likely to be eased back into things, and the 49ers have a bye next week to get him more up to speed. That being said, he doesn’t figure to be a huge part of this passing game if the 49ers can get more of their receivers back healthy after the bye.

items.name: Deshaun Watson
items.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 25-of-36 attempts for 308 yards and an interception in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding three rushes for 19 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Watson again led the Browns to a heart-stopping fourth quarter comeback after the Titans tied the game late in the fourth quarter. Watson connected with Harold Fannin for a long gain that put the Browns in field goal range before they won the game at the buzzer. Watson targeted KC Concepcion a team high ten times, mostly on well-designed short area passes. He was 7 percent over his expected completion rate — one of his best rates of the 2026 season. Watson rushed for a touchdown in the second half after being flushed out of the pocket; it was his first rushing score of the season. Watson, who now has two straight games without a passing score, should remain in superflex lineups next week against a pass-funnel Pittsburgh defense.

items.name: Brandin Cooks
items.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 1-of-3 passes for 13 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
items.analysis: Cooks was out-targeted and outplayed by both Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing. Cooks did run the most routes of any receiver on the team, but he didn’t command targets or look like a key piece of the receiving game. With Mike Evans likely back in Week 9, it’s hard to hold onto Cooks through the Week 8 bye in fantasy leagues.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks rushed 19 times for 66 yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants, adding one catch for 15 yards on his only target.
items.analysis: Marks was the only game in town for the Texans, playing 54-of-61 snaps, but couldn’t convert the empty-box looks he was getting into real fantasy value. It was actually a reasonable game compared to most Texans box scores this year. Marks looked to have been hurt at one point in the third quarter but was able to escape the tent and go right back to work. Assuming David Montgomery (groin) is back after the bye week, Marks will head back to FLEX work on most fantasy rosters.

items.name: Jauan Jennings
items.headline: Juan Jennings caught 2-of-3 targets for 34 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Jennings caught a 20-yard pass, his longest reception of the season. He was targeted three times, nearly catching a long touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter, but failing to haul it in. Jennings is outside of the top-three pass-catching options for the Vikings and is irrelevant for fantasy purposes in this role. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on him in case he is traded, but Jennings does not need to be in fantasy lineups heading in to Week 8.

items.name: Jordan Watkins
items.headline: Jordan Watkins caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
items.analysis: Watkins was second among receivers in routes, running a route on 30 of the team’s 43 dropbacks, and was also third on the team overall in targets. He made a few nice catches over the middle of the field, and his day could have been much better as he caught a 20-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the second half. Unfortunately, while his feet were in bounds, the ball shifted a couple of inches when his back slammed into the ground, and replay review overturned the call of touchdown on the field. Depending on the status of the 49ers’ wide receivers coming out of next week’s bye, Watkins could be an interesting fantasy option, but it’s hard to know that for sure until we know who will be healthy for the 49ers.

items.name: C.J. Stroud
items.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 17-of-28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 27-21, Week 7 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: The Texans seemed to always be playing from well behind the sticks today with 10 penalties and Stroud was let down by a ghastly drop from Marvin Harrison Jr. with someone in his face in the fourth quarter. The Giants did a better job than other teams had at getting interior pressure on Stroud. Still, it wasn’t a bad game outside of an immediate overtime three-and-out, one that was punctuated by a dropped pick by Kayvon Thibodeaux. Stroud heads into the bye as a reasonable high-end QB2 with a Week 9 matchup against the Chargers.

items.name: George Kittle
items.headline: George Kittle caught 8-of-10 passes for 88 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
items.analysis: Unfortunately, Kittle also lost a fumble on the team’s final drive of the game as he was trying to earn extra yardage and set the team up for a better shot at the end zone. Even with that mistake, Kittle was tremendous on the day and the clear top option in the passing attack. The 49ers will be on a bye in Week 8, and then some of their injured receiving corps should return in Week 9, which might impact Kittle’s usage a bit. He will remain a rock-solid TE1 in fantasy leagues though.

items.name: Cam Ward
items.headline: Cam Ward completed 20-of-31 attempts for 181 yards and an interception in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
items.analysis: Ward did his best game manager impression in this one and made a handful of solid high-leverage throws using various arm angles. He had a positive EPA per drop back and was slightly over his expected completion rate, small victories being what they are. The Titans deployed no-huddle for much of the game and operated at a quick pace — a strategy that seemed to get Ward into some sort of rhythm early on. Ward’s accuracy issues showed up on the fourth quarter when he sailed a pass over the head of a wide open tight end who had beaten the entire Cleveland secondary. It would’ve likely been a game-winning touchdown. Ward has now cracked 200 passing yards just once through Week 7 and should only be rostered in superflex formats.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Addison also got a carry for three rushing yards. His usage involved designed touches in the shallow area, with the Vikings trying to get him out into space. His utilization dropped in the second half and he did not see many looks downfield. Addison is the clear No. 3 pass-catching option in the Vikings offense, a role that warrants WR4 consideration for Week 8 against the Lions.

items.name: Kaelon Black
items.headline: Kaelon Black rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons
items.analysis: Black’s day did not start great as he was stuffed on three straight plays inside the three-yard line on the first drive. Then he watched as Christian McCaffrey scored a touchdown on fourth down. However, McCaffrey also picked up a thigh injury on that drive and missed the remainder of the first half, which allowed Black the opportunity to rip off some nice chunk runs and a long touchdown. McCaffrey did return in the second half, and Black also lost a fumble in the second quarter, so there were some moments of inconsistency. That being said, Black looks like one of the best handcuff running backs in fantasy football.

items.name: Isaiah Likely
items.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: It was his first game with fewer than five targets all season. New York’s passing game simply targeted Houston outside the numbers and they ran the ball effectively enough that they didn’t need to feed Likely. He’ll be on the TE1 line in Week 9 against the Eagles once the Giants return from their bye week.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Jefferson led the Vikings in targets and yards on a low-volume day for the passing game. He hit a career milestone, crossing 600 career catches with a four-catch day. The Vikings’ offense continues to post low-efficiency outings as the defense lifts the team to an undefeated record. Jefferson is still the No. 1 wide receiver but banks on high volume usage and touchdowns to be a fantasy WR1. A lack of touchdown opportunities and red zone usage will be an issue in the Vikings offense, but Jefferson has a soft matchup against the Lions for Week 8. He should be back in the WR1 rankings next week.

items.name: Jerry Jeudy
items.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans.
items.analysis: Jeudy was second on the team in pass routes — behind Denzel Boston — and fourth on the team in targets. This comes after Jeudy’s Week 6 performance against the Ravens in which he went for a season-high 69 yards on four receptions. Jeudy is well behind Boston and KC Concepcion in the pass-catching pecking order and should only be rostered in the deepest leagues for now.

items.name: Jameis Winston
items.headline: Jameis Winston rushed four times for four yards and a touchdown in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: He became New York’s short-yardage tush-push option with J.J. McCarthy starting, managing a touchdown in the first half and a fourth-down conversion in the second half. That makes him more of a thorn in McCarthy’s side than anything else for fantasy purposes.

items.name: Kyle Pitts
items.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all five of his targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
items.analysis: The touchdown is nice to see, and Pitts finished tied for second on the team in both catches and targets. However, preliminary snap counts say he played on 37 of the team’s 67 snaps and ran a route on 20 of their 37 dropbacks. Charlie Woerner ran a route on 11 dropbacks and Austin Hooper ran a route on 10 dropbacks, so the Falcons continue to get tons of tight ends on the field. That makes Pitts more of a high-end TE2 option because he does have good touchdown equity.

items.name: Zachariah Branch
items.headline: Zachariah Branch caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
items.analysis: It seemed like Branch would be in for a bigger role in Week 7 with Olamide Zaccheaus out with a shoulder injury. However, Branch ran a route on just 18 of 37 dropbacks and was only targeted twice. It doesn’t seem like he’s anywhere close to playing a large enough role for fantasy value and doesn’t need to be held through the bye weeks in redraft leagues.

items.name: Aaron Jones
items.headline: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 26 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts, adding one reception for zero yards.
items.analysis: Jones got the start in the Vikings backfield, ripping off four straight carries for nine yards on Minnesota’s first possession. Outside of the opening possession, Jones took a backseat to Jordan Mason, seeing a mix of passing-down snaps and short-yardage carries. He caught his only target in the red zone but had it punched out for a fumble out of bounds. Jones left in the fourth quarter with a knee injury; he had been playing through an MCL injury and may have aggravated the issue. Prior to the injury, Jones was getting out-snapped by Mason and ends with 15 snaps to Mason’s 38, while getting six less touches. Jones is a low-end fantasy RB2 if healthy for Week 8.

items.name: Devin Singletary
items.headline: Devin Singletary rushed five times for 41 yards and a touchdown in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: He didn’t get much usage in this one, managing just 19 snaps despite Tyrone Tracy leaving in the second quarter, but Singletary made the most of his final opportunity with a 30-yard touchdown run in overtime to walk off the Texans. With Tracy and (apparently) Skattebo both managing injuries throughout the bye, Singletary could wind up with a reasonable Week 9 role. You probably don’t need to chase it on waivers this week unless you’re in a very deep league.

items.name: Chase Brown
items.headline: Chase Brown rushed 11 times for 39 yards in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens, adding four receptions for 19 additional yards.

items.name: Jahan Dotson
items.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
items.analysis: Dotson was also targeted on three different deep passes that resulted in San Francisco penalties. That doesn’t help your fantasy team, but it is indicative of his role in this offense. Dotson did run the second-most routes of any receiver on the Falcons; however, he is really only targeted on deep shots down the field, which will make his production inconsistent.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: Skattebo looked rejuvenated after his benching, bulldozing a few Houston tacklers on his touchdown run that ended with a backflip. He did pull up late on a 42-yarder that could have sealed the game, and he seemed to be gesturing towards his hamstring on the sideline. We don’t have a full update on that as the Giants quickly closed out the game thereafter, but Skattebo will get a bye week to heal up as we try to figure out how this Giants backfield will sort itself out. Skattebo’s fantasy value looks to have bounced back to some real extent today.

items.name: Elic Ayomanor
items.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
items.analysis: Ayomanor has shown signs of life of late in a Titans offense operating quickly in recent weeks. Against the Browns he tied Carnell Tate for the team lead in targets while running a route on nearly 90 percent of the team’s drop backs. Even with more involvement in the Tennessee offense, Ayomanor should remain on the waiver wire in most fantasy formats ahead of the Titans’ Week 8 matchup against the Steelers.

items.name: Caleb Douglas
items.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: Douglas was active for the first time since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2. Though he logged a measly 14 percent target share, Douglas was involved early, turning a first-quarter red zone target into his first NFL touchdown. Douglas turned his second catch of the day, a short out route, into a 63-yard touchdown by toe-tapping his way along the sideline for a game-sealing score. His role is only going in one direction after the breakout performance. He will be in the WR3 mix when the Dolphins take on the Pats next week.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 7-of-11 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ 43-13, Week 7 win over the Panthers.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-7 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.

items.name: J.J. McCarthy
items.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 20-of-28 passes for 252 yards in New York’s 27-21, Week 7 win over the Texans.
items.analysis: Nine threatened a really good box score, crossing 200 yards by the third quarter, but both the Texans (playing more aggressive coverage) and the Giants (using Jameis Winston in short-yardage situations) conspired to keep McCarthy scoreless. Still, it was a nice debut start. McCarthy took three sacks but had zero turnovers while managing a handful of nice throws. The Giants head on bye in Week 8, but McCarthy has played like a reasonable superflex QB2 against the Eagles in a few weeks.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate caught 5-of-7 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
items.analysis: It was another solid if unspectacular outing for the rookie. The Titans operated a fast-pace offense through much of the game against Cleveland, using no-huddle for long stretches of the ballgame. That seemed to put Cam Ward in some sort of rhythm — to the benefit of a few Titans skill position players. Tate now has at least six receptions in three of his past four outings. Tate, who entered the week with a 46 percent air yards share and a 25 percent target share, is an every-week starter who could be a WR3 option next week against a pass-funnel Bengals defense.

items.name: Khalil Herbert
items.headline: Khalil Herbert rushed two times for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
items.analysis: Herbert was filling in for Brian Robinson in Week 7, but he did not have anything close to Brian Robinson’s workload. Hebert also caught one pass for 19 yards and was a couple of inches from taking that into the end zone for a score. The 28-year-old will likely be back on the practice squad next weekend if/when Brian Robinson returns.

items.name: Bucky Irving
items.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
items.analysis: The two-score day on the ground was somehow the first of Irving’s career. He led the way as the Bucs rolled up a ridiculous 258 yards rushing in a stunning road clobbering of the Panthers. That means Irving ceded plenty of work to Kenneth Gainwell and a little to Sean Tucker, but everyone got home as the Bucs simply dominated on the ground. Irving’s scores came from four and one yards out, meaning he had the goal-line advantage on Tucker while the game was still in doubt. It was a really strong performance, and a nice bounce-back effort after a rough Week 6. This figures to remain an up and down offense and rushing attack, but Irving has proven to be a high-end RB2 more weeks than not. That will include for Week 8 against the Falcons.

items.name: Jordan Mason
items.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 15 times for 68 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Mason did not start for the Vikings, but out-touched and out-snapped Aaron Jones. He was the primary early-down back and saw two targets as well, though he did not catch either of them. Jones (knee) exited the game in the fourth quarter, leading to Mason finishing out the game for the Vikings. Even before the Jones injury, Mason was the the back with the highest utilization. Mason is a low-end fantasy RB2 heading into a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions; he could emerge as a top-15 option if Jones misses time.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 137 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.

items.name: Bijan Robinson
items.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 20 times for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
items.analysis: Robinson did add 59 yards receiving on five catches to help salvage his fantasy day, but this is the third straight week he has delivered a modest fantasy return after explosive performances in Weeks 3 and 4. In fact, this is now five of seven games this season that Robinson has been held under 90 yards rushing. He’s contributing as a pass-catcher, and he looks elusive when he can get beyond the line of scrimmage, but the Falcons may need to make an adjustment on offense with defenses clearly keying on stopping Robinson. We’d expect them to focus on getting him going next week against the Bucs.

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 148 yards and one touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-8 targets for 25 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans.
items.analysis: Boston was third in targets among Browns pass catchers and saw lots and lots of air yards from Deshaun Watson, who nearly connected with Boston for two long touchdowns on the day. So it goes with a high-variance downfield option like Boston, who now has three straight quiet outings. With a 45 percent air yards share headed into Week 7, Boston will certainly have his big box scores in the coming weeks. Predicting when that might happen will be tough for fantasy managers. He should be a flex play in Week 8 against the Steelers.

items.name: Michael Penix
items.headline: Michael Penix Jr. completed 25-of-34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ 29-20, Week 7 win over the 49ers.
items.analysis: The stats may make it seem like Penix had his way with the 49ers, but it didn’t seem like a seamless performance in reality. He missed some deep passes and overthrew Drake London on a clear touchdown in the second half. He really wasn’t able to get much going down the field, but the Falcons’ defense forced four turnovers, which set up some short fields that Penix was able to take advantage of. He gets a good matchup against the Bucs next week.

items.name: KC Concepcion
items.headline: KC Concepcion caught 8-of-10 targets for 129 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding three rushes for 23 yards.
items.analysis: The Browns slot man shredded the Tennessee secondary from start to finish. Coming into the game with a season-high of 64 receiving yards, Concepcion eclipsed that mark in the second quarter and didn’t look back. He continually shed tacklers against a low-effort Titans defense and functioned as the centerpiece of the Cleveland passing game. He led the Browns in targets, mostly seeing designed short-area throws from Deshaun Watson. In a Browns offense with a top-10 neutral pass rate, Concepcion should be a weekly top-36 option in PPR formats. He’ll get the Steelers in Week 8.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 5-of-6 targets for 115 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Cooper was an electric deep threat once again, bringing down catches for 60 and 52 yards, neither of which was his touchdown. He scored shortly after the 52-yard grab by lining up as a running back and cruising past his defender for an easy three-yard touchdown reception. Cooper Jr. is the first rookie in franchise history with back-to-back games with 100+ receiving yards and a touchdown. While we can’t say he has overtaken Garrett Wilson already, this is looking like, at worst, a co-WR1 situation. Cooper will flirt with a WR2 ranking when he takes on the Raiders next week.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Brock Purdy completed 27-of-40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the 49ers’ 29-20, Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
items.analysis: After losing seemingly every wide receiver to injury, it was only a matter of time before we finally had a down Purdy game. The truth is, he didn’t even play poorly. His first interception was on a pass that he was trying to throw away when safety Jesse Bates made an incredible toe-drag interception. The second pick was on a really nice play by linebacker Kendal Daniels over the middle. Purdy looked good and gave his team a chance to win despite a depleted offense. The 49ers will have a bye next week and then hopefully get back at least one of their primary receivers before a Week 9 game against the Raiders.

items.name: Tony Pollard
items.headline: Tony Pollard had 25 rushes for 129 yards and three touchdowns in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 26 yards.
items.analysis: Pollard, whose last big game before Sunday was against these same Browns in 2025, scored two first quarter touchdowns against a Cleveland rush defense that seemed uninterested in tackling Pollard. He scored a third rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter, and could have had a fourth score if not for a Browns goal line stand. Pollard has seen big workloads with Tyjae Spears (knee) sidelined but hadn’t done much with the opportunity before Sunday. The Titans offense operated quickly, using no-huddle through much of the game. That created more play volume that benefited Pollard and the rest of the Titans offense. As long as Spears remains sidelined, Pollard should remain in 12-team lineups next week against the Bengals.

items.name: Malik Willis
items.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns in the Dolphins’ 28-28, Week 7 win over the Jets.
items.analysis: Willis also added 37 yards and a touchdown on eight rush attempts. It was, by far, his best performance as a Dolphin. It was also the first win for both Willis and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Willis picked apart the Jets for chunk play after chunk play. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard completion to Caleb Douglas, though nearly all of those yards came after the catch. He had already connected with Douglas earlier in the game for his first touchdown of the day. Things will be a lot tougher for Willis and the Miami offense when they take on the Patriots next week. Despite the strong showing today, Willis will remain buried in the QB2 ranks for Week 8.

items.name: Tyler Huntley
items.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 23-of-34 passes for 298 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens’ 35-13, Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: This makes it two-straight games where Huntley and the Ravens failed to score in the second half. Huntley was solid in the first half, throwing for 227-1-0 on 21 passes, with his lone touchdown pass coming on a 48-yard screen pass to Zay Flowers on the Ravens’ opening drive. He would lead the Ravens on two drives that ended in field goals in the second quarter, but the Ravens struggled mightily in the second half as the Bengals rallied for 35 unanswered points. At one point, Huntley had the Ravens in position for a short field goal to go up 16-14, but passed on the points and opted to go for it on fourth-and-two, which resulted in an incomplete pass to tight end Josh Cuevas. It was reported during the game that Lamar Jackson (ankle) would be back for Week 8’s game against the Ravens. Now sitting at 4-3 on the year, it goes without saying that the Ravens are in desperate need of Jackson in what is shaping up to be a highly competitive AFC North division.

items.name: Kyler Murray
items.headline: Kyler Murray completed 14-of-24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ 16-10, Week 6 win over the Colts, adding five carries for 39 yards.
items.analysis: The story of the Vikings season has been a vaunted defense with a mediocre offense. That remained true in Week 7, with the Minnesota offense scoring just one touchdown on a Kyler Murray five-yard toss to T.J. Hockenson. Murray averaged 6.3 yards per attempt and struggled to connect with open receivers much of the day. He added 39 yards as a rusher, most of those coming on a 35-yard scamper prior to his passing touchdown. Murray came up limping after a second quarter play but did not miss any plays and finished the game. He threw an end zone interception in the second quarter, but the defender was ruled out of bounds. On the flip side, Murray nearly had Juan Jennings for a long passing touchdown in the second quarter, but Jennings failed to haul it in. Murray is a high-variance fantasy quarterback due to his rushing upside, but his passing ability remains poor and caps his ceiling. He will be in the fantasy QB2 ranks for a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions.

items.name: Joe Burrow
items.headline: Joe Burrow completed 22-of-30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 35-13, Week 7 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: After throwing for just 55 scoreless yards in the first half, Burrow and the Bengals came out firing on all cylinders in the second half. Trailing 13-0 at halftime, Burrow immediately orchestrated a nine-play, 66-yard drive that ended with a six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and followed that up with four more touchdown drives on his team’s next four possessions to jump out to a 35-13 lead. Burrow was as sharp as could be in the second half, completing 16-of-18 attempts while also completing two passes of 20-plus air yards. Burrow has now thrown four touchdowns in back-to-back games and has four multi-touchdown games this season. He’ll be on the QB1 radar next week when the Bengals play host to the Titans.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: Daniel Jones completed 13-of-22 passes for 108 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 16-10, Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding four carries for 13 yards.
items.analysis: The Colts passing game struggled to get going against an elite Vikings defense. Jones crossed 100 passing yards on the Colts’ last possession of the game, finishing the drive off with a game-ending interception. He nearly threw a first quarter interception just off Vikings LB Blake Cashman’s hands and threw the ball into danger several other times. Jones was sacked four times and was ineffective as a runner against the Vikings’ pressure-inducing front-seven. Out of the Colts’ first 35 offensive plays, 16 had gone for zero or negative yardage. It was ultimately a poor passing day against a tough defense for Jones and the Colts. Jones is in the fantasy QB2 ranks against another tough defense in the Jaguars for Week 8.

items.name: Tytus Howard
items.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) is questionable to return in Week 7 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Howard left the game in the first half with a head injury and had not returned as of the start of the fourth quarter. Losing Howard would be a tough blow for a Cleveland offensive line that has been solid in both run and pass blocking in 2026. Look for Howard to enter the league’s concussion protocol in the coming days.

items.name: Aaron Jones
items.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) is questionable to return Week 7 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Jones suffered a knee injury after a fourth quarter run against the Colts. He has notably been playing through an MCL injury and may have re-aggravated it here. Jones struggled to walk and spent time in the medical tent. Jordan Mason is the team’s top running back while Jones is out.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Bryce Young completed 14-of-27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Panthers’ Week 7 game against the Bucs, also losing a fumble-six.
items.analysis: With the Panthers somehow losing 43-6 in the fourth quarter, Young gave way to Kenny Pickett for the final 10:11. Pickett immediately engineered a garbage time touchdown drive. This was by far Young’s worst game of what had so far been a legitimate breakout campaign, as he short-circuited one drive after another and set up Bucs short fields with turnovers. The fumble-six was the most costly mistake, but Young’s second interception was probably his worst throw. He was fooled by the coverage under pressure and threw the ball right to Tykee Smith. Young’s first pick came after Jalen Coker fell down. In between all the miscues, Young could get nothing going with either Coker or Tetairoa McMillan. It was hard to see this coming — especially against the Bucs — but it is even harder to see it continuing for Thursday’s short-week date with the Packers. With that contest likely to feature shootout game script, Young will remain in the low-end QB1 ranks.

items.name: Erick All
items.headline: Erick All (knee) wil not return in Week 7 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: All exited in the third quarter with a knee injury and walked off the field on his own. The third-year tight end has a history of bad knee injuries, so this one is a bit concerning. All was having a decent day against the Ravens and left the game with three receptions for 26 yards on three targets.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Rams declared CB Trent McDuffie, QB Ty Simpson, LB Nate Landman, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost and TE Max Klare inactive for Week 7 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during a Week 6 practice. The Rams have listed him as questionable to play despite the fact that he has not yet resumed practicing. He was playing extremely well prior to the injury. His loss is consequential. The Rams elevated LB Eric Kendricks and CB Cam Lampkin to the active roster for today’s game.

items.name: Cade Mays
items.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is active for Week 7 against the Packers.
items.analysis: Lions declared TE Jackson Meeks, S Bishop Fitzgerald, C Seth McLaughlin, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DE Ahmed Hassanein inactive against the Packers.

items.name: T'Vondre Sweat
items.headline: T’Vondre Sweat suffered a knee injury in Week 7 against the Dolphins and will not return.
items.analysis: Sweat went down in the second quarter. He walked off the field under his own power but immediately went into the medical tent. The team ruled him out after halftime. Sweat has 15 combined tackles and two TFLs this year.

items.name: Aaron Banks
items.headline: Aaron Banks (knee/toe) is active for Week 7 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Banks was questionable headed into the weekend. He’ll miss at least one game with toe and knee injuries, a potential blow to Jordan Love, Josh Jacobs, and the Green Bay offense. With Jacobs active for the first time this year, the Packers will keep Kaleb Johnson inactive. Packers declared CB Benjamin St-Juste, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, OL Jager Burton, OL Donovan Jennings, and G Kevin Zeitler inactive against Detroit.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: Puka Nacua (calf) is active for Week 7 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Start him. The Rams clearly feel comfortable with their superstar playing today, and we should too. Nacua’s upside is too high for him to remain on fantasy football benches. Reporting on Nacua’s ailment suggests he is not necessarily dealing with a strain. It can perhaps be best described as muscle fatigue, though we are doctors here at Rotoworld. Re-injury is possible, but we can safely expect him to handle a large workload whenever he is on the field. Nacua is a high-end WR1.

items.name: Mike Washington Jr.
items.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is active for Week 7 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Whether Washington plays all that much remains to be seen. He is not a recommended FLEX starter. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak has misdirected at times with injury-related comments. The Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker IV, DE Cian Slone, S Dalton Johnson, DT Jonah Laulu, G Bryan Cabeldue, S Tristin McCollum and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 7 against the Rams. O’Connell will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

items.name: Vega Ioane
items.headline: Ravens OG Vega Ioane (knee) will not return in Week 7 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Ioane exited late in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and was ruled out shortly after halftime. The rookie first-rounder appeared on 16 snaps and has started every game for the Ravens this season, splitting time between right guard and center. He was replaced by Emery Jones.

items.name: Budda Baker
items.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is active for Week 7 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Baker was reportedly good to go as of this morning, so this doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Even in his 10th NFL season, Baker is still wreaking havoc on opposing offenses. He has four pass breakups, one pick, and 3.5 sacks this year. Inactive for the Cardinals are RB Jeremiyah Love, QB Carson Beck, DT Walter Nolen III, S Andrew Wingard, OL Jon Gaines, CB Max Melton, and OL Albert Reese.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: Christian McCaffrey (thigh) returned to the game in Week 7 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: McCaffrey was injured on the first drive of the game when the 49ers scored a touchdown. The training staff was working on his thigh before he jogged into the locker room in the second quarter and was listed as questionable to return. It was a 14-3 49ers lead when McCaffrey went into the locker room, and it’s 19-14 in favor of the Falcons now, so the team is gonna see if their star running back can get them back in front.

items.name: Pat Surtain
items.headline: Broncos declared CB Pat Surtain, QB Sam Ehlinger, S Talanoa Hufanga, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Jordan Jackson, and DL Tyler Onyedim inactive for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Surtain is expected to return for a crucial matchup with the Chiefs next week. The Broncos will be without one of the league’s superstar corners in the meantime. Surtain’s absence should make life a little easier for Michael Wilson, who is in the midst of a two-game slump.

items.name: Jonah Coleman
items.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is active for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper is also active. Coleman hasn’t played since Week 2, when he turned 10 carries into 39 yards and a score. The Broncos were banged up at running back that week. They have since established a stable two-man rotation with JK Dobbins operating between the tackles and RJ Harvey handling passing downs. Coleman will likely take a backseat to those two this week.

items.name: Tyrone Tracy
items.headline: Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) is questionable to return to New York’s Week 7 game against the Texans.
items.analysis: Tracy had six carries for 15 yards and a touchdown before leaving, adding a two-yard catch on his only target. He was spotted in pads on the sideline, stretching his legs, so it looks like there’s a non-zero chance he returns.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: Christian McCaffrey is questionable to return to Week 7 against the Falcons with a thigh injury.
items.analysis: McCaffrey was used heavily on the first drive with the 49ers down so many offensive players, and he came out of that drive with a touchdown but also a thigh injury. The trainers worked on him on the sideline for two drives before finally bringing him into the medical tent. The 49ers do have a bye next week, so they could try to get him back into the game, but they are also up 14-3 at this point, so the Falcons will likely need to get the game closer. Kaelon Black will continue to see a workhorse role while CMC is sidelined.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: CBS Sports’ Tracy Wolfson reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Reporting from the sideline of Sunday’s Ravens vs. Bengals game, Wolfson reports that Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told her Jackson would play in Week 8. According to Wolfson, the late decision to sit Jackson this week came after the team had a chance to review footage of Jackson in practice. Minter said Jackson still didn’t look like himself in practice, which is why the team opted to give him one more week away. This is the first time Minter has committed to Jackson returning, so hopefully this is a good sign for his Week 8 availability. We will, of course, be monitoring his practice throughout the week until he is fully removed from the injury report.

items.name: Juwan Johnson
items.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Johnson was solid over the first four weeks of the season, but this was another clunker for the 30-year-old tight end. After going over 50 yards in his first four games and bringing in three touchdowns, Johnson has just 23 total yards without a score in the next three. Because of positional value Johnson can’t be completely ignored, but the Saints haven’t paid much attention to him lately, so it’s time to look for alternatives, at least.

items.name: Barion Brown
items.headline: Barion Brown caught all three of his targets for 57 yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Brown did virtually all of his damage on a 49-yard connection that helped set up the only touchdown of the day for the Saints. The 22-year-old also had 97 yards in return yardage, and the athleticism of Brown was apparent even on a limited amount of touches. The sixth-round selection is worth keeping an eye on in in dynasty leagues, but isn’t someone fantasy managers can trust in redraft formats as of yet.

items.name: Devaughn Vele
items.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-5 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Vele brought in a one-yard touchdown on fourth-and-goal late in the second quarter to tie the game at 10-10. It would be the last points the Saints would score. Vale has hovered around these numbers through the first half of 2026, and while it provides Shough with a nice safety valve, it’s not exactly what fantasy managers should be chasing. He’ll be a WR4 in Week 9 against the Browns after the Saints “enjoy” their bye in Week 8.

items.name: Devaughn Vele
items.headline: Devaughn Vale caught 5-of-5 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.

items.name: Chris Olave
items.headline: Chris Olave caught 6-of-10 targets for 57 yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Olave was once again a shorter-yardage target with a long gain of just 14 yards in the contest. Tyler Shough missed the 26-year-old on what would have been a walk-in touchdown from deep on a disappointing day for the top target in the Saints’ passing attack, at least based on expectations. He’ll remain one of the top fantasy receiving options in his next game, but that won’t come for two weeks as the Saints get a bye before facing the Browns in Week 9.

items.name: Pat Freiermuth
items.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Freiermuth didn’t appear to be bothered by his calf injury, and he quadrupled the targets of Darnell Washington (4-to-1) in this game. Washington was able to convert his only target for a touchdown, however, and Freirmuth dropped what would have been a 20-yard gain in the third quarter. Freiermuth will likely get a similar amount of targets in Week 8 against the Browns, for better or worse.

items.name: Darnell Washington
items.headline: Darnell Washington caught his only target for a four-yard touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Washington used his massive — massive seems like a huge understatement — size to haul in a touchdown near the sideline. That’s his third touchdown in four games, and it’s pretty clear that he’s become a focal point once the Steelers get inside of the red zone. He just isn’t much of one outside of those opportunities, and that makes him the most touchdown dependent tight end to ever exist. Maybe a little bit of hyperbole there. Washington will try and score again in Week 8 against the Browns.

items.name: Germie Bernard
items.headline: Germie Bernard caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Aaron Rodgers was focused on hitting his halfbacks out of the backfield much more than his wideouts, and Bernard was unable to get much done outside of a 20-yard reception. The rookie wideout had gone over 80 yards in his last two games, but this shows the volatility in Bernard’s fantasy profile as a rookie. He’ll look to bounce back against the Browns in Week 8.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for five yards in the Saints’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers, adding seven receptions for 57 yards.
items.analysis: Tyler Shough ended up leading the Saints with seven rushing yards. Yikes. Kamara was effective as a receiver out of the backfield, but to say that New Orleans struggled to run the ball is quite the understatement; finishing with 18 yards on 17 attempts. The good news for fantasy managers that used Kamara is that he was effective out of the backfield as a receiver, but it’s a modest day for the 31-year-old. Kamara and the Saints will try and get something going after a bye against the Browns in Week 9.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: DK Metcalf caught 2-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: After having a whopping 15 targets in the Week 6 win over the Bucs, Metcalf was essentially a non-factor in this one. He was able to haul in a 51-yard connection that set up the lone touchdown for the Steelers, but for the second time in three weeks, Metcalf was held under four catches. He’ll be a volatile WR2/3 for Week 8 in a matchup with the Browns.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed nine times for 48 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding six catches for 45 yards.
items.analysis: Dowdle was the clear backup to Jaylen Warren, but he was able to have a solid day thanks in large part to checkdowns from Aaron Rodgers. The 28-year-old had a long rush of 16 yards, and the toe injury that sidelined him earlier in the campaign doesn’t appear to be bothering him. Dowdle is a FLEX option for Week 8 against the Browns, at best.

items.name: Jaylen Warren
items.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 18 times for 101 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding three catches for 36 yards.
items.analysis: Warren got off to a hot start with 43 yards on the first drive, with 29 of those coming on a play that set up a short field goal. He totaled 78 yards in the first half, but found the sledding a little tougher in the final two periods with the Saints focused on stuffing the run. He outcarried Rico Dowdle 18-9, although Dowdle did add six catches to make the touches a little more even. Warren will look to impress again in Week 8 against the Browns’ front seven.

items.name: Tyler Shough
items.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-38 passes for 273 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Saints’ 16-10, Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Shough’s seven rushing yards led the team, which isn’t ideal. The 27-year-old was mostly accurate and on-time with his throws, but he should have had three turnovers on the first half — one dropped interception, one strip-sack that was overturned and one fumble that luckily went out of bounds — and he threw a costly red-zone interception. It wasn’t Shough at his best, but there were some flashes of brilliance in the loss. Shough will get a bye week before he faces the Browns in Week 9.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 19-of-30 passes for 219 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ 16-10, Week 7 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Rodgers dinked and dunked for the overwhelming majority of the game with over half of his completions coming to his running backs. He did connect with DK Metcalf for a 51-yard connection on a beautiful deep ball, and he found Darnell Washington for his lone scoring play. Outside of that passing touchdown, the biggest play for Rodgers was a scramble on third-and-six just before the two-minute warning that essentially cemented the game. Rodgers and the Steelers move to 5-2 with the win in Paris, and they’ll face the Browns in Week 8. He’ll be a QB2 for that contest, on paper.

items.name: Za'Darius Smith
items.headline: Za’Darius Smith (neck) and Gervon Dexter Sr. (hamstring) will both play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Both defenders were both listed as questionable for the Falcons, but both of them will be able to suit up, which is great news for the Falcons against a really banged-up 49ers offense. It remains to be seen if either player will play a full complement of snaps.

items.name: Olamide Zaccheaus
items.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

items.name: Denzel Ward
items.headline: Denzel Ward (hand) is active for Week 7 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Ward missed some practice time this week with a right hand injury. He’ll suit up against Cam Ward and the atrocious Titans passing attack. Browns declared QB Taylen Green, LB Justin Jefferson, CB Noah Igbinoghene, RB Audric Estime, DT Mike Hall Jr., and C Parker Brailsford inactive against Tennessee.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Colts declared TE Tyler Warren, LB Bryce Boettcher, LB CJ Allen, CB Sauce Gardner, TE Tyler Warren, WR Anthony Gould, G Dalton Tucker, and QB Riley Leonard inactive for Week 7 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Warren was declared out earlier in the week due to a groin injury. Sauce Gardner (calf) and Anthony Gould (concussion) were also already declared out while Bryce Boettcher (groin) and CJ Allen (ankle) were declared out after having a questionable tag. Riley Leonard will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

items.name: Jaelan Phillips
items.headline: Panthers declared EDGE Jaelan Phillips, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, C Sam Hecht, OT Stone Forsythe, and EDGE TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 7 against the Bucs.
items.analysis: Phillips is a big loss, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the Panthers vs. a more-injured and undermanned Bucs squad. Phillips is week to week after pulling his hammy in Week 6 against the Eagles.

items.name: Jalen Tolbert
items.headline: Dolphins declared WR Jalen Tolbert, LB Willie Gay, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., CB Reese Taylor, DE Rob Beal Jr., OL DJ Campbell, and OT Chukwuebuka Godrick inactive for Week 7 against the Jets.
items.analysis: With Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell both healthy, Tolbert doesn’t have a spot on the game-day roster and is a healthy scratch this week. Douglas is back after missing a month because of an ankle injury.

items.name: Shemar Stewart
items.headline: Bengals declared S Russ Yeas, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, DE Shemar Stewart, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 7 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: The Bengals are coming off their bye at near-full strength, with all five inactives healthy scratches. Stewart, who was the No. 17 overall pick in last year’s draft, has appeared in just three games this season, totaling three tackles and one sack.

items.name: Theo Johnson
items.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) is inactive for New York’s Week 7 game against the Texans.
items.analysis: Johnson was doubtful before being ruled out. He’ll have a chance to come back after New York’s Week 8 bye. Also inactive for the Giants are: OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow (knee), CB Greg Newsome II (concussion), S Jevón Holland (concussion), QB Jake Haener (3rd QB) and CB Nikko Reed. OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and Tyler Nubin (neck) are playing despite being tagged as questionable on Friday.

items.name: Jordan Mason
items.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Colts.
items.analysis: The Vikings activated Mason off injured reserve and he is officially active for the first time since suffering a thumb injury in Week 1. He will split backfield touches with Aaron Jones, with Jones likely getting more of the passing-down work and Mason more the early-down work. Mason is a fantasy RB3 in his return. The Vikings declared S Jakobe Thomas, QB Max Brosmer, CB Chuck Demmings, RB Demond Claiborne, DL Elijah Willliams and OT Caleb Tiernan inactive for Week 7 against the Colts.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, WR Elijah Sarratt, FS Jaylinn Hawkins, OG Andrew Vorhees, and DE Broderick Washington inactive for Week 7 against the Bengals
items.analysis: Washington was the only player carrying a questionable designation heading into Sunday’s game, but he has officially been ruled out with an ankle injury. Jackson, who is also dealing with an ankle injury, will miss his third-straight game, paving the way for Tyler Huntley to start in the pivotal AFC North matchup.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: When last we left Mayfield, he was struggling mightily in Weeks 1-3. Predictably, UDFA Jalon Daniels was not any better in his stead. Mayfield returns to an undermanned skill corps, as Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) is out for Week 7. Mayfield is a shaky option in the QB16-18 range. Joining Egbuka on the shelf are OT Luke Goedeke, S Antoine Winfield, OG Billy Schrauth, DL DeMonte Capehart and CB Ayden Garnes.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Jets declared Breece Hall (quad) inactive for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Hall was reportedly unlikely to play as of this morning, so the news of his absence doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Braelon Allen will draw the start once again. Facing a dreadful Miami defense, Allen is on the RB1/2 border for Week 7. Also inactive for the Jets are CB Jarvis Brownlee, OG Dylan Parham, EDGE Joe Ossai, RB Kene Nwangwu, OG Max Mitchell, and DT Jack Heflin.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
items.analysis: As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

items.name: Jalen Pitre
items.headline: Texans declared S Jalen Pitre (shoulder), RB David Montgomery (groin), S Reed Blankenship (concussion), T Blake Fisher (thumb), OL Febechi Nwaiwu, OL Nate Thomas and TE Marlin Klein inactive for Houston’s Week 7 game against the Giants.
items.analysis: Both Pitre and Montgomery, who are week-to-week, have a chance to come back after Houston’s Week 8 bye. They’ve both missed two weeks now with their respective injuries. The latter three are healthy scratches.

items.name: Brian Thomas
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes the Jaguars “might be willing to listen” to trade offers for Brian Thomas Jr.
items.analysis: Schefter didn’t directly cite any sources, but the dots are extremely easy to connect. Thomas Jr. has been the subject of trade rumors for the past year and his role has all but disappeared this season. He hasn’t caught a pass since Week 4 and was benched in the second half of the team’s Week 6 loss to Houston. At this point, a trade is seemingly in the best interest of both parties. Expect the market for Thomas Jr. to heat up ahead of the November 10th deadline.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined, life will not be easy for Tanner McKee on Monday evening, even in a plus matchup. Wicks drew some summer hype as a well-paid reclamation project for the Eagles, but he has caught more than three passes only two times all season and has not reached 70 yards since Week 2. He is a poor hold in 12-team leagues with five-man benches.

items.name: Peyton Manning
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Peyton Manning is not expected to be a candidate for the Colts’ general manager vacancy.
items.analysis: Manning was floated as a potential replacement for Chris Ballard after the latter was fired, but it was just baseless speculation. According to Schefter, the Colts have not discussed hiring Manning in any capacity. With no front office experience to his name and loads of media obligations to tend to, it doesn’t make sense for Manning to take a job with an NFL team at this time.

items.name: Alontae Taylor
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Alontae Taylor is expected to be active for Week 7 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Taylor, who was signed to a three-year, $60 million contract in the offseason, was a healthy scratch last week. That appears to be a temporary benching as Taylor will be back in the mix against Cleveland. Pro Football Focus currently has Taylor ranked 101st in coverage grade among all corners. His return doesn’t move the needle for Tennessee’s defense.

items.name: Mike Washington Jr.
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Mike Washington (foot/back) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Washington Jr. didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday but still received a questionable designation for Week 7. Fowler added that there is “some optimism” that he plays this week, but the pre-game workout will be the determining factor. Washington saw an uptick in carries last week with nine totes for 43 yards. We don’t expect as much work to go this way given the injury situation.

items.name: Grant Delpit
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Grant Delpit (concussion) will play in Week 7 against the
items.analysis: Delpit cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend and is good to go. Denzel Ward, on the other hand, will go through warmups to see if he can play. Ward is dealing with a hand injury and is listed as questionable for Week 7.

items.name: Budda Baker
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Budda Baker (groin/illness) is expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Baker was listed as questionable for Week 7 after getting in a limited practice on Friday. He is good to go after making it through the weekend unscathed. Baker has one interception, four pass breakups, and a stunning 3.5 sacks this year.

items.name: Nick Emmanwori
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Nick Emmanwori (hip) is expected to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Uchenna Nwosu, also dealing with a hip injury, is also expected to suit up. No free lunch for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs this week. The Seahawks will be at full force. Facing the best defense in the league by most measures, Mahomes is on the QB1/2 border for Week 7.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) is likely to play in Week 8 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Rapoport added that Jackson was really close to playing this week. With Tyler Huntley playing well enough to go 1-1 so far, the Ravens took a cautious approach and ruled him out for Week 7. Huntley will start versus the Bengals later today. If all goes well in practice next week, Jackson should be back and vying for the QB1 crown in a shootout with the Bills for Week 8.

items.name: Myles Garrett
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Rams are hopeful Myles Garrett (knee) returns to practice at least next week.
items.analysis: Rapoport didn’t go as far as to say they hope he is back for Week 8’s game against the Commanders, but it’s at least on the table. Garrett is currently on injured reserve, so we’ll know if he’s making progress if they open his practice window next week. The reigning DPOY has been out since Week 1 after undergoing surgery on his knee.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Rams are “confident” Puka Nacua (calf) will play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Nacua is going to test out his calf issue in warmups. Rapoport said Nacua isn’t necessarily dealing with a calf strain. He simply didn’t feel he could explode like he needed to. Nacua’s groin injury was described similarly earlier this year. Fantasy managers will want to keep an eye on this injury ahead of kickoff. If Nacua can’t go, Jordan Whittington will take on a larger role in the offense.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Josh Jacobs is expected to get “a normal allotment of reps for a starter” in Week 7 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Packers OC Adam Stenavich told reporters Jacobs looked “great” in practice earlier this week, so we’re going to assume he’s in football shape and ready to go for Week 7. Given Garafolo’s reporting, Jacobs is already back on the RB1/2 border for a potential shootout with Detroit.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
items.analysis: As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

items.name: Za'Darius Smith
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Za’Darius Smith (neck) is expected to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: The same is true of Gervon Dexter, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Rapoport added that there is “much less optimism” for Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). That could mean an uptick in snaps for rookie wideout Zachariah Branch. He’s worth an add in deep leagues, but this offense isn’t likely to support another fantasy-relevant pass-catcher.

items.name: Pat Surtain
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Pat Surtain (ankle) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Surtain will miss his third straight game with the ankle injury. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. With the Chiefs in the hole for Week 8, holding Surtain out one more game to get him back for a must-win AFC West showdown makes sense. Per Rapoport, there’s a “good chance” he’s back next week.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is active for Week 7 against the Saints.
items.analysis: The knee issue was new for Dowdle and limited him to three partial practices this week. He was listed as questionable for Week 7 on Friday. Dowdle will once again form the 1B portion of Pittsburgh’s backfield committee. He’s a low-end RB3 versus the Saints.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall (quad) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Rapoport added that Hall might work out to see if he can go, but it’s “a bit early” for him to return. That means he won’t be playing this week. Hall returned to practice on Wednesday but never got in a full session. The team will give him another week to ramp up. He should be back for Week 8 versus the Raiders. Braelon Allen will draw the start again this week, putting him near the top of the RB2 ranks versus Miami.

items.name: J.J. McCarthy
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Giants are expected to start J.J. McCarthy “beyond their Week 8 bye.”
items.analysis: The Giants pivoted to “NINE” after he lit up the Saints for 243 yards in the fourth quarter of Week 6. Having already spent some draft capital to acquire McCarthy, the team is going to give him an extended tryout as the starter. If he does well, the Giants will likely hang on to him as Jaxson Dart’s backup next year. They could also trade him in the offseason if he plays well to garner interest from other teams.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cam Skattebo “is expected to resume his role as the team’s lead back” in Week 7 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Skattebo was benched for his fumbling issues last week. He did not touch the ball once, while Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy, and Devin Singletary all got a few opportunities. The team then cut Harris a few days after Sunday’s loss. After a week in the doghouse, Skattebo appears to be back as the team’s top runner, though we still expect a committee approach from John Harbaugh. Rapoport even said that it’s unclear who will draw the start, so we aren’t sold on Skattebo as a safe fantasy option this week. At best, he’s a high-risk RB3.

items.name: Josh Simmons
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chiefs coach Andy Reid told Josh Simmons to leave a team meeting on Wednesday.
items.analysis: According to Rapoport, Simmons was sitting with his feet up during a meeting and Reid told him to put his feet down. Simmons then “pushed back” by saying he had to sit that way because of his back injury. Reid then sent him to get treatment from the training staff. Even Patrick Mahomes chimed in and told Simmons to leave. Simmons was placed on injured reserve the next day. The former first-round pick appeared in just eight games as a rookie and hasn’t taken the field yet this year. Now he’s becoming a problem in the locker room on top of his never-ending health issues. We wouldn’t expect to see him play in a Chiefs uniform again anytime soon.

items.name: Brian Branch
items.headline: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
items.analysis: The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

items.name: Brandin Echols
items.headline: Steelers declared CB Brandin Echols, WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, RB Eli Heidenreich, and CB Terell Smith inactive for Week 7 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Echols and Skowronek are the only players on Pittsburgh’s active roster who will miss today’s game because of injuries, though they have several key players on IR. Both players have more snaps on special teams than offense or defense this year.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: 49ers activated Christian Kirk (calf) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: The 49ers would normally have Kirk on a pitch count for his first game of the year. With their top four receivers unavailable for today’s game, Kirk may be thrust into a full-time role right away. He will be in the mix for WR1 duties in San Francisco alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. Kirk is a long-shot FLEX option for his first game as a 49er.

items.name: Maliek Collins
items.headline: Browns signed Maliek Collins to a two-year, $30 million contract extension.
items.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the deal includes $23 million in total guarantees. Collins has heated up recently with 3.5 sacks over his past three games. He is coming off a career-high 6.5 sacks in 2025 and now has a chance to top that number this year. Collins’ new deal keeps him under contract with the Browns through 2028.

items.name: Cesar Ruiz
items.headline: Saints declared OG Cesar Ruiz, S Mike Reid, TE Treyton Welch, EDGE Tyree Wilson, DL Nathan Shepherd, DT John Ridgeway III, and QB Zach Wilson inactive for Week 7 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Ruiz and Shepard were the only Saints listed as questionable for Week 7. Jeremiah Wright will take his spot at right guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 8 against the Bears.
