https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed reportedly avoided a major injury in the collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone in Week 7, an injury that will claim at least one game from the veteran speedster. There’s not really a ton of fantasy value behind Smith-Njigba in Seattle, although veteran Cooper Kupp could see a target or two trickle his way in Shaheed’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) remained sidelined for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed is now firmly on the wrong side of questionable heading into Monday evening’s game against the Bears. If he was in your third receiver or second FLEX spot in a 14-team league, it is time to start making other plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed received positive news on his knee injury that caused him to leave Sunday’s blowout win over the Chiefs, but there’s a pretty good chance that he’s going to miss at least Week 8’s game against Chicago on Monday. Assuming that’s the case, it will lead to more snaps for Tory Horton both as a receiver and as the primary returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the “early returns are positive” on Rashid Shaheed’s knee injury he suffered in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Macdonald didn’t elaborate on how much time Shaheed could miss, if any, but it doesn’t sound like this is expected to be a long-term injury based on what he had to say on Monday. Shaheed’s impact is largely felt in the punt and kick return game, as he has just 16 receptions for 163 scoreless yards on the season for Seattle. We will update his practice status throughout the week, but Shaheed won’t have any fantasy relevance even if he does suit up next week against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is questionable to return in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed was involved in a collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone on an interception in the waning moments of the first half and did not retake the field out of the break. Tory Horton received the kickoff to begin the second half, after which Shaheed was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury. Expect Cooper Kupp and Horton to see a small bump in opportunity behind Smith-Njigba for the remainder of the game. Shaheed caught 2-of-3 targets for one yard prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks’ sporadic producer will be on the field against the Chiefs this week. Shaheed has been involved as a receiver and as a rusher, scoring touchdowns in consecutive weeks. He offers a low floor, but he makes for a viable FLEX starter this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed will be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 7 game against the Chiefs, barring a setback. Unfortunately, his terribly volatile performances keep him in the boom-bust FLEX tier despite four teams being on bye. For what it’s worth, this could be a fantasy-friendly game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed was heavily involved in the Seahawks’ high-volume passing game in Week 6. He seemingly came out of the week banged-up and will open this week as a limited practice participant. Shaheed competes with Cooper Kupp for the No. 2 pass-catching role on the team but is only a boom-or-bust option for deep leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 5-of-8 targets for 66 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding two yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed’s eight targets were a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in a game the Seahawks could not find any room to run on the ground. He lost a fumble on a fluke play in the second quarter in which he rolled over the tackling defender, only for the defender’s knee to knock the football loose before Shaheed’s rear end touched the playing surface. he would fumble a punt return in the fourth quarter but easily had time to regain control before the ball was in real trouble. Shaheed remains the third option through the air for an offense typically not seeing this level of volume, making him a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option, for the time being. That doesn’t change ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Chiefs in Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards and rushed twice for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: It wasn’t a ton of volume, but it was easily Shaheed’s biggest offensive day of the year. He took a pitch for a touchdown for his first score of 2026. He was once again not involved in the passing game, however, and he didn’t do much as a returner again, as well. Shaheed will be back in action — and should not be in lineups — against the 49ers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) is expected to be active for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: The team has yet to activate Charbonnet from injured reserve but removed him from the injury report Saturday, leaving only the procedural step in the way of his season debut. He likely returns to a limited role as the team manages his reps in his first game since tearing his ACL in 2025. Rookie Jadarian price is also expected to play after being removed from the injury report. He, too, will need to be activated from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to “limited” for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: It’s not particularly concerning — this is probably part of a pre-established practice plan as Charbonnet completes his injury comeback — but Jadarian Price’s Friday return to full practice certainly has our attention. Now even if Charbonnet does manage to make his 2026 debut on Monday evening against the Bears, he could have even more company in Seattle’s crowded backfield. Both backs returning would make all three of Charbonnet, Price and Emanuel Wilson shaky FLEX plays. We will receive official game designations on Saturday afternoon. Until then, hang tight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: It’s obviously a positive development for Charbonnet, who appears to be on track for his season debut against the Bears in Week 8. Fantasy managers just have to keep in mind that the rug was pulled from underneath last week when the Seahawks ruled the tailback out late in the week. Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant, but fantasy managers who want to use a Seattle tailback on Monday night won’t have clarity until Saturday at the earliest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald declined to say whether or not Zach Charbonnet (knee) would play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Macdonald said the team will continue to stick to their plan regarding Charbonnet’s return. The 25-year-old running back was activated from the PUP list last week, only to be ruled out before the weekend as the Seahawks were preparing to face the Chiefs. It’s worth noting that Charbonnet was a full participant in practice last week, so we would assume he will log another full week of practices this week. Should the Seahawks opt to sideline Charbonnet next week, Emanuel Wilson would again assume the role as lead back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks declared RB Zach Charbonnet, QB Drew Lock, LB Drake Thomas, RB Robert Henry Jr., LB Chazz Surratt, LB Connor O’Toole, and G Beau Stevens inactive for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Lock will serve as the emergency quarterback while the team will have to wait another week for the season debut of Zach Charbonnet. The Seahawks look to make up ground in the NFC West following the loss from the 49ers against one of two remaining undefeated teams in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks activated Zach Charbonnet (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet underwent ACL reconstruction after suffering his season-ending knee injury in the Seahawks’ Divisional Round win over the 49ers. He will make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against the Chiefs, facing his former teammate, Kenneth Walker. Charbonnet’s expected workload is unknown, though he could handle enough touches to be FLEX-viable. As long as he stays healthy, Charbonnet should advance to the RB2 ranks in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet was expected to get a full week of practice, so this is no surprise. He is listed as a full participant for the first time since returning to practice and is trending to be activated off the physically unable to perform list ahead of a Week 7 matchup against the Chiefs. With Jadarian Price on injured reserve, he is headed for a sizeable share of the Seahawks’ ambiguous backfield. Charbonnet is in the RB3 ranks if activated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Mike Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a “good chance” to play in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Finally, some good news for both Seahawks fans and fantasy managers, alike, after the Seattle run game has gotten off to a sluggish start to the 2026 season. Charbonnet has been on the physically unable to perform list through the first six weeks of the season but appears likely to make his return to the active roster for a marquee matchup against the Chiefs in a game some would consider a must-win for the suddenly reeling Seahawks. Macdonald added that the veteran back would get a full week of practice this week before any decision was made. Fantasy managers can add Charbonnet from waivers, if available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) will be out for the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet was already expected to miss Week 6, so no surprise here. The Seahawks also ruled out LB Drake Thomas and LB Chazz Surratt. There are no other players with injury designations heading into Seattle’s Thursday showdown against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks removed Jadarian Price (chest) from the injury report Saturday and he is expected to play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: The team has yet to activate him from injured reserve, a procedural move that is expected to come before they take the field in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday Night Football. Zach Charbonnet is also expected to be activated from injured reserve, giving the team their top two backs for the first time this season. No word yet on an expected snap count for either, although Price would seem to be in line to serve as the top option in the backfield considering it will be Charbonnet’s season debut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was upgraded to “full” for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price was upgraded to full while Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to limited. That is probably part of a pre-planned process with Charbonnet, but as of Friday evening, we suppose Price is now technically closer to returning than his veteran backfield mate. As it is, both players now seem more likely than not to suit up, which would make for an extremely chaotic fantasy situation with Emanuel Wilson still in the fold. With the Seahawks playing on Monday evening, we will receive official game designations Saturday afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price gets in the limited session after coach Mike Macdonald said that it was realistic that the tailback could be back Monday night against the Bears in Week 8. Zach Charbonnet was a full participant Thursday, so the Seattle backfield could finally be at full strength — or close to it, anyway — for the stretch. That’s nice for the Seahawks, but creates a lot of confusion from a fantasy perspective.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said it’s “realistic” that Jadarian Price (chest/IR) could return in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: With Zach Charbonnet’s status also in some doubt, Seattle’s backfield situation likely won’t be sorted out until Saturday (or MNF inactives), but if Price is back that’s probably the end of Emmanuel Wilson’s short-term RB2 ride. We’ll keep an eye on the situation. Wilson-reliant managers might want to consider alternative arrangements for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks coach Mike MacDonald said the team would designate Jadarian Price (chest) to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price has missed the minimum four games and being immediately designated to return should have him making his debut sooner rather than later. Of course, with Zach Charbonnet also returning to the fold soon, this could be a split backfield rather than the RB2 zone that Price looked to be opening the year in. Price probably will only reach the FLEX ranks when active until we see what the touch counts look like; perhaps he could have a Blake Corum-ish role if all goes well for the Seahawks offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks placed RB Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated a chest injury during the team’s Wednesday practice and will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to the injury. The backfield will be left in the hands of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani in Week 4 against the Chargers but should get reinforcements in short order with Zach Charbonnet set to resume practicing. Price’s season continues to trend poorly for fantasy managers that invested a mid-round pick in his services this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks rule out Jadarian Price (chest) for Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated his chest injury on Wednesday. That is unfortunate. With Price out of the picture against the Chargers, and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still rehabbing, burly RB Emanuel Wilson and receiving specialist RB George Holani will split backfield reps. Wilson can be started as a volume-based RB2/FLEX while Holani is FLEX-viable in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: It’s possible that this is just a precautionary rest day, but those typically occur on Wednesdays. Price should be viewed as questionable to play in Week 4 against the Chargers. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald favorite, Zach Charbonnet (knee), returned as a limited participant. Backup RB Emanuel Wilson would likely get the start if Price and Charbonnet are both out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks designated Zach Charbonnet (knee) to return from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Charbonnet will return to practice this week. The team now has 21 days to officially activate him from the injured reserve. It’s unclear how much of that window they will use to get him up to full speed. He has to miss at least one more game while on the PUP list. Charbonnet tore his ACL in Seattle’s first playoff game last year. The team talked about his quick recovery throughout the offseason and that will be the case, even if he uses all three weeks of his practice window. Once he returns, Charbonnet will at least take over the roles of George Holani and Emanuel Wilson, who have been splitting the backfield with Jadarian Price so far. He could even work himself into the starting job if Price continues to struggle with fumbles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice ahead of Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price was able to play in Week 3 despite the chest ailment, although he was benched for most of the first half after giving up a second fumble of the season. If Price can’t go, George Holani and Emmanuel Wilson — not necessarily in that order — would be the replacements, and are likely to be involved regardless.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos placed RB RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whoa, that escalated quickly. Harvey reportedly suffered a knee injury in practice this week that initially caused the Broncos to rule him out for Week 8, with the team then making the procedural move of placing him on injured reserve Saturday. Harvey will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he rehabs the injury, leaving rookie Jonah Coleman and veteran J.K. Dobbins to handle primary backfield duties with Tyler Badie also on injured reserve. Coleman warrants weekly FLEX status, at minimum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday with a knee injury before being unable to practice Friday, ultimately ruled out for the team’s divisional clash against the Chiefs. Expect Jonah Coleman to serve as the primary rusher in addition to the possibility he sees his pass game involvement tick up in the absences of both Harvey and Tyler Badie, the latter of whom is on injured reserve. The increase in opportunity is enough to vault Coleman into viable FLEX territory for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday after being limited in practice due to a knee injury, something fantasy managers will want to monitor as the weekend approaches. Either way, Harvey now has two healthy backs to compete with for touches with the return of Jonah Coleman in Week 7, keeping him on the fringes of FLEX consideration entering a difficult matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey caught two passes for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey only ran the ball three times for six yards. Jonah Coleman, who was active for the first time since Week 2, ran nine times and also caught a pair of passes. Harvey’s role took a hit, but he made the most of his limited opportunities with a 52-yard screen in the third quarter. Sean Payton’s play-call schemed half of the Cardinals’ defense out of the play and Harvey blew by the other half on his way to the end zone. Despite the spike week for fantasy managers, Harvey’s declining role will have him tumbling down the running back ranks for Week 8. He will be on the RB3/4 border versus Kansas City next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey rushed six times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding 31 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The fact that the 31 yards through the air led the team in receiving is a comment on the state of an offense that gained only 168 yards of total offense against the defending Super Bowl Champions. Even so, a relentlessly aggressive defense willed the team to victory behind a consistently positive game script, which allowed J.K. Dobbins to handily lead the backfield in opportunities. Harvey remains a matchup-dependent fantasy option best utilized in trailing game environments, which is unlikely to be the case when the Broncos face the struggling Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey picked up seven yards on three carries in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was a non-factor in this one, and a week after his big receiving game, he was held without a catch with just one target. The second-year tailback was clearly the backup to JK Dobbins, and was unable to make the most of his limited opportunities. He’s off the radar for Week 6 versus the Seahawks on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey had seven rushes for 25 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding ten catches for 68 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Playing against a 49ers defense allowing the league’s highest target share to running backs, Harvey led the Broncos in targets and receptions — thanks in part to negative game script that forced Denver to go pass heavy in the second half. It was a nice little PPR cheat code outing for Harvey, who now has 20 receptions in three games this year. JK Dobbins, meanwhile, led the Denver backfield with 11 rushes in Week 4. Harvey could be a PPR flex play next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: RJ Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week 3 and is not on the injury report today, meaning both backs are good to go for Week 4. Dobbins saw 17 carries versus the Rams compared to just two for Harvey, though the latter caught six passes. Dobbins caught one pass. The rushing advantage will keep Dobbins in the RB3 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Chiefs placed CB L’Jarius Sneed (knee) on inured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: That was somewhat unexpected. Sneed missed Wednesday’s practice for personal reasons and was limited Thursday and Friday. He was moved to injured reserve a day later. The Chiefs are now down their top two corners after Mansoor Delane was ruled out for Week 8, creating a much softer matchup for the Broncos on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: The Kansas City Star’s Pete Sweeney reports that Chiefs WR Rashee Rice is participating in warmups and play installations, but is not yet participating in team drills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: The Chiefs are doing the same thing with CB L’Jarius Sneed. There is nothing to be worried about here. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said the team is “just building them up,” which will “take a little bit of time.” Rice is still working on conditioning at this point, but once his cardio is good to go, we should see him practicing fully. He was cleared to practice on July 24th after undergoing an offseason clean-up procedure on his knee. Rice is a WR2 with WR1 upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Chiefs signed CB L’Jarius Sneed, formerly of the Titans, to a one-year, $5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schultz was first to report the reunion between the Chiefs and Sneed. The veteran corner last played for the Chiefs in 2023 and was traded to the Titans in the 2024 offseason. Over the last two seasons, Sneed has struggled with multiple injuries, limiting him to just 12 games. Sneed, 29, will also reunite with defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, which could bode well for him as he returns to a familiar environment and a team he helped lead to two Super Bowl titles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Free agent CB L’Jarius Sneed visited with the Chiefs on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Clearly there was no rush to add him to the roster. It’s the first sniff of NFL interest we’ve seen for the former star cornerback since he was released by the Titans, and unsurprisingly it was with his former employers in Kansas City. We suspect this has a chance of happening at some point this offseason, but the 29-year-old Sneed is likely to sift through options ahead of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the criminal charges against L’Jarius Sneed have been dismissed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Sneed had been “charged with aggravated assault that was reduced by the grand jury to the misdemeanor offense of failure to report the commission of a felony,” according to Schefter. That could clear the way for the mega-bust to sign on with a cornerback-needy team in the coming weeks. Sneed, 29, was released by the Titans in March after signing four-year, $76.4 million deal in 2024 that included $55 million in guaranteed money. He will probably have to settle for a prove-it deal for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans released CB L’Jarius Sneed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Sneed’s contract will go down as one of the worst in recent memory. The 29-year-old corner joined the Titans in 2024 on a four-year, $76.4 million deal that included $55 million in guaranteed money, and appeared in just 12 games during his two seasons with the team. Knee injuries plagued the majority of Sneed’s time with the Titans, but it was a quad injury that landed him on season-ending IR last October. Sneed was one of the top corners in the league during his time with the Chiefs, but his recent string of injuries begs the question of how much is left in the tank at this stage of his career. If he wants to continue playing, he will likely need to do so on a one-year prove-it deal to show he can stay healthy for a full season while still contributing at a high level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans placed CB L’Jarius Sneed on injured reserve with a quad injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: A balky knee has impeded Sneed’s play for much of the year. The 28-year-old perimeter cornerback is currently allowing 17.2 yards per reception, 5.3 more than his prior career-worst average. Adding a quad issue to the mix was only going to make things worse. Sneed will now miss at least four games and will be eligible to return in Week 13. The team’s bye occurs in Week 10. CB Darrell Baker Jr. is listed as his backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans interim head coach Mike McCoy said DT Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) is considered week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed is expected to miss some time with a quad injury. McCoy didn’t rule out Simmons for Week 8, but it doesn’t sound like he is expected to play this week. Simmons has been one of the few bright spots for the Titans this year with 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble through eight games. The Titans’ defense will continue to struggle in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans DC Dennard Wilson said “guys will have to step up” without L’Jarius Sneed (quad) against the Colts in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Sneed left Week 7’s game against the Patriots and was quickly ruled out. This seems to confirm he has little chance to play this week. Frankly, with how poorly Sneed has been playing in his limited snaps, the Titans could probably use those snaps to evaluate younger players. The Sneed contract has been a boondoggle for Tennessee through two years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans declared DL Shy Tuttle, CB Jalyn Armour-Davis, S Kevin Winston, CB Samuel Womack, OL Jackson Slater, OL Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, and DL CJ Ravenell inactive for Week 1 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: La’Jarius Sneed, struggling with a knee issue, will suit up for the Titans for Cam Ward’s first NFL regular season game. Even with Sneed healthy and active, the Titans defense should struggle to stop Bo Nix and the Denver offense. It could be a running theme in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers placed S Derwin James (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Previous reports indicated the team was considering a stint on injured reserve following an aggravation of his hamstring injury, with Saturday’s transaction confirming those suspicions. James will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, as the Chargers look to reverse course on a sinking season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: James reportedly suffered a setback with his hamstring injury, with the team now considering injured reserve. His absence is a big hit to their defense as a primary interior defender against the heavy personnel sets from the Rams, upgrading the matchup for Tyler Higbee and company.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Derwin James (hamstring) is a candidate for injured reserve after suffering a setback.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Brutal. This team cannot catch a break. Losing James makes the center of their defense fairly vulnerable. The Chargers’ stalwart safety plays a do-it-all role. If James lands on injured reserve this week, he will be eligible to return for the Chargers’ Week 12 game against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: That is back-to-back weeks of no James. Donte Jackson (hamstring) was also ruled out. We’re almost through the Chargers blurbs. We think they should just put some people on injured reserve too. Keep reading.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Chargers OG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Derwin James (hamstring) and CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) also remained sidelined. The Chargers take on the division-rival Chiefs this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) also did not practice. Neither player played in Week 5 and both will need at least a limited practice before they can be considered questionable for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Donte Jackson (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Derwin James was also held out because of a hamstring injury. He is considered week-to-week. We don’t anticipate him suiting up on Sunday. A DNP for Jackson puts him on the wrong side of questionable as well. LA’s secondary will be an easy target for Bo Nix as he looks to bounce back from a lackluster Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said S Derwin James (hamstring) is “week to week” but not an injured reserve candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Sounds like we should be counting James out for Week 5’s game against the Broncos, and perhaps Week 6 as well. The safety did not play in Week 4’s loss to the Seahawks, leaving Tarheeb Still as the main slot cornerback with 2026 fourth-rounder Genesis Smith seeing an elevated role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: James sandwiched a Thursday absence with two limited sessions. The veteran safety plays through injuries whenever possible, and the Chargers will need all hands on deck to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James said he will play the rest of the season in a cast after suffering a fractured pinky finger in Week 2’s loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: James will look to play out the Chargers’ final 15 games of the season with a cast. The Chargers are off to an 0-2 start and will be desperate to turn things around in Week 3 against the 2-0 Bills on the road in Buffalo. The veteran safety has totaled 10 tackles and one pass breakup in the first two games of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Chiefs downgraded Mansoor Delane (shoulder) to out for Week 8 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: Delane entered the weekend listed as questionable for the team’s divisional showdown against the Broncos, ultimately downgraded to out on Saturday. His absence could influence Steve Spagnuolo’s ability to utilize man coverage at the hefty rates he has through the first six games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is questionable for Kansas City’s Week 8 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: Delane didn’t practice either of the last two days after popping on to the injury report on Thursday. Andy Reid could only muster a “We’ll see how he does here going forward” when asked about it. We’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: Delane’s absence raises concerns surrounding his potential availability when the Broncos in Week 8. Coming off their first loss of the season, the Chiefs will look to rebound against a divisional opponent after managing only three points against the Seahawks. Delane has been a big part of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s weekly game plan, allowing the team to rank near the top of the league in man coverage rate through the first third of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Chiefs DT Chris Jones (calf) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is also questionable to play this week, though Chiefs coach Andy Reid said earlier this week “there’s a pretty good chance” Delane will suit up in Week 1. Jones remained limited all week. Delane logged two full sessions before downgrading to limited on Friday, which could indicate he suffered a setback. We will find out soon enough.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said “there’s a pretty good chance” Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is in uniform and available for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: Delane left Week 1 with a right shoulder injury and did not return. He underwent X-rays after exiting the game and the results were negative. Reid specifically said he expects Delane to be available, but that doesn’t rule out a reserve role if the team wants to play it safe with the rookie. He is expected to practice today, presumably in a limited capacity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) left Week 1’s win over the Broncos and will have an MRI on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: X-Rays were negative and Delane’s shoulder was stable after he left upon falling down on his interception three snaps in. We saw plenty of L’Jarius Sneed in Week 1’s win over the Broncos, with Kristian Fulton also joining the fold against three-wide sets. The Chiefs are hoping the No. 6 overall pick won’t be sidelined too long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane was seen in a full-contact jersey on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: Sporting a full-contact jersey and shoulder pads for the first time in training camp, Delane appears set to be a full-go for the Chiefs. The first-round rookie had been recovering from a shoulder injury he suffered earlier this offseason and was practicing on a limited basis in camp after avoiding the PUP list. With roughly three weeks to go before the start of the season, Delane appears to be on track to play in Week 1 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) said he is hoping to be fully cleared for camp “some time soon.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: Delane suffered a shoulder injury this offseason at OTAs and was sporting a non-contact jersey at the Chiefs’ first training camp. The No. 6 overall pick in this year’s draft said things are “getting better every day” and has spent most of his time in the playbook and conditioning. The fact he didn’t open camp on the PUP list suggests this is a relatively minor injury for Delane, who is expected to provide an immediate boost to a new-look secondary that last starting corners Trent McDuffie (trade) and Jaylen Watson (free agency) to the Rams this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: The Chiefs signed No. 6 overall pick CB Mansoor Delane to a four-year, $41.9 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: The Chiefs now have both of their 2026 first-rounders under contract after signing DT Peter Woods just hours before announcing Delane’s deal. Delane spent four seasons in college and closed out his career at LSU after transferring from Virginia Tech. He joins a secondary that was dealt two key losses this offseason in Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, and projects as the Chiefs’ top corner to start the season. Last season, Delane earned a PFF coverage grade of 90.7 and allowed just 14 receptions for 165 scoreless yards on 35 targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.headline: Chiefs traded up with the Browns to select LSU CB Mansoor Delane at No. 6 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mansoor-de.analysis: The Chiefs gave up pick No. 74 and 148 to move up. A three-time All-ACC performer at Virginia Tech, Mansoor Delane (6’0/190) put together a sensational 2025 season as LSU’s top cover corner, earning elite PFF marks with a 90.7 overall grade and 91.0 coverage grade to go with a 74.4 run-defense and 76.4 tackling grades. Over 339 coverage snaps, he was targeted only about one in every ten snaps, giving up just 10 completions on 36 attempts for 119 yards with zero touchdowns allowed, recording two interceptions, 11 pass breakups and a microscopic 3.9 QBR. He choked off big plays on the perimeter, allowing only a single completion of 20+ yards, just 3.3 yards per target and 0.35 yards per coverage snap, numbers that sit firmly in shutdown-corner territory. In run support, he added 35 tackles (20 solo) with an 83.3% tackle rate and 13 total havoc plays, showing he was more than just a cover specialist. The consensus All-American is instinctive, fluid and a relentless ball hawk who stands to parlay a standout four-year collegiate career into NFL gridiron success. After trading away Trent McDuffie and letting fellow corner Jaylen Watson walk, the Chiefs had to address this position. Delane will be tasked with CB1 duties right away.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) cleared protocol and will play in Week 8 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Howard gains clearance just in time to be charged with slowing an aggressive Pittsburgh pass rush, likely in line to handle his fair share of T.J. Watt on Sunday. There should be no reason for Howard to see a decline in snaps or performance after suffering a concussion in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) is questionable for Week 8 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Howard returned to the practice field Friday after missing both sessions to start the week, keeping the door open for him to clear concussion protocol in time for Sunday’s game against the Steelers. Howard will need to remain asymptomatic and gain clearance from an independent neurologist to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Elgton Jenkins and Jared Verse practiced Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Both players emerged from their Week 7 win a bit banged up, with their return to practice Thursday a positive development toward an active game-day status. Right tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) remained sidelined, who will have one more opportunity to get on the practice field and remain asymptomatic to have a chance at playing against the Steelers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) is questionable to return in Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Howard left the game in the first half with a head injury and had not returned as of the start of the fourth quarter. Losing Howard would be a tough blow for a Cleveland offensive line that has been solid in both run and pass blocking in 2026. Look for Howard to enter the league’s concussion protocol in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: His Wednesday DNP suggested worse, but Howard will try to play through the knee injury that cost him roughly half of Cleveland’s snaps against the Jets last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: It’s good progress after he had a Wednesday DNP. Howard should have a real chance at playing on Sunday as long as his Friday status stays neutral or trends positively.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: The Browns acquired Howard from Houston in the offseason. Howard left Week 5 with the knee issue and a DNP today suggests he will miss at least one week. Dawand Jones took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and would presumably draw the start at right tackle if Howard is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Browns acquired RT Tytus Howard from the Texans in exchange for a fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: This is the first big move the Browns have made to address their offensive line. The acquisition of Howard gives them an experienced right tackle who has started all 16 games he has appeared in for each of the last two seasons, and he has allowed just five sacks on 1,175 pass blocking snaps per TruMedia. Shortly after trading for Howard, the Browns announced they would be signing him to a three-year, $63 million extension, keeping him with the team through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans G Ed Ingram (knee) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: After missing each of the last two games with a knee injury, Ingram looks likely to go on Thursday night. Ingram has posted back-to-back full practices this week. Tytus Howard (ankle/knee) and Trent Brown (hand/knee) were both limited participants on Monday and Tuesday and also look to be trending towards playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans OL Ed Ingram (knee) is questionable for Houston’s Week 11 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Ingram, one of Nick Caserio’s better OL scrapheap finds this year, missed last week’s game with the injury but had limited practices on Thursday and Friday after a full on Wednesday. Juice Scruggs wound up seeing most of the time at right guard after an ugly debut series from Sidy Sow. Tytus Howard (concussion) cleared protocol and will start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jets placed NT T’Vondre Sweat (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The vaunted Jets run defense takes a major blow as Sweat is moved to injured reserve. Defensive end David Bailey is also doubtful to play in Week 8, boosting the matchup for Ashton Jeanty on Sunday. Sweat will be sidelined for four games, at minimum, as the Jets struggle to cling to another lost season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: T’Vondre Sweat suffered a knee injury in Week 7 against the Dolphins and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sweat went down in the second quarter. He walked off the field under his own power but immediately went into the medical tent. The team ruled him out after halftime. Sweat has 15 combined tackles and two TFLs this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jets acquired DT T’Vondre Sweat from the Titans in exchange for EDGE Jermaine Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As Schefter notes, the deal won’t become official until the new league year, which starts in a few weeks. Johnson was the subject of trade rumors at the deadline last year, but nothing materialized. He now gets a new home in Tennessee. Sweat, a former second-round pick, had a quiet rookie season with one sack and four TFLs. Despite appearing in five fewer games, Sweat upped his sack total to two in 2025. Pro Football Focus also charted him as a markedly improved player. He ranked fourth in run defense grade and top-20 in pass-rush grade among defensive linemen. Sweat has two more years on his rookie contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans activated NT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sweat makes his return to a roster that has allowed the fourth most fantasy points per game to opposing backfields this season. Sweat has continually graded as a top performer against the run throughout this career, making his return a significant boost to a struggling unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans placed NT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans will now be without their big man against the run for the next four games, at minimum. Expect Shy Tuttle to fill in in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans DT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) will not play in Week 3’s game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rejoice, Jonathan Taylor fantasy managers, as Sweat is one of the best young nose tackles in the game. Sweat was a Friday downgrade to not participating, opening up the possibility that he’s had a setback. At the very least, he should be considered extremely questionable for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans OT JC Latham (hip) will not play in Week 2 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Neither will T’Vondre Sweat, who has been sidelined with an ankle injury. Oli Udoh looks to be next in line for snaps at right tackle for Tennessee. It’s a big downgrade for Cam Ward’s protection as the rookie quarterback continues to fight against his supporting cast to produce aesthetically pleasing statistics.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans RB Kalel Mullings (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: That makes two absences for Mullings this week. If the sixth-round rookie cannot suit up for Week 2, that would leave the Titans with just Tony Pollard and Julius Chestnut as the available running backs on the active roster. Pollard totaled 19 touches against the Broncos last week, with Tyjae Spears (ankle) on injured reserve. He is likely to do so again against a slightly softer Rams defense. Titans OT JC Latham (hip) and DT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) were also not seen practicing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans OT JC Latham (hip) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Latham aggravated a preseason hip injury in Week 1 against the Broncos. The 22-year-old tackle played 45 snaps before exiting, with Oli Udoh replacing him at right tackle. Latham’s status for Week 2 and the foreseeable future remains in doubt. Also not practicing for the Titans Wednesday were S Quandre Diggs (hand) and DT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans DT T’Vondre Sweat (eye) left Week 16 against the Colts and returned.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sweat was poked in the eye in the first half of the Titans’ Week 16 matchup against the Colts. He left the game and went to the locker room, but returned to the sideline. Sweat returned late in the second quarter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys activated S P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke spent the previous five weeks on injured reserve with a plantar fascia issue and is expected to be active for the team’s Week 8 game against the Cardinals. He brings a veteran presence to a defense that struggled mightily to start the season as the Cowboys continue inching closer to full health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys placed S P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: The team had already ruled him out for multiple weeks and will now make the administrative move of sending him to injured reserve. He will first be eligible to return for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer said CB Cobie Durant (hamstring) and S P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) will miss “a few weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Durant suffered a hamstring strain and Locke suffered a torn plantar fascia in the team’s Week 2 win over the Commanders. Both players are reportedly going to miss multiple weeks, while a stint on injured reserve is not yet being ruled out for either player. In what has become somewhat of a yearly tradition in Dallas, the secondary is suddenly extremely thin on healthy bodies after the team invested significant capital re-tooling the back end this offseason. Expect Markquese Bell and Shavon Revel to enter the starting lineup for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys agreed to terms with S P.J. Locke, formerly of the Broncos, on a one-year, $5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: After starting all 15 games he appeared in during the 2024 season, Locke made just three starts in 16 games last season, totaling 16 tackles and three pass breakups. The former UDFA became a major contributor for the Broncos in 2023 when he emerged to total 53 tackles, three sacks and five pass. Locke will join former Broncos DB coach Christian Parker in Dallas, and is capable of lining up from multiple spots. Even if he doesn’t earn a “starting” role in Dallas, Locke will likely see plenty of work for the Cowboys next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos S P.J. Locke said he underwent spinal fusion surgery after the team’s playoff loss in January.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke is one of the first NFL players to undergo spinal fusion surgery, sharing his journey in a personal documentary YouTube video. He dealt with the pain from the surgery early on, but says he does not feel pain now. Locke started 15 games and the playoff loss for the Broncos and is a key member of a daunting secondary. The 28-year-old missed offseason workouts due to rehab and is preparing to be ready for the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos declared S P.J. Locke (thumb), QB Zack Wilson, CB Kris Abrams-Draine, T Alex Palczewski, TE Greg Dulcich, LB Dondrea Tillman and DL Eyioma Uwazurike inactive for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke was considered doubtful for the bout against the Panthers, and will unsurprisingly miss the contest. Wilson will operate as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos S Brandon Jones suffered a hamstring strain at training camp on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: The training staff has yet to determine the injury’s severity but the Broncos are already in a tough spot at safety. The front office released four-time second-team All-Pro S Justin Simmons this offseason and both S Caden Sterns (patellar tendon) and S Delarrin Turner-Yell (ACL) are currently on the active/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. P.J. Locke is the only active Broncos safety who logged triple-digit defensive snaps last year, though he worryingly earned a 55.2 PFF coverage grade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos re-signed S P.J. Locke to a two-year, $9 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke played sparingly his first three seasons in the league but became one of the standouts of the defense while filling in for the injured Kareem Jackson in 2023. Locke returns to a secondary now devoid of Justin Simmons after the latter’s release, creating the opportunity for Locke to see a significant bump in playing time in the immediate future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos re-signed QB Brett Rypien, ILB Jonas Griffith, and S P.J. Locke to one-year contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: All three were exclusive rights free agents. Rypien had a four-interception start against the Jets in 2020, but only attempted two passes in 2021 as a backup. He may be in line to be Russell Wilson’s backup in 2022 unless the Broncos sign someone else, as they’ve traded Drew Lock and Teddy Bridgewater is a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: The Athletic’s Dane Brugler projects Texas S P.J. Locke to Round 7 or as an undrafted free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke (5'10/200) entered the draft mix after his senior season, but it’s been a really quiet draft season for the former Longhorn. However, as a senior, Locke racked up an impressive 58 solo tackles with a career-high 5.5 tackles for loss. That level of production is nice to see for a deep sleeper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Raiders are expected to activate WR Jack Bech (forearm) from injured reserve ahead of Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech has been on the shelf since fracturing his arm in Week 3, missing the minimum required four games due to the injury. He returns to a passing offense that has been heavily concentrated amongst Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker, unlikely to be a usable weekly fantasy asset. Fantasy managers can stash the youngster in hopes of a growing role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jack Bech (forearm) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 8 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: He practiced in full all three days. Klint Kubiak was evasive when asked if he would be activated, but players that practice in full three days in a row while trying to come off injured reserve rarely aren’t activated. Bech will be restored to the roster on Saturday if he’s going to play. He doesn’t need to be proactively rostered outside of the deepest leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jack Bech (forearm) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: That’s back-to-back full practices for Bech after the Raiders opened up the 21-day window for the wideout. He’s worth monitoring in redraft leagues in part because the options ahead of him aren’t exactly elite, but fantasy managers don’t need to consider a stash just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders designated Jack Bech (forearm) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: His 21-day practice window will open this week. Bech could, in theory, start eating into Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker’s snap counts. The Raiders are probably pretty happy with how Tucker has played, though, and Nailor is more of a fit as an outside receiver than Bech is. The 2025 second-rounder is worth monitoring but not exactly someone you should be stashing ahead of his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders placed WR Jack Bech (forearm) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Bech had five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown in the first two weeks of the season, but played just 11 snaps in Week 3 before fracturing his forearm. The Raiders signed Cody White — he of the three touchdowns in the last two weeks — to the active roster as his replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders ruled out Jack Bech in Week 3 against the Saints with a forearm injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech reportedly fractured his forearm against the Saints. Bech earned an end zone target on the Raiders’ fourth drive. The pass was overthrown and ruled incomplete, but Bech was hit by a defender late, resulting in a personal foul. The Raiders accepted it, erasing Bech’s target from the box score along the way. He finished the game with zero statistics and will likely miss a few weeks due to injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jach Bech caught both of his targets for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech got in the end zone last week but was still held to three catches for 23 yards. Without a touchdown to his name in Week 2, there wasn’t much fantasy production to be had. Bech is the WR3 on an offense centered around Ashton Jeanty and eventually Brock Bowers. He is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jack Bech caught 3-of-4 for 23 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech scored a 15-yard touchdown, running a post route from the slot, on the Raiders’ first drive, bouncing off contact before running into the end zone. Bech’s day was largely quiet outside of that, although Kirk Cousins overthrew him on another post route, and the ball was picked off by a Dolphins safety. Bech remains a touchdown-dependent FLEX against the Chargers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the team is still trying to find a wide receiver who is “accountable and can help us on Sunday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: He punctuated his point by saying only, “still looking.” Kubiak’s ambiguous phrasing could suggest that the Raiders are seeking a wide receiver via trade, but it can also be read simply as an indictment of players like Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech and Malik Benson. None of the three turned in a great game last night, while Tre Tucker was given the night off. Tucker makes for a boom-bust FLEX option in an underwhelming position group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 22 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Both Nailor and WR Jack Bech played tonight while WR Tre Tucker took the night off. Bech failed to earn a target and played into the fifth drive. Nailor called it a night after the third drive. The Raiders’ top-three wide receivers appear to be Tucker, Nailor and Bech, in that order. Tucker might warrant matchup-based FLEX treatment in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson first popped on the injury report with a missed practice Thursday before maintaining that status to end the week, ultimately unable to play through the ailment while being ruled out Saturday. Rhamondre Stevenson steps into a potential workhorse role against the downtrodden Dolphins, where he will be an upside RB2 in Week 8. Expect the team to elevate another back from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is questionable for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson missed practice Thursday with an illness, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for the team’s Week 8 divisional clash with the Dolphins. That places fantasy managers in a precarious position considering the team plays in the afternoon portion of the Sunday slate. It would be prudent to make alternate plans at FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Illnesses typically don’t hold back NFL players, so we’d be surprised if Henderson missed time, but it is worth noting that it was a Thursday addition to the report. Because of that, if he missed Friday, it wouldn’t be surprising if he was listed as questionable. We’d still expect him to play either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed three times for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 14 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson continues to play second, or third, fiddle behind Rhamondre Stevenson when the Patriots are forced into “gotta have it” mode, with Stevenson the back most trusted in key situations. The Patriots fell into an early hole and were playing catch-up throughout against the Bears, something that could help to explain the lowly opportunity total for the back widely considered the more explosive of the two. Furthermore, the team continued to rotate Corey Kiner through the opportunity pecking order, placing another sizable dent in the weekly floor of Henderson. Although he could find more opportunities in a softer matchup in Week 8, he’ll be a difficult click to insert into fantasy lineups against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson will be active for the Patriots’ Thursday Night Football game, but his usage is up in the air. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel got RB Corey Kiner going late last week after Henderson fumbled. The Patriots won’t simply discard their former second-round pick, so he remains FLEX-viable, but he may be playing with a very limited touch count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It’s been a stunningly quick recovery from what looked to be a high-ankle sprain that could sideline him. Henderson has practiced in full both days this week. We’re not concerned that he won’t play, but after fumble problems struck last week and Corey Kiner closed out the Jets in the fourth quarter, we do have slightly lowered expectations for his Thursday night stat line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed seven times for 31 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, adding a nine-yard reception and losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Surprisingly active, Henderson was unsurprisingly disappointing. Although his lost third quarter fumble was his first of the season, it predictably landed him in the doghouse. He touched the ball just two times thereafter, and the Patriots decided to ride No. 3 running back Corey Kiner is closeout mode. Kiner took 11 carries in the final 16:30 of game time. We know Henderson has big-play ability, but now playing at less than 100 percent in a backfield that is beginning to look like a three-man ordeal, he’s not a particularly appealing RB3/FLEX heading into Thursday’s short-week date with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: As are A.J. Brown (ankle) and LT Will Campbell (knee). It’s a rare day where all the injury news went right for a team. We can’t imagine Henderson will be in large for a particularly big backup role behind Rhamondre Stevenson, but the fact that a player the Pats didn’t even really “need” for Week 6 is giving it a go suggests he is close to regular health. Henderson is a boom/bust FLEX option. Inactive for the Patriots are CB Carlton Davis, CB Karon Prunty, QB Behren Morton, CB Channing Canada, OT Dametrious Crownover and TE Tanner Arkin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is likely to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: The same is true of left tackle Will Campbell, who also went down with an ankle injury in Week 5. It’s a remarkable turnaround for Henderson, who was initially expected to miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable on Friday. We expect Henderson to be on a pitch count this week, but he’s still capable of breaking a long run on just a few touches. Henderson is a high-risk FLEX play for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: The Patriots’ No. 2 running back was limited all week after being diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain. He told reporters today that he was surprised he could practice this week, and is feeling “pretty good.” If active, he will be a FLEX starter, but Rhamondre Stevenson should lead the backfield in touches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This was always thought to be the case after Brown missed Thursday and Friday with a “flare up” of an existing knee injury, the same issue that ultimately saw the Rams back out of trade negotiations this offseason. Brown’s absence comes at a horrible time for a team already without Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs, leaving only DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Fantasy managers in a bind could consider taking a shot on upside through Williams’ downfield role against a Dolphins team bleeding explosive passing through the first seven weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said A.J. Brown (knee) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This feels like a very optimistic questionable after Brown missed the last two practices of the week with a new knee tweak. Brown-reliant managers should be making contingency plans ready for Sunday. “We’ll see when he comes in tomorrow, and we’ll make a decision,” Vrabel said.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown has now missed back-to-back practices and is at serious risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Dolphins. Brown’s knee injury was reported as a “flare-up” from a previous knee injury, which is never a good sign for a player. Brown has been dealing with injuries like this for a few years but has always found a way to play through them. While it’s possible he ends up doing so again this week, fantasy managers should begin considering other options in the event he is held out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: The downgrade in participation raises serious questions surrounding his potential availability when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Brown had been mostly limited in practice since being activated from injured reserve due to a separate ankle issue, with the absence Thursday marking the first fully missed practice in that window. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status Friday as they make plans for their weekend ahead. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported Thursday that the veteran receiver’s absence is due to a “flare up” of a previous knee injury, placing his status for Sunday in doubt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Setting Brown’s drops aside, Brown still looked like he was working his way back from his high-ankle sprain last week against the Bears. He was laboring through his routes at times, particularly downfield. Targets should continue flowing his way, but Brown is perhaps best viewed as a volume-driven WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown has not yet clicked with his new team after going down with injury in Week 1 and spending the subsequent four games on injured reserve. He committed yet another drop against the Bears after three drops the week prior, this time on what would have been a long gain down the left sideline. Brown’s burst off the line and at the top of routes appears to remain hampered, something both the Patriots and Brown’s fantasy managers hope will remedy in short order. You can’t really sit Brown at this point, but fantasy managers have to be growing impatient of their first or second-round selection. Brown remains a teeth-gritting start ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown practiced in full on Friday. It is his first time doing so since returning from injured reserve last week. This is great news for his Week 7 outlook. The Bears field a beatable pass defense, setting up Brown for a bounce-back performance after last week’s disappointing showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown spoke with the media today and there’s no reason to believe he’ll actually miss this game, but he was regarded as “limited” in both sessions this week and it’s fair to wonder if he’s 100 percent just yet after his drop-filled, rough Week 6. He’s best-treated as a WR2 this week — you’re still probably starting him regardless of what the ranking is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-10 targets for 27 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 1, Brown had an even more disastrous outing than that inefficient box score would indicate, as he was charged with at least three official drops and could end up with 4-5 when it is all said and done. One was a potential long score where the ball literally went through his hands. It was unbecoming of a highly-paid No. 1 wideout. Brown also looked stiff moving side to side, and might not be particularly close to 100 percent health returning from his high-ankle sprain. We assume things can only get better from here, but they absolutely have to in Thursday evening’s short-week potential shootout with the Bears’ leaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: As are A.J. Brown (ankle) and LT Will Campbell (knee). It’s a rare day where all the injury news went right for a team. We can’t imagine Henderson will be in large for a particularly big backup role behind Rhamondre Stevenson, but the fact that a player the Pats didn’t even really “need” for Week 6 is giving it a go suggests he is close to regular health. Henderson is a boom/bust FLEX option. Inactive for the Patriots are CB Carlton Davis, CB Karon Prunty, QB Behren Morton, CB Channing Canada, OT Dametrious Crownover and TE Tanner Arkin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) is out for Week 8 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: No surprise here as Monangai hasn’t practiced since Week 4. He’s set to miss his fourth consecutive game against the Seahawks in Week 8. Roschon Johnson figures to continue to serve as the Bears’ RB2 with Monangai sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: We’d be floored if Monangai got on the questionable line on Saturday. He hasn’t played or practiced since Week 4. We’re still waiting for some kind of positive movement here. Roschon Johnson will likely be Chicago’s second-string back again in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai has yet to practice after sustaining thumb and toe injuries in Week 4, with the potential that he misses his fourth consecutive game a very real possibility. The Bears held a walkthrough Thursday ahead of a Monday Night Football showdown against the Seahawks, meaning Monangai will have two more opportunities to get on the practice field ahead of Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best making alternate arrangements considering the timing of the team’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was not spotted at Chicago’s Tuesday practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: The Bears elected to have a practice Tuesday, as they prepare for a MNF matchup with the Seahawks, so they won’t have an injury report until Thursday. This isn’t exactly a strong sign that Monangai won’t make it back this week, but it also isn’t good news for managers that would like to see him active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears declared Kyle Monangai, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Jack Sanborn, OL Jordan McFadden, DT Jayden Loving, CB Nick McCloud and QB Case Keenum inactive for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: D’Andre Swift will serve as the team’s top back, while Roschon Johnson rotates in behind him. Johnson’s Week 6 fumble could result in less playing time. The Bears face the Seahawks in Week 8. Monangai was unable to practice all week. Hopefully, he returns next week and can be on the field on game day. Keenum will serve as the emergency third quarterback today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai will miss his third game in a row this week. Exactly two weeks ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury would be an issue for 1-2 weeks. Technically, his statement remains accurate. This week’s Thursday Night Football game complicates things. If the Bears thought Monangai would miss four games, they likely would have put him on injured reserve, so he should, theoretically, be able to play in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Of course, nothing is guaranteed, and for those wondering, the Bears go on bye in Week 10. D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson have been splitting touches with Monangai sidelined. We do not yet know if Johnson will be punished for last week’s fumble though.
