https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: He hasn’t practiced yet this week and appears very unlikely to go on Thursday night. It would seem to be trending towards another week with Roschon Johnson as the backup runner for the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Exactly one week ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury jeopardized his availability over the next 1-2 weeks. Unfortunately, he is on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Roschon Johnson could contribute on passing downs if Monangai cannot play, but D’Andre Swift will handle the majority of the backfield touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai missed Week 5 due to thumb and toe injuries; he did not practice all of last week and was estimated as a non-participant for the Bears’ Wednesday walk-through. A DNP listing after already missing a week is not a good sign for the 24-year-old’s availability. Starter D’Andre Swift (hip) was notably not on the injury report. Monangai will need to practice to have a chance to play but fantasy managers will need to start looking at backup Roschon Johnson as a potential fill-in for Week 6 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne suffered the injury during Friday’s practice. A previous report from Ian Rapport stated the 29-year-old defensive tackle suffered a significant foot injury and would be out for the foreseeable future. Payne will be placed on injured reserve as he’s set to miss the rest of the season. He recorded a sack, a forced fumble and 14 tackles in six games with the Commanders this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Daron Payne suffered a “significant foot injury” in practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Rapoport adds that the injury is likely to sideline the standout defensive tackle “for the foreseeable future,” with a stint on injured reserve appearing likely. The Commanders continue to be dealt significant injuries, this time on the defensive side of the ball, as they fight to remain in contention in a fragile NFC East division. The team will know more about the extent of the injury when Payne undergoes further testing Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders EDGE Odafe Oweh (calf) will play in Week 1 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: The Commanders will also have Daron Payne (knee) and K’Lavon Chaisson (knee) on the field for Sunday when they travel to Philly to take on the Eagles. Washington made several defensive additions this offseason in hopes of improving a unit that ranked among the league’s worst last season in its second year under Dan Quinn.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. (illness) is inactive for Week 17 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Rodriguez was a late add to the injury report with an illness and is now officially inactive for the Commanders’ Christmas afternoon game against the Cowboys. Jacory Croskey-Merrit is an RB3 with Rodriguez out. The Commanders also declared QB Jayden Daniels, QB Marcus Mariota, QB Sam Hartman, LT Laremy Tunsil, LB Nick Bellore, and DT Daron Payne out against the Cowboys. Payne did not practice all week with a back issue. Jeff Driskel is Josh Johnson’s backup while Sam Hartman is the emergency third quarterback for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne has been suspended for one game after punching Amon-Ra St. Brown in Week 10’s loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne could appeal this, but the tape doesn’t exactly work in his favor. Payne took a blatant, cheap shot at St. Brown during the second quarter of Sunday’s game and was immediately ejected for his actions. Assuming this holds up, which it should, Payne will miss Week 11’s game against the Dolphins in Spain and will be eligible to return in Week 13 after the Commanders’ bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne was ejected from Week 10 against the Lions after committing an unnecessary roughness penalty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne was flagged after a hard-fought 13-yard touchdown run made by Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. Payne can be clearly seen punching Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown on the left side of his facemask. Astonishingly, Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw was not ejected after striking a referee in the forehead, though he was penalized, after Payne was ejected. The Commanders also may have lost CB Trey Amos, who entered the game with a hip injury, and required two trainers’ assistance to leave the field after injuring his ankle on the play. Amos is currently questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders ruled out DT Daron Payne (knee/finger) for the NFC Championship game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne came into the weekend listed as questionable but will ultimately miss the team’s NFC Championship game against the Eagles. The Commanders have struggled mightily against the run and will now be without one of their top run defenders on the interior of their defensive line. That could spell trouble against Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts after the two ran wild in both of these teams’ previous meetings this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne (knee/finger) is questionable for the NFC Championship Game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Linebacker Bobby Wagner was removed from the report and will play. Payne did not practice at all this week, putting him on the wrong side of questionable heading into the weekend. However, with a Super Bowl berth on the line, he will be doing everything in his power to get on the field. Payne has four sacks and five TFLs this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Daron Payne (knee/finger) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne suffered his finger injury in the team’s wild card win over the Buccaneers. He was limited in two of three practices last week but appears to have picked up a knee injury in the divisional round win over the Lions. Back-to-back DNPs to open the week is a concerning sign for Payne’s availability, but the team could be exercising caution for their star tackle. We’ll see where things stand come Friday when the Commanders release their final injury report before the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne is questionable to return to the wild card game against the Bucs with a finger injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: This is a big blow for the Commanders. The 320-pound defensive tackle has 42 tackles, four sacks, and five tackles for a loss on the season while soaking up attention from blockers in the middle of the defensive line. Payne injured his finger early in the second quarter of the game and seemed to be in immense pain on the sideline. It would be a huge boost for the Tampa Bay running game if Payne can’t come back in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NBC 26 Northeast Wisconsin reports “newly released records show additional women contacted the Hobart/Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Josh Jacobs.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: The Wisconsin television station received “heavily redacted” police reports on Friday evening, though they included allegations from three other women. There are multiple extremely disturbing allegations of physical violence. One alleged incident took place in January 2022. The accuser “contacted investigators in June after learning about the May investigation, telling police the allegations sounded similar to her prior experience with Jacobs.” She also said the incident had “never been reported to law enforcement, (and that she) contacted police when she believed her alleged experience with Jacobs could be relevant to the case.” The allegations highlight the folly of the NFL’s apparent wish that the situation would just go away. It has not, and now it is quite possible, if not likely, that Jacobs ends up suspended for the remainder of the 2026 season. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs rushed 21 times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers, adding six catches for 13 yards and another score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs’ fantasy game was salvaged with two scores, but the tailback didn’t look particularly spry in the process. He had a long gain of just six, and there was almost no burst even against the porous Panthers’ run defense. He was involved in the passing game, but again, outside of his four-yard receiving score, there really wasn’t much there. It’s clear this is Jacobs’ backfield despite the scuffles, as MarShawn Lloyd had just three touches in the contest for seven yards. He’s a volatile low-end RB1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs rushed 11 times for 36 yards in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions, adding five receptions for 55 additional yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs saw 18 opportunities come his way in his return from the Commissioner’s Exempt List. He played on 35 offensive snaps compared to MarShawn Lloyd’s 22, but did little to solve the Packers’ woes in the run game. Jacobs managed a forgettable 36 yards on the ground on 11 carries, but was solid in the passing game. His biggest play came in the third quarter when he turned a short pass from Jordan Love upfield for a 25-yard touchdown, tightroping along the sidelines as he attempted to stay in bounds and reach the end zone. Head coach Matt LaFleur suggested Jacobs would be “limited” to about 30 plays in his first game of the season, but his 35 snaps are on par with the 36.8 snaps per game he averaged last season. We would certainly expect him to handle more of the rushing work in the weeks ahead, but this felt like a fairly normal day for Jacobs. He will be a fringe RB1/RB2 play next week against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Josh Jacobs is expected to get “a normal allotment of reps for a starter” in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Packers OC Adam Stenavich told reporters Jacobs looked “great” in practice earlier this week, so we’re going to assume he’s in football shape and ready to go for Week 7. Given Garafolo’s reporting, Jacobs is already back on the RB1/2 border for a potential shootout with Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs is on track to play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: LaFleur said Jacobs’ Week 7 status depends on how he gets through Friday’s practice. The 28-year-old back has looked “great” in practice this week, per an earlier quote from OC Adam Stenavich, and seems to be trending toward a return after a six-week stay on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. At this point, we would be surprised if Jacobs didn’t play this week against the Lions, but it’s too early to assume he will see his normal workload in his first game back. Even if he doesn’t get a full assortment of touches, we would still expect Jacobs to get enough work to justify starting him at RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers OC Adam Stenavich said Josh Jacobs “will help for sure” and that he “looks great.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Matt LaFleur did not publicly commit to playing Jacobs ahead of Week 7’s date with the Lions, but his offensive coordinator — who also said he’d “provide a spark for our offense” — seemed to let the cat out of the bag that Jacobs will be involved in some way. Whether that’s a start or as part of a committee remains in some limbo, but we’d be surprised if Jacobs wasn’t involved in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he is undecided on whether or not Josh Jacobs will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: LaFleur said Jacobs will log a full week of practice but also pointed out that the 28-year-old back has “missed the exposure to football” over the last several months while on the commissioner’s exempt list. Jacobs was reinstated by the league late last week and is eligible to play immediately, but whether or not he will be active next week is to be determined. We’ll see how this week unfolds, but it would be a bit surprising if Jacobs was inactive in a pivotal NFC North matcup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the NFL “could step back in and create a longer suspension” for Josh Jacobs if the video showing his altercation with a woman is released.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Fowler is surprisingly saying the quiet part out loud here, though this has been the general consensus for fans and analysts for a while. Jacobs is scheduled to come off the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The NFL is reportedly trying to get hold of the video, and Jacobs has sued to block its release. Fowler adds that the woman’s attorney said her client has not participated in the league’s investigation due to privacy concerns. If the video stays under wraps, Jacobs could be allowed to continue playing in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Josh Jacobs is being removed from the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: According to Schefter, “the investigation will remain open for the NFL, so it reserves the right to add further discipline if and when warranted.” Yesterday, ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reported that the league is trying to get ahold of the video showing Jacobs’ altercation with a woman at his home. Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Week 7 against the Lions. The situation clearly remains in flux, but Jacobs can be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports that Josh Jacobs “has filed a civil suit seeking a permanent injunction restricting access to records from his May 23 altercation with a woman at his home.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Demovsky notes that the NFL is trying to get the video of the altercation as part of its investigation. Jacobs is trying to prevent anyone from seeing it, citing everything from protecting the woman’s anonymity to future burglary prevention. We have no idea how this will play out, but Demovsky reported in late September that Judge Marc Hammer “denied the request by the victim in the Josh Jacobs case to have the records permanently sealed.” Jacobs is appealing this ruling. It is unclear when or if Jacobs will play in the NFL again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Micah Parsons (knee) is expected to practice next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: If Parsons returns to practice next week, the Packers will have a 21-day window where he can practice before activating him to the 53-man roster. Pelissero also reported that Parsons’ most likely return date is in Week 11 against the Rams. Including the playoffs, Green Bay is 5-8 since Parsons tore his ACL last December.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “there’s a chance” Micah Parsons (knee) practices next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: When asked about Parsons’ chances of practicing next week, LaFleur said, “I sure hope so.” He followed that up with, “I’m saying there’s a chance.” Parsons opened the season on the PUP list after an ACL tear late last season. The Packers have a Thursday game for Week 8, leading to a mini-bye where Parsons’ door to practice is at least cracked open.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) still isn’t practicing.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: The Packers play the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football on NBC and Peacock in Week 6, but Parsons still isn’t practicing. According to Pelissero, it’s unlikely the 27-year-old defensive end plays before Green Bay’s matchup with the Patriots in Week 9 at the earliest. The Packers’ defense has certainly struggled without Parsons, but they have enough offensive firepower to win shootouts, which only adds to the fantasy floor for Jordan Love and Green Bay’s skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) isn’t expected to practice next week and could return in November, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is coming back from tearing his ACL late last season. The 27-year-old defensive end didn’t practice this week and isn’t expected to practice next week, according to Pelissero. Parsons hasn’t had any setbacks in his rehab, but still isn’t ready for the Packers to open the 21-day window for him to practice before he’s activated. Pelissero points out that it could be November before Parsons is ready for game action. Green Bay is 1-2 this year and 1-8 without Parsons in the lineup over the last two years (including playoffs).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers HC Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons (knee) will not practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is nearing a return, but the star pass-rusher isn’t ready to get on the field just yet. LaFleur did say that Parsons has not suffered any setbacks in his recovery, while adding that this is “just part of the process.” Parsons’ return window can be opened at any time, which would then give the Packers a 21-day window to ramp him up before activating him from IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers placed Micah Parsons (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: This move was expected. Parsons himself said a few weeks ago that a Week 6 return was his “most optimistic” timeline. A spot on the reserve PUP list means Parsons must miss at least the first four months of the season. He is still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in Week 15 of the 2025 season. Parsons should still be a force on the defensive front when he’s back, but that won’t happen until at least October.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons said Week 6 is his “most optimistic” return date as of right now.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Interestingly, Week 6 is when the Packers play host to the Cowboys, Parsons’ former team. The star pass-rusher did note that he could also return later and that there is always the possibility of setbacks, but it sounds like the earliest we should expect to see him is Week 6. Parsons opened camp on the PUP list, which didn’t come as a surprise given the timing of his injury last season. It’s been widely believed that Parsons would miss the first few games of the season. If he were to open the year on the PUP list, he would be forced to sit out at least the first four games of the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers placed EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) on the active/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is unlikely to return before Week 4, the question ahead of us appears to be if it’ll be Week 4 or Week 5. If it’s Week 5, Parsons can be stored on the reserve/PUP list ahead of the season. This timeline has been a consistent drum beat coming out of the Packers since March, so this placement comes as no surprise.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman considers it unlikely Micah Parsons (knee) returns before Week 4.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: The Packers are famously conservative when it comes to injury recoveries, and Schneidman reports they have a hard and fast rule of “nine months without any football activity for players rehabbing major injuries.” We still wouldn’t be stunned if Parsons is a player who ends up breaking that supposed “rule,” but it would not be the first time fans were frustrated by the slow pace of a Packers rehabilitation. For his part, Parsons reported to training camp with a sunny social media post. If he is indeed going to miss regular season time, the first month feels like a good over/under.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons confirmed that he is likely to start the 2026 season on the Physically Unable to Perform List.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: “The goal for me is to complete the season,” Parsons said Wednesday. “The goal has always been playoffs.” Parsons added that the team has a strict nine-month policy for ACL rehab for players with more than one tear and that he had an associated meniscus procedure in December. The updated timeline places Parsons back to full football activities some time in September, likely looking at October before he returns to the field for the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts haven’t discussed benching QB Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones received a vote of confidence from Colts HC Shane Steichen earlier this week and now there’s a report from prominent NFL Insider Pelissero that the organization hasn’t discussed benching him. While that’s all well and good, the Colts still seem like they’re in the early stages of a process that will likely end with benching Jones at some point this year. The fact that Pelissero mentioned Jones’ contract includes a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 is an ominous sign. Once the 2-5 Colts are officially eliminated from playoff contention, Indianapolis won’t have much incentive to risk injury with the oft-injured Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said he has not thought about a change at quarterback and he has “a ton of faith” in Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Always a good sign for the quarterback when the coach has to defend his plan to keep starting said quarterback in back-to-back postgame availabilities. While we empathize with the Indianapolis media that clearly has seen enough of Jones, we’re not sure what exactly they think will go differently with Anthony Richardson — who spent his press availability on Sunday noting that he doesn’t “really regret a lot of things I do” after a citation for marijuana possession — under center. Richardson’s in the final year of his rookie contract. The Colts remain a mess after firing Chris Ballard. Jones probably won’t play this poorly next week against a non-Vikings defense, but it’s hard to deny that he’s playing poorly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 13-of-22 passes for 108 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 16-10, Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding four carries for 13 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The Colts passing game struggled to get going against an elite Vikings defense. Jones crossed 100 passing yards on the Colts’ last possession of the game, finishing the drive off with a game-ending interception. He nearly threw a first quarter interception just off Vikings LB Blake Cashman’s hands and threw the ball into danger several other times. Jones was sacked four times and was ineffective as a runner against the Vikings’ pressure-inducing front-seven. Out of the Colts’ first 35 offensive plays, 16 had gone for zero or negative yardage. It was ultimately a poor passing day against a tough defense for Jones and the Colts. Jones is in the fantasy QB2 ranks against another tough defense in the Jaguars for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Daniel Jones will remain the team’s starting quarterback against the Vikings in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones has yet to crack 270 yards or throw multiple touchdowns in a start. He’s also thrown six interceptions and is completing a career-worst 59.6 percent of his passes. It is not an uncommon observation to say that he is struggling to drive the ball on his throws. While the Colts are not going away from Jones now, that does not necessarily mean he will remain the starter all year if he continues to play like this. Given what the Vikings have been up to this year, we’d be surprised if Jones escaped the bottom five of quarterback fantasy points this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-42 passes for 269 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Colts’ 26-20, Week 6 loss to the Titans, adding three carries for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: This one is going to leave a mark. The Colts led 13-0 at halftime but couldn’t get anything going after the break, where they committed two turnovers and Jones provided just 116 yards passing. His third quarter pick came only moments after a lost Jonathan Taylor fumble. It went right to Titans corner Cor’Dale Flott. Jones was not helped by some shaky hands from default No. 1 receiver Josh Downs, but he simply was not standing and delivering. Jones is really struggling to drive the ball this season, and he’s contributing far less than usual with his legs. In other words, he looks like a 29-year-old coming off a torn achilles’ tendon. There is little reason to expect things to get better in the near term, very much including Week 7 against Brian Flores’ ferocious Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: A full practice today means Jones will play through the issue in Week 6, but it’s never a good sign to see a starting quarterback unexpectedly pop up on the injury report. Jones has also struggled mightily this year, so the last thing he needs is a lingering ankle issue, even if it’s a minor one. Needless to say, we aren’t itching to get Jones in our fantasy lineups in a low-scoring affair with the Titans. He is buried at the back of the QB2 ranks for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 24-of-44 passes for 267 yards in the Colts’ 34-22, Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The 267 yards aren’t a terrible total for Jones, but the Colts’ offense was not effective for most of the game. They were stuffed inside the Steelers’ three-yard line at least four times during the game, and the only touchdown they scored was on a one-yard sneak to tight end Tyler Warren. Even on that play, Warren was stuffed short of the end zone and had to be pushed in from behind. Jones was unable to connect with any receivers down the field and overthrew a few deep shots on the day. The Steelers spent a lot of energy trying to corral Jonathan Taylor, and you’d assume other defenses will deploy the same strategy, which means Jones is going to need to start to make them pay. Things should get easier next week against the winless Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 19-of-34 passes for 143 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 30-13, Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones was disastrously inaccurate in the first half, making even routine catches absurdly difficult for his banged-up receiver room. He also began the game by losing the football after his left tackle was pushed into him, resulting in a fumble. He eventually got the grain on the tracks with back-to-back scoring drives to close the first half. Daniels settled in after the break, though the Colts mostly leaned on Jonathan Taylor, who scored twice, to salt away the game. Jones is averaging a dismal 188.5 yards per game with just three scores to his name. He is barely in the QB2 mix for Indy’s Week 5 game versus the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 24-of-36 passes for 235 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Indianapolis’ 19-17, Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: He added three fumbles, two of which were recovered by the Texans on Will Anderson Jr. strip sacks. It wasn’t pretty, and expectations should be held in check for the Colts passing game given the lack of relevant options, but Jones held on to help snap Indianapolis’ nine-game losing streak dating back to last season. His most impressive play was probably a middle-of-field ball to Laquon Treadwell that put the Colts in field-goal range for Spencer Shrader’s go-ahead kick with less than 30 seconds remaining. The Colts have a better matchup next week against the Commanders, but Jones would be tough to trust as more than a bottom-rung superflex QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-31 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Colts’ 33-30, Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, adding 10 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones lost one of his top receivers at the end of the first quarter when Alec Pierce departed with a heel injury. He was largely unable to attack downfield following Pierce’s departure. That would all change on the team’s lone possession of overtime when Jones hit Laquon Treadwell for a 48-yard shot on the first play following a Chiefs field goal, but the team would be unable to punch their ticket to a win while settling for a field goal of their own. The team could be forced to play possession ball moving forward considering the short-area nature of the remaining pass-catchers, pending the status of Pierce. That spells trouble against the vaunted Houston defense in Week 3, where Jones will be a fringe QB2 while potentially down his field-stretching option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports Giants HC John Harbaugh called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about trading for DT Jeffery Simmons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: With Giants GM Joe Schoen stonewalled, Harbaugh broke with traditional NFL trade-talk norms and called the Titans owner himself. Unfortunately for the Giants, the message was the same, that Simmons was off limits in trade talks. Previous reporting from Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer stated that Bears GM Ryan Poles’ long-standing relationship with Titans GM Mike Borgonzi played a huge role in Simmons ending up in Chicago. Poles and Borgonzi first met in 2007 when Poles was a guard at Boston College and Borgonzi was a recruiting assistant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: Connor Hughes reports Giants head coach John Harbaugh is expected “to be aggressive in targeting ex-Ravens in free agency.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: After coaching the Ravens for 18 years, it’s no surprise Harbaugh would try to get the band back together in New York. That could include C Tyler Linderbaum, who played under Harbaugh in Baltimore from 2022 to 2025. Linderbaum, 26, is an unrestricted free agent this offseason and a potential upgrade for a Giants offensive line that struggled throughout 2025. Harbaugh could also pursue Patrick Ricard and Isaiah Likely in free agency. Harbaugh could also bring in coaches he had during his time in Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Ian O’Connor reports that John Harbaugh “needed it in writing that he would report to John Mara, and not to [GM Joe] Schoen.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: “This wasn’t about Schoen; the coach definitely feels he can work with the GM. Harbaugh wanted the ability to impact the entire operation, from security to training to analytics to media relations to staff size to assistant salaries to relocation expenses to you name it. And yes, in the unlikely event there’s a stalemate on draft day between Harbaugh and Schoen, there’s no longer any question who will prevail,” O’Connor writes. Well then. Joe Schoen begins the Harbaugh Era as a convenient scapegoat the second it takes more than a year to get things going in the right direction. What could go wrong for him?

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: Giants signed former Ravens HC John Harbaugh to a five-year contract to be their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: And... it’s done. After numerous delays amidst contract minutiae, the two sides have agreed on a five-year contract to make Harbaugh the team’s next head coach. The former Ravens head coach was one of the longest tenured head coaches in the league before being fired last week, quickly landing on his feet with one of the more desirable head coaching vacancies in the league. He’ll be tasked with turning around a franchise that has had little success in the post-Eli era.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan speculates the holdup with John Harbaugh’s five-year contract to be the Giants next head coach involves the organization’s chain of command.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Duggan reports that while Harbaugh coached the Ravens for 18 seasons, the 63-year-old head coach reported directly to owner Steve Biscotti and not the general manager. While that has not been the Giants’ chain of command historically, it appears Harbaugh prefers that same setup rather than reporting to Giants GM Joe Schoen. Harbaugh is the first major domino to fall in this offseason’s coaching carousel, which gives the Giants some options if this deal were to fall through, though that’s not seen as likely at this point. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the negotiations are heading in the right direction, according to a source, and the Giants hope to introduce Harbaugh at a press conference on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Giants are still expected to sign former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh to a five-year contract to be their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Over the last few hours, multiple reports have indicated that the two sides are still expected to come to an agreement. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said it “seems like something was lost in translation” during early negotiations, specifically regarding the “reporting structure” and decision-making powers. He adds that the Titans are still “interested and waiting” to find out what happens, while noting that former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski could be “the one” for the Giants if things fall through with Harbaugh.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Giants are finalizing a five-year contract with John Harbaugh to be their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Per Rapoport, the Giants will spend the morning hammering out the details, but Harbaugh has accepted the job. We should get confirmation on the deal later today. He will become one of the league’s highest-paid coaches once the ink is dry. Things have been moving in this direction for a while. Harbaugh visited the Giants’ facility yesterday, met with the New York brass, and even talked with Jaxson Dart in person. There were reports that he would meet with the Titans today, but those plans have likely been called off. The Giants have won more than eight games just twice in the past 13 seasons. Harbaugh, on the other hand, never won fewer than eight games during his 18-year run as the team’s head coach. He will bring an unmatched floor and cultural shift to the organization. The question now will be what kind of ceiling he can achieve. That was ultimately his issue at the end of his Baltimore days, and it will be the determining factor in whether or not his Giants tenure is a success.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Giants are expected to hire John Harbaugh as their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: That’s “barring setbacks.” Things have been trending this way for the past few days, though the Titans and Falcons were still hoping to make a race of it. The Giants have the quarterback and the seeming pure desperation to put them over the top in the fight for Harbaugh’s services. We would expect official word to arrive some time on Thursday, likely early in the day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Dianna Russini reports the Titans interview former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh on Thursday for their head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: The Giants reportedly made a “massive push” to get Harbaugh to sign with them today. Of note, Harbaugh met with the Giants at their facility, toured the grounds, and even met with Jaxson Dart today. The Titans, on the other hand, are meeting him at his home. While it does seem like the Giants are in pole position to land the cycle’s hottest name, Harbaugh is still going to talk to the Titans. He will likely meet with Atlanta before making a decision as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports the Giants are making a “massive push” to sign John Harbaugh for their head coaching vacancy today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Harbaugh is currently in New York, meeting with Giants ownership, and they clearly don’t want him walking out of the building without a deal. Per Hughes, “They’re willing to not only pay him, but also whatever his staff wants.” A blank check plus a roster with the quarterback position already figuired out will be hard to turn down. Harbaugh, however, is also being pursued by the Titans and Falcons. Neither job looks as enticing on paper, but it would make sense for him to hear them out, even if that is just to drive up his asking price for the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports WR Garrett Wilson won’t be traded.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson told reporters this week that he hasn’t requested a trade. Now Schefter reports, citing a “well-placed” source, that there’s “no way” the Jets will trade the 26-year-old wide receiver before the trade deadline. Wilson was held to two catches and 26 yards in Week 7, but remains in the WR2 mix heading into Week 8’s matchup against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson told reporters he has not requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson said he loves it in New York. He then immediately added, “Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I’m hopeful.” It’s hard to blame Wilson. The Jets are 24-51 since drafting Wilson and he has routinely caught passes from some of the league’s worst quarterbacks. The offense has been better under Geno Smith this year, but the team is still struggling to win games. Wilson could likely force his way out of New York if he wanted to, but it sounds like he’s content to go down with the ship again this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The Dolphins shut down Wilson, opting to let Omar Cooper Jr. and Mason Taylor beat them through the air. The duo combined for 177 yards and three touchdowns while Wilson was stuck with decoy duties. Wilson was spotted screaming at Geno Smith in the fourth quarter after Smith took a back-breaking sack on third down at the goal line. Wilson downplayed the altercation after the game, saying he was “collaborating” and then noting that he wasn’t even talking to Geno. He was. With several young players taking on larger roles in the Jets’ offense, Wilson’s role as the team’s unquestioned WR1 on the team has taken a hit. Still, he should at least stay in the fantasy WR2 mix for his Week 8 date with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 4-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson’s second quietest effort of the season came as he dealt with Christian Gonzalez’s stingy coverage and first-round rookie teammate Omar Cooper Jr. returning from his ankle injury. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) likely — hopefully — soon returning from his marathon absence, Wilson is set to have a lot more target competition in the Jets’ receiver corps, but those extra bodies should also create more space for the Jets’ No. 1. Wilson remains a high-end WR2 heading into next week’s plus matchup with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-11 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The 100-yard effort was Wilson’s second in three weeks. It was no easy feat on a rainy afternoon in Jersey where Geno Smith completed only 17 passes. Wilson’s score was a 32-yarder where he spun out of a tackle for a catch-and-run house call. In addition to the 100-yard efforts, Wilson now has a score in three of his past four appearances. It’s like Wilson’s lost 2025 never happened, which is exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers were hoping for. A weekly fixture in the low-end WR1 ranks, Wilson has a Week 6 date with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: No one on the Jets offense got home for fantasy purposes as the Bears held on to the ball for several long drives in the second half. The Jets possessed the ball for just 17 minutes on the day. Wilson’s four targets led the New York offense, as Geno Smith was limited to a mere 15 pass attempts. Wilson continues to dominate air yards and targets in the Jets offense and should remain in all lineups next week against Cleveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson was evaluated for a concussion and was cleared to return in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson took a hard hit late in the fourth quarter and was slow to get up. The Jets turned the ball over on the next play, so we never got to see Wilson return, but it sounds like he would have been back on the field had the game gone to overtime. Wilson ended the day with 10 catches for 107 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets. He found the end zone on an incredible circus catch late in the fourth quarter to tie the game up. As expected, Wilson was the focal point of the Jets’ passing attack with Adonai Mitchell sidelined. Even if Mitchell returns next week versus the Bears, Wilson will be moving up the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 5-of-7 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson saw five fewer targets than Adonai Mitchell, but played more snaps and ran more routes. Mitchell simply sees more quick-hitter looks close to the line of scrimmage, while Wilson is used more over the middle of the field. The Packers also frequently sent safety help over to Wilson’s side, but the 26-year-old was still able to make a few big catches when they mattered. He should be in for a bigger day against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards in the Jets’ Week 1 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: With the Jets in the unusual position of dominating a game from whistle to whistle, new QB Geno Smith dropped back just 24 times. Translation, Wilson coming away with seven targets was actually a pretty good outcome. The Jets’ blocking appeared much improved, but this was not a true test, even if it came on the road. That will come in Week 2 for the Jets’ home opener against the Packers. Wilson will remain a solid WR2 whose high floor will hopefully be accompanied by more ceiling efforts this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he’s been “so impressed” with Geno Smith’s play.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Reich has reportedly added wrinkles to the offense he deployed as head coach of the Colts and Panthers. At both of those stops his offenses were near the bottom of the league in most basic offensive metrics. Smith, meanwhile, has looked sharp as the team’s starting quarterback throughout training camp and in limited preseason snaps. He’ll look to bounce back from a nightmarish statistical 2025 season in Vegas. Jets players, including Garrett Wilson, told The Athletic that they have enjoyed the “player empowerment” that comes along with Reich’s coaching style and his offensive scheming, which leaves room for improvisation. The Jets offense could be functional as long as Smith, 35, is healthy and upright.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts are open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Multiple teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old Taylor and talks are active and ongoing, according to Schefter. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts already turned down an offer for Taylor that included a 2027 second-round pick and another pick. While previous reports stated the Colts weren’t interested in trading Taylor, who signed an extension before the season, Indianapolis appears to be holding out for the best offer they can get. Taylor would see a slight boost in fantasy value if acquired by another team while Seth McGowan would likely take over the Colts’ backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Steichen said Taylor will see a full workload despite being the subject of trade rumors for a Colts team that will clearly be sellers at the deadline. Taylor is healthy and not on the injury report, so this is strictly an update to inform fantasy managers they can start him with confidence this week. Taylor remains a high-end RB1 as long as his normal workload remains intact.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor has not requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: The Colts this week dealt DeForest Buckner to the 49ers and Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks in what looks like a fire sale ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline. Taylor could be next if the Colts are ready to go all in on a rebuild in 2027 and beyond. A contender would likely have to part with a second round draft pick if they want Taylor in the coming weeks. Teams that could be suitors for Taylor include the Bengals, Vikings, and Seahawks, all of whom have backfield issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Colts ownership does not want to trade Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Schefter said that if he had to guess today, he doesn’t think the Colts will part with Taylor. There are still a few weeks ahead of the trade deadline, and it’s certainly possible that a team bowls them over with an offer. This is going to remain a topic of conversation until the deadline passes. But it is worth noting that ownership believes in Taylor as a difference-maker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor said trade rumors have “been out there already” so he doesn’t think his wife Ayanna talking about it on social media “really change[s] anything.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Ayanna Taylor has been discussing the trade on TikTok. Her husband added: “You know everybody’s on TikTok these days. So, you just have to come into work and stay focused.” Since Chris Ballard’s firing, Taylor trade rumors have picked up steam. He refused to address them when asked after last week’s game, but his wife has posted about them, saying: “They have a losing record, they just fired their 10-year GM and they have no (first-round) draft picks. How are they gonna get new leadership to come in when they really have no options to transform the team?” Ayanna Taylor knows ball. We’ll see if the Colts ultimately trade Taylor; the price will be quite high and Jonathan Jones reported on Saturday it hasn’t been discussed internally yet. The rest of the NFL clearly seems to want it to happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 18 times for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding 2 receptions for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor once again operated as the Colts’ lead back, though rookie Seth McGowan took on more work as the game went on. A first quarter 38-yard touchdown by Taylor was the Colts’ most explosive play of the game; the rest of his rushes averaged just over three yards per carry. It was a tough matchup for the Colts against a high-motor Vikings defense and the offense was not able to sustain drives long enough for Taylor to get opportunities. He saw red zone snaps later in the game but the Colts were unable to move the ball close to the goal line. With another Indy loss, Taylor remains in trade rumors. Regardless of where he plays the rest of the season, Taylor is still a fantasy RB1 moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Colts aren’t discussing a Jonathan Taylor trade yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Jones writes that his understanding is the Colts will wait a few weeks before deciding what to do with their star running back. Indianapolis decided to move on from GM Chris Ballard after a 2-4 start. The way things are trending, it’s easy to imagine the Colts still on the outside of the playoff race in a few weeks. At that point interim GM Ed Dodds could look to recoup draft assets the team lost in previous trades. According to Jones, moving Taylor “would be the most expedient route” to acquiring a high draft pick. Citing sources, Jones lists the Giants and Vikings as potential suitors if Taylor is made available on the trade market. Taylor signed a two-year extension with the Colts in August that hasn’t even kicked in yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that several teams are interested in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis:
According to Holder, multiple teams would be open to trading for Taylor, but it remains unclear whether the Colts are ready to be sellers before the trade deadline. Colts GM Chris Ballard was recently fired, and “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming” after the eventual hiring of a new general manager.
Seth McGowan
should be stashed on benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will likely try to trade for a running back, and Cam Skattebo is unlikely to return to his prior role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Hughes makes clear that he thinks Skattebo’s time as the clear-cut lead back is over, recapping coach John Harbaugh’s offseason attempts to acquire a bellcow, while noting that Skattebo is currently in the doghouse. Hughes believes Skattebo is a nice complementary player who can function as a physical change-of-pace option. The biggest issue the Giants face in replacing him is cost. He thinks a player like Jonathan Taylor will cost a Day 2 pick, at least, and he is not sure Taylor is worth that, given the Giants’ long-term plans for the 2027 draft capital they’ve accrued via various personnel moves. Trading away Kayvon Thibodeaux is an option, but doing so is challenging with Brian Burns (knee) out for the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Week 8 will mark the second consecutive absence for the veteran kick returner, with little-to-no impact on the offensive pieces around him considering he has played more than 12 offensive snaps only once all season. Fantasy managers are more interested in the potential status of George Pickens, who is listed as questionable. If Pickens can’t go, Ryan Flournoy could see a slight uptick in opportunities on the perimeter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new. He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status. Meanwhile, WR/KR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was an estimated DNP in practice after not playing last week. The Cowboys may be missing Turpin again as a kick returner and gadget player on offense, but Pickens should still be the WR2 for Sunday against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys ruled out KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for Week 7 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin’s absence will be felt most on special teams, with the team now forced to find a replacement on punt and kick returns. Otherwise, there is almost zero fantasy impact as the team’s WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin departed before the first offensive play run from scrimmage after sustaining a ribs injury on the opening kickoff. He was taken to the locker room for x-rays and is listed as questionable to return by the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVonte Turpin failed to haul in his only target in Week 18.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin ends the season with 26 catches on 38 targets for 396 yards and two touchdowns. He also added 16 carries for 82 rushing yards, but his primary value was as a kick returner. On the season, he had 69 kick returns for 1,814 yards, which leads the league as of the end of this game. That will be his primary role in 2026 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught his only target for an 86-yard touchdown in the Cowboy’s Week 17 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: It took all of one target for Turpin to make his mark felt in the win as he broke free of primary coverage and split the safeties deep down the middle for an 86-yard, catch-and-run score. Turpin continues to play behind Jalen Tolbert but his flashy touchdown demonstrates his big play ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys listed WR KaVontae Turpin (shoulder) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin played through the same shoulder injury in Week 13’s win over the Chiefs. The Cowboys’ special teams ace has posted a meager 19-260-1 receiving line this season and isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 14 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: George Pickens (knee/calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: KaVontae Turpin was also cleared to play. Pickens was held out of practice on Monday but returned for a limited session on Tuesday. He was full-go today before being removed from the injury report entirely. Pickens has worked himself into a weekly WR1 ranking and is even threatening to overtake CeeDee Lamb. Both he and Lamb are elite fantasy options for Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys WR KaVontae Turpin (shoulder/illness) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin was a DNP on Monday. The shifty slot receiver/returner looks to be trending towards playing on a short week after taking three touches for a combined 52 yards on Sunday afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught his only target for 17 yards in Dallas’ Week 7 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin played 20 snaps according to early PFF data, well behind Jalen Tolbert’s 33. But Turpin remains the preferred fantasy option here given that Tolbert is an elite sacrificial X receiver who almost never commands a target. Turpin is not a preferred FLEX target against the Broncos in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) is questionable for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens saw a hamstring designation added to his status this week after playing through a shoulder ailment the previous two games, which was enough for the team to list him as questionable after a week of limited sessions. Although we expect Pickens to continue to play through his injuries, fantasy managers will want to confirm his status when the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick. If active, Pickens is an upside WR2 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: It’s the second consecutive limited showing for the co-alpha receiver, who will likely need to upgrade to a full showing on Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend. Pickens has played through the shoulder issue for two weeks, but the hamstring ailment is worth monitoring as the weekend approaches. Pickens is a viable WR2 in a solid matchup against the Cardinals, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new. He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status. Meanwhile, WR/KR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was an estimated DNP in practice after not playing last week. The Cowboys may be missing Turpin again as a kick returner and gadget player on offense, but Pickens should still be the WR2 for Sunday against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (shoulder) said he will play in Week 7 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: The Cowboys face the Eagles in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, giving Pickens an extra day to recover. ESPN’s Todd Archer said yesterday that Pickens has been icing his shoulder in-game during the Cowboys’ last two games. He encouragingly practiced in full today. Start him as a WR2 as usual this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (shoulder) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Reliable ESPN beat reporter Todd Archer notes that Pickens has had ice on his shoulder during the Cowboys’ last two games. He does not think that this injury threatens Pickens’ Week 7 availability. Thanks, Todd. Ideally, Pickens jumps back up to full participation tomorrow, and we head into Sunday carefree. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 6-of-11 targets for 73 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens was targeted just once in the first half as the Cowboys were held under 100 yards of total offense before the break. He would remain quiet through the third quarter, adding a single catch to his ledger on two additional targets before seeing eight looks in the final frame with the Cowboys in desperation mode. The 11 targets finished second on the team to CeeDee Lamb’s 18 while the 73 yards slightly edged the 70 of Lamb. Pickens remains an upside WR2 ahead of a divisional matchup against the inside-funnel Eagles’ secondary in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 9-of-13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens was the primary target throughout the game against the single-high-heavy Buccaneers, scoring a late fourth quarter touchdown to cap off his first impressive fantasy outing of the young season. Furthermore, fellow receiver CeeDee Lamb departed the game in the fourth quarter with a quad injury that he was unable to play through, potentially setting up Pickens for immense volume in a Week 6 meeting with the Packers at Lambeau. Fantasy managers have patiently watched as Lamb stole the show through the first four games of 2026, but it now appears as if Pickens will have his time to shine, pending the severity of Lamb’s soft tissue injury. Pickens is a WR2 with Lamb active and a surefire WR1 with Lamb out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 2-of-3 targets for 75 yards in Dallas’ Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: He had a 53-yard mossing of Kamari Lassiter in the third quarter to set up a big Cowboys drive, and also wound up drawing two different penalties against Lassiter in the end zone to sustain a touchdown drive, one on fourth down. Pickens isn’t playing poorly, but the Cowboys simply are feeding CeeDee Lamb and it’s hard to argue with the results. Eventually the touchdown worm will turn and Pickens will be back on the WR2 line against the Bucs in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 7-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens finally looked like the player we expected to see after his breakout 2025 campaign. While we’re still waiting for the first true explosive play from Pickens this season, he did manage to haul in all four targets he saw in the intermediate area of the field and picked up 19 yards on a third-and-10 on a drive that ended with a Jake Ferguson touchdown two plays later. Pickens would have had a much bigger day if not for a 20-yard reception that was called back due to a penalty, but fantasy managers won’t be upset with this performance. We’ll see if he can build on this week’s outing next week against the Texans, where he will be on the WR2 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 6-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: At some point, things will break in Pickens’ favor, but it was not to be in Sunday’s win over the Commanders, despite Dak Prescott throwing for 279-4-0 and having just five incompletions on the day. Pickens hasn’t generated any explosive plays yet, with his longest catch of the season coming on a 12-yard gain in the second quarter of today’s game. He’s still averaging 7.0 targets through the first two weeks of the season, so hopefully the big plays will follow soon. He should be treated as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier saw a steady progression in practice throughout the week, starting off with a “DNP” before upgrading in each subsequent session, culminating in a full practice Friday. He will be available to form a likely three-headed timeshare with Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight against the Cowboys and likely does not warrant fantasy consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier was able to get a bump up after a DNP for Wednesday. It appears to just be a case of rest for the 26-year-old, but fantasy managers who will consider Allgeier for Week 8 against the Cowboys if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) can’t go — Love was also limited Thursday — should keep an eye on Friday’s designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier popped up on the injury report with a toe issue as rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) returned to practice in a limited fashion. Though we don’t know the severity of Allgeier’s injury, it may be worth keeping Bam Knight rostered despite Love’s return. If Allgeier cannot play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Knight will get another week of fantasy viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: We were hoping to see Love practice in full after taking two weeks off. While today’s limited session puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are still worth stashing on benches, just in case. The Cardinals are finally handling Love’s recovery patiently, after giving him far too many touches early in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed eight times for 19 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos, adding three catches for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier only saw one more carry than Bam Knight. Both backs caught three passes, but Knight was the recipient of five targets. Through two Jeremiyah Love absences, Allgeier has 26 carries for 57 yards. He’s barely playing ahead of Knight and has been the far less efficient member of the backfield. Knight has 128 yards on four fewer attempts. Even if Love is out again next week, Allgeier will barely crack the RB3 ranks versus Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Tyler Allgeier is “always” going to serve as a complementary running back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: LaFleur really laid it all out there at today’s press conference, saying Allgeier “is always going to complement that next guy” when the starter is out. He adds that Allgeier is “extremely smart” and can be trusted in pass protection and short-yardage situations on third down. While Allgeier “can” do what the Cardinals need him to do on first and second down, LaFleur said Bam Knight will take “a lot” of that work with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined. LaFleur closed by saying he does not think any of these running backs can hold up in a full-time role over the course of the season. Allgeier handled a hefty 19 touches in this complementary role last week. He can be started as a high-volume FLEX with touchdown-based upside against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed 18 times for 38 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams, adding one reception for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier got the start, but looked slow compared to his backfield mate Bam Knight today. It was an extremely disappointing showing and the Cardinals seemingly leaned on Knight more and more as the game progressed. Allgeier still totaled 19 touches, including 18 carries, but he was routinely stopped around the line of scrimmage and critically ceded red zone snaps to Knight. Knight may have injured his right hand or wrist late in the game, but he continued playing. With Jerermiyah Love (ankle) currently sidelined, Allgeier could end up being the lead back again next week against the Broncos. Keep an eye on the Cardinals’ injury report this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: The Cardinals officially ruled Love out for this Sunday’s game against the Rams after he was. DNP in practice all week. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Love is not considered a candidate to be placed on injured reserve at this time, but the fact that he even has to mention that is cause for some concern that Love could be looking at a multi-week absence. LaFleur also added that Love’s lack of involvement in the passing game is due to his inability to run routes on his injured ankle. His practice status will be one to monitor next week when the Cardinals begin preparing for the Broncos. Tyler Allgeier should be in line for a busy day against the Rams and will be a volume-based RB2 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is questionable for Denver’s Week 8 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle got in two limited sessions after missing practice on Wednesday. It feels like he’s on the optimistic side of questionable given the trend line, though of course you would have preferred to see a full session somewhere in here. It’s also possible he winds up on a snap count, so we’ll see if any insiders dig up anything on that this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Waddle’s status for Week 8 against the Chiefs has not been determined. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver aggravated his preexisting chest injury in Week 7 against the Cardinals. Backup plans should be made at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle left Week 7’s game against the Cardinals with an apparent chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Up by 14, Sean Payton dialed up a trick play for Waddle, giving him a pitch as Waddle came across the formation. Waddle bobbled the ball and was clobbered by Josh Sweat. He writhed in pain while holding his left shoulder. Trainers came onto the field and eventually walked him into the locker room. With less than four minutes on the clock at the time of his departure, we don’t expect to see him again today. Waddle’s day ends with four catches for 48 yards on seven targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle upgraded to full on Friday after logging two limited sessions to begin the week. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver has struggled to deliver usable stat lines with Bo Nix intent on checking down. The Cardinals’ pass defense could facilitate a bounce-back game for Waddle, but he remains a WR3/FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: The Broncos’ big-name offseason acquisition has totaled more than 35 yards just once all year, and now he has a chest injury. Waddle is on track to play, and he faces a beatable Cardinals pass defense this week, but he can only be treated as a FLEX starter at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle briefly exited the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks before returning to the game. He now pops up on the practice report as a limited participant on Wednesday with a chest injury. Waddle is not in jeopardy of missing time just yet, but his poor fantasy production to start the season makes him a volatile fantasy option for Week 7 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) returned to the game in the fourth quarter of Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle departed in the third quarter and was deemed questionable to return with a shoulder injury but made his way back to the field in the fourth quarter, catching two additional passes in the final frame. He ended with four receptions for 24 yards on seven targets and has quickly become a difficult weekly start in fantasy circles. An enticing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 7 is sure to give fantasy managers a hint of potential, but if he fails again to return a usable fantasy week, it might be time to reconsider entering him in weekly lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle departed early in the third quarter and was quickly deemed questionable to return with a shoulder injury. It is unclear when the injury occurred. Waddle managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for 15 yards prior to departing, keeping his usable weeks total at just two games through the first six weeks of the 2026 season. Fantasy managers that invested a fourth-round pick on the veteran wide receiver have got to begin to make alternate plans at wide receiver moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jamree-kromah/.headline: Dolphins claimed EDGE Jamree Kromah off waivers from the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jamree-kromah/.analysis: You thought you could just sneak this guy through waivers, did you? Well the Miami Dolphins are going to claim him.
