They’ve got to look busy here as they try to find one or two front seven pieces that will still have jobs in two years. The 26-year-old Kromah is their latest attempt to find one of them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jamree-kromah/.headline: Patriots declared OLB Anfernee Jennings, TE Jaheim Bell, DE Jamree Kromah, QB Joe Milton III, OT Vederian Lowe, LG Michael Jordan inactive for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jamree-kromah/.analysis: The Patriots’ front-seven is down three starters at this point. It’s an unideal situation facing the 49ers’ vaunted rushing attack. The 49ers’ pass rush should also effectively generate pressure against the Patriots’ problematic offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jamree-kromah/.headline: Rutgers junior DL Jamree Kromah has entered the transfer portal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jamree-kromah/.analysis: Kromah (6'4/275) was a three-star prospect from the 2018 recruiting class and was the 99th ranked defensive end in his class per 247Sports’ composite rankings. Kromah spent three seasons at Rutgers, and posted career-highs in 2021 according to Pro Football Focus, when he appeared on 169 defensive snaps while totaling nine tackles and one quarterback pressure on the year. 2021 marked the first season in which he surpassed 100 defensive snaps, as the soon to be fifth-year player will now look to build on his newfound experience elsewhere in 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s WR4 status will continue aplomb against the Patriots in Week 8, though Caleb Douglas’ return probably has capped his ceiling case for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Back-to-back limited sessions probably leave Washington in a good spot for Week 8. He’s more likely than not to be cleared off the injury report on Friday as long as there’s not a sudden downgrade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington has cooled off in recent weeks. Although his knee injury is unlikely to keep him out of the Dolphins’ Week 8 matchup against the Patriots, he is barely a WR5 in fantasy football. Washington does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets, adding two carries for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s previous season-low in targets was five. He had also reached at least 43 receiving yards in every game before today. It shouldn’t come as a surprise that his worst box score of the season came in Caleb Douglas’s first game back from a month-long absence. With more competition for targets on a team that doesn’t want to pass the football, Washington is trending in the wrong direction headed into Week 8. He will be a low-end WR4 versus the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 6-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington was the most involved Dolphins receiver, leading the team in targets and receiving yards. He started things off with an 18-yard rush and saw a steady peppering of low-depth targets. Though he led all Dolphins skill-position players in snaps, Washington doesn’t see many scoring opportunities in the Miami offense. After a Week 6 bye, The 25-year-old is a volume-based FLEX play Week 7 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-5 targets for 67 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington remains one of the Dolphins’ primary returners despite his increased receiving involvement. His day began with a muffed punt that he successfully recovered in the end zone for a touchback. Things improved from there. Washington delivered multiple double-digit gains, functioning effectively as a weapon behind the line of scrimmage and in the flats. He also turned in a 17-yarder via a corner route on play action. Rookie WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) may return for next week’s game against the Saints. If he remains sidelined, Washington should be FLEX-viable, though his ceiling is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: We expect to see Douglas listed with a second DNP next to his name today, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4 against the Vikings. Were he indeed to miss this week’s game, WRs Chris Bell (knee) and Malik Washington would benefit. Washington’s target volume is somewhat intriguing, but Bell looks like the far more talented player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Douglas, who has shown flashes in limited action so far this season, did not suit up in Week 3 against the Chiefs and looks like a long shot for Week 4 against the Vikings. Douglas’ absence would be a potential boost for Malik Washington, who leads the Dolphins in targets and air yards through Week 3. Minnesota’s defense, while elite, has allowed the fourth most air yards this season and profiles as a pass-funnel.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-10 targets for 56 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, adding two carries for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Every total was a new season high for Washington, including the carries. It briefly appeared Washington might be the Dolphins’ emergency lead back, as De’Von Achane was knocked out with a knee injury and Ollie Gordon was cramping. With Achane seemingly set for a long absence, Washington could indeed be in line for more rushing usage. That makes him a slightly more viable WR4, but rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas still offer more overall upside heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. That’s, of course, if Douglas returns from his ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Caleb Douglas (ankle) won’t practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Douglas suffered an ankle injury in Miami’s Week 2 loss to the 49ers and did not return. He was spotted in a boot after the game. Hafley has been noncommittal when talking about Douglas’s Week 3 status, though we suspect he won’t suit up versus the Chiefs. Malik Washington is locked in as the team’s No. 1 receiver now, giving him some appeal as a FLEX option this week. Rookie Chris Bell should also see an uptick in routes, making him worth stashing in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The fringe TE2 life awaits Dulcich against the Patriots on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Still, back-to-back practices are a good sign that Dulcich will be ready to go for Week 8’s game against the Patriots. That isn’t necessarily an endorsement of using him in fantasy football — even after last week’s surprise 5/86 against the Jets — but hey, the Dolphins will be glad he’s around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The Dolphins’ tight end finally had a decent game, only to tweak an ankle along the way. He should be fine for Week 8 against the Patriots, but he is barely in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught all five of his targets for 86 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich made the most of National Tight Ends Day with a 32-yard catch on the Dolphins’ opening drive and two more gains of 15+ yards throughout the contest. He led the team in catches and targets. Dulcich now has at least four receptions in three of his past four games. Miami’s run-first approach is preventing him from finding spike weeks, but Dulcich has worked himself into the TE2 conversation ahead of Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich also added a two-point conversion to his total. It was a low-efficiency passing offense for the Dolphins once again, leading to Dulcich averaging under 10 yards per reception. The 26-year-old tight end is a fantasy TE3 as the Dolphins head into a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 5-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Held under 20 yards in each of the Dolphins’ first two games, Dulcich finally had something of a pop-up effort as the ‘Fins tried in vain to match points with the Chiefs. It was nice to get some proof of TE2 concept, but it is going to be exceptionally difficult for Dulcich to carve out streamer value in a low-volume passing attack focused on seeing what it has in its intriguing rookie receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 1 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Both of Dulcich’s targets occurred on the third drive. One was a six-yarder via play action. The other was a delayed screen pass, which Dulcich admirably ran for 12 yards, picking up a first down along the way. The fact that he was barely involved in a pass-heavy game script bodes poorly for his TE1 viability. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones believes Jalen Tolbert “appeared to be” one of Malik Willis’ top targets in OTAs and minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Furones also lists Greg Dulcich as a player that was a primary receiver for Willis, but we’ve done plenty of offseason hype on Dulcich. Tolbert appears to be a potential “someone has to catch a ball here” deep league pick, as he’s well off the fantasy radar at this point. He’s not off the board among the top-100 wideouts in ADP. The ceiling is likely low, but if he can emerge as the top option amongst Miami’s wideouts, Tolbert could be a viable WR3/WR4 at points this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports Greg Dulcich was “one of the primary targets” for Malik Willis in spring practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich turned into a nice contributor for the Dolphins during the second half of last season. He didn’t play his first snaps until Week 8 due to an injury that landed him on injured reserve, but in 10 games, Dulcich caught 26 passes for 335 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets, earning four or more targets in five of those games. This isn’t the first time we have heard Dulcich has flashed in practice, and given the thin receiver room in Miami, it’s easy to envision a meaningful role for him in 2026. Dulcich is a former third-round pick who posted a 33-411-2 line as a rookie back in 2022 in 10 games with the Broncos, but injuries have slowed him in recent years. Now that he’s healthy and making a strong early showing this offseason, Dulcich could make for an intriguing late-round draft pick in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team’s passing offense is “a work in progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Malik Willis, Hafley said during a Tuesday presser, is still building chemistry with the team’s pass catchers in OTAs and working on timing. That presumably includes Malik Washington, who had 46 catches for 317 yards and three scores last season, and Greg Dulcich, who’s expected by Miami beat writers to “figure heavily” into the team’s passing attack in 2026. Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell could also see heavy snaps in the Miami passing game this season. Tolbert, who flashed in Dallas in 2024 with 610 yards and seven touchdowns, could emerge as the Dolphins’ top pass-catching option with a solid training camp. There likely won’t be much target volume to go around, however, considering the team’s plans to operate a run-heavy offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey’s concussion was always unlikely to hold him out for Week 8 with the team coming off their bye, with Friday’s injury report confirming that notion. The Chargers have under-performed offensive expectations more than any team through their first six games, leaving McConkey in the FLEX range for Week 8, a far cry from the WR2 range he was drafted in this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver could resume practicing in full today, after recovering during the team’s Week 7 bye. If McConkey is limited, an update will be provided. Exactly one week ago, The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reported that the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks. They face an underperforming Rams defense in Week 8 and could (maybe) generate a bounce-back performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (head) was ruled out in Week 6 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey exited the game after a 17-yard reception in the first quarter and was seen entering the blue medical tent before being helped to the locker room. The quickness with which he was ruled out could mean the injury is on the severe side. The Chargers are down to their fifth and sixth wideouts on the depth chart. Justin Herbert likely won’t be fantasy relevant for the rest of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he did not know if McConkey or Quentin Johnston would be on snap counts on Sunday. Cool. What we do know is that the Chargers desperately need a win and McConkey is their best receiver, so the incentives are certainly aligned to get McConkey into the fantasy WR3 discussion even with a pitch count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is on track to once again be active on game day, but it is unclear how involved he will be. Two limited sessions are a good sign, but it would be great to see him practice fully tomorrow. In that instance, starting him as a WR2 would be far more palatable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he expects Ladd McConkey (foot) to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: We, in turn, expect McConkey to be listed as a limited participant. An update will be provided if he practices in full. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver was an emergency active last week, goose-egging in the box score. His early-week return to practice puts him on track to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but it would be great to see him practice in full by the end of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said it’s “possible” that Ladd McConkey (foot) is “working back in this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was active last week but an emergency-only player and played zero snaps. With the Chargers having a Week 7 bye, we’d be surprised if they pushed McConkey to play unless they really needed him. Unfortunately, since he was already active last week, we know that they may really need him. His status is up in the air ahead of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is not expected to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey did not practice at all this week but was still given a questionable tag on Friday. He was always a long-shot to play after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4. With Quentin Johnston out this week as well, Tre’ Harris will be Justin Herbert’s No. 1 receiver. That puts him in the WR3 mix despite the Chargers’ dismal offensive performance through four weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is questionable for Washington’s Week 8 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The rare limited-DNP-limited injury report shows up here after Burks suffered a late foot injury in Week 6’s Monday night football. Burks probably is best considered truly questionable at this point. If he’s absent, it could help Antonio Williams get into the 80 percent snap range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks downgraded from a limited showing Wednesday to a “DNP” Thursday, indicating he might be headed toward an absence when the Commanders take on the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Considering the team is already without Terry McLaurin, who was lost for the season in Week 6, this would appear to be setting up for the best chance for rookie Antonio Williams to finally break out in Washington. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the status of Burks on the team’s final injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks was limited due to a foot injury; this is notable with the Commanders coming out of a bye week. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Burks has the opportunity to earn an increased role in the receiving corps. Fantasy managers don’t need to roster the 26-year-old yet, but Dyami Brown and Antonio Williams could see a boost in targets if Burks sits out Week 8 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Terry McLaurin’s knee injury is considered “significant.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Washington head coach Dan Quinn said after the team’s Monday night loss to the 49ers that there was “fear” McLaurin could be lost for the long-term after going down with a non-contact injury and was carted to the locker room. McLaurin has functioned as the team’s lone downfield threat for much of the season, and could be replaced with Treylon Burks, who on Monday night caught four balls for 66 yards before sustaining a late-game injury. Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown could also see an increase in routes and targets if McLaurin is sidelined for a while. Look for Chig Okonkwo to see an uptick in targets too. Okonkwo had seven grabs for 69 yards against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 4-of-6 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks stepped into an increased role in the offense following the first quarter injury to Terry McLaurin, the latter of whom appears to have suffered a significant knee injury. The six targets ranked third on the team behind tight end Chig Okonkwo and veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs, but a late injury could immediately halt his momentum. Burks was injured on a contested ball in the end zone on fourth down with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and was escorted to the locker room by training staff. Fantasy managers interested in a potential waiver addition will want to track updates from the team regarding his health in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 1-of-3 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks only catch of the day came on a double-move that saw him burn Sauce Gardner for a massive touchdown, though he may have simply been working back to the quarterback before realizing the throw was going over his head. Either way, Burks turned on the jets, tracked down the ball, and ran in the Commanders’ only touchdown of the day. Burks isn’t on the fantasy radar despite the long catch, but it’s nice to see him carving out a role in Washington.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught both of his targets for 13 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 3 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: You heard that right, Treylon Burks plays for the Commanders. The former first-round pick hauled in just his third receiving touchdown of his career on a throw over the middle from Marcus Mariota. Burks has the size to be a red-zone threat, but despite the scoring play Sunday, he’s too far down the depth chart to be a fantasy consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Last Man Standig’s Ben Standig reports that Commanders WR Treylon Burks (foot soreness) sat out Thursday’s “on-field work.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn also said the team doesn’t see the soreness as a long-term issue, but it is a disappointing follow-up to what was reportedly a strong showing for Burks at the first training camp practice. The Commanders have a very thin wide receiver corps, so every injury matters. Hopefully, Burks is back before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders re-signed WR Treylon Burks to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks had a Catch Of The Year candidate on his lone touchdown catch last season, finishing with a 10/130/1 line in spot duty. He’s not likely to start out the year in the Commanders starting three-wide, but he’s a reasonable depth option and should have a good shot to win a roster spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Commanders’ Week 18 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks signed to the Commanders’ practice squad in October after the Titans released him. He finished his year with the Commanders totaling 10 receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. Burks’ touchdown was a candidate for catch of the year, a highlight-reel five-yard grab with one hand in Week 13 against the Broncos. With Luke McCaffrey and Jaylin Lane out towards the end of the season, Burks became the team’s WR3, seeing a variety of targets as an outside receiver opposite Terry McLaurin. He is certainly an option to return to Washington next season, though he is likely to be a depth piece on whichever team employs him for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris returns to the lineup after missing Week 6, with the team’s bye week providing enough time for the veteran receiver to get back to the active game-day roster. That doesn’t mean he should be inserted into fantasy lineups after such a slow start to the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was labeled week-to-week early in Week 6 and was unable to face the Chiefs that weekend. After resting and rehabbing through the Chargers’ Week 7 bye, Harris has a chance to resume playing in Week 8. We expect to see him listed as a limited participant, but an update will be provided if he practices in full. Brenen Thompson (quad) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He did not practice this week and Jim Harbaugh called him “week to week.” Harris stands a chance at returning after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tre’ Harris (hamstring) is “more of a week-to-week [thing].”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris will probably have a real chance to play in Week 8, after the Chargers’ Week 7 bye. He thudded to a 16-yard outing in his big chance last week with Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey out and doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered if you’re in a bye week crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught 2-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was a complete non-factor even against the depleted Broncos’ secondary. The second-year wideout was the top target with Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston unavailable, and that extra attention didn’t help. Harris will try and bounce back in Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is not expected to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McConkey did not practice at all this week but was still given a questionable tag on Friday. He was always a long-shot to play after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4. With Quentin Johnston out this week as well, Tre’ Harris will be Justin Herbert’s No. 1 receiver. That puts him in the WR3 mix despite the Chargers’ dismal offensive performance through four weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught 3-of-5 targets for 60 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: For the second straight week, Harris finished with the most receiving yards on the day for the Chargers. For the second straight week — and fourth week in a row for Los Angeles — it wasn’t enough. If Ladd McConkey (foot) is unable to go, Harris will be the top target again in Week 5 against the Broncos, but against that tough group, he can’t be treated as more than a FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Javon Kinlaw (knee) will not play in Washington’s Week 8 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: He didn’t practice all week after Dan Quinn acknowledged it would be “tough” for him to play. An IR stint probably is in play on Saturday, if not, Kinlaw will probably start Week 9 on the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Javon Kinlaw (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw is dealing with a knee issue. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Wednesday it will “likely be tough” for the 29-year-old defensive tackle to play Sunday. We can expect Kinlaw to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (back/shoulder) is not on Washington’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: He was limited on Thursday and practiced in full today to avoid the questionable line. The 28-year-old defensive tackle can look forward to a Sunday of trying to stop Jadarian Price runs right up the gut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (back/shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw dealt with a back injury last week but played in Week 2. He came out of the loss against the Cowboys with an additional injury to the shoulder. Kinlaw’s status for Week 3 is in question as he sits out of practice with back and shoulder issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn said RG Sam Cosmi is in concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Cosmi will need to clear concussion protocol in time to play in Week 3’s home opener against the Seahawks. Cosmi took a hard helmet-to-helmet shot from teammate Kaytron Allen while trying to make a block and immediately went down on the field for several minutes. Rookie sixth-rounder Matt Gulbin took over in his absence and could be in line to draw the start for him next week if Cosmi is unable to play. Quinn also said DT Javon Kinlaw suffered a shoulder injury and LT Brandon Coleman suffered a finger injury in the loss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne was ejected from Week 10 against the Lions after committing an unnecessary roughness penalty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Payne was flagged after a hard-fought 13-yard touchdown run made by Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. Payne can be clearly seen punching Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown on the left side of his facemask. Astonishingly, Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw was not ejected after striking a referee in the forehead, though he was penalized, after Payne was ejected. The Commanders also may have lost CB Trey Amos, who entered the game with a hip injury, and required two trainers’ assistance to leave the field after injuring his ankle on the play. Amos is currently questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders agreed to terms with DT Javon Kinlaw, formerly of the Jets, on a three-year, $45 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw will get $30 million in guaranteed money on this deal. A former 49er who was drafted No. 14 overall in 2020 reunites with general manager Adam Peters, who has already added two other former 49ers to the roster this offseason. Kinlaw signed a one-year deal with the Jets last offseason and posted career highs in tackles (40) and sacks (4.5) in his age-27-season. Turning 28 in October, Kinlaw could make for a nice addition if he’s able to live up to the potential that once made him the 14th pick in the draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Jets agreed to terms with DT Javon Kinlaw, formerly of the 49ers, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: With his career derailed by his 2021 ACL tear, Kinlaw started just six games last season, though he did appear in all 17. He notched a career-high four sacks but earned horrid PFF pass-rushing marks in the process. Going on 27, Kinlaw isn’t exactly young and projectable. It’s a flier that is unlikely to pan out for Gang Green.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: 49ers declined to exercise DL Javon Kinlaw’s fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw has played just 10 regular season games in two years and has yet to rebound from a 2021 ACL tear to become the same player he was as a prospect. Declining the option was a formality. The 49ers brought in Javon Hargrave to take Kinlaw’s place in the starting lineup this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows writes the 49ers are “unlikely” to pick up Javon Kinlaw’s fifth-year option in May.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Coming off an ACL reconstruction in mid-2021, Kinlaw has started just 10 regular season games in the last two years. Kinlaw has yet to have a PFF grade above 55 in three seasons and had a ghastly 28.8 PFF run defense grade in 2022. It’s possible he rebounds in 2023 at full health, but it’s easy to understand why the 49ers wouldn’t want to guarantee him big money in 2024 from this start to his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) is not on Washington’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: He should be a mid-range WR3 with Terry McLaurin out of the picture in Washington. Diggs practiced in full each of the last two sessions of the week after a Wednesday DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs shook of the absence Wednesday with a full showing Thursday, indicating he is tracking well to suit up when the Commanders face off against the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. The tam previously indicated that Diggs’ modest role would not grow in the absence of Terry McLaurin, potentially paving the way for rookie Antonio Williams to see an increase in role and opportunity in the second half of the season. Fantasy managers will want to confirm Diggs’ status on the final injury report Friday, but it appears as if he will be available in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring/rest) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn already said Diggs won’t practice Wednesday, so this is not a surprise. Quinn also confirmed the veteran will return to practice Thursday and the additional rest designation should stave off concerns of Diggs dealing with a long-term injury. He should be in the WR3/FLEX mix for Week 8 against the Eagles. Also not practicing for the Commanders was TE John Bates (shoulder).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Stefon Diggs will practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs won’t practice Wednesday with an undisclosed injury. He should be fine for Washington’s Week 8 matchup against the Eagles, however. Diggs could see a slightly bigger role in the Commanders offense with Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year. Diggs drafters should keep an eye on the veteran’s practice status in the coming days. Diggs has been targeted on a team-high 28 percent of his pass routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he doesn’t anticipate Stefon Diggs taking on a larger role with Terry McLaurin lost for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Quinn did mention usage from “elsewhere” and the name “Antonio Williams” came up. Williams won’t be a buzzy waiver wire claim this week but could find himself in a reasonable WR3/WR4 sort of situation as the year unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-7 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: While the end line looks good in the box score, the fact that Diggs continued to operate in a situational role following the departure of Terry McLaurin in the first quarter was somewhat concerning for the veteran receiver’s upside potential in McLaurin’s absence, although the fact that he came into the game listed as questionable with a hamstring injury could have influenced his snap rate. Either way, Diggs continues to produce when on the field, returning significant value for fantasy managers that invested a middle-round pick for his services this summer. Diggs will be an upside WR3 when the Commanders take on the division rival Eagles in Week 8 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs returns from a one-game absence due a hamstring injury. Although possible he sees his route participation curtailed, fantasy managers that made it this far are likely forced to ride with the veteran receiver in a solid schematic matchup against the zone-heavy 49ers. Inactive for the Commanders are QB Marcus Mariota, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, OLB T.J. Magunranyanga, G Tanoa Togiai, and DE Charles Omenihu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is questionable for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs returned to the practice field Friday as a limited participant, following it with another practice with the same status a day later. The listed his as questionable for Monday Night Football against the 49ers as he attempts to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Fantasy managers might be better off playing it safe considering the timing of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: After missing all of practice last week and being a DNP on Thursday, Diggs was back on the field Friday, which is a good sign for his Week 6 availability with one practice left to go in the week. The Commanders take on the 49ers on Monday Night Football this week and will likely announce Diggs’ availability sometime Saturday, but he could be on track to return in what is a must-win game for the 1-3-1 Commanders. Diggs has caught 18 passes for 170 yards and three touchdowns this season and would be in the mix as a fringe WR3/WR4 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: It’s a bit of a surprise questionable because Davis got in three full practice sessions this week. Still, he is coming off a long-term neck injury that has sidelined him most of the year so we understand the Patriots being cautious here. We’d consider Davis on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis and both of the Patriots’ top perimeter backups, CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) are practicing in full this week. This is very good news. The trio has been sidelined for some time, weakening the Patriots’ secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots ruled out Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Patriots will also be without their top-two backup CBs, Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots listed S Kevin Byard (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder) and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable. This is good news for the Bears’ passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: It was an upgrade from an estimated Monday DNP. Davis has missed Week 2, Week 3, Week 5 and Week 6 to the neck listing so far. Perhaps he’ll try to give it a go on Thursday night, but we’d be surprised if he did better than a questionable tag on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has not played since Week 3, but he returns in time to cover Garrett Wilson in a divisional showdown. Gonzalez primarily lines up on the perimeter, but he has taken 15 combined snaps in the slot and in the box. He could take a few reps on the inside this week, but perimeter CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) is out, so Gonzalez could be asked to simply stay out wide.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: He has not practiced or played since Week 3. Nothing we’ve seen has suggested he’ll be a Saturday IR candidate, but it also wouldn’t necessarily be surprising if that happened. The Pats also ruled out fellow starting CB Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 5, leaving non-existent Raiders receivers with matchup upgrades. (Cody White is about to touch the end zone paint again.)

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez and fellow starting perimeter CB Carlton Davis (neck) have missed each of the Patriots’ first two practices this week, putting them on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Raiders. Las Vegas lines up Brock Bowers as a wide receiver most of the time. Missing both starting coverage defenders would make life tough on the defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has been sidelined with a shoulder injury since last week, missing the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills. Also not practicing were Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring). We’ll see if any of these corners can practice enough to play for Week 5, but Raiders WR Tre Tucker is headed for a good matchup against a banged up Patriots secondary this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) is inactive for Week 2 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis did not practice all week due to a neck injury and was officially ruled out on Saturday. The Patriots will look for reinforcements in the secondary for Week 2 against the Steelers. Also inactive for the Patriots are OT Dametrious Crownover, OT Walter Rouse, TE Tanner Arkin, DT Leonard Taylor, and QB Behren Morton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots downgraded CB Carlton Davis (neck) to out for Week 2 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis was unable to practice all week with a neck injury and will ultimately be held out of the team’s Week 2 game against the Steelers. Pittsburgh will be without starting wide receiver Michael Pittman, so it will be interesting how the Patriots choose to deploy Christian Gonzalez. Gonzalez could find himself in shadow coverage of opposing alpha DK Metcalf.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase is not on Cincinnati’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: He will play and be on the overall WR1 line against the Titans. Zac Taylor spoke earlier today and said he had no concerns about Chase. Everyone has downplayed concerns about Chase’s ankle for the majority of the week. He will be a smash play against a Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase quickly puts his fantasy managers’ worries to rest, returning to a full session Thursday after being limited Wednesday. The Bengals will be playing without two tight ends and their WR3 in Andre Iosivas, but their primary contributors remain one of the healthier units as we approach the half way point in the regular season. Chase can be started as a top tier WR1 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ja’Marr Chase’s ankle injury “is not considered a major deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Rap isn’t breaking much news here. Chase didn’t practice on Wednesday, but the Bengals listed him as getting a rest day on top of the ankle issue. It was just a maintenance day for one of the league’s best wideouts. Chase remains in the WR1 overall mix for his Week 8 game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (NIR-rest/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: The rest aspect suggests Chase’s ankle injury can effectively be treated as a non-issue, but NFL teams have played games with the injury report at times this season, so we are cataloguing it here to be safe. Assuming Chase resumes practicing tomorrow, he can be started as an elite WR1, as usual, in Week 8 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-7 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase caught just two passes for 23 yards in the first half, but he popped up for a 30-yard gain in the fourth quarter on a drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown to save the day for his fantasy managers. His seven targets tied Tee Higgins for the team-high this week, but Higgins had the far more productive day. He’s still in search of his first 100-yard performance of the year, but Chase has now found the end zone five times and has gone for 60-plus yards in four of six games this season. He’ll be on the WR1 radar next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 6-of-10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase returned from a concussion he suffered last week, seeing 10 targets in a productive fantasy day. He saw a goal-line fade target on the Bengals’ first drive and was later tackled at the one-yard line towards the end of the first half. Joe Burrow missed Chase for a 70-yard touchdown in the second half but Chase made a miraculous catch with his right arm for a 45-yard touchdown later in the half. He finishes with a successful fantasy day and is squarely in the WR1 ranks heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Tee Higgins (neck/groin) also expected to play, it’s business as usual for the Bengals this week. Higgins could be on a pitch count, while Chase won’t have any restrictions. Facing a pitiful Miami defense, Chase is in the running for WR1 overall this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) is questionable for Cincinnati’s Week 5 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: He did fully practice today — it feels like this is trending in the right direction, but it’s hard to know without detailed reporting of where he is in the protocol how likely he is to sit. We’re sure there will be many more report on Chase over the next 24-36 hours. He enters the weekend a true question mark.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase still needs to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to suit up for Week 5’s game against the Dolphins. That said, he appears to be trending toward being able to play after logging back-to-back practices to close out the week. Tee Higgins (groin/neck), who was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday was also seen sprinting and running routes on Friday, which suggests he could also be good to go for Sunday’s game. We will check back in with official game day statuses in the coming hours when the team releases its final injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) is present and wearing pads at practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: It looks like Chase will practice in some capacity today. He made the long walk to the Bengals’ practice field, fully suited up in pads, carrying his helmet. Given the NFL’s five-phase concussion protocol, we expect to see him listed as a limited participant today, but we will provide an update if he upgrades to full participation. Chase has a chance to play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell didn’t practice all week and his availability for Week 9 is likely in question as well. Campbell has 49 tackles in seven starts this season despite spending a few early October weeks as an injury report fixtures. IDP leaguers will need to make other plans this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell came out of the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys dealing with hamstring and quad injuries. He starts out the week as an estimated DNP. Campbell will likely need to practice in some capacity in order to play Week 8 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Zack Baun (concussion) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: He cleared concussion protocol and will, judging by online comments about the Eagles offense, spend 40 minutes Sunday morning throwing himself at Jaguars running backs who are trying to kill clock. Jihaad Campbell (knee) was also cleared.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles LB Zack Baun (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: This is Baun’s second limited practice this week. Fellow LB Jihaad Campbell (knee) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and S Marcus Epps (groin) remain sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Zack Baun (concussion) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Baun entered the league’s concussion protocol last week and was unable to practice at all. His return means he is making progress through the protocol and should be able to play in Week 5. On the other hand, fellow lineback Jihaad Campbell is not expected to practice with an unknown injury. It’s still a net positive injury report for Philly, but far from ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles LB Jihaad Campbell (shoulder) is expected to be ready for training camp after undergoing shoulder surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell also underwent surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder back in March 2025. He dealt with a triceps injury in-season last year. Per Eagles DC Vic Fangio, Campbell is doing well and might have a chance to participate in a limited capacity later in organized team activities. Campbell totaled 62 tackles, 14 quarterback pressures, two pass breakups and one interception in his rookie season last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles RB Will Shipley (oblique) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Shipley should resume No. 2 running back duties and can be stashed as a high-upside player in re-draft formats. Stud RT Lane Johnson (stinger) practiced in full on Thursday and Friday. The Eagles lost star OLB Nolan Smith (triceps) to injured reserve earlier this week. He will be eligible to return after missing four games. They got good news on LB Zack Baun (knee), LB Jihaad Campbell (triceps) and backup QB Tanner McKee (right thumb), though. All three are good to go. Unfortunately, CB Adoree’ Jackson (groin) is doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles LB Zack Baun (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Baun, LB Jihaad Campbell (triceps) and Adoree’ Jackson (groin) all took the day off on Wednesday, which was slightly alarming given the Eagles’ other defensive injuries. Eagles OLB Nolan Smith (triceps) and CB Jakorian Bennett were placed on injured reserve yesterday. Baun, Campbell and Jackson should all be good to go for Week 4, barring setbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles LB Zack Baun (knee) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Baun missed Wednesday with a knee issue, his first instance of an injury in 2025. Also out on Wednesday were LB Jihaad Campbell (triceps) and Adoree’ Jackson (groin). The Eagles’ front seven has been driven by Baun and Campbell’s contributions and absences in Week 4 would leave the middle of the field open for the Buccaneers. If Jackson misses time, Kelee Ringo is next in line for opportunities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles signed No. 31 overall pick LB Jihaad Campbell to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Second-round safety Andrew Mukuba is the only unsigned draft pick for Philly. Campbell is currently recovering from surgery related to the torn labrum he suffered in his final collegiate season. The versatile defender has been observing the inside linebackers in Philly’s offseason program, giving us some idea of where he will play to start his career. After trading up one spot to land Campbell in the first round, it’s safe to assume the Eagles will ramp up his workload as soon as he is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 8 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley gave a cryptic response when asked if he would play earlier in the day, ultimately ready to gut out multiple injuries as the Eagles continue to trudge forward in an injury-decimated season. The veteran back added that the injuries are both something he will need to manage throughout the game but that he feels as if he can play through them. That leaves fantasy managers in a sticky situation, likely forced to start Barkley if he’s on the roster. Barkley is a middling RB2 in a difficult matchup on the ground against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: After being a DNP in each of the Eagles’ first two practices of the week, it’s far too early to be confident that Barkley will suit up on Sunday night against the Commanders. That said, his return to the field is still an encouraging sign for the Eagles, whose backfield is suddenly among the most banged up in the league. We will check back in when the Eagles announce Barkley’s Week 8 status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this ends up being a game-time decision, which could prove frustrating for fantasy managers. We should know more on his availability in the next few hours.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: This doesn’t look ideal. Barkley practiced all week leading up to his return, and at this point he doesn’t even have a limited session ahead of Sunday’s game with the Commanders. There’s probably not a zero percent chance that Barkley is playing, but at this point the best Barkley-reliant managers can likely hope for is a questionable tag on Friday. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue would be in line to form some sort of committee if Barkley can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley was predictably a non-participant after re-aggravating his hamstring injury and additionally injuring his back in Week 7 against the Cowboys. Despite the injuries, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Barkley said his hamstring “came out great” and he doesn’t believe his back will keep him out. With every other Eagles running back suffering long-term injuries, Barkley is attempting to gut out his injury issues. Given his re-aggravation last week, it is well within the range of outcomes for Barkley to see limited snaps in Week 8 against the Commanders. His motivation to play makes us think he is on track to be active on Sunday but Barkley is a risky RB2 as he deals with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (back) is questionable to return in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Things seemed to be going well for the veteran back in his first game since injuring his hamstring in Week 4 until the second quarter. Barkley was in and out of the lineup through that second frame before being seen on the sideline getting his hip worked on by the training staff, with what was later deemed a back issue. He continued to play through discomfort into the fourth quarter before the team declared him questionable to return with a new injury than the one that cost him two games. Barkley looked spry during his time on the field, gaining 62 yards and a touchdown on seven carries while adding nine yards on two receptions prior to departing. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status in the coming days. Dameon Pierce would be in line to once again operate as a borderline workhorse, should Barkley’s injury prove significant, considering the lack of depth in the backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is active for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley returns from a two-game absence, which could not have come at a better time for a team missing its starting quarterback and top two wide receivers. The divisional tilt against the Cowboys is a game of great importance to each team as they look up at the division-leading Giants as we approach the half way point in the regular season. Although Barkley could see his touches monitored in his first game in three weeks, fantasy gamers that waited him out through the weekend are likely forced to ride with the veteran for lack of other options. Inactive for the Eagles are OLB Nolan Smith, WR DeVonta Smith, WR Dontayvion Wicks, QB Cole Payton, DB Michael Carter II, and OL Jake Majors.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is “trending toward playing” in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Garafolo pointed out that Barkley isn’t a guarantee to play on Monday, but said “everything is looking good” for Barkley to make his return. Barkley was updated to a full participant in practice on Saturday but still carries a questionable tag into Monday night’s game against the Cowboys. While it’s always good to have a backup plan in case Barkley can’t go, we would be surprised if he doesn’t suit up, given his practice status all week and this latest report from Garafolo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is questionable for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Although getting in a full practice Saturday, the Eagles head into Monday’s game against the Cowboys with Barkley listed as questionable following a two-game absence. Fantasy managers have a decision considering the Eagles play in Week 7’s final game on Monday Night Football, with no clear fall back options should he be unable to play. It would seem prudent to make alternate plans at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: We had really hoped to see Barkley practice in full today. He still has a chance to take the field when the Eagles face the Cowboys in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, but he is inching toward a questionable designation right now. Upgrading to full tomorrow would increase his odds of playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley has been sidelined since straining his hamstring in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the division-rival Giants. He is now on track to make his triumphant return against the division-rival Cowboys in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game. The Eagles threw the ball at an 84 percent rate in neutral situations with Tanner McKee at the helm last week. Barkley’s expected return will allow them to run the ball more often, though they will likely remain a pass-first offense. Although Barkley’s rushing workload may decrease, his passing game involvement could get a serious boost, benefiting him in the box score. Barkley was officially limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and has not practiced since the build up to Week 6. As with colleague DeVonta Smith, Wicks enters next week questionable to play and with the Eagles having a Week 10 bye, we wouldn’t be surprised if Wicks sat that game out as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has not practiced since before Week 6’s loss to the Panthers and should be seen as doubtful heading into Friday’s practice session. We’d be surprised if he played in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were estimated DNPs for the Eagles’ walkthrough. Both players missed Week 7 against the Cowboys and start off on the wrong side of questionable to open Week 8. Smith and Wicks will need to at least get a limited practice session in before they can be considered as potential fantasy options against the Commanders. With Britain Covey (knee) also DNP, the receiving corps is sparse. If neither can go, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown get a boost from the WR group while TE Dallas Goedert becomes the No. 1 pass-catcher in the Eagles offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined, life will not be easy for Tanner McKee on Monday evening, even in a plus matchup. Wicks drew some summer hype as a well-paid reclamation project for the Eagles, but he has caught more than three passes only two times all season and has not reached 70 yards since Week 2. He is a poor hold in 12-team leagues with five-man benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has been banged up for weeks, and the Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said Wicks might miss the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks swaps out his multi-week hamstring injury for an ankle injury. He managed to play through it in Week 6 against the Panthers after meeting with the training staff. We expect him to face the Cowboys on Monday night, but he is just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks wasn’t much of a factor in this one. Tanner McKee seemed far more comfortable throwing to DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, which left few targets for Wicks. Initial reports have Wicks playing on 40 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 32 of their 52 dropbacks, which was actually fewer than Makai Lemon and only five more than Darius Cooper. Some of that could be because Wicks grabbed at his ankle and left the field after a tackle in the second half. He was able to return to the game later in the half, but he missed a few plays while being tended to by trainers. With McKee at quarterback, it’s hard to trust Wicks in fantasy, regardless of matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Apparently, Wicks’ day off on Thursday was only a rest day. The Eagles’ veteran wide receiver was limited on Wednesday and practiced fully today. Wicks played through the injury last week, posting a 5/63 receiving line with DeVonta Smith sidelined. Smith is back this week. Wicks is a boom-bust FLEX starter, catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks played through the hamstring injury in Week 5 and may have made it worse. Downgrading to a DNP on Thursday is a bad sign. He is unlikely to play at this time, and if active, he would be prone to re-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: He has not practiced since Week 6. It’s hard to count on Smith to be up for Week 9, though we obviously can’t say anything beyond him being questionable. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye and it might be preferable for them at this point if Smith sat through that — though that is just our speculation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith was not spotted at practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Assuming there’s not a non-media practice portion that adds him to the report, Smith will enter Friday as fairly unlikely to play. We’ll see if he can get on the practice field on Friday. A limited session might get him on to the questionable line. Smith last practiced ahead of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were estimated DNPs for the Eagles’ walkthrough. Both players missed Week 7 against the Cowboys and start off on the wrong side of questionable to open Week 8. Smith and Wicks will need to at least get a limited practice session in before they can be considered as potential fantasy options against the Commanders. With Britain Covey (knee) also DNP, the receiving corps is sparse. If neither can go, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown get a boost from the WR group while TE Dallas Goedert becomes the No. 1 pass-catcher in the Eagles offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said he got “the sense” that DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Like Thursday, Smith was sidelined for Friday’s practice. The Eagles have been managing his practice reps and pulled him out for multiple drives in their Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night, giving Smith an extra day to rest. Consider him highly questionable to play at this time. McLane adds that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could also sit out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles held Smith out for multiple drives in Week 6 against the Panthers, in his first game back from a multi-week hamstring injury. He was also dealing with a toe issue. The latter injury is now behind him, and we suspect that his day off today is just a veteran maintenance day. He should be good to go for the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith caught 7-of-14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith was easily the focal point of the passing attack after coming back from injury. He saw the most targets of anybody on the team by six, but many of them were not catchable. However, Tanner McKee kept taking shots down the field, and he made a beautiful pass to Smith in the end zone for a touchdown. The game itself might not be pretty when McKee is under center, but it seems like Smith is going to see the volume to continue producing solid fantasy value. He’s a low-end WR2 in a good matchup against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) is not on the final injury report for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith sat out on Wednesday, but practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday before upgrading to full on Friday. Smith told media members earlier today that he is “good,” and that the toe injury is not an issue. Jalen Hurts (blood clot) is out indefinitely, so Smith will be working with pocket-passing backup Tanner McKee. The Panthers are currently without both of their starting perimeter cornerbacks. It might be a bit uncomfortable, but Smith is a WR2 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said he is “still hearing optimism he’ll play Sunday. We’ll see.” Given his follow-up comment, it doesn’t seem like he shares the organization’s optimism. If active, Smith would be catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee. Jalen Hurts is sidelined indefinitely by a blood clot. McKee, a pocket passer, could lock onto Smith, keeping him in the WR2 tier if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Devonta Smith (hamstring/toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith was already reported to be working off to the side on Wednesday, but he now adds a toe injury to his existing hamstring injury on the official practice report. Given he is not practicing yet and a new injury is added to his designation, Smith is currently trending in the wrong direction for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and would seem to be trending towards playing. With Carnell Tate down this week, Elic Ayomanor is probably the Titans dart throw wideout for the desperate against the Bengals if you’re choosing between him or Ridley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) returned to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley did not practice once last week. He was listed as questionable on Friday but never appeared likely to suit up and was eventually ruled out ahead of kickoff. Elic Ayomanor popped up for 44 yards on three catches and seven targets in his absence. Ridley’s return will prevent Ayomanor from building any momentum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday, and we’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable. Not that you were thinking about playing him anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Firmly off the fantasy radar when healthy, Ridley downgraded from a limited session on Wednesday and does not seem likely to play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The 31-year-old player has a hip injury. Ridley mostly runs cardio and game day and is not fantasy-relevant at this time. Were he to sit, Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike could get more playing time — which would be a positive outcome for the offense as a whole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Is this doing anything for anybody? Ridley had a 23-yarder to open the game and vanished thereafter. He has not cracked more than two catches or three targets all year and does not need to be in fantasy consideration in the vast, vast majority of leagues.
