https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley failed to catch his only target in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley has been held without a catch in 2-of-3 games this year. He’s losing routes to Elic Ayomanor and not earning targets when on the field. He can be cut even in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-2 targets for 35 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The grabs were Ridley’s first two of the season. He also cost the Titans with a 15-yard personal foul penalty. Although it’s good to see Ridley’s Week 1 doughnut was something of an aberration, it’s not like he can be counted on for high-volume days going forward as the Titans sort out the rotation in their revamped skill corps. Despite his pedigree, Ridley can be safely left on 12-team league waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley was not targeted in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley’s 25 routes run were good for third-most among Titans receivers in Sunday’s loss, but the 31-year-old receiver went without a target despite his team trailing the entire game. Any hope that Ridley would improve on last year’s 17-303-0 performance will need to be put on hold for now, as Ridley and the Titans offense as a whole struggled mightily in the season opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll said the team’s downfield passing attack has to improve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Cam Ward’s preseason has been as bad or even worse than his rookie campaign. Ward in last week’s preseason game against Seattle completed eight of his 12 attempts for 69 yards. His average depth of target on completed passes this preseason sits at a meager 1.2 . Carnell Tate, meanwhile, has been targeted five times on his 23 preseason routes and does not have a reception to show for it. Daboll has been somewhat defensive this month when asked about Ward’s immense struggles after working on basic fundamentals with the second-year QB in the offseason. Ward, one of the most inaccurate passers in recent NFL history, is unlikely to support more than one fantasy-viable pass catcher in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears had three DNPs and has not practiced since last Thursday. Michael Carter filled down as the third-down back last week, though all that actually meant is that Tony Pollard got full-time workload. We expect that to continue in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, Spears looks unlikely to play on Sunday. He also missed Week 7 with the knee issue. Tony Pollard racked up 28 touches and scored three rushing touchdowns. While we’re not banking on another multi-score outing anytime soon, his role alone is worth an RB2 ranking if Spears remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears had been playing through the knee issue for a few weeks before being sidelined because of it in Week 7. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Tony Pollard will handle the bulk of the backfield touches again this week. He remains a volume-based RB2 versus the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears has been active off a questionable line twice since Week 4. We’d imagine he’d get there again after a limited Friday session. The touch upside just isn’t there for him to be more than a deep-league FLEX play at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears notched a one-yard carry and seven-yard reception in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears’ two touches were a new season low, though he’s now been held to three or fewer in three of the past four weeks. The Titans have decided Tony Pollard is more of an every-down back than committee member, erasing what had been low-end FLEX status for his “1B” backfield partner. Despite his supposed contingency value, Spears is droppable if you find yourself in a roster crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears is active for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: He was questionable after a full practice, but will play against the Colts as a reasonable-if-unexciting FLEX option. Inactive for the Titans are S Kevin Winston Jr., CB Alontae Taylor (coach’s decision), RB Nick Singleton, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, DL Jordan Elliott and DT Jackie Marshall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears didn’t practice Thursday but was a full-go on Friday. He’ll be a sketchy FLEX option against the Colts in Week 6 assuming he plays; it sure does seem like he will after a full session.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It was a surprising downgrade from Wednesday’s limited session, putting Spears’ status for Week 6 into real question. If he sits, we’re not entirely sure which Titans third-string back would get breather duties. Kalel Mullings, who was a practice squad activation, got the only non-Tony Pollard/Spears snap in Week 5. Nicholas Singleton and Michael Carter are also both on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: The Titans’ receiving specialist has been an injury report staple thus far, though he has previously been listed with an ankle issue. An early-week limited session puts him on track to play, though he is only relevant in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is out for Week 8 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate’s game-day designation comes on the heels of three missed practices this week. His absence leaves behind an alpha’s target share to go claimed by the remaining pass catchers, most notable of whom is slot man Wan’Dale Robinson. Robinson also draws the top matchup on paper against he inside-funnel nature of the Cincinnati defense, appearing to have a clear path to leading the team in targets and receiving. Fantasy managers can start Robinson as a viable WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate was a DNP all week and is at risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Bengals. The team will announce his official status shortly, but if he is unable to go, Wan’Dale Robinson and Elic Ayomanor would be the early favorites to see an uptick in targets against a Bengals secondary that ranks 18th in points allowed to opposing receivers this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate has now missed two practices with the shoulder issue, making him truly questionable for Sunday’s game versus the Bengals. Tate has been operating as the Titans’ clear WR1, meaning there would be plenty of opportunities up for grabs if he can’t go. Wan’Dale Robinson could be in line for more targets, but his slot-only role doesn’t have much overlap with Tate’s job. Second-year wideout Elic Ayomanor might be the best bet to see more work if Tate is out this week, though that would only move him into the WR4 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Apparently Tate picked up the shoulder injury in Week 7’s loss to the Browns, when he caught five passes for 69 scoreless yards. If Tate is unable to practice headed into the weekend, Elic Ayomanor, who last week ran a route on 79 percent of the team’s drop backs and had 44 yards on three catches, would likely be the de factor WR1 for Tennessee. Tate has dominated air yards and targets this season and profiles as a positive regression candidate in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 5-of-7 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: It was another solid if unspectacular outing for the rookie. The Titans operated a fast-pace offense through much of the game against Cleveland, using no-huddle for long stretches of the ballgame. That seemed to put Cam Ward in some sort of rhythm — to the benefit of a few Titans skill position players. Tate now has at least six receptions in three of his past four outings. Tate, who entered the week with a 46 percent air yards share and a 25 percent target share, is an every-week starter who could be a WR3 option next week against a pass-funnel Bengals defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 6-of-7 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate’s eight-yard fourth quarter score was the first of his career. He simply beat the defense to the spot in the end zone. Although the touchdown was great, it was Tate’s 19-yard grab early in the third frame that was the highlight of the day. He skied over CB Justin Walley. Playing much better football of late even as second-year QB Cam Ward struggles to return the favor, Tate has stabilized his WR3 value and will be pushing for WR2 status with injuries mounting and bye weeks in full swing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Well, at least last week was good. He did have a 40-plus yarder pulled off the board because of a holding penalty. Next week offers a more welcoming Colts defense and Tate should have a path to low-end WR3 numbers there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (back) is active for Tennessee’s Week 5 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: The Titans had named him questionable despite Robert Saleh saying he’d play on Friday, so this outcome was no surprise. Inactive for the Titans are: RB Nick Singleton, RB Michael Carter, S Amani Hooker (concussion), CB Jaylon Jones, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE David Martin-Robinson (hamstring) and DT Jackie Marshall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (back) is good to go for Week 5 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: He was officially listed as questionable with two limited sessions on Thursday and Friday. Tate popped up on Thursday’s injury report with a back injury, but Titans coach Robert Saleh said it was just some random tightness that isn’t expected to slow him in Week 5. Tate has seen 21 targets over the last two weeks and has posted a 15-203-0 line over that span. He has some solid WR3/FLEX appeal against a Texans defense that has struggled against the pass early in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (back) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate was limited today, suggesting he suffered a back injury in practice. That is not good. He, of course, still has a chance to play, but we will have to monitor this situation closely. For now, Tate must be viewed as questionable to play in Week 5 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) will play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Like teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown, Gibbs started the week off with a missed practice before upgrading to a full participant in both sessions to end the week. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will be ready for a normal workload against the division rival Vikings Sunday. Fantasy managers are clearly starting Gibbs, regardless of matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: The return to practice comes on the heels of a missed practice Wednesday for the veteran workhorse, immediately putting fantasy managers at ease for Week 8. Managers will want to confirm his practice status Friday before making final preparations for the weekend, but it certainly appears as if Gibbs will be good to go for a normal, and massive, workload when the Lions take the field against the division rival Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 29 times for 116 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers, adding five receptions for 27 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t balk at what was an overall solid performance, but they probably would have liked to see Gibbs rush in a touchdown; the Packers were more than willing to give him one late in the fourth quarter. Gibbs intentionally fell short of the end zone twice on the Lions’ final drive to ensure Jake Bates’ game-winning field goal attempt would be the final play in regulation, which worked to the Lions’ advantage in the 20-17 win. Gibbs ripped off multiple chunk gains in this one, with 13 of his 29 carries going for five or more yards. He did lose a fumble deep inside Packers territory near the end of the second quarter, which likely cost his team at least three points, but as usual, Gibbs was a big reason why the Lions constantly found themselves in position to win. It’s worth noting that on his final play of the game, Gibbs appeared to suffer a knee injury when his left leg bent awkwardly as he attempted to stop and fall to the turf to keep the clock running, but he was able to jog off under his own power. We would ultimately expect him to be fine, but his practice status will be one to monitor this week as the Lions prepare to take on the Vikings. Assuming he is good to go, Gibbs will be an obvious RB1 candidate next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding five receptions for 56 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs scored twice today, bringing his career touchdown total up to 57, breaking the NFL record set by former Lions RB Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns scored by a player under 25 years old. The exceptionally talented player gets a boost from his sharp coaching staff, who continue to maximize Gibbs’ strengths. OC Drew Petzing dialed up a trick-play screen pass for Gibbs after the two-minute warning, in which Gibbs took the handoff, pitched it to Amon-Ra St. Brown, who pitched it back to Jared Goff, who then chucked it back to Gibbs with three offensive linemen in front of him on the left side of the field. An 18-yard gain ensued. Gibbs later produced a season-long 22-yard run. Although he scored two touchdowns today, he could have had a third. On the Lions’ ninth drive, Gibbs got two chances from the one-yard line on the ninth drive before the coaching staff greenlit a successful QB sneak for Goff. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but he returns to the top of the running back ranks against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 15 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers, adding 31 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs had eclipsed 100 combined yards against all three opponents to start the season before the Panthers held him largely in check, with fantasy’s top asset cashing in on a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to avoid a disastrous outing. The two teams were knotted at 16 entering the half but it was the Panthers that dictated terms following the break, winning the time of possession battle by over six minutes. Gibbs maintained an elite workload by seeing all but two backfield opportunities and every available carry on the evening, keeping his fantasy value sky-high ahead of a potential shootout against the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 20 times for 99 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets, adding seven catches for 65 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Per usual, Gibbs was dynamic with the ball in his hands, making defenders miss at will while racking up 27 touches. He put an exclamation point on the game with an 11-yard touchdown grab that eventually gave Detroit the win. He’s already up to six touchdowns this year and has no fewer than five catches and 113 yards from scrimmage in his three appearances. With the ability to crush on the ground and through the air, Gibbs is an unstoppable fantasy force. He remains the RB1 overall heading into his Week 4 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 16 times for 52 yards in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills, adding 61 yards and a touchdown on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs was effectively the entire game plan out of the gates, scoring the team’s only first-half touchdown from 11 yards out in the second quarter. He would be used far less after the break as the Lions attempted to come back from multiple 17-point deficits, although the six receptions on eight targets and a touchdown through the air helped push his counting stats into clear RB1 territory for the second consecutive week to start the season. Fantasy managers that were lucky enough to secure the 1.01 in drafts this offseason are sure to be content with the early returns. Gibbs will once again be an elite fantasy option when the Lions host the Jets in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints, adding five catches for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: As expected, the Lions elevated Gibbs to a true workhorse role sans David Montgomery and he never looked back. He ceded a grand total of three touches to backup Sione Vaki. Gibbs logged career highs in touches and carries. Despite this, Gibbs still cruised past 5.4 yards per carry, consistently gashing the Saints for chunk gains. To no one’s surprise, Gibbs is the runaway favorite to be the RB1 overall this year. He will hold that spot in the Week 2 rankings when he takes on Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: The Athletic’s Robert Mays said new Lions OC Drew Petzing spent “the first couple of weeks after he got the job” learning the offense from QB Jared Goff.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: The Lions are retaining “all” of last year’s play-calling verbiage, and “it was on Drew Petzing to learn the offense,” not the other way around. Goff apparently “had as much of a hand in getting Petzing familiar with the offense as the offensive staff did.” Mays believes these developments speak to the command, agency and autonomy that Goff possesses at this stage in his career. We agree. For those who were concerned about the Lions scrapping the tactics that coach Dan Campbell employed as the Lions’ play caller in Weeks 10-18 last year, it sounds like those concepts aren’t going anywhere. Will Petzing be allowed to add his own elements to that playbook? Yes, we assume so. At the end of the day, this year’s offense could look a lot like last year’s fantasy-friendly unit, though. Draft accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) will not play in Detroit’s Week 8 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Dan Campbell said Joseph has been used only in individual and group practices so far and that he’s handled that well. Next week he’ll get in on real practice. Joseph probably stands a decent chance of being active for Week 9 assuming he acclimates well to that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph dealt with a cartilage issue in his knee last year and has spent the entirety of 2026 working his way back from it. As of a month ago, Dan Campbell didn’t sound optimistic that Joseph would be able to play at any point this year. Joseph is currently on the PUP list. His return to practice means the team has opened his 21-day practice window. We expect them to use most of the window to ramp Joseph up to full speed, but it’s still a great sign for the playmaking safety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) is hopeful he’ll be available later this season, reports NFL Insider Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Lions HC Dan Campbell didn’t sound optimistic about the prospects of Joseph, who is dealing with a potentially career-threatening knee cartilage issue, helping the Lions this year. In two separate media appearances in the last week, Campbell said that there wasn’t anything he could say about Joseph that would make anyone “feel good.” Pelissero reported Saturday morning that Joseph, who missed all of training camp and hasn’t played since last year’s Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, is hopeful he’ll be available to help the Lions down the stretch. While that may be the case, whether Joseph is able to return to play this year remains an open question. Without Joseph and S Brian Branch (Achilles), the Lions are severely shorthanded in the backend heading into Week 3’s home matchup against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said S Brian Branch (Achilles) “has a chance” to resume practicing sooner than S Kerby Joseph (knee), “but it won’t be this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Campbell spoke in a dejected tone when asked about the Lions’ safety duo returning to practice, particularly when discussing Joseph’s outlook. Campbell said Joseph did not suffer a setback, but stopped short of fully explaining the situation. It sounds like Joseph’s recovery stalled. The training staff was focused on strengthening Joseph’s knee, “but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do.” The Lions will not ask Joseph to play until he gets his knee as strong as it can possibly be, “and he feels comfortable.” Branch could return to practice in the coming weeks, but at this point, Joseph’s career status seems like it might be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph will begin the season on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph is still nursing a knee injury that hampered him last season. He will remain on the PUP list to open the season, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions placed S Kerby Joseph on the active/PUP list with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Just yesterday, Joseph implied via social media that he would avoid the physically unable to perform list. So much for that. Joseph dealt with a recurring knee issue for the entire 2025 season, which was first reported on at the end of July 2025, roughly three months after the Lions made him the NFL’s highest-paid safety. Given Joseph’s post, one imagines he has a chance to resume practicing relatively soon, but only time will tell. Branch suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 14 last year. As of June 13th, Lions coach Dan Campbell said there was no timetable for his return. The Lions also placed TE Tyler Conklin on the physically unable to perform list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) implied that he’ll avoid the PUP list ahead of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Lions veterans won’t report to training camp until Monday, but Joseph implied in a tweet on Saturday morning that he’ll avoid the PUP list. In response to a question about going on the PUP list, the 25-year-old safety wrote, “How much y’all wanna bet I’m not on there.” It’s not much, but it’s the first positive signal for Joseph’s health in quite some time. After missing the last 11 games of the 2025 season with a knee injury, Joseph was held out of minicamp. In early June, Dan Campbell told reporters he didn’t know what to expect from Joseph this season. Joseph started all 17 games in 2024, when he had a league-leading nine interceptions and was named a first-team All-Pro. The former third-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft signed a massive four-year, $86 million extension prior to last season. Joseph’s 20 interceptions are the second-most all-time for a safety in his first four seasons (Ed Reed, 22). A healthy Joseph would be a game-changer for the Lions defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters there’s no timetable on S Brian Branch (Achilles) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Campbell said that Branch hasn’t had any setbacks in his recovery from a torn Achilles, but wouldn’t put a timeline on the 24-year-old safety’s eventual return. Branch attended practice in a T-shirt and shorts on Thursday. Campbell jokingly set the timetable for Branch to return in December, just so the media would stop asking about it. Christian Izien and Chuck Clark continue to take the first-team safety reps for the Lions in practice with Branch and Kerby Joseph (knee) sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters “I honestly don’t know” what to expect from S Kerby Joseph this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph was named a first-team All-Pro in 2024, but played only six games last year with what’s turned into a debilitating knee injury. Campbell noted at Thursday’s press conference that Joseph continues to build strength in his knee and receive treatment, but the team isn’t going to push him until they absolutely have to. Detroit acquired veteran safeties Chuck Clark and Christian Izien this offseason while retaining Avonte Maddox and Thomas Harper to give themselves options with Joseph and Brain Branch (Achilles) on the mend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said the team is prioritizing S Kerby Joseph’s (knee) 2026 availability over participation in spring workouts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Both of the Lions’ starting safeties, Joseph and Brian Branch (Achilles), are rehabbing significant injuries. While it would be great to get one or both of them back on the field this spring, Campbell does not want to hurry his injured stars back and risk re-injury. Late in April, Lions general manager Brad Holmes said both safeties are “trending in the right direction.” However, last we heard, Branch was not expected to be ready to play in Week 1. Joseph will likely sit out spring practices, but seemingly has a chance to participate in training camp. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown started the week off with an absence before logging consecutive full sessions to end the week or preparations, ultimately removed from the injury report entirely heading into the weekend. He should be good to go for a normal workload against the stingy Minnesota defense, where fantasy managers can start him with confidence as a WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: The upgrade from “DNP” to a full session indicates St. Brown will be fine for a normal workload when the Lions face off against the Vikings Sunday, easing fantasy managers’ collective minds after the star receiver was not present at practice Wednesday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on Friday’s injury report, but it certainly appears as if the team will have their veteran alpha for the divisional tilt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Monday that St. Brown would likely miss today’s practice, so this isn’t much of a surprise. Campbell also told reporters that St. Brown “should be good” for Week 8, so we’re not panicking just yet. St. Brown is one of the few players who can suit up after missing an entire week of practice. Even a DNP tomorrow wouldn’t be the end of the world. For now, fantasy managers can treat St. Brown as a WR1, but a backup plan should be in place. Jameson Williams would vault into the WR1 ranks if St. Brown misses Week 8 versus the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) “should be good” to play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown is dealing with what sounds like a minor ankle injury after Week 7’s win over the Packers. Campbell said he could likely be held out of practice on Wednesday before the team begins ramping him up on Thursday, but tempered any optimism by adding, “We’ll see when we get there.” The 4-2 Lions are playing host to the undefeated Vikings in a game that could end up deciding the winners of the NFC North later in the season. Unless this injury is more serious than Campbell is letting on, we would expect St. Brown to be on the field and operating as a high-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 9-of-11 targets for 153 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: The Sun God didn’t find the end zone in this one, but he did rip off multiple big gains, which included plays of 28 and 40 yards on the Lions’ first two drives — both of which ended with points. St. Brown’s 11 targets led all Lions’ pass-catchers in this one, and his 153 receiving yards are good for the fifth-most he has had in any game in his career. It’s the first time in his career that ARSB has gone for 140-plus yards but failed to score a touchdown, but this was easily one of his best games to date this season. St. Brown hasn’t scored since Week 3’s game against the Jets, but he has gone for 69 or more yards in each of his last three games while seeing 11 targets in every outing. He continues to be as steady a fantasy asset as there is at receiver, and will be in the WR1 mix in Week 8 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-11 targets for 69 yards in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: Lions coach Dan Campbell tasked St. Brown with punt return duties (2/36) after Tom Kennedy got hurt. While St. Brown looked great weaving through traffic, his first return nearly ended in a lost fumble, but a teammate dove on the loose ball, bailing him out after it was punched out of St. Brown possession. St. Brown nearly had a 43-yard touchdown on a sideline play-action shot on the Lions’ seventh drive, but he couldn’t quite get his hands on it. He almost bagged short scores via out routes on the Lions’ eighth and ninth drives, but his coverage defender effectively challenged the pass on the first and the pass was just out of his reach on the second. He had a nice 36-yard catch-and-run on the eighth drive and nearly nabbed another explosive gain on the sixth drive, but Sam LaPorta accidentally knocked him down 11 yards downfield after St. Brown leapt over a downed Cardinals defender. He had another fumble recovered by a teammate after snagging a pass on a crosser. The Lions’ stud wide receiver will be an elite WR1 against the Packers following the Lions’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 8-of-11 targets for 75 yards in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: It was quite the disappointing outing for the fantasy darling considering the Panthers were without their top two corners, with opposing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero dialing up consistent pressure that caused quarterback Jared Goff fits throughout the evening. Two of Goff’s incompletions that were directed at St. Brown were batted down at the line of scrimmage, ultimately enough to keep St. Brown out of the end zone for the first time this season. St. Brown remains a top-tier WR1 ahead of a potential shootout against the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 4-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown couldn’t get much going other than a handful of check-downs in this game, but he saved his fantasy backers with an end zone fade for six to close the first half. Despite the quiet showing, St. Brown still led the team in targets, tied with Jahmyr Gibbs at eight apiece. He’s now up to five touchdowns on the season. St. Brown isn’t quite in the WR1 overall mix right now, but he’s not far behind for his Week 4 matchup with Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 9-of-13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown did not catch his first pass until six minutes left in the second quarter but was the primary cog of the offense after the break as the Lions worked to overcome multiple 17-point deficits. He found paint for the first time on the team’s first possession after the break before adding a second in the two-minute drill from 27 yards out. St. Brown now has 209 yards and four touchdowns on 19 receptions through two games an looks every bit of the elite WR1 fantasy managers invested a first-round pick into this offseason. Although volume through the air might be more difficult to come by in Week 3, St. Brown remains a top-tier WR1 when the Lions host the Jets in Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 10-of-14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: The Lions couldn’t get their deep passing game going, but that’s not an issue for St. Brown. He simply racked up a 36 percent target share including plenty of red zone and work and paid off in a big way for fantasy managers. The Saints’ frantic comeback also pushed the pace of the game, juicing the fantasy scores of everyone involved. With another shootout versus the Bills on tap for Week 2, St. Brown will remain near the top of the wide receiver ranks next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) did not practice Friday and is questionable to play in Week 8 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers managed back-to-back limited sessions to begin the week of preparation but was downgraded to a “DNP” Friday, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for Week 8 against the Colts. An absence could require additional offensive snaps for two-way player Travis Hunter and a slight uptick in route rate for Brian Thomas Jr and Josh Cameron. This is one to monitor for fantasy managers of all Jacksonville pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has put together a pair of limited sessions out of the bye and seems likely to play against the Colts in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr.'s disappearing act has left Meyers capable of putting up WR3 lines, but the Colts may not be opponent enough to force that kind of production out of Meyers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The hamstring issue is new, but it’s not one we expected to prevent Meyers from playing. A limited practice this early in the week is typically maintenance, especially midway through the season. Meyers will remains a fantasy WR4 for his Week 8 matchup with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 5-of-10 targets for 83 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: It’s his highest target total of the season and the first time Meyers has managed 10 targets since Week 14 of the 2025 season. No touchdown here, but Meyers is a fine real-life third receiver who has mostly been left to the FLEX life in Jacksonville. He enters the bye as someone who can be dropped in shallow leagues in a roster crunch, but also someone solidly in the top 50 wideouts in the league on a good offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 37 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been held to two and three catches over his past two games. It’s probably not a coincidence that Brenton Strange leads the team with 14 catches during Meyers’ two-game slump. Meyers is still operating as the Jags’ WR2, but his role will come down to matchup nuances on a week-to-week basis. He is sliding back into the WR5 fantasy ranks ahead of his Week 6 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 3-of-4 targets for 33 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers continues to see the most snaps among all Jaguars wide receivers as Liam Coen utilizes him as both an outside target and willing blocker. He was second in targets against the Bengals as Trevor Lawrence threw just 23 passes on the day. Meyers now seems to be ahead of Brian Thomas Jr. on the wide receiver pecking order and is WR3 fantasy play for a London game against the Eagles in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: He should be trusted as a low-end WR3/FLEX play against the Bengals. Meyers has cleared the injury report with this thumb listing three times in three weeks, though he was questionable in Week 2. It clearly isn’t bothering him enough to impact his play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: No real surprises here; Meyers has played through this thumb listing in two consecutive weeks and will likely be removed from the injury report on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been playing through the thumb issue all year and that won’t change in Week 4. With Brian Thomas Jr.'s role disappearing, Meyers has quietly emerged as the No. 2 receiver on one of the league’s best offenses. He remains a solid FLEX play for his Week 4 date with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 7-of-8 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers made the most of his opportunities in a revenge game against his former team. After totaling three catches for 68 yards in his first two games of the season, Meyers led the Jaguars in targets and grabs against New England, catching one of Trevor Lawrence’s three touchdown throws. Meyers entered the game with a meager six percent target share and a 11 percent air yards share. He could have some flex viability in Week 4 against a middling Bengals secondary that gave up a big day to Steelers pass catchers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is out for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was unable to practice all week as he tends to a knee injury, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 Friday. It will go down as his second consecutive absence, with his next opportunity to take the field to come in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) missed practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was absent for the second consecutive day, requiring some level of participation Friday to avoid a designation for the team’s showdown against the Bills in Week 8. The team got good news on other fronts as Lamar Jackson, Ioane Vega, Kyle Hamilton, and Roquan Smith were all present Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Neither did fellow Ravens safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who is also dealing with a knee injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said a few of his players were dealing with “after game type things” when asked about Hamilton, so it doesn’t sound like this is a major issue. Still, with multiple members of the secondary banged up, this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Ravens agreed to terms with S Jaylinn Hawkins, formerly of the Patriots, on a two-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins signed with the Pats as a backup two years ago. He was elevated to a starting role in 2025 and put some of his best play on tape. Hawkins totaled six pass breakups, four interceptions, and 1.5 sacks across 15 games. He will likely serve as Jesse Minter’s third safety in Baltimore’s new defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Patriots released S Jabrill Peppers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Peppers has $4.32 million in guaranteed money remaining on his contract for this season. The 29-year-old safety started 26 games over the last three seasons with the Patriots. New England could be looking to start Jaylinn Hawkins and rookie Craig Woodson now, according to ESPN’s Mike Reiss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Patriots re-signed S Jaylinn Hawkins to a one-year, $2.25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins will handle backup safety duties while primarily contributing on special teams. He earned a 69.5 PFF special teams grade last year, though he does not return punts nor kicks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Chargers claimed S Jaylinn Hawkins off waivers from the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was primarily a special teams contributor for Atlanta to start the season. He saw a handful of defensive snaps in each of his first three games but has only played on defense one time in the past three weeks. Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the Chargers were not the only team to put in a claim on Hawkins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: The Falcons waived S Jaylinn Hawkins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was a 2020 fourth-round pick by the Falcons, starting 16 games in 2022. He has four career interceptions and was in the last year of his rookie contract, but Hawkins has now been cut loose by Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Falcons placed rookie S Jaylinn Hawkins on the reserve/COVID list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins (6'0/208) was a highly recruited wide receiver in high school but transitioned to Cal’s secondary after a redshirt year. He was a three-year starter and earned an All-Pac 12 honorable mention as a redshirt senior. He has racked up 10 interceptions over the last three seasons, but he is a below-average tackler and makes too many gambles for a free safety. Hawkins was a projected undrafted free agent and The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s 30th ranked safety in the 2020 NFL Draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Falcons selected Cal S Jaylinn Hawkins with the No. 134 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins (6'0/208) was a highly recruited wide receiver in high school, but transitioned to the secondary at Cal after redshirting. He was a three-year starter and earned an All-Pac 12 honorable mention as a redshirt senior. He has racked up 10 interceptions over the last three seasons, but he is a below-average tackler and makes too many gambles for a free safety. Hawkins was a projected undrafted free agent and The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s 30th ranked safety in the 2020 NFL Draft. Most considered him as a special teamer. The Falcons seem to be expecting more.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: Smith upgraded his level of participation with each practice this week, starting with an absence before moving to limited and, finally, a full session. He appears to be ready for a normal workload in the interior of the Baltimore defense, a welcome development for the Ravens as they prepare to face the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) and Vega Ioane (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: Both players missed practice Wednesday, with their return Thursday a good step in the right direction for their availability in a marquee matchup against the Bills in Week 8. Quarterback Lamar Jackson and safety-linebacker Kyle Hamilton were also present at practice Thursday as the team inches closer to full strength.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: Smith was one of several Ravens defenders to miss today’s session, though we’re expecting some of them to get back on the field later in the week. Smith has one interception, one forced fumble, and two sacks across seven games this year. We’re already expecting a shootout between the Ravens and Bills on Sunday, but Smith missing the contest would certainly increase the odds of fireworks on offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Ravens S Kyle Hamilton (groin) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: Neither are CB Chidobe Awuzie (hamstring), ILB Roquan Smith (hamstring), or CB Marlon Humphrey (illness) — and outside of Humphrey missing Wednesday’s practice all four of those players got in full sessions all week. Baltimore’s defense finally looks to mostly be recovered from their early October swoon. Will they actually play better in Week 8? That’s the real question.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey (illness) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: The Ravens’ defensive health is improving, though it still lacks a capable pass rush. CB Chidobe Awuzie (hamstring) is practicing in full, as are S Kyle Hamilton (groin) and LB Roquan Smith (hamstring). This unit was one to target for fantasy purposes pre-bye, in Weeks 1-6, and will likely remain fantasy-friendly until it improves its defensive-front personnel. This week’s results against the Bears are worth watching.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Roquan Smith (hamstring) said he expects to play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: Smith has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury but was able to log a practice in his return from the Ravens bye week. With several days to go until Sunday’s game against the Bears, Smith is clearly trending in the right direction heading into a pivotal matchup with the Ravens’ season on the line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Ravens head coach John Harbaugh said he expects QB Lamar Jackson (hamstring) to return after the team’s Week 7 bye.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: The Ravens’ offense has struggled to move the ball downfield with Jackson sidelined. The team initially turned to backup QB Cooper Rush after Jackson was injured in Week 4, but Rush was benched in-game during the Ravens’ 17-3, Week 6 loss to the Rams. From Weeks 4-6, Rush completed 34-of-52 passes for 303 yards and four interceptions, adding four rushes for minus-eight yards. Fellow backup QB Tyler Huntley completed 10-of-15 passes for 68 yards and rushed three times for 39 yards after subbing in. Jackson’s expected return should immediately improve the fantasy-scoring prospects for all Ravens starters. Harbaugh said he expects LB Roquan Smith (hamstring) to return in Week 8 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Ravens LB Roquan Smith (hamstring) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: He didn’t practice at all this week. Neither did fellow ruled-out defender Chidobe Awuzie (hamstring) — both players probably have a chance to come back after Baltimore’s Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Ravens CB Chidobe Awuzie (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: Awuzie is now on the wrong side of questionable. CB Marlon Humphrey’s calf injury and S Kyle Hamilton’s groin injury are evidently progressing, though. Hamilton’s full participation puts him firmly on track to play in Week 6 against the Rams. The Ravens have been a fantasy-friendly unit thus far. Improved health would go a long way toward reversing course. LB Roquan Smith (hamstring) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.headline: Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roquan-smi.analysis: Linebacker Roquan Smith and fellow corner Chidobe Awuzie both missed Wednesday’s practice with hamstring injuries. With Lamar Jackson unlikely to play this week, the Ravens may ultimately choose to sit the bulk of their injured players for a likely loss to the Rams on Sunday. They then get their bye week, allowing them to return close to full strength for Week 8 versus the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (knee) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday but was evasive when asked if he’d go at his locker yesterday. In the end, it would have been very impressive for him to play through a sprained MCL one week later. Ioane’s practice augurs well for his chances of playing in Week 10, at the very least. Week 9, on Thursday Night, might be too big of an ask.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) and Vega Ioane (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Both players missed practice Wednesday, with their return Thursday a good step in the right direction for their availability in a marquee matchup against the Bills in Week 8. Quarterback Lamar Jackson and safety-linebacker Kyle Hamilton were also present at practice Thursday as the team inches closer to full strength.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he is not ruling out Vega Ioane (knee) for Week 8 against the Bills yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ mauling rookie guard suffered an MCL sprain in Week 7 against the Bengals. He is likely on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8, but Minter said he has been impressed by Ioane’s resilience and thinks he could recover quickly. In the meantime, OL Emery Jones Jr. and OT Andrew Vorhees will compete for the potential starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Vega Ioane suffered an MCL injury and will miss time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane went down with a knee injury on Sunday against the Bengals and did not return to the game. Though Rapoport said the injury is not considered long term, Ioane — an impressive rookie — will be sidelined for a while. Baltimore’s offensive line ranks 20th in pass block win rate and 19th in run block win rate, according to ESPN.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens OG Vega Ioane (knee) will not return in Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane exited late in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and was ruled out shortly after halftime. The rookie first-rounder appeared on 16 snaps and has started every game for the Ravens this season, splitting time between right guard and center. He was replaced by Emery Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens C Jovaughn Gwyn (fibula) will miss 2-3 months.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Gwyn went down with a serious leg injury in Week 3 against the Cowboys and will require surgery in the coming days, per Fowler. That will leave Lamar Jackson and the Ravens offense without their starting center for at least the next couple months. Rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane will likely start at center for the Ravens in Week 4. It’s a blow to a Baltimore offensive line that ranks 29th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and third in run blocking win rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens signed No. 14 overall pick OG Olaivavega Ioane to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane gets a fully guaranteed $24.2 million deal with a $14.1 million signing bonus and a fifth-year team option. Ioane is expected to start in year one. He primarily played left guard at Penn State, but should be able to line up at right guard, if need be. Vega (6'4/320) earned an 87.0 PFF pass-blocking grade and a 78.6 PFF run-blocking grade last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens selected Penn State OG Olaivavega Ioane with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane (6’4/320) is a powerful interior blocker who delivered one of the cleanest pass-protection seasons among Big Ten linemen in 2025. The 6-4, 328-pound guard allowed zero sacks and just a 0.7 percent pressure rate across 294 pass-blocking snaps, posting a 99.7 percent pass-block efficiency and an outstanding 87.1 PFF pass-blocking grade while committing only one penalty. Ioane also logged 306 run-blocking snaps with a 78.6 PFF run-block grade, finishing the year with only a 1.6 percent blown-block rate on run plays, illustrating his consistent execution in Penn State’s physical rushing attack. Built like a prototypical power-scheme guard, Ioane wins with thick limbs, core strength and excellent contact balance, using strong hands and hip roll to generate displacement on base blocks and double teams. His firm punch and sturdy anchor allow him to absorb power rushers effectively, while his vice-like grip strength helps him stay connected through the rep. With elite pass-protection acumen and the most complete resume of any interior lineman in the class, Ioane projects as a high-floor guard who can step into a starting role on day one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen (ankkle) will play in Week 8 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen ended the week of practice with consecutive full showings after being limited Wednesday, while backfield mate Breece Hall officially drew the questionable tag following a week full of limited sessions. Allen would remain an upside RB2 in a solid matchup should Hall be held out for another week, likely maintaining FLEX status should Hall play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be limited in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: This will be the third straight limited practice for Hall, which is an encouraging sign as he looks to return to action since last playing in Week 3 against the Lions. If he’s active, Hall will likely find himself in a bit more of a timeshare with Braelon Allen, who has rushed for 357 yards and a touchdown on 72 carries in Hall’s absence while averaging a solid 5.0 YPC. We will provide an update on Hall’s Week 8 availability when the team announces it, but at worst, we would expect him to carry a questionable tag entering the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday limited session. We’re pretty sure Allen will play this week and was just being managed on Wednesday, but how often he’ll be playing will depend on how Breece Hall’s situation shakes out on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall returned to practice last week for two limited sessions. He was listed as questionable on Friday but didn’t seem to be in the running to play by Sunday morning. The Jets ultimately ruled him out before kickoff. That ramp-up period suggests he should be back to face the Patriots this week. Braelon Allen has likely played himself into a large role even once Hall is healthy, but the latter should still operate as the team’s clear No. 1 back this week, putting him in the RB2 mix versus Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 17 times for 104 yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins, adding six catches for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen almost turned a solid fantasy outing into an RB1 performance in the fourth quarter, but the Dolphins stonewalled him at the goal line. Geno Smith was sacked on the next play and the Jets settled for a field goal. Allen appeared to get banged up late in the game and missed a few snaps on the Jets’ final drive, but he ultimately got back on the field just before the team’s last snap on offense. With Breece Hall expected to return next week, Allen’s days as low-end RB1 might be at an end. Fantasy managers should still hold on to him in case he forces a committee in Week 8 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall (quad) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Rapoport added that Hall might work out to see if he can go, but it’s “a bit early” for him to return. That means he won’t be playing this week. Hall returned to practice on Wednesday but never got in a full session. The team will give him another week to ramp up. He should be back for Week 8 versus the Raiders. Braelon Allen will draw the start again this week, putting him near the top of the RB2 ranks versus Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be questionable for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Glenn said Hall will be limited in Friday’s practice and that the team will “see how that goes” to close out the week. Hall has missed the last three games with his quad injury but the fact he is closing out the week with two-straight limited practices suggests he’ll be a true game-time decision entering Sunday. If he’s unable to play, Braelon Allen would again serve as the primary back in the Jets’ backfield and would be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what is shaping up to be a plus matchup against the lowly Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 17 times for 78 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots, adding two receptions for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen ceded a little more work to Isaiah Davis than he did the past two weeks during Breece Hall’s (quad) ongoing absence, but he still cleared 100 yards from scrimmage for the second consecutive outing. Allen was thundering around the field, handing out some nasty stiff arms and broken tackles. Never placed on injured reserve and out for the past three contests, Hall has to be getting close to a return, but we thought the same thing heading into Week 6 before Adonai Mitchell missed his fourth consecutive game with a finger injury. The Jets don’t seem particularly great at this roster management thing. Allen will remain a high-end RB2 if Hall sits against the lowly Dolphins in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction for Hall all week. The 25-year-old back was a DNP on both Wednesday and Thursday, and will now miss a third straight game as a result of his injury. Braelon Allen will again lead the Jets’ backfield this week against the Patriots and has handled 44 of the Jets’ 48 running back opportunities since Week 4. Allen will be a volatile RB2 against a Patriots defense that ranks 18th against running backs in fantasy scoring this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports that Breece Hall (quad) is working with trainers on the side field on Thursday, yet remains week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: This is a small but positive update. Hall typically works on his quad rehab program elsewhere or simply observes practice. Today’s return to the side field will still result in him being listed as a non-participant, but as Cimini says, this is measurable “progress” for the Jets’ top running back. Braelon Allen will undoubtedly get the start this week, but perhaps Hall has a chance to return in Week 7 against the Dolphins. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton managed a full session to clear the report after a Wednesday DNP. While the Ravens are missing some key players on defense, having their star safety ready to deal with Josh Allen is a big get for them in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton was seen in full pads, participating in practice the day after being held out due to a knee injury. The All Pro safety-linebacker hybrid is arguably the most important piece of the Baltimore defense considering his absurd flexibility to play multiple positions on the field. While the official status of his return has not been provided by the team, it’s a step in the right direction ahead of a divisional showdown against the Bills in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Neither did fellow Ravens safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who is also dealing with a knee injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said a few of his players were dealing with “after game type things” when asked about Hamilton, so it doesn’t sound like this is a major issue. Still, with multiple members of the secondary banged up, this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ravens S Kyle Hamilton is “more likely to play than not” for Week 16 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton was a surprise addition to the injury report on Friday, being listed as a limited participant because of the ankle issue. Per Rapoport, Hamilton will still need to go through a pre-game workout before the team makes a final call on his status. The standout defensive back has 87 tackles, seven pass breakups, and one sack this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens S Kyle Hamilton (ankle) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 16 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: It’s a surprise listing and comes with a Friday limited session. Hamilton would be a huge absence for the Ravens defense if he can’t push through this listing and play on Sunday night. We’d tentatively tag him as a true game-time decision.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens WR Rashod Bateman (ankle) and S Kyle Hamilton (shoulder) were limited in Tuesday’s practice after initially announced to be full participants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Head coach John Harbaugh had announced both Bateman and Hamilton to be full participants on Tuesday, but the team’s official injury report has them listed as limited participants. It’s not the first time Harbaugh and the Ravens have had discrepancies in practice reporting, but we’ll take the official limited listing as the truth for now. Bateman opens the week with back-to-back limited practices and has a shot to return to his starting role on Thanksgiving against the Bengals. Meanwhile, Hamilton has played through injuries before and we would not rule out the same happening again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said Kyle Hamilton (shoulder) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton looks on track to play Thursday despite being pulled from Baltimore’s Week 12 game against the Jets multiple times. The star safety is the straw that stirs Baltimore’s drink on defense and they’ll badly need him as they try to keep control of the AFC North with another win on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens HC John Harbaugh said Kyle Hamilton (ankle) will “have a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton was already playing through a shoulder injury entering Week 12, and was knocked from Sunday’s win over the Jets with an ankle injury that he suffered after slipping on the turf. Hamilton is one of the premier defenders in the league and would make for a massive loss if the Ravens are without him against Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Kyle Hamilton (ankle) exited Baltimore’s Week 12 game against the Jets and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton was running down Tyrod Taylor in the fourth quarter when his right foot slipped on the turf, appearing to roll his ankle. The star safety remained down after the play before hobbling his way to the sideline with a trainer. Hamilton was already playing through a shoulder injury and was in obvious pain after the play. With a short week to prepare for Thursday’s game against the Bengals, it wouldn’t be surprising if we saw him miss Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones departed the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts after aggravating an existing knee issue. He was held out of practice Wednesday before retaking the practice field on consecutive days to end the week, ultimately deemed healthy enough to play against the division rival Lions in Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best off finding a suitable alternative considering Jones is struggling through a sprained MCL and the team got Jordan Mason back a week ago, although managers in a bind can safely expect him to be on the field come Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was forced from the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts due to an aggravation of an existing knee injury. The fact he was able to return to the practice field in any capacity after missing Wednesday’s session is good news for his potential availability against the Lions. We would expect him to form a loose committee with Jordan Mason, if active Sunday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his level of participation Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones has reportedly been playing through a sprained MCL in one knee since Week 2. He seemingly aggravated it in Week 7 and left the game early in the fourth quarter. On Monday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Jones is considered “day-to-day.” Jones could once again play through the issue this week against the Lions. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Jones is considered “day-to-day” after suffering a knee injury in Week 7’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones’ status will be one to watch this week as the Vikings prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Lions. While the team calling him day-to-day is encouraging, Jones was already dealing with a knee injury entering Week 7, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Vikings opted to sit him this week to give him some additional time to recover. Jordan Mason, who rushed 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday’s win over the Colts could be in line for a busy day against the Lions if Jones is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 26 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts, adding one reception for zero yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones got the start in the Vikings backfield, ripping off four straight carries for nine yards on Minnesota’s first possession. Outside of the opening possession, Jones took a backseat to Jordan Mason, seeing a mix of passing-down snaps and short-yardage carries. He caught his only target in the red zone but had it punched out for a fumble out of bounds. Jones left in the fourth quarter with a knee injury; he had been playing through an MCL injury and may have aggravated the issue. Prior to the injury, Jones was getting out-snapped by Mason and ends with 15 snaps to Mason’s 38, while getting six fewer touches. Jones is a low-end fantasy RB2 if healthy for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) is questionable to return Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones suffered a knee injury after a fourth quarter run against the Colts. He has notably been playing through an MCL injury and may have re-aggravated it here. Jones struggled to walk and spent time in the medical tent. Jordan Mason is the team’s top running back while Jones is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes the Vikings could target a running back with ‘home-run burst’ in a move for the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Lewis connects the Vikings to Chargers backs Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as well as Tennessee’s Tony Pollard, Tampa Bay’s Kenneth Gainwell, and Arizona’s Tyler Allgeier. These are just whispers at the moment, but any kind of costly trade acquisition would cut into the playing time and fantasy value of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. The Vikings have clearly already been shuffling depth pieces around so we believe there could be more urgency there as the trade deadline gets closer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints, adding three catches for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones had been seeing elite workloads ever since Jordan Mason was placed on IR with a thumb injury. He hadn’t done all that much with the opportunities but finally got going downhill today. Jones ran right over a New Orleans defender for a short touchdown early in the fourth quarter. He then salted the game away with a handful of chunk gains late in the contest. Mason is eligible to return after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, so this may be the last we’ve seen of Jones in a three-down role for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed 20 times for 94 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins, adding four receptions for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was an offensive focal point for the Vikings today, consistently churning out moderate ground gains with a few decently long runs sprinkled in. He had a four-yard run called back by a penalty and lost out on a likely double-digit receiving gain on a route out of the backfield because Kyler Murray’s throw was late and low. A Dolphins defender managed to punch the ball out of Jones’ possession at one point, but it bounced out of bounds, preserving Jones’ fantasy box score. The Vikings’ offensive line health is worth monitoring heading into Week 5, but these types of workloads keep him locked firmly in the reliable RB2 tier. Treat him accordingly against the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones had 17 rushes for 58 yards in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs, adding five catches for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Only Jordan Addison saw more targets than Jones, who retained his lead back role for a second straight week with Jordan Mason injured. Demond Claiborne was the only other Minnesota running back to see a carry (he had three.) Jones was a grinder against the Bucs, picking up key first downs and shedding tacklers on screen passes in the second half. The Vikings seem intent on feeding Jones the rock for now. That should keep him in all lineups next week against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver has been on the shelf since sustaining a knee injury in Week 4, returning in Week 8 following two missed games plus the team’s Week 7 bye. He played a healthy 81 percent snap rate in his only fully healthy game this season as he continues to struggle through multiple injuries, with his return a welcome sight for a defense that has allowed the second most yards and third most points per game this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Ed Oliver (knee) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver missed the Bills’ previous two games with the knee issue. He got in one limited practice in Week 6 before the team’s bye week but did not play. A week of rest appears to have done the trick. He will return to action this week if all goes well over the next two practices.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Moore was considered legitimately questionable entering the weekend after logging only one practice. He will now miss a second straight game with the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 4, paving the way for Keon Coleman to again see significant snaps. While Moore is out, Josh Palmer, who was questionable with his own shoulder injury, is active. The Bills declared DT Ed Oliver, LB Mike Danna, and OG Ar’ma Reed-Adams inactive for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Bills slot CB Dee Alford (ankle) is also questionable. Coach Joe Brady said a week ago that both players avoided long-term injuries. They might actually have a chance to play this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
