https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: The Bills’ stud defensive tackle is on the wrong side of questionable for the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders. Fortunately, the pass rush is playing very effectively despite Oliver’s continued injury issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver was listed as a non-participant in the Bills’ Wednesday walk-through report. He suffered a knee injury in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots and avoided long-term injury, though he has yet to see the practice field. Bills fans should stay tuned to his practice status the rest of the week; Oliver will need some level of participation before the Bills can consider making him active for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said the team thinks Ed Oliver (knee) avoided a long-term injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Brady said the same goes for nickel CB Dee Alford (ankle). While this is positive news for the Bills’ defense, Oliver has already missed one game this season with a hip injury. Alford is not a top-tier coverage defender, but both players will be missed in the short term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver is questionable to return with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: It’s unclear when Oliver got hurt or what happened. He was on the bench without a helmet for a few drives before heading into the locker room. The Bills are down 21-17, and without T.J. Sanders as well, so they can’t afford to lose Oliver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (hip) is active for Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver was a late scratch from last Thursday’s game against the Lions when he hurt himself during pre-game warm-ups. It seems that he’s feeling good now and will have a great matchup against a Chargers offensive line that is missing multiple starters in the interior.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (hip) is questionable for Week 3 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver was a surprise scratch in last week’s game against the Lions after suffering an injury in pre-game warmups. It was reported on Sunday that Oliver was day-to-day with “a chance” to play against the Chargers. After being limited in back-to-back practice to close out the week, it’s fair to assume he’ll have a chance to suit up on Sunday barring any setbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Spencer Brown (back) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against Baltimore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown has a history of not practicing and getting up for the game on Sunday, so we wouldn’t necessarily read too far in to his two DNPs on Wednesday and Thursday. That said, it also wouldn’t be surprising if Brown had to sit against the Ravens on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Spencer Brown (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown initially suffered the back injury in Week 5. He missed most of that game but was back on the field for Week 6. Coming out of the bye with a DNP today suggests the issue isn’t getting better. If Brown isn’t able to play this week, Tylan Grable will take his spot at right tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills TE Dawson Knox is not on Buffalo’s final Week 15 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Neither are Joey Bosa (hamstring/wrist) or Spencer Brown (shoulder) as the Bills look to be healthy in the trenches against the Patriots in a must-win game if they want any hope at the AFC East title this year. Joshua Palmer (ankle) is questionable after three limited sessions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills declared WR Joshua Palmer, OT Spencer Brown. OT Chase Lundt, DE Joey Bosa, DT Phidarian Mathis, LB Terrel Bernard, and S Darnell Savage inactive for Week 14 vs Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: The Bills’ offensive line held up well last weekend, even with Brown and left tackle Dion Dawkins (concussion) out. Dawkins is back for this one, but the Bills will still be down their starting right tackle in a snow game, where they could rely on James Cook and the rushing attack a lot. Joey Bosa continues to be week-to-week, but his loss is a big one for this pass rush, and Shaq Thompson will start again with Terrel Bernard out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills RT Spencer Brown (shoulder) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 14 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown was limited in practice all three days this week. Buffalo has tended to be fairly conservative with Brown compared to how some teams treat their tackles — being limited is not a guarantee that Brown will play. Still, we’d bet on him being on the optimistic side of questionable after showing up at practice three days this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: He did, however, shed his non-contact jersey, so he may be closer to clearing concussion protocol. Dawkins and Spencer Brown (shoulder, limited for the second day in a row) are both trending towards playing on Sunday, or at least hitting the questionable line on Friday. It would do wonders for Buffalo’s offense to have their bookend tackles back on Sunday against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Bills RT Spencer Brown (shoulder) also upgraded to limited. Both players were sidelined for the entirety of Week 13. The Bills face the Bengals’ pushover pass-rush unit in Week 14. Although the offense can likely get by without their starting offensive tackles, having them on the field would give Buffalo a significant edge in the trenches. Bills LB Terrel Bernard (elbow) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) will not play in Week 13 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Head coach Sean McDermott also ruled out RT Spencer Brown (shoulder), LB Terrel Bernard (elbow), and WR Curtis Samuel (elbow/knee), for Sunday’s contest. With both bookend tackles sidelined, the Bills will likely roll with Ryan Van Demark at left tackle and Chase Lundt at right tackle, which could make life tough for Josh Allen against a defense that has the fourth-highest blitz rate and fifth-highest sack total (34) this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills coach Sean McDermott said RT Spencer Brown (shoulder) could go on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Brown left Week 12’s loss to the Texans twice and came back with a sling towards the end of the fourth quarter. While doctors are still evaluating him, it doesn’t sound like good news. Ryan Van Demark came on for Brown towards the end of the game and would likely be his replacement going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.headline: Bills LB Matt Milano (pectoral) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 5 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/spencer-br.analysis: Ditto DL Ed Oliver (ankle) and OL Spencer Brown (calf) — all three of these players got in limited practices on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday ahead of Sunday night football. We’d tentatively expect them all to play given the fact there were no setbacks. Milano and Oliver have not played since Week 2, while Brown missed Week 4 despite practicing on Friday ahead of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Elgton Jenkins (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: The interior lineman managed a full session on Friday. Cleveland will have its starting center ready for Pittsburgh’s front in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Elgton Jenkins and Jared Verse practiced Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: Both players emerged from their Week 7 win a bit banged up, with their return to practice Thursday a positive development toward an active game-day status. Right tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) remained sidelined, who will have one more opportunity to get on the practice field and remain asymptomatic to have a chance at playing against the Steelers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Elgton Jenkins (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: Jenkins missed Week 4 while in the league’s concussion protocol. A full practice today means he is in the final stages and should be cleared by the end of the week. He will draw the start at center this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Browns declared C Elgton Jenkins, RG Teven Jenkins, QB Taylen Green, WR Tylan Wallace and LB Justin Jefferson inactive for Week 4 against the Steelers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: The Browns enter Thursday Night Football without their starting center and right guard. Running the ball up the middle against the Steelers’ talented defensive tackle group could be challenging. Green will serve as the Browns’ emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Elgton Jenkins (concussion) will not play in Week 4 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: Teven Jenkins remains sidelined with a back injury. Elgton didn’t practice once this week and the short turnaround to Thursday Night Football was simply too quick for him to clear the league’s concussion protocol. Luke Wypler will start at center for Cleveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Browns G Teven Jenkins (back) and C Elgton Jenkins (concussion) did not practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: The Browns have a quick turnaround as they prepare to face the Steelers on Thursday Night Football in Week 4, making it highly unlikely that Elgton Jenkins will be able to clear concussion protocol in time to suit up. That makes the practice status of Teven Jenkins of primary concern considering an absence would mean the Browns would be without two of their starting interior offensive linemen against one of the better pass rushes in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Browns C Elgton Jenkins (back) is active for Week 2 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: Jenkins missed some practice time this week with a lingering back issue. He’ll suit up against a Tampa defense that last week pressured the passer at a lowly 24 percent rate. Browns declared QB Taylen Green, LB Justin Jefferson, S Daniel Thomas, CB Toriano Pride Jr., C Parker Brailsford, and G Teven Jenkins inactive for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Cleveland Plain-Dealer’s Dan Labbe believes Elgton Jenkins will likely play center for the Browns in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: There is a bit of an out in Labbe’s analysis, which is that this is contingent on Joel Bitonio returning to the team rather than retiring. Bitonio has yet to make a decision if he’ll return or not. If not, Jenkins and Zion Johnson would likely both play guard. Jenkins has said he’s open to playing either position to help the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Browns signed OL Elgton Jenkins, formerly of the Packers, to a two-year, $24 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: Roughly 24 hours after being released by the Packers, Jenkins now lands in Cleveland. The Browns continue to work to overhaul their line, and have now added Jenkins, along with guards Zion Johnson and Teven Jenkins, to the roster. It’s possible Jenkins continues to play center, as he did in 2025, but he also has experience at tackle. It’s possible the Browns experiment with him at a few spots to see where he best fits for the upcoming season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.headline: Packers released OL Elgton Jenkins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elgton-jen.analysis: They were trying to shop him for a pick, but couldn’t find a taker. Jenkins enters his age-31 season off a disastrous experiment at center, but he’s got a long track record of high-quality play and should be one of the more highly-regarded free agents on the board.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: Jared Verse (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: The star edge player will go after a limited session on Thursday and a full practice on Friday. Cleveland’s in a good place this week on the injury report heading into their matchup with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: Elgton Jenkins and Jared Verse practiced Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: Both players emerged from their Week 7 win a bit banged up, with their return to practice Thursday a positive development toward an active game-day status. Right tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) remained sidelined, who will have one more opportunity to get on the practice field and remain asymptomatic to have a chance at playing against the Steelers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: Jared Verse (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: Head coach Todd Monken told reporters that Verse is dealing with some swelling in his knee. He doesn’t expect the young EDGE defender to miss Week 8, and the Browns are giving him a rest day to heal up. Verse hasn’t done much since being traded to Cleveland in the offseason. He has 12 pressures and zero sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Browns acquired EDGE Jared Verse from the Rams in exchange for DE Myles Garrett and a 2027 first-round draft pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: The Browns also received a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick from the Rams. Verse is a rising star in the league who has totaled 12 sacks in 34 regular season games. The 25-year-old, however, became a key part in the deal that sent Myles Garrett to the Rams, as GM Les Snead reportedly wouldn’t take no for an answer in his endeavors to acquire the 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Verse is a former first-round draft pick from the 2024 class and has two years left on his rookie deal, plus a fifth-year option that the Browns will need to decide on whether or not to pick up next offseason. He won’t completely fill the void left by Garrett, but verse has displayed a good knack for getting after the quarterback, generating 157 QB pressures and another 35 hits since entering the league, per PFF.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: Rams OLB Jared Verse left practice early after bumping knees with DE Braden Fiske.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: Rams head coach Sean McVay was unable to share details beyond saying the Rams “hope that he ends up being OK.” We hope so too. The Rams’ D/ST unit is far more potent with the defending Defensive Rookie of the Year on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: Jared Verse was named Defensive Rookie of the Year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: Verse was named the winner of the award after receiving 37 of the 50 first-place votes. The 24-year-old was a force for the Los Angeles defense in 2024 while picking up 4.5 sacks and forcing four fumbles. He led all edge players in Pro Football Focus’ charting with 66 hurries while helping the Rams to a division title. Quinyon Mitchell finished second with nine first-place votes, and Verse’s teammate Braden Fiske finished third.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: Rams selected Florida State EDGE Jared Verse with the No. 19 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: Verse (6’4/254) worked his way up from the lower levels of college football, attending Albany for his first two seasons before transferring to Tallahassee to play for the Seminoles in 2022. He wasted little time making an impact at the FBS level, posting the eighth-highest PFF pass rush grade in the Power Five (88.6) with 17.0 TFL and 9.0 sacks, though he produced an elevated 27% missed tackle rate en route to being named First Team All-ACC. The Dayton, Ohio native would go on to exceed even those lofty standards this year, creating the second-most pressures in the nation (62) with a sterling 91st percentile pass rush grade that ranked fifth overall. An ACC quarterback’s worst nightmare, Verse was responsible for an 11.7% pressure rate (4th in P5) and 21.8% Win Rate (2nd in P5) in passing situations. Verse performed the full range of tests at the combine. He ran a 1.59s 10-yard split (95th%) and 4.58s 40-yard dash (9.78s) at 254 pounds, which are breathtaking times for his size. His 31 bench reps were five more than the next closest edge in the 2024 group, and second among all Combine defenders, for an extraordinary 9.60 Relative Athletic Score. He explodes into contact and unleashes a furious bull rush that can stagger even the most rooted OTs, which sets up a devastating push-pull move. Verse will sometimes lose sight of the ball carrier and over-pursue, leaving himself vulnerable to cutbacks. Still, he has a captivating power-edge profile with verified athleticism that bears a resemblance to Boye Mafe. After watching Aaron Donald retire this offseason, the Rams wasted no time retooling their pass rush by making Verse their first round-one pick since Jared Goff in 2016.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.headline: Florida State received a verbal commitment from former Albany freshman DE Jared Verse.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jared-verse/00.analysis: The ninth-ranked prospect in the transfer portal per 24/7 Sports, Verse (6'4/221) shined in his two seasons for the Great Danes. He was named rookie of the year in the Colonial Athletic Conference during the shortened spring season and amassed 9.5 sacks and 11.5 tackles for loss this fall. He spent a lot of time talking to last year’s transfer edge rushers for the Seminoles Jermaine Johnson and Keir Thomas and their production stuck out to him in their first year with the program. Verse will have three seasons of eligibility remaining.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson got in two full sessions to close out the week and should be a low-end RB3/FLEX play in limited snaps against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: He played last week just fine, so it seems like he was just given a bit of a breather on Wednesday during a limited session. Sampson should handle 5-10 touches for the Browns on Sunday against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: The Browns’ No. 2 running back played through his knee injury effectively last week, totaling 79 scrimmage yards and three receptions against the Titans. He should be expected to continue playing productively on his limited workload moving forward. He is not a must-start player in Week 8 against the Steelers, but he belongs in the FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson had six rushes for 45 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding three catches for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: In his first action of 2026, Sampson looked spry and explosive as the Browns’ No. 2 back behind Quinshon Judkins, who totaled over 100 yards and scored two touchdowns on the day. Sampson, meanwhile, logged more pass routes and targets than Judkins. It would appear Sampson is the next guy up in the Cleveland backfield if Judkins misses time in the coming weeks. He should be rostered in most 12-team leagues as a bench stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns activated RB Dylan Sampson (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable for Week 7 against the Titans. Now that he’s officially been activated from injured reserve, he’s likely to be Cleveland’s change-of-pace back behind Quinshon Judkins this week. Sampson is worth stashing on fantasy benches, but is truly just a desperation FLEX play coming off a knee injury that’s sidelined him since Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee/IR) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: If active, he will be a change-up back for Quinshon Judkins, who is not carrying a status this week. Coming off a long-term injury, it would be a real leap of faith to put Sampson in a FLEX role this week, even against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: The Browns could get their receiving specialist back in the lineup this week, though it would be nice to see him practice fully tomorrow. Sampson injured his knee while returning a kickoff in Week 1 against the Jaguars and has been sidelined ever since.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Browns coach Todd Monken indicated earlier today that Sampson has a chance to return from injured reserve in time to face the Titans on Sunday. The Browns’ skill position corps is banged up and could use an explosive player. Sampson might end up warranting FLEX treatment right off the bat, if he is active this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s “optimistic” Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Monken sounded like Judkins and Dylan Sampson will be active and ready to go against Tennessee. Judkins had been the locked-in lead back for Cleveland before his Week 5 ankle injury, seeing 71 percent of the team’s designed rushing attempts. The potential return of Sampson, a good pass catcher, could complicate things for Judkins’ involvement in the pass game going forward. Judkins will be a touchdown-dependent flex play against a Titans defense allowing the NFL’s ninth lowest rushing success rate in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson practiced each of the last two days, but it was too little, too late, for Week 6. He stands a chance at returning in Week 7. As long as Quinshon Judkins is relatively healthy, Sampson won’t have standalone value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie has missed the previous two games as he tends to a groin injury suffered ahead of Week 6. He made it back to the practice field this week but was unable to prove healthy enough to avoid the questionable designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: This is McDuffie’s first practice since he injured his groin during a Week 6 practice. He will be limited on the official injury report. Rams LB Nate Landman (concussion) will be listed as a full participant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams declared CB Trent McDuffie, QB Ty Simpson, LB Nate Landman, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost and TE Max Klare inactive for Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during a Week 6 practice. The Rams have listed him as questionable to play despite the fact that he has not yet resumed practicing. He was playing extremely well prior to the injury. His loss is consequential. The Rams elevated LB Eric Kendricks and CB Cam Lampkin to the active roster for today’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie has not practiced since straining his groin in Week 6’s Thursday practice. Labeling him as questionable to play seems like a formality before a game-day inactive listing, but only the Rams’ staffers know for sure. The Rams ruled out LB Nate Landman (concussion). Practice squad LB Eric Kendricks will be promoted to the active roster for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie, the Rams’ No. 1 cornerback, and LB Nate Landman (concussion) were both sidelined today. Both players are on the wrong side of questionable for the Rams’ Week 7 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during last Thursday’s practice and did not play in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He starts out this week not practicing, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 7. Also not practicing was LB Nate Landman (concussion). The Rams defense continues to lose players to injury; the Raiders face this defense in Week 7 and could see more fruitful fantasy performances than usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams declared CB Trent McDuffie, WR CJ Daniels, WR Tutu Atwell, QB Ty Simpson, DL Larrell Murchison and OL Bill Murray inactive for Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during Thursday’s practice and was unable to participate on Friday. Losing their top cornerback may not cost them the game, but it certainly makes it easier for Cardinals pass catchers to produce fantasy points. The Rams also activated OL Keagan Trost from injured reserve and promoted CB Cam Lampkin from the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie reportedly injured his groin during Thursday’s practice, and is now questionable to play. Frankly, the Rams can probably get by without their No. 1 cornerback this week, though obviously it would be preferable to have him out there. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams signed CB Trent McDuffie to a four-year, $124 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the deal, which includes $100 million in guaranteed money. The two-time All-Pro becomes the highest-paid corner in NFL history and will now be under contract through the 2030 season. The Rams traded a bevy picks to the Chiefs last week, including a 2026 first-rounder, to acquire McDuffie, who totaled 63 tackles, one interception, and seven pass breakups last season before a knee injury prematurely ended his season. The Rams hope McDuffie, who will turn 26 shortly after the start of next season, will prove to be the missing piece they need to make a deep postseason run in the limited time they have left with Matthew Stafford under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Rams have made “significant progress” on an extension for CB Trent McDuffie.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Garafolo reports the team hopes to sign McDuffie to a deal “in the near future,” adding that he’ll likely become the highest-paid corner in the league when all is said and done. McDuffie, 25, was acquired by the Rams last week in exchange for a haul of picks that included the Rams 2026 first-round pick. The fourth-year corner totaled 63 tackles, one interception, and seven pass breakups in 13 games last season and was named a First-team All-Pro in 2023 and a Second-team All-Pro in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson gutted out an injury to his midsection against the Raiders a week ago when he was in and out of the lineup while clearly dealing with significant discomfort. He was unable to practice through Thursday this week, prompting the questionable designation ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Chargers. Already down multiple primary pass catchers, the Rams could see further concentration of volume should Parkinson miss, a situation that could also pave the way for Davis Allen to see an uptick in opportunities in the 12- and 13-personnel-heavy Rams offense. Fantasy managers likely won’t get further updates on Parkinson’s status before the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson has meaningfully contributed to the Rams’ offense in each of the last two weeks, but he is now at risk of missing his team’s Week 8 game against the Chargers. Were Parkinson to sit out on Sunday, Tyler Higbee would likely benefit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson was in and out of the game with various injuries, picking up a new ailment on seemingly every reception. Parkinson logged 16 pass routes while Tyler Higbee led the team’s tight ends with 18 routes. Davis Allen, meanwhile, ran a route on 12 of the Rams’ drop backs and caught two touchdowns from Matthew Stafford. Parkinson should be a viable desperation option in deeper formats next week against the Chargers if the Rams keep using three tight end sets at a high rate. He has ten receptions over his past two outings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 31 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson played effectively against the Cardinals’ zone coverage this afternoon. He bagged a first down after finding a soft spot downfield on the Rams’ fourth drive, and deftly hurdled a defender on a one-yard gain a few plays later. His touchdown occurred on the Rams’ final possession and required post-catch effort, barreling through contact and extending for the score. Parkinson is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Allen is dealing with a foot injury and is listed as a DNP on the Rams’ estimated practice report. Fellow tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was listed as limited, though he has been dealing with the shoulder injury for a few weeks now and the Rams are likely managing his workload. Parkinson is trending to play. Allen’s potential absence may lead to the Rams activating rookie Max Klare to play alongside Parkinson and fantasy streaming option Tyler Higbee in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson is unlikely to be startable as a TE1 if he plays on Monday night, but his return will likely reduce Tyler Higbee’s snap share. Higbee has been TE1-viable in each of the last two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson has a chance to return for the Rams’ Monday Night Football game against the Bills. If this is the case, he would hurt Tyler Higbee’s snap share, threatening the latter’s TE1 viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 8 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: He was limited all three days. Skowronek carries no standalone value but could eat into snaps for the other Steelers receivers if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek is not fantasy-relevant and should not be picked up in 12-team formats. His potential return provides Aaron Rodgers with a trusted target. Skowronek also serves as a reliable run blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 7 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Ruled out on Thursday before traveling, Skowronek probably has a real chance to get back in Week 8. With Marquez Valdes-Scantling now on the roster, Skowronek has likely lost whatever desperation fantasy value he might have had either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Colts with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: There hasn’t been a lot of word on what happened to Skowronek. He went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter to have his leg looked at and then headed into the locker room. When the Steelers returned the kickoff to start the second half, Skowronek, who is a key special teamer, was not on the field. He was ruled out shortly after. With Michael Pittman Jr. already out, the Steelers are getting a little thin with their wide receiver depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek caught his only target for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: It was a play-action pass where Skowronek went against the flow of the defense and it almost operated like a screen, with Steelers receivers blocking downfield to create an easy crease for the 28-year-old receiver. Skowronek doesn’t need to be chased in fantasy leagues after only playing 10 of 53 snaps for the Steelers in this one. He’s operating more-or-less in a timeshare for Pittsburgh’s third receiver role with Roman Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers re-signed WR Ben Skowronek to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek caught five passes for 69 yards with the Steelers last season while playing in a very limited role. Skowronek’s 46 routes run and five targets marked the second fewest amongst any receiver on the team in 2024. A good blocker and willing special teamer, Skowronek probably has an inside track to a roster spot even if what he does isn’t worthy of fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers WR Ben Skowronek (hip) is questionable to return to Week 16 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek was involved early, catching both targets for 25 yards, but departed early in the second quarter with a hip injury and was deemed questionable to return by the team. Already shorthanded at wide receiver due to the continued absence of George Pickens, it will be up to Calvin Austin, Van Jefferson, and Mike Williams to step up for a team fighting to clinch the AFC North against their great division rivals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers elevated WR Ben Skowronek for Week 2 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: The team also elevated Skowronek in Week 1, but he wasn’t a factor against the Falcons and shouldn’t be one this week either. If anything, it’s likely not a good sign for the chances that rookie WR Roman Wilson makes his NFL debut this weekend. Skowronek will have most of his value of special teams this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers elevated WR Ben Skowronek for Week 1 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek should fill a depth role on offense while contributing to special teams and is not in the fantasy discussion for Week 1 barring injury. The elevation likely has a lot to do with rookie Roman Wilson’s absence for Sunday for a team lacking in depth at the wide receiver position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is questionable for New York’s Week 8 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: It’s been a full week of limited practices for Hall, so he profiles as a true game-time decision at this point as we head to the weekend. New York’s franchise running back declined to answer reporter questions in the locker room about whether he’d play or not. Hall would profile as an RB2 if he’s deemed ready to go, presuming no snap count, against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be limited in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: This will be the third straight limited practice for Hall, which is an encouraging sign as he looks to return to action since last playing in Week 3 against the Lions. If he’s active, Hall will likely find himself in a bit more of a timeshare with Braelon Allen, who has rushed for 357 yards and a touchdown on 72 carries in Hall’s absence while averaging a solid 5.0 YPC. We will provide an update on Hall’s Week 8 availability when the team announces it, but at worst, we would expect him to carry a questionable tag entering the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall appears more likely than not to play this week if he can get in one more practice on Friday. At the very least, he’s likely headed for an actual questionable tag this week. We’ll see what Aaron Glenn has to say Friday morning. Braelon Allen-reliant managers will want to pay attention to that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall returned to practice last week for two limited sessions. He was listed as questionable on Friday but didn’t seem to be in the running to play by Sunday morning. The Jets ultimately ruled him out before kickoff. That ramp-up period suggests he should be back to face the Patriots this week. Braelon Allen has likely played himself into a large role even once Hall is healthy, but the latter should still operate as the team’s clear No. 1 back this week, putting him in the RB2 mix versus Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets declared Breece Hall (quad) inactive for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall was reportedly unlikely to play as of this morning, so the news of his absence doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Braelon Allen will draw the start once again. Facing a dreadful Miami defense, Allen is on the RB1/2 border for Week 7. Also inactive for the Jets are CB Jarvis Brownlee, OG Dylan Parham, EDGE Joe Ossai, RB Kene Nwangwu, OG Max Mitchell, and DT Jack Heflin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall (quad) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Rapoport added that Hall might work out to see if he can go, but it’s “a bit early” for him to return. That means he won’t be playing this week. Hall returned to practice on Wednesday but never got in a full session. The team will give him another week to ramp up. He should be back for Week 8 versus the Raiders. Braelon Allen will draw the start again this week, putting him near the top of the RB2 ranks versus Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be questionable for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Glenn said Hall will be limited in Friday’s practice and that the team will “see how that goes” to close out the week. Hall has missed the last three games with his quad injury but the fact he is closing out the week with two-straight limited practices suggests he’ll be a true game-time decision entering Sunday. If he’s unable to play, Braelon Allen would again serve as the primary back in the Jets’ backfield and would be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what is shaping up to be a plus matchup against the lowly Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Reporters on the scene said that Hall headed to the rehab area after reporters left the scene, so he’ll probably be given a limited session. Still, he moved well and likely at least has a chance to suit up for Week 7 after this update. Friday’s practice will be telling. It would be surprising if Hall doesn’t at least hit the questionable line as long as he practices on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Head coach Aaron Glenn noted that Hall’s status will be evaluated throughout the week. Hall hasn’t played since injuring his quad in Week 3. If the Jets expected him to miss four games, they likely would have placed him on injured reserve. On the other hand, Adonai Mitchell just missed four games with a hand injury and was not placed on IR, so the team seemingly doesn’t have a great read on their players’ health. Hall will likely miss Week 7. Braelon Allen, in turn, is in line for a high-end RB2 ranking versus a weak Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction for Hall all week. The 25-year-old back was a DNP on both Wednesday and Thursday, and will now miss a third straight game as a result of his injury. Braelon Allen will again lead the Jets’ backfield this week against the Patriots and has handled 44 of the Jets’ 48 running back opportunities since Week 4. Allen will be a volatile RB2 against a Patriots defense that ranks 18th against running backs in fantasy scoring this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Andy Reid said Rashee Rice (hamstring) will play in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice will make his return to the game-day roster after missing two games due to a hamstring injury sustained in Week 4, returning as the top option through the air for an offense that has struggled with him off the field. The Chiefs scored a combined 25 points against the Chargers and Seahawks without Rice, the latter of which tied the fewest points scored in quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ career. Fantasy managers can comfortably re-insert Rice into rosters as an upside WR2 against the Broncos, against whom Rice caught both targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) was present at practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: That now marks consecutive days on the practice field for the veteran receiver whom has missed the previous two games. The Chiefs also had their bye in Week 5, giving Rice a full three weeks of recovery, which combines with his recent practice availability to make it likely he returns to face the Broncos. The Chiefs managed just 25 combined points in the two games without Rice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice, who hasn’t played since Week 4 against the Raiders, would be a big addition to the struggling Kansas City offense if he’s able to practice this week and suit up in Week 8 against the Broncos. Rice had been dominating targets in the Chiefs’ check-down offense, and would likely continue in that role if he can return this weekend. No other pass catcher in the Chiefs offense is a must-play for fantasy purposes for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Chiefs declared WR Rashee Rice, OT Jaylon Moore, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DB Jadon Canady, FB Ben VanSumeren, and DE Jack Pyburn inactive for Week 7 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: No real surprise here after Rice was ruled out on Friday, with the Chiefs once again shorthanded as they look to remain one of two remaining undefeated teams in the league following the loss by the 49ers earlier in the day. Expect Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals to serve as the top two receivers with Rice inactive and Tyquan Thornton done for the season, with Andrew Armstrong and rookie Cyrus Allen on hand to soak up situational snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice didn’t practice all week despite Andy Reid’s optimistic spin that he’s a “quick healer.” It’s hard to make much sense of how available he’ll be for Week 8 at this point as Rice hasn’t practiced since before the team’s Week 5 bye. Xavier Worthy will again get a WR3-caliber workload as The Only Game In Town for the Chiefs wideouts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters that Rice’s strain was only a “tweak” in his Week 4 post-game remarks. So much for that. The Chiefs will almost assuredly be without their No. 1 wide receiver against the Seahawks this week, leaving Xavier Worthy to handle the role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Right tackle Jaylon Moore was also held out of practice with a concussion. Rice went down with the hamstring issue in Week 4. Even with a bye week to heal before Week 6, he wasn’t ready to return. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Xavier Worthy led the Chiefs with seven catches for 73 yards in his absence last week. He would be in line for another high-usage game if Rice remains out for Week 7’s game against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Chiefs declared WR Rashee Rice, TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DB Jadon Canady, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, and OT Josh Simmons inactive for Week 6 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice did not come close to playing in this one and was ruled out on Friday. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Week 7; Andy Reid called him a “quick healer” on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: It seems like Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce will be getting Only Game In Town treatment against the Chargers, with Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals also in the mix at wideout now that Rice and Tyquan Thornton are both out. Andy Reid said Rice is “wanting to jump in on everything” and suggested he’s a “quick healer.” He has to be regarded as questionable for Week 7, but Reid’s words point to him having a chance to play in that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice strained his hamstring in Week 4. Although Chiefs coach Andy Reid initially said Rice only “tweaked” it, The Athletic’s Mike Silver reported a few hours later that Rice could be out for several weeks. The fact that Rice remains sidelined for the first two practices following his team’s Week 5 bye is a bad sign. He is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6 against the Chargers. If he can get in a limited session tomorrow, that could put him on track to play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) is questionable for Tampa’s Week 8 game against Atlanta.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: His absence would free up more work for Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker. Presumably Gainwell will play after logging a full practice on Friday. Either way, with an injury also nipping at him, he’s an unenviable FLEX option at best against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell missed Wednesday’s session with the hip issue. He will likely be listed as limited today, but that still puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Falcons. Gainwell racked up 14 carries in a blowout win over the Panthers last week, but that hasn’t been the norm for him. Gainwell is averaging 6.4 touches per game and has topped out at three receptions in a week. He is buried in the RB4 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell suffered the hip injury while logging a season-high 14 rush attempts in Week 7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers and racked up 49 carries as a team. Bucky Irving would be in line for more work on passing downs if Gainwell is out for Week 8. Sean Tucker could also see an uptick in snaps, though his normal role has very little overlap with what Gainwell does. Per usual, Irving looks like a high-end RB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed 14 times for 88 yards in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell was not targeted in the passing game, but that’s because Baker Mayfield attempted only 11 throws. That in turn was due to the fact that Tampa road paved Carolina on the ground as the Panthers committed four turnovers. It’s why Gainwell rushed for a season-high 88 yards after never perviously reaching 20. He was still out-carried 24-14 by Bucky Irving, who found the end zone twice as Sean Tucker hit pay dirt once. We are sure this is a formula the Bucs would like to replicate moving forward, but it is not going to be doable most of the time. It does at least make Gainwell a slightly more realistic FLEX option heading into Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed two times for 17 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: There isn’t much to say here. Gainwell has topped out at five carries in a single game this year, and that came all the way back in Week 1. He hasn’t caught more than three passes in a game either, so even the PPR scam that he operated in Pittsburgh has been shut down. Gainwell isn’t in the fantasy conversation headed into Week 7 versus Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed three times for five yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers, adding two catches for 22 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell wasn’t awfully involved in the Bucs’ game plan, but he took the field for almost as many routes as Bucky Irving and cashed in with a 10-yard score in the second half. It was his first touchdown as a Buccaneer. Gainwell is still averaging just 5.3 touches per game, but this performance could earn him more work going forward, specifically on passing downs. He will be a low-end RB4 for Week 5 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said game flow and productivity have limited RB Kenny Gainwell’s usage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: The Buccaneers are 0-3, so if trailing game scripts aren’t the ideal setup for a receiving specialist, we aren’t sure what is. Robinson said he would like to get Gainwell more involved, but also added that Gainwell has to earn those reps by being more productive. Robinson said he also wants to get RB3 Sean Tucker more involved during the same presser. It sounds like this backfield still belongs to starting RB Bucky Irving, who is dealing with a glute injury, but changes are at least being considered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said he wants to get RB Sean Tucker going.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Robinson described Tucker as being “special with the ball in his hands,” and said that it’s on the coaching staff to find spots to mix him in. Whether this impacts starting RB Bucky Irving basically comes down to how and when — and if — the Buccaneers get Tucker involved. Taking a few snaps away from RB2 Kenneth Gainwell would be no big deal. Utilizing Tucker in the red zone would be consequential for Irving. Hopefully, Robinson provides more insight before his team’s Week 4 game against the Packers. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving “is not on the team’s injury report” after Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Irving was spotted on the sideline for the majority of the fourth quarter. It’s possible that Irving just did something that irked Bowles rather than actually suffering an injury, but given how Irving’s injuries quickly manifested last season, we’re going to want to see that on the official injury report on Wednesday before we dial the status down to “unconcerned.” This news does seem to leave Kenny Gainwell as a lower-priority waiver claim.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell had three rushes for -4 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings, adding two catches for 14 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell was once again inefficient with his limited opportunities. He operated as the team’s lead back, however, when Bucky Irving exited with a lower body injury. If Irving misses any time, Gainwell would profile as a top-24 PPR option, even if he loses touches to Sean Tucker. Tampa could be without Baker Mayfield (thumb) for a while. That would dampen the prospects of everyone in the offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson (ribs) is “good to go” for Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: He’ll get cleared off Arizona’s injury report later today. Wilson is in a nice spot in one of the games with the highest over/under total on the slate against Dallas, but may run into Joey Porter Jr. shadow coverage. Still, even with how things have trended of late, this feels like a spot where Wilson has to be started in the majority of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: It was the second consecutive day in which Wilson practiced with a yellow non-contact jersey after stating Wednesday that the team was simply being overly cautious. Wilson appears on track to maintain a high-volume role in the pass-heavy Cardinals offense in Week 8 against the Cowboys, where he will be a borderline WR1, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson was on the practice field wearing a non-contact jersey on Wednesday. He is dealing with a rib injury, presumably suffered in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos. He will be limited as long as he wears the non-contact jersey and ideally finishes the week without it in order to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Kendrick Bourne suddenly becomes the WR1 if Wilson cannot go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Jacoby Brissett once again tried to get Wilson going downfield, but the best he could muster was 16 yards on their longest connection. Without a long play to juice the box score, Wilson was held under 10 PPR points for the third week in a row. All three of those games have been on the heels of the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, or his one-game absence leading into the transaction. The target totals have held steady, but the production is lacking. The good news for Wilson is that he gets the Cowboys in Week 8. Facing one of the league’s worst pass defenses, Wilson will stick in the WR2 ranks next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson’s day would have looked a lot different if a would-be 36-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett had not glanced off Wilson’s fingertips while he dove for it in the end zone. He had another 30-yarder go off his hands on the following drive, and had a five-yard catch overturned by a penalty. The disappointing box score results could allow fantasy managers to send a successful buy-low offer. Wilson is a WR2/3 next week against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for 30 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions, adding one pass for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson almost scored a passing touchdown via an end-around trick play on the Cardinals’ opening drive, but his receiver, Jacoby Brissett, was stopped two yards shy of the end zone. Heartbreak struck again two drives later, when Wilson only got one foot in bounds along the sideline on a would-be 19-yard catch. Brissett went right back to him on the following play, but the contested pass edged past Wilson’s outstretched hands. Wilson tacked on a couple of short gains before snagging a 17-yard pass on the Cardinals’ ninth drive, and he nearly bagged a 47-yard touchdown down the left sideline on the 10th drive, but his coverage defender effectively contested it, resulting in an incompletion. Wilson should handle a WR2-level workload against the Rams in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 7-of-13 targets for 95 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson is now up to a staggering 30 targets over the past two weeks after that number was “just” 14 across Weeks 1 and 2. He is managing to drew more looks than one of the biggest target sponges in the league Trey McBride, though the seam man still has 23 targets the past two weeks. Wilson and McBride have turned this offense into a two-man affair, with No. 3 Marvin Harrison Jr. now a distant role player. That’s all good and well in fantasy for the time being, but Jacoby Brissett has quietly been amongst the most ineffective QBs in the league. The rebuilding Birds may decide to get a look at Carson Beck sooner rather than later. Either way, that won’t be before next week’s potential shootout with the Lions. Wilson is now a weekly WR3 pushing for top-24 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 11-of-17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson saw season-highs across the board as the Cardinals played catch-up against the 49ers for much of the day. He operated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver, seeing over three times the opportunities as Marvin Harrison Jr. Catching much of the outside passes and intermediate crossers for the day, Wilson scored on a five-yard Jacoby Brissett pass in the third quarter. It’s clear he is Brissett’s top target in the offense, especially when the team is playing from behind. Wilson ranks as a high-end fantasy WR3 heading into Week 4 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 2-of-7 targets for 18 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson had a brutal day. The Seahawks prevented two receptions by committing defensive pass interference, and QB Jacoby Brissett prevented at least two more with a pair of overthrows. One led to an interception. The other led to a dropped interception. Wilson remains WR3/FLEX-viable against the 49ers in Week 3, coming off consecutive seven-target games. He is stuck in a tough situation, but the opportunities to score fantasy points should be there next week. Not every defense is as well-designed and talented as Seattle’s.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore has practiced with a non-contact jersey on, in a limited fashion, both of the first two days of the practice week after coming off bye. This isn’t exactly an exciting run-out after the bye, but Moore probably is on the optimistic side of questionable and any fantasy player that is breathing should be elevated in a game projected to have Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The consecutive limited showings seems to indicate Moore is on track to return from a two-game absence, something we should get further fidelity on after Friday’s practice. There remains a possibility that Moore carries a questionable designation into the weekend if he is unable to upgrade to a full participant Friday, leaving fantasy managers hopeful yet uncertain as we near the weekend. Moore would return to a WR2 profile when the Bills take on the Ravens, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore missed the Bills’ past two games because of the recurring shoulder injury. He got in one limited practice in Week 6. The team listed him as questionable but ultimately held him out. A Week 7 bye could not have come at a better time, and he now appears likely to return for Buffalo’s upcoming date with the Ravens. In a likely shootout with Baltimore, Moore will be back in the WR2 mix once he gets the green light to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore was considered legitimately questionable entering the weekend after logging only one practice. He will now miss a second straight game with the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 4, paving the way for Keon Coleman to again see significant snaps. While Moore is out, Josh Palmer, who was questionable with his own shoulder injury, is active. The Bills declared DT Ed Oliver, LB Mike Danna, and OG Ar’ma Reed-Adams inactive for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia notes that Moore resumed practicing today after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. He did the same thing last week before being labeled questionable and ultimately ruled out on game day. It looks like he’s a game-time decision again this week. If active, he can be started as a WR2, but re-injury remains a risk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: It looks like the Bills could again be without their No. 1 wide receiver on game day. Josh Allen and Co. take on the Raiders this weekend, in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. Hopefully, Moore resumes practicing soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 4 and only practiced with a non-contact jersey on Saturday of last week. After missing Week 5, Moore starts out as a non-practice participant in the Bills’ Wednesday walk-through. He will need at least a limited practice before fantasy managers can start considering him for Week 6 lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore’s absence leaves only Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Greg Dortch, and Skyler Bell as healthy wide receivers on the active roster with Joshua Palmer also sidelined. Expect heavy snap rates for Coleman and Shakir alongside tight end Dalton Kincaid, with the possibility the team elevates their 12-personnel rates through the inclusion of Dawson Knox. Also inactive for the Bills are WR Joshua Palmer, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Ed Oliver DL, Landon Jackson, and NCB Dee Alford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore failed to practice until Saturday after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4, returning to the field in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. That was apparently enough to keep the door open for an appearance on Monday Night Football against the Rams, although he certainly appears to be on the wrong side of the questionable tag. Fantasy managers would be wise to seek alternate options considering the timing of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) practiced with a non-contact jersey Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: This is the first time Moore has returned to the practice field after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4. Still no word on his game-day injury status, which will come later in the afternoon, but it a small step in the right direction for the veteran receiver. Fantasy managers likely want to continue the search for alternatives with the Bills playing on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (chest) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid was limited in both of the first two practices this week. We’d imagine he’s on the optimistic side of questionable, though it’s not altogether great news that he wound up on the questionable line after a bye week to heal up. Kincaid will have to be started if active in what projects as a scoring bonanza against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid briefly left the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders with this injury, though it was called a rib issue at the time. He returned to the contest in the fourth quarter. Buffalo then got a well-timed Week 7 bye. A limited session today is nothing out of the ordinary for Kincaid. We fully expect him to play in Week 8 against the Ravens. In what could be the best game environment of the week, Kincaid remains a solid TE1 option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 targets for 38 yards in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid did nearly all of his damage in the short area of the field, but his fantasy managers will take any kind of volume they can get after a three-week stretch where Kincaid saw a dismal seven combined targets. Kincaid’s eight targets led all Bills pass-catchers in this one, and were it not for an 18-yard touchdown taken off the board by a holding penalty, he could have been in line for a much bigger day. It’s far too early to say that Kincaid is “back,” but fantasy managers can at least be happy with a decent day of production. The Bills are now entering their bye week, but Kincaid will be boom-or-bust TE1 in Week 8 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ribs) returned in the fourth quarter of Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: With the game tied at 23-23, Kincaid returned to the field with the Bills attempting to take the lead. Whatever he’s dealing with appears to be minor at this point, so he’ll likely attempt to gut out the remainder if this one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ribs) is questionable to return in Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid exited in the third quarter and went to the blue medical tent before eventually heading for the locker room. Kincaid could be seen holding his ribs while running a route earlier in the game and was in the midst of a good performance. We will check back in with any updates we receive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: The Bills clearly came into this one intent on establishing the run, attempting 37 rushes to just 19 Josh Allen pass attempts in a game played without both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Kincaid has now seen three or fewer targets in each of his last three games after erupting for 225 yards through the air in the first two weeks. The ceiling was never in question, but fantasy managers have to be reeling after three consecutive down performances for the enigmatic tight end. Kincaid remains an upside TE1 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills head coach Joe Brady said he wants to find a way to get more targets for Dalton Kincaid.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid had just two targets in Sunday’s loss to the Patriots after seeing three looks last week against the Chargers. He’s cooled off considerably after a hot start to the 2026 season. “There’s no reason Dalton Kincaid should have two targets, especially with the flow of the game and how that goes,” a visibly frustrated Brady said after Buffalo’s Week 4 loss. “Gotta find a way to get the ball in his hands and do a better job of that.” Against the Patriots Kincaid was targeted on just 8 percent of his routes. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: The Bills’ offense was struggling to move the ball during this game, and DJ Moore left early with a shoulder injury, so it’s almost inexcusable that Kincaid wasn’t used more often. Kincaid played one fewer snap than Dawson Knox but ran 22 routes to Knox’s 10. Still, Josh Allen dropped back to throw 40 times, and Khalil Shakir ran a route on 34 dropbacks, so there is no reason for Kincaid to run 12 fewer than that over the whole game. He ran fewer routes than Josh Palmer and only six more routes than Moore, who only played one and a half quarters. The Bills will need to find a way to get Kincaid back into their plans before Monday night’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-3 passes for 38 yards and a fumble in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid almost had another big catch over the middle of the field for another 15 or more yards, but he was lit up by a safety and dropped the ball at the end of the play. It was the type of hit where you’re just happy that he wound up healthy and able to stay in the game. The 26-year-old later made a nice catch and broke three tackles as he moved closer to the Chargers’ end zone, but the ball was poked out from behind by a chasing defender. Kincaid still ran the second-most routes of any receiver on the Bills and remains a TE1 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid truly did it all in this one, routinely in the middle of the blocking scrum on long James Cook runs in addition to his work through the air. His 95 yards handily paced the team, with his first touchdown of the young season coming from 16 yards out near the end of the second quarter. Kincaid remains one of the most efficient pass-catchers in the league on a per-route basis and has worked his way into the upper echelon of fantasy assets at the position. He remains a locked-in TE1 when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: After missing the last two games with an ankle injury, Love will return to the Cardinals in what could be a three-way split after the recent emergence of Bam Knight. Love was averaging 16.2 opportunities per game before being sidelined, with most of that work coming on the ground. With only two top-24 PPR performances to his name so far this season, he shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a boom-or-bust RB2 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: That’s a second straight limited session for Love. The Cardinals are taking this slowly with the 21-year-old ahead of a potential return in Week 8 against the Cowboys, but fantasy managers will obviously need to pay close attention to how much he practices Friday and his injury designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: We were hoping to see Love practice in full after taking two weeks off. While today’s limited session puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are still worth stashing on benches, just in case. The Cardinals are finally handling Love’s recovery patiently, after giving him far too many touches early in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to practice on Wednesday.
