https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: This news comes from head coach Mike LaFleur, who spoke with the media on Monday. After missing the last two games with a nagging ankle issue, Love’s return to the field in any capacity suggests he could have a chance to suit up in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love’s ankle injury slowed his production through the first five weeks of the season, with the rookie saying at one point that he would “probably just hinder the team” if he had to play through it. Love’s status will be one to watch throughout the week, but even if he’s active, he’ll likely be forced to split touches with either Tyler Allgeier or Bam Knight, who has been solid in Love’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love starts out not practicing for the second straight week due to an ankle injury. He missed Week 6 against the Rams and a DNP Wednesday puts him on the wrong side of questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos. Love will need to practice in some capacity to have a chance of playing this week, but Tyler Allgeier is back in the RB2 range if Love cannot go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals declared RB Jeremiyah Love, QB Carson Beck, S Andrew Wingard, S Wydett Williams, S Jerrick Reed and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Tyler Allgeier is a volume-based RB2 with Love sidelined this week. The Cardinals are smartly giving Love time off to heal his injured ankles. Beck will again serve as the Cardinals’ emergency third quarterback. Wingard (knee) and his direct backup Williams (concussion) are both out, but Budda Baker (groin) and EDGE Zaven Collins (hip) are active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The Cardinals officially ruled Love out for this Sunday’s game against the Rams after he was. DNP in practice all week. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Love is not considered a candidate to be placed on injured reserve at this time, but the fact that he even has to mention that is cause for some concern that Love could be looking at a multi-week absence. LaFleur also added that Love’s lack of involvement in the passing game is due to his inability to run routes on his injured ankle. His practice status will be one to monitor next week when the Cardinals begin preparing for the Broncos. Tyler Allgeier should be in line for a busy day against the Rams and will be a volume-based RB2 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Tyler Allgeier should be rostered in 10-team leagues. The Cardinals have downplayed Love’s ankle issues, but two missed practices are not a good sign. He still has a chance to suit up in Week 6 against the Rams, but he is currently on the wrong side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: “We do think we will have Lamar this game,” Minter said. Jackson practiced in full on Friday and has missed the last three weeks with his high-ankle sprain. He was officially cleared off the injury report. Jackson told reporters that he feels like “I’m no longer a statue.” Jackson will be “safe” to use as a QB1 against the Bills in what profiles as a fantasy points bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: It’s the second consecutive full practice for Jackson, who is attempting to return from a three-game absence to face the Bills in Week 8. The two full sessions were also his first such practices since injuring his ankle, a positive development toward an active status in a marquee matchup. He’ll have one more opportunity to maintain his level of participation, which would likely keep him off the injury report heading into the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: It’s Jackson’s first full practice since suffering the ankle injury in Week 4. Even with the many twists and turns in this latest injury saga, we’re comfortable assuming Jackson will play this week. The fact that he was held out this long hopefully means that he’s close to 100 percent healthy. Facing a likely shootout with the Bills, Jackson projects for the second-most fantasy points at his position, behind only Josh Allen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) is practicing Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Though it’s unclear what, exactly, is going on with Jackson’s lingering ankle injury, a Wednesday practice puts him in a good spot to suit up in Week 8 against the Bills. His return will be a boon for Zay Flowers and the rest of the Baltimore offense. If Jackson can’t play, Tyler Huntley will get another start and should be used in superflex formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: ESPN’s Jamison Hensley believes only Lamar Jackson (ankle) knows when he’ll be able to play again.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson surprisingly missed the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals with his lingering ankle injury, which has been described as neither high nor low. “If Jackson’s injury history has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be complicated and an extended absence can derail the Ravens’ season,” Hensley said. “But ultimately, the only one who truly knows when Jackson will return is Jackson himself.” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said on Tuesday that he expected Jackson to suit up in Week 8 against the Bills. We likely won’t be sure of that until pre-game warmups. Tyler Huntley would continue as Baltimore’s starter if Jackson remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports he expects Lamar Jackson (ankle) to play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against Buffalo.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: It’s Tuesday, so we’re only 10 more Lamar updates from getting to the weekend. Rapoport believes according to people he’s spoken with that Jackson will play, and he is “believed to be as close to 100 percent as he has been.” Rapoport also noted that the Ravens weren’t “shocked” that Jackson didn’t play in Week 7, but with a Sunday and a Thursday coming up, wanted him ready for Week 8 and Week 9 badly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) is in a “decent spot” to be ready to play in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: This comes just over 24 hours after it was reported that Jackson would play in Week 8 against the Bills. Speaking with the media on Monday, Minter played coy with his remarks about his QB1 while adding that the team will know more about his status when they take the practice field on Wednesday. Jackson was reportedly close to suiting up for Week 7 against the Browns, but we heard similar reports three weeks ago when the Ravens faced the Falcons. While Jackson missing another game would be a bit surprising at this point, it’s hard to be surprised by any games he misses at this stage in his career, as they often seem to linger longer than expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: CBS Sports’ Tracy Wolfson reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Reporting from the sideline of Sunday’s Ravens vs. Bengals game, Wolfson reports that Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told her Jackson would play in Week 8. According to Wolfson, the late decision to sit Jackson this week came after the team had a chance to review footage of Jackson in practice. Minter said Jackson still didn’t look like himself in practice, which is why the team opted to give him one more week away. This is the first time Minter has committed to Jackson returning, so hopefully this is a good sign for his Week 8 availability. We will, of course, be monitoring his practice throughout the week until he is fully removed from the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, WR Elijah Sarratt, FS Jaylinn Hawkins, OG Andrew Vorhees, and DE Broderick Washington inactive for Week 7 against the Bengals
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Washington was the only player carrying a questionable designation heading into Sunday’s game, but he has officially been ruled out with an ankle injury. Jackson, who is also dealing with an ankle injury, will miss his third-straight game, paving the way for Tyler Huntley to start in the pivotal AFC North matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) is likely to play in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Rapoport added that Jackson was really close to playing this week. With Tyler Huntley playing well enough to go 1-1 so far, the Ravens took a cautious approach and ruled him out for Week 7. Huntley will start versus the Bengals later today. If all goes well in practice next week, Jackson should be back and vying for the QB1 crown in a shootout with the Bills for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said James Pearce Jr. (suspension) will be added back to the Falcons 53-man roster next week when eligible.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: “He’s done everything that we have asked, everything that he has been allowed to do, he’s done a great job,” Stefanski said while saying that Pearce would play in Madrid against the Bengals. Pearce was suspended after violating the league’s personal conduct policy for three felonies and one misdemeanor for his role in a car chase with ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. Pearce’s felony charges were aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi reports that the NFL suspended Falcons EDGE James Pearce for the first eight regular season games.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: The NFL determined that Pearce violated the league’s Personal Conduct Policy. He will be suspended without pay, but is allowed to participate in all preseason activities, including games. The suspension begins on August 30th, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on November 2nd. The Falcons go on bye in Week 11, so Week 9 marks his earliest possible return to the field. Pearce was arrested in February and initially charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor, including aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes the NFL is “likely” to suspend Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Atlanta “appears to be waiting” on the league to decide how they want to punish Pearce. Cameron Sutton was suspended eight games in 2024 for a similar incident, which Kendall mentions and certainly could serve as a blueprint for how this plays out. Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said they have not received any communication from the league on this subject. It certainly would be surprising if Pearce weren’t eventually suspended to some extent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Fox5 Atlanta’s Justin Felder reports James Pearce will be in attendance for Falcons minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce is in the middle of an ongoing legal situation stemming from a February arrest that resulted in him being charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor. The 22-year-old pass-rusher recently entered a pre-trial intervention program that can result in all charges being dismissed if he meets the conditions of the program, and the league is reportedly “closely monitoring all developments” with Pearce. We don’t yet know if the league plans to hand down a suspension to Pearce, but it wouldn’t be surprising if some disciplinary action was taken after everything is resolved in his case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the NFL is “closely monitoring all developments” in Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr.'s legal situation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: From Rapoport, “Earlier today, Pearce entered into a six-month pre-trial intervention program that, if conditions are met, will result in all charges being dismissed.” Pearce was initially charged with a misdemeanor and three felonies: aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. This deal would allow him to walk away with no jail time and no admission of guilt. The NFL could still suspend him at some point, but it does look like he has avoided career-altering legal trouble.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Falcons DE James Pearce is not expected to attend the team’s voluntary offseason workout program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: This does not come as a surprise, as Pearce is currently facing charges for three felonies, including aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, stemming from a February arrest in which he reportedly used his vehicle to collide with another vehicle during a domestic incident with WNBA player Rickea Jackson. The team has remained non-committal about when Pearce could return, but it’s possible they will opt to keep him away from the facilities until this matter is resolved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski and GM Ian Cunningham were non-committal on EDGE James Pearce Jr. reporting to the first day of the spring program on April 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce was charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor for his role in a car chase with ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. Pearce’s felony charges were aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. Stefanski said “we’re working through it” and Cunningham said it was an “ongoing legal matter” while adding he’s “not gonna touch on that right now.” Pearce’s status with the team continues to be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi reports that Falcons EDGE James Pearce is being charged with 3 felonies and one misdemeanor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce’s felony charges include “aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.” His fourth arrest charge of felony aggravated stalking was changed to a misdemeanor. Per Raimondi, “Pearce allegedly followed the car of [WNBA player Rickea] Jackson, his ex-girlfriend, and repeatedly used his vehicle to collide with hers as she attempted to reach the Doral (Florida) police station.” A police chase allegedly ensued. After crashing his vehicle, Pearce fled on foot but was eventually caught and arrested. Pearce’s 2026 availability appears to be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi reports that court records show Falcons EDGE James Pearce is “facing five felonies” after being arrested on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce is reportedly being held in Miami-Dade County on a $20,500 bond. The case “was assigned to the felony domestic crimes intake unit,” and Pearce was “given a pre-trial conditional stay-away order” regarding WNBA player Rickea Jackson. We expect more updates in the coming days. Given the reporting so far, it would not be surprising if Pearce’s availability for the 2026 season were in question at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons EDGE James Pearce was arrested on Saturday in Miami after crashing his car at the end of a police chase.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce is alleged to have been fleeing a domestic dispute. Not good, to put it mildly. It somehow gets worse when you factor in the charges Pearce is facing following the chase and subsequent crash, including two counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and aggravated stalking. That’s in addition to “fleeing or eluding police with lights or siren.” Social media footage shows what appears to be Pearce in a struggle with police following the chase. The 22-year-old had a sensational rookie season following the Falcons’ aggressive move up to get him late in the first round, but this has him in danger of a massive suspension, perhaps missing all of 2026. There’s also the very real possibility of a jail sentence. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Sauce Gardner (calf) will be active for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner missed last week’s game after suffering a calf strain in Week 6 against the Titans, but will return after getting in a limited session on Wednesday and a full practice on Thursday. We’re assuming that means he’s in line for another full practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner is considered week-to-week because of the calf strain he suffered in Week 6. He’s not expected to miss an “extended period”, but it’s safe to assume Gardner is out for Week 7. Maybe that will help kickstart the Vikings’ sluggish passing attack, though we doubt it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sauce Gardner is considered week-to-week after suffering a calf strain in Week 6’s loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: According to Rapoport, an MRI revealed a mild calf strain for Gardner, who is expected to be week-to-week with the injury. While he is expected to miss some time, Rapoport also notes that Gardner is not expected to miss “an extended period,” which suggests he won’t be placed on injured reserve. Gardner sounds like a virtual lock to miss Week 7’s game against the Vikings, so we’ll see if a week away gives him enough time to be ready for Week 8’s game against the Jaguars. Gardner has totaled 17 tackles and four pass breakups for the Colts this season while earning a PFF coverage grade of 62.6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Sauce Gardner did not return to the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans after suffering a calf injury in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner injured his left calf today, which is concerning because he injured the same calf twice last year. The first injury occurred in Week 13. He resumed playing in Week 17, lasting 35 snaps before re-injuring it. Gardner was labeled questionable to return following today’s injury, but he never made it back onto the field. He will likely undergo imaging on Monday. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Colts CB Sauce Gardner (calf) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 18 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner was only able to start four games for the Colts after coming over at the trade deadline before a long-term calf injury derailed his season. He should be fine for training camp and, assuming Lou Anarumo retains his defensive coordinator job, we can look forward to a healthy Gardner shadowing in man in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Colts CB Sauce Gardner (calf) left Indianapolis’ Week 17 game against the Jaguars and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: It’s not all that surprising after Gardner barely practiced all week before being made active. The Colts have no incentive to push him. It wouldn’t be surprising if this were the last game he played in this year. Gardner had three tackles and a pass defensed before leaving in the second half.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Colts CB Sauce Gardner (calf) is active for Indianapolis’ Week 17 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: He’ll give it a go despite Indianapolis being eliminated from playoff contention last night. Also playing off questionable tags are WR Ashton Dulin and OT Bernhard Raimann. Inactive for the Colts are C Tanor Bortolini (concussion), RB Tyler Goodson (ankle), S George Odum, DE JT Tuimoloau (oblique), G Dalton Tucker (shoulder) and S Reuben Lowery.

This strikes us as a bit of a desperate play, which makes sense as the Colts are a loss away from elimination. If Gardner can play up to his talent for the whole game, he’ll likely lower Brian Thomas’ upside in Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.headline: Colts declared CB Sauce Gardner, LB Jaylon Charlies, RB DJ Giddens, WR Anthony Gould, S Reuben Lowery III, TE Will Mallory, and T Bernhard Raimann inactive for Week 16 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sauce-gard.analysis: Gardner’s absence is likely the most detrimental after the Colts shifted away from a Cover-3-heavy structure in favor of increased rates of man coverage after acquiring the standout cornerback at the trade deadline. Expect the team to turn back to a Cover-3 base in his stead in what amounts to a must-win game for the Colts.

We’ll gain further clarity when the team released inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: Deablo suffered a forearm injury in Week 6 and opens Week 7 not practicing. Also not practicing was CB Billy Bowman (hamstring). Both will need to practice in some capacity to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes Billy Bowman (Achilles) will be back on the field during training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: Bowman suffered a torn Achilles in late November and is a potential PUP candidate. Darnay Holmes and second-rounder Avieon Terrell are candidates to fill the void if Bowman — who was having a marvelous rookie year before he got hurt — is unable to make it back before the start of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: Head coach Raheem Morris said last week of Bowman’s injury that it was “not good.” He was right. The fourth-round rookie who has played on 300 snaps for the defense this season now sees his rookie campaign come to an end thanks to the devastating injury. Bowman played 232 of his snaps from the slot this season and earned a PFF coverage grade of 52.8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.headline: Falcons coach Raheem Morris said DB Billy Bowman suffered an Achilles injury in practice and will not play in Week 12’s game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: It was “not good” in Morris’ words, which probably means this is a season-ending injury. For any normal team, this would be a devastating blow. For the Falcons, it is business as usual on a Friday. Bowman had a 52.8 PFF coverage grade over 300 snaps in his rookie season while mostly playing nickel corner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.headline: Falcons HC Raheem Morris said Michael Penix (knee) will be day-to-day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: Penix practiced in the days leading up to Week 8’s game against the Dolphins but was ultimately ruled out in favor of Kirk Cousins. The second-year quarterback is one of several Falcons players who are day-to-day to start the week, as Morris also said S Jessie Bates (ankle), DL Zach Harrison (knee), CB Billy Bowman (hamstring), and EDGE Jalon Walker (groin) would also be day-to-day to open the week. Penix appears to be trending in the right direction but if he’s unable to go, Cousins would again draw the start on the road against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.headline: Falcons ruled out EDGE Jalon Walker (groin) for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: Falcons rookie slot DB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (forearm) have also been ruled out. None of the three practiced this week. On the plus side, LT Jake Matthews (ankle) will play. The defensive injuries soften up the Falcons’ interior, which benefits Dolphins RB De’Von Achane.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.headline: Falcons ruled out EDGE Jalon Walker (groin) for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: Falcons rookie DB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) will also be out this week. Losing two standout rookies for a bout with the 49ers’ efficient passing attack is unfortunate, but the Falcons’ defense as a whole has played well this year. Walker has totaled nine tackles, eight quarterback pressures and one sack. Bowman boasts 13 tackles, one pass breakup and one interception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.headline: Falcons selected Oklahoma S Billy Bowman Jr. with the No. 118 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/billy-bowm.analysis: A four-year starter and defensive spark plug at Oklahoma, Bowman Jr. brings dynamic ball production and plus instincts to the 2025 safety class. A twitchy, versatile field safety in Zac Alley’s 4-2-5 scheme, Bowman logged snaps all over the back end—box, nickel, and deep—and racked up 11 career interceptions, returning three for touchdowns. His 2023 campaign (6 INTs, 63 tackles) landed him first-team All-Big 12 honors and showcased his elite reaction skills and nose for the football. Bowman tested well athletically (4.42 forty, 35.5-inch vert), but his size (5’10”, 192 lbs, 28.5-inch arms) is a limiting factor. He diagnoses quickly and plays fast, but his lack of play strength shows when tackling bigger targets or disengaging from blocks. He’s more of a drag-down finisher than a thumper, and his open-field tackling has been inconsistent throughout his career. Still, Bowman’s blend of football IQ, fluid hips, and versatility is rare. He can cover the slot, rotate post-snap, or disguise coverage from two-high shells. Though he may never be a box enforcer, he brings disruptive, turnover-hungry energy to the backend. He’s an immediate contributor on special teams and sub-packages, with starting upside in a split-safety system.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) is questionable for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Deablo returned to the practice field in limited capacity Thursday after missing the team’s Week 7 win over the 49ers, keeping the door open for a return to the active game-day roster. https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) and Billy Bowman (hamstring) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Both players missed the team’s Week 7 win over the 49ers before starting Week 8 preparations with absences. A return to the practice field Thursday keeps the possibility of returns open ahead of a matchup against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: It’s a slight upgrade for Christian McCaffrey, not that you were thinking about not starting McCaffrey anyway. The Falcons also ruled out CB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) — neither player practiced this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Deablo suffered a forearm injury in Week 6 and opens Week 7 not practicing. Also not practicing was CB Billy Bowman (hamstring). Both will need to practice in some capacity to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) are questionable for Week 4 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Ebukam and Deablo are the only two players listed on the Falcons’ injury report for their Week 4 divisional showdown agains the Saints on Monday Night Football. Ebukam returned to a full practice Saturday for the first time since injuring his hamstring in practice ahead of Week 3. The Falcons remain relatively healthy as they prepare to challenge the Saints for the division lead through the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons placed LB Divine Deablo (forearm) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Deablo suffered a fractured forearm in the team’s Week 7 loss to the 49ers and will now miss at least four games on injured reserve. His absence creates a significant hole in the interior for a defense allowing the second fewest yards per game this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons ruled out EDGE Jalon Walker (groin) for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Falcons rookie slot DB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (forearm) have also been ruled out. None of the three practiced this week. On the plus side, LT Jake Matthews (ankle) will play. The defensive injuries soften up the Falcons’ interior, which benefits Dolphins RB De’Von Achane.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons coach Raheem Morris said LB Divine Deablo (forearm) is “week to week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: He fractured the forearm against the 49ers in Week 7 and will “miss some time.” JD Bertrand replaced Deablo and played acceptably on the inside against the 49ers in what was a down game for the unit in run defense. He’ll replace Deablo going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons agreed to terms with LB Divine Deablo, formerly of the Raiders, on a two-year, $14 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: The deal will reportedly pay Deablo $8 million for the 2025 season. The 26-year-old recorded 63 tackles, two passes defended, and one sack in 14 games for the Raiders in 2024 but had posted 106 tackles and a sack in a full 17-game season in 2023. He was originally a third-round pick of the Raiders in 2021. He had been a safety and a wide receiver at Virginia Tech, which allows him to be solid in coverage as a linebacker. He will bring speed and plus athleticism to the middle of the Falcons’ defense in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Linebacker Divine Deablo missed Week 3 with an oblique injury and did not practice on Wednesday. Crosby was limited in all three practices last week before playing through the ankle injury. The DNP today is a bit more concerning, but Crosby routinely missed practices last year while dealing with a knee injury only to suit up on Sunday anyway. Crosby is more likely to play than to sit, seemingly regardless of what the injury report says.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson will miss a second straight game with his hamstring injury, which positions Khalil Herbert to again serve as the backup to Bijan Robinson. Herbert rushed two times for nine yards in last week’s win over the 49ers while adding one reception for 19 additional yards. He will not be on the streaming radar this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: He hasn’t practiced since before Week 6 and looks likely to be ruled out again on Friday. Khalil Herbert ran in Robinson’s place as the backup last week and would handle those duties again against Tampa on Sunday if Robinson is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Bijan Robinson handled 20 carries and five targets with his backup, Brian Robinson, sidelined in Week 7. The backup should be considered questionable to play at this time, though he could make a late-week return. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Bijan should get a larger-than-usual workload this week against San Francisco. The Falcons only have two running backs on the 53-man roster so it may be Khalil Herbert or Jam Miller filling in as (Bijan) Robinson’s backup on Sunday. Herbert seems like the logical choice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson is the immediate backup to Bijan Robinson in the Falcons’ backfield, seeing his best usage in run-heavy game scripts. He was limited with a hamstring injury on Wednesday but is still trending to play Week 7 against the 49ers, barring setbacks. Also limited was Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Both players are depth options at best behind the Falcons’ star-studded skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson, Jr. had two rushes for one yard in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: With the Falcons down by three touchdowns and abandoning the run game in the second half, Robinson had little chance of paying off as a Week 6 flex in the usually run-first Atlanta offense. Chicago snuffed out the Falcons run game and forced Michael Penix to try to beat them through the air. Robinson will be a game-script sensitive RB3 option in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson rushed 14 times for 62 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints, adding five yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson watched from the sidelines as Bijan cashed in on two first quarter rushing scores, getting in on the fun in the second quarter with a touchdown from four yards out. He would add one from eight yards out in the third quarter and cap off his outburst with an 11-yard touchdown scamper in the fourth quarter to send the Falcons to a 2-2 record ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens. Brian Robinson remains an elite handcuff but is unlikely to return consistent fantasy production for as long as Bijan remains healthy, despite the eruption against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson rushed 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Brian Robinson’s 10 carries paled in comparison to the 29 of Bijan Robinson but were enough to give him his first fantasy-relevant week of the young season. His third quarter score came from seven yards out after Bijan has pulled himself from the game following extensive work on the drive. Brian Robinson remains one of the top pure handcuffs in fantasy circles but will be a difficult start until bye weeks start piling up in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (ankle) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson was limited on Monday for the estimated practice session. It seems like he’ll be able to go behind Bijan Robinson in Week 3’s TNF showdown with the Packers.

He would likely return to a sizable role over the middle of the field against the pass-funnel Jaguars, if active in Week 8.

With Josh Downs failing to step up in his absence, the Colts desperately need Warren back in the lineup as their de facto WR1. Downs has also requested a trade, which would open up even more work for him. If all goes well in practice this week, Warren will be back in the TE1 mix for his Week 8 matchup with the Jags.

Though he was reportedly considered a game-time decision over the weekend, the Colts shut him down on Sunday. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Keenan Allen led the Colts with eight catches for 82 yards last week. He remains an unfortunately viable PPR scam as long as Warren is out versus the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Colts TE Tyler Warren is inactive for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren suffered a groin injury during Friday’s practice and was put on the questionable line; this is not great news for his chances of playing in Week 7’s game. https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren suffered the groin injury during Friday’s practice. He was added to the injury report and listed as questionable for Week 6. Of note, Warren also dealt with a groin injury late in training camp, though he was ready to go for Week 1 and had not appeared on the injury report again until this week. Even if he does suit up, Warren will be at far less than 100 percent. Expect Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to take on more work whether or not Warren is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) is questionable for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren popped up on the injury report on Friday after suffering the injury in practice. Fantasy managers who were relying on Warren likely won’t find a good enough option to replace him with proactively on waivers at this point, so it makes some sense to sit and wait for more reporting to come out or for him to be ruled out. This was, frankly, the last thing the Colts needed given how banged up their receiving corps has been.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Josh Downs will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars despite his trade request.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Steichen confirmed that Downs did indeed request a trade, but that won’t stop him from being on the field this week against the Jaguars. The Colts appear to be in full sell mode after trading away OG Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner earlier this week. Downs has been on the practice field this week and profiles as a fringe WR3/WR4 after a string of tough outings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs has requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs was cagey when asked on Wednesday morning whether he had officially asked for his ticket out of Indianapolis, but Fowler maintains the wideout has requested the Colts trade him before the NFL’s trade deadline. That could very well happen in the coming days with the miserable Colts in fire sale mode, having dealt Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to the Niners. Downs, who has 26 receptions for 307 scoreless yards this season, would make sense as a trade target for the wideout-needy Chiefs, the Steelers, and perhaps the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts could trade Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Schefter listed out DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, and Downs as players that could potentially be on the move as the Colts continue what from all outside appearances looks to be a fire sale. He thinks Buckner will be the next player on the move and likely go for less than Quenton Nelson. Downs certainly hasn’t impressed with his opportunity this season, but he’s a valuable receiver and Indianapolis didn’t exactly but him in an ideal scenario with Alec Pierce hurt and Keenan Allen playing alongside him while Daniel Jones struggles to regain his 2025 form.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 2-of-4 targets for 18 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs’ four targets were the most on the team, though he caught just two for 18 yards. His lack of red zone usage and deep targets cap his ability to get explosive plays or touchdowns. He led all Colts wideouts with 52 snaps, tallying seven more than second-place Laquon Treadwell. Even with Tyler Warren (groin) out, Downs is losing middle-of-the-field targets to Keenan Allen. Given his low output with both Warren and Alec Pierce out, Downs is a low-ceiling WR4/FLEX play for Week 8 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Pierce, dealing with a heel injury since mid-September, will continue rehabbing and remain on injured reserve ahead of the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings. Since Week 3, Keenan Allen leads the Colts with a 24 percent target share, while Josh Downs has 17 percent of the team’s targets and 26 percent of the team’s air yards. Neither wideout is a great option in Week 7 against a marauding Minnesota defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans, adding a seven-yard rush.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: It was a rough fantasy day for Downs, who committed two terrible drops and was stopped at the one-inch line on his second quarter end-around. He was also the intended target on one of Daniel Jones’ two interceptions, though the miscue was Downs’ fault after he bobbled a ball up into the air. On top of everything, Downs also tweaked his shoulder. He did at least remain in the game. Just not looking up to the No. 1 receiver task as the Colts await Alec Pierce’s return, Downs is sadly maxing out as a low-ceiling WR3 option in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Given how Downs’ season is going, it’s hard to believe he’s going to do much with the extra runway, but Tyler Warren (groin) popping up on the report could shift more targets to Downs and Keenan Allen on Sunday against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The good news is that it looks like Downs is trending towards getting off the injury report on Friday. The bad news is that it’s hard to make much more than a WR3 case for the receiver given how bogged down Indianapolis’ passing offense looks at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Typically, rest days are entirely inconsequential. Recently, the Colts listed Keenan Allen with a rest designation on Wednesday. He picked up a groin injury during the practice week, and although they added the groin injury to the injury report, they kept the rest designation on there as well. He didn’t play. Downs could end up being perfectly fine, but given the Colts’ recent handling of a similar situation, his participation levels on Thursday and Friday are worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-6 targets for 47 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The good news is that Downs ran a route on 44 of the Colts’ 47 dropbacks. He was also targeted down the field a few times. The bad news is that Daniel Jones was not effective and hasn’t been throughout the season. Downs did have another 15-yard completion called back due to a penalty away from the ball, but it wouldn’t have made a huge difference in his day. Downs is still on the WR3 radar because the Colts play the Titans next week, but until Jones can get it going, it’s hard to trust anybody other than Tyler Warren in this passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Antoine Winfield Jr. will return in Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield has missed the last three games due to fractured ribs he suffered in Week 4. Winfield has earned a 76.8 defensive grade per PFF this season while racking up 24 tackles. The Panthers’ secondary held up fairly well during his three-game absence, allowing only 235.0 passing yards per game, but his return will be a welcomed one for Bowles and his defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Antoine Winfield (ribs) for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield’s absence is consequential. The centerfield prowler makes an impact when he is in the game. The Steelers should have a slightly easier time moving the ball against the Buccaneers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Antoine Winfield (ribs) has a fracture and will miss 2-4 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: That timeline makes it possible he’ll be sent to injured reserve before Week 5’s Thursday Night Football game against the Cowboys. Winfield missed only five snaps in Tampa’s loss to the Packers; this would appear to open a pretty deep hole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers S Antoine Winfield (toe) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: He and Lavonte David (knee/rib) both upgraded to full practices on Friday and were removed from the report. The Buccaneers will have their back-seven leaders ready for a divisional matchup against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Bucs S Antoine Winfield (toe) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: It seems like, with Wednesday’s practice being a walkthrough, the Buccaneers opted to go easy on some of their veterans. Lavonte David (knee/rib) and Winfield both upgraded from DNPs to limited sessions on Thursday, putting them in line to play. The same can’t be said for EDGE Haason Reddick (ankle/knee), who remained a DNP and could be in line to miss more weeks. We’re a little surprised Todd Bowles didn’t rule out Reddick when he said that Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin weren’t going to play this week, but he did say they were still waiting for the results of his MRI when asked about it on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Bucs EDGE Haason Reddick (ankle/knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Several Tampa Bay defenders did not practice on Wednesday. Lavonte David and Antoine Winfield are among the most notable names on the list. David is dealing with knee and rib issues while Winfield has a toe injury. Coming off a Monday night game, the Bucs might be giving their veterans some maintenance days because of the short week. Still, it’s notable just how many big names they have on the injury report. A banged-up Bucs defense could help Spencer Rattler get back on track after throwing three interceptions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers restructured S Antoine Winfield Jr.'s contract to free up 2025 cap space.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield had a $21 million base salary that was shifted to a minimum salary and bonus, with the Bucs also adding a void year. He signed a four-year, $84.1 million contract last offseason and now Tampa Bay frees up $15.86 million in cap space for 2025 by restructuring a contract that ends in 2027. The Bucs also restructured WR Mike Evans’ contract, though it was not for any cap savings. Evans had some compensation moved forward to pay him sooner, but cap space was not created.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cade Otton (knee, questionable) is expected to play in the Wild Card Round against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Otton is one of five players who entered the weekend listed as questionable who are expected to play on Sunday night. The third-year tight end who broke out for 59-600-4 in 14 games this season has missed the last three weeks due to a knee injury but will be back in the mix on Sunday night, barring anything unexpected. In addition to Otton, safeties Antoine Winfield Jr., and Mike Edwards, along with cornerback Jamel Dean, and defensive end Logan Hall are also expected to play despite being listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Antoine Winfield will play in the Wild Card Round against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: The Bucs will also have Jamel Dean back in the lineup after Dean missed Week 18’s game with a knee injury. Winfield, who hasn’t played since Week 14, is also returning from a knee injury, providing two immediate boosts to a secondary ahead of the Buccaneers’ biggest game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers S Antoine Winfield Jr. (knee) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield has been unable to suit up on game day since suffering the knee injury in Week 14 and his return could prove pivotal in a potentially high-scoring game against the Commanders. Winfield returned to practice in a limited capacity last week so his continued improvement is a great sign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Emeka Egbuka (foot) will not play in Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka did clear concussion protocol, but the foot injury he has been dealing with for the last two weeks will officially sideline him for this week’s game against the Falcons. Hopefully this isn’t any kind of a major setback for Egbuka, who shed his non-contact jersey in Thursday’s practice and was limited in the first two practices to start the week. Ted Hurst will again operate as the Buccaneers’ primary outside target but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a risky WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: After being limited in back-to-back practices to start the week, and shedding his non-contact jersey on Thursday, Egbuka being a DNP on Friday is a notable setback. Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman speculated that Egbuka will “be ruled out again” for Week 8’s game against the Falcons, but we’ll wait for official word from the team before drawing conclusions. That said, the Bucs could again have Ted Hurst operating as their primary outside threat.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) shed his non-contact jersey for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: There’s a good chance Egbuka has been upgraded to a full participant in practice, meaning he is making his way through the league’s concussion protocol. He remains on track to play this week after missing Week 7. With Baker Mayfield back under center, Egbuka may be able to turn around his season after a rather quiet start to the year. He is in the WR2 mix for Week 8 versus the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka logged one limited practice on Friday last week but was ruled out shortly after. It looks like he is trending in the right direction for Week 8, but the Bucs’ next two injury reports will be more revealing. Assuming all goes well, Egbuka should be back in the WR2 ranks with Baker Mayfield under center and playing well in Tampa Bay’s Week 7 demolition of the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Just minutes after head coach Todd Bowles said the team would list Egbuka as doubtful, the official injury report listed him as out, despite his limited participation in Friday’s practice. Egbuka was unable to clear concussion protocol in time to be active for this week, and will now set his sights on returning in Week 8 in time to face the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers head coach said Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) will be doubtful for Week 7’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka remains in concussion protocol and initially said “I’d say he’s out [for Week 7], too,” before saying the second-year receiver would be listed as doubtful. Fantasy managers holding out hope that Egbuka will suit up for Sunday’s game against the Panthers should ensure their backup plan is in place, as players listed as doubtful seldom end up playing on game day. Assuming he’s out, Ted Hurst could be tasked with operating as the Bucs’ WR1. Hurst has caught 11-of-22 targets for 168 yards and one touchdown this season but wouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play even with Baker Mayfield (thumb) back under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka missed the first two practices of the week, but could have a shot at suiting up after appearing on the practice field Friday. Head coach Todd Bowles should give an update on Egbuka shortly after practice, so we’ll check back on his official status once we have word on his Week 7 availability. Whether or not he has a chance to play will largely depend on the team’s independent neurologists clearing him from the league’s concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: The Buccaneers’ No. 1 wide receiver is now firmly on the wrong side of questionable. It is a huge bummer, particularly after Egbuka earned 16 targets last week. Chris Godwin and rookie Ted Hurst earned targets most effectively behind him, though they are likely best viewed as FLEX starters at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka finished the Bucs’ overtime loss to the Steelers, so his concussion symptoms likely arose in the hours or days after the game. He will now need to pass through the league’s concussion protocol to be cleared for Week 7. Players typically miss one game while in the protocol, and we don’t know the severity of his foot injury. Fantasy managers should prepare to be without him for at least a week. His absence would free up more looks for Chris Godwin and rookie Ted Hurst, both of whom would be in the WR4 mix if Egbuka can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 7-of-16 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Fantasy managers can’t complain about 17.8 PPR points, but this should have been an explosion spot for the second-year wideout. Jalon Daniels routinely missed him on routine throws, the most painful of which was a long would-be touchdown that grazed Egbuka’s hands as it sailed past him. There were several other throws that were behind, low, or simply too late. A short, two-yard score at the top of the second quarter will have to suffice. Egbuka is pulling away as the Bucs’ alpha receiver, pushing him back into the WR2 ranks for the team’s Week 7 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield was seen without his protective glove during Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield wore the protective glove during last week’s game to avoid further damage to the thumb he injured in Week 3. Mayfield attempted only 11 passes in his return against the Panthers last week, but that was all he needed in a game where the Buccaneers totaled over 250 yards on the ground. Hopefully the shedding of his protective glove is a sign that he’s no longer at risk of re-injury heading into Week 8’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 7-of-11 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ 43-13, Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Making his first start since Week 3 but missing Emeka Egbuka, Mayfield got his first “quarterback win” of the season in a game where he had to attempt only 11 passes. Go figure. The Bucs road paved the Panthers on the ground — 49 carries for 258 yards — and continually took advantage of short fields set up by Panthers turnovers. This, in a game where Mayfield committed zero giveaways. It was the exact kind of day this offense needed, though there aren’t many going-forward takeaways for Mayfield seeing how little he had to throw. Mayfield will presumably be called on for more against the Falcons in Week 8, hopefully with Egbuka back in the fold. Mayfield is just a mid-range QB2 for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: When last we left Mayfield, he was struggling mightily in Weeks 1-3. Predictably, UDFA Jalon Daniels was not any better in his stead. Mayfield returns to an undermanned skill corps, as Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) is out for Week 7. Mayfield is a shaky option in the QB16-18 range. Joining Egbuka on the shelf are OT Luke Goedeke, S Antoine Winfield, OG Billy Schrauth, DL DeMonte Capehart and CB Ayden Garnes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles told reporters earlier today that Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go” for this week’s game. Mayfield seemingly has solid odds of suiting up this week, but we must wait for an official ruling. Hopefully, that arrives tomorrow. If active, Mayfield will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help keep his recently dislocated thumb in place. He is a QB2 for the occasion, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) “looks like he’s ready to go” for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield was a full participant in practice all week and should be removed from the team’s final injury report when it’s released later in the day. Mayfield is expected to wear a protective glove on his throwing hand, which should prevent injury to the thumb he dislocated in Week 3, and will be on the QB2 radar in what is a must-win game for the 1-5 Buccaneers. Hopefully he can improve on a rough start to the season in which he threw for 615-2-2 in his first three games while completing 63.5 percent of his passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield said his injured thumb has “gotten to a place where it’s strong enough to play” in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield has played through injuries regularly over the years. We expect him to be out there for the Buccaneers’ Week 7 game against the division rival Panthers. He is a QB2 for his first game back. A run-heavy game plan could be in the works as they ease him in. If his thumb really is good to go, though, this game could turn into a shootout. He practiced in full for the second time this week on Thursday, and told reporters that he will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help prevent re-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield going down as a full participant is a bit of a surprise given that it’s his first time practicing in any capacity since Week 3. Todd Bowles told reporters earlier this week that the team was preparing for Jalon Daniels to start. Now it looks like Mayfield may be the favorite to draw the start versus Carolina. This is ultimately a rather ambiguous situation, likely by Bowles’ design. Fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place if they are counting on either of the Bucs’ quarterbacks this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield hasn’t played since dislocating his thumb in Week 3. As of late last week, he hadn’t even thrown a football since suffering the injury. Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that he’s preparing for Jalon Daniels to start, but Mayfield’s return to practice puts things up in the air. His practice statuses over the next few days will be telling. For now, fantasy managers should still plan on seeing Daniels under center, but this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) is “supposed to practice Wednesday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Bowles has already said that the team is preparing as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7, but the team will be evaluating Mayfield to see how he is progressing in his recovery from a dislocated thumb. Mayfield reportedly pushed to play last week after throwing on Monday, but his thumb swelled up, which factored into the decision to sit him in Week 6’s loss to the Steelers. Given Bowles’ comments about the team’s plans entering the week, it sounds like Mayfield is at risk of missing at least one more game, but we’ll see how his hand responds when he gets on the field on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said the team is planning as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Bowles said this week will be an important evaluation week for Baker Mayfield, who is still rehabbing a dislocated thumb that has sidelined him since Week 3. Daniels hasn’t been overly impressive in his three starts this season, throwing for 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions while also taking nine sacks. That said, he did manage to pull off a win over the Cowboys in Week 5 and had the Buccaneers in position to beat the Steelers in Week 6 before Pittsburgh erupted for 16 points in the fourth quarter to force overtime. We’ll see how things unfold throughout the week, but it sounds like Mayfield is at least one week away from returning. Daniels would be on the fantasy radar as a low-end QB2 if he gets the start against Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: Panthers named DL coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: Wash will take over for the now-departed Ejiro Evero, who was dismissed shortly after the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers. Wash, who has been with the Panthers since 2023, spent five seasons as the Jaguars’ defensive coordinator (2016 to 2020), with his defense finishing top five in both yards and points allowed in 2017 and 2018. Wash’s first task will be finding ways to improve a run defense that ranks among the worst in the league through the first half of the season, but given that his fingerprints are all over the defensive line, it’s hard to imagine a noticeable improvement is on the way over the final 10 weeks of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: Lions hired ex-Jaguars DC Todd Wash as DL coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: Wash, 52, was the Jaguars’ DC the last five seasons but was ushered out with coach Doug Marrone’s staff. He spent eight seasons in Jacksonville where he was the previous DL coach prior to his promotion. He’s been coaching defensive linemen in the NFL since 2007 and will work under first-time Lions DC Aaron Glenn in Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: Jaguars DC Todd Wash will miss Sunday’s game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: The Jaguars’ defensive coaching staff has been working remotely following a positive COVID-19 test. This likely means Wash was the one who tested positive and won’t be cleared to return for Week 12. With Wash out, DB coach Joe Danna will call plays against Cleveland this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: The Jaguars entire defensive coaching staff was sent home on Tuesday following a positive COVID-19 test.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: Contract tracing is underway. Per NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero, it is “not yet clear how it may impact who’s available.” The Jags play the Browns on Sunday. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: Jaguars DC Todd Wash said his unit is “not a true 3-4 or two-gap team.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: “It’s funny: everybody says we’re going to a 3-4,” Wash said. “You will see some different fronts, but we want to still continue to give teams a lot of multiple looks. Most importantly, we want to put the players on our roster in a position to be successful in any scheme that they fit.” There’s been some speculation this unit will move from a 4-3 defensive scheme to a 3-4 this upcoming year, but Wash clearly isn’t having it. The organization added rookies C.J. Henderson and DE K’Lavon Chaisson, not to mention free agents Aaron Lynch and Cassius Marsh, but will move forward with the same defensive front it’s leaned on the past two seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: Jaguars announced they will retain Todd Wash as the defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: It is a bit of a surprise considering Wash had been with former coach Gus Bradley for several years, but the Jaguars are clearly favoring continuity. Promoted to coordinator this time last year, Wash’s unit finished sixth in total defense and surrendered the fifth-fewest passing yards and touchdowns in the league. While Jags fans might not be thrilled Wash is returning, his defense was not the issue this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: The Florida Times-Union reports Jaguars DL coach Todd Wash is “the leading candidate” to land the team’s defensive coordinator position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: The Jaguars interviewed Jim Schwartz for the position, but he landed in Philadelphia. With Schwartz out of the picture, coach Gus Bradley will likely take on a bigger role on defense, allowing Jacksonville to hire an inexperienced coordinator. Wash, Falcons DBs coach Marquand Manuel and ex-Dolphins interim DC Lou Anarumo all fit the bill. The Jags are expected to make their decision by this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.headline: Jaguars promoted DL coach Todd Wash to defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/todd-wash/.analysis: The Jags struck out on all their veteran candidates, leaving them to hire from within. Promoting Wash is a sure sign coach Gus Bradley is planning to take on a bigger role in defensive play-calling as he prepares for a make-or-break season. Wash has coached alongside Bradley for over a decade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: Panthers fired DC Ejiro Evero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: Just hours after a 27-19 loss to the Packers that saw the Panthers fall below .500 for the first time this season, the team has decided to part ways with Evero after nearly four full seasons with the team. Evero was a holdover from Frank Reich’s 2023 staff and drew a handful of head coaching interviews during the last hiring cycle after his defense finished 15th in points allowed and 16th in yards allowed. The Panthers’ best defensive performances of the season came in games where Cooper Rush and Tanner McKee made starts, but they’ve allowed 35.2 points per game when facing opposing teams’ QB1s this season. From 2022 to 2023, Evero’s defenses ranked seventh and fourth in yards allowed per game, but his units have struggled in more recent seasons. They have particularly struggled on the ground and rank near the bottom of the league in rushing yards allowed and YPC allowed, while allowing a league-high 12 rushing touchdowns. He’ll likely get another job in a coaching role next offseason, in hopes of earning another coordinator job over the next few seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Panthers DC Ejiro Evero is “still in the mix” for the Raiders’ head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: Seahawks OC Klint Kubiak is viewed as the favorite for the role, but Evero is evidently still in it. Per Fowler, Evero conveyed detailed plans for the offense and, specifically, the quarterback position during his in-person meeting with the Raiders. The presentation apparently went over well. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: Steelers completed a virtual interview with Panthers DC Ejiro Evero, amongst others.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: The Steelers reportedly completed virtual interviews with seven coaches during the previous week, to include, Evero, Packers DC Jeff Hafley, 49ers OC Klay Kubiak, Chargers DC Jesse Minter, Rams pass game coordinator Nate Scheelhaase, Rams DC Chris Schula, and Dolphins DC Anthony Weaver. The team will also reportedly conduct in-person interviews this week for the select few that made it through their first round of questioning. More to come following the unexpected departure of Mike Tomlin, who had been the league’s longest tenured coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Raiders will interview Panthers DC Ejiro Evero for a second time regarding its open head coaching position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: Evero met virtually with the Raiders this week and will have an in-person interview sometime next week. The 45-year-old defensive coordinator also has an interview with the Steelers coming up. Evero has been a defensive coordinator for the last four years (three with the Panthers, one with the Broncos) with mixed results, though he remains respected around the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: Raiders completed an interview with Panthers DC Ejiro Evero for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: This is Evero’s first reported interview. He has also received interview requests from the Steelers and Falcons this week. Evero’s defenses have delivered volatile results over the last three seasons, but the 45-year-old coach evidently remains a respected figure in league circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: Steelers requested an interview with Panthers defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero for their head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: Evero has been one of the more highly-regarded defensive coordinators in the league for a while. He has been with the Panthers as their DC for three years and previously spent a year in Denver with the same role. The Panthers just finished in the top half of the league in yards and points allowed, though they were a below-average unit by EPA per play. Evero has head coaching interviews with the Raiders, Falcons, and Steelers. He also received head coaching looks last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: The Raiders have requested permission to interview Panthers DC Ejiro Evero for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: The same is reportedly true of the Falcons. Evero has been on something of a three-year journey in Carolina, overseeing a strong unit in 2023, a disastrous one in 2024, and respectable one in 2025. We would consider him a long shot for either opening, but he’s clearly a name getting around in league circles. He also interviewed for openings following 2023. Evero turned 45 earlier this month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Ejiro Evero will return as the team’s defensive coordinator next season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: Evero fielded a handful of interviews for a head coaching gig last offseason after the Panthers’ defense ranked top-10 in yards allowed in 2023. Evero’s defense was anything but a high-end unit in 2024, ranking last in the league in yards allowed, points allowed, success rate, and EPA per play. It’s not hyperbolic to say things couldn’t have gotten much worse for Evero and the Panthers’ defense in 2024. While Evero could still field head coaching interviews in the coming days, that seems unlikely given his unit’s struggles this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person reports Panthers DC Ejiro Evero “is staying with the Panthers, and most of his defensive staff is also expected to return” in 2024.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: This is good news for the Panthers and newly minted head coach Dave Canales, who spoke glowingly of Evero. Having competed against Evero in 2023 as the Buccaneers’ offensive coordinator, Canales said Evero’s defense “was really hard to deal with,” and he’s “really excited to learn more about the ins and outs” of his calls and adjustments. Evero has been on the head coaching radar in back-to-back offseasons and probably isn’t long for Carolina beyond this season. His defense was the lone bright spot for the Panthers in 2023 and will likely be a highlight again next season. Another successful year could be enough for another team to hire him into a head coaching role in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Falcons have requested a second interview with Panthers DC Ejiro Evero for their head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ejiro-ever.analysis: Evero has already received a request for a second interview from the Seahawks and can now add the Falcons to that mix. The 43-year-old defensive coordinator has been a popular name throughout this coaching cycle and received a handful of interviews last year as well. Evero and his defense were one of the few bright spots for the Panthers last season, allowing the fourth-fewest yards per game while ranking in the top 10 in passing yards allowed and net yards per attempt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young’s knee injury may be limiting his mobility.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young declined to get into details about his knee injury after Thursday night’s loss to the Packers, saying, “Everyone’s dealing with something; it’s no excuse,” when speaking with the media after the game. Canales didn’t seem overly concerned about Young’s injury after the game, but did acknowledge that he didn’t appear to have the “quick, make you miss” aspect to his game against the Packers.
