Young was listed on the Panthers’ injury report throughout the week, but was also a full participant in practice. Young’s knee could be partly to blame for the six sacks he took in Thursday’s loss, and his health will be one to monitor in the weeks ahead, especially with the team already past its Week 5 bye. Assuming he’s good to go in Week 9, Young will face an uphill battle against a stout Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Panthers’ 27-19, Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Those who believe that sacks are a quarterback stat might change their mind watching the Panthers block Thursday night. The 25-year-old had no time to throw and couldn’t get out of the pocket while taking six sacks and being pressured on what seemed like every throw. That’s not to say that Young was completely a victim of his circumstance; he struggled with accuracy and couldn’t get the ball downfield in another ugly performance for the 25-year-old sans a 26-yard passing score to Jalen Coker in the middle of the fourth. Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers listed Bryce Young (knee) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young was listed with the same knee injury last Friday but remained a full participant and was good to go in Week 7. Whatever issue he’s dealing with appears minor, especially if the team is still listing him as a full participant. At this point, there’s no reason to think he won’t be active for Week 8’s game against the Packers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 14-of-27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Panthers’ Week 7 game against the Bucs, also losing a fumble-six.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: With the Panthers somehow losing 43-6 in the fourth quarter, Young gave way to Kenny Pickett for the final 10:11. Pickett immediately engineered a garbage time touchdown drive. This was by far Young’s worst performance of what had so far been a legitimate breakout campaign, as he short-circuited one drive after another and set up Bucs short fields with turnovers. The fumble-six was the most costly mistake, but Young’s second interception was probably his worst throw. He was fooled by the coverage under pressure and threw the ball right to Tykee Smith. Young’s first pick came after Jalen Coker fell down. In between all the miscues, Young could get nothing going with either Coker or Tetairoa McMillan. It was hard to see this coming — especially against the Bucs — but it is even harder to see it continuing for Thursday’s short-week date with the Packers. With that contest likely to feature shootout game script, Young will remain in the low-end QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (knee) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: It’s the first time we’ve seen Young o the injury report with this knee issue, though a full practice today is nothing to worry about. He will be good to go for his date with the Bucs. Young is currently the QB4 by fantasy points per game. Even if he does cool down this week, Young should be in most starting fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 20-of-39 passes for 281 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ 25-14, Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: This game was never quite as easy as many thought it would be given Philadelphia’s injuries. Young looked pretty good, but he was often under pressure, and the Panthers continued to make things harder on themselves with 13 penalties for 149 yards. A few of those really killed the momentum on some Panthers drives. Still, Young made enough big throws and receivers were schemed open into space repeatedly throughout the day. We’d expect that to continue next week against a Bucs defense that might not be as talented as this Eagles one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 29-of-41 passes for 329 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions, adding three yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: The NFL’s passing leader through four weeks, pending Monday Night Football, took complete advantage of a defense still working to find their identity through the first month of play, leaning on his top option in Tetairoa McMillan throughout. Young now leads the league in passing and can only be caught by Tyler Shough on Monday Night Football, while only Kirk Cousins and Brock Purdy have more touchdown passes than Young’s nine. Even more impressive was the fact that he did what he did to the Lions without two of his top three receivers with both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette out of action in Week 4. Young and the Panthers head to their Week 5 bye at 2-2 and alone atop the NFC South, soon to be joined by the winner on Monday night. He’ll be a legitimate QB1 when he returns to action against the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers QB Bryce Young (knee) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young visited the blue medical tent a couple of times after taking a cleat to the knee in Week 3 against the Browns. He reportedly underwent imaging to assess the injury. We never received an official follow-up report, but he is practicing in full already, so the imaging evidently checked out just fine. After years of frustrating performances, Young is suddenly a low-end QB1 against an injury-impacted Lions pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (leg) will undergo imaging “just to make sure” on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Canales didn’t want to get specific about Young’s status after he took a cleat to the leg, but deferred also to the idea of “other things.” It’s never incredible news to be looking down the barrel of imaging, but Young was able to return and play through the injury on Sunday and this has the feel of an “out of an abundance of concern” test for the 25-year-old quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 26-of-48 passes for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Panthers’ 21-18, Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young was also in and out of the blue tent with a “lower-body injury” head coach Dave Canales said was affecting the power on some of his throws. That does not include his game-sealing interception, which was a batted pass around the 0:10 mark as a timeout-less Panthers offense desperately drove for what would have been a game-tying field goal. It was a day of adversity on the road, as Young also lost Jalen Coker to a quad injury after the wideout entered the proceedings with an ankle issue. That was one reason Young was spreading the ball around to fantasy nonentities like Brycen Tremayne and Mitchell Evans. The Browns put the clamps on Tetairoa McMillan. Today was probably an inevitable correction to Young’s sizzling start, though the volume is still what fantasy managers are looking for. He has a bounce-back Week 4 spot in the defense-less Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-6 targets for 53 yards with a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was able to bring in a score between a pair of defenders to give the Pack a 6-0 lead in the first quarter. That’s back-to-back games for the tight end with a score, and three in the first half of 2026. Kraft has seen a similar amount of involvement throughout the campaign, and he’ll likely put up a similar statline — hopefully with a touchdown for fantasy managers who roster him — in Week 9 versus the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-6 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft found the end zone on a 14-yard touchdown near the end of the second quarter, giving him his second touchdown of the season and his first since Week 4 against the Buccaneers. Kraft has seen six or more targets in four of his last five games and has posted double-digit PPR points in three of his last four. Even when he isn’t finding the end zone, his volume, coupled with his big-play ability, is enough to keep him in the TE1 conversation. Kraft gets a nice matchup next week against the Panthers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was forced from the game in the second quarter after taking a scary hit to his thigh area that generated torsion on his knee while his foot was still planted. It was the opposite knee to the one he injured a season ago and the veteran tight end would miss only one drive before returning to the game after the half, providing a collective sigh of relief for fantasy managers that have tasted the despair of a major knee injury already. Kraft could be busy in Week 7 against the defense allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends when the Packers face off against the division rival Lions in a potential shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-5 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The five-catch effort was Kraft’s second straight after previously having zero. His 54 yards were also his most since Week 1. His 46-yard reception in the third quarter was his longest of the season. All of that is good, though it was still somewhat disappointing amidst a 367-yard Jordan Love outburst where Christian Watson and Matthew Golden both eased by 100 yards. Kraft is averaging a pedestrian six targets. He’s going to need both more looks and big plays to remain a higher-end TE1. It will nevertheless be impossible to bench him for Week 6 against the Cowboys’ shaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-7 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Jordan Love made it a point to get Kraft going in this game, peppering him with easy-button targets throughout the contest. Kraft led the team with a 23 percent target share. His six grabs also led the team and are a new season high. He found the end zone with an impressive toe-dragging catch at the goal line. Kraft is still looking for the explosive play, but the team is getting him more involved every week. He is back in the TE1 ranks after a slow couple of weeks to start the season. Kraft will look to stay hot versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft has not yet looked himself after recovering from a torn ACL suffered in 2025, this time committing two drops for the first time in his career. To add additional context, Kraft has never had more than three drops in an entire season entering his fourth year in the league. The game plan clearly consisted of getting Kraft involved early to circumvent the offensive line struggles, but the connection with Jordan Love was off throughout. Kraft appears likely to need time to get back to full speed for the Packers, although his snaps and route participation rate were back to normal for the second consecutive week. Fantasy managers are likely forced to ride through the turbulence considering the state of the tight end position throughout the league, but he is a shaky start ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The good news is that Kraft played 52 of the team’s 53 snaps and ran a route on 32 of their 34 dropbacks. The bad news is that he wasn’t commanding targets, and he also fumbled one of his catches, but the replay review couldn’t determine for sure who recovered it, so the Packers were able to maintain possession. Perhaps we should have been a little less aggressive in expecting Kraft to return from tearing his ACL less than a year ago and go right back to being himself at the start of the season. His role remains elite, but it may take another couple of weeks before he’s physically able to play like we’re used to seeing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft, who tore his ACL in Week 9 last year, told reporters he would not be on a snap count in Week 1. He was. Kraft ran 20 routes to Jonnu Smith’s 18. The good news is that Kraft looked as explosive as ever, racking up gains of 30, 23, and 12 yards. Even with the weak route rate, this goes down as a win for a player whose game is built around big plays. His route rate should climb in the coming weeks, keeping him in the TE1 mix versus the Jets next Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Packers signed TE Tucker Kraft to a four-year, $75 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Kraft’s deal, which runs through the 2030 season, has a maximum value of $92 million and includes a $26.5 million signing bonus. He’s now the NFL’s highest-paid tight end. Kraft had 32 receptions, 489 yards and six touchdowns before tearing his ACL in Week 9 last year. Not on the injury report for Week 1, Kraft is a surefire TE1 even in a tough matchup against the Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel’s Tom Silverstein reports that the Packers and TE Tucker Kraft are unlikely to agree on a contract extension before the season opener.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Silverstein believes the deal’s total value likely isn’t as important to the Packers as the structure. Kraft is still likely to reset the tight end market, but since he is returning from a season-ending ACL tear and has “yet to show he’s picked up where he left off last year, it may take some time for the deal to come together.” In the meantime, as long as he takes the field, Kraft can be treated as a TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 8-of-10 targets for 113 yards in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The fact that Watson was able to even play in the second half was incredible, as the 27-year-old was forced to be examined at the hospital following a chest injury. He didn’t do much after putting up 100 yards in the first half, but again, that’s not really the story here. Watson told reporters after the game that he was coughing up blood and suffered a fractured rib before returning. Assuming no setbacks, he’s a WR1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots, but keep in mind Christian Gonzalez — on top of this injury — can make things difficult.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (chest) returned to action in Week 8 against the Panthers in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson went to the hospital to have his chest injury examined, but obviously checked out well if the Packers were willing to reinsert him into a game where they were leading by two scores. It’s a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, as Watson has been sensational Thursday night with six catches for 100 yards in just one half thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated and will head to the hospital to be further examined. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson remained limited through the first two practices this week. We do not yet know his Friday participation level, but he seems to be ready for action. Watson belongs in the WR1 tier against a Lions’ pass defense that has freely surrendered big plays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson appears to just be being managed at this point as Matt LaFleur said there are no concerns on him playing in Week 7. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Watson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Matt LaFleur said he has no concerns about Christian Watson’s ankle injury ahead of the Packers’ Week 7 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The same is true of Matthew Golden, who is dealing with a shoulder issue. Both players were estimated as limited participants for Wednesday’s walkthrough. It doesn’t look like either wideout is at risk of missing the Packers’ upcoming shootout with Detroit. Watson is currently fifth in the league in receiving yards at 538. Golden is sixth at 501. Both players hold a spot in the WR1 ranks heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The Packers held a walkthrough today, so Watson’s status is only an estimate from the team. Given his lengthy injury history, fantasy managers should keep an eye on Green Bay’s injury report tomorrow, though we suspect this isn’t a major issue for Watson. Assuming he gets up to a full practice at some point this week, Watson will be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 versus Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 3-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson drew lockdown corner Joey Porter Jr. for much of the game, something that aided teammate Matthew Golden in leading the team in both targets and receiving in the win. The talented fifth-year receiver is already within 74 yards of setting a new career high in receiving while also being just one touchdown shy of a new high water mark, two achievements he will look to unlock when the Packers face off against the Lions in a potential shootout in Week 7. Watson remains a back-end WR1 for that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson’s 143-yard outburst was the third highest receiving total of his career, joining a Week 11 2024 effort and his 6/147/2 broadside against the Vikings this Week 1. Rather amazingly, the two-score effort was his seventh. This one came in true Watson fashion, as he found the end zone from 42 and 53 yards out. For the 42-yarder he ran right by the defense. For the 53-yarder, he high-pointed the ball off the defender’s helmet in the end zone. It was just that kind of day for the Packers, and it’s been just that kind of season for a wideout in Watson who continues to break out. Now firmly in the weekly WR1 mix, Watson has a potential Week 6 smash spot in the sorry Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: After scoring four touchdowns over the first three weeks, Watson finally cooled off with his first quiet game of the year. Jordan Love couldn’t get the deep ball going in this game and funneled the short targets to Tucker Kraft and Matthew Golden, leaving Watson without much to do. For a player known for having a low floor, 47 yards is a stunningly reasonable floor game. Watson is simply too good at picking up chunk gains to have the bottom truly fall out. He remains a boom/bust WR2 for his Week 5 date with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 7-of-13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden is rarely boring, that’s for sure. He dropped two passes, and one of those was a wide-open touchdown in the second quarter. The good news for Golden, Jordan Love and fantasy managers was that he was wide open again on the next play, and he was able to bring that pass in. Golden’s athleticism and ability to get down field is unquestionable, but to say the efficiency isn’t there is an understatement. He’ll be back at it in Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is active for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden got in a lone limited session in preparation for the team’s Week 8 meeting with the Panthers on a short week, ultimately able to go as he looks to continue to recent hot stretch in fantasy production. No limitation in expected role has been passed by the team, meaning Golden should be good to go for a normal workload against the Panthers. Fantasy managers can confidently insert him into Week 8 rosters as an upside WR2. Inactive for the Packers are TE Jonnu Smith, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, G Donovan Jennings, C Sean Rhyan, and G Travis Glover.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden was estimated as a DNP for two walkthroughs this week before being limited in the Packers’ only real session. The short turnaround to Thursday Night Football likely forced the Packers to take an extra cautious approach with him in practice. While he almost certainly isn’t at 100 percent, Golden looks like a good bet to play in a sneaky shootout with the Panthers tonight. He will be on the WR1/2 border if he gets the green light.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is questionable for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: The Packers held two walkthrough practices to start the week. Golden was estimated as a DNP for both. He was limited in the team’s final practice before being hit with the questionable tag. Fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-time decision for tomorrow’s game. Savion Williams has been operating as the team’s No. 3 receiver over the past two weeks. He would presumably be the next man up if Golden can’t go, though Williams would still be a high-risk FLEX bet for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said the team is “still working through it” when asked if WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) will play Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky relayed LaFleur’s noncommittal response to questions on Golden’s status. LaFleur said the team hopes Golden plays, but the 23-year-old has been an estimated DNP for the first two practices of the week due to shoulder and foot injuries. With the Packers playing on a short week against the Panthers, Golden’s status will likely rely on the final practice report before a Week 8 Thursday showdown against Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: This does not have us optimistic that Golden will play on Thursday night. If he’s sidelined, Savion Williams will be a candidate for more work on offense and perhaps a worthwhile FLEX streamer, while Tucker Kraft will likely ascend to the No. 2 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers listed Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) as a DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden has been dealing with the shoulder injury since last week, but the foot injury is a new one. While this is only an estimated injury report, the DNP is still mildly concerning for Golden, with the Packers playing on a short week. His status will be one to monitor in the coming days, but hopefully this is a minor issue. Golden played the entirety of the game in Week 7’s loss to the Lions and didn’t appear to be hampered by any nagging issues. We’ll see if he get upgraded to a limited participant on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden’s 12 targets led all Packers receivers, but the speedster was unable to convert them into anything meaningful. Of the 12 targets Golden saw, four came on passes of 20-plus air yards. He managed to secure one of those passes for a 22-yard gain, but that was all he could manage in what ended up being a relatively low-scoring game despite the two teams combining for over 700 offensive yards. The 39 yards Golden posted on Sunday were good for his second-lowest total of the season, but he’s an air-yards king who is seeing the kind of volume we expect of a true WR1. He’s primed for a bounce-back in next week’s game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: A few Packers got a little banged up against the Cowboys last week, including Golden, but the breakout second-year wide receiver is good to go. This game profiles as a fantasy-friendly shootout. Golden should be started as a high-end WR2 with solid upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden appears to just be being managed at this point as Packers coach Matt LaFleur said there were no concerns on him playing in Week 7 on Wednesday. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Golden. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers while also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker’s fumble came on the last play of the game as the Panthers played pitchy woo woo in their attempt to tie the game. The 24-year-old didn’t have a catch in the first half, but salvaged his fantasy day — to a point, anyway — with a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young. The 24-year-old has just three catches over the last two games, and he’ll try and get things going against the Broncos in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was at little risk of missing tomorrow’s game after getting in a full practice on Tuesday. He was listed as a full participant again today before being cleared for action. Despite the quiet Week 7 showing, which saw Coker catch just one pass, fantasy managers should still treat him as a WR2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (shoulder) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Seems there’s little doubt that Coker will play on Thursday night. He’ll likely be removed from the injury report on Wednesday. Even after last week’s fiasco he likely belongs in the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers listed Jalen Coker (shoulder) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: The Panthers won’t have their first official practice until Tuesday, but Coker would have been limited on Monday had the team been on the field. Coker caught one pass for nine yards in Week 7’s loss to the Buccaneers. His struggles came on a day when the entire Panthers offense was stymied for much of the day, so hopefully he’ll be in line to bounce back against the Packers on Thursday if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was also the intended target on the first of Bryce Young’s two interceptions. The wideout fell down, leading to the miscue. It was simply a nightmarish day for the Panthers’ offense, who also watched Young cough up a fumble-six. With the Panthers trailing 33-6 at halftime and 43-6 at the 10:21 mark of the fourth, the first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. A disaster for fantasy managers, but likely a short-lived one with the Panthers heading to Green Bay for a short-week Thursday night matchup with the Pack. Coker must still be fired up as a WR2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 6-of-13 passes for 97 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker missed Week 4 with a quad injury but was able to heal up over the bye week and play a full complement of snaps in Week 6. Initial reports had him playing 59 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 39 of 46 dropbacks, which was second most on the team. He also led the team in targets, catches, and receiving yards. He’s a rock-solid WR2 against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters earlier this week that Coker was returning from both quad and ankle injuries, though the team is only listing the quad issue. We take this as a good sign for his overall health. Coker can be treated as a WR2 in his first game back, facing an Eagles defense that struggles to cover opposing slot receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker (quad) is “on track” to play in Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was spotted practicing on Tuesday (there will be no injury report for this one) and seems like he’s well on track to return. He’ll be a fringe WR2/WR3 against the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quadricep) is inactive for Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: This was though to be the most likely scenario after head coach Dave Canales told reporters Friday that the team would elevate Ja’Seem Reed if the belief was that Coker could not go on Sunday Night Football. Reed was, in fact, elevated Saturday and Coker was declared inactive. Brycen Tremaine appears to be in line for a featured role after playing 81 percent of the team’s offensive snaps a week ago. Expect John Metchie to also see additional snaps and opportunities, while David Moore could see package usage on the perimeter. Also inactive for the Panthers are TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, G Damien Lewis, OT Albert Reese, and DT Cam Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jalen Coker (quad) is “unlikely to play” in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker injured his quad in Week 3. He got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. It doesn’t sound like a long-term injury, but the team is being cautious with a young wideout who has already suffered multiple lower-body injuries this year. With Xavier Legette on IR, Brycen Tremayne is Carolina’s WR2 for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 40 yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Feel lucky McMillan even reached those marks, as the Panthers simply did not compete in a game where they committed four turnovers and trailed 33-6 at halftime. The first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. McMillan had a better go of it than Jalen Coker, who caught one pass and fell down to create an interception. A shambles, though one the Panthers have to move on from quickly, as they are headed to Green Bay for a potential short-week shootout on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 passes for 86 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan saw a lot of Quinyon Mitchell in tight coverage on Sunday, but he had a solid day that could have been much better after a fourth-quarter pass went off his hands in the end zone. It would have been a difficult catch with Mitchell draped all over him, but it was a catchable pass. More importantly, it shows that McMillan remains a key piece of this passing game, and he did run the most routes of any receiver on the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 14-of-16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan set career highs in both receptions and yardage in the first half with nine catches for 147 yards before the break. He operated as the clear alpha in a pass attack without both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, routinely dusting everyone the Lions had at their disposal in an injury-ravaged secondary. While the receiving line surely turns heads, fantasy managers were left even more ecstatic about the way in which he was utilized, with the second-year receiver catching six passes for 94 yards and both touchdowns while aligned in the slot. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik is providing structure, sequencing, and situational tendencies unlike anything fans had grown accustomed to when head coach Dave Canales was helming the offense, resulting in quarterback Bryce Young leading the league in passing while averaging more than 30 points per game through the first month of play. McMillan’s ceiling remains sky-high as a legitimate WR1 when the Panthers square off against the Eagles fin Week 6 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: By far McMillan’s quietest outing of the young season came with Jalen Coker departing midway through with a quad injury. No. 3 Xavier Legette didn’t even suit up as he battled a knee issue. That allowed the Browns’ defense to key in on T-Mac, and key they did. Fill-in No. 2 Brycen Tremayne took advantage with four receptions for a team-leading 83 yards. Heinous stuff for McMillan managers, but he has an immediate Week 4 bounce-back spot in the defense-less Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5-of-10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan took a backseat to Jalen Coker last week. The opportunities were distributed more evenly this time around. McMillan led the team with 10 targets and a 28 percent target share. Coker wasn’t far behind with nine targets. McMillan easily led the team in yards, though Coker caught eight balls and Darren Waller popped up for a two-score game. This offense may ultimately be too spread out for McMillan to reach his full potential, but Week 2 reaffirmed his status as the team’s top dog. He will be in the WR2 mix when the Panthers take on the Browns next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5-of-8 targets for 75 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan played distant second fiddle to Jalen Coker, who cooked the Chicago secondary for 138 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Panthers in air yards and targets. A bulked-up McMillan appeared a little slower than he was as a rookie in 2025, and had trouble separating for most of the game. Coker’s involvement and Bryce Young’s trust in his WR2 might be a problem for McMillan’s upside this season. He should, however, remains a decent weekly floor option, including next week against a gettable Atlanta defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that the Panthers will “likely” decide whether to offer QB Bryce Young an extension in the 2027 offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Young has two years remaining on his contract, but is currently eligible for an extension. According to Wolfe, Young needs to improve in three areas. First, Young must check down when it’s the responsible thing to do, in turn elevating his completion rate to the “high 60s, low 70s” range. Second, Young must be comfortable playing with tempo and diverse personnel formations, including WR Tetairoa McMillan lining up in the slot more often. Third, Young must play quickly and decisively. Whether he can accomplish these feats is up in the air. He’s a mid-to-low QB2 for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Person reports that Panthers WR Chris Brazzell will undergo season-ending knee surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Brazzell was initially expected to avoid surgery and instead rehab the “moderate LCL tear in his left knee.” After getting a second opinion, the player and team decided surgery was the “best option” for the rookie’s long-term health. According to Person, Brazzell was expected to challenge WR Xavier Legette for the No. 3 role, while also potentially allowing WR Tetairoa McMillan to line up in the slot more often. The latter storyline is worth tracking. Hopefully, the plan remains in place and Brazzell makes a full recovery ahead of the 2027 season. We expect him to be placed on injured reserve soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Person reports that Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan (foot) practiced at training camp on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan was a limited participant in spring practices due to a foot issue. As of June 10th, he was hoping to be ready for training camp. As of yesterday, that was indeed the case, which is great to hear. McMillan, 23, took home Offensive Rookie of the Year honors last year via a 70/1,014/7 receiving line. He aims to build on that this season, and NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reported yesterday that the team hopes to have McMillan run routes from the slot “a lot more” this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers, adding seven receptions for 38 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard was easily the most effective offensive player for the Panthers, but that’s at least partially an insult to everyone else as much as it was compliment to him. The tailback was able to make the most of the limited rushing room, and with Bryce Young having zero time to throw the football, he was a frequent target of Young’s checkdowns. Trevor Etienne received just one carry for one yard, meanwhile. Hubbard’s usage makes him a high-end RB2 for Week 9 against the Broncos, even if it’s more floor than ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Panthers’ 43-13, Week 7 loss to the Bucs, adding four receptions for 27 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: With Bryce Young committing three turnovers — killing drives and setting up Bucs short fields that took the Panthers out of run-friendly game script — Hubbard had little shot at providing fantasy-friendly returns this afternoon unless he found the end zone late. He did not, with those honors going to “Anthony Tyus III” in garbage time. It was just one of those days in Charlotte. Thankfully the Panthers don’t have long to stew, as they must now get ready for a short-week Thursday evening road date with the Packers. With most Pack — and Panthers — games projecting as shootouts these days, Hubbard will remain safely ensconced in the high-end RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 28 times for 120 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: It wasn’t easy for Hubbard, who didn’t have many runs over 10 yards, but he ran hard, broke tackles, and was able to find the end zone in the fourth quarter for a short touchdown run. Still, the Panthers did have some issues running the ball up the gut against the Eagles and continued to do it, rather than try to get Hubbard going on the edge. Trevor Etienne was the only other running back to have a carry in this game, and he had just one rush, so this backfield belongs entirely to Hubbard, which is tremendous for his fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 20 times for 122 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions, adding seven yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard’s successes on the ground allowed the Panthers to remain balanced on a night they were without two of their top three wide receivers due to the absences of Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, cashing in on two scores from 15 and two yards out. Hubbard appears to be locked into an RB1 workload in the absence of Jonathan Brooks, who will be out for 6-8 weeks after undergoing core muscle surgery. His 26 opportunities dwarfed the six of current backup AJ Dillon, the latter of whom gained just seven total yards on six touches. Fantasy managers can start Hubbard with confidence when the team returns from their bye to face the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 19 times for 82 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns, adding four receptions for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: With Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve, Hubbard’s 23 touches were nine more than he handled in Week 2, and 10 more than Week 1. Although he ceded a smattering of snaps to new backup AJ Dillon, he was a near every-down player in this road loss. Hubbard lacks high-end fantasy upside, but his floor right now is very much that of a locked-in RB2. That will be especially true for matchups like next week’s date with the defensively-challenged Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Panthers will host a workout for Austin Ekeler, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Carolina is in need of some backfield reinforcements after losing Jonathon Brooks to a core injury that will leave him sidelined for at least six weeks. AJ Dillon is set to fill in for Brooks while Chub Hubbard presumably continues as the team’s lead back. Ekeler, 31, who hasn’t played since injuring his Achilles last September, could be an emergency running back if Hubbard or Dillon go down with injuries in the coming weeks. First he’ll need to make the squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 12 times for 53 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons, adding two catches for 11 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard operated as the Panthers’ unquestioned RB1, out-carrying Jonathon Brooks 12-5. He got on the board early with a touchdown catch near the goal line. It was his second touchdown grab of the year and his third time finding the end zone in total. Brooks also left the game early with a groin injury and his status for Week 3 is up in the air. Hubbard was already going to project for RB2 numbers with Brooks in the middle. He will push to the middle of the RB2 pack if Brooks is out versus the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard had ten rushes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding three catches for 38 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard was the clearcut lead back for the run-heavy Carolina offense. Jonathon Brooks saw five touches on the day, and ran six pass routes for 29 routes for Hubbard, who was the Panthers’ primary red zone back throughout the game. For now Hubbard’s role in the run-first Panthers offense seems secure while the team eases Brooks into action. That could change at some point this season. Hubbard will be a locked-in RB2 option next week against a middling Falcons defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Jonathon Brooks had four rushes for 14 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding one catch for 48 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: In his first regular season action, Brooks played well behind lead back Chuba Hubbard, who finished the day with ten carries and three receptions. The highlight of Brooks’ day came on a sideline throw from Bryce Young that went for 48 yards. Brooks, coming off multiple major knee injuries, showed impressive burst and speed on the catch and run. That Hubbard was the team’s primary option inside the ten yard line is bad news for Brooks’ touchdown upside in the Carolina offense. For now he profiles as a bench stash in case Hubbard misses time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: We’ll have a better sense of Brooks’ Week 1 availability in a few hours when the Panthers release their final injury report for the week, but the third-year back logged limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday and is trending in the right direction for Sunday’s game against the Bears. If he’s active, Brooks is expected to split touches with Chuba Hubbard, which could put a hard cap on both players’ upside in the season-opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 30-of-41 passes for 288 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Packers’ 27-19, Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love completed 17 of his first 20 passes, and two of those incompletions were drops. He threw a seed to Tucker Kraft for his first touchdown between defenders, found Matthew Golden wide open in the end zone for his second score — one play after Golden dropped a touchdown — and connected with Josh Jacobs for his third score of the day. The interception was a heinous decision where he didn’t see the safety, but outside of that, it was an impressive evening for the 27-year-old. Love gets zero, well, love from the run game and doesn’t have a quality offensive line, but he’s still putting up respectable numbers. He’ll look to add to those numbers in Week 9 against the Patriots in what should be a fun matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 27-of-45 passes for 274 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 20-17, Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Even with Josh Jacobs back in the mix, the Packers still struggled to get the ground game going. As a result, Love aired it out early and often, throwing a ridiculous 10 passes for 20-plus yards, but only three were completed. Love’s first touchdown pass came on a third-and-nine when he connected with Tucker Kraft for a 14-yard score, and in the third quarter, a short pass to Jacobs was turned upfield for a 25-yard touchdown after Jacobs tight-roped along the sideline to find pay dirt. Love nearly connected with Jacobs for another score late in the fourth quarter, but Jacobs was unable to complete the diving catch in the end zone for the go-ahead score. On the next play, Trey Smack had a 35-yard field goal blocked, which ultimately set the Lions up for the game-winning field goal on the ensuing drive. Love continues to play an aggressive style of football, airing it out to his speedsters in Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. He and the Packers now have a short turnaround to prepare for the Panthers in Week 8, where he will be on the QB1 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was limited on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that his starting quarterback was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys. Hopefully, he is feeling much better by now. This divisional showdown looks like one of the most fantasy-friendly game environments in Week 7. He’s a QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s limited session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Love was “pretty beat up” after Sunday night, but Love doesn’t appear to be in any danger of missing the game. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Jordan Love (back) was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love got checked out by the team’s chiropractor after the game and was listed as limited for yesterday’s practice. LaFleur told reporters they haven’t determined whether he will be limited for today’s session. Either way, he said yesterday that there is no chance Love misses Week 7, so the practice reports are a moot point. Love is a top-half QB1 for his date with Detroit this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Wednesday’s session was a walkthrough, so this is just an estimate from the team. We don’t believe it will be much of an issue for Love in Week 7. Barring a setback, Love will remain in the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Lions on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-41 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 23-13, Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love isn’t typically a threat to punch in a touchdown with his legs, but the state of the backfield and flow of the game gave him that opportunity late in the second quarter, which he would cash in for his first rushing score since Week 11 of 2024. Fantasy managers shouldn’t get too excited about the touchdown on the ground considering running back Josh Jacobs is expected to be activated from the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Even so, Love has now accounted for two touchdowns in all six games played through the first third of the season and has gone over 300 yards through the air in half his appearances to start the 2026 season, leaving plenty of meat on the bone for continued fantasy production as the Packers enter their most difficult stretch of the schedule. Love remains a locked-in QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the division rival Lions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 25-of-31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers’ 31-7, Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: With the Packers’ backs against the wall in a rivalry grudge match, Love had one of the best starts of his NFL life by simply cutting it loose. His 367 yards passing were the third most of his career, and accompanied by zero turnovers. He found each of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft for at least one 46-yard gain, including a 53-yard touchdown to Watson. That does not include an earlier 42-yard scoring strike to Watson. Each score had serious air underneath them. This really was Love airing it out, something less competent quarterbacks had been struggling to do vs. the Bears’ vulnerable defense. We have seen this Love and Packers movie before — a step forward not followed by another move in the right direction — but neither Packers fans nor fantasy managers could have asked for more this afternoon. Love will have a good shot at keeping the good vibes going vs. the Cowboys’ struggling defense in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 22-of-30 passes for 197 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 17-14, Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Green Bay entered this game in desperate need of a win. They got it, though it was not pretty. Kneel downs aside, the Packers had five drives that gained fewer than 10 yards. Love nearly threw the game away with an interception straight into the hands of Jacob Parris in the red zone with less than four minutes left on the clock. The Bucs could not score on the ensuing drive and Love got to kneel out the clock. The Packers’ offense still looked disjointed today. They simply found an opponent that wasn’t a threat to put more than a handful of points on the board. Love is slipping further back in the QB2 ranks as he prepares to take on the Bears in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 28-of-53 passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 35-14, Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was completely overrun by consistent pressure throughout on a night the Packers attempted 53 passes to just eight running back carries. The Atlanta defensive line took advantage of mounting injuries and ineffective play along the Green Bay offensive line to disrupt any offensive rhythm for the Packers. Love’s two touchdowns went to his top two options through the air in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, the latter of whom notched the first regular season touchdown of his young career late in the fourth quarter. Matt LaFleur, Love, and the rest of the Packers have some significant work to do if they are to save their quickly sinking season. Love falls to a middling QB2 ahead of a road matchup with an aggressive Buccaneers defense in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, OLB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, G Damien Lewis, G Torricelli Simpkins, and DT Bobby Brown inactive for Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: The Panthers are extremely shorthanded along the offensive line and on the defensive side of the ball, most notably in the secondary and with the pass rush. That could spell trouble agains the high-powered Green Bay passing game, particularly with wide receiver Matthew Golden active. The Panthers look to halt their recent skid on the road in hostile territory at Lambeau Field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, WR John Metchie, QB Haynes King, S Zakee Wheatley, OT Albert Reese, OLB Patrick Jones II, and DT Cam Jackson inactive for Week 1 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders, who worked through a lingering ankle injury this offseason, won’t suit up for the team’s season opener. That leaves Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble as the Panthers’ top two tight ends against Chicago. Waller will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 option who probably won’t run many routes in the run-first Carolina offense. Tremble should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person reports Ja’Tavion Sanders (ankle) looked good running around in the early offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders broke his ankle in Week 17 against the Seahawks, ending his season. It would seem that he’s on track to participate in training camp, and this report doesn’t really dwell on if he’ll be a possibility for the PUP list. In theory, Sanders could still emerge as the preferred pass-catching option at the position for the Panthers. In actuality, the 2024 fourth-rounder probably would have made more strides in either of the past two years if that was going to happen. He’s simply a TE3 hold in deep leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person believes the Panthers could target TE Kenyon Sadiq in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Person said the Panthers, who hold the 19th pick in the 2026 draft, could target two Oregon players: Sadiq, who had 51 receptions for 560 yards and eight touchdowns in his final collegiate season, and safety Dillon Thieneman, one of the most sought-after secondary options in this year’s draft. The team would likely have to trade up to make sure they have a shot at Sadiq, who would join Tommy Tremble and Ja’Tavion Sanders in the Carolina tight end room if he lands with the Panthers. The Panthers in 2025 targeted the tight end position at a 21 percent clip, the seventh lowest mark in the NFL. “Could that change with Brad Idzik taking over the play calling and the addition of offensive specialist Darrell Bevell, who was in Seattle with Canales when the Seahawks traded for All-Pro tight end Jimmy Graham?” Person said. “Possibly.” Sadiq, who ranks 11th in yards per route run among tight ends in the 2026 draft class, would probably be a rotational player in Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers GM Dan Morgan says he believes Ja’Tavion Sanders (ankle) will be ready for the team’s offseason program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders underwent season-ending ankle surgery late last season and was placed on injured reserve before the Week 18 finale. Sanders, who was selected in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL Draft, caught just 29 passes for 190 yards and one touchdown last season while starting five of the 13 games he appeared in. The third-year tight end will likely battle with Tommy Tremble for playing time this season, but the Panthers could also look to add to their tight end room through the draft with a talented rookie class incoming.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Ja’Tavion Sanders (ankle) would undergo season-ending surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: He’ll almost certainly be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 18’s game against the Buccaneers. Sanders broke his ankle on Carolina’s first play from scrimmage yesterday against the Seahawks. The 2024 fourth-rounder enters the 2026 offseason in the third year of his rookie contract having not taken a noticeable step forward in his sophomore year while struggling through a midseason high-ankle sprain. He doesn’t figure to offer a lot in fantasy leagues in 2026 from where we sit at the end of the 2025 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders suffered an ankle injury in Carolina’s Week 17 game against the Seahawks and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders’ right foot got rolled up run blocking on the literal first play of the game. He was in a world of pain before being carted to the locker room. It’s quite possible the 22-year-old’s season is through. The second-year pro entered today sitting on a 29/190/1 line, with the touchdown coming last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught both of his targets for nine yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 16 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders was targeted just twice, but one of those targets was a six-yard touchdown catch. The other one was an attempted hurdle for a three-yard gain in the first half. Rookie Mitchell Evans caught three passes for 23 yards as well. The tight end spot in Carolina is a mix of multiple players. Sanders ran 20 routes and saw 31 snaps, while Tommy Tremble saw 23 snaps and Evans saw 16 snaps. Sanders is the pass-catching tight end while Evans is more of the blocker, but neither should be on fantasy radars for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught all four of his targets for 22 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders led the team’s tight ends in targets and catches, but Tommy Tremble was the hero of the day with a 54-yard reception to set up a game-winning field goal. Rookie tight end Mitchell Evans also caught a pair of passes. With all three tight ends seeing some work every week, Sanders is barely in the TE2 mix ahead of Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught 5-of-5 targets for 32 yards in Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jatavion-s.analysis: Sanders flashed with at least five receptions in a game for the second time this season. The second-year tight end is at the mercy of the Panthers’ passing game when it comes to fantasy value, though. Bryce Young has thrown for at least 200 yards in a game once all year so it’s best to look elsewhere for a tight end in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Colts have told teams they won’t move Adetomiwa Adebawore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.analysis: Adebawore, a fourth-round pick in 2023, played under 200 snaps in each of his first two seasons and was a pass-rush specialist in 2025. In 2026, he’s taken a step forward, with an 81.8 PFF grade buoyed by an 86.3 pass rush grade. It would be reasonable to expect the Colts to try to extend a player like this, but they sure didn’t seem to have any urgency to do it before the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.headline: Colts selected Northwestern DT Adetomiwa Adebawore with the No. 110 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.analysis: Despite lacking the desired length for edge work and having a three-tech frame, Adebawore (6’2/282) is one of the great athletic marvels from the 2023 NFL Draft class. His 4.49s 40-yard dash is the 10th fastest edge time in the history of the NFL Scouting Combine. If that weren’t impressive enough, he did it at 282 pounds which is 20+ pounds heavier than every single one of the 10 edge players ahead of him on that list (Amare Barno #1 All Time - 4.37). Though he had been a primary edge for his first three years on Northwestern’s campus, last year he logged 261 reps in the B-Gap compared to 440 on the outside. Adeboware’s 80.3 PFF pass rush grade is very solid, but there’s plenty of room for improvement in the run game as Adebawore missed 25.5% of his tackle attempts this year. A success story who bulldozed his way through just about every OL put in front of him last season, He was being considered as a likely mid-Day 3 pedestrian contributor before he took over the Senior Bowl’s 1-on-1 blocking sessions. While there is still some question about whether he plays three tech or edge, Adebawore has tantalizing traits that cannot be taught with an athletic profile of a faster, more agile Ed Oliver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs special teams coach Dave Toub said Harrison Butker is “our kicker.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: “He went 10-for-10 yesterday, with Justin Tucker right there. ... We’re going to keep working it,” Toub continued. It sounds like despite signing Tucker, Butker will continue to kick for the Chiefs. At least this week, anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs signed Justin Tucker, formerly of the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Tucker will start on the Chiefs practice squad. His signing comes a few days after Harrison Butker missed two field goal attempts against the Seahawks. On the season Butker has missed five of his 16 attempts, and over his past 11 games he’s missed seven kicks. Tucker, who recently competed for the Dolphins kicker job, hasn’t kicked since 2024 in Baltimore, when he missed eight of his 30 field goal tries. The Ravens released Tucker in 2025 after 16 massage therapists accused him of sexual misconduct.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker converted both of his field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 15 loss against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker bounced back from his Week 14 miss against the Texans in a close loss. He’s missed just four of his 28 field goal attempts through Week 15. Butker’s fantasy prospects might be affected by Patrick Mahomes’ potential absence after Mahomes went down with a knee injury near the end of KC’s loss to the Bolts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker went 1-for-2 in field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 14 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: He connected from 36 yards and made his only point after attempt, missing from 43 yards at the end of the second quarter when his kick hit off the right upright. That missed field goal contributed to the Chiefs being shut out in the first half for only the third time in quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ career, making the failed conversion slightly more meaningful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs activated K Harrison Butker from injured reserve ahead of Week 15’s matchup with the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Matthew Wright was waived in a corresponding move. The Chiefs designated Butker, who missed a month with a knee injury, to return from injured reserve earlier this week and deemed him good to go after logging three limited practices. He has plenty of time to shake off the rust before the playoffs, but may be difficult to trust in his first game back in the fantasy playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker (knee) is questionable for Week 15 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker practiced in a limited capacity all week, logging his first practice repetitions since undergoing a mid-season meniscus trim in his left knee. Given the Chiefs’ Super Bowl aspirations, the team is unlikely to let him suit up this week if his re-injury risk is significant. If he plays, it stands to reason that he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs designated Harrison Butker (knee) for return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker underwent a meniscus trim on his left knee in November, as he was sent to injured reserve. The talented kicker could play as early as Week 15, however, he understandably makes for a slightly less certain K1 than fantasy managers are used to. It would be unsurprising to see him turn in an up-and-down performance in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs K Matthew Wright will start in Week 14.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: The journeyman kicker made four of his five field goal tries last week in a win against the Raiders and will get at least one more start before Harrison Butker returns from a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve. The Chiefs put K Spencer Shrader on IR this week. Wright is a solid fantasy option with the Chiefs sporting an implied Vegas total of 23.5 points against LA.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs placed K Harrison Butker (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero was the first on the scene, reporting that Butker is expected to miss 3-4 weeks due to a meniscus injury in his left knee — which is his non-kicking knee. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport later reported that Butker is expected to have surgery to trim his meniscus, which is why the team went ahead and placed him on injured reserve. In a corresponding move, the Chiefs have already signed kicker Spencer Shrader off the Jets practice squad. Shrader is a rookie who went undrafted out of Notre Dame earlier this year. During his five years of college, he converted on 43-of-62 field goals while making 98.7 percent of his extra point attempts. He’ll now be tasked with replacing one of the most reliable kickers in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs signed K Harrison Butker to a four-year contract extension worth $25.6 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: The new deal for Butker includes $17 million in guarantees and makes him the league’s highest paid kicker. The former Panthers castoff has been one of the NFL’s best kickers over his seven seasons with Kansas City, hitting 89 percent of his field goal attempts and 94.5 percent of his extra points. After a down year in 2022, Butker came back strong in 2023 with 33 field goals on 35 attempts. He made all five of his attempts of more than 50 yards after struggling from distance in 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Keisean Nixon (shoulder) is questionable for Thursday Night Football against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon was added to the injury report Thursday with a shoulder injury and is now listed questionable for Week 8 against the Panthers. We’ll get his final determination 90-minutes prior to first kick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Keisean Nixon (groin) is not on Green Bay’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: He got in a pair of limited sessions on Thursday and Friday to get off the report. Nixon will be tasked with the unenviable duties of taking on George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb in front of a national audience on Sunday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Keisean Nixon (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon is the Packers’ top outside corner. He has three pass breakups and one interception this year. His absence would be a big loss for a defense that is only slightly above average in EPA per play and points allowed this year. It would be a particularly big development for George Pickens, who leads the Cowboys in outside receiver routes this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers CB Keisean Nixon (neck) left Green Bay’s Week 12 game with the Vikings and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: He suffered a stinger. Kamal Hadden took over at outside corner for the Packers. Luckily for them, Minnesota doesn’t seem to have any interesting in throwing the football today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers agreed to terms with DB Keisean Nixon on a three-year, $18 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon totaled 80 tackles and one interception for the Packers last season, but he’s been more known for his play on special teams. Nixon has been named a First-team All-Pro in back-to-back seasons for his return efforts and has led the league in kick return yards in both of those seasons. Nixon is now under contract with the Packers through the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers re-signed CB/KR Keisean Nixon to a one-year, $6 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: In his first year as a returner, Nixon turned in an All-Pro effort, leading the league in kick returns (35) and kick return yards (105). Nixon also appeared on 290 defensive snaps last season, but was a liability in coverage, allowing 22 receptions on 28 targets for 214 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers signed CB Keisean Nixon, formerly of the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon is a three-year NFL vet who joined the Raiders as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2019. Nixon has appeared in 40 career games throughout his career, with most of his snaps coming on special teams. His signing with the Packers reunites him with former Raiders interim head coach Rich Bisaccia, who is now Green Bay’s special teams coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: South Carolina senior CB Keisean Nixon (neck) has been ruled out for the Belk Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon (5'11/193) was experiencing numbness and soreness during the regular season, with a CAT scan administered after the close of the campaign revealing that he was dealing with a fracture in his neck. Yikes. This injury for all intents and purposes ends the cornerback’s season. He has already accepted an invitation to the East-West Shrine Game as he looks to get his draft process started. Just how healthy he will be for that postseason evaluation bowl remains to be seen. Draft Analyst’s Tony Pauline stamped him with a UDFA grade over the summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: South Carolina senior CB Keisean Nixon accepted an invitation to the East-West Shrine Game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon (5'11/193) was a four-star commitment from the JUCO ranks who spent two years in the Gamecocks secondary. He gets quality reviews for his ability to help in the run game, and also as an instinctive defender as a cover corner. He profiles best in the slot, but he’ll get a chance to show his coverage skills on the outside as well. He projects as a Day 3 selection at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: South Carolina signed four-star JUCO DB Keisean Nixon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Score one for Will Muschamp, who also grabbed former Clemson cornerback Kaleb Chalmers on the JUCO trail. Nixon enrolled at South Carolina this month, which means he’ll be ready to roll for spring practices. “Nixon is a 6-foot, 200-pound cornerback with the length and physicality to play anywhere in the secondary,” wrote ESPN’s Gerry Hamilton. “A complete player, Nixon sheds blocks quickly and closes with the ability to strike against the run. In coverage, he’s instinctive and adept in zone with quick and explosive reactions to get his hands on passes.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (rest) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving was absent from Thursday’s sessions with an official “rest” designation, allowing fantasy managers to breath a collective sigh of relief after the veteran back has morphed into a borderline workhorse in recent games. Managers can likely continue forward with Irving in their starting lineups as an upside RB2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Gainwell missed Wednesday’s session with the hip issue. He will likely be listed as limited today, but that still puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Falcons. Gainwell racked up 14 carries in a blowout win over the Panthers last week, but that hasn’t been the norm for him. Gainwell is averaging 6.4 touches per game and has topped out at three receptions in a week. He is buried in the RB4 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Gainwell suffered the hip injury while logging a season-high 14 rush attempts in Week 7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers and racked up 49 carries as a team. Bucky Irving would be in line for more work on passing downs if Gainwell is out for Week 8. Sean Tucker could also see an uptick in snaps, though his normal role has very little overlap with what Gainwell does. Per usual, Irving looks like a high-end RB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The two-score day on the ground was somehow the first of Irving’s career. He led the way as the Bucs rolled up a ridiculous 258 yards rushing in a stunning road clobbering of the Panthers. That means Irving ceded plenty of work to Kenneth Gainwell and a little to Sean Tucker, but everyone got home as the Bucs simply dominated on the ground. Irving’s scores came from four and one yards out, meaning he had the goal-line advantage on Tucker while the game was still in doubt. It was a really strong performance, and a nice bounce-back effort after a rough Week 6.
