This figures to remain an up and down offense and rushing attack, but Irving has proven to be a high-end RB2 more weeks than not. That will include for Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) is not on the Buccaneers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: As is typically the case with ill players, Irving is good to go for this week’s game. He upgraded to full participation today after getting a limited session in on Thursday. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back has been a volatile producer this season, yet even with last week’s flop, he still totaled 21 touches. That type of workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back is on track to play in Week 7 against the Panthers. The offense is expected to be led by Baker Mayfield (thumb), who will play with a protective plate on his hand to prevent re-injury. Irving should be good to go this week and can be treated as a high-end RB2, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Players missing time because of an illness this early in the weekend almost always get cleared to play by Sunday. We expect no difference from Irving. Coming off his third 20-touch game of the year, Irving remains a high-end RB2 for his Week 7 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 19 times for 46 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers, adding two catches for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving was bottled up on nearly every attempt, with the Steelers’ defensive front simply winning the battle in the trenches far too often. On the bright side, Irving out-carried Kenneth Gainwell 19-2 and saw three targets to Gainwell’s one. The role was there. The production was not. That role was also bolstered by the absence of Sean Tucker, who missed today’s game with a quad injury. Irving will remain in the RB2 mix for Week 7 versus the Panthers, but Tampa Bay’s grizzly offensive environment will prevent him from cracking the RB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sean Tucker (quad) is not expected to play in Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Despite seeing just eight total carries this year, Tucker has two attempts inside the five compared to one for Bucky Irving. Though he isn’t leaving that many total carries behind, Tucker’s absence will still create some extra fantasy value for Irving, who is on the RB1/2 border for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: FOX Sports’ Greg Auman reports that Sean Tucker (quad) will be a pregame decision for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Tucker is officially listed as questionable. If he ends up being inactive, that is good news for Bucky Irving, who handled 23 touches last week, ceding seven to Kenny Gainwell and five to Tucker. Irving warrants borderline RB1/2 treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: Colts signed OT Charlie Heck, formerly of the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: Heck spent the offseason with the Dolphins but did not make their final roster. He has 29 career starts, with all but two of them coming at right tackle. His most recent action came in Tampa Bay, where he started six games in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: Dolphins signed OT Charlie Heck, formerly of the Buccaneers, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: Heck is a six-year veteran of the league who has 29 games of starting experience under his belt. In his lone season with the Buccaneers, Heck started six of the 17 games he appeared in, with all of his starts coming at right tackle. He earned a PFF grade of 45.2 last season while allowing 32 pressures and three sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: Buccaneers signed OT Charlie Heck, formerly of the 49ers, to a one-year, $1.6 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: Heck will serve as a backup swing-tackle option behind the Buccaneers’ bullying offensive tackle duo of LT Tristan Wirfs and RT Luke Goedeke. Heck flashed pass-protection potential early in his career but has settled into a journeyman role. He got into a few games with the 49ers late last year as injuries struck the line, and was previously on the Arizona practice squad after a four-year rookie contract run with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: 49ers signed T Charlie Heck off Arizona’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: The 49ers desperately need bodies with several of their linemen set to miss the final two weeks of the season. Heck played 30 snaps for the Cardinals as a reserve this year and was active in five games. He was a passable backup with the Texans in their Lost Era of 2020-2022, starting 13 games for David Culley’s crew in 2021.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: Texans re-signed OT Charlie Heck to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: Heck, who was a fourth-round pick of the Texans in 2020, can earn up to $3.3 million on this deal, and started four games for them in 2023. The four-year vet has started 21 of the 41 games he’s appeared in for his career, and has allowed eight sacks on 839 pass blocking snaps for PFF. He’ll likely have a chance to earn a role as one of the team’s backup tackles in camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: Texans signed fourth-round OT Charlie Heck to a four-year, $4 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: His rookie deal includes a $710,704 signing bonus. Primarily a blocking tight end in high school, Heck (6'7/311) is still developing after three years as North Carolina’s starting left tackle. Fortunately, he benefits from growing up around the game under his father and former No. 15 overall pick Andy Heck. Charlie’s diverse athletic background translates onto the field as his footwork checks the necessary boxes at the next level. There’s also no question about his toughness after he played through a broken right hand in his senior year. Heck’s timing and technique need to dramatically improve but his existing skillset will allow him to battle for a role at the end of Houston’s roster in camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: Texans traded up with the Rams to select North Carolina OT Charlie Heck with the No. 126 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: Rams soaked up picks No. 136, No. 248, and No. 250 in exchange for Bill O’Brien to trade up. Primarily a blocking tight end in high school, Heck (6'7/311) is still developing after three years as North Carolina’s starting left tackle. Fortunately, he benefits from growing up around the game under his father and former No. 15 overall pick Andy Heck. Charlie’s diverse athletic background translates onto the field as his footwork checks the necessary boxes at the next level. There’s also no question about his toughness after he played through a broken right hand in his senior year. Heck’s timing and technique need to dramatically improve but his existing skillset will allow him to battle for a role at the end of Houston’s roster in camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: Texans traded up with the Rams to select North Carolina T Charlie Heck with the No. 126 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: Primarily a blocking tight end in high school, Heck (6'7/311) is still developing after three years as North Carolina’s starting left tackle. Fortunately, he benefits from growing up around the game under his father and former No. 15 overall pick Andy Heck. Charlie’s diverse athletic background translates onto the field as his footwork checks the necessary boxes at the next level. There’s also no question about his toughness after he played through a broken right hand in his senior year. Heck’s timing and technique need to dramatically improve but his existing skillset will allow him to battle for a role at the end of Houston’s roster in camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: NFL Media’s Lance Zierlein compared North Carolina T Charlie Heck to free agent T Sam Young.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: “Heck has the talent to handle swing tackle duties and should be fully functional in all run-blocking schemes,” Zierlein writes. On the pass-pro front, the analyst is less enthused, calling those sets “just average” while noting that Heck “needs to get on top of rushers with his length early in the rep to maintain feel and widen the arc when needed.” While Heck is not a spectacular athlete -- testing in the 38th SPARQ percentile of NFL offensive linemen -- he comes to the draft well-seasoned after starting 33 games with the Tar Heels.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.headline: NFL Media’s Lance Zierlein compares North Carolina T Charlie Heck to former Miami Dolphins T Sam Young.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-he.analysis: Depending on how you look at it, Young has put together a heck of a career. Young went in the sixth round in 2010 and has made an NFL roster every year since then, playing in 88 games with 21 starts over that span. Considering Zierlein’s praises of Heck’s size and ability to bend with pass-rushers around the edge, it is well within reason for Heck to follow a similar career arc as Young. Zierlein graded Heck as a backup / special teamer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles signed RB Jaydon Blue from the practice squad to the active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Blue was called up as the replacement for Dameon Pierce, who was placed on injured reserve this week. Saquon Barkley entered Week 7 with a lingering hamstring issue. He then suffered a back injury and was in and out of the lineup for the remainder of the game. With little left to play for, the Eagles may choose to put their star running back on ice for a while. That would leave Blue and Elijah Mitchell as the next men up. Mitchell was the RB3 for Philly in Monday’s game, but he wasn’t signed to the active roster. Our money is on Blue seeing more work this week, though it’s a messy situation at best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Jaydon Blue was signed from their practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move. Pierce went down with an injury on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter of Monday’s game. The team has not announced the exact injury yet, but Pierce will now miss a minimum of four games. Blue will back up a still-very-injured Saquon Barkley. Barkley returned from his hamstring injury in Week 7, only to suffer a back injury in the process. Blue has an outside chance at starting for the Eagles this week, making him worth a look on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles waived RB Jaydon Blue.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: They tacked on a waived/injured listing for Carson Steele, leaving the backfield with just Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Blue did not officially get into a game with the Eagles after signing at the end of August. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Carson Steele left Week 6 against the Panthers with a shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Steele caught a screen pass in the flats and lowered his head to try and run over the defender. He came up holding his shoulder and had to have the shoulder immobilized as he walked into the locker room with his pads off. It had the look of a dislocation, which would mean Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue are the only two healthy running backs for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tank Bigsby will have core muscle surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Rapoport reports there are hopes that Bigsby will be back “in six weeks or shorter.” The 24-year-old back will be required to miss at least four games now that he’s headed for an IR stint. With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also at risk of missing at least one game, third-string RB Will Shipley could be in line for a busy day in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but could be a sneaky option in PPR leagues given his pass-catching profile during his days at Clemson, when he caught 85 passes over three seasons. It also wouldn’t be surprising if Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue were promoted off the practice squad and saw early down touches while Shipley serves in more of a third-down role. There’s a lot to figure out here over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cowboys “are bracing for an extended absence” after RB Malik Davis suffered a hip injury on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Regarding Davis’ injury, Fowler’s source said simply, “it’s bad.” The Cowboys’ No. 2 running back is undergoing further testing, but we expect them to place him on injured reserve before long. The Cowboys waived RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah last month. Blue has since signed with the Eagles’ practice squad. The Cowboys have RB Emari Demercado on the active roster behind RB Javonte Williams. Currently, only RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad in Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles signed RB Jaydon Blue to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Blue was waived by the Cowboys and went unclaimed, and the 2025 fifth-round pick will remain in the NFC East. He’ll begin the campaign behind Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley as backups to Saquon Barkley, but some strong performances in practice could give the 22-year-old a chance to receive touches in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Former Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue goes unclaimed on waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Blue now becomes a free agent and can be signed by any running back-needy team, including the ability to sign onto the Dallas practice squad. It has been quite the fall from grace for Blue over the previous 24 hours, seemingly going from the favorite for backup duties for the Cowboys to without a home. It is also noteworthy that only one running back was claimed during the waiver period, veteran Emari Demercado, by this same Cowboys team. Blue appears to have lost all fantasy value and faces an uphill battle for a meaningful role in his sophomore campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Bears acquired DT Jeffery Simmons and a fifth-round pick from the Titans in exchange for two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: The Titans’ fourth-round pick is in 2027 and the fifth-round pick heading back to Chicago is in 2028. It’s a massive haul for a Titans team that is once again staring down the barrel of a lost season. Simmons has been the subject of trade rumors for a while, but an offseason extension quieted the murmurs this year. Tennessee inked him to a three-year, $106 million extension in June. Simmons has consistently been one of the league’s best interior pass-rushers. He racked up a career-high 11 sacks last year and already has four to his name in 2026. Though the Titans clearly wanted Simmons to be around for years to come, they couldn’t pass on the chance to hoard draft picks as they prepare for another rebuild. With Caleb Williams healthy and playing at an elite level, the Bears are going all in on this current window. They currently rank 14th in EPA per play allowed, a mark that will certainly improve in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Bears acquired DT Jeffery Simmons from the Titans in exchange for two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: It’s a massive haul for a Titans team that is once again staring down a lost season. Simmons has been the subject of trade rumors for a while, but an offseason extension quieted the murmurs this year. Tennessee inked him to a three-year, $106 million extension in June. Simmons has consistently been one of the league’s best interior pass-rushers. He racked up a career-high 11 sacks last year and already has four to his name in 2026. With Caleb Williams healthy and playing at an elite level, the Bears are going all in on this current window.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Jeffery Simmons (back) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: He went from a Wednesday DNP to a Friday full session and should see his normal allotment of snaps and havoc-causing against Houston’s beleaguered interior offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Jeffery Simmons (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Robert Saleh has been liberal with rest days for veterans, so this could be nothing. It’s still notable that the centerpiece of his defense did not practice today. Simmons has two sacks on 12 pressures this year. The defense wasn’t necessarily good with him in the lineup, but it would be even more of a disappointment if he does miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Titans signed DT Jeffery Simmons to a three-year, $105.8 million extension through 2030.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the contract makes Simmons, 28, the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history and includes $100 million guaranteed. Per PFF, Simmons led NFL defensive tackles with 12 sacks last season, while ranking in the top three in both quarterback pressures (64) and TFLs (12). His 43 solo tackles tied for sixth. Through seven NFL seasons, Simmons has appeared in four Pro Bowls, while earning two second-team All-Pro spots and one first-team All-Pro spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Titans WR Calvin Ridley (hamstring) is active for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Ridley’s hamstring injury kept him down from Weeks 7-9, not including a Week 10 bye. He’ll be on the WR4/WR5 line in a tough matchup against a good Texans pass defense. Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) and Arden Key (quad) are also active. Inactive for the Titans are: S Xavier Woods (hamstring), S Jerrick Reed II, G Drew Moss and T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Titans DT Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) is expected to play in Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Simmons hasn’t played since Week 7. It looked like he would be out again this week when the Titans held him out of practice on Wednesday. However, he returned for two limited sessions and a questionable designation entering the weekend. It sounds like the Titans will have their top pass-rusher back versus Davis Mills and the Texans. Simmons has 4.5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: The 1-7 Titans will be without their defensive leader in a matchup against one of the league’s top offenses. It’s a tough break for a team that will also be without its WR1, as Calvin Ridley will miss a third-straight game with a hamstring injury of his own. Simmons has totaled 21 tackles and 4.5 sacks in seven games this season and will likely be replaced by C.J. Ravenell, who is listed behind him on the depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Titans DT Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Simmons is now on the wrong side of questionable, which is a tough loss for the Titans’ defense. The unit could also be without OLB Arden Key (quadricep) and backup OLB Jihad Ward (undisclosed) who were also absent during the portion of practice open to the media. The Titans are tasked with containing the Chargers’ offense in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Titans DT Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) did not practice Wednedsay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: Simmons missed Week 8’s game with the same hamstring issue. He now looks likely to miss a second week because of it. Fellow pass-rusher Arden Key also remains out of practice. He is dealing with a quad issue. The Titans didn’t have a great defense before these injuries. Losing Simmons and Key will make them an easier matchup for the Chargers on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.headline: Titans DT Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) will not play in Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeffery-si.analysis: He didn’t practice at all this week. We’d bet more on a Week 10 return than a Week 9 return for Simmons given how this has gone thus far, and we probably can’t rule out an IR placement on Saturday. Without their best defensive player the Titans will be in (searching for word that is worse than deep trouble) deeper trouble than usual against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Jalen Carter said he “probably won’t be 100-percent this year” due to a wrist injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: Carter has been dealing with a wrist injury since the beginning of the season, playing through it for the last seven weeks. He will continue to play through it, though the Eagles defensive tackle admits the wrist won’t be fully healed this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (wrist) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: Eagles CB Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) was also cleared to play, though S Andrew Mukuba (knee) is questionable to play after logging a limited session on Friday. The Eagles’ D/ST should have a decent week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (wrist) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: Eagles CB Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) and OLB Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) joined Carter for a limited session. Eagles S Andrew Mukuba (knee) did not practice. Fortunately, the Eagles have a winnable game against the Titans this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (wrist) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: Carter pops up on the injury report with a wrist issue Wednesday. A DNP listing to start the week is not the best sign, but the 25-year-old has a couple more chances to practice in at least a limited fashion. Should Carter miss time, the Eagles may turn to Byron Young for more snaps at defensive tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Eagles signed DT Jalen Carter to a four-year, $152 million extension with $106 million in guarantees.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: After the smoke seemed to say that the Eagles were reluctant to sign Carter to a market-setting extension, GM Howie Roseman swoops in and does a deal right as training camp is open instead. Carter looked like a shell of himself at times towards the end of last season as he dealt with surgery on both of his shoulders, but this is a sensible extension assuming that the shoulders aren’t set to be a long-term problem. He was clearly the best lineman on the defense in 2024 and the Eagles clearly expect that sort of play going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer believes the Eagles are “hesitant to pay” DT Jalen Carter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: It’s not a major surprise given how Carter needed offseason surgery on both of his shoulders and didn’t look anything like 2024 Jalen Carter down the stretch last season. The Eagles likely want to see a healthy season before committing. Carter did not participate in team drills at mandatory minicamp and the Eagles have him under team control through 2027 via the fifth-year option. This could be a standstill to keep an eye on for a while.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter skipped organized team activities and did not participate in team drills at mandatory minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: Carter is participating in individual drills. He sat out for a month of the 2025 season after undergoing procedures on both shoulders last year. Late in May, Eagles DC Vic Fangio said Carter “had a good offseason of lifting” and that Carter’s shoulders “are fine,” so Carter’s limited participation is unlikely to be health-related. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni gave a non-answer when asked if this was injury-related or perhaps contract-related. We suspect it is the latter. The front office picked up Carter’s fifth-year option last year, keeping him under contract through 2027. He has a $3.7 million salary this year and a $27.1million salary next year. He is likely seeking a rich, long-term investment from the team. It remains to be seen how this will pan out, but GM Howie Roseman is a very savvy salary cap manager.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Eagles DC Vic Fangio said Jalen Carter’s shoulders “are fine” after surgery last season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: Carter missed a month of football last season due to having surgery on both of his shoulders. Speaking with the media, Fangio said Carter appears fine and that the star lineman has “had a good offseason of lifting,” which Fangio believes he began earlier than usual. Carter totaled 33 tackles, three sacks, and five TFLs in 11 games for the Eagles last season, and has remained a key piece of the defense since being drafted No. 9 overall in 2023. It sounds like he should be in good shape for the start of training camp for a defense that ranked fifth in points allowed and 13th in yards allowed last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: Eagles exercised the fifth-year option for DT Jalen Carter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: Carter is one of two Eagles players to have his fifth-year option picked up this offseason, with LB Nolan Smith also having his option exercised. Carter has been a disruptive force for the Eagles since being drafted by them in 2023. The former ninth overall pick has tallied 13.5 sacks and 25 TFLs in 43 career games, and earned Second-team All-Pro honors in 2024. He has also been named to back-to-back Pro Bowls. The decision to pick up Carter’s option means he will remain under contract with the Eagles through the 2027 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Eagles have received trade calls on DT Jalen Carter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-cart.analysis: The phrasing is always important on these — that the Eagles have received trade calls does not necessarily mean that they’re interested in moving Carter. But if Philadelphia decides it isn’t interested in extending Carter’s contract, it would make some sense to deal him in the wake of Jordan Davis’ contract extension. We’d be surprised if the Eagles didn’t extend Carter, because as has been pointed out several times during the A.J. Brown sweepstakes, GM Howie Roseman isn’t in the business of getting rid of good players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans claimed Jonah Laulu off waivers from the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Tennessee waived Timmy Horne in a corresponding move. Laulu appeared in five games for the Raiders this year and recorded .5 sacks plus three QB hits. He made 15 starts for the Raiders last year and appeared in all 17 games. Laulu will be a depth option for the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders activated WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was his last possible day to be reinstated in his 21-day window. The fact that Klint Kubiak spent much of Thornton’s 21-day window talking about how he had to go show us something makes us think Thornton will probably just be a depth piece for the time being. The Raiders waived Jonah Laulu to make room for Thornton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Colts selected Oklahoma DT Jonah Laulu with the No. 234 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Laulu, 6'5" and 289 pounds, demonstrated “rare fluidity and closing burst to the football” at Oklahoma, NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein said. A powerful bull rusher, Laulu is considered raw but his impressive traits drew attention from several team in the pre-draft process. He’ll try to crack the roster of a Ravens team that sports one of the league’s elite defensive lines.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Former Hawaii junior DL Jonah Laulu has committed to the Oklahoma Sooners.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Laulu (6'6/280) entered the transfer portal following the end of the 2021 season after playing his first three collegiate years with the Warriors. He posted career-highs in nearly every category as a junior, finishing the season with 36 tackles, 40 quarterback pressures and four sacks according to Pro Football Focus, all of which are career bests. Laulu started every game at defensive end for the Warriors in 2021, lining up on both the right and left side of the line, and also played a career high 675 defensive snaps. For a team that has seen several players hit the transfer portal following the departure of Lincoln Riley, getting a player from the portal feels like a small victory for the Sooners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Pat Surtain (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Surtain is now on track to make his return after missing multiple games with an ankle injury. The good news comes at the right time, with a bout against the division-rival Chiefs upcoming this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Broncos declared CB Pat Surtain, QB Sam Ehlinger, S Talanoa Hufanga, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Jordan Jackson, and DL Tyler Onyedim inactive for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Surtain is expected to return for a crucial matchup with the Chiefs next week. The Broncos will be without one of the league’s superstar corners in the meantime. Surtain’s absence should make life a little easier for Michael Wilson, who is in the midst of a two-game slump.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Pat Surtain (ankle) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Surtain will miss his third straight game with the ankle injury. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. With the Chiefs in the hole for Week 8, holding Surtain out one more game to get him back for a must-win AFC West showdown makes sense. Per Rapoport, there’s a “good chance” he’s back next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Pat Surtain (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Surtain never managed to practice in full this week. Keeping him sidelined until he is able to do so could make sense. The 4-2 Broncos are currently second in the AFC West. They face the 5-0 Chiefs in Week 8. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Pat Surtain (ankle) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reported last week that Surtain was likely to return for the Broncos’ Week 8 game against the Chiefs, rather than face the Cardinals in Week 7. Given Surtain’s multi-week absence, and Palmer’s reporting, we expect to see Surtain listed as a limited participant on the final injury report. Whether he returns in time for the Cardinals’ game remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that returning in Week 8 against the Chiefs is more likely for Pat Surtain (ankle) than in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Palmer also clarified that Surtain did not suffer a non-contact injury, as has been reported previously. Surtain apparently injured his ankle two plays before he exited the Broncos’ Week 5 game against the 49ers. The Broncos might be able to get by without Surtain next week, but getting him back before facing Patrick Mahomes would be huge.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable for the Broncos’ Week 6 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Moss missed Week 5 due to a rib injury but has a chance to return Thursday against the Seahawks after three straight limited practices this week. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) and S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice all week and were ruled out, as expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Broncos CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Neither Surtain or Riley Moss (ribs) practiced on Wednesday. Head coach Sean Payton said the Broncos don’t anticipate placing Surtain on injured reserve. The injuries to both corners look to be shorter-term; Surtain is week-to-week while Moss’ return timeline is not disclosed yet. Both are on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Broncos CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) is “week-to-week” with one source bracing for him to miss “about two weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: It sounds like this is overall good news for the Broncos, but their defense will take a major short-term hit without one of the best corners in the league. The Broncos, who also lost Riley Moss to a rib injury against the 49ers, will probably have to change some things up next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Patrick Surtain’s ankle injury is not believed to be season-ending.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: According to Rapoport, there are no longer any concerns that this is an Achilles injury for Surtain, who left Week 4’s game against the 49ers with a non-contact injury. Surtain could be looking at a multi-week absence and will undergo an MRI soon to confirm the severity of his injury, but it sounds like he avoided anything too serious. In addition to Surtain, the Broncos are also evaluating the status of CB Riley Moss, who is dealing with a rib injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Texans claimed Emari Demercado, formerly of the Cowboys, off waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Demercado will need to contribute on special teams to be active on game day, and he might also need David Montgomery (groin) to remain sidelined after the Week 8 bye. Demercado does not need to be added in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Cowboys waived Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: It’s not the first time they’ve done so this season, so we’re not exactly sure that Demercado is done here. However he was a healthy scratch last night and the Cowboys are looking at activating some players off IR, so it’s possible if Demercado stays it’ll be as part of the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Cowboys declared WR KaVontae Turpin, LB Dee Winters, OT Drew Shelton, OLB Tyrus Wheat, and RB Emari Demercado inactive for Week 7 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: No real surprises here after KaVontae Turpin was ruled out earlier in the week, with the biggest impact being how the team will handle kick and punt returns on special teams. The Cowboys continue to inch closer to full strength as they near the half way point in the regular season, desperately needing a win over the shorthanded Eagles to keep pace in the NFC East.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports the Cowboys are expected to re-sign RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: He’ll apparently get a 53-man roster spot after some roster machinations over the next few days. Demercado has lost the backup job to Tyler Goodson and doesn’t need to factor into any fantasy calculations at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Cowboys waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Tyler Goodson has had the RB2 role for the past couple of weeks and is set to continue now that Demercado was waived to make room for Tyler Smith to come off injured reserve. Demercado has now been waived twice in two months, and though he may be claimed again, he could also wind up on a practice squad next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports the Cowboys are signing RB Tyler Goodson off the Falcons’ practice-squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Goodson will backfill the roster spot lost to placing Malik Davis on IR at the end of last week. It’s unclear whether Emari Demercado or Goodson would be the head of a committee if Javonte Williams were injured, as both of them showed up with the Cowboys after last cuts. Neither player is a must-roster as things stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports that Cowboys Malik Davis (hip) will have surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: It is unclear whether this is a season-ending injury or if Davis has a chance to return later in the year. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier that the Cowboys were “bracing for an extended absence” and that a source told him, “it’s bad.” It sounds like Davis’ 2026 season may be over. Cowboys RB Emari Demercado now sits behind starting RB Javonte Williams, and RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cowboys “are bracing for an extended absence” after RB Malik Davis suffered a hip injury on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Regarding Davis’ injury, Fowler’s source said simply, “it’s bad.” The Cowboys’ No. 2 running back is undergoing further testing, but we expect them to place him on injured reserve before long. The Cowboys waived RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah last month. Blue has since signed with the Eagles’ practice squad. The Cowboys have RB Emari Demercado on the active roster behind RB Javonte Williams. Currently, only RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad in Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: DLLS Sports’ Clarence Hill Jr. reports Malik Davis was carted off the field on Friday with an injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Hill was quickly ruled out for Week 1. Dallas cut Phil Mafah and Jaydon Blue at the end of camp, briefly leaving Davis as the only backup running back on their roster. They eventually signed Emari Demercado after he was released by Kansas City. If the injury is serious, the Cowboys could bring either Mafah or Blue back, given their familiarity with the system. The Dallas Morning News’ Calvin Watkins reported shortly afterward that Davis has suffered a hip injury, though no further details were given.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Cowboys claimed RB Emari Demercado off waivers from the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Demercado enters a wide open backfield depth chart behind starter Javonte Williams and primary backup Malik Davis, the two of whom were the only running backs to survive 53-man roster cuts Sunday. It does not appear the Cowboys are finished adding to their backfield, with most teams keeping four running backs on the active roster throughout the season. More to come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Jaydon Blue was signed from their practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move. Pierce went down with an injury on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter of Monday’s game. The team has not announced the exact injury yet, but Pierce will now miss a minimum of four games. Blue will back up a still-very-injured Saquon Barkley. Barkley returned from his hamstring injury in Week 7, only to suffer a back injury in the process. Blue has an outside chance at starting for the Eagles this week, making him worth a look on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) was taken to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce was injured on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter and was taken to the locker room almost immediately following the ailment. No word on the nature of the injury, but Pierce would appear to be on the wrong side of questionable to return considering there is less than six minutes remaining to play in the fourth quarter. Saquon Barkley was previously deemed questionable to return with a back injury, leaving Elijah Mitchell to fill in for the remainder of the game. Pierce rushed 14 times for 47 yards and a touchdown prior to departing, adding one yard on one reception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Dameon Pierce rushed 12 times for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: With Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley all hurt, and Carson Steele getting injured early in this game, Pierce took every single carry for the Eagles on Sunday. He also played on 61 of the team’s 64 snaps. However, that wasn’t able to amount to much on the ground with all of Philadelphia’s injuries. Pierce was also asked to pass block a lot, which means he only ran a route on 15 of the team’s 52 dropbacks. That’s going to limit his fantasy value, and he looks like a TD-dependent FLEX play while he remains the starter. The upside is that there doesn’t seem to be anybody coming for his job until Barkley (hamstring) returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Dameon Pierce rushed 11 times for 14 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce “added” two catches for -2 yards. He took over as the Eagles’ lead back after Will Shipley went down with a foot injury in the first half. Carson Steele did not see the field for a single offensive snap. Pierce would presumably in line for a workhorse role in Week 6 if Shipley and Saquon Barkley are both out, but his efficiency today speaks for itself. This isn’t an offense capable of opening running lanes, nor is Pierce a back who can make a lot out of a little. Pierce is a low-priority waiver wire add for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Will Shipley (foot) will not return to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Shipley suffered the foot injury in the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable to return. He will now miss the remainder of the contest. Dameon Pierce is the only other running back on the roster with a touch today. Carson Steele is also active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Shipley got stuffed on a carry in the second quarter and was checked out by trainers after the play. He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Barkley will likely be listed as a non-participant on today’s official injury report. He is unlikely to play in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Aside from Barkley, the Eagles have RBs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Shipley will probably lead the backfield in touches this week, but it could be a messy workload split.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles activated RB Dameon Pierce to the team’s active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce will probably operate as the team’s No. 2 back behind Will Shipley this week against the Jaguars, one of the league’s best rush defenses. Tank Bigsby and Saquon Barkley are sidelined, leaving the Eagles scraping bottom for backfield depth. Look for Pierce to get some early-down work against the Jaguars. Shipley, who had six carries for 23 yards last week, is the only viable fantasy option of the two, though head coach Nick Sirianni heaped praise on Pierce Wednesday. “He’s an NFL starting running back,” Sirriani said of Pierce. “Maybe wouldn’t have said that when he was on our practice squad publicly, because of the fear of losing him. But he’s an NFL starting running back.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback has been dealing with back spasms in recent weeks, likely delaying his rookie season debut. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck threw the ball well on Tuesday. Today, they will see how things go. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck left Thursday’s practice with back spasms and was listed as a DNP. Head coach Mike LaFleur said he was not overly concerned about the injury and that he doesn’t believe it will be anything long-term. Beck’s injury shouldn’t change his Week 7 availability, as he has been the emergency QB3 all season. He was officially listed as questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck appeared on the injury report last Friday, as a limited participant. He remained limited on Wednesday and was downgraded today. Beat reporters saw him at practice briefly, but he ended up going inside with a trainer. This could help preserve Jacoby Brissett’s job security. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, OL Josh Fryar, DL Andrew Billings, and WR Reggie Virgil inactive for Week 3 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck continues to be the Cardinals’ third quarterback and will be a gameday inactive for Week 3 behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. Dadrion “Rabbit” Taylor-Demerson (back) was scratched on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Team reporter Darren Urban reports that Cardinals QB Carson Beck (ribs) is unlikely to play in Friday’s preseason game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: This is unfortunate. Beck looked great before injuring his ribs in the Hall of Fame game. Per Urban, Beck has been a very limited participant in practice ever since, which is costing him valuable reps. Only starting QB Jacoby Brissett will take first-team practice reps once the regular season begins. Beck practiced the week after the injury, “struggling much of the time,” and has sat out since then. The Cardinals have an extremely difficult schedule, so a rough record could bring Beck back onto the field at some point this year. Ideally, he would have spent all of August refining his play, though. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team re-draft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said QB Carson Beck (rib) is unlikely to play in Saturday’s preseason game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck is scheduled to resume throwing after practice today, though, so the Cardinals’ rookie is indeed on the mend. Beck looked good in his prior preseason action. Hopefully, he has a chance to return in time for his team’s final preseason game against the Packers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur said he has ‘no concern’ over the rib injury that sidelined Carson Beck in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: LaFleur said Beck would have been well enough to throw if it were seven-on-seven drills, adding that the team “didn’t want to risk it” when it came to starting the rookie in Thursday’s preseason game. Beck already has some preseason experience under his belt. He threw for 188 yards and a touchdown in the Hall of Fame Game last week against the Panthers and will hopefully have a chance to suit up in next week’s preseason game against the Cowboys on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals QB Carson Beck completed 15-of-19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in Thursday’s Hall-of-Fame Game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck played two-plus quarters. No offense to the Hall-of-Fame Game, but it’s not a contest we typically go into expecting highlights. The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback provided several of them, hitting Jalen Brooks for a 49-yard deep strike and Simi Fehoko for a five-yard end zone fade touchdown. In between were several smart in-rhythm completions, with Beck navigating the pocket well. 24-year-old Beck’s arm strength remains a massive question mark — even his Brooks completion drifted a bit toward the middle of the field — but his processing was on point against the Panthers’ second- and third-team defense. Although he was a highly polarizing pre-draft prospect, the fact that the rebuilding Cardinals were willing to use a Day 2 selection strongly suggests he will make late-season starts as the organization keeps an eye on the future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Walter Nolen (ankle) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: Nolen did not play in Week 7 against the Broncos. Were he to miss this week’s game against the Cowboys, his absence would only further insulate this game as a fantasy-friendly environment. The Cardinals’ permissive defense is a unit to target via matchups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: Baker practiced in a limited capacity on Friday, and the veteran safety is no stranger to playing through injuries. The Cardinals ruled out DL Walter Nolen (ankle) and S Andrew Wingard (knee). Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (knee) has been cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: Baker played through the groin injury in Week 6 but starts out this week not practicing due to both the groin injury and an illness. Also not practicing for the Cardinals defense were DL Walter Nolen (ankle), S Andrew Wingard (knee), and CB Garrett Williams (knee). Each player will likely need to practice in some capacity in order to play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Cardinals declared Marvin Harrison Jr., QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas, Andrew Wingard and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 5 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: Life continues to be rough for fantasy managers rostering Harrison. The soon-to-be ex-Cardinal will not participate in what should be a fantasy-friendly game against the porous Lions defense. Bummer. Still no definitive word on where he will end up next week. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne benefit from his absence. The Cardinals will be without Wingard, one of two starting safeties, but will have DT Walter Nolen (calf) available to them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Cardinals DT Walter Nolen (calf) is questionable for Arizona’s Week 5 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: Nolen was limited in back-to-back practices after popping up with the calf listing on Thursday. He’s played 319 snaps in 21 career opportunities so far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Cardinals DT Walter Nolen (calf) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: The Cardinals’ defense is fairly banged up, and now their star defensive tackle is ailing. He appeared on the injury report as a limited participant today, indicating he suffered the calf injury in practice. Hopefully, it is minor. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said DL Walter Nolen avoided suffering a knee injury on Friday and will practice today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: Phew. Nolen suffered a surgery-worthy meniscus injury in his left knee last season, ending his rookie campaign prematurely. Nolen left practice early last Friday and appeared to be in considerable pain, indicating to team trainers that something was wrong with his left knee. Apparently, this is more so a mental hurdle than anything else. Speaking to the media before practice, LaFleur explained that sometimes when a player is returning from a serious injury, discomfort can, understandably, cause a scare. The Cardinals’ promising youngster will take the practice field with his teammates this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Cardinals signed DT Brodric Martin, formerly of the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: While we are happy for Martin, we can’t help but wonder if this is related to the apparent left knee injury DT Walter Nolen appeared to suffer at today’s practice. Hopefully, the Cardinals are just playing it safe. Martin entered the NFL as a 2023 third-round pick with the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.headline: Cardinals DL Walter Nolen left practice early on Friday after suffering an apparent knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/walter-nol.analysis: This is a bummer. A torn meniscus in his left knee ended Nolen’s 2025 rookie season. Multiple beat reporters say Nolen appeared to injure his left knee today. He had been drawing positive reviews in training camp thus far. Hopefully, this is only a short-term injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: 49ers released Jack Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: Jones was released to create room on the roster for DeForest Buckner, whom the 49ers just acquired from Indianapolis. Jones hasn’t played much this year, but he has been active in all seven games and sees some work on special teams. He started 17 games for the Dolphins in 2025 and 16 games for the Raiders in 2024. He shouldn’t have any issues finding a new team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: 49ers signed CB Jack Jones, formerly of the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: This is a one-year contract for Jones. He entered the NFL as a 2022 fourth-round pick with the Patriots. He was waived in November 2023 after dealing with a lengthy hamstring injury. The Raiders added him right away, but eventually waived him in April 2025. He was signed by the Dolphins during the 2025 offseason. PFF credits him with six forced incompletions and one interception last year. Jones has a chance to compete for a starting role here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: Dolphins CB Jack Jones was carted away from practice after suffering an apparent lower-body injury on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: Retired OT Terron Armstead was present and reportedly carried Jones off the field. Trainers then examined him, and although he was reportedly seen walking on the sidelines, he was ultimately carted to the locker room. If Jones is sidelined, the Dolphins’ already-thin cornerback corps would be in even worse shape.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: Raiders waived CB Jack Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: Jones has one year left on the rookie deal he signed with the Patriots in 2022, meaning he will have to clear waivers before being an outright free agent. Jones allowed a league-high 10 touchdown receptions last season, per PFF, but also tallied a career-best three interceptions and 16 pass breakups. At just 27 years old, Jones has plenty of upside to offer a team needing secondary help. There should be plenty of teams interested in taking a one-year flyer on him for this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: Raiders beat writer Vincent Bonsignore reports the team is looking to trade CB Jack Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: If the team can’t find a suitor for Jones, the soon-to-be fourth-year corner will be released on Monday, per Bonsignore. Jones was a fourth-round pick by the Patriots back in 2022 and tallied 69 tackles, 16 pass breakups, and a career-high three interceptions last season. Per PFF, Jones also allowed opposing receivers to catch 54 passes for 679 yards and 10 touchdowns, tied for the most touchdowns allowed of any corner last season. It’s possible the Raiders find a team willing to part with a late Day 3 pick in exchange for Jones’ services, but it wouldn’t be surprising if any teams interested waited until his release to make him an offer. Jones is entering the final year of his rookie contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: Raiders CB Jakorian Bennett (shoulder) is out for Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: Fellow cornerback Nate Hobbs is out with an ankle issue. Jack Jones returned to practice on Friday and will presumably be listed as questionable. Down at least two starting corners, the Raiders are as good of a matchup as Bo Nix could ask for.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: Raiders CB Jakorian Bennett (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: Raiders slot CB Nate Hobbs (ankle) and No. 2 perimeter CB Jack Jones (back) were also unable to practice on Wednesday. The development pushes the Broncos’ ascending rookie QB Bo Nix firmly into the QB1 ranks. His pass catchers are likewise on the rise this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: The Raiders claimed DB Jack Jones off waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: Jones was waived by the Patriots after playing just 10 snaps in Week 10. He was a fourth-round pick of the Patriots in 2022 and was let go after declining opportunity his sophomore year. Jones now joins the Raiders secondary as a young player with rookie year production. DE Isaac Rochell was waived by Las Vegas in a corresponding move.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: Patriots waived DB Jack Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: Jones played on just 10 snaps in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Colts. Since being activated off injured reserve, Jones has seen his snaps decline in each of the last four weeks, with Sunday’s 10 snaps marking the fewest since Week 14 of last season. As a rookie, Jones allowed just 20 receptions for 306 yards and one touchdown while earning a PFF coverage grade of 76.0. Jones was arrested in June for possession of a concealed weapon, possession of ammunition without an ID card, unlawful possesion of a firearm, carrying a loaded firearm, and possession of a large-capacity feeding device at Logan Airport. The charges were eventually dropped, but things have only gone downhill for Jones since then. A team will almost certainly look to claim him off waivers in the coming days, but Jones’ time with the Patriots appears to be coming to an end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.headline: Patriots activated DB Jack Jones from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-jones.analysis: The Patriots get a small boost to their secondary with the return of Jones, who will be making his season debut in Week 7 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Dolphins claimed Christian Haynes off waivers from the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It was initially reported that the Ravens claimed Haynes off waivers. The Dolphins, however, also claimed him. A worse record than the Ravens gave Miami a higher priority on waivers and they were awarded Haynes. The former third-round pick will be a useful depth option for the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Ravens claimed Christian Haynes off waivers from the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Seattle cut the former third-round pick earlier this week after trading for Quenton Nelson. Haynes made five starts at right guard this year. Ravens rookie guard Vega Ioane is the latest in a long line of banged-up interior linemen for Baltimore. Haynes will give the team some extra depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Seahawks placed G Christian Haynes on injured reserve and designated him for return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Haynes, a third-round pick from 2024, was unable to play in the last two preseason games due to an elbow injury. The 25-year-old projects as a backup at this stage, and won’t be able to return until October at the earliest. The Seahawks also placed WR/KR Stephen Sims on IR while placing DE Rylie Mills and NT Jonathan Hankins on NFI (non-football injury list).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Seahawks declared RG Christian Haynes, WR DK Metcalf, CB Nehmiah Pritchett, LB Trevis Gipson, OG Sataoa Laumea, TE Noah Fant, and DE Myles Adams inactive for Week 9 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Both Metcalf and Fant were ruled out on Friday. The Seahawks are hopeful Metcalf will be back after their upcoming bye. Fant is expected to miss multiple weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Seahawks selected Connecticut OG Christian Haynes with the No. 81 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Haynes was an unheralded two-star high school recruit lacking in Power Five interest when he enrolled at UConn back in 2018. He took a redshirt before going on to log four seasons of 800+ snaps, with every single one of his 3,319 career reps coming at right guard. Haynes’ blocking prowess crested in 2022, when he allowed just three pressures and zero sacks on 328 pass reps, good for a 91st percentile PFF pass block grade that ranked tops amongst FBS interior linemen. His stiff hands have the striking power to jolt rushers off their line and the torque to latch on and drive opponents to the ground. In sync with his linemates on stunts and swiftly climbs to nullify linebackers when running the ball. Haynes lacks positional malleability and is undersized for interior work, but he has a keen understanding of leverage that helps him get underneath opponents’ pads and stall out their rush. Haynes’ overall value at the next level could be suppressed if teams deem him as a right guard only.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) successfully underwent surgery, and his return timeline is “probably closer” to the shorter end of the expected 6-10 week timeline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: If Adams hit the absolute soonest return date, week-wise, he theoretically could face the Chiefs in Week 13, but that game takes place on Thursday night. We suspect facing the 49ers in Week 14 is more likely, though nothing is guaranteed for a 33-year-old player. Adams should be stashed in injured reserve spots, where possible. He makes for a tough cut in leagues without them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is still determining “the best time” to schedule Davante Adams’ (hamstring) “cleanup” procedure.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the Rams have not had discussions about bringing in a receiver with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for 6-10 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Earlier today, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.” Obviously, McVay doesn’t want to tip off other wide receiver-needy NFL teams about their potential entrance into the trade market, and he has no reason to be honest with us. Acquiring a new wide receiver makes sense, and the Rams were aggressive players in the trade market last offseason. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams is set to undergo a procedure after rupturing his hamstring tendon in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He will be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. The Rams were already very thin at wide receiver and Puka Nacua has spent multiple weeks on the injury report as well. Acquiring a capable wide receiver makes sense, but as Graziano mentions, the Rams have already traded away a lot of their draft capital. Thus far, GM Les Snead has already given up their 2027 first- and third-round picks, and their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. He notes that Rams QB Stetson Bennett played for Browns coach Todd Monken in college. Perhaps Monken would be interested in a reunion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) will miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured tendon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams had a non-contact injury at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Cardinals and unfortunately is as serious as it appeared. He’ll likely be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7. His absence will further focus targets on Puka Nacua and likely elevate Konata Mumpfield into a bigger role. Adams had put together a 30/480/4 line in his first six games of the season. Adams will reportedly have surgery to “clean” out the tendon, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, in hopes he can return around the team’s bye week, which is scheduled for Week 11. It’s a major blow for a Rams team that is already reeling at 2-4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams appeared to injure his left knee while running a route in the red zone on the Rams’ final possession. He cut, turned upfield and quickly began limping his way to the back of the end zone, removing himself from the play while grabbing at the inside of his left knee. He subbed himself out after that. No word on his status, but we expect an update soon. Prior to that, the Cardinals’ pass rush made life tough on the Rams’ passing attack. Adams caught his first pass a minute and a half into the second quarter. Stafford was looking his way in the end zone later on the same drive, but Josh Sweat got to him for the strip-sack. Adams banked 16-yard receptions on the sixth and seventh drives, impressively getting wide open via a downfield out route on the second one. If Adams escaped with a minor injury, he would be a WR2 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 5-of-7 targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams cashed in on a corner fade from four yards out in the second quarter and ran a beautiful route on a double move slant from five yards out for his second score in the fourth quarter, proving that he remains an elite red zone weapon for an offense that has now attempted 51 or more passes in three straight games. Adams is back to modest target rates following the Week 4 return of Puka Nacua but remains a weekly WR2 due to his red zone acumen, which remains true ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 4-of-9 targets for 32 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams was the victim of a bad Matthew Stafford ball or two in rainy Philadelphia conditions, but he sadly immediately reverted to clear No. 2 wideout status with Puka Nacua back in the lineup. Nacua went off for 9/125. Adams now has seven catches for 58 scoreless yards in two games with Nacua in the lineup compared to 15/332/2 in two games without. Hopefully that trend normalizes a bit for a potential Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 7-of-13 targets for 137 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams’ 137 yards combine with the 195 yards he erupted for in Week 2 to set a new high in receiving yards in consecutive games during his remarkable career. Even more stunning was the fact that he did so against one of the top corners in the league in Pat Surtain, who shadowed Adams for all but a handful of his routes, proving his ability to get open against top competition even in the later stages of his career. Puka Nacua missed both Week 2 and Week 3 and his injury timeline remains convoluted, at best. Adams will remains a top-tier WR1 should Nacua miss more time, and would be solid WR2 should Nacua return for a Week 4 meeting with the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (groin) is “not making great progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: In a surprisingly candid interview with ESPN Los Angeles, McVay certainly did not sound optimistic that Nacua would play in Week 3. Nacua has already missed one practice this week and there’s been no indication that he will get back on the field over the next two days. Davante Adams racked up 195 yards and two scores with Nacua out in Week 2. It will be hard not to rank him as a WR1 once Nacua is ruled out. Terrance Ferguson operated as the team’s No. 2 receiver last week and will be in the TE1 mix without Nacua.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported last week that Ferguson’s return was still going to take “some time.” That doesn’t make it sound like he’s awfully close to getting back on the field. Tyler Higbee leads the Rams’ tight end room in routes since Ferguson went down, but his production has vanished over the past two weeks. Colby Parkinson scored in Week 6 and Davis Allen found the end zone twice last week. Higbee remains the best fantasy option of the bunch, but he’s nothing more than a low-end TE2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Terrance Ferguson (ankle) “will take some time” to come off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson is eligible to come off injured reserve next week, but Schefter reports that a source told him Ferguson’s recovery “will take some time.” The Rams placed Davante Adams on injured reserve this week and are in desperate need of pass-catching help behind Puka Nacua. Ferguson is a rising receiving tight end for the Rams, but has been on injured reserve since suffering an ankle injury in Week 3. Though he is a good IR stash for fantasy purposes, Ferguson is going to take longer than the minimum four weeks to return. Without a good timeline for return, he can be released from fantasy rosters in dire need of more immediate help during bye weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This escalated quickly. Ferguson briefly returned in Week 3 after getting X-rays on his injured ankle, but he was ultimately unable to continue. Ferguson can be kept on squads possessing an injured reserve spot, but dropping him for a needed starter makes sense. He will be eligible to return in Week 8 against the Chargers.
