https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle) for Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson suffered the ankle injury in Week 3 against the Broncos and was taken to the locker room for X-rays. He was cleared to return, but only did so briefly. The intriguing youngster remains a worthwhile hold, but he could end up being questionable to play next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson was unlikely to play against the Eagles, and this certainly puts him on the “out” trajectory. The timing could not possibly be worse, as Ferguson was finally producing a little bit, and Puka Nacua (groin) is now set to return. That makes Ferguson a shaky hold in standard-sized 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will likely miss Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson briefly departed after injuring his ankle in the team’s Sunday Night Football loss to the Broncos, returning for two snaps prior to departing again after his lone reception of the evening. The ankle injury now appears likely to cost the talented young tight end at least one game, with the potential for the absence to linger if the sprain is “more high than low.” McVay also relayed that fellow tight end Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and is considered day-to-day. Veteran Tyler Higbee would be in line to operate as the primary receiving tight end after amassing 62 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Week 3, should both miss. Higbee should be added in all formats as a potential TE1 in the immediate future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) left the game a second time in the second quarter of Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson initially departed after being tangled up on a target in the first quarter. He was taken to the locker room for x-rays but returned after missing only one drive. He would then depart again following his lone reception and would not return the rest of the game. Ferguson caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards prior to departing for good. His status for Week 4 would appear to be murky at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was taken to the locker room for x-rays in the first quarter of Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson got tangled up on a target half way through the first quarter and limped to the sideline under his own power. He was then escorted to the locker room for x-rays. No additional update has been provided.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Colby Parkinson (knee) is “trending in the right direction” for Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Parkinson did not practice once this week because of the knee issue, so it’s a bit of a surprise that McVay sounds optimistic about him suiting up today. The team may have kept him out of practice as a precaution. He will handle an inline tight end role while Terrance Ferguson handles de facto WR2 duties with Puka Nacua out. Ferguson remains in the TE1 mix while Parkinson is a touchdown-or-bust TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson is set to handle No. 2 pass-catcher duties with WR Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined this week. The young tight end posted a 6/54/1 receiving line in Week 2 and can be viewed as a TE1 in this matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Myles Garrett (knee) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: There was hope within the organization late last week that Garrett could get back on the practice field today. That will have to wait at least one more week. Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 because of a knee issue that required surgery. His absence will make life for Jayden Daniels substantially easier in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Rams are hopeful Myles Garrett (knee) returns to practice at least next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Rapoport didn’t go as far as to say they hope he is back for Week 8’s game against the Commanders, but it’s at least on the table. Garrett is currently on injured reserve, so we’ll know if he’s making progress if they open his practice window next week. The reigning DPOY has been out since Week 1 after undergoing surgery on his knee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) won’t have his 21-day practice window opened this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett went on injured reserve after Week 1 and is therefore eligible to have his 21-day practice window for activation off IR opened this week. However, McVay said the 30-year-old pass-rusher won’t have his window opened, indicating Garrett is not ready to practice yet and it will still be some time before we see him back on the field. His initial timeline after undergoing a knee scope was roughly six weeks. It’s been four weeks so far, but Garrett could still hit the six-week return timeline if his practice window is opened next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Myles Garrett “was given a timeline of roughly six weeks for his recovery from knee surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett attempted to play through the knee issue in Week 1 but was clearly bothered by the balky knee. He underwent a knee scope shortly after the Rams’ opener and was placed on injured reserve. It was initially expected to be closer to a four-week absence for the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Now he’ll miss a bit longer than that, and Rapoport added that the team will be cautious with his return, so he could be sidelined beyond even the six-week timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said he doesn’t have a timeline for when Myles Garrett (knee) will return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett will miss at least four games after going on injured reserve. The All-Pro pass-rusher is set to undergo arthroscopic surgery on his knee after struggling to play through the injury in Week 1. Garrett’s absence is a massive blow to the Rams’ defense, but they should have enough players in place to get through what they hope is a short time away.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: According to Pelissero, Garrett had been dealing with lower leg pain and “wasn’t himself” in Week 1 against the 49ers. Garrett was routinely taken off the field and failed to record a single stat in the contest. Per Pelissero, the team hopes he will miss only a minimum of four weeks while on injured reserve. The impending return of Aaron Donald should help ease the loss of Garrett, but this is undoubtedly a massive blow to the Rams’ defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett said his goal ahead of Week 2’s game against the Giants is to “get healthy.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Coming off an underwhelming debut in which he failed to even record a tackle in Week 1’s loss against the 49ers, Garrett said he was “the worst version” of himself in Thursday’s game. The star pass rusher was dealing with a knee injury in the days leading up to the game, but was ultimately removed from the injury report on Wednesday. Speaking after the game, he said his knee didn’t feel 100 percent, but Garrett still managed to play on 40 snaps, per PFF. Unfortunately, he generated only three pressures and failed to get a hit on the quarterback. Hopefully, some extended time off before next Monday’s game against the Giants will be enough for Garrett to get right in the Rams’ official 2026 home debut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: As expected, Garrett gets in a full practice ahead of the Rams’ Week 1 Australia matchup against the 49ers. He did not practice Tuesday but it was likely a load management day for the star pass-rusher’s knee. Expect more of these kinds of practice weeks from Garrett moving forward; he is good to go for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) did not participate in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett was a non-participant in practice Tuesday, but it looks to be a load management day with other Rams players listed as DNP due to rest and head coach Sean McVay saying Tuesday he expects Garrett to play Week 1. Though the team will be without Aaron Donald for opening day, the Rams are still expecting to have Garrett good to go against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Myles Garrett (knee) will be ready to go for Week 1’s game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Heavily load-managed in the offseason, Garrett will enter his age-31 season fresh and ready to try to top last year’s 23-sack season in a new defense. We won’t be surprised if Garrett continues to be listed on the injury report going forward, but if he’s going to play through this there’s probably no need to be concerned about the report unless new concerns arise.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot/quad) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is a mediocre bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon playing well in the lead role. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he may be able to slightly improve his efficiency if his health continues to improve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for eight yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright managed just six touches, even with Miami running the ball 41 times today. Wright is the only running back seeing work outside of Ollie Gordon, but the latter is pushing for workhorse status, leaving Wright without much to do. He is somewhere well beyond the RB4 ranks for his Week 8 matchup with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright has rushed 14 times for 28 scoreless yards this season and has yet to receive a target in the four games he has appeared in. Fellow running back Ollie Gordon has emerged as the unquestioned RB1 for the Dolphins since the team lost De’Von Achane (knee) in Week 3. Wright is well off the fantasy radar at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright played through this listing ahead of Week 5, but it appears that he simply won’t shake it this year. It makes him hard to trust him as someone who could suddenly usurp the lead role from Ollie Gordon, but we’d be surprised if he didn’t play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: The Dolphins’ speedy back will likely serve as a change-of-pace option behind Ollie Gordon, who has outplayed Wright since De’Von Achane’s season-ending knee injury. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for 11 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright entered the day questionable with a foot injury and wound up playing nine offensive snaps with special teams mixed in. The 23-year-old is the clear backup to Ollie Gordon for now, he is best left off fantasy rosters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) is active for Week 5 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright had back-to-back limited practices to close out the week after seemingly reaggravating a foot injury. He is active against the Bengals and will backup Ollie Gordon for Week 5. The Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), RB Kaytron Allen, CB Reese Taylor, EDGE Rob Beal Jr., G DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 5 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) is questionable for Miami’s Week 5 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright was limited on Thursday and Friday after seemingly reinjuring his foot. He feels like a true wild card for Sunday. Ollie Gordon-reliant managers would benefit if Wright were ruled out, as it appears Kaytron Allen, who was just claimed on waivers today, would be the backup if Wright can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: It’s unclear if this was related to the foot that was giving Wright problems earlier this year, but a mid-week downgrade is never great news for a player. Wright has a real chance to miss Week 5. We’ll probably have a better sign of how likely it is that he plays Friday morning if no national reporters pick up the story earlier than that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed five times for seven yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: The best thing we can say about Wright’s day is that he got the start. The Dolphins kept him out there for the first drive, giving him a chance to keep his position, but he was unable to do so. Ollie Gordon outplayed him as the game progressed, rushing nine times for 100 yards and one touchdown, while Wright was relegated to unproductive offensive snaps and five kick returns for 97 yards. Wright is a zero-floor FLEX against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: While we are happy to see Willis practicing in full, we are slightly unhappy to see that he has a new injury. The Dolphins’ quarterback has already dealt with toe and right thumb injuries this season. Willis remains a viable QB2 starter against the Patriots, but this is worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns in the Dolphins’ 28-28, Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also added 37 yards and a touchdown on eight rush attempts. It was, by far, his best performance as a Dolphin. It was also the first win for both Willis and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Willis picked apart the Jets for chunk play after chunk play. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard completion to Caleb Douglas, though nearly all of those yards came after the catch. He had already connected with Douglas earlier in the game for his first touchdown of the day. Things will be a lot tougher for Willis and the Miami offense when they take on the Patriots next week. Despite the strong showing today, Willis will remain buried in the QB2 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (right thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports that Willis received treatment for his thumb injury on his right, throwing hand, though he did not share what exactly the injury is. Hopefully, it is nothing serious. If his ball placement is impacted, the Jets’ D/ST would benefit. Willis is a volatile QB2 against them this week. Willis underwent surgery on his left thumb in August 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik “is our quarterback.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “Malik needs to be better, but that’s not the headline -- we all need to be better ... everything in the pass game has to be better.. It’s the receivers, it’s the tight ends, it’s the protection,” Hafley continued. Willis is by all statistical measures one of the weakest quarterbacks in the league with his arm, but at least he’s skimping some superflex QB2 value with his legs. There’s not much reason for the Dolphins to bench him either way, as they have nobody they pressingly need to evaluate. Willis should return after the Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 137 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 31-24, Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding eight rushes for 74 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis had a poor passing day, finishing the first quarter completing 0-of-4 passes. He threw a pair of second quarter interceptions to Jordan Battle, the first coming off a tip and the second on a cross-body throw and poor decision. He also fumbled and recovered a snap in the two-minute drill while a potential third interception was dropped in the endzone in the second half. Willis recovered with a touchdown throw to Kevin Coleman in the fourth quarter but fumbled deep in the Dolphins’ own territory late in the game. He capped off his day with a quick goal-line rushing score at the end of the game but it was too little, too late. Between his decision-making and lack of ball security, Willis had a poor game but good fantasy production due to his rushing output. Willis is a fantasy QB2 heading into a Week 6 Dolphins bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 9-of-17 passes for 85 yards in the Dolphins’ 10-15, Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for 11 yards and one fumble lost.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis’ biggest plays of the day are the ones that didn’t count. Willis rolled out of the pocket, escaping pressure, on the Dolphins’ third drive and hit Chris Bell downfield for what could have been a 68-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, the officials determined that the tiniest edge of Bell’s right cleat grazed the sideline pre-catch, during the scramble drill, negating the play altogether. Heartbreaking. Willis also had a 10-yard scramble called back due to holding on the Dolphins’ fifth drive. He attempted a running fadeaway pass 25 yards downfield to Bell on 3rd-and-8 on the Dolphins’ ninth drive, but the catch was contested and ultimately fell incomplete. He is a QB2 against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said increasing Malik Willis’ designed run rate will be discussed game by game, “when we need him to.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Hafley’s full quote is fairly non-committal. The first-year head coach was asked whether Willis could receive more designed rushes with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the year. Hafley said the game planning in that regard will “go game by game,” and be employed “situationally when we need him to.” For those hoping that Willis will consistently be involved in the run game, those outings could come, but the occurrences could be volatile. Willis remains a QB2 at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 20-of-36 passes for 210 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 24-10, Week 3 loss to the Dolphins, adding nine carries for 56 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also lost a fumble late in the second quarter. Willis made some of his best throws of the season this afternoon, though the two turnovers were also his first of the year. He also missed impressive rookie Chris Bell on what could have been a pair long-ish touchdowns. He was at least running more after combining for just eight carries between Weeks 1 and 2. That is going to remain a must, especially now with De’Von Achane being waylaid with a serious knee injury. That will further change the face of this undermanned offense, and make things even harder for Willis in this no-win setup. Despite his intriguing young wideouts, he will be difficult to trust as a superflex option vs. the Vikings’ blitz-happy defense in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-23 passes for 197 yards and one touchdown in a 35-13, Week 2 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis was also held to just six yards on the ground as the 49ers’ defensive line was in his face all game long. 77 of Willis’ 197 passing yards came on one busted coverage pass to Ryan Miller in garbage time against defensive backups. There was a belief that Willis would provide fantasy value because of his talent as a runner, but the Dolphins offense has been so bad through two games that we’d find it hard to recommend playing Willis outside of the deepest two quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins Malik Willis (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis practiced in full all week, so his toe injury should not be an issue against the 49ers. The Dolphins’ quarterback told reporters this week that he is focused on taking fewer sacks moving forward. As his team fell farther behind on the scoreboard last week, Willis began holding onto the ball for far too long. Getting the ball out quickly or throwing on the run could help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus’ shoulder injury caused him to miss the Falcons’ Week 7 game against the 49ers. Although he is not fantasy-relevant, his absence reduces the target competition for the remaining pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Za’Darius Smith (neck) is expected to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: The same is true of Gervon Dexter, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Rapoport added that there is “much less optimism” for Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). That could mean an uptick in snaps for rookie wideout Zachariah Branch. He’s worth an add in deep leagues, but this offense isn’t likely to support another fantasy-relevant pass-catcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Robinson is the immediate backup to Bijan Robinson in the Falcons’ backfield, seeing his best usage in run-heavy game scripts. He was limited with a hamstring injury on Wednesday but is still trending to play Week 7 against the 49ers, barring setbacks. Also limited was Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Both players are depth options at best behind the Falcons’ star-studded skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus caught 1-of-3 targets for three yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus has caught exactly one pass in each of his first two games as a Falcon. With Jahan Dotson ahead of him on the depth chart and Zachariah Branch fighting for more work, Zaccheaus is not in the FLEX mix for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus caught his only target for five yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus was on the field for 18 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 11 of their 29 dropbacks. Rookie Zachariah Branch ran a route on eight dropbacks. Neither player appears to be a major factor on an offense that really wants to run the ball, especially with Cooper Rush at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Falcons agreed to terms with WR Olamide Zaccheaus, formerly of the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: It’s far from a splashy free agent signing, but the Falcons have work to do to shore up a receiver room that is glaringly thin behind Drake London. Zaccheaus caught 39 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns in his lone season with the Bears while playing on 580 snaps — his most since 2022. Zaccheaus’ ability to play both out wide and in the slot will give some versatility to the Falcons’ offense, but we would expect more receivers to join the mix in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Bears’ Divisional round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus signed a one-year deal with the Bears this offseason and wound up being a thorn in the side of Luther Burden’s fantasy managers for the first half of the season. The veteran receiver occupied his normal role in the slot early in the year, but later saw more work on the outside. Zaccheaus caught 39 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns in the regular season, and finished the year with the third most routes run (335) of any Bears receiver, per PFF. Whether he’s back with the Bears in 2026 or playing elsewhere, Zaccheaus seems destined to play out the rest of his career on one-year deals and will likely ink another deal similar to his current one this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheus caught 1-of-2 targets for 8 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Wild Card Round victory over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheus came down with just the one catch, but it was a big one; a touchdown over the middle that got the Bears to within three points. The wideout is well behind the other targets in the Chicago passing attack, and likely won’t be a big factor against the Eagles or Rams next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will continue calling plays.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel gets the bye week to recalibrate after six weeks of disgraceful football from his unit, but it’s clear McDaniel’s leash is incredibly short. PFT’s Mike Florio reported a week ago that the Chargers could ultimately replace McDaniel with Adam Gase, who currently holds the title of pass game specialist. They currently rank dead last in points and 28th in yards. If the results are no different versus the Rams this week, McDaniel may be out of a job by Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that there is “growing buzz” that the Chargers could fire OC Mike McDaniel “soon,” and potentially replace him with pass game specialist Adam Gase.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: According to Florio, Gase “is expected to take over if McDaniel is fired.” The Chargers go on bye in Week 7, so this is the best time to install a new offense if they really intend to do so. Gase previously served as head coach of the Jets and Dolphins, though those stints are hardly reassuring. His offenses have frequently fallen short of expectations. The 0-6 Chargers are searching for answers, though, and the McDaniel-Justin Herbert pairing does not seem to be working out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: When asked if Chargers OC Mike McDaniel is going to continue calling plays, coach Jim Harbaugh said the team is “going to look at everything.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: Harbaugh made clear that his team has to “address everything,” especially the offense, and acknowledged that the Chargers aren’t scoring enough points. He added that the plan is to watch today’s game tape and “get with our offensive coaches” to figure things out. Although McDaniel could end up losing play-calling duties, Harbaugh owned the team’s offensive woes, saying it “starts” with him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said he doesn’t plan to intervene in the offense if it continues to struggle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: When asked if he had any plans of intervening, Harbaugh offered his endorsement of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, saying, “No. We trust Mike. We believe in Mike.” The 0-3 Chargers have struggled mightily out of the gate to start the season, failing to score more than 16 points in a game while also turning the ball over six times. Even in a game where the Chargers forced five turnovers off of Josh Allen and the Bills and registered four sacks, they were unable to capitalize on multiple opportunities to take the lead in the 24-16 defeat. We’ll see how long Harbaugh can go continuing to let McDaniel run the show, but it wouldn’t be surprising if the team decided to make a change if things continue in this direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers hired Max McCaffrey as their new running backs coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McCaffrey is a former undrafted free agent NFL wide receiver who spent time with five different NFL teams. He joined the college coaching ranks as a wide receivers coach at Northern Colorado in 2020. He added offensive coordinator to his title in 2021 and held both roles for two seasons. McCaffrey joined the NFL coaching ranks as a member of former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel’s coaching staff in 2023, serving as an offensive assistant through the 2025 season. McCaffrey’s new role reunites him with McDaniel, who was hired as the Chargers’ offensive coordinator in January. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey and Commanders WR Luke McCaffrey are Max’s younger brothers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers hired former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel continued to entertain head coaching offers even after it was rumored he would join the Chargers. Now, after much deliberation, McDaniel is officially joining the Chargers to pair with Justin Herbert and company. McDaniel’s offense finished 11th or better in points scored in two of his four seasons with the Dolphins, but his final two seasons proved forgettable as Tua Tagovailoa’s limitations became apparent and defenses took advantage. McDaniel gets a top-flight QB and talent young playmakers in Ladd McConkey and Omarion Hampton to help guide his offense into 2026. All will make for enticing fantasy picks, and Herbert should enjoy a bounce back if his offensive line can stay healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel is “still in the mix” for the Raiders’ head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: According to Rapoport, McDaniel is ultimately expected to take the Chargers’ offensive coordinator role, but until the Raiders officially rule him out as a candidate, he will remain an option for the Silver and Black. McDaniel most recently canceled his interview with the Bills on Friday and withdrew his name for consideration for the Browns before that. McDaniel has made several rounds this coaching cycle to speak with teams, but the Chargers seem like the most likely fit barring a team sweeping in to hand him a head coaching gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel canceled his interview with the Bills to discuss the team’s head coaching position on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: While the Bills are just beginning their search for a new head coach after dismissing Sean McDermott earlier this week, McDaniel has already withdrawn his name from the Browns head coaching search and interviewed for multiple offensive coordinator positions before agreeing to sign on with the Chargers. Schultz says McDaniel and the Bills remain in contact for a potential interview, but there’s a “strong possibility” he moves forward with the Chargers. McDaniel’s presence in Los Angeles would be massive as fantasy managers could expect the 42-year-old coach to get the most out of Justin Herbert and the rest of the Chargers’ offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Bills are expected to interview former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel for their head-coaching vacancy on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel is expected to take the job as the Chargers’ offensive coordinator, but he’ll still take time to speak with the Bills about their head-coaching opening before settling for a coordinator role. McDaniel withdrew his name from the Browns’ head-coaching search earlier this week in favor of the Chargers’ job, but having the chance to lead a team with one of the best quarterbacks in the game in Josh Allen could be too much for McDaniel to pass up should the opportunity present itself. The Bills are early in their head-coaching search and still have other potential suitors to meet over the weekend, but for now, McDaniel is in the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel is “expected to become” the Chargers’ new offensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: The Chargers have won the Mike McDaniel sweepstakes, expecting to hire the former Dolphins head coach to their open offensive coordinator role. Several teams were in on the 42-year-old, who was interviewing for both head coaching and offensive coordinator roles. According to Schefter, McDaniel is informing teams they are out and staying in Los Angeles for the evening with the expectation he is the next Chargers’ offensive coordinator. For fantasy purposes, we are in for a faster-paced offense under Justin Herbert. Omarion Hampton is in line for more opportunity in the passing game while the wide receiver room gets better opportunities in McDaniel’s offense when compared to former offensive coordinator Greg Roman’s passing game concepts. Fantasy managers can expect to be more bullish on Herbert and the Chargers offense for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Rams signed K Joshua Karty, formerly of the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Karty spent time with the Rams from 2024-25. He now resides on their practice squad and could end up kicking on game day, as the Rams work through their ongoing kicker issues. The Rams also signed LS Jake McQuaide and LB Jon Rhattigan to the practice squad. They released OL Austin Blaske, CB Nyzier Fourqurean and LB Elias Neal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Titans work out K Joshua Karty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Karty appeared in 25 games over the past two seasons for the Rams. He made 39-of-49 field goals over that time span, with a career-long of 58 yards. The Titans re-signed their kicker from 2025, Joey Slye, but are still looking to bring in competition with Karty’s tryout on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Cardinals waived K Joshua Karty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Karty produced a 67 percent field goal conversion rate and an 88 percent extra point conversion rate with the Cardinals last year. He was slated to compete with K Chad Ryland this offseason. It appears as though Ryland is the victor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Cardinals signed K Joshua Karty to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Karty and DL P.J. Mustipher were exclusive rights free agents and both signed their one-year tenders to return to the Cardinals. Karty joined the Cardinals at the end of last season after beginning his career with the Rams. He’ll get the chance to compete with Chad Ryland for a kicking role in 2026. Mustipher was a steady contributor with the Cardinals’ defensive line rotation and will get a chance to carve out a role once more.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Cardinals signed K Joshua Karty off the Rams’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Will we get a Chad Ryland release move here, or will the 2025 Cardinals create some sort of two-kicker abomination scenario with their remaining time? There are so many questions to ask, and so little that we know. And so little of it that feels like it matters. Someone will kick and be a decent option against the Bengals in Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Rams signed K Joshua Karty to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: The move comes just three days after the team waived the veteran kicker. He had been a healthy inactive for three straight games prior to his release, but it appears the team wants to keep him close as they continue their march to the postseason. Harrison Mevis is expected to continue on as the starter, at least for the time being, after going a perfect 17-for-17 on PATs and 2-for-2 on field goal attempts in his four games with the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Rams waived K Joshua Karty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Harrison Mevis, aka “The Thiccer Kicker,” has won the in-season kicking battle over Karty. Karty has been a healthy scratch by the Rams for three straight weeks after going 10-for-15 on field goal attempts and 23-for-26 on his extra point attempts. In those three games, Mevis has made both of his field goal tries and is a perfect 13-for-13 on PATs. Karty is a sixth-round pick from the 2024 draft class and fared much better in his rookie season, going 29-for-34 on his field goal tries which included six made field goals from 50-plus yards. There are enough kicker-needy teams in the league that suggest Karty should land on a practice squad soon, but his time with the Rams is over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Rams declared K Joshua Karty, WR Xavier Smith, RB Jarquez Hunter, S Chris Smith II, OL David Quessenberry, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 12 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Karty is inactive for the second consecutive week, with the team electing to go with Harrison Mevis as their kicker. Smith (concussion) was unable to practice this week and will miss his first game of the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Rams declared K Joshua Karty, QB Stetson Bennett IV, RB Jarquez Hunter, OL Beaux Limmer, OL D.J. Humphries, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 11 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Karty will be a healthy scratch for a second straight week, with Harrison Mevis, the so-called Thiccer Kicker, starting for the Rams. Mevis is a decent fantasy option in what could be a high-scoring affair. Davante Adams, dealing with an oblique injury, will play against Seattle after practicing in full on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Harrison Mevis will again be the team’s kicker in Week 11 against Seattle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-kar.analysis: Mevis, the “Thiccer Kicker,” did not attempt a field goal against the 49ers, settling for six made extra points. Seattle will probably force some more attempts this week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Devonte Wyatt (ankle) is questionable for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Wyatt got in two limited practices this week, so we’re going to assume he gets the green light ahead of kickoff. Wyatt has two sacks and one forced fumble across seven starts this year. Green Bay signed him to a three-year extension in the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers signed DT Devonte Wyatt to a three-year, $57 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schultz was the first to report the deal, which includes a $20 million signing bonus. Wyatt, 28, is entering the final year of his rookie contract, but will now be under contract with the Packers through the 2029 season. The 2022 first-rounder was on pace for a career year in 2025 before an ankle injury ended his season in Week 13. Wyatt has totaled four or more sacks in each of the last three seasons while totaling 21 TFLs and three fumble recoveries over that span.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said DL Devonte Wyatt (ankle) is out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Wyatt finishes his fourth season with his best PFF tackling grade (76.8) of his career and continued to be a solid contributing pass rusher. He’ll enter his fifth-year option season in 2026 after he recovers from this ankle fracture, and will likely be available for training camp at some point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Devonte Wyatt suffered a fractured ankle in Week 13’s win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said after the game that things “didn’t look good” for Wyatt. Now that the nature of his injury has been revealed, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport notes that Wyatt’s season “is expected to be over.” Wyatt has totaled 27 tackles, four sacks, and six TFLs for the Packers this season, and is among the league’s best interior linemen. His absence will be felt by a defense that ranks fourth in points and yards allowed this season, as rookie sixth-rounder Warren Brinson now appears slated for more work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Devonte Wyatt (knee) is “week to week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Wyatt’s injury appeared to be a big factor in Green Bay’s trouble stopping Dallas on Sunday night. Nazir Stackhouse and Karl Brooks filled in inside, but neither is as effective as the 2022 first-rounder had been in the first few games of the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers exercised DL Devonte Wyatt’s fifth-year team option for 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Wyatt has proven himself as a capable interior pass rusher over the last two seasons, totaling 77 quarterback pressures and 12 sacks. He can be a liability in run defense, though. If he is able to take a step in the latter role, he has strong odds of receiving a hefty long-term contract next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers have exercised DT Devonte Wyatt’s fifth-year team option for 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: The 27-year-old, who was the 28th overall pick in 2022, has played in 47 games in three seasons with the Packers, recording 12.5 sacks, including five in 2024. Wyatt, who will make $13.9 million in 2026 (per OverTheCap), was the Packers’ highest-graded defensive lineman last season, per PFF.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said the team would “like to keep those guys around for 2026 and beyond” when asked about DL Devonte Wyatt and LB Quay Walker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Wyatt and Walker have not been dominant forces, so the beat writer scuttlebutt has been that both may not have their fifth-year options picked up only due to cost. An extension ahead of the deadline to exercise the fifth-year option in a few weeks is a possibility. Wyatt has been an adequate pass rusher through his first three seasons with Green Bay, but his run defense has been questionable — he had a 52.0 PFF run defense grade in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers DL Devonte Wyatt (lower leg) left Green Bay’s Wild Card round game against the Eagles and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Wyatt left the game early in proceedings, totaling just five snaps before leaving. Should the Packers come back and advance to the Divisional Round, his status will be questionable. Wyatt played 14 games and racked up five sacks and 23 combined tackles in the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.headline: Packers declared DL Devonte Wyatt, DE Brenton Cox, TE John FitzPatrick, T Travis Glover, C Jacob Monk, and FS Kitan Oladapo as inactive for Green Bay’s Week 7 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonte-wy.analysis: Wyatt has missed three straight games since suffering an ankle injury. All of the rest of these inactives are healthy scratches as Dontayvion Wicks and Colby Wooden are playing off questionable tags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Coby Bryant (knee) has not yet resumed change-of-direction activities, which will be a “big hurdle” in his recovery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on August 11th that Bryant would miss 4-6 months after injuring his knee in training camp. The high-priced free agent signee was brought in to help revamp the Bears’ safety unit. This remains a unit to target in fantasy, with Bryant out until at the NFL playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Coby Bryant (knee) underwent surgery and will miss 4-6 months.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: “Bears are hoping he can return for the playoffs,” Schefter notes. It’s a brutal blow for the Bears to lose their star free-agent acquisition before training camp even concludes. Chicago didn’t exactly have a stellar defense last year, so perhaps this will make every Bears game a track meet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Bears S Coby Bryant is “expected to be sidelined 8-10 weeks” due to a knee injury he suffered on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: Bryant was carted from Monday’s practice and is now set to miss significant time. The fifth-year safety suffered a hyperextended knee, a bone bruise, and a small fracture, per Schefter, but he is not expected to need surgery. Bryant signed a three-year, $40 million deal with the Bears this offseason and is expected to take over the position vacated by Kevin Byard. Bryant’s absence will cost him some games in the regular season and could put him on track to return some time between Week 3 and Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: Bears S Coby Bryant was carted from the practice field on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: We are still waiting for more details on this one, but according to reporters who were at the field, Bryant could be seen grabbing at his left knee as he made his way off the field. The 27-year-old safety signed a three-year, $40 million contract with the Bears this offseason after spending the previous four seasons with the Seahawks. Bryant totaled 66 tackles and four interceptions with the Seahawks last season and is expected to see a significant role for the defense this season. We will check back in when we learn more about Bryant’s injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: Bears agreed to terms with S Coby Bryant, formerly of the Seahawks, on a three-year, $40 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: Bryant appears to be replacing Kevin Byard — though we’ll see what the Bears wind up doing here, it could be that they plan to invest heavily at safety with Jaquan Brisker also a free agent. Bryant played a career-high 1,163 snaps on defense for the Seahawks last year and had a 67.2 PFF coverage grade. He’s not an amazing tackler, but Bryant should provide plenty of range for the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: Seahawks declared LT Josh Jones (ankle/knee) active for Week 18 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: Jones will be the starting left tackle agaisnt the 49ers with Charles Cross (hamstring) unable to go. The inactives for the winner-take-all game for Seattle will be Cross, TE Nick Kallerup, S Coby Bryant, QB Jalen Milroe, LB Jared Ivey, OL Mason Richman and OL Bryce Cabledue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: Seahawks LT Charles Cross (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: Cross suffered the injury in the Seahawks’ Week 15 win over the Colts and missed Week 16 against the Rams. He was reported to have a 2-4 week hamstring injury last week, marking this the second week of the reported timeline. Cross is likely to miss Week 17 with a DNP designation on Wednesday. Also listed as DNP Wednesday was S Coby Bryant (knee), who suffered a knee injury in Week 16. Bryant will need to practice the rest of the week to play in Week 17 against the Panthers, but he is in jeopardy of missing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Seahawks CB Riq Woolen’s knee injury is “not considered serious.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: Seahawks S Coby Bryant (knee) is expected to miss “some time.” Woolen has broken up seven passes and intercepted one pass this season. Fowler describes him as being only “banged up.” Bryant has broken up two passes and ranks second on the team with four interceptions. Losing either player hurts. Hopefully, Woolen can play in Week 17 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: Seahawks declared DB Coby Bryant, CB Tre Brown, CB Artie Burns, FB Nick Bellore, OT McClendon Curtis, OT Charles Cross, and G Ben Brown inactive for Week 4 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: Most notably, both tight end Will Dissly and tight end Noah Fant are absent from the inactives list, which should allow the Seahawks to play primarily from 12-personnel again in Week 4. The snap rates amongst the three primary tight ends have been mostly split evenly, but the bigger news is the expected low snap rates for rookie wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.headline: Seahawks CB Tariq Woolen (chest) is doubtful for Week 3 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/coby-bryan.analysis: Fellow corner Coby Bryant is listed as out because of a toe injury. Though Seattle’s secondary is decimated heading into Week 3, it’s hard to imagine their opponents taking advantage of the situation. The Panthers are starting Andy Dalton this week while Bryce Young deals with an ankle issue. Dalton ranks near the bottom of the starting quarterback for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Carolina also ruled out left guard Damien Lewis, who is dealing with a knee issue. Phillips also missed last week’s game because of a hamstring injury. The hope is that the mini-bye after Thursday Night Football is enough to get him back for Week 9. Phillips has 2.5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers declared EDGE Jaelan Phillips, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, C Sam Hecht, OT Stone Forsythe, and EDGE TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips is a big loss, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the Panthers vs. a more-injured and undermanned Bucs squad. Phillips is week to week after pulling his hammy in Week 6 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips came into this game questionable with a hamstring injury but was able to suit up. Unfortunately, he got hurt early in the first quarter and is unlikely to return. Considering he had the bye week to heal and is not 100 percent, it seems likely that the EDGE rusher will miss some time with the injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Devin Lloyd (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Lloyd was one of the Panthers’ premier free agent additions this offseason, and he’s already proven to be worth the investment. Lloyd terrorized the Falcons in Week 2 with a sack and two interceptions, one of which was a pick-six. Fellow free agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips was also absent from practice today. He is dealing with a back injury. Though the Browns aren’t a particularly good offense right now, it would still be a massive boon for them if Lloyd and Phillips are out for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers agreed to terms with EDGE Jaelan Phillips, formerly of the Eagles, on a four-year, $120 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the deal includes an eye-popping $80 million guaranteed. The Eagles were reportedly working to retain the 27-year-old (in May) pass rusher, but got outbid by the typically free-spending Panthers. A former Dolphin who flourished during his eight-game trade cameo for the Eagles last season, Phillips finally stayed healthy last year after an injury marred 2023-24 run. That’s a concern going forward, but Phillips is a pass-rushing difference maker when on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports “Philly isn’t done trying” to re-sign Jaelan Phillips before the legal tampering period begins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: It sounds like the Eagles are making a push to re-sign Phillips before the legal tampering period begins on Monday. Phillips, whom the Eagles acquired at last year’s trade deadline, totaled 28 tackles, two sacks, and one fumble recovery in his eight games with the team last season, and is believed to have a strong market should he become available. While the soon-to-be 27-year-old dealt with two serious injuries in 2023 and 2024, he managed to play in all 17 regular season games in 2025 and is a clear difference maker for any defense he’s on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Odafe Oweh, Jaelan Phillips, Trey Hendrickson and Boye Mafe are on Dallas’ “radar” in the coming days.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: The Cowboys lost out on the Maxx Crosby trade sweepstakes and will have to pivot — they reportedly had some interest in Hendrickson at the deadline. Oweh probably makes more sense as a younger upside swing, and this is the third of four NFC East teams in on Jaelan Phillips that we’ve heard about.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: ESPN’s Tim McManus believes the “expectation” is the Eagles will make a push to re-sign EDGE Jaelan Phillips.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips came over in a midseason trade from Miami and had a great half-year in Philadelphia, posting a 77.1 PFF defensive grade in nine games. The Eagles stand to net a high compensatory pick if Phillips leaves, but it seems like they’d rather just keep the player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens designated Adam Randall to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall was placed on injured reserve at the end of training camp with an undisclosed injury. The team now has three weeks to officially activate him from injured reserve. Once healthy, Randall will be contending with Rasheen Ali for the Ravens’ rarely used RB3 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens placed Adam Randall on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Cornerback Bilhal Kone was also placed on IR. Both players can return after four games. Randall was likely parked behind Justice Hill as the Ravens’ RB3 heading into the season. That role now belongs to Rasheen Ali, at least until Randall is back in action. He played in the team’s final preseason game and the team has not said what this injury is yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec believes the Ravens see Justice Hill “as a good complement to Derrick Henry and really value his ability out of the backfield and in blitz pickup.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Hill ended 2025 on injured reserve because of a neck issue. He was reportedly a cut candidate during the offseason and the team selected Clemson running back Adam Randall on Day Three of the draft. It seemed possible that the team planned on replacing Hill this year, but Zrebiec shot that idea down, at least for the start of the season. Zrebiec answered, “I can’t see that happening from the jump,” in reference to a question about Randall opening the season as Baltimore’s backup running back. Hill caught 21 passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in 10 games last year. He also punched in a pair of touchdowns on the ground despite running just 18 times. His ceiling is extremely limited, even in the event of a Henry injury, but Hill should have some standalone RB4 value in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens signed fifth-round pick RB Adam Randall to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Per Spotrac, the deal is worth $4.62 million and includes a $379,480 signing bonus. Randall is the team owner, Steve Bisciotti’s first handpicked player. He converted from wide receiver to running back for Clemson’s 2025 season and posted a 168/814/10 rushing line and a 36/254/3 receiving line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens’ Ryan Mink reports that team owner Steve Bisciotti was allowed to draft a player for the first time ever this year and chose former Clemson RB Adam Randall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: The Ravens drafted Randall with the No. 174 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft’s fifth round yesterday. Bisciotti has been the Ravens’ majority owner since 2004 and was reportedly “begging” general manager Eric DeCosta for the chance to draft a rookie this year. According to DeCosta, Bisciotti “did his research and studied the tape, talked to people.” Bisciotti notably has a really good relationship with Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney. Swinney moved Randall (6’3/232) from wide receiver to running back for the 2025 season after Randall showcased shifty moves when given the chance to run the ball and contribute as a returner late in 2024. Whether Randall can earn the No. 2 or No. 3 running back role remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens selected Clemson RB Adam Randall with the No. 174 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall could be the next big-bodied WR-to-RB convert to earn an NFL roster spot. He suffered a torn ACL during a 2022 spring practice and recovered in time to resume playing in Week 3 that year. Randall’s splash plays in the run game and return game late in 2024 inspired coach Dabo Swinney to move Randall from WR to RB for the 2025 season. Built to handle a three-down workload, Randall, 21, measured 6’3/232 at the NFL Scouting Combine. In his lone season at running back, Randall produced a 168/814/10 rushing line and a 36/254/3 receiving line. Randall is still learning how to play running back, so he comes with a very low floor, but his frame and dual-threat profile make him a name to know for fantasy purposes. He will likely get a crack at replacing Keaton Mitchell’s part-time role as a rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Clemson freshman WR Adam Randall is rehabbing well from his torn ACL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall (6'3/198) suffered a torn ACL on April 6th during spring practice. He is reportedly doing well in his rehab and head coach Dabo Swinney said that he expects Randall to return at some point this season. A four-star recruit from this year’s class, it’s unlikely Randall makes much of an impact even if he does return to the field this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Clemson incoming freshman WR Adam Randall has torn his ACL in spring practice, will undergo surgery later this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: It’s a big blow for the Tigers, who are losing their top receiver Justyn Ross to the draft. Randall (6'2"/215) was a four-star recruit in the 2022 class, the 17th ranked WR and the fourth ranked player from South Carolina. He could have helped jolt a disappointing passing game for Clemson, but he’ll miss his true freshman season and almost certainly medical redshirt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Clemson received a verbal commitment from four-star 2022 WR Adam Randall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall (6'3/198) is a big, physical outside receiver from Myrtle Beach, SC that is considered the fourth best recruit in South Carolina and 19th best wideout from the 2022 prep class. The commitment is a pivotal in-state get for Clemson, as Randall fits the size and speed traits that HC Dabo Swinney covets. Randall was heavily pursued by Tennessee, Georgia, LSU, Miami, Florida State, Oregon and a host of other schools.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: Chiefs signed Justin Tucker, formerly of the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: Tucker will start on the Chiefs practice squad. His signing comes a few days after Harrison Butker missed two field goal attempts against the Seahawks. On the season Butker has missed five of his 16 attempts, and over his past 11 games he’s missed seven kicks. Tucker, who recently competed for the Dolphins kicker job, hasn’t kicked since 2024 in Baltimore, when he missed eight of his 30 field goal tries. The Ravens released Tucker in 2025 after 16 massage therapists accused him of sexual misconduct.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: Free agent K Justin Tucker visited the Dolphins on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: Since his 10-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy over sexual misconduct allegations, Tucker has tried out for the Saints, Colts, Jets, and now Dolphins over the past two seasons. He lost out to Zane Gonzalez for this job despite what, per Aaron Wilson, was an impressive workout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: Jets hosted Justin Tucker for a workout.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero notes that the Jets hosted a group workout and are exploring all options at kicker. They already claimed Blake Grupe and re-signed Jason Sanders to their practice squad this week. Tucker worked out for multiple teams last year after serving a 10-game suspension for violating the team’s personal conduct policy. He was never signed and hasn’t kicked in a game since the 2024 season, which was the worst of his career by far. Tucker made just 73.3 percent of his field goal tries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: Free agent K Justin Tucker visited with the Colts on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: We can see why the Colts wouldn’t have wanted that to get out ahead of signing Blake Grupe. Still, this is two teams in two weeks that have kicked the tires on Tucker despite his 10-game suspension over sexual misconduct allegations. He’s probably going to continue to get work on the kicker tryout circuit. The Colts also brought in Maddux Trujillo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Saints will host free agent K Justin Tucker for a tryout this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: Tucker’s 10-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy due to his involvement in sexually inappropriate behavior was lifted two weeks ago. Now, the 36-year-old kicker will have a chance to try out for the Saints, who are looking for a potential upgrade over Blake Grupe after his two missed field goals in Week 12’s loss to the Falcons. Tucker had his worst season as a pro in 2024, converting on a career-low 73.3 percent of his field goal attempts while going 11-for-19 from 40-plus yards. Among other participants in the tryout will be Cade York, who last kicked for the Commanders in 2024, going 0-for-2 on his attempts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: The NFL suspended free agent K Justin Tucker without pay for the first 10 weeks of the 2025 regular season for violating the league’s personal conduct policy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: Tucker was released by the Ravens in early May, roughly three months after 16 massage therapists accused Tucker of sexual misconduct. The suspension is the culmination of a multi-month investigation conducted by the NFL. Per ESPN’s Jamison Hensley, Tucker may still sign with a team and “attend training camp and play in preseason games before the suspension starts” on August 26. He will be eligible for reinstatement on Tuesday, November 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: Ravens released K Justin Tucker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: The writing was on the wall after the draft, where Baltimore drafted rookie kicker Tyler Loop as Tucker’s replacement. Tucker has spent most of the late season and offseason dealing with sexual misconduct allegations from massage therapists in Baltimore-area spas, and had by far the worst season of his career in 2024, making 73.3 percent of his 30 field-goal attempts. The Ravens stood by him throughout the process and framed moving on from him as a “football decision” in a statement, but it’s hard to believe they would have moved on from him if not for the allegations. Tucker will likely have to clear his name, as Brandon McManus did this past offseason, before he gets another NFL chance. The NFL’s investigation into Tucker’s behavior is, per CBS’ Jonathan Jones, still “under review.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: Ravens head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that personnel decisions regarding the kicker position “will be based on football.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: Reporters asked Harbaugh about the NFL’s open investigation into Justin Tucker’s 16 sexual assault allegations, and whether the Ravens might move on from Tucker with sixth-round rookie K Tyler Loop now in the fold. Harbaugh answered by saying the Ravens’ organization does not know “anything” about the investigation and has not been given any information by the league. Per Harbaugh, “every decision” the Ravens make must therefore “be based on football,” citing things like practice performance, draft capital and salary cap implications as critical factors. Loop promisingly converted 45-of-47 field goals attempted from 0-to-39 yards out in his college career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: ESPN’s Jamison Hensley reports the Ravens have “invested countless hours” into scouting incoming rookie kickers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: Ravens senior special teams coach Randy Brown has traveled across the country in recent weeks scouting incoming kickers as Justin Tucker’s 2025 status remains in question. Sixteen massage therapists from Baltimore-area spas have accused Tucker of sexual misconduct. Tucker, 35, has denied the allegations as the league investigates. “Obviously, there are a lot of layers to that whole conversation, but it’s something we would have to do no matter what,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “At this point in time, you have to look. You always have to do your due diligence, so we will be prepared to do that on draft day if we feel like we need to and if the right guy is there.” The Ravens are the only team in the NFL to never take a kicker in the draft. That could change this year: The team is holding a private workout for Florida State’s Ryan Fitzgerald, who made all 13 of this field goal attempts last season and is widely expected to be the first kicker off the draft board.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.headline: Ravens HC John Harbaugh said “it’s something we have to do, no matter what, at this point in time,” when asked about the possibility of drafting a kicker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-tuc.analysis: It goes without saying that Justin Tucker’s tenure with the Ravens is likely trending toward an end as the Ravens and the league continue to investigate the sexual misconduct allegations that have followed the veteran kicker since the season’s end. Tucker converting on a career-low 73.3 percent of his field goal attempts last season likely isn’t helping his case, either. This is the strongest any member of the Ravens organization has sounded so far about moving on from Tucker, as the organizational message has more often been one of letting the league’s investigation play out. Saying “no matter what” sure paints a picture of some unsavory results in that investigation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Cardinals signed Zay Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: He was deemed the best of a huge tryout with Ronnie Bell, Xavier Guillory, Jack Plummer and James Proche. Jones will work as a depth piece in Arizona, and for all you know that hasn’t always been the case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Texans released WR Zay Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: He didn’t sign until late August after rehabbing a torn Achilles in Week 10. Jones was an emergency signing for the Texans, but they followed up on it by trading for Kayshon Boutte. The Boutte deal made Jones’ path to a roster spot tenuous. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Texans signed WR Zay Jones, formerly of the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: Jones and former Buccaneers WR Sterling Shepard have been brought in to help shore up the Texans’ wide receiver corps. Second-year WR Jayden Higgins (knee) was placed on injured reserve today. The Texans are also still trying to figure out what they have in WR Tank Dell (knee), and WR Jaylin Noel (finger/hamstring) missed time in training camp with a pair of injuries. Jones is coming off a season-ending Achilles tendon rupture. Neither he nor Shepard are worth drafting.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Free agent WR Zay Jones worked out for the Texans on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: Jones played for the Cardinals last year, catching 12 passes for 183 yards before rupturing an Achilles tendon in Week 10 against the Seahawks. The Texans are hoping to bolster their wide receiver corps after losing WR Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Free agent WR Zay Jones visited the Jaguars on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: The 31-year-old is coming off a torn achilles’ tendon suffered last November. He spent 2022-23 in Jacksonville, but that was under Doug Pederson’s coaching staff. Were Jones to end up back in Duval, it would be as a pure depth piece for one of the league’s deepest receiver groups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Cardinals WR Zay Jones suffered a torn Achilles in Week 10’s loss to the Seahawks and will be out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: Jones felt his Achilles pop in Sunday’s loss and was assisted off the field by medical trainers. The nine-year vet has caught 12 passes for 183 scoreless yards this season and re-upped with the Cardinals on a one-year deal earlier this offseason. The 30-year-old receiver will now have surgery to repair his Achilles, but could be set to join a team next offseason once healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Cardinals WR Zay Jones (knee) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: Jones is rarely on the FLEX radar these days, but a matchup against the Cowboys can help anyone score fantasy points. Jones remains limited through two practices, so he is clearly less than 100.0 percent. If active, he can be started by managers in need as a boom-bust FLEX option, reliant upon the deep ball.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Cardinals WR Zay Jones (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: The Cardinals face the Cowboys in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game, so Jones should have plenty of time to get his knee game-ready. The volatile downfield wide receiver is a boom-bust FLEX option, given the matchup. His odds of catching another deep pass could increase if QB Kyler Murray (foot) misses another game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Zay Jones caught 2-of-2 targets for 67 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: Jones made a pair of grabs in the Cardinals’ two minute drills, keeping possessions alive for Jacoby Brissett. He first converted a 43-yard reception in the first half to keep a scoring drive going for the Cardinals. His next target and catch came towards the end of the fourth quarter, catching a pass for 24 yards to continue the final Cardinals drive. Jones was oft-used last week with Marvin Harrison (concussion) exiting the game, but he took a backseat with Harrison back. Jones is best left on fantasy benches for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.headline: Cardinals WR Zay Jones (knee) is questionable for Week 7 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-jones/.analysis: Jones returned to practice in a limited capacity on Friday, making him truly questionable to play this weekend. With No. 1 WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (concussion) cleared to play, Jones would only be a dart-throw FLEX option, if he is also active. The Packers’ top-tier defense does not make for a matchup to target.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: 49ers acquired DeForest Buckner from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: Buckner exits the Colts the same day Quenton Nelson does. It’s a coup for a 49ers defense that has lacked some oomph in one-on-one situations on the defensive line. Buckner, who was with the 49ers early in his career before being traded to the Colts for a first-round pick, will run it back with his original team. The Colts simply weren’t in a position to ask much for the 32-year-old, as they were capped at receiving only a fifth-round compensatory pick for him due to his age. The 49ers are generating a pretty nice playoff-ready defense assuming (as is always the question in San Francisco) it can there healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts could trade Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: Schefter listed out DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, and Downs as players that could potentially be on the move as the Colts continue what from all outside appearances looks to be a fire sale. He thinks Buckner will be the next player on the move and likely go for less than Quenton Nelson. Downs certainly hasn’t impressed with his opportunity this season, but he’s a valuable receiver and Indianapolis didn’t exactly but him in an ideal scenario with Alec Pierce hurt and Keenan Allen playing alongside him while Daniel Jones struggles to regain his 2025 form.
