https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: Colts DT DeForest Buckner (neck) has been cleared to practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: It’s great news for the Colts after Buckner had surgery on his neck late in the season. Buckner didn’t participate in any offseason activities. He’ll likely be brought along slowly, but this is terrific news for the odds of him suiting up for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports a return for DeForest Buckner (neck) at the start of training camp is “very much up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: The article cites Buckner resuming running in April, but he was not involved in spring workouts and the picture painted here is one where a Week 1 return is no sure thing. Buckner underwent neck surgery late last season and turned 32 years old in March. The Colts defense looks like a shaky unit this year anyway, but if Buckner or Charvarius Ward (concussions) can’t make it to Week 1 they could potentially be flammable and a unit to stream against.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he would “definitely love to be a Colt for life,” as he enters the final year of his contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: Taylor, 27, has totaled more than 320 offensive touches in each of the last two seasons. His current $14 million annual salary makes him the seventh-highest-paid running back in the league. Taylor has set multiple Colts records, operating as the centerpiece of Indianapolis’ offense for years. FOX 59’s Mike Chappell writes that it is “uncertain whether there’s a mutual desire to keep Taylor in Indy beyond 2025.” Multiple Colts stars, including DTs DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, OG Quenton Nelson and WR Josh Downs, are also entering the final year of their deal. Chappell believes owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon “might believe it’s more prudent to allow the upcoming season to run its course rather than reinvest in lucrative contracts.” Time will tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: Colts DT DeForest Buckner (neck) began running this week and believes a return for training camp remains possible.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: Buckner underwent season-ending neck surgery late last year. It’s a good sign that he’s meeting with reporters and that GM Chris Ballard also had the same timeline for his return yesterday. The star defensive tackle is entering his age-32 season and the final year of his contract in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: Colts placed DL DeForest Buckner (neck) on season-ending injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: He re-aggravated his neck injury in Monday night’s loss to the 49ers. Steichen said that Buckner will undergo surgery next week and that he “expects Buckner to play again next season.” Buckner has a $26.6 million cap hit in the last year of his contract in 2026 and might be a candidate for a restructure given how this year went. His age-31 season ends with 10 starts, four sacks, and 47 combined tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.headline: Colts activated DT DeForest Buckner from injured reserve for Week 16’s game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deforest-b.analysis: As a procedural move to activate Buckner, the Colts also waived QB Brett Rypien. It was reported before the weekend that Buckner was expected to play in Week 16’s game, but the Colts made it official on Monday with his activation. Buckner has been sidelined with a neck injury since Week 9 and should provide an immediate boost to a defense that ranks 22nd in total yards allowed but has been a top-10 run-stopping unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: Giants GM Joe Schoen, asked about the future of the team’s quarterback position said: “To have two young guys with Jaxson and J.J., both talented players, it’s a good position to be in.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: In other words, it wasn’t exactly an endorsement that Jaxson Dart is the franchise quarterback. Dart, out for the year with a meniscus repair, will enter the third year of his rookie contract as the likely favorite to start assuming Nine hasn’t just blossomed into a great quarterback overnight. But it sounds like the Giants are at least open to the idea that McCarthy could alter the calculus here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said the possibility of Jaxson Dart (knee) returning during the playoffs “may be a bit ambitious.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: Everyone but Harbaugh knew Dart wasn’t returning for the playoffs the moment his meniscus repair procedure was announced. Harbaugh, meanwhile, held out hope that his starting quarterback could return in time for a deep playoff run. Even he isn’t keeping that facade up anymore, though he noted that Dart’s surgery “went well.” Coming off an ugly win, Jameis Winston will make his second start of the year in Week 4. J.J. McCarthy will get a crack at the job when the Giants inevitably start losing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: The Giants could trade for a QB in the wake of Jaxson Dart’s injury by Monday, reports NFL Insider Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: According to Pelissero, Giants GM Joe Schoen is “working the phones” and a trade could be done as soon as Monday. The Giants gave Dart’s backup Jameis Winston a two-year contract extension just before the start of the regular season. While the Giants are looking to add to their quarterback depth, it seems unlikely that whoever they acquire at this point would be able to unseat Winston as the starter immediately. New York takes on Tennessee in Week 3 at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Jaxson Dart (knee) will undergo surgery on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: According to Raanan, the belief is that Dart will have surgery to repair his meniscus and MCL. The second-year quarterback is looking at a 4-6 month recovery period after his surgery, which will sideline him for the remainder of the regular season. Head coach John Harbaugh said earlier in the week that Dart could return in the postseason if Jameis Winston pulls off the unthinkable and leads the G-Men to their first playoff berth since 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Giants coach John Harbaugh kept “open the possibility for a postseason return” for QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: Garafolo notes that a meniscus repair typically requires a 4-6 month recovery timeline. If Dart heals at the fastest possible speed, he could return in late January. This seems somewhat unlikely, given the fact that he will also have his MCL surgically fixed and must rehab the injured PCL, but apparently Harbaugh is feeling optimistic. In the meantime, QB Jameis Winston has been named the starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: Jaxson Dart will undergo surgery on his injured knee and miss the remainder of the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: The extent of Dart’s knee injury was not initially understood, but further testing showed a serious injury to his MCL and PCL. He’ll be sidelined for the rest of the season, effectively ending the Giants’ season. Jameis Winston will likely take over as the team’s starter. It’s a letdown for Dart, who started the year hot against the Cowboys. In relief of Dart in Week 2, Winston was 25 percent below his expected completion rate, the worst mark in the league. Look for the Giants to be a run-heavy, hyper-conservative offense going forward with targets concentrated between Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers. Winston might be usable in superflex formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: FOX Sports’ Ralph Vacchiano believes the Giants’ “best bet is to commit all their first-team reps” to backup QB Jameis Winston rather than trading for a potential fill-in starter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: Vacchiano explores myriad trade options that the Giants could explore in a lengthy article, but ultimately determines that rolling with Winston, while QB Jaxson Dart (knee) is sidelined, is the team’s best course of action. According to Vacchiano, the Giants viewed Winston “as a solid veteran who was smart and talented enough to get them through a short stretch if Dart went down” when they signed him to a two-year, $13 million contract extension two weeks ago. “Their faith gets shakier when it’s a long-term proposition they were hoping to avoid,” but alas, this appears to be the situation the team is currently facing. If Winston can return to something resembling his 2019 Buccaneers form, when he posted a 5,109/33/30 passing stat line en route to an overall QB3 finish, he could facilitate usable outings for Giants pass catchers. Betting on that exact outcome is unwise, but Winston could be a QB1 streamer in the right situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said “evaluations were still ongoing” on Jaxson Dart (knee) and declined to comment on his timeline to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: Harbaugh was scooped to his press conference by multiple reporters saying that Dart was likely to miss the remainder of the season, so he probably didn’t have time to change the talking points. It feels like we’re just waiting on this to be official at this point; the Giants will likely name Jameis Winston their starter on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jaxson Dart’s knee injury is “worse than initially thought” and the team is now “facing the possibility of season-ending knee surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxson-dar.analysis: Obviously we’re looking for a follow up from the team, but this is absolutely brutal news for the Giants. Jameis Winston looked abysmal in his fill-in action against the Rams in Week 2 and, if he played like that going forward, would lower expectations for all Giants skill position players. More importantly for Dart, he’ll miss most of his second season and enter the third year of his rookie contract trying to rehab and prove to the Giants that he’s going to be their quarterback of the future. It’s a rough, rough break for the 23-year-old quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders activated WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: It was his last possible day to be reinstated in his 21-day window. The fact that Klint Kubiak spent much of Thornton’s 21-day window talking about how he had to go show us something makes us think Thornton will probably just be a depth piece for the time being. The Raiders waived Jonah Laulu to make room for Thornton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) has “got to go show us something” in the final week of his 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: This is rough. Currently on injured reserve, Thornton began practicing in Week 5, activating his 21-day practice window. The young wide receiver told reporters that he was “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” Two weeks later, the team has not yet officially removed him from injured reserve. Per Kubiak, Thornton “had a good first week, had a good second week,” but he still has to go “out there to practice to show us that he’s ready.” He’s been practicing in full for two weeks. The fact that the wide receiver-needy Raiders have not yet activated him is not encouraging. Thornton does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is getting “closer” but won’t play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton is in Week 2 of his 21-day window and figures to return in Week 7 or Week 8. Obviously there’s not much reason to trust him in fantasy at this time, but he may find a real role on Las Vegas’ depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders ruled out Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The Raiders activated Thornton’s 21-day practice window this week. Despite the young wide receiver saying he feels “ready to play,” the team has determined that he needs more time. With Jalen Nailor (concussion) also ruled out, Cody White (ankle) and Malik Benson will round out three-wide receiver sets behind Tre Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice and feels “ready to play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been on injured reserve since late August, practicing in full for the first time on Wednesday. He told Raiders media that he is “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” With Jack Bech on injured reserve, there is room for the 23-year-old speedster to earn targets if he plays in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said it’s too early to say whether WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. (undisclosed) will resume practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The lanky speedster was placed on injured reserve late in August. He is not exceptionally talented, but he can contribute meaningfully to an NFL offense. Getting him back would help keep safeties honest. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders placed WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. on the reserved/injured list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been dealing with an undisclosed injury that has prevented the wideout from practicing over the last month. The 23-year-old can return in four weeks, but there’s no timeline as to when the 2025 fourth-round pick will return to the Vegas lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton is still working his way back from an undisclosed injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: We still don’t know what Thornton is dealing with, but the second-year receiver hasn’t practiced since August 7th. Kubiak said earlier this month that he expected Thornton to return sometime during the preseason, but that didn’t come to fruition. Even if he’s able to make it back on the practice field ahead of Week 1, Thornton is unlikely to make any major contributions to the offense at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said he expects Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) to return at some point in the preseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has missed nearly a whole week of practice, paving the way for Jack Bech and rookie Malik Benson to see more reps. Kubiak said Thornton has “been banged up a little bit” this training camp, but did not go into further detail on his situation. Thornton caught 10 passes for 135 scoreless yards last season after generating plenty of camp hype. He is not on the fantasy radar at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) missed his fourth straight practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton was at practice in street clothes Tuesday, missing his fourth straight. He left a training camp practice early last week and has not received a diagnosis or return timetable. Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor, and Tre Tucker are listed as the Raiders’ starting wide receivers on the team’s first unofficial depth chart of the preseason. Thornton is listed as Nailor’s backup but may be losing ground to Malik Benson as he misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Colts placed Cam Taylor-Britt (undisclosed) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four games. Taylor-Britt has played just 91 snaps for the Colts this year after coming over as a Lou Anarumo reclamation project. He has one sack, 13 tackles, and two passes defensed so far this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Colts CB Cam Taylor-Britt has returned from his one-game suspension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Taylor-Britt is eligible to play in the Colts’ Week 2 game against the Chiefs after serving his one-game suspension in Week 1 against the Ravens. The 26-year-old corner signed a one-year deal with the Colts earlier this offseason and started two of the eight games he appeared in last season with the Bengals. Taylor-Britt totaled 21 tackles and five breakups for the Bengals last season and has spent three seasons in defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo’s scheme during their time with the Bengals, which could give him a chance to see meaningful work on game days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Colts CB Cam Taylor-Britt was suspended one game for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Taylor-Britt was sentenced to five days in jail after pleading guilty to traffic charges in January. This suspension could be related to that. Taylor-Britt, 26, closed the 2025 season on injured reserve with a foot injury. He entered free agency after four seasons with the Bengals, and the Colts signed him in March. PFF credits him with three forced incompletions last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Colts signed CB Cam Taylor-Britt, formerly of the Bengals, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Taylor-Britt has worked under DC Lou Anarumo before in Cincinnati. Entering his age-27 season, Taylor-Britt proved capable of combustible moments with the Bengals despite some flashes of great play. He’s a fine depth signing behind Charvarius Ward, who has a concussion history that can’t be ignored at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Bengals CB Cam Taylor-Britt was sentenced to five days in jail after pleading guilty to traffic charges.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Taylor-Britt, who in late November was placed on injured reserve with a foot injury, pleaded guilty to reckless driving and an unclassified no-license charge stemming from an incident in September, according to media reports. His sentence is expected to start immediately. Taylor-Britt, 26, selected by the Bengals in the second round of the 2022 NFL draft, has seven interceptions over 47 games in the NFL. It’s unclear if the team or the league will take action against him for the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Bengals placed CB Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve with a foot injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Taylor-Britt has had a rough season. He was declared inactive in Week 7, in favor of CB Josh Newton, which was purely a coaching decision, not injury-related. It has now been confirmed that Taylor-Britt has suffered a season-ending Lisfranc injury, following a report from earlier this week that he will likely require surgery. Hopefully, Taylor-Britt can successfully rehab the issue and return to play in good shape next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Bengals HC Zac Taylor said Cam Taylor-Britt is likely to need Lisfranc surgery, which would end his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Taylor-Britt played on only 10 defensive snaps in Week 11’s loss to the Steelers before exiting with a foot injury. If his season is over, Taylor-Britt will have totaled 21 tackles and five pass breakups while earning a PFF coverage grade of 57.0 on 220 coverage snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Bengals declared EDGE Trey Hendrickson, CB Cam Taylor-Britt, C Matt Lee, WR Jermaine Burton, TE Tanner Hudson and DT McKinnley Jackson inactive for Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Hendrickson is sidelined by a hip injury, though the Bengals fortunately get EDGE Shemar Stewart (ankle) back after a four-game absence. Taylor-Britt has evidently been benched in favor of CB Josh Newton this week. The Bengals’ offense lost two tight ends last week, with Hudson suffering a concussion and Mike Gesicki suffering a pectoral injury that landed him on injured reserve this week. Bengals TE Noah Fant is suddenly on the streaming TE1 radar as a result.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Bengals HC Zac Taylor said CB Cam Taylor-Britt (ankle) will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Taylor-Britt’s return comes at a solid time after the defense struggled against the Vikings in Week 3. It’s a substantial return for a secondary that has performed over expectations through three weeks, largely due to heavy zone rates that require consistent communication on the back end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.headline: Bengals declared CB Cam Taylor-Britt, WR Jermaine Burton, TE Tanner Hudson, DT McKinnley Jackson and EDGE Shemar Stewart inactive for Week 3 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-taylor.analysis: Frequently injured, Taylor-Britt heads back to the sidelines after serving as an every-snap player in Weeks 1 and 2. It’s the last thing this struggling defense needed, but the bigger injury problems, of course, are on the offensive side of the ball with Joe Burrow’s lengthy absence beginning this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Elijah Mitchell rushed three times for 11 yards in Philadelphia’s Week 7 loss to the Cowboys, adding three receptions for 23 yards on four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: With both Saquon Barkley (back) and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) shuttling off in the fourth quarter, it was practice squad elevation Mitchell helping to close out a loss to the Cowboys. It’s certainly possible that Mitchell will be involved in whatever happens next week given the two injuries ahead of him, making him an interesting waiver wire thought.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Eagles signed RB Eljiah Mitchell to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: This time, they mean it. Mitchell has a decent chance to be elevated for Week 7 based on what we know today, which is that the Eagles waived Ian Wheeler from the practice squad and have only Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. This appears to be quite a fluid situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Eagles signed RB Elijah Mitchell.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: Mitchell now gets to be the “other” player who has been on New England and Philadelphia’s rosters this offseason. Released by the Patriots after the draft, Mitchell will try to catch on as a depth back behind Saquon Barkley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Free agent RB Khalil Herbert attended Eagles rookie minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: Free agent RB Elijah Mitchell attended as well. Herbert appeared in three games with the Jets last year, rushing 16 times for 52 yards and earned three targets. Mitchell logged zero touches and earned one target, playing for the Patriots. The Eagles already have five running backs on the roster, so both players face uphill battles to snag a roster spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Patriots released RB Elijah Mitchell.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: It was almost a three-month stay on New England’s offseason roster. Seventh-rounder Jam Miller appears to have taken Mitchell’s spot on the depth chart, though Terrell Jennings is likely the third back in the pecking order behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Patriots signed RB Elijah Mitchell to a reserve-future contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: Mitchell played just one game with the Chiefs in 2025 before being released in December. He ended the season on the Patriots’ practice squad and the team has decided to bring him back for the offseason. Mitchell rushed for 963 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie with the 49ers but has struggled to find a role since. Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson headline the Pats’ backfield, but Mitchell will get a chance to compete for a depth role this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Patriots signed RB Elijah Mitchell to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: The signing doesn’t seem like great news for TreVeyon Henderson (concussion) in Week 17. Mitchell had been with the Chiefs all year and was cast aside for Dameon Pierce last week in what we’d call a “mercy” waiver. It’s possible he’ll be elevated for Week 17 if Henderson isn’t able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Chiefs signed RB Dameon Pierce to the active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: The team waived running back Elijah Mitchell in an associated move. Mitchell had been active in only once game this season, whereas Pierce can contribute to special teams on game day. The Chiefs enter “evaluation mode” for the first time in over a decade after being eliminated from postseason contention in Week 15.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Chiefs declared RG Trey Smith, TE Noah Gray, S Chris Roland-Wallace, RB Elijah Mitchell, WR Jalen Royals, OT Esa Pole and CB Kristian Fulton inactive for Week 13 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: Losing Smith for this one is unfortunate. The capable pass blocker will be missed against an ascending Cowboys pass-rush unit. Both Mitchell and Royals are healthy scratches. Gray was unable to practice this week, due to a concussion. This matchup should produce a high-scoring game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.headline: Chiefs declared CB Kristian Fulton, RB Isiah Pacheco, WR Jalen Royals, TE Jared Wiley, RB Elijah Mitchell, OT Josh Simmons, and OL CJ Hanson inactive for Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-mit.analysis: Even with Isiah Pacheco (knee) out, the Chiefs are not going to have Mitchell active, which means Clyde Edwards-Helaire has surpassed him on the depth chart. Simmons remains out due to unclear personal reasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) expressed confidence that he’ll be fine after the bye week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely was spotted limping at times during Week 7’s win over the Texans, which helps explain his subpar production. We’ll keep an eye on this one coming out of the bye, but we’re certainly not expecting anything serious here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: It was his first game with fewer than five targets all season. New York’s passing game simply targeted Houston outside the numbers and they ran the ball effectively enough that they didn’t need to feed Likely. He’ll be on the TE1 line in Week 9 against the Eagles once the Giants return from their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 6-of-11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely scored his fifth touchdown of the season and third over the last two games. He also caught a two point conversion, with all his scoring coming in the fourth quarter from J.J. McCarthy. The pass-heavy game script helped Likely salvage his fantasy day late in the game as he saw double-digit targets for the third straight game and fourth time this season. Now averaging 9.8 targets per game, Likely is squarely in the fantasy TE1 ranks heading into a tough Week 7 matchup against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 11-of-13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely set a new career-high with 11 receptions in this one, and came up with two clutch touchdowns in the process. His first score came on a three-yard strike from Jameis Winston on a third-and-goal play that the Giants needed to stay in the game, cutting the Commanders’ lead to 19-13. Then, in the fourth quarter and with the Giants facing a fourth-and-eight, Likely turned an eight-yard reception upfield for a 17-yard touchdown that nearly looked like a fumble and turnover at the goal-line. Likely has been targeted 25 times in his last two games and has now gone for 66 or more yards in three of five games to start the season. He’s starting to show good chemistry with Jameis Winston and will be on the TE1 radar in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: The Giants’ passing offense is tethered to Jameis Winston’s scattershot arm, but Likely has a favorable matchup against the Commanders’ defense this week. He can be started as a low-end TE1 in this divisional showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely is on track to face the Commanders’ fantasy-friendly defense in Week 5. Ideally, we will see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Giants’ starting tight end warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his workload and plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely evidently got a little banged up while handling a second-high 12 targets last week. His early-week participation puts him on track to face the Commanders in Week 5, but new injuries are worth keeping an eye on. He is a TE1 if active this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 7-of-12 targets for 66 yards in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely’s 12 targets were a new season high as fill-in QB Jameis Winston finally got a little something going through the air. That included two heinous interceptions, but we were beginning to wonder if Winston was ever going to complete another pass. That he did stabilizes Likely’s low-end TE1 value, though we have no doubt the giveaways will stick in the coaching staff’s mind. This is still an offense that is going to work to hide the quarterback and potentially start trade acquisition J.J. McCarthy at some point this fall. Those variables limit Likely’s upside even if the floor is now looking a little better heading into Week 5 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gregory-de.headline: Giants signed RB Gregory Desrosiers off the Chargers’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gregory-de.analysis: The first-year UDFA rushed for 166 yards on 23 carries in the preseason for the Chargers, adding one touchdown and one eight-yard reception. We’d be surprised if he got real run in this backfield but at least he has the bye week to acclimate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants GM Joe Schoen said the Giants will place Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Well that sorts out the Giants backfield for the short term. Devin Singletary will take over as the primary passing down back behind Cam Skattebo and should be a usable FLEX play going forward. Tracy will miss the next four weeks after going down with the hamstring injury in the second quarter of New York’s win over the Texans in Week 7. Schoen indicated this isn’t a season-ender for Tracy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) is questionable to return to New York’s Week 7 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tracy had six carries for 15 yards and a touchdown before leaving, adding a two-yard catch on his only target. He was spotted in pads on the sideline, stretching his legs, so it looks like there’s a non-zero chance he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cam Skattebo “is expected to resume his role as the team’s lead back” in Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Skattebo was benched for his fumbling issues last week. He did not touch the ball once, while Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy, and Devin Singletary all got a few opportunities. The team then cut Harris a few days after Sunday’s loss. After a week in the doghouse, Skattebo appears to be back as the team’s top runner, though we still expect a committee approach from John Harbaugh. Rapoport even said that it’s unclear who will draw the start, so we aren’t sold on Skattebo as a safe fantasy option this week. At best, he’s a high-risk RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants released Najee Harris.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: The move comes a couple days after Harris criticized the New York coaching staff for its handling of the backfield touch distribution. “It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays...if you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do,” Harris said after the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints. “I’ve never been through none of this before.” Harris had 31 rushes for 99 scoreless yards before getting the boot. With Harris gone, Cam Skattebo could get another chance to see increased playing time after being all but benched last week. Tyrone Tracy, who led the team in rushing attempts against New Orleans, could be the de facto lead back for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh, asked about the running back room, said carries are “earned” and told his players to “do something” in their opportunities and more will come.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tyrone Tracy appeared to do the most with his opportunities last week, scoring the game’s only two touchdowns. Najee Harris was bottled up and Cam Skattebo was soft benched while Devin Singletary led the team in snaps while they were in comeback mode for most of the second half. By the letter of what he’s offering here, Tracy is probably the player who should get the majority of the snaps against the Texans. In actuality, we have no idea what will happen here and this quote doesn’t really help us. “I don’t like (rotating backs) either,” Harbaugh said per The Athletic’s Dan Duggan after the game. “One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back. And none of those guys have done that yet.” We suspect we’ll be diving beat writer opinions ahead of Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Tyrone Tracy rushed six times for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints, adding two receptions for 27 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: With Cam Skattebo facing a soft benching due to fumbling issues, Tracy saw the second-most running back snaps in a pass-happy game script. He opened scoring with a 17-yard catch-and-run in the first quarter and followed it up with a five-yard rushing score in the fourth quarter. The Giants backfield remains murky after Skattebo saw zero touches and no Giants back rushed for over 20 yards. Tracy is worth rostering as a potential FLEX play for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Tyrone Tracy (knee) is not on New York’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tracy upgraded to a full practice session, but looks to have lost most of his backup work to Najee Harris at this point. Tracy does not need to be kept in shallow leagues, but at least he’s good to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: The Giants’ RB3 is seemingly on track to be active for Week 4 against the Cardinals. Unfortunately, Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. He did not practice yesterday either and should currently be considered questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: The Giants’ backup is not presently fantasy-relevant, and a knee injury certainly won’t improve his stock, though coach John Harbaugh said he is only “day-to-day.” Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was also sidelined, but he played through it last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Bears signed RB Zavier Scott to their active roster from the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: The Bears had run out of elevations with him, so had to sign him to the roster to have him active for Week 8. Scott has played 46 special teams snaps and 0 offensive snaps so far and does not need to be rostered for fantasy purposes. It’s hard to not read this as bad news about Kyle Monangai’s health in the short term, but we’re trying.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings waived Zavier Scott.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Scott signed his ERFA tender with Minnesota this offseason but was ultimately beaten out for the RB3 job by rookie Demond Claiborne. He is a candidate to sign with the Vikings practice squad after rosters settle. Claiborne is officially a name to know in deeper leagues, though he remains parked behind Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings re-signed exclusive rights free agent Zavier Scott to a one-year deal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Scott managed a 32/114 line on the ground, adding 14 catches for 98 yards and a score on 16 targets, as Minnesota’s third-string back last year. He’s currently in line for the No. 2 role behind Jordan Mason with Aaron Jones expected to be released or traded. Scott probably doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value right now, but his first year certainly showed he has something to offer in the passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings RB Jordan Mason (ankle) is not on the injury report for Week 18 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Mason is in line to start this week with RB Aaron Jones (hip) having been ruled out. The Packers have already locked up a playoff spot. The Vikings are simply trying to get a better read on QB J.J. McCarthy. Mason is on the RB3/FLEX radar this week. He will likely cede passing down snaps to No. 3 RB Zavier Scott.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings RB Jordan Mason (ankle) practiced fully on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: With RB Aaron Jones (hip) sidelined by a hip injury, Mason has a chance to start. Vikings No. 3 RB Zavier Scott would likely play in passing situations, if this is indeed, the case. Mason would be on the RB3/FLEX radar. The Vikings face the playoff-bound Packers in Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Aaron Jones (ankle) returned to the Vikings’ Week 16 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Jones left in the first quarter with an ankle issue and was listed as questionable. Jordan Mason also suffered an ankle injury and was taken to the locker room on a cart. Assuming he remains out, Jones and Zavier Scott will split the backfield for the remainder of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Aaron Jones (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 16 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Jordan Mason left for the locker room with an ankle injury of his own. That leaves Zavier Scott as the only active running back on the Vikings’ roster. Fullback C.J. Ham will likely see an uptick in snaps as well. Scott will get three quarters of workhorse duties if both Mason and Jones remain out today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Aaron Jones is believed to be day-to-day after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 13’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Jones “is likely to be considered day-to-day” with his injury. Jones exited in the third quarter of Sunday’s shutout loss to the Seahawks and didn’t return to the field. The phrasing in Schefter’s report suggests the Vikings are still waiting to get a final word on Jones’ injury, but it sounds like he avoided the worst. If he is day-to-day, Jones will have a chance to suit up in Week 14 when the Vikings face the Commanders this week, but if he’s unable to go, we can expect Jordan Mason to step into a lead role with Zavier Scott likely working in on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Zavier Scott had three rushes for 17 yards in the Vikings’ Week 13 loss against the Seahawks, adding one catch for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Scott could see an increased role in Week 14 if Aaron Jones misses time with the shoulder injury he sustained in the second half of the team’s loss against Seattle. Jones has a history of shoulder ailments and was quickly pulled from the game. Jordan Mason would likely take over as the Vikings’ lead back, but it could be Scott who takes on the pass-catching tole with Jones sidelined. Scott had a six-catch game in Week 3 with Jones out. He should be picked up in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings RB Aaron Jones (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: The Vikings activated Jones from injured reserve on Tuesday, allowing him to practice in a limited capacity twice in the lead up to the team’s Thursday Night Football game against the Chargers this week. One would assume that the team would prefer to let Jones ramp up in practice with a few full practice sessions before keeping him active on game day, but anything is possible. Check back on Thursday to find out if the Vikings’ starter will make his return. He would be a volatile RB2 candidate if active. Fellow Minnesota running back Zavier Scott is also questionable, though Scott won’t have much fantasy value in any scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Bengals placed Erick All (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, this is believed to be a third torn ACL. Obviously it’s not good news that All, who missed a season-and-a-half the last time he damaged his knee, is dealing with another long-term knee injury. He’s in the third year of a four-year rookie contract but his NFL future looks to be in doubt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Erick All (knee) wil not return in Week 7 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: All exited in the third quarter with a knee injury and walked off the field on his own. The third-year tight end has a history of bad knee injuries, so this one is a bit concerning. All was having a decent day against the Ravens and left the game with three receptions for 26 yards on three targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Tanner Hudson caught 3-of-3 targets for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: Hudson saw three targets on the day, catching a Joe Burrow touchdown pass towards the end of the first half. The Bengals used all of their tight ends against Miami; Hudson saw 19 snaps while Mike Gesicki saw 28 and Erick All and Drew Sample tied with 33 snaps. It was a run-heavy day for Cincy, but the four tight ends all combined for nine targets. All caught all three of his targets for 25 yards while Sample caught his only target for five yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Mike Gesicki was not targeted in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: The rollercoaster ride that is “tertiary target in a Tee Higgins/Ja’Marr Chase-centric offense.” Erick All (2/5 on three targets) lead Bengals tight ends in receptions. Drew Sample (36 of 60) led Bengals tight ends in snaps. Starting Gesicki will pay off at times, but this wasn’t one of them. He’s a TE2 in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Erick All was not targeted in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: Three Bengals tight ends caught at least one pass, but All somehow was not one of them. That will probably change going forward, but this is confirmation that it’s going to be a while if All is to develop back-end streamer relevance this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Bengals QB Joe Burrow said TE Erick All (knee) “looks fit, fast, explosive” and will “play a big role for us this year.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: Late in June, the Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. identified All as a key cog in the Bengals’ intended schematic switches this season. The team hopes to run more plays from under center while also increasing its play-action rate. It remains to be seen how much receiving involvement All will garner, but the team is very clearly excited about his blocking ability, both in-line and as a fullback. A pair of knee surgeries limited All’s availability through his two NFL seasons. If he can truly return to form, who’s to say he can’t be the Bengals’ long-term TE1? All recently told Dehner that getting hit by a three-wheeled truck in Greece this summer restored his confidence in his ability to take a hit. A modern-day odyssey.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. believes Bengals RB Chase Brown can benefit from the team’s potential playcalling changes in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: Dehner reports that the Bengals have rigorously practiced lining up under center in spring practices. He believes they will remain a shotgun-first team, but thinks they could improve on their 31st under-center ranking by more than 10 spots. Among the top-40 qualifiers from 2024-25, Brown averages 5.1 yards per carry (fourth) and a 12.3 percent explosive run play rate (third) on runs when QB Joe Burrow lines up under center. From shotgun formation, Brown averages 4.5 (24th) and 7.3 percent (22nd), respectively. Even a minimal increase in under-center snaps would benefit Brown. The Bengals believe TE Erick All’s (knee) return gives them the needed flexibility to do so. He is capable of motioning into the backfield as a fullback, and “setting the edge with vicious crack blocks and overall serving as a hammer in front of Brown in the run game.” Brown finished as the RB7 last year and is being drafted as the consensus RB10 in best ball. Beating that ADP seems plausible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Bengals TE Erick All (knee) is practicing, but said he isn’t “fully cleared yet.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: All missed the end of the 2024 season and the entire 2025 season with a pair of knee surgeries, one to clear out damage done from a surgery at Iowa, and another to repair a torn ACL. He enters the third year of his rookie contract as a deep, deep sleeper in fantasy leagues behind Mike Gesicki, but All did look pretty good in 2024 while healthy. He should at least give the Bengals some usable multi-TE set snaps if necessary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: Bengals placed TE Erick All on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: This was the expected outcome after All suffered from complications arising from a previous surgery in college. That left the second-year tight end looking at two offseason surgeries instead of one after suffering a torn ACL in Week 9 of his rookie year. Expect Mike Gesicki to serve as the primary pass-catching tight end for the Bengals in the coming season, a role that is likely to yield a handful of spike weeks considering the general lack of options behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reports Bengals TE Erick All Jr. (knee) is expected to miss the entire 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/erick-all/0000.analysis: Due to “complications” from a previous knee surgery in college, Dehner Jr. writes, the rookie tight end will now undergo two knee surgeries instead of just one. All being sidelined for the 2025 year will undoubtedly put more emphasis on the Bengals to re-sign Mike Gesicki and Tanner Hudson. Hopefully All will be able to return for the 2026 season after a decent 20/158/0 receiving line for the Bengals in two months before tearing his ACL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers general manager John Lynch said the team would continue starting Eddy Pineiro after the team’s Week 7 bye.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: Lynch in a Tuesday interview acknowledged Pineiro is “going through a rough patch” but committed to sticking with him for now. “We have a lot of belief in Eddie,” Lynch added. “He has had a tough run early this year, but we extended Eddie for his body of work with us but then throughout the history of his career.” Pineiro has missed three of his nine field goal tries on the season and four of his 25 extra point attempts. Pineiro, who made 96 percent of his field goal tries in 2025, will have at least a couple more games before the Niners brings in kicker competition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers K Eddy Pineiro (illness) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, the 49ers will sign a kicker to the practice squad as insurance, in case Pineiro cannot play. This is unfortunate. The 49ers’ starting kicker should bank a decent number of extra points, and ideally field goals, against the Dolphins this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers K Eddy Pineiro (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: NFL players generally play through illnesses. We expect Pineiro to be active on game day, though two absences are a bit concerning. Hopefully, he is back on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers K Eddy Pineiro (illness) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: Pineiro was a non-participant in practice due to an illness. It’s still early in the week, so the 31-year-old kicker will likely return in time for Week 2 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers signed K Eddy Pineiro to a four-year, $17 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: The deal includes $10 million in guaranteed money and ties Pineiro to San Francisco through the 2029 season. Kicking on a one-year deal in 2025, Pineiro converted all 22 attempts from inside 50 yards, also converting 6-of-7 attempts of 50 yards or more. His 96.6% conversion rate on 29 field goal attempts led the league, bringing stability to a position that long plagued the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers general manager John Lynch said the team is “not anticipating” using the franchise tag on K Eddy Pineiro.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: Pineiro had an efficient season for the 49ers, missing just one of his 29 regular season attempts. Lynch said, “we got a couple weeks before free agency to continue to work towards something.” Pineiro is a pending free agent and eligible for the franchise tag should the 49ers not reach a deal with the 30-year-old. Lynch indicated it is not likely the team will tag Pineiro and there is interest to reaching a new deal with the kicker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: Eddy Pineiro made both of his field-goal attempts in San Francisco’s Divisional Round loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: Pineiro missed just one of his 29 attempts on the season — 32 if you count the postseason — after the 49ers finally moved on from Jake Moody following Week 1. He now has hit 139-of-155 regular season attempts in six years in the league. It’s very funny that he was freely available to anyone before Week 2 and had a season this good. A 2026 free agent, the 49ers will probably prioritize re-signing him after this performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers released K Matt Gay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: Gay made four field goals and four extra points without missing a kick in two games for the 49ers. But starter Eddy Pinero is healthy enough to be active again, and so the 49ers will move on. Gay joins the workout kicker circuit again and figures to get a third opportunity at some point in the last month of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers declared K Eddy Pineiro, LB Tatum Bethune, DE Sam Okuayinonu, RB Jordan James, WR Jordan Watkins, OL Connor Colby, and DT Kevin Givens inactive for Week 13 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: Pineiro missed practice this week with a hamstring issue and will miss a second straight game. Matt Gay, who made both of his field goal tries and both extra point attempts in Week 12 against the Panthers, will kick for the Niners against the Browns. He’s not a great fantasy option considering the weather conditions expected in Cleveland on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.headline: 49ers K Eddy Pineiro (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eddy-pinei.analysis: Pineiro is still not back at practice after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 11. Matt Gay kicked in his stead in Week 12 and is likely to do so again for Week 13 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks acquired Quenton Nelson from the Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: With the Colts’ season all but over, the team could trade away a series of key player as they look toward a total tear down/rebuild scenario following the 2026 season. That includes Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler who now has a chance to compete for a title now that he’s out of Indianapolis. Nelson will join a Seattle offensive line that ranks 21st in pass blocking win rate and 27th in run blocking win rate. His addition should be a boon for Sam Darnold and the Seahawks’ pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he would “definitely love to be a Colt for life,” as he enters the final year of his contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Taylor, 27, has totaled more than 320 offensive touches in each of the last two seasons. His current $14 million annual salary makes him the seventh-highest-paid running back in the league. Taylor has set multiple Colts records, operating as the centerpiece of Indianapolis’ offense for years. FOX 59’s Mike Chappell writes that it is “uncertain whether there’s a mutual desire to keep Taylor in Indy beyond 2025.” Multiple Colts stars, including DTs DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, OG Quenton Nelson and WR Josh Downs, are also entering the final year of their deal. Chappell believes owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon “might believe it’s more prudent to allow the upcoming season to run its course rather than reinvest in lucrative contracts.” Time will tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson returned to Week 2 against the Broncos after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was the downfield blocker on a delayed Tyler Warren screen pass when he was hurt. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga went low on Nelson, which resulted in Nelson driving his quad-knee area into the diving Hufanga. Nelson immediately grabbed just above his knee as he went down. He then limped off the field under his own power and was seen talking to teammates with his helmet on, along the sideline. He returned on the following drive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (ankle) is questionable for Week 17 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was able to practice on Friday, though only in a limited capacity. He appears to be on the right side of questionable but will need to make it through pre-game warmups before being cleared. Tanor Bortolini would likely take his spot in the lineup if he is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts listed OG Quenton Nelson (ankle) as questionable for Week 18 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was a limited participant in back-to-back practices to close out the week and should have a chance to suit up in what’s arguably the Colts’ biggest game of the season. In addition to Nelson, the Colts also listed center Ryan Kelly (ankle), cornerback Kenny Moore (back), and running back Zack Moss (forearm) as questionable heading into the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson missed practice last Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to a full session on Friday. He played through a questionable tag on Sunday. He will likely get a similar practice regimen this week. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann missed practice with a concussion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (toe) is questionable for Week 3 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday but was upgraded to a full session today. He played through the toe issue last week and should do the same versus Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts OL Quenton Nelson missed practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was present at Colts practice but was barefoot and did not go through any drills. The starting guard was battling through a toe injury last week but was able to suit up against the Texans. With starting center Ryan Kelly also not practicing, the Colts could be down two starting offensive linemen against the Ravens in Week 3. With Anthony Richardson (concussion) also hurt, the Ravens defense could be in for a big game on Sunday if the Colts can’t get healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Kyler Murray is still “acclimating to the [Vikings’] progression-based passing game.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Minnesota’s offensive ineptitude has reached stunning levels in recent weeks, including last Sunday against the Colts, when Murray had 150 yards and a touchdown while completing 58 percent of his pass attempts. “We’ll continue to get better,” Murray said Sunday night. “I know we will. I know we keep saying that, but I felt like we moved the ball well (against the Colts). We’ve just got to put the ball in the end zone.” The Vikings, who rank 25th in pass rate over expected this season, have operated conservatively on offense while their defense dismantles opponents week in and week out. As Lewis pointed out, the 2026 Vikings are the first team in a century to win five straight games with five or fewer TDs over that span. Murray through Week 7 ranks 28th out of 40 qualifying QBs in EPA per pass attempt and 33rd in fantasy points per drop back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 14-of-24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ 16-10, Week 6 win over the Colts, adding five carries for 39 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: The story of the Vikings season has been a vaunted defense with a mediocre offense. That remained true in Week 7, with the Minnesota offense scoring just one touchdown on a Kyler Murray five-yard toss to T.J. Hockenson. Murray averaged 6.3 yards per attempt and struggled to connect with open receivers much of the day. He added 39 yards as a rusher, most of those coming on a 35-yard scamper prior to his passing touchdown. Murray came up limping after a second quarter play but did not miss any plays and finished the game. He threw an end zone interception in the second quarter, but the defender was ruled out of bounds. On the flip side, Murray nearly had Jauan Jennings for a long passing touchdown in the second quarter, but Jennings failed to haul it in. Murray is a high-variance fantasy quarterback due to his rushing upside, but his passing ability remains poor and caps his ceiling. He will be in the fantasy QB2 ranks for a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 24-of-30 passes for 229 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ 23-13, Week 5 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray was extremely active on the ground, addnig 51 yards on 10 rush attempts. His deep ball, on the other hand, remains a work in progress. His lone touchdown of the day came on a dime to Justin Jefferson on the back of the end zone. He was hesitant to even pull the trigger on deep shots at other times, even when his receiver was wide open. Murray is largely a game-manager right now, but that’s enough to win football games when the Minnesota defense is simply shutting down every opponent they face. Murray will be a mid-range QB2 when he returns to take on the Colts after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 27-of-37 passes for 247 yards in the Vikings’ 15-10, Week 4 win over the Dolphins, adding six rushes for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: The Dolphins’ pass rush made life tougher than expected for the Vikings’ signal caller. Murray managed to turn a few extended plays into successful scrambles, but he also took four sacks, at times simply holding the ball too long. As the game progressed, Murray locked in on T.J. Hockenson when the pass rush was closing in, linking up with him 13 times for 119 yards. The duo should have shared a late touchdown, but Hockenson smartly downed himself at the Dolphins’ five-yard line, so Murray could kneel out the clock from there. Murray will be a high-end QB2 against the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 15-of-29 attempts for 168 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs, adding two rushes for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: In his first action since sustaining a concussion in Week 1, Murray wasn’t asked to do much in this one. He was about four percent below his expected pass rate on the day with an average depth of target of 9.4 yards. Murray targeted Jordan Addison heavily after Justin Jefferson left the game with an ankle injury, connecting with Addison on a 41-yard score and narrowly missing the speedy downfield wideout for another touchdown. Murray took three sacks and avoided a handful of other sacks against a Tampa front seven missing key players. Murray likely won’t be a 12-team starting play in Week 4 against the Dolphins even if Jefferson suits up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: The 2-0 Vikings will hopefully get their first full look at Murray, who exited in Week 1 after just 11 snaps. Murray will face a Buccaneers defense that ranks 24th in points allowed through the first two weeks and has allowed the 11th-most passing yards and the 10th-highest net yards per pass attempt. Murray has a nice supporting cast to work with and brings plenty of rushing upside, but fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a mid-QB2 until we see how he functions in his first full game or two with the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Vikings declared QB Kyler Murray, WR, Jauan Jennings, CB Zemaiah Vaughn, S Jakobe Thomas, C Nick Samac, OT Caleb Tiernan and DL Elijah Williams inactive for Week 2 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning Murray is “on track” to return in Week 3 against the Bucs. Jennings, who is out for non-football reasons, has a less clear return timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kyler Murray (concussion) “is on track” to play in Week 3 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Schefter added that Murray is expected to clear concussion protocol next week. He was limited throughout practice this week before being ruled out on Friday. Murray made progress through the protocol during the week but couldn’t get the green light before the weekend. Carson Wentz will make one more start. Even with another strong showing, Wentz is all but certain to return to backup duties once Murray is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Vikings ruled out QB Kyler Murray (concussion) for Week 2 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Reports regarding Murray’s progress in the NFL’s concussion protocol were positive this week, but it looks like he needs another week to fully recover. The Vikings will instead roll QB Carson Wentz as the starter in what could be a high-scoring game against the Bears. He is a QB2 for the occasion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Vikings QB Kyler Murray (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray logs his second limited session of the week. He has a chance to play, but we simply will not know his status until the team announces that he has passed the NFL’s concussion protocol. If Vikings QB2 Carson Wentz gets the start against the Bears, he would be a worthwhile QB2 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-7 targets for 48 yards in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert has now returned consecutive games of middling production with Tanner McKee under center, which is a somewhat troubling realization considering DeVonta Smith missed both games and Dontayvion Wicks departed Week 6 with an injury before missing Week 7. Goedert’s fantasy value appears strictly tied to the state of a sinking Philadelphia ball club, now fighting through declining quarterback play in addition to poor offensive structure and shoddy play calling. Fantasy managers are likely forced to endure the middling production for lack of better options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play against the Cowboys in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert reportedly aggravated his previous knee injury but got back on the practice field for a full session Saturday before being removed from the injury report. He could be stepping into a massive target share with both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out. Fantasy managers can start him as an upside TE1 in a great matchup against the Cowboys in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys. The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that as of Thursday, there was “optimism” about Goedert’s Week 7 availability. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert missed time with a knee injury earlier this year, but he was not on the injury report last week. This could just be a maintenance day, but it is worth keeping an eye on in the lead up to the Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Early in the game, when Tanner McKee was struggling to get anything going, he seemed locked onto Goedert. When the Panthers were up by multiple scores and the defense seemed to allow some more space in the secondary, McKee felt more confident in taking shots down the field to his receivers, which meant Goedert was quiet in the second half. Still, he was second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards and will be a low-end TE1 against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert returned to the lineup after missing three games with a knee injury. Already without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, Goedert was immediately thrust into a high-usage role. He led the team in targets and catches, though much of his looks were simply check-downs. Even if that’s his role going forward, Goedert should catch enough passes to sustain borderline TE1 numbers until DeVonta Smith returns. He gets a date with the Panthers in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert got in a full session on Friday and is cleared. With DeVonta Smith down, he has some TE1 potential against the Jaguars on volume. He’s always been one of Jalen Hurts’ favorite red zone targets, and Saquon Barkley being down may lead the Eagles to throw more once the field condenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert’s return cannot come soon enough. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) remain sidelined, and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) got hurt in today’s practice. If Goedert can play this week, he will vault right back into the TE1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: It’s Goedert’s first practice since going down with a knee injury in Week 2. Even a limited session today puts him on track to suit up for Philly’s Week 5 game against the Jags. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) unlikely to play, Goedert could be in line for a large role right away. He will be on the TE1/2 border for Week 5 if he is cleared for action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and will again be replaced by the combination of Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt in Week 4. Neither of those players are particularly appealing options, though Ertz has enough of a history of success and the Eagles are bereft enough of targets to make him a viable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 7-of-8 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon showed out with the best game of his career in the absence of both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, operating as the top option through the air throughout the game against the Cowboys. He started his night off with a 21-yard reception on the team’s first possession before adding a fourth quarter touchdown on a quick slant from four yards out.
