The rookie wideout showed some real promise at times while Tampa dealt with wideout injuries, and could be in line for more targets in 2026 depending on what the Bucs do with their crowded wideout room. He likely won’t be a factor in the playoffs if the Buccaneers are able to clinch the division with a Saints win over the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson was not targeted in the Bucs’ Week 14 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: At least not officially. Johnson did draw a 28-yard DPI early in the third quarter. Fair enough, but today’s doughnut comes as Mike Evans is probably on the right side of questionable to return for Thursday’s game against the Falcons. Even if he doesn’t, rookie Johnson has proven to be a safe 12-team league drop with bye weeks over and the fantasy playoffs beginning in Week 15.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Bucs’ Week 13 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: With Bucky Irving finally back in action and Chris Godwin getting more involved, Johnson’s usage cratered. The only time he made a noticeable impact in the game was when his second quarter OPI penalty took a Rachaad White touchdown off the board. Johnson should continue to soak up snaps and run routes in this short-handed offense, at least until Mike Evans returns. It’s just not providing WR4 numbers in fantasy with the playoffs almost here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught 1-of-3 passes for six yards in a Week 11 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: He also rushed three times for zero yards. Johnson has been a nice story as a seventh-round rookie, but he has never topped 60 yards receiving in a game, so his fantasy value is excessively tied to touchdown value. That makes him really difficult to trust, especially next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports Bucky Irving (shoulder/foot) and Chris Godwin (fibula) are in “rehab mode.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: It’s not a great mode to be in as the Bucs head into their Week 11 matchup against the Bills. Stroud said he did not expected Godwin or Irving to practice Wednesday, and both players would seem unlikely to suit up against Buffalo. Look for Rachaad White and Sean Tucker to continue splitting the Bucs’ backfield workload against a weak Buffalo rush defense, and for Tez Johnson to operate as the team’s WR2 with Godwin sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker rushed seven times for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker’s 46-yard touchdown came with the Bucs already leading 36-6 early in the fourth quarter. He covered more ground on the score than he had rushed for all season heading into Week 7. Six of Tucker’s carries came in the fourth frame of a blowout. Although he has proven he will mix in for the occasional 1-2 yard vulture TD, Tucker is a distant third on the depth chart behind Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell, and is not much of a hold in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (quad) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker should be back after missing Week 6’s loss to the Steelers. He doesn’t offer much fantasy value of his own, but he does occasionally plunder goal-line work from Bucky Irving. Expect him to be a thorn in Irving’s side again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Bucs declared RB Sean Tucker, DL DeMonte Capehart, OG Luke Haggard, QB Baker Mayfield, CB Benjamin Morrison, G Billy Schrauth, and S Antoine Winfield Jr. inactive for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker has stolen the occasional goal line carry from Bucky Irving this year, though he only has eight attempts in total. His absence will move Irving up a spot or two in the RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sean Tucker (quad) is not expected to play in Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Despite seeing just eight total carries this year, Tucker has two attempts inside the five compared to one for Bucky Irving. Though he isn’t leaving that many total carries behind, Tucker’s absence will still create some extra fantasy value for Irving, who is on the RB1/2 border for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: FOX Sports’ Greg Auman reports that Sean Tucker (quad) will be a pregame decision for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker is officially listed as questionable. If he ends up being inactive, that is good news for Bucky Irving, who handled 23 touches last week, ceding seven to Kenny Gainwell and five to Tucker. Irving warrants borderline RB1/2 treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (quad) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker missed Wednesday’s session with a quad issue. He previously missed one game due to a hamstring injury. Tucker should be good to go for Week 6, though we don’t expect much fantasy production from the Bucs’ RB3. He has eight carries and zero catches over the past two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker rushed three times for 10 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Bucs OC Zac Robinson talked about getting Tucker the ball more earlier this week. Tucker entered this game with zero touches on offense. Though his role was limited, Robinson subbed him in where it counts the most and Tucker punched in a goal line score in the first half. He still doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value, but Tucker reclaiming the goal line role he had last year would be brutal for Bucky Irving’s fantasy outlook. Tucker is, at best, a touchdown-based RB5 for Week 5 versus Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said game flow and productivity have limited RB Kenny Gainwell’s usage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: The Buccaneers are 0-3, so if trailing game scripts aren’t the ideal setup for a receiving specialist, we aren’t sure what is. Robinson said he would like to get Gainwell more involved, but also added that Gainwell has to earn those reps by being more productive. Robinson said he also wants to get RB3 Sean Tucker more involved during the same presser. It sounds like this backfield still belongs to starting RB Bucky Irving, who is dealing with a glute injury, but changes are at least being considered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said he wants to get RB Sean Tucker going.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Robinson described Tucker as being “special with the ball in his hands,” and said that it’s on the coaching staff to find spots to mix him in. Whether this impacts starting RB Bucky Irving basically comes down to how and when — and if — the Buccaneers get Tucker involved. Taking a few snaps away from RB2 Kenneth Gainwell would be no big deal. Utilizing Tucker in the red zone would be consequential for Irving. Hopefully, Robinson provides more insight before his team’s Week 4 game against the Packers. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (hamstring) is active for Week 2 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker was out last week with the hamstring issue. His return to the Tampa lineup could take a few touches away from Bucky Irving and/or Kenneth Gainwell. Last week against the Bengals, Irving out-carried Gainwell 8-5 and led the backfield with a 59 percent route share. Bucs declared CB Jacob Parrish, CB Ayden Garnes, DL Elijah Simmons, DL DeMonta Capehart, OL Billy Schrauth, and OL Luke Haggard inactive for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 3-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Running a route on 23 of the team’s 34 drop backs, Helm was a little more involved than usual in the Titans’ low-octane passing attack. With fewer than 30 receiving yards in every game this season, Helm should not be rostered in any fantasy format for now. He’s been targeted on just 12 percent of his routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm failed to catch his only target in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: 45 snaps, one target. Helm has somehow grown less relevant than his 4/28 Week 1 showing would have even suggested. He can be dropped in most leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm continued to split reps with Daniel Bellinger, who also caught two passes today. Helm hasn’t topped 30 yards in a game this year and his four catches in Week 1 remain a high-water mark. He isn’t even in the TE2 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now sitting on a scoreless 6/41 through the Titans’ first two contests. Helm is an intriguing second-year pro, but there’s not going to be much intrigue in the Titans’ offense for the time being. 24-year-old Helm is best left on 12-team league waiver wires head of Week 3 vs. the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 4-of-5 targets for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm gobbled up snaps as he tied Carnell Tate for the second most Titans receptions on an afternoon where Cam Ward completed just 19 passes. Helm is looking heavily involved in the offense, it’s just unclear if that will even amount to anything in this situation. Week 2 is going to be tough against the Eagles before a slightly more forgiving Week 3 date with the Giants. For now, Helm is not a recommended TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) will not play in Tennessee’s Week 18 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm finishes a successful rookie season with a 44/357/2 slash line, and looked to be making a climb up Tennessee’s target pecking order before injuries largely derailed his final month. It’s hard to rely on anything in Tennessee’s offense until we see exactly what happens with the coaching staff, but there are offseason runouts that will put Helm as a high-end TE2 with Chig Oknokwo slated for free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now on the wrong side of questionable, which benefits TE Chig Okonkwo, who has scored a touchdown in consecutive weeks. Okonkwo is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the season and has a chance to earn a decent payday with another strong showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 17 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is good to go, which is nice for QB Cam Ward. The promising rookie tight end has made good on his fourth-round draft capital, though the Titans’ distributive offense makes him too dicey a start for Week 17. Helm is up to 52 targets on the year, while averaging 1.58 yards per route run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans have been distributing the ball across the skill position corps in recent weeks, and we see no reason for that to change in Week 17 against the Saints. Helm is a touchdown-dependent fantasy-starter in re-draft formats. His rookie season showings have been encouraging overall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-3 targets for nine yards in the Titans’ Week 16 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm’s missed connection was a fourth down grab where he couldn’t quite get both feet in bounds. It wasn’t the best awareness from the rookie tight end, but a rare notable mistake for a player who has been looking lively down the stretch, even if it’s not always reflected in the box score. Despite that intrigue, Helm will not be a top-24 option for the fantasy finals against the Saints. The Titans don’t generate enough pass attempts, and spread the ball around too much on the targets they do disperse.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor got off to a hot start on National Tight Ends Day by mossing Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr in the end zone. Not content with just one score, Taylor double-dipped with a leaping touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter. He also scored the two-point conversion after the play. Taylor is running well ahead of first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq right now and there’s no reason to expect anything different in Week 8 versus the Raiders. Taylor will be in the TE2 mix next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 4-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is now up to 7/57 in two games since returning from his thumb injury. First-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who missed most of Week 5 with a concussion, is 3/15 during the same timespan. This Jets tight end targets battle figures to oscillate back and forth, but Taylor is the preferred option for the time being. It’s still not resulting in more than desperation TE2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 2, Taylor caught the second most balls on the team as Kenyon Sadiq departed with a third quarter concussion. Those are awful developments for Sadiq managers, but almost certainly not enough to create TE2 value for Taylor, even if Sadiq misses Week 6 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Jets TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s return could be problematic for rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq posted a 7/105/1 receiving line two weeks ago before goose-egging last week. Taylor is not a serious receiving threat, but he can eat into Sadiq’s snap share. Sadiq likely remains a viable TE1, but his volatility just increased a tad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor was sidelined all of last week and, so far, all of this week with the thumb injury. He’d need to mount a major comeback on Friday to get on to the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor missed Week 3 with the thumb issue and is currently considered week-to-week. A DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4. Assuming he is out, Kenyon Sadiq, coming off a breakout performance versus the Lions, will be in line for a larger role once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) will not play in Week 3 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday morning that Taylor would miss Sunday’s game after being sidelined in practice throughout the week. It was reported on Tuesday that Taylor would be week-to-week with his injury, so it isn’t all to surprising to learn that he will be sidelined for this one. Taylor has -2 yards on two receptions this season and wouldn’t have been on the fantasy radar even if he was active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: He’s considered week-to-week and didn’t practice on either of the first two days of the week. Taylor will likely be ruled out on Friday, opening the door for Kenyon Sadiq to see a workload elevation against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 4-of-6 targets for seven yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: The check downs for Robinson will continue until morale improves. Running a pass routes on 27 of 34 Titans drop backs, Robinson was third in targets among Tennessee pass catchers and couldn’t make anything happen after the catch on each of his four grabs on the day. He now has two games of more than 50 receiving yards on the season with an average depth of target below six. Robinson should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 3-of-7 targets for 22 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: We suppose 3/22 isn’t an awful outcome on a day where the quarterback completed only 11 passes, but supposed targets hog Robinson is falling further and further behind No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate, who is suddenly stacking impressive box scores and highlight-reel plays. You would like for that to eventually add an extra element to this anemic offense — and perhaps more play volume — but until it does, Robinson is looking like little more than a last-gasp WR4 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 6-of-7 targets for 53 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Unbelievably, that’s the most efficient Robinson has looked all season. He remains ticketed as the undercard to Carnell Tate and should only be viewed as a FLEX option. A matchup against the Colts next weekend at least is a lot more interesting of a spot than one against Houston’s defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Robinson was bailed out of a disappointing fantasy day when he hauled in a three-yard touchdown pass from Cam Ward late in the fourth quarter. Robinson was heavily out-targeted by Carnell Tate in this one, but he and Tate continue to be the only fantasy-viable receivers in this Titans offense. Robinson could be in play as a desperation FLEX play in next week’s game agains the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 7-of-11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Robinson got in the end zone for the first time as a Titan on a quick out route late in the fourth quarter. He comfortably led the team in targets and catches, though Carnell Tate beat him by one yard. Robinson and Tate are the only game in town for receiving opportunities on this team, but Cam Ward’s struggles make it hard to trust either for fantasy purposes. Robinson is a FLEX consideration in deeper leagues for his Week 4 matchup with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught a nine-yard pass in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Robinson’s third quarter reception was his lone official target, though he had a second catch wiped out by penalty in the fourth frame. 25-year-old Robinson is highly paid to be a compiler over the middle of the field, but he’s somewhat predictably looking like a poor fit with Cam Ward’s scattershot skill-set. He did at least catch five balls in Week 1. He is now heading on the road for a “revenge game” with his former team the Giants in Week 3. He will be a low-end WR4 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: It’s a standard-issue Robinson statline for his Titans debut. Ominous, since this should have been an 8-9 reception Robinson outing with the Titans spending the entire game in comeback mode. Cam Ward and company simply could not sustain drives. In theory, Robinson could form a compelling inside-out duo with Carnell Tate, but Ward did not look like a player ready to break out on Sunday. Things could get worse before they get better with the Titans forced to take on the Eagles’ tough defense in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Titans WR Wan’Dale Robinson “is not believed” to have suffered a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: This is good to hear. New Titans OC Brian Daboll brought Robinson with him from the Giants to serve as a reliable go-to option for QB Cam Ward, particularly on third down. Robinson has a chance to lead the Titans in targets this season, though questions about the offense’s overall effectiveness could keep him stuck in FLEX spots, rather than the WR3 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Team reporter Jim Wyatt reports that Titans WR Wan’Dale Robinson is being evaluated for a concussion on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: FOX Sports’ Ben Arthur reported earlier that Bears DB Xavier Woods “laid out Wan’Dale Robinson over the middle of the field” during today’s joint practice, which “justifiably” prompted a response from the Titans’ sideline. Titans coach Robert Saleh called the hit “cheap.” The NFL reviews practice footage when available. We’ll see if anything comes of it. Losing Robinson for Week 1 would be consequential for QB Cam Ward, and would likely shift more work toward rookie WR Carnell Tate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: ESPN’s Turron Davenport reports that Titans OC Brian Daboll’s intent to improve on third down was a “key reason” for signing WR Wan’Dale Robinson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Davenport penned a lengthy piece detailing how OC Brian Daboll is focused on developing QB Cam Ward’s play on third down, in the red zone and in the two-minute drill. This is pretty straightforward. Those are all high-leverage situations, so harping on Ward’s performance there makes sense. Robinson played on all three drives in the Titans’ first preseason game while veteran Calvin Ridley was on the field for one. Rookie WR Carnell Tate was on the field for the first and third drives. A featured role on third downs could help Robinson return FLEX value — he’s certainly being paid like he is going to be featured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: That might not look like much, especially with Emeka Egbuka on the shelf, but it was actually a 45 percent target share in a game where the Bucs attempted just 11 passes in a 43-13 victory. Promising in theory, we suppose, though Godwin has not cracked 40 yards receiving since Week 2. He has not reached 50 all year. It feels like he will have to get more involved at some point, but then again, this team has a lot of young receiving talent. Godwin’s WR4 prospects are hanging on by a thread heading into Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s eight targets today go down as a season-high, but he failed to make much of his opportunities, per usual. The veteran wideout hasn’t hit 50 receiving yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. With Emeka Egbuka pulling away as the team’s WR1, there isn’t much volume headed Godwin’s way. With Jalon Daniels likely to make another start next week, Godwin is tumbling down the WR4 ranks ahead of Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three targets for 37 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Emeka Egbuka, Cade Otton, and Kenny Gainwell on a night backup quarterback Jalon Daniels attempted only 25 passes. Week 5 now marks the fourth game in five tries in which Godwin was held to four targets or fewer, leaving the veteran wide receiver completely unusable in a fantasy setting, for the time being. He can safely be stashed on benches ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 6-of-7 targets for 31 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels made his first career start and leaned on Godwin for some easy completions. Godwin led the team in catches and targets, though Cade Otton surprisingly led the way in yards with 37. Godwin set new season highs in targets and catches. The Bucs are operating an incredibly low-wattage offense without Baker Mayfield, but Godwin could continue to see enough work to return WR4 numbers in PPR leagues. He will put that to the test versus the Cowboys in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin was a full participant for two straight days after a Wednesday DNP. The insertion of Jalon Daniels makes him (well, makes every Buccaneers player) hard to trust for Week 4, but Godwin is probably still in the FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin should be expected to play in Week 4 against the Packers at this point, although he has mostly underperformed thus far. Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said earlier that Godwin Jr. “is a stud and will continue to do his thing. The ball will find him.” That might be harder than one imagines with an undrafted free agent rookie at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: It will likely go down as a limited session for the veteran wideout, but Godwin should be on track to play in Week 4. The bad news is that he will do so with UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels as his quarterback. Godwin was already off to a slow start, and things aren’t likely to improve with a backup quarterback under center. He is low-wattage FLEX play for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s history of lower-leg injuries makes this a little bit concerning. The veteran wide receiver is already set to catch passes from a backup quarterback. If active, he may be playing on an injured ankle. He can only be viewed as a boom-bust FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin had a long touchdown grab called back on a holding penalty in the second half — a deflating moment for the Bucs in their comeback attempt against the elite Minnesota defense. Godwin was third on the team in targets on a low-volume day for the Tampa offense. Godwin, who has ten receptions over three games this year, won’t have much fantasy appeal going forward if Baker Mayfield’s hand/thumb injury proves to be of the long-term variety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three of his targets for 46 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: The Bucs main slot receiver saw some early involvement but was invisible for most of the second half as the Bucs pushed the ball downfield. Godwin, who now has 86 yards on seven grabs through two games, is a WR4 option in a struggling Tampa offense. Until Baker Mayfield improves, Godwin should stay on benches in most fantasy formats, especially against the formidable Minnesota defense in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught his only target for six yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The first-round rookie was held to one catch for the second week in a row. He has four catches over his past four games. It wouldn’t be surprising for his role to expand as the season wears on, but there were no signs of that happening this week. He isn’t worth holding onto in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Although there was an injury-shortened appearance mixed in, Sadiq now has just three catches for 15 yards over his past three games. This, as Mason Taylor has caught nine balls for 57 yards over the past two weeks. Sadiq’s big-play ability is going to come back into play sooner rather than later, but he is unsurprisingly maxing out as a zero-floor TE2 in fantasy for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq left Week 5 with a concussion. He was upgraded to a full practice on Friday and seemingly cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. back for Week 6, there will likely be fewer targets to go around in a Jets offense that has regressed heavily over the past two weeks. Sadiq is a low-end TE2 for his date with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He did upgrade to a full practice and Aaron Glenn told reporters he expects Sadiq to play. Sadiq’s fantasy upside is well-known, but with Mason Taylor back and Omar Cooper Jr. also pushing to play, his target volume has shrunk quite a bit from some of the early-season scenarios we’ve seen. He’s likely a TE2 at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He has been limited twice and doesn’t look close to clearing concussion protocol. It’s become rarer for players to launch a Friday comeback to get off protocol, but it’s not unprecedented. Sadiq looks like he’s on the doubtful side of questionable heading into Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq suffered a concussion in the Jets’ Week 5 game against the Browns and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: To make matters worse, Sadiq suffered the injury in the process of losing a fumble. Targeted on a 3rd-and-9 near the goal line in the third quarter, Sadiq was short of the first down and got “Peanut punched” for the giveaway. With neither side getting anything going in rainy New Jersey conditions, Sadiq had just two receptions for three yards before going down, getting out-produced by a returning Mason Taylor in the process. Now highly questionable for Week 6 against the Patriots, Sadiq will not be on the streamer radar if given the go-ahead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Jets TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor’s return could be problematic for rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq posted a 7/105/1 receiving line two weeks ago before goose-egging last week. Taylor is not a serious receiving threat, but he can eat into Sadiq’s snap share. Sadiq likely remains a viable TE1, but his volatility just increased a tad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq did not catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: A week after breaking out with 105 yards on seven catches against Detroit, Sadiq came up empty. He ran a route on 12 of the Jets’ 20 drop backs on a miserably low volume day for the New York offense. Sadiq split routes with Jeremy Ruckert, a less-than-bullish sign for the rookie’s involvement in the Jets offense moving forward. Sadiq will have some streaming appeal in Week 5 against the Browns if Mason Taylor remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Isaiah Davis caught all three of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Davis only carried the ball one time. He got onto the field on the Jets’ final drive after Braelon Allen got shaken up. Geno Smith proceeded to pepper him with check-downs, one of which he took for 41 yards. Davis hasn’t been seeing the ball much with Breece Hall out. Now that Hall has a good chance to return next week, Davis can be dropped even in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Isaiah Davis rushed seven times for 16 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots, adding a 10-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: This was by far Davis’ biggest workload during Breece Hall’s (quad) ongoing absence, though Braelon Allen continued to dominate snaps and touches. Hall has to be getting close to a return, but even if he remains out for Week 7 against the Dolphins, Davis has not shown enough earn to merit second FLEX treatment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Isaiah Davis rushed two times for eight yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns, adding a nine-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Davis at least touched the ball after his Week 4 doughnut, but Pro Football Focus charted him as getting out-snapped 60-10 by fill-in No. 2 Braelon Allen. Decisive, to say the least. Even if Breece Hall (quad) is forced to miss his third straight game in Week 6, Davis hasn’t shown enough to warrant a 12-team league looksee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Braelon Allen rushed four times for 14 yards in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions, adding three catches for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Breece Hall suffered a thigh injury late in this game and did not return, leaving Allen as the lead back for the Jets’ final two drives. He touched the ball six times on the pair of drives. Fellow backup Isaiah Davis did not touch the ball once. His role would likely grow if Hall misses time, but Allen is the clear target in his backfield on waivers. Allen would push for an RB2 ranking if Hall is sidelined for Week 4 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports Jets RB Breece Hall (groin) said he is “good to go and can handle a full workload, if necessary.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: It’s unclear whether Hall added the “if necessary” bit or if Cimini did, but regardless, this is good to hear. Hall is practicing in full leading up to the Jets’ Week 1 game against the Titans and can be treated as an RB1. Jets RB3 Isaiah Davis (knee) is also practicing fully.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall suffered a strained groin in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Glenn said he doesn’t believe Hall’s injury “was a big deal,” but said the star RB will be evaluated. It sounds like Hall avoided anything too serious, but given the nature of these types of injuries, it wouldn’t be surprising if Hall was sidelined for at least a few days. With Hall and Isaiah Davis (knee) both sidelined, the Jets are relatively thin at RB at the moment. Braelon Allen will slide into RB1 duties until Hall can return, and remains an intriguing late-round pick as the handcuff for Hall in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt believes Isaiah Davis is the “early favorite” for the Jets’ backup running back job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Rosenblatt led his breakdown by noting that Davis and Braelon Allen will both get snaps, so there isn’t likely to be a clear winner behind Breece Hall. Allen missed most of the 2025 season with a knee injury. In his absence, the Jets leaned on Davis as a pass-catcher to give Hall the occasional breather. He was targeted 28 times and brought down 21 of them for 186 yards. Davis has also been effective between the tackles, averaging 5.6 yards per carry through two seasons compared to 3.7 for Allen. The Jets’ backup job could have some appeal in deeper fantasy leagues, but it sounds like fantasy managers will want to get more info from training camp before placing their bets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said he’s planning to use Breece Hall, Braelon Allen, and Isaiah Davis as a “three-headed monster” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Glenn reportedly wanted to use his backfield in a similar fashion last season before Allen went down in Week 4, according to an article published by ESPN. This would be potentially brutal news for fantasy managers eyeing Breece Hall in drafts, although it is worth pointing out that in the three complete games both Hall and Allen played together, Hall appeared on 59 percent of the team’s snaps while Allen played on 29 percent of snaps, and Davis just 15 percent. Hall also had 51 total opportunities over that span, while Allen and Davis combined for 22 opportunities. Time will tell if Glenn and offensive coordinator Frank Reich really do lean into this “three-headed monster” idea, but it’s hard to imagine Hall, who recently signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract, losing enough work to be forced out of the mix as a fringe RB1/RB2 given his three-down skillset. That said, both Allen and Davis could serve as viable late-round handcuffs for Hall should he ever miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Braelon Allen said he is up to 250 pounds and is the biggest, strongest, and fastest he has ever been.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Despite adding 15 pounds since entering the NFL, Allen said this is the lowest his body fat percentage has ever been. Allen missed most of the 2025 season with a knee injury that eventually required surgery. At this point, it sounds like his recovery is complete. Head coach Aaron Glenn talked up his potential in the passing game, though he said that he views Breece Hall, Allen, and Isaiah Davis as a “three-headed monster.” Allen could have some minor stand-alone value as a short-yardage back this year, but the presence of Davis will likely prevent him from making much of an impact on the redraft fantasy landscape.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Jets RB Breece Hall (knee) is questionable to play in Week 18 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: When asked if Hall will play, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said, “we’ll see.” Glenn has played coy with most start-sit decisions in the Jets’ 3-13 season. No reason to stop now. Hall logged just two limited sessions to close the week. He is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the season. Preserving his health for free agency could be the smart move. He may wish to put his stamp on the season with a strong showing, though. It would be difficult to project his playing time if he is active. Treat him as a volatile RB2 if he suits up. His backup, RB Isaiah Davis (concussion), has been ruled out, leaving Kene Nwangwu (quad) and Khalil Herbert behind Hall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller scored a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller’s second quarter touchdown came after he beat a linebacker on a post route. It was also one of just two targets in a game the Panthers went on to lose 43-13. Waller’s score was the only black and teal tally before garbage time. Nice, though Waller had previously not found the end zone since Week 2. He has 14 total catches through six games. The limited overall workload has made Waller difficult to trust as a TE2 because of his zero-point floor. He will have some big-play potential Thursday against teh Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller did not have a catch on two targets in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Initial reports have Waller playing on 36 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 21 of their 46 dropbacks. Tommy Tremble, the other tight end, ran a route on 14 dropbacks, so Waller is technically the primary option in the passing game of the two. However, Tremble scored two touchdowns this week. We don’t recommend chasing either guy in fantasy right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) is not on Carolina’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He upgraded to a full practice today. Waller will be a low-end TE2 with Jalen Coker (quad) playing in Week 6 against a Jalen Hurts-less Eagles outfit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He appears to be trending towards playing, though Waller is old enough that we probably shouldn’t count it as a sure thing that he’ll get off the questionable line. Waller would be a reasonable TE2 if he plays against the Eagles on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: The Panthers should have their veteran receiving tight end on the field when they take on the Eagles this week. Waller remains a viable TE1, albeit as a somewhat volatile producer. We expect him to be practicing in full by the end of the week, coming off a restful bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller saw minimal involvement as quarterback Bryce Young leaned into his top option through the air, feeding Tetairoa McMillan 16 targets on 41 pass attempts in the absence of both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. Fantasy managers that scooped Waller off of waivers following his two-touchdown game in Week 2 are surely left disappointed in the recent returns, making Waller a potential drop candidate as the Panthers head to their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 5-of-8 targets for 51 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: With Xavier Legette (knee) sidelined and Jalen Coker (quad) joining him, Panthers tight ends Waller, Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined for 11/128. It was Waller’s most prolific receiving day of the season even though he didn’t find the end zone. Waller is undoubtedly providing valuable real-life reps for the Cats, but with 10 total receptions through three contests, he is looking like too much of a role player to rise above TE2 streamer status heading into Week 4 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller saw as many targets as Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined. Unlike the other Carolina tight ends, Waller is still an explosive pass-catcher and a de facto wide receiver. When Bryce Young looked his way, it was for a big play. He made good on the minor role with his first two touchdowns as a Panther. Waller only has five targets through two weeks. He will make the occasional big play, but it’s hard to get him in fantasy lineups with such a limited role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller had a short touchdown grab called back on offensive pass interference while rotating snaps and routes with Tommy Tremble. Both Panthers tight ends ran 19 routes on the day and saw two targets from Bryce Young. Waller will continue as a touchdown-reliant TE2 option in Week 2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, WR John Metchie, QB Haynes King, S Zakee Wheatley, OT Albert Reese, OLB Patrick Jones II, and DT Cam Jackson inactive for Week 1 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Sanders, who worked through a lingering ankle injury this offseason, won’t suit up for the team’s season opener. That leaves Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble as the Panthers’ top two tight ends against Chicago. Waller will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 option who probably won’t run many routes in the run-first Carolina offense. Tremble should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was second on the team in targets while leading in receptions and yards against the Vikings. He saw just 30 snaps but operated as a quick release valve over the middle of the field for Daniel Jones against a blitz-happy Vikings defense. In an otherwise low-volume day, Allen had another game with a high share of the Colts’ receiving output. He will be in the WR3 ranks ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 8-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Each of Allen’s targets, receptions and receiving yards were new personal bests for his embryonic Colts career. Allen is doing what he’s supposed to be doing in Indy, but that’s not true for many of his teammates. Then again, we don’t really care in fantasy football, as Allen’s WR3 checks are clearing all the same. Allen’s short-area looks will be in high demand in Week 7 as Daniel Jones tries to survive the Vikings’ onslaught of blitzes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen did not play a full complement of snaps in his first week back from a groin injury. He played 32 of the team’s 71 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 47 dropbacks. That makes him leading the team with nine targets even more impressive. Of course, the Colts were forced to throw almost 50 times because the Steelers made it a priority to contain Jonathan Taylor. It’s highly unlikely Daniel Jones throws that much going forward, but Allen remains the top target in the offense. The issue is that most of his targets are in the short-yardage areas of the field, so he is more of a fringe-FLEX option unless you’re in a full PPR league. Next week against the Titans is a good matchup for the Colts, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) is active for Week 5 against the Steelers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen got in a full practice on Friday, so he seemed to be trending towards being active, but now we know for sure. With Jamel Dean out this week and Joey Porter Jr. now in Dallas, the Colts’ passing game gets a slight bump, which is good news for Daniel Jones, who really needs to get back on track. The Colts inactives are: LB Jaylon Carlies, WR Ashton Dulin, QB Riley Leonard, WR Darius Slayton, and G Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Keenan Allen (groin) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen missed Week 4 with the groin issue but returned to practice this week and even managed a full session on Friday. The team still listed him as questionable, though he appeared to be on the right side of that designation heading into the weekend. Allen will be a low-ceiling WR4 for his date with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) is questionable for Indianapolis’ Week 5 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: He did upgrade to a full practice today so he’s at least likely on the optimistic side of questionable. Still, we were hoping he’d be cleared off the line entirely today, so it does give us a little hesitation that he could practice all three times this week, including one full, and still be questionable. The Colts don’t really have much else behind him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Two straight practices, albeit limited ones, should put Allen on the right side of questionable on Friday barring something new popping up. Allen will be an unexciting FLEX play against the Steelers in Week 5 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen suffered a groin injury in practice last week and was unable to play in Week 4 against the Commanders. His early-week return puts him on track to play in Week 5 against the Steelers, but he can likely only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Colts WR Keenan Allen (groin) is out for Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable. Now he’s been ruled out for Week 4 against the Commanders. Josh Downs is locked in as the Colts top wide receiver this week and Tyler Warren should also see a boost in value with Allen sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) is questionable for Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: This one went under the radar. Allen was limited on Wednesday with a “rest” designation. He remained limited on Thursday, but the Colts tacked a groin injury next to his name while maintaining the “rest” designation and hope for a Week 4 appearance along the way. Allen was downgraded on Friday, unable to practice, and should be considered truly questionable to face the Commanders this week. Were he to sit, No. 1 wide receiver Josh Downs would get a helpful target share boost.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 23-of-30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Jets’ 28-25, Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith posted another impressive box score and was almost perfect in this game, but his few mistakes were extremely impactful. The first was a red zone interception where Dolphins safety Michael Taaffe simply read Smith like a book and jumped the throw for an easy interception. The second catastrophic blunder was a 12-yard sack at the goal line that forced the Jets to settle for a field goal. Smith simply stared down Chop Robinson as the EDGE rusher ran straight at him for an easy sack. Smith isn’t at risk of losing his job anytime soon, but he needs to get back on track against the Raiders next week before taking on the Chiefs and Bills in the following weeks. Smith will be a mid-range QB2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 20-of-30 passes 252 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Jets’ 26-19, Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith was missing Adonai Mitchell for the fourth consecutive contest, but he found returning rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. for a sizzling 6/103/1 on seven targets. That was a necessary development with Garrett Wilson being limited to 4/44 as he was hounded by Christian Gonzalez. The 252 yards were Smith’s second most of the season, though his first interception of 2026 was a dreadful, costly mistake in the fourth quarter. He threw it in Keyon Sadiq’s direction, but Charles Woods ran the rookie tight end’s route for him. Disappointing, though we now have six games of evidence that Smith isn’t the bottom-three QB he appeared to be amidst the Raiders’ 2025 fiasco. Things could also get better if Mitchell soon returns and forms a legit trio with Wilson and Cooper. Smith won’t rise above mid-range QB2 status even for premium matchups, but he does have a primo Week 7 spot in the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 17-of-30 passes for 182 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ 17-12, Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith “added” five carries for seven yards. He also lost a fumble. Coming off a generationally bad Week 4 clunker against the Bears, Smith was hardly outstanding in rainy MetLife Stadium conditions, though he was superior to Deshaun Watson. Not that you would have noticed in real time. Smith fumbled “just” once compared to Watson’s four, also taking “only” four sacks to Watson’s staggering eight. Like Watson, Smith also lost a key pass catcher to a concussion, with Kenyon Sadiq going down in the third quarter. Both before and after Sadiq’s injury, the Jets mostly rode the run, with Braelon Allen turning his 24 carries into a strong 116 yards. Smith has predictably faded a bit after his relatively “hot start,” while he now has a tough Week 6 road test in the reviving Patriots. Smith’s decent weapons — which will hopefully include Adonai Mitchell next week — keep him in the QB2 mix, but only as a low-end option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 8-of-15 attempts for 119 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The Jets had the ball for a mere 17 minutes, as the Tyson Bagent-led Chicago offense dominated time of possession from start to finish. Smith, who had a combined 58 pass attempts over his past two outings, struggled against consistent pressure from the Bears front seven. His only highlight of the day came on a 58-yard touchdown strikes to Isaiah Williams in the fourth quarter. Smith should be a superflex option next week against the Browns. The return of Adonai Mitchell (finger) would boost Smith’s ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 31-of-37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the Jets’ 31-24, Week 3 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith also ran for 12 yards and completed one of his two two-point conversion attempts. The sacks, of which he took five, were an issue, but it was an otherwise flawless game from the veteran passer. He got particularly hot in the second half, getting points on the board in three of his four drives after the break. Smith was unfortunately sacked and lost the football on the final drive of the game, giving Detroit the win. The Jets don’t look like a team that is going to win many games this year, but it’s not because of Geno. Smith will be a viable Superflex option when he takes on the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 27-of-41 passes for 247 yards and a touchdown in New York’s 20-17, Week 2 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The Jets weren’t able to make many big plays in this one. Geno’s longest completion was a 43-yard connection to Breece Hall that Hall caught three yards beyond the line of scrimmage. There was not another pass completion longer than 17 yards on the day. That being said, Geno didn’t make many bad decisions and took what the Packers’ defense was giving him. The offensive line provided no push in the running game, so the Jets may need to let Geno play more aggressively if they’re going to put up more points. That could start in Week 3 against a Lions team that figures to score a lot of points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 19-of-24 passes for 215 yards in the Jets’ 23-10, Week 1 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith “added” six rushes for seven yards. Although it was not a productive day in fantasy football, it was a highly encouraging one in “real life.” At least for one game, the Jets’ blocking was 10x better than what Smith experienced in Las Vegas last season, and he took advantage by taking zero sacks and hitting several down-field passes to his talented skill corps. Three different receivers generated gains of 30-plus yards, but Omar Cooper Jr.'s was more of a catch-and-run. Unfortunately, the rookie injured his ankle in the process. Smith is going to be a “highs and lows” quarterback in even the best of years, but there is now reason to believe 2026 will not be all lows like 2025 was with the Raiders. The Packers will be a tougher opponent for the Jets’ home opener in week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Cade Klubnik will be the team’s QB2 to start the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: What this means is that Geno Smith has plenty of job security. Klubnik in the preseason completed 21 of 34, passes for 190 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception while taking four sacks. Klubnik would be a marked downgrade from Smith if the veteran misses time in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he’s been “so impressed” with Geno Smith’s play.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Reich has reportedly added wrinkles to the offense he deployed as head coach of the Colts and Panthers. At both of those stops his offenses were near the bottom of the league in most basic offensive metrics. Smith, meanwhile, has looked sharp as the team’s starting quarterback throughout training camp and in limited preseason snaps. He’ll look to bounce back from a nightmarish statistical 2025 season in Vegas. Jets players, including Garrett Wilson, told The Athletic that they have enjoyed the “player empowerment” that comes along with Reich’s coaching style and his offensive scheming, which leaves room for improvisation. The Jets offense could be functional as long as Smith, 35, is healthy and upright.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports Geno Smith (foot soreness) will start Friday’s preseason game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith will undoubtedly only play a series or two, but it’s confirmation he’s over the “soreness” that held him out last weekend. Smith would have reportedly played through the “injury” during the regular season, so it was never believed to be serious. Any injury is worth noting for a 35-year-old player coming off a rough, rough year, but this one is in the rear-view mirror.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed 11 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding one reception for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: With Jonathan Taylor trade possibilities swirling, McGowan quietly saw an increase in usage against the Vikings. He turned 12 touches into 48 yards, seeing 20 offensive snaps to Taylor’s 41. Though Taylor is still the definitive RB1, it is notable that the rookie 25-year-old is getting more opportunities, including a couple red zone snaps. McGowan has not quite achieved standalone fantasy value but should be added as a bench stash. He would be the Colts’ RB1 should Taylor be traded later this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that several teams are interested in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis:
According to Holder, multiple teams would be open to trading for Taylor, but it remains unclear whether the Colts are ready to be sellers before the trade deadline. Colts GM Chris Ballard was recently fired, and “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming” after the eventual hiring of a new general manager.
Seth McGowan
should be stashed on benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed six times for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan got a whole drive to himself early in the second quarter. Three of his carries and one of his two targets came on this drive. He was otherwise tasked with normal backup duties. McGowan is the only backup of note on the team, but he doesn’t have a standalone fantasy role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed four times for 14 yards in Indianapolis’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: It was McGowan’s first real taste of snaps with Jonathan Taylor, as he had 11 to Taylor’s 60 while the Colts were trying to grind clock with a lead against a hapless Texans offense. We doubt there’s much to this extra usage, it was likely just Taylor managing something minor on the sideline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts RB DJ Giddens (knee) was added to the injury report and did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: He did not play behind Seth McGowan in Week 1 and neither of them have fantasy value while Jonathan Taylor is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd left DJ Giddens off his 53-man roster projection.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: It’s been hard to find a good word from a beat on Giddens this offseason, so this isn’t an overly surprising conclusion to see listed out. He’s been sidelined for most of camp with a hamstring injury. The Colts look like they’ll keep Seth McGowan as their main backup to Jonathan Taylor. In this projection, Giddens loses the third running back spot to Ulysses Bentley IV.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Seth McGowan has “flashed” in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Describing his style as “decisive and violent,” Boyd believes McGowan is “building his case” to overtake DJ Giddens for the No. 2 role on the Colts depth chart behind Jonathan Taylor. Neither player will have a major role as long as Taylor is healthy, but it wouldn’t be stunning if McGowan won this battle in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports DJ Giddens “didn’t develop as quickly as the Colts hoped during his rookie season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Giddens was supposed to provide some relief to Jonathan Taylor last year, but “that plan was mostly shelved” as the Colts apparently didn’t love what they saw. Giddens and sixth-rounder Seth McGowan figure to battle for the main backup job behind Taylor, but neither is a priority backup to target late in drafts as they’d likely form a committee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes DJ Giddens and Seth McGowan are “poised to compete for the backup role” on the Colts running back depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: With Tyler Goodson gone, Giddens is the incumbent and has the higher draft capital, so we’re surprised to see a beat writer giving some leeway to the idea that McGowan could be the backup right away. Neither player figures to play much without a Jonathan Taylor injury, but they could be interesting contingency holds in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts selected Kentucky RB Seth McGowan with the No. 237 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan was a four-star recruit coming out of high school. He saw work as a backup for Oklahoma in 2020. After his freshman season, McGowan was arrested on charges of robbery, conspiracy to commit robbery, and assault and battery with a dangerous weapon. He eventually pleaded guilty to a felony charge of larceny of a person at nighttime. McGowan was kicked off the team and ultimately spent three months in jail, followed by a year-long probation. He returned to football at the JUCO level for two seasons before landing on New Mexico State’s roster in 2024, where he ran for 823 yards and three scores. McGowan then transferred to Kentucky and posted a 165-725-12 rushing line. He punctuated his draft profile with a 4.49 40 and strong burst measurables at 6’/223. McGowan is a decisive runner who shows great anticipation when choosing his lanes. On the other hand, he is an average receiver who needs to improve in pass-pro, even if a third-round role isn’t in his future. Fumbles were also an issue, as he coughed the ball up six times across his three seasons of limited FBS action. McGowan ultimately looks like a developmental backup for an NFL team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He did draw a defensive pass interference and a defensive holding, so at least he helped in points per penalty leagues. The Giants had defenders draped all over Collins for the majority of the game, and he was punished when he did catch the ball. It was Collins’ worst box score return since his rookie season, and one of only four games in his career where he was targeted and did not return at least 13 yards. The Texans wideout situation is complicated, but we’d still bet on Collins returning from the bye as a low-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 76 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He added a long defensive pass interference penalty drawn on Travis Hunter to set up Houston’s second third-quarter touchdown. Collins also took an end around in the red zone for five rushing yards. Close, but ultimately not the line that fantasy managers were hoping for. Collins will remain in the low-end WR1 region against the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He went for 3/45 in the first half and was mostly managed down with the Texans not really threatened in a major way after he sealed a block for their first touchdown in the third quarter. Collins took a hard fall after a leaping grab and did look a little worse for the wear on the sideline. We wouldn’t be surprised if he saw injury report time this week. That said, he looked good and the Texans simply didn’t need to throw the ball much late in this one. It’s back to the low-end WR1 line next week against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 7-of-8 targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He immediately busted out of the gates with a 45-yarder, caught a touchdown to end that drive, then found the end zone a second time in the second half when he worked to the other side of zone coverage and C.J. Stroud was able to find him on an improvised throw. Pretty good player. Collins handled 36-of-53 snaps, highest on the team. He’ll be a low-end WR1 against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He got in a full session and will escape the line. Collins doesn’t play the same amount of snaps that most of the league’s top wideouts play anyway, so even if he is managed a bit, he can be trusted as a low-end WR1 in what looks to be a smash spot against a bad Cowboys pass defense, though one that is integrating new trade acquisition Joey Porter Jr. against Collins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: We’re still waiting for the final injury report to drop, but Collins appears set to return in Week 4 after missing the last two games with a hamstring injury. Collins was listed as limited in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices and has been trending in the right direction all week. We’ll check back in when the Texans officially confirm Collins’ status ahead of the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander reports that Nico Collins (hamstring) was “optimistic” about playing in Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Alexander caught up with Collins after the Texans’ star player logged his second consecutive limited practice. Collins should probably still be treated as sitting somewhere in the questionable-to-probable range, but this is great to hear. Collins is a WR1, as usual, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Another limited session keeps Collins in the questionable column as he attempts to return from a multi-week hamstring strain. The Texans would surely like to have their star wide receiver back for what could be a back-and-forth game environment against the Cowboys this week, but balancing short-term and long-term needs is critical. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported over the weekend that Collins had a “decent chance” to return in Week 4. Even a limited practice today is a big step in the right direction. The winless Texans desperately need a playmaker on offense and Collins is their only option. While he could be on a pitch count in his first game back, Collins has to be in fantasy lineups the moment he is cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is a “decent chance” Nico Collins (hamstring) returns for Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Collins injured his hamstring in practice last week and has already been ruled out for the second game in a row. He did not practice this week, so the Texans’ first injury report of Week 4 will be telling. Dalton Schultz will continue to vacuum up targets in the meantime. He saw 14 targets last week and caught 12 of them for 140 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: To add insult to injury, Mitchell had a two-point conversion catch called back because of a penalty. Omar Cooper Jr. once again stole the show, reeling in several long catches en route to his second 100-yard game in a row. Playing in his first game in over a month, Mitchell did not appear awfully involved in the team’s game plan. The hope will be that he earns more opportunities next week, but Cooper Jr. may have already cemented himself as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Mitchell will be stuck in the WR5 ranks when he takes on the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It is too early to say whether Mitchell and his surgically repaired finger will be ready to face the Dolphins this week. He is a worthwhile bench stash, though. Mitchell played well early in the year, pre-injury and pre-breakout from rookie Omar Cooper. It is unclear whether Mitchell will return to the No. 2 wide receiver role or if he will be asked to unseat the youngster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has missed the past four weeks with a finger injury that required a “small procedure” to fix. Though a limited practice today doesn’t guarantee he will be back for Week 7, it’s a big step in the right direction. Mitchell had nine catches for 123 yards in his first two appearances this year. If he’s able to return this week, he would at least earn a spot on the WR3/4 border versus the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It was reported earlier this week that Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on the finger he injured in practice ahead of Week 3. Given that news, it doesn’t come as much of a surprise to learn that Mitchell will miss his fourth straight game with the injury. With rookie Omar Cooper Jr. set to play in his first game since Week 1, Mitchell could face additional competition for targets when he finally returns to the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on his hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: As expected, he did not practice today. Per Glenn, Mitchell remains week to week. This explains the lengthy absence for Mitchell, who hasn’t played since injuring his finger in practice ahead of Week 3. According to Glenn, Mitchell is moving his fingers around well, which is hopefully a sign that he will be back soon. With Omar Cooper Jr.'s practice window now open, Mitchell could return to a rather crowded receiver room once he is healthy.
