https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss his third straight game with the finger injury he sustained in practice, ahead of Week 3’s game against the Lions. During Mitchell’s absence, Isaiah Williams has run 59 routes, the second-most of any Jets receiver, but has seen just five targets. Garrett Wilson is the only reliable receiver in this passing game, while rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq is a boom-or-bust option against a defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to tight ends this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) remains week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will likely miss his third straight game with the finger issue. He suffered the injury just as he was coming on as the team’s clear No. 2 wideout behind Garrett Wilson. With Mitchell sidelined last week against the Bears, Isaiah Williams was second on the team in pass routes, saw three targets, and caught a 58-yard touchdown from Geno Smith. Williams will have some deep-league viability in Week 5 against a Browns defense allowing the most air yards in the NFL. Adonai was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets declared WR Adonai Mitchell, RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LB Kiko Mauigoa, DE Kingsley Enagbare, OL Dylan Parham, and TE Mason Taylor inactive for Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss another game with his finger injury and Hall will be sidelined with a quad injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Garrett Wilson, with Mitchell out, should continue dominating air yards and targets in the balanced Jets offense. Braelon Allen will take over as New York’s lead back for now and should be in all fantasy lineups against a suspect Chicago run defense. Kenyon Sadiq has some streaming appeal with Mitchell out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell was a DNP in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices, so the team’s decision to rule him out on Friday doesn’t come as a surprise. Mitchell will now aim to return in Week 5 against the Browns. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, who saw a season-high eight targets last week in Mitchell’s absence, will be on the fantasy radar as a fringe TE1 with Mitchell again sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison caught 1-of-4 targets for six yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison had to come back to the ball in the end zone, one that was placed to his back shoulder by C.J. Stroud to fit it around a zone defender. That was the good. Harrison also added an egregious drop while playing just 13 snaps. Your guess is as good as ours about fantasy value here as we sort through the names. Harrison doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered through his Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 34 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It tied his season-high for receptions in four games with Arizona. Harrison played just 12 snaps. The Texans do seem dedicated to giving him the ball — as you’d hope after he was acquired for a second-round pick — and we imagine he’ll be in the FLEX conversation next week against the Giants after a full week to hone trust with the coaching staff. His first two catches were on in-breaking routes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Marvin Harrison Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It’s a slightly short turnaround for MHJ, who was traded to the Texans on Sunday, and a weird travel schedule with Houston flying to London to take on the Jags. On the other hand, a week is still more than enough time to get Harrison Jr. installed at least as a part-time player. He isn’t much of a fantasy option this week, but a week or two of practice reps could get him in the FLEX mix if Houston proves to be a better fit for the former No. 4 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans acquired WR Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison, 24, gets a fresh start partway through his third NFL season. The former first-round pick has averaged just 47.8 receiving yards per game in 33 career games. Adjusting to a new scheme on the fly could be challenging, and Harrison has not proven himself to be a reliable fantasy contributor. It could be tough sledding for fantasy managers, but if Harrison quickly adjusts to his new team, he has a clear runway to No. 2 wide receiver duties next to Nico Collins. He should be rostered in 12-team leagues. The Cardinals are also sending a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals declared Marvin Harrison Jr., QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas, Andrew Wingard and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 5 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Life continues to be rough for fantasy managers rostering Harrison. The soon-to-be ex-Cardinal will not participate in what should be a fantasy-friendly game against the porous Lions defense. Bummer. Still no definitive word on where he will end up next week. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne benefit from his absence. The Cardinals will be without Wingard, one of two starting safeties, but will have DT Walter Nolen (calf) available to them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr., reports ESPN’s Adam Schefter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: The Cardinals informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday’s game against the Lions as the details of the trade are finalized, according to Schefter. While it’s unclear where Harrison is headed, Schefter mentions the Houston Texans as one team known to have interest. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported this morning that the Cardinals could be seeking a second-round pick and a mid-round pick in return. Harrison has just five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown in four games this year. According to Schefter, no Harrison trade will be completed until after Sunday’s games. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals would want a second-round pick and more to consider trading WR Marvin Harrison Jr., reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Pelissero says the Cardinals would want a second-pick and perhaps a mid-round pick in exchange for Harrison. The 24-year-old receiver was drafted fourth overall two years ago, but under new coach Matt LaFluer he has 85 yards in four games this year. Pelissero points to Harrison’s decision to hire an agent last month as evidence he could be preparing for a trade. While Harrison has obviously been a disappointment in fantasy this year, he should find his way into some starting lineups against the Lions secondary in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught a 12-yard touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison capped the Cardinals’ opening drive with a beautiful 12-yard end zone grab against Deonte Banks’ 1-on-1 coverage. It was the best possible start to the beleaguered wideout’s day. It would also prove to be a false start, as he caught zero other passes on three scattered targets. Admittedly, that does not include a late DPI that set the Cardinals up at the Giants’ four-yard line as they desperately sought a potential game-winning touchdown. Good, but nowhere close to enough for all involved. MHJ has now been out-targeted 30-9 by Michael Wilson over the past two weeks. That is to say nothing of Trey McBride. The Lions are a plus Week 5 matchup, but Harrison Jr. remains more waiver wire fodder than potential upside FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports teams are “doing their due diligence” on Marvin Harrison Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Schefter noted that the Cardinals aren’t “enthralled” with the idea of trading Harrison Jr. He also said point-blank that “it would not be a surprise” for MHJ to be traded. As much as the Cardinals may not want to admit it, this experiment needs to come to an end. The team has Michael Wilson and Trey McBride locked up on long-term contracts and MHJ has done nothing this year. He has four catches for 73 scoreless yards this year. At this point, it’s likely in the best interest of both sides for Harrison Jr. to find a new home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison finished the day with a modest 3/40 receiving line, though that represents a small share of the Cardinals’ offensive output on the day. His first target was a declined offensive pass interference on third down and his first reception came in the second quarter. Harrison did make a clutch catch on third-and-long in the fourth quarter but he ultimately saw just five targets on a day where Jacoby Brissett threw 52 passes. Michael Wilson looks like Brissett’s preferred wide receiver while the deep looks Harrison can excel at are not easily obtainable in this iteration of the Cardinals offense. Harrison is a low-end fantasy WR4 at best against the Giants next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants, adding two carries for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: One of the carries came on Houston’s last goal-to-go sequence of the game, where they wound up setting up what looked like a Hutchinson pass only to see him tuck the ball and run. We got nothing. With Tank Dell back and Marvin Harrison Jr. looking for work as well, it would seem that Hutchinson’s days as a FLEX option are over. But we would have said that before this game as well, and Hutchinson wound up with more wideout snaps than anyone but Nico Collins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He led the team in receiving and didn’t have any contested drops today, so that’s a step up from where he’s been most of the year. Still, he played just 27-of-65 snaps. Kayshon Boutte (39-of-65) would be our main target as Houston’s third receiver if we thought the offense was good enough to warrant that kind of respect; they aren’t.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He managed to get his finger underneath a sideline ball for a 21-yarder, and the replay booth upheld the ruling of catch on the field. He also managed fewer targets than Xavier Hutchinson (five), as well as 10 fewer yards, despite Hutchinson playing 16 snaps to Boutte’s 32. The Nick Caley WR platoon will continue until morale improves, making nobody much of a FLEX play against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 51 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Hutchinson left the game after catching a 28-yarder in the fourth quarter and visited the blue medical tent. The Texans never announced a status for him, so it’s something to monitor. He lead the team in targets and yards. We guess that’s just where things are for the Texans now. If Hutchinson is healthy and Nico Collins is not in Week 4, he’ll have fringe FLEX/WR4 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-9 targets for 37 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Through two games, Hutchinson has 15 targets and 69 yards. If you’re going to be this bad, you at least want the meme number. Hutchinson let a (admittedly hard to reel in) C.J. Stroud ball hit him in the hands in the end zone before dropping it and repeatedly struggled to finish contested catches, as he did in Week 1. Hutchinson is a fine depth receiver who has been pushed into a role he simply can’t do at the NFL level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would not be surprised” if Texans WR Jaylin Noel is more involved in Week 2 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Rapoport adds that Noel is “really talented.” We agree, but the Texans have consistently played WR Xavier Hutchinson ahead of him. Noel, 24, is an explosive player, and the Texans will be looking for playmakers to contribute with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined this week. Noel is officially on the boom-bust FLEX radar in Week 2 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 32 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He let two of the other three non-catches glance off his hands. Marie Kondo loves mess, so she’d love this Texans WR2 situation. Hutchinson led the four non-Collins receivers with 44 snaps. This should not be confused with him being a desirable fantasy football play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson caught1-of-2 targets for minus-one yard in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Hutchinson also failed to execute his blocking assignment on a run play that resulted in no gain for RB Woody Marks. Playing only with the first-team offense, Hutchinson nearly hauled in a tough sideline catch that would have picked up a first down, but the pass glanced off his fingertips. It wasn’t a great outing for him, but the Texans need him all the same, with their receiving corps awfully banged up at the moment. He should not be drafted in 12-team fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Jayden Higgins tore his ACL during practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: It’s a devastating blow for the second-year pro and the Houston offense. Higgins was set to be the team’s No. 2 wideout behind Nico Collins this season after posting 525 yards and six touchdowns as a rookie operating mostly as a downfield threat. Higgins’ absence in the Texans offense leaves the team without much depth at the position. Expect Xavier Hutchinson to take on a much more prominent role in the balanced Houston offense while Tank Dell and Jaylin Noel see a bump in snaps and routes. It’s hard to say any Texans receiver not named Nico will have much in the way of fantasy value in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell caught his only target for 43 yards in Houston’s Week 7 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He added a two-yard rush on an end around. While it was good to see him back on the field, it should be noted that it looked like his 43-yard catch glanced off Jaylin Noel’s hands and seemed to immaculately find it’s way into Dell’s as he scampered off for some yards after the catch. Dell further confounded the Houston Wideout Situation, playing just 14 snaps. We have no idea what to trust here beyond Nico Collins. Dell seemed to be running just fine, though it sounded like at times his delay in getting up to speed was about recovery. We’ll all get the Week 8 bye to sort this one out. Dell isn’t a must-roster through it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell (knee) will play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell will make his long-awaited return next week against the Giants. By the time he takes the field in Week 7, Dell will have been more than 22 months removed from his last regular-season game, which came in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell suffered a torn ACL, LCL, and MCL, along with a dislocated knee, in that game against the Chiefs and has been on a long road to recovery. He’ll join a crowded receiver room that recently acquired Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jaylin Noel has posted a solid 17-334-2 line through the first six weeks of the season and topped 100 yards in Sunday’s win over the Jaguars. Targets could be hard to come by for Dell, but his return next week is an impressive feat on its own given the injury he had to work through.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans ruled out Tank Dell (knee) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans depart for London tonight to face the Jaguars on Sunday, and Dell will remain in Texas. He is currently practicing in full, but the team has not yet cleared him for game-day activities. Dell does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans are facing the Jaguars in London this week. If Dell travels, that would indicate that Dell has a chance to play for the first time since suffering a multi-ligament tear in 2024. He would be a low-floor FLEX if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) won’t play in Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He did not practice on Friday and was ruled out. The Texans reportedly pushed hard on Dell in full pads on Thursday’s practice despite the questionable listing, it seems his body did not react as they’d hoped. This leaves Jaylin Noel in a potential FLEX-useful spot against a rough Titans secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The diminutive wide receiver remains limited through two practices. In most situations, that would put him on track to play. In this case, Dell might need to consistently practice fully before the Texans let him go out there on game day. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: It is unclear when Dell will take the field on game day, but he is officially participating in his 21-day practice window. His range of potential outcomes is quite wide. Stashing him on fantasy benches is a reasonable move at this time, though he is not guaranteed to be a fantasy contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell (knee/IR) will have his practice window opened.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell has missed the mandatory four games on injured reserve, but may be a week-to-week proposition at this point. None of the Texans secondary receivers have really hit the bar of fantasy interesting — partially because none of them gets full playing time — and we’d be skeptical that Dell would hit that either early in his return. But he could grow into a bigger role as the season plays out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans agreed to terms with WR Tank Dell on a one-year, $1.7 million contract restructure.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The deal includes $1 million in guarantees while saving the franchise almost $2 million against the cap. Dell is reportedly nearing a return from the devastating knee injury suffered in Week 16 of the 2024 season but will begin 2026 on the physically unable to perform list, meaning he will miss the first four games of the regular season. The contract restructure hints at a potential “prove it” year for Dell, giving the team options following 2026 pending health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Tank Dell (knee) is “close” but “not quite there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He was already placed on injured reserve, so he’ll miss the first four games of the season. Reading between the lines it sounds like Dell has a chance to miss more than just the first four games of the season. Kayshon Boutte and Dalton Schultz will battle for the role of lead secondary target behind Nico Collins while Dell is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jacob Cowing caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: With Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, De’Zhaun Stribling, and more out with injuries, Cowing was asked to do more as a receiver in this one. He ran the third-most routes of any receiver, but did have more targets and catches than Brandin Cooks, who ran the most routes. Still, with the 49ers on bye next week and likely to be healthier when they return in Week 9, Cowing is not a recommended add on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: KhaDarel Hodge (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is a low blow, even for the subsation. Hodge began the year on San Francisco’s practice squad but was promoted to the active roster when De’Zhaun Stribling went down with an ankle injury. He wound up running 45 percent of the routes in Week 3 but was not targeted once. With Mike Evans also banged up, Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins could be in line for more work this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes Jacob Cowing could be the primary replacement for Demarcus Robinson (ankle).
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Robinson suffered a severe ankle sprain in Sunday’s win against the Dolphins and could miss significant time. Cowing ran seven pass routes after Robinson’s exit from the game — the most among all Niners receivers besides Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans. Cowing was not targeted against Miami. If he gets a bump on snaps and routes this week against the Cardinals, Cowing would be nothing more than a deep league flex play who would likely be a boom-bust option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel will take over “a portion” of the Z-receiver role, while also contributing as a “wide back.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows notes that at 30 years old, Samuel is “not going to be close to an every-down player.” 49ers WRs Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing are competing to be Samuel’s backup, though neither player will be reliable in fantasy. Samuel may also struggle to return FLEX value at this point in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk missed practice due to a broken finger on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Juszczyk missed practice Wednesday due to a broken finger. Also missing practice was WR Jacob Cowing, who was dealing with a hip flexor strain. It is unclear how much time the two will miss, but add them to the long list of offensive skill player injuries for the 49ers in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Nick Wagoner believes 49ers WR Jacob Cowing has “a chance to carve out a role as a returner with some opportunities in the passing game.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This doesn’t exactly sound like a fantasy-friendly role. Wagoner listed him as the 49ers’ player who was the “biggest surprise” of organized team activities and mandatory minicamp, “consistently making big plays down the field in team drills and 7-on-7.” Unfortunately, the wide receiver room is crowded. Despite the solid play, Cowing will have a tough time earning a reliable role in the offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he is excited by the work WR Jordan Watkins and WR Jacob Cowing have been putting in this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Watkins drew positive reviews as a rookie last summer, but September ankle and calf injuries stunted his development, pushing him to the bottom of the depth chart. Cowing’s second NFL season was derailed by a recurring hamstring strain. The Athletic’s Matt Barrows listed him as a standout at Thursday’s practice, but he caught just four passes as a 2024 rookie. Expectations for him must be tempered. Watkins is worth monitoring for deep-league managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers designated WR Jacob Cowing (hamstring) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team now has 21 days to observe Cowing in practice before officially activating him from injured reserve. The move comes at the right time. 49ers WR Ricky Pearsall aggravated his knee injury in Week 17 and was unable to play in Week 18. Cowing is not a full-on replacement for Pearsall, if the latter player remains sidelined, but having another wide receiver available is at least mildly helpful. The team also signed LB Milo Eifler to a reserve/future contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said the team will not open Brandon Aiyuk’s (knee) return window this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Niners continue to push back the return for Aiyuk, who is still working his way back from the season-ending knee injury he suffered in 2024. 49ers general manager John Lynch said last week that the team still plans to get Aiyuk on the field at some point this season, but the timeline for his return remains a mystery. In addition to Aiyuk, the Niners also said they won’t be opening Jacob Cowing’s return window until after their Week 14 bye. Cowing has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers placed Jacob Cowing (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He’ll miss at least the first four games of the season. Cowing dealt with problems in the hamstring throughout training camp and ultimately won’t be able to take advantage of a golden chance while Brandon Aiyuk is out early in the season. The 49ers re-signed P Thomas Morstead to take Cowing’s spot on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson operated as the Vikings’ No. 2 pass-catcher on the day, seeing a lot of Kyler Murray’s targets in the flats. He caught a five-yard touchdown in the second half and finished with 35 receiving yards. Two of his targets came in the end zone, giving him a solid floor as a red zone receiver. Hockenson’s red zone usage is a good sign for his fantasy value; he is in the low-end TE1 range for Week 8 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) is not on the Vikings’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and was able to heal up over the Vikings’ Week 6. He demonstrated a solid connection with Kyler Murray in Week 4, posting a 13/119 receiving line against the Dolphins. Hockenson can be treated as a TE1 this week against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson did the same yesterday and can be safely expected to start in Week 7 against the Colts’ beatable defense. Hockenson has seemingly developed a strong connection with Kyler Murray and can be started as a fantasy football TE1 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson was ruled out in Week 5 against the Saints after suffering a concussion. The Vikings were on bye in Week 6. The extended absence gives Hockenson decent odds of practicing in full this week, and we expect that to be the case. An update will be provided if he is limited today. Hockenson developed a strong connection with Kyler Murray in Week 4, and warrants TE1 treatment in Week 7 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson was slammed into the ground on his first catch of the day. He got up slowly and was immediately checked out by the medical staff. Hockenson was eventually evaluated for a concussion and ruled out. With a bye week on deck for Week 6, Hockenson should be able to return for the team’s next game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 13-of-13 targets for 119 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: With just over two minutes left in the game, Hockenson took a knee at the Dolphins’ five-yard line, allowing Kyler Murray to seal the game with a trio of kneel-downs after that. Although Hockenson surrendered the touchdown, he still delivered a TE1-worthy stat line on the day. The veteran tight end served as Murray’s go-to receiver, regularly nabbing passes on short-to-intermediate slants and curls. Hockenson mostly dove forward for a couple of extra yards after catching passes, but he did manage to drag a defender on a 14-yard gain early in the fourth quarter. The Dolphins’ pass rush was very effective today, and Murray seemed to hone in on Hockenson as his primary pressure fix as the game progressed. Hockenson will be a borderline TE1/2 against the Saints in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Running a route on 29 of the team’s 37 drop backs, Hockenson was uninvolved in the offense even after Justin Jefferson exited the game with an ankle injury in the first half. Hockenson, who has nine grabs over the Vikings’ first three games, profiles as a low-floor weekly option in a Minnesota offense that has not passed at its usual volume early in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson more or less repeated his Week 1 statline, only this time on far less passing volume for the Vikings’ offense. Carson Wentz attempted just 20 throws as the Vikes went “survive and advance” mode in weather-addled Chicago. With Kyler Murray expected to return from his concussion in Week 3 in Tampa, perhaps Hockenson can post a higher-end TE2 statline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson finished second on the team in targets, though his 17 percent target share isn’t much to write home about. He found paydirt late in the third quarter on a red zone strike from Carson Wentz over the middle of the field. Wentz was filling in for a concussed Kyler Murray, who will likely miss Week 2. Hockenson is more of a TE2 than a true TE1, but his strong Week 1 outing at least puts him on the border versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings restructured the contract of TE T.J. Hockenson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: The move saves $5 million against the cap for the Vikings in 2026, a franchise that is now scrambling to get under the salary cap following numerous high profile moves made the year prior. Hockenson is coming off the worst statistical season of his career following a devastating knee injury suffered in 2024. Now two years removed from the injury and playing with something to prove, the fantasy needle could be pointing up should he find more consistent quarterback play moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 5-of-6 targets for 45 yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Nothing groundbreaking here, though this was more like reasonable low-end TE1 work than reasonable low-end TE2 work. Schultz heads into the Week 8 bye with 137 yards in six games against non-Bengals defenses this year and unless you’re in a TE-premium league likely does not need to be on the roster while on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: He’ll be good to go, but given how much Houston’s wideout usage has expanded of late, Schultz is probably just a passable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Correcting a previous item, Schultz ended up practicing today. He was limited, as was Brevin Jordan (foot), who evidently picked up a new injury. Schultz’s return gives him a chance to face the Giants this week. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow, though it is possible he gets hit with the questionable tag if he remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz is unlikely to play in Week 7 against the Giants, and now Texans TE4 Brevin Jordan (foot) appears to have suffered an injury. Jordan was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. The injuries elevate TE2 Foster Moreau to the streaming ranks for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz never left the Texans’ Week 6 game against Jacksonville, but he was spotted with a limp after taking a knee to the leg. It’s possible the injury was worse than initially expected. If he were to miss Week 7, Foster Moreau, who scored twice last week, would be the next man up. Given that Schultz was barely putting up TE2 numbers as the starter, our hopes for Moreau as a streaming option would not be high.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: If you’re thinking all Dalton Schultz lines have started to blur together, you’re not wrong. He’s had eight catches for 69 yards since his Week 2 explosion against the Bengals. There’s not much upside here, but at least he’s providing a safe TE2 floor for those of you who get five points per TE reception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-2 targets for nine yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Not the most inspiring entry of #RevengeGame lore. Schultz was outgained by Cade Stover and Brevin Jordan. He’s trending towards TE2 usage with Nico Collins back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz told the CBS booth before the game that he “hopes to not have stat lines” like he had in Week 2, an anecdote they related as he had just one catch in the fourth quarter. Sounds like news that fantasy managers wish they had heard yesterday. He didn’t have a catch in the first half and yielded a red zone touchdown to spoiler Foster Moreau. Schultz has low-end TE1 status in a classic #RevengeGame against the Cowboys in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 12-of-14 targets for 140 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: An incredible PPR scam as the Texans had him as the main checkdown receiver while trailing for much of the game. Eight of the 12 catches came in the fourth quarter as C.J. Stroud tried in vain to push the rest of this offense anywhere. Don’t expect this much next week with Collins apparently questionable again, but Schultz clearly elevates in the pecking order and has TE1 appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk was not targeted in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was activated off the injured list this week after missing the first six games of the season with a calf injury. He played on just 20 of the team’s 66 snaps and ran a route on 14 of their 43 dropbacks. Kirk was always likely to be eased back into things, and the 49ers have a bye next week to get him more up to speed. That being said, he doesn’t figure to be a huge part of this passing game if the 49ers can get more of their receivers back healthy after the bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers activated Christian Kirk (calf) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The 49ers would normally have Kirk on a pitch count for his first game of the year. With their top four receivers unavailable for today’s game, Kirk may be thrust into a full-time role right away. He will be in the mix for WR1 duties in San Francisco alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. Kirk is a long-shot FLEX option for his first game as a 49er.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus after being activated from injured reserve Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk is on track to make his 2026 debut this week in the 49ers’ game against the Falcons. As strange as it sounds, Kirk has a chance to vault into the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver role with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to sit out this week. Kirk should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was limited all of last week but starts out this week listed as a full participant for the 49ers’ Wednesday walkthrough practice. He remains on injured reserve, but head coach Kyle Shanahan said Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7. A full practice listing is a good start and Kirk could see WR3 volume immediately with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel dealing with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Christian Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk has been on injured reserve with a calf injury but could return to the Niners’ injury-ravaged receivers room this Sunday against the pass-funnel Falcons defense. “He had two good practices (last week). It was just his first two practices of the year,” Shanahan said of Kirk, who last year had 239 yards and a touchdown in 13 regular season games for the Texans. “We were down on wideouts, so it was still something we discussed, but we decided to give it another week.” If Kirk returns and plays something close to a full complement of snaps against Atlanta, he could function as the team’s No. 1 receiver with Mike Evans (Achilles) seemingly unlikely to suit up. Kirk should be rostered in most 12-team leagues and all deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 6 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He won’t be activated off injured reserve for this one, but he did practice three times this week and he may be a consideration for Week 7’s game if things continue to trend in this direction. This means Brandin Cooks should operate as San Francisco’s No. 2 wideout assuming Mike Evans plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk is a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game against the Commanders. His status is worth tracking considering the absence of Deebo Samuel and general lack of depth at the position. Fantasy managers could be forced to wait until Week 7 for more fidelity considering the team plays in the final game of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk’s inability to practice fully despite his lengthy injured reserve stint suggests he might need another week or two to get ready for an NFL game. Still, the 49ers don’t face the Commanders until Monday night. If active, he could end up warranting FLEX treatment with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers designated Christian Kirk (calf/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: His 21-day window to practice before being activated begins today and he’ll be limited in practice. It would be surprising if Kirk were activated this week given the timing, but perhaps Week 7 will be a realistic target, assuming practice goes smoothly and there are no setbacks. He was limited in his first practice back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 25-of-36 attempts for 308 yards and an interception in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding three rushes for 19 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson again led the Browns to a heart-stopping fourth quarter comeback after the Titans tied the game late in the fourth quarter. Watson connected with Harold Fannin for a long gain that put the Browns in field goal range before they won the game at the buzzer. Watson targeted KC Concepcion a team high ten times, mostly on well-designed short area passes. He was 7 percent over his expected completion rate — one of his best rates of the 2026 season. Watson rushed for a touchdown in the second half after being flushed out of the pocket; it was his first rushing score of the season. Watson, who now has two straight games without a passing score, should remain in superflex lineups next week against a pass-funnel Pittsburgh defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 16-of-26 passes for 164 yards in the Browns’ 13-10, Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson has now taken 13 sacks over the last two weeks. The Browns’ QB1 was under pressure all afternoon by the Ravens, but found himself in position to lead a game-winning drive with 1:59 left on the game clock. Watson started the drive with a nine-yard completion to Jaleel McLaughlin, but came up big on a third-and-five when he found Jerry Jeudy for a 33-yard gain to move into Ravens territory and position his team for the game-winning field goal attempt. Three plays later, Andre Szmyt, who missed the go-ahead field goal earlier in the game, converted on a 37-yard try to propel the Browns into first place in the AFC North. It wasn’t a pretty game for Watson, but that’s nothing new. He has thrown for just 319 yards and one touchdown in his last two games and has just two touchdowns in his last three games. He shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a low-end QB2 in next week’s road game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 15-of-33 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ 17-12, Week 5 loss to the Jets, adding six rushes for 40 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson also fumbled four times in rainy New Jersey conditions, somehow losing only one. Rather nonsensically drawing some “he’s back” chatter of late, Watson was indeed back this week, but just to the miserable form he’s displayed for nearly his entire Browns tenure. Alibis abounded — the weather, losing KC Concepcion to an early concussion — but Watson just wasn’t spinning a good ball, with the rather large exception of his 29-yard touchdown strike to Denzel Boston down the left sideline in the fourth quarter. That was a single-coverage thing of beauty. But other than that, Watson’s ball was fluttering and he was not making good decisions. That included on the Browns’ final play from scrimmage, a 4th-and-11 from their own 19 where Watson bafflingly did not attempt a throw, instead pulling the ball down and losing a fumble as he ambled near the sideline. Terrible. Although this will likely be an outlier performance in terms of its ineffectiveness, today was a reminder that Watson is never going to reclaim his long-ago Texans form. That should include for Week 6 against the Ravens, where Watson will struggle for superflex relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 24-of-33 passes for 268 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Browns’ 27-24, Week 4 win over the Steelers, adding 33 yards on seven carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson made very few mistakes through the air against a solid Pittsburgh defense, although a third quarter fumble on a scramble attempt and a fourth quarter interception on tipped pass at the line of scrimmage allowed the Steelers the runway to make the game interesting late. Watson also badly missed a wide open Harold Fannin on a third down play that would have allowed the Browns to ice the game, instead giving the ball back to Aaron Rodgers with under four minutes to play while up eight points. Rodgers would work his late-game magic to knot the game at 24 before Watson drove the Browns into field goal range to set up the go-ahead kick with 10 seconds on the clock. Watson had a 20-yard carry wiped from his ledger due to penalty that would have padded his counting stats further. The two turnovers notwithstanding, Watson played a largely clean game that saw the Browns improve to 3-1, currently alone atop the AFC North, pending the outcomes of the Ravens and Bengals games Sunday. The Browns turn the page to a Week 5 meeting with the Jets, where Watson will remain a surprising high-end QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Deshaun Watson has earned more opportunities to start for the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Per Fowler, sources around the league say Watson could get six total starts this year. The bar is low in Cleveland. Watson has not yet thrown for 240 yards in a game and has just five passing touchdowns this year. He is a QB2 against the Steelers tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 16-of-30 passes for 144 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions in the Browns’ 21-18, Week 3 win over the Panthers, adding 11 rushes for 45 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: The multi-score start was Watson’s second straight, though his yards per attempt fell precipitously for the second consecutive week. He’s now gone from 9.3 YPA in Week 1 to 7.9 to 4.8. Absolutely everything was underneath this afternoon, though we suppose the effort did come in a win. Watson found Harold Fannin for seven catches and a pair of scores after hitting the tight end seven total times between Weeks 1 and 2. The flip side was that Watson had just one completion longer than 20 yards, a 28-yard strike to Denzel Boston. Watson also missed a snap late after taking a big hit, but ended up returning ahead of what proved to be the game-winning field goal. Watson hasn’t been quite as bad as feared, but he’s hardly silencing the critics, including Browns fans who occasionally booed Sunday. The Steelers will be a tough short-week matchup this Thursday. Watson won’t be in the superflex mix for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 24-of-30 attempts for 238 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding six rushes for 23 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson was far more accurate than he was in Week 1’s meltdown loss to the Jaguars. He was 6.5 percent over his expected completion rate and once again hit rookie WR Denzel Boston for a long touchdown. Watson navigated the pocket well and was passably accurate on short-area throws (his 3.6 aDOT is as low as it gets for a full game’s work). His Week 2 play all but guarantees he’ll hang on to the Browns’ starting QB gig for at least a few more weeks before Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel get another shot under center. Watson will have superflex appeal in Week 3 against a gettable Carolina defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Shedeur Sanders could start in Week 3 if Deshaun Watson plays poorly in Week 2.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Schefter said it “feels like Shedeur’s time is coming” if Watson bombs in the Browns’ Week 2 matchup with the Bucs following his Week 1 collapse against Jacksonville. Sanders, in that scenario, would be under center for the Browns’ home opener against the Panthers in Week 3. Sanders, who is slightly more accurate than Watson in the short and intermediate areas, would be an upgrade for Harold Fannin and KC Concepcion. He would likely be a downgrade for downfield air yards eater Denzel Boston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports “the belief is that the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point” for Deshaun Watson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: The Browns open the year with a two-game road trip before returning to Cleveland for their home opener next week. Watson was a disaster in Week 1, turning the ball over twice while throwing for 205 yards and one score. Another showing like that versus the Bucs this week and he could be sent to the bench. Shedeur Sanders would then draw the start against Carolina in Week 3. It’s unlikely the Browns offense turns things around under Sanders, but things truly cannot get worse than they are right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Browns coach Todd Monken said he “anticipates” Deshaun Watson will start for the Browns in Week 2.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Monken had been a little more evasive on the issue in his post-game interview after Week 1’s shellacking. It appears the Browns would like to touch the hot stove at least one more time against the Buccaneers. Expectations for all Browns pass-catchers and runners can be lowered even against a middling Bucs defense. Monken added “there were some really good things on film.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 1-of-3 passes for 13 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks was out-targeted and outplayed by both Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing. Cooks did run the most routes of any receiver on the team, but he didn’t command targets or look like a key piece of the receiving game. With Mike Evans likely back in Week 9, it’s hard to hold onto Cooks through the Week 8 bye in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Jordan Watkins caught his only target for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Watkins drew the start in place of the injured Deebo Samuel but was unable to take advantage of the opportunity, with 23 of Brock Purdy’s 29 targets going to the team’s top three options in Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle. Evans departed at the end of the second quarter with an aggravation of his Achilles injury, something that appears likely to cost the veteran a Week 7 game against the Falcons. That could leave Watkins in line for a second consecutive start, although the upside remains modest. Fantasy managers are likely best leaving both Watkins and veteran Brandin Cooks on the waiver wire, the latter of whom caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes Brandin Cooks is the “next man up” in the 49ers receivers room.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: With Deebo Samuel sustaining a serious hamstring injury in Week 5 against Seattle, Cooks stepped in and functioned as San Francisco’s No. 2 receiver behind Mike Evans. Cooks was targeted on 17 percent of his pass routes against the Seahawks and caught a touchdown on his only reception. Though Jacob Cowing could mix in with Samuel sidelined, Cooks should be in line for a few targets a game. The well-traveled veteran can be picked up in deeper fantasy formats this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: 49ers signed WR Brandin Cooks, formerly of the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Cooks is signing with the 49ers’ practice squad initially “to get up to speed for games.” Cooks, 32, posted a 24/279/0 receiving line in the regular season last year, before chipping in five catches for 78 yards in two playoff games. He is perhaps unlikely to be fantasy-relevant right away, but there is a real chance he could work his way into the 49ers’ wide receiver rotation, given their influx of injuries at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Free agent WR Brandin Cooks worked out for the Ravens on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: This is probably a bad sign regarding WR Zay Flowers’ (hamstring) Week 2 availability, though the Ravens also placed rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on short-term injured reserve this week. A signing seems likely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Bills GM Brandon Beane said he’s had conversations with Brandin Cooks and his agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks is probably a fallback plan for the Bills if they don’t draft someone. Even if he’s signed, the pecking order in targets in Buffalo has radically changed with DJ Moore in town and fantasy managers shouldn’t be expecting more than a WR5 role for Cooks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 2-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Bills’ Divisional Round loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks made two spectacular almost catches. On one of them, he caught the ball while twisting on the sideline, and his knee came down in bounds, but his wrist landed a fraction of a second earlier and landed out of bounds. The other play was far more controversial. It seemed like Cooks had hauled in a 44-yard pass to set the Bills up for a game-winning field goal in overtime, but the ball was stripped away by a Broncos defender. The Bills believed Cooks was down by contact before the ball was stripped loose, but the call was not reviewed, and the Broncos would then drive for a game-winning field goal of their own. The 32-year-old came on down the stretch for the Bills, showing that he still has enough deep speed to make big plays. He finished the season with 24 catches on 36 targets for 279 yards and no touchdowns in 15 games with the Bills and Saints. Some team will sign him in free agency and give him a role as a deep threat.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 3-of-5 targets for 58 yards in the Bills’ Wild Card Round win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks came down with a 36-yard bomb from Josh Allen late in the fourth quarter that eventually set up a go-ahead score. He finished the day second on the team in catches, targets, and yards. With Josh Palmer on IR, there was already plenty of volume up for grabs in the receiver room. The Bills then lost Gabe Davis to a knee injury late in this game. His status for the Divisional Round is up in the air. Cooks will likely operate as the team’s No. 2 receiver next week, putting him squarely on the DFS radar as a salary relief option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Bills declared WR Brandin Cooks inactive for Week 18 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Every other player the Bills declared inactive is a key starter, like Dion Dawkins or Greg Rousseau, so this says a lot about how important Cooks is to the Buffalo offense despite only being on the roster for three games. The 32-year-old posted a 100-yard game last week and has emerged as the primary deep threat for Josh Allen and the offense. Expect Cooks to be a key contributor in the playoffs for as long as the Bills can keep winning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 19 times for 66 yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants, adding one catch for 15 yards on his only target.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was the only game in town for the Texans, playing 54-of-61 snaps, but couldn’t convert the empty-box looks he was getting into real fantasy value. It was actually a reasonable game compared to most Texans box scores this year. Marks looked to have been hurt at one point in the third quarter but was able to escape the tent and go right back to work. Assuming David Montgomery (groin) is back after the bye week, Marks will head back to FLEX work on most fantasy rosters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that David Montgomery (groin) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Like we said yesterday, Montgomery is still seemingly in the week-to-week camp. Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale will likely split backfield touches this week. The Texans used both Marks and Jawhar Jordan last week, but Jordan suffered an injured reserve-worthy injury. Marks should be in starting lineups, but he may be more of a FLEX than a reliable RB2. Ogunbowale is a low-floor PPR dart throw.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: We were told early last week that Montgomery is week-to-week. Today’s absence suggests he is still week-to-week and will likely be ruled out again on Friday, though we do not know that for sure. We will provide an update before then if his status changes. In the meantime, Woody Marks will get the start again this week, potentially with less touch competition. Jawhar Jordan totaled 50 yards and a touchdown on seven total touches last week, but was surprisingly placed on injured reserve today. Dare Ogunbowale remains a receiving factor, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 15 times for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars, adding two catches for 25 yards on three targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was mostly bottled up, though he did manage 9/41 in the second half behind a few reasonably big runs to become the first back all year to hit 40 rushing yards against the Jaguars. He played 49-of-63 snaps. The Texans run game is still bad, but against the Giants in Week 7 Marks should probably be on the RB2 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: We already knew that Montgomery was considered week-to-week, so this is unsurprising. Woody Marks will start for however long Montgomery is sidelined. The Jaguars field one of the NFL’s best run defenses, but Marks ceded just one snap to Dare Ogunbowale last week. Theoretically, he should remain in a near-full-time role, elevating him to the RB2/FLEX tier despite the tough matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery will be week-to-week with the groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Ryans said Woody Marks “will carry the load” for the team while Montgomery is sidelined. It’s been a tough start to the season for Montgomery, who scored three times in Week 1 but has been locked out of the end zone ever since while averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per touch. Marks has been slightly more efficient than Montgomery this season, but the Texans’ running game as a whole has left much to be desired. Marks’ expected workload makes him worth a waiver wire claim where available, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect anything more than RB3 levels of production at this time. The Texans will take on the Jaguars in London in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 15 times for 62 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans, adding four catches for 23 yards on four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: He had a 20-ish yard touchdown taken off the board on what appeared to be a ticky-tack holding penalty. The more important story here is that David Montgomery (groin) went down mid-game and the Texans gave Marks a full workload. He had 56-of-65 snaps and no other back received a carry or touch. Marks won’t get that kind of workload next week against the Jaguars, but if Montgomery is destined for a long absence, he should threaten 70 percent of the snaps and a majority of the workload, making him one of the day’s bigger fantasy winners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed six times for 22 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: His touchdown came on a two-minute play where the Cowboys line wasn’t even set, aka the only way any Texans runner can advance the football. Still, he’s faster than David Montgomery and that’s really all the Texans have in their backfield. He’s a FLEX option against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed five times for 15 yards and a touchdown in Week 3’s loss to the Colts, adding one catch for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks managed just 20 snaps to David Montgomery’s 32 in a game where there was only one hurry-up drive that got off the ground for the Texans, but at least he cashed in with a one-yard touchdown plunge. He remains a volatile FLEX next week against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Juan Jennings caught 2-of-3 targets for 34 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings caught a 20-yard pass, his longest reception of the season. He was targeted three times, nearly catching a long touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter, but failing to haul it in. Jennings is outside of the top-three pass-catching options for the Vikings and is irrelevant for fantasy purposes in this role. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on him in case he is traded, but Jennings does not need to be in fantasy lineups heading in to Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jauan Jennings “would be a name for me to keep an eye on” for the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been a major disappointment in Minnesota, falling behind Tai Felton on the depth chart. A small stakes trade could make sense for the 49ers, who are down to hoping Brandin Cooks can provide for Brock Purdy in a major rash of injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Tai Felton caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jordan Addison missed this game with an ankle injury and the Vikings deployed Felton as their WR2 over Jauan Jennings. Jennings ran fewer routes and failed to catch his only target. Felton wasn’t awfully productive either, but it’s good to see the former third-round pick picking up more work in his second season. He will return to a rotational role, assuming Addison is cleared to play after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings simply isn’t meaningfully involved in the Vikings’ game plan. That is unlikely to change in Week 5 against the Saints, especially with the Vikings’ offensive line getting banged up in Week 4. Jennings could be asked to contribute more as a run blocker next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-2 targets for one yard in the Vikings’ Week 3 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings hasn’t been part of the Minnesota passing attack through three weeks. Against the Bucs Jennings ran the second most pass routes on the Vikings, behind only Jordan Addison. The low-volume Vikings passing offense likely can’t support more than one fantasy viable pass catcher per week. Jennings should remain on waivers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jauan Jennings (personal) is expected to return for Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings was targeted just once in Week 1. It could be argued that we’re not sure what his target count would look like in a normal Vikings game given how quickly Kyler Murray got hurt, but there’s never been a normal Vikings game anyway. Jennings is best monitored from the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (personal) is out for Week 2 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Head coach Kevin O’Connell ruled out veteran receiver Jauan Jennings, citing a death of a close family member. Jennings will step away from the team to mourn the passing, leaving Tai Felton as the player most likely to step into his vacated role when the Vikings take on the Bears. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison should take on all the volume they can handle with the team also without Jordan Mason. Jefferson is a locked-in WR1 while Addison offers an intriguing upside-WR2 profile after putting up a dud in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings failed to catch his only target in the Vikings’ Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Things went off the rails in the first quarter when Kyler Murray left with a concussion, but one target is a bad omen no matter who is under center. Jennings was also a distant third on the team in routes behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He is not on the fantasy radar headed into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports that Jordan Addison remains the Vikings’ No. 2 wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Pelissero affirmed Addison’s role as a guest on the Rich Eisen Show. He prefaced the remarks by saying that WR Jauan Jennings’ signing “immediately raises questions” about whether the Vikings planned to move on from Addison before saying that they, in fact, do not. Jennings was brought in on a “cut-rate,” one-year deal to play the No. 3 wide receiver role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports that Jauan Jennings will replace Jalen Nailor as the Vikings’ No. 3 wide receiver this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: We assumed this was the case, though Jennings’ size allows one to wonder if he might be valuable in heavy personnel packages. Nailor departed for the Raiders earlier this offseason. Vikings No. 2 WR Jordan Addison was suspended for Weeks 1-3 last season. From Week 4 on, Addison out-snapped Nailor 714-to-507. Expecting a similar split from Addison and Jennings this season is reasonable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins was second among receivers in routes, running a route on 30 of the team’s 43 dropbacks, and was also third on the team overall in targets. He made a few nice catches over the middle of the field, and his day could have been much better as he caught a 20-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the second half. Unfortunately, while his feet were in bounds, the ball shifted a couple of inches when his back slammed into the ground, and replay review overturned the call of touchdown on the field. Depending on the status of the 49ers’ wide receivers coming out of next week’s bye, Watkins could be an interesting fantasy option, but it’s hard to know that for sure until we know who will be healthy for the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught his only target for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins drew the start in place of the injured Deebo Samuel but was unable to take advantage of the opportunity, with 23 of Brock Purdy’s 29 targets going to the team’s top three options in Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle. Evans departed at the end of the second quarter with an aggravation of his Achilles injury, something that appears likely to cost the veteran a Week 7 game against the Falcons. That could leave Watkins in line for a second consecutive start, although the upside remains modest. Fantasy managers are likely best leaving both Watkins and veteran Brandin Cooks on the waiver wire, the latter of whom caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: KhaDarel Hodge (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: This is a low blow, even for the subsation. Hodge began the year on San Francisco’s practice squad but was promoted to the active roster when De’Zhaun Stribling went down with an ankle injury. He wound up running 45 percent of the routes in Week 3 but was not targeted once. With Mike Evans also banged up, Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins could be in line for more work this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught both of his targets for 60 yards in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins saw increased opportunity with Mike Evans (rib) exiting in the second quarter. He caught a pair of long targets from Purdy despite KhaDarel Hodge and Jacob Cowing beating the 24-year-old in snaps. Watkins could certainly be on the fantasy radar if Evans misses an extended period of time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers declared RB Jordan James inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: James has officially lost the backup job to rookie RB Kaelon Black, who should be safely stashed on fantasy benches before kickoff. The 49ers also declared QB Kurtis Rourke, CB Ephesians Prysock, WR Jordan Watkins, LB Tatum Bethune and OT Enrique Cruz inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel will take over “a portion” of the Z-receiver role, while also contributing as a “wide back.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows notes that at 30 years old, Samuel is “not going to be close to an every-down player.” 49ers WRs Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing are competing to be Samuel’s backup, though neither player will be reliable in fantasy. Samuel may also struggle to return FLEX value at this point in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he is excited by the work WR Jordan Watkins and WR Jacob Cowing have been putting in this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins drew positive reviews as a rookie last summer, but September ankle and calf injuries stunted his development, pushing him to the bottom of the depth chart. Cowing’s second NFL season was derailed by a recurring hamstring strain. The Athletic’s Matt Barrows listed him as a standout at Thursday’s practice, but he caught just four passes as a 2024 rookie. Expectations for him must be tempered. Watkins is worth monitoring for deep-league managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers WR Jauan Jennings (ankle/ribs/shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Jennings is very difficult to trust after last week’s meltdown. He was limited twice to begin the week, and we do not yet know his Friday participation level. At this point, the big-bodied wide receiver can only be viewed as a boom-bust WR4/FLEX option. If and when he resumes practicing in full consistently, we will be able to upgrade him to WR3 status. 49ers rookie WR Jordan Watkins (calf) is also expected to play this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Jordan Watkins (calf) is expected to resume practicing this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: We were just thinking the 49ers wideout projections needed another variable to deal with. Watkins briefly wowed in training camp before dealing with a high-ankle sprain and later this calf issue. It’s possible he cuts into some veteran playing time if the 49ers wideout room remains unsettled, but he’s not someone to rush and pick up in re-draft leagues without seeing some real signs of fantasy life.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers ruled out QB Brock Purdy (toe) for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Purdy remained sidelined all week, as did WR Ricky Pearsall, who is dealing with a PCL sprain in his knee. Just eight days ago, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Purdy is considered week-to-week, so the starting quarterback’s absence is hardly surprising. Hopefully, Purdy can remain setback-free and return for the 49ers’ Week 7 game against the Falcons, though that outcome should not be viewed as guaranteed. The 49ers also ruled out WR Jordan Watkins (calf), DL Kevin Givens (pectoral) and EDGE Yetur Gross-Matos (knee/hamstring).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 8-of-10 passes for 88 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Unfortunately, Kittle also lost a fumble on the team’s final drive of the game as he was trying to earn extra yardage and set the team up for a better shot at the end zone. Even with that mistake, Kittle was tremendous on the day and the clear top option in the passing attack. The 49ers will be on a bye in Week 8, and then some of their injured receiving corps should return in Week 9, which might impact Kittle’s usage a bit. He will remain a rock-solid TE1 in fantasy leagues though.
