https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-8 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle got the scoring started with an 11-yard touchdown on a dime from Brock Purdy to the corner of the end zone, contributing to the offense steadily through a dominant first half before pushing his yardage totals with a 35-yard reception to start the third quarter. It was a tale of two halves for the San Francisco offense, which managed a staggering 303 yards of total offense in the first half and only 72 yards of total offense after the break, likely heavily influenced by the departure of Mike Evans at the end of the second quarter. Evans is expected to miss the team’s Week 7 contest against the Falcons, where Kittle could step into additional volume in his already-solid TE1 profile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: After three straight big weeks, Kittle finally came back down to earth in Sunday’s win over the Seahawks. His longest reception came on a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but proved inconsequential after Deebo Samuel lost a fumble on the following play to end the drive. Kittle has been targeted 19 times over the last three weeks and has gone for 70-plus yards in three of his last four games. He should be primed for a bounce-back next week when the Niners play host to the Commanders on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle (illness) is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but that he was still expecting to play. Kittle was not listed with the 49ers’ inactives when the team announced them 90 minutes before kickoff, meaning he is good to go and can be treated as a TE1 as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a quiet day for Kittle before a fourth quarter screen pass went for a 58-yard score that sealed the game for the Niners. Displaying explosiveness less than a year after tearing his Achilles tendon, Kittle outran the Broncos secondary for his second touchdown in as many weeks. His six looks from Brock Purdy was second most among Niners pass catcher, trailing only Mike Evans (eight targets). Kittle’s big play upside and his role in the red zone make him a potential matchup flipper in fantasy. He gets the Seahawks in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-7 targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle saw a season-high seven targets in the 49ers’ win, becoming the team’s No. 1 pass-catcher after Mike Evans (rib) left the game. He caught a 10-yard touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter and later sealed the win with a 20-yard score with under two minutes left. Kittle seems to be all the way back from his Achilles tear, leading all 49ers offensive skill players in snaps, only trailing Brock Purdy and the offensive line. With Evans’ status in the air, Kittle is the team’s top receiver and is squarely in the fantasy TE1 conversation for Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle looked good in this one, finding space over the middle of the field and showing good burst after the catch. That’s important considering he’s still working his way back from last year’s Achilles injury. The veteran played just three fewer snaps than Mike Evans and was fourth on the team in routes run, just one behind Christian McCaffrey. His playing time will continue to increase as the year goes on, but he looks pretty close to the George Kittle we’ve gotten used to.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle will likely remain on a snap count in Week 2, though his usage should continue steadily ticking upward. He can be started as a TE1 against the Dolphins’ fantasy-friendly defense this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle’s continued limited participation is not concerning. The 49ers are likely just managing the veteran’s reps early in the year, coming off a season-ending injury. Kittle is a TE1 for the 49ers’ Week 2 game against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 20-of-31 attempts for 181 yards and an interception in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward did his best game manager impression in this one and made a handful of solid high-leverage throws using various arm angles. He had a positive EPA per drop back and was slightly over his expected completion rate, small victories being what they are. The Titans deployed no-huddle for much of the game and operated at a quick pace — a strategy that seemed to get Ward into some sort of rhythm early on. Ward’s accuracy issues showed up on the fourth quarter when he sailed a pass over the head of a wide open tight end who had beaten the entire Cleveland secondary. It would’ve likely been a game-winning touchdown. Ward has now cracked 200 passing yards just once through Week 7 and should only be rostered in superflex formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 11-of-22 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Titans’ 26-20, Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward added just three carries for seven yards. Ward got the “quarterback win” as the Titans finally broke their five-game losing streak to begin the season, but this was more about the Colts imploding and setting up one short Titans field after another with turnovers. Ward did keep his connection with No. 4 overall rookie Carnell Tate going, finding him for 6/70/1 on seven targets. Ward didn’t find veteran Calvin Ridley for what would have been a wide open end zone grab, but we digress. His interception was a second quarter sail job as he was getting leveled by the blitz. Ward’s increasing chemistry with Tate is the Titans’ first real good news of the season, but today was not a particularly inspiring victory. They now get the Browns for a Week 7 home matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said he had a “cool conversation” with Cam Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s head, per Saleh, is in a “good place” ahead of the Titans’ Week 6 game against the Colts. Ward has been dreadful through five weeks, ranking 24th in EPA per drop back and 27th in drop back success rate. Only five quarterbacks have a lower adjusted yards per attempt than Ward this season. Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent are the only QBs who average fewer fantasy points per drop back. Saleh has defended his second-year QB at every turn and does not seem close to benching him in favor of journeyman backup Mitchell Trubisky.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 170 scoreless yards and an interception in Tennessee’s Week 5, 26-3 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans led off the day with a 58-yard field-goal drive that fell apart from a red zone first-and-5. They would not even flirt with crossing 30 yards in a drive for the rest of the game and crossed into Texans territory on only 11 more snaps all game, including just one inside the Houston 40. Ward took four sacks and avoided several others by turning Tyjae Spears into a PPR hero. The closest he came to actually putting points on the board was a double-covered bomb to Carnell Tate’s general area. It was, well, what you would have expected from both sides in the preseason. Ward remains a last gasp supeflex QB2 heading into Week 6’s game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 20-of-31 passes for 222 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Titans’ 24-18, Week 4 loss to the Ravens, adding four carries for 27 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s second pass of the game resulted in an interception, but he would settle in to put together his most productive outing of the season. Ward linked up with rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate on multiple long gains and ended the day with four completions of 20-plus yards. The two would connect on a 33-yard pass late in the fourth quarter on a fourth-and-10, and on the next play, Ward would find Wan’Dale Robinson for a three-yard score to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-18. Ward did a good job at evading pressure in this one. Despite being pressured on 11 dropbacks, per PFF, only one of those resulted in a sack. Ward has been sacked just once over the last two weeks, but will have a tough challenge ahead of him next week when the Titans play host to the Texans. Ward projects as a low-end QB2 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Titans pass catchers and the team’s defense are to blame for Cam Ward’s sloppy footwork.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Asked about Ward’s continuing footwork disaster, Saleh said the second-year quarterback “usually starts off good then fades into old habits.” Titans beat writer Terry McCormick then asked Saleh “why if his footwork gets worse as the game goes on, why the offense has had such slow starts. [Saleh] said it has been dropped passes vs. Giants and defense not getting off field vs. Eagles.” Saleh has made a point to shield Ward from all criticism throughout the preseason and through three horrific regular season outings. Ward ranks 20th in accuracy and 29th in EPA per drop back this season. He’s fresh off throwing a game-deciding end zone interception against the lowly Giants in Week 3. Mitchell Trubisky will probably get a couple starts this season if Ward can’t turn things around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said “no” when asked if he’d consider sitting QB Cam Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s gotten off to a slow start in 2026, completing 62.5 percent of his passes for a meager 504 yards and two touchdowns in three games. He has improved his sack rate quite a bit, cutting it from 9.2 percent in 2025 to 5.38 percent so far this year. The Titans backup is Mitch Trubisky. It is probably too soon to give up on Ward, but it doesn’t bode well for his future that Saleh is already being asked the question. Ward will be one of the bottom five quarterbacks in the Week 4 fantasy rankings against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 181 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Titans’ 7-12, week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans’ offense looked dead on arrival with 34 yards on their six first-half drives. They opened the game with four consecutive three-and-outs and didn’t get on the board until late in the fourth quarter, when Ward tossed a short touchdown to Wan’Dale Robinson. It looked like Ward was getting in rhythm late in the game, but he ended the contest with a ghastly interception directly into the hands of Jevon Holland, who was standing in the end zone waiting for the ball. Ward took care of the ball until the game-ending throw, but this was a one step forward, two steps back showing from the young passer. That has unfortunately been the case for the better part of the last three weeks. Ward is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4 against the Ravens, and his poor play is making all of the team’s fantasy options largely irrelevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 13-of-20 passes for 183 yards in the Titans’ 24-20, Week 2 loss to the Eagles, adding four rushes for seven yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s two scores on the ground doubled his previous career total, though he is now sitting on one passing touchdown through eight quarters. He is at least not turning the ball over, and has taken “just” five sacks. He has been so far unable to heat up his connections with offseason additions Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson, but he found Elic Ayomanor for two critical gains vs. Philly. Cutting out the negative plays was an absolutely essential first step for Ward, but he has yet to supplement them with big gains or consistent chain-moving. That included botching a Hail Mary in the fourth quarter this afternoon. Ward won’t be much of a superflex option for next week’s road date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 19-of-32 passes for 140 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ 23-10, Week 1 loss to the Jets, adding four rushes for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward also took three sacks for 13 yards. His touchdown was a too little, too late 11-yard strike to Elic Ayomanor with the Titans trailing 23-3 at the 2:42 mark of the fourth quarter. As was the case down the stretch last season, Ward did a good job of avoiding turnovers, but he struggled to generate positive plays of any kind. He was besieged by pressure, but he just wasn’t making anything happen. That could come in time — there’s a new experienced play-caller in Brian Daboll and several new weapons in the skill corps — but this was a highly discouraging start to the year at home vs. a not-exactly-amazing Jets defense. It was certainly confirmation that Ward is on the outside looking in of top-24 status in superflex leagues for the time being. The Eagles are a rough Week 2 matchup, even if the Titans are at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison also got a carry for three rushing yards. His usage involved designed touches in the shallow area, with the Vikings trying to get him out into space. His utilization dropped in the second half and he did not see many looks downfield. Addison is the clear No. 3 pass-catching option in the Vikings offense, a role that warrants WR4 consideration for Week 8 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison, well-rested coming off his team’s Week 6 bye, is ready to go. The Colts’ defense has played poorly, and they will likely be without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf). Addison can be a volatile producer at times, but he warrants WR3/FLEX treatment this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings declared Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison seemingly gave it a go this morning but wasn’t quite ready to play. The Vikings get a Week 6 bye, so Addison should be ready to go when they return to face the Colts in two weeks. Also inactive for the Vikings are OT Christian Darrisaw, S Jakobe Thomas, WR Odell Beckham, CB Chuck Demmings, DT Elijah Williams, and QB Max Brosmer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Jordan Addison (hamstring) “isn’t likely to be active” for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. He was considered a game-time decision as of this morning, but it sounds like the team is going to hold him out for at least one week. Justin Jefferson, on the other hand, is expected to suit up. The offense will run through him, per usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Justin Jefferson will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: The same is true of Jordan Addison. Both Minnesota wideouts are currently listed as questionable for Week 5. Jefferson is from Louisiana and has already told reporters he plans to play in the homecoming game. We expect him to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan for him and Addison to be safe.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison practiced on Thursday and Friday after taking Wednesday off. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable for Sunday’s game against New Orleans, but he will probably only be a WR3/FLEX play if Justin Jefferson (ankle) also returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 2 wide receiver sat out on Wednesday due to “a little hamstring soreness.” If he can get through today and tomorrow without aggravating the sore muscle, he should be able to play in Week 5 against the Saints. His WR3/FLEX viability is subject to Justin Jefferson’s (ankle) status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: According to O’Connell, Addison has “a little hamstring soreness,” though it is “considered minor.” Keep an eye on this. Hamstring injuries can quickly become problematic at the wide receiver position. If active and practicing fully by the end of the week, Addison will be a WR3/FLEX against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 4-of-6 targets for 52 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison’s box score could have looked a little bit better, had his 21-yard gain on a curl route during the Vikings’ third drive not been erased by a penalty. Regardless, he played sidekick to T.J. Hockenson in this one. For his part, Addison maximized his opportunity, delivering the longest play of the game via a 27-yard catch on a crosser in which he barreled through multiple Dolphins defenders to generate extra yardage. The Vikings also gave him the ball on a jet sweep, but he lost one yard on it. Addison will be a WR3 against the Saints next week if Justin Jefferson (ankle) is still sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 5-of-9 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison dominated air yards and targets with Justin Jefferson sidelined with an ankle injury he sustained in the second quarter. His 41-yard touchdown grab from Kyler Murray was one of three downfield looks he got on the day; he nearly converted the other two as well. A non-factor in the Vikings’ first two games of the season, Addison should be locked into lineups if Jefferson misses any time with the ankle issue. If Jefferson returns for Week 4 against the Dolphins, Addison would figure to be flex-viable as long as Murray is under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black’s day did not start great as he was stuffed on three straight plays inside the three-yard line on the first drive. Then he watched as Christian McCaffrey scored a touchdown on fourth down. However, McCaffrey also picked up a thigh injury on that drive and missed the remainder of the first half, which allowed Black the opportunity to rip off some nice chunk runs and a long touchdown. McCaffrey did return in the second half, and Black also lost a fumble in the second quarter, so there were some moments of inconsistency. That being said, Black looks like one of the best handcuff running backs in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Christian McCaffrey is questionable to return to Week 7 against the Falcons with a thigh injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: McCaffrey was used heavily on the first drive with the 49ers down so many offensive players, and he came out of that drive with a touchdown but also a thigh injury. The trainers worked on him on the sideline for two drives before finally bringing him into the medical tent. The 49ers do have a bye next week, so they could try to get him back into the game, but they are also up 14-3 at this point, so the Falcons will likely need to get the game closer. Kaelon Black will continue to see a workhorse role while CMC is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: 49ers RB Kaelon Black (illness) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black was limited on Wednesday, but upgraded to full participation on Thursday and Friday. There are no concerns about his ability to handle backup duties against the Seahawks this week. That said, he has just 10 carries over the last two weeks and cannot be started in 12-team FLEX spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black (illness) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: This should be a non-issue for Black by the time Sunday comes around. Black cut into Christian McCaffrey’s role again last week with six carries, though he only turned that into 13 yards. He doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value but remains one of the better contingency options headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black had six rushes for 13 yards in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: After seeing 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, Black now has 17 rushing attempts over his past three games as the Niners’ No. 2 back behind Christian McCaffrey. Black should be rostered in most leagues as one of the best contingency options in the game. As long as CMC is healthy, Black should remain on benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black rushed four times for 17 yards in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black has seen his role decrease with Christian McCaffrey returning to bell cow usage. The rookie saw four carries and one target, totaling eight offensive snaps. He saw a red zone touch but otherwise did not get close to scoring opportunities. Black is one of the most valuable handcuffs in fantasy football moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black rushed seven times for 25 yards in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: After splitting work fairly evenly with Christian McCaffrey in Week 1, Black took a clearer backup role here. He had some snaps on the first drive of the game, but then Black mixed in sporadically until the game was decided early in the fourth quarter. At the end of the day, the rookie played on 16 of the team’s 45 snaps and is unlikely to have any standalone value; yet, he remains one of the better bench stashes in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: 49ers declared QB Kurtis Rourke, WR Jordan Watkins, CB Ephesians Prysock, LB Tatum Bethuneand OL Enrique Cruz Jr. inactive for Week 2 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Black was expected to play, and now we get confirmation that he will. The rookie had 14 carries in his NFL debut in Week 1, and it remains to be seen if that will be the 49ers’ plan going forward or if that had something to do with Christian McCaffrey cramping or the entire team traveling abroad to Australia for the first game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black picked up 14 carries while Christian McCaffrey dealt with cramps in Week 1. Now it’s Black who is banged up, meaning we might get more CMC versus Miami this week. Black was added to the injury report midweek and logged two limited practices before receiving the questionable designation. He is in the RB4 range for Week 2, making him a middling FLEX play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: 49ers RB Kaelon Black (groin) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black appeared on the 49ers’ injury report yesterday as a limited participant. He was seen practicing today during the portion of practice open to the media, but we do not know if he managed to practice in full. If so, that would be encouraging. The 49ers face the Dolphins’ unimposing defense this weekend. If Black is active, he can be started in FLEX spots, though ideally we get an update on his health beforehand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson led the Vikings in targets and yards on a low-volume day for the passing game. He hit a career milestone, crossing 600 career catches with a four-catch day. The Vikings’ offense continues to post low-efficiency outings as the defense lifts the team to an undefeated record. Jefferson is still the No. 1 wide receiver but banks on high volume usage and touchdowns to be a fantasy WR1. A lack of touchdown opportunities and red zone usage will be an issue in the Vikings offense, but Jefferson has a soft matchup against the Lions for Week 8. He should be back in the WR1 rankings next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Coming off the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, Jefferson got in a limited session on Wednesday before returning to full participation on Thursday. The star wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be treated as an elite WR1 against a Colts pass defense that will be without CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be feeling even better at this point, coming off a Week 6 bye. The Colts will notably be without No. 1 cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) this weekend, making life even easier on Jefferson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is just a maintenance day for the Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver. Jefferson has an excellent matchup this week against the struggling Colts’ defense. The unit will likely be without No. 1 CB Sauce Gardner (calf), further enhancing Jefferson’s WR1 outlook for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson didn’t miss a beat after returning from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. He made several spectacular grabs in this game, the most amazing of which was a toe-tapping catch in the back of the end zone with three defenders covering him. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson is simply one of the best receivers in the league. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when the Vikings face the Colts after their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is active for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jordan Addison is out. Jefferson would normally see plenty of targets anyway, but the absence of Addison all but guarantees that he will see one of the highest target shares in the league. Jefferson remains a top-end WR1 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Justin Jefferson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jordan Addison, on the other hand, is not expected to suit up because of a hamstring issue. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson will dominate the targets for Minnesota, especially with Addison on ice. Barring a setback in warmups, Jefferson remains a top-half WR1 play for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Justin Jefferson will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The same is true of Jordan Addison. Both Minnesota wideouts are currently listed as questionable for Week 5. Jefferson is from Louisiana and has already told reporters he plans to play in the homecoming game. We expect him to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan for him and Addison to be safe.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Justin Jefferson (ankle) plans to play in Week 5 against the Saints, but the team “has to see how he feels on Saturday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is great news. We will not have to wait for the dreaded game-time decision call with Jefferson this time around. If active, Jefferson should be started as a WR1 against the Saints. He remained limited in practice all week. We will provide an update on the matter as soon as possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson practiced on Friday after limited sessions on Thursday and Wednesday. He also insisted that he plans to play when asked earlier this week. We think he’s on the optimistic side of questionable as he returns as close to LSU as he can in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy was second on the team in pass routes — behind Denzel Boston — and fourth on the team in targets. This comes after Jeudy’s Week 6 performance against the Ravens in which he went for a season-high 69 yards on four receptions. Jeudy is well behind Boston and KC Concepcion in the pass-catching pecking order and should only be rostered in the deepest leagues for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 4-of-4 targets for 69 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy made the most of his limited volume in this one, with his longest play coming on a 33-yard reception on the final drive of the game as the Browns were driving down the field to complete the comeback victory. This was easily the best game of the season for Jeudy, who hadn’t gone for more than 36 yards in any other game this season. He’s seen four or fewer targets in four of his five games played and won’t be on the fantasy radar heading into Week 7 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Browns would like a third or fourth-round pick for WR Jerry Jeudy but he’s not sure they’ll be able to get it.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: We, too, would like to simply be given valuable things for no reason. Jeudy has fallen off the fantasy map enough that we’re now simply blurbing trade possibilities for him. The 27-year-old’s only real fantasy value at this point is hoping he gets traded somewhere where he can get involved again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jerry Jeudy “could be had” before the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: With Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning large roles right away, Jeudy has all but vanished from the box scores. He went two games without catching a single pass before bringing down three balls for 36 yards on Thursday night. Jeudy got pushed out of the Browns’ long-term plans on draft night and isn’t even part of the week-to-week game plan at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: KC Concepcion caught 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Concepcion continues to operate as the primary slot receiver for a Browns team clearly looking to their youth while phasing out veteran Jerry Jeudy, the latter of whom managed three receptions on three targets for 36 yards. Concepcion has yet to lead the team in receiving while working in a short area role, with this the first game thus far which he has gained more then 43 yards. He’ll be a difficult start in fantasy circles when the Browns take on the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy did not catch his lone target in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: After his two-catch performance in Week 1, Jeudy is off to a roaring start. Denzel Boston has established himself as Cleveland’s de facto No. 1 wideout while KC Concepcion is being force fed the ball on gadget plays near the line of scrimmage. With almost no avenue to fantasy relevance, Jeudy should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Browns WR Jerry Jeudy (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy is on track to play, but he is seemingly being phased out of the offense. Browns rookie WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are establishing themselves as impactful starters, and their roles should only grow in the coming weeks. Jeudy should be left on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 2-of-4 targets for 26 yards in the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy felt like an afterthought behind the two rookie wideouts in the Browns’ passing game. He tied for second in targets and was a distant third in yards behind Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. The veteran is still involved as a starter on the outside, but Todd Monken made it a point to make Boston the deep target and Concepcion the primary offensive weapon. In a fantasy-unfriendly offense, Jeudy is best left off the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Browns WR Jerry Jeudy (hamstring) did not practice at mandatory minicamp on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot reports that Jeudy “felt something in his hamstring today,” so he sat out. Coach Todd Monken made clear that he does not give veterans rest days right now, so if a player sits, it’s because they are being cautious with an injury. Today was the Browns’ final mandatory minicamp practice. They will now go on break until training camp begins in July. Early in May, Cabot reported that the team is hoping Jeudy reclaims his WR1 role this season. Browns rookie WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have been taking full rotations with both the No. 1 and No. 2 offensive groups. Yesterday, ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi reported Boston “has been one of the Browns’ standouts this summer.” Get well soon, Jeudy. The youngsters look promising.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot reports that the Browns hope WR Jerry Jeudy “can rebound from a down 2025 season and reclaim his role as the No. 1 receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Cabot later writes that “the Browns really need Jeudy to return to his Pro Bowl form, and are confident he will.” We think her initial, hopeful framing is closer to the truth. Last week, Browns general manager Andrew Berry said rookie WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston’s presence has “zero impact” on Jeudy. There’s an awful lot of reassurance going on here. Jeudy posted a 92/1,229/4 receiving line in 2024 before cratering to a 50/602/2 receiving line in 2025. Jeudy is under contract through 2027, but the dead money and salary cap savings are nearly even if designated as a post-June 1 cut next year. Given the Browns’ pass-catching investments over the last two drafts, and Jeudy’s poor 2025 showing, he looks like a dicey pick in fantasy for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: Jameis Winston rushed four times for four yards and a touchdown in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: He became New York’s short-yardage tush-push option with J.J. McCarthy starting, managing a touchdown in the first half and a fourth-down conversion in the second half. That makes him more of a thorn in McCarthy’s side than anything else for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said they’re “working through that now” when asked which quarterback would start against the Texans in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: The fact that he has to think about it probably tips the hand that it will be J.J. McCarthy sooner or later — if not outright now. Jameis Winston was replaced by McCarthy in the fourth quarter yesterday and McCarthy showcased his deep arm and almost erased a large deficit by throwing for 243 yards on 21 attempts. If McCarthy did start against the Texans, he would likely be a bottom five superflex option on the Week 7 slate because of his established history as a starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said he “can’t answer that now” when asked about who his starting quarterback would be heading into Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: It’s the exact kind of answer we would expect from a coach who is just minutes removed from his team nearly completing a comeback victory. J.J. McCarthy stepped in for Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter and lit up the Saints for 243 yards and one touchdown in the fourth quarter, leading the Giants on three scoring drives and 17 unanswered points in a game that the Saints won 34-27. Whether it’s in Week 7 or a point later in the season, McCarthy feels like a lock to start multiple games for the Giants, who now sit at 3-2-1 on the season. The Jameis Winston Experience, while fun, is often short-lived, and his underwhelming performance on Sunday against the Saints (152-1-2) comes a week after Winston struggled for the entire first half against the Commanders before he turned it on in the second half. Harbaugh will likely announce his Week 7 starter in the coming days, but it wouldn’t be surprising to learn the team is handing McCarthy the keys for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: Jameis Winston completed 14-of-26 passes for 152 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Giants’ 34-27, Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: Winston led a struggling offense in Week 6, scoring one touchdown in the first half. Winston’s offense did all of its scoring in the first half and possessed the ball in a very limited fashion in the second half. He averaged 5.8 yards per attempt and threw a pair of interceptions in the second half in an otherwise lackadaisical offensive day. Winston was replaced by J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter; the Giants scored 17 points under McCarthy. Winston remains a volatile fantasy QB2, though it is a very real possibility that he is not the starter for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: According to ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, Giants coach John Harbaugh hinted that the Giants have “more in store for the J.J. McCarthy package.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: Who is asking for this? McCarthy was on the field for three plays in Week 5. They gained three yards, two of which came from McCarthy on a pair of rush attempts. After flaming out as a traditional quarterback in Minnesota, McCarthy is working his way toward becoming the next Taysom Hill. Jameis Winston remains the starter, but Harbaugh will use McCarthy as a change-of-pace option a few times each week. He could also take over as the starter if Winston struggles for an extended period of time, though we appear to be at least a few weeks away from that being a consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: Jameis Winston completed 33-of-54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns in the Giants’ 27-27, Week 5 tie with the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: After a shaky first half in which he threw for just 72 yards on 16 passes, Winston locked in for the second half and nearly led the Giants to a comeback win. Winston completed 21-of-28 passes for 211-3-0 in the second half, leading the Giants on touchdown drives of 63, 75, and 72 yards. Winston connected with tight end Isaiah Likely on a three-yard touchdown pass for his first of the day, and found Likely again for a 17-yard score on a fourth-and-eight to cut Washington’s lead to 27-20. On their final touchdown drive, Winston connected with Malik Nabers four times and found him in the end zone for a leaping touchdown grab to tie the game at 27-27 with less than two minutes left in regulation. In overtime, Winston twice moved the Giants into field-goal range. Unfortunately, they would only get one chance at attempting a go-ahead field goal. After Dominic Zvada missed the first try, a fumble by Cam Skattebo would cost the Giants any hopes of a second attempt to win the game. Winston has thrown for 576 yards, six touchdowns, and two interceptions in his last two games while attempting just over 60 percent of his passes. He profiles as a mid-to-low-end QB2 next week against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: Jameis Winston completed 18-of-29 passes for 250 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions in the Giants’ 36-24, Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: Today was something of a “Full Jameis,” as the unpredictable No. 2 quarterback also took four sacks. He thankfully didn’t add any fumbles, while he found each of Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields and reserve TE Theo Johnson for touchdowns. The Nabers grab, a 25-yarder vs. LB Mack Wilson’s hopeless coverage, was Winston’s longest score. His longest completion was a 40-yarder to Fields where he got flushed from the pocket on a third quarter 3rd-and-20. It was a devastating outcome for the Cardinals, to put it mildly. Winston’s mistakes were legion this afternoon — both of his picks were awful, awful passes — but it was a much livelier effort than the G-Men or fantasy managers saw in Weeks 2 and 3. This version of Jameis might actually keep the G-Men in games while holding off J.J. McCarthy for a little while. The Commanders are an unimposing Week 5 road matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said the possibility of Jaxson Dart (knee) returning during the playoffs “may be a bit ambitious.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: Everyone but Harbaugh knew Dart wasn’t returning for the playoffs the moment his meniscus repair procedure was announced. Harbaugh, meanwhile, held out hope that his starting quarterback could return in time for a deep playoff run. Even he isn’t keeping that facade up anymore, though he noted that Dart’s surgery “went well.” Coming off an ugly win, Jameis Winston will make his second start of the year in Week 4. J.J. McCarthy will get a crack at the job when the Giants inevitably start losing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants could start JJ McCarthy in “the near future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameis-win.analysis: New York acquired McCarthy from the Vikings on Monday in exchange for a 2027 fifth round draft pick. Hughes spoke with NFL sources who said “the Giants do not give up a fifth-round pick unless they plan to play McCarthy in the near future.” Head coach John Harbaugh and the team’s coaching staff, per Hughes, see McCarthy as a starting-caliber quarterback despite his immense struggles in Minnesota last season. “The Giants welcomed the chance to add a player they view as a competitor, gritty, mobile, and who has all the tools to be a plus passer in the NFL,” Hughes said. With Jameis Winston playing worse than any QB in recent memory, McCarthy could be just a couple weeks away from taking over as New York’s starter. He would be a mild upgrade for Malik Nabers and the rest of the Giants pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all five of his targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: The touchdown is nice to see, and Pitts finished tied for second on the team in both catches and targets. However, preliminary snap counts say he played on 37 of the team’s 67 snaps and ran a route on 20 of their 37 dropbacks. Charlie Woerner ran a route on 11 dropbacks and Austin Hooper ran a route on 10 dropbacks, so the Falcons continue to get tons of tight ends on the field. That makes Pitts more of a high-end TE2 option because he does have good touchdown equity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-7 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was one of the beneficiaries of a pass-heavy second half for a Falcons offense that was forced to abandon the run game facing a multi-touchdown deficit. Pitts took advantage of single coverage a couple times, including on his first touchdown grab. He now has three touchdowns over his past two games as Michael Penix brings some stability to the Atlanta offense. Pitts, who ran a route on 26 of the team’s 38 drop backs against Chicago, will be a viable play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts remained largely confined to short area work with his game-long reception going for only 13 yards. A second quarter touchdown from five yards out gave the veteran tight end his first trip to paint through five games and his five receptions doubled that of his previous four appearances. Pitts remains a difficult weekly start for as long as Drake London and Bijan Robinson remain healthy. A Week 6 meeting with the Bears in Atlanta should see him remain in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all three targets for 47 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts played just one snap on the team’s first two possessions before seeing modest usage the rest of the game. His counting stats were padded in the second half with a 28-yard, catch-and-run reception on a play action pass out of the flat. Pitts isn’t getting the snaps or route participation to return consistent fantasy production and is best left on fantasy benches for as long as Drake London remains healthy. That won’t change ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was the recipient of Michael Penix’s first completion of the 2026 season, with the latter making his season debut following ACL surgery. The return of his starting quarterback was not enough to give Pitts his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season as he watched blocking tight end Austin Hooper score the lone receiving touchdown of the evening from five yards out in the second quarter. Fantasy managers are stuck in the constant hype cycle with Pitts with very little to show for it through three games, making Pitts a difficult start on the road against the Saints in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Cooper Rush was a disaster once again, tanking the fantasy prospects of every Falcon. Pitts narrowly avoided his second straight bagel with a lone catch late in the second quarter. He failed to catch his only target last week. There’s not much to say about Pitts and the entire offense when Rush simply shuts down all production from the jump. Pitts will reclaim a spot in the TE1 ranks if Michael Penix is back for Week 3. He is not on the fantasy radar if Rush is under center once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts Sr. had no catches on one target in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts owes most of this to a poor performance by Cooper Rush under center. Pitts played on 39 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 22 of their 29 dropbacks. He simply wasn’t a factor with Rush struggling to move the ball down the field. We should note that the Falcons were very run-heavy with Rush at quarterback, and Charlie Woerner played 38 snaps and was on the field for 22 run-blocking snaps to just 16 for Pitts. If the Falcons are going to continue to be so focused on rushing the ball, that could cut into some of Pitts’ snaps and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Falcons TE Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-3 targets for 59 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts ripped off multiple double-digit gains, moved well and looked tough to bring down. He delivered a 37-yard catch on the Falcons’ first drive, securing the pass on a quick out route from bunch formation before taking off down the right sideline. He later had a 16-yard gain on a sort crossing route, where he again chewed up yards after the catch. Pitts is a mid-tier TE1 entering the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports “Falcons people on the ground” believe Kyle Pitts is moving better than he has in years.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler settles on Pitts being a “certified first or second option in the passing game.” Pitts sets up as a potential high-end TE1 on an offense that loves to use the tight end, and the fact that he finished second in fantasy points among TEs last year is proof of concept that he was already playing better in 2025. With his contract taken care of, perhaps this will be the year Pitts ascends to the top of the tier, the writer said forgetting any of the last five years had happened.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It seemed like Branch would be in for a bigger role in Week 7 with Olamide Zaccheaus out with a shoulder injury. However, Branch ran a route on just 18 of 37 dropbacks and was only targeted twice. It doesn’t seem like he’s anywhere close to playing a large enough role for fantasy value and doesn’t need to be held through the bye weeks in redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch’s primary duties still come on kick and punt returns, but Kevin Stefanski made it a point to get him more involved this week. He was held without a catch or even a target in Week 1. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar yet, but dynasty managers can be pleased with his role taking a step in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch had no targets in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: On one hand, no targets is bad. On the other hand, Branch played one more snap than Olamide Zaccheaus and ran only three fewer routes. This is not a passing attack that you want pieces of right now, but there is a chance that Branch could take the WR3 role by the middle of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will play in Week 1 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch was limited by the hamstring issue for the first two practices of the week. He got up to a full practice on Friday and was cleared for Week 1. Branch will likely see a few designed touches in his NFL debut, but fantasy managers will want to wait until he overtakes Olamide Zaccheaus on the depth chart before getting him into their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: The Falcons’ third-round rookie wide receiver could end up playing this week, but his inability to practice fully will keep him in a pure backup role. Branch does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch ran behind Olamide Zaccheaus for most of training camp. A light workload in practice heading into Week 1 all but guarantees he won’t threaten the veteran receiver for a starting role to open the year. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar for his NFL debut versus the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall reports that Falcons WR Zachariah Branch is “looming” behind WR Olamide Zaccheaus for the starting slot role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: According to Kendall, “everyone in Atlanta can see” Branch’s ascension. The diminutive rookie has been “a standout in Atlanta from the moment he stepped on the practice field.” Zaccheaus is still taking most of the first-team snaps, so Branch may have to continue fighting for the starting role in-season. That said, the coaching staff plans to line up Branch at all three wide receiver spots. Obvious questions remain regarding Branch’s ability to play in the NFL at 5'10/180, but the youngster bench-pressed 225 pounds 20 times at the NFL Combine, so his strength is not in question. Even if Branch assumes a starting role, it will probably be tough for Branch to reliably return FLEX value, earning targets behind WR Drake London, TE Kyle Pitts and RB Bijan Robinson, but showing up with a few big performances is possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes Zachariah Branch will finish among the team’s top three receivers in targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It’s not really a stretch when you consider Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus are the two other receivers behind Drake London that are competing for real time on the Falcons. Branch isn’t exactly a lock to be fantasy-relevant as a rookie, but if he shows more than expected, the door is wide open for him in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed five times for 41 yards and a touchdown in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: He didn’t get much usage in this one, managing just 19 snaps despite Tyrone Tracy leaving in the second quarter, but Singletary made the most of his final opportunity with a 30-yard touchdown run in overtime to walk off the Texans. With Tracy and (apparently) Skattebo both managing injuries throughout the bye, Singletary could wind up with a reasonable Week 9 role. You probably don’t need to chase it on waivers this week unless you’re in a very deep league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants released Najee Harris.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: The move comes a couple days after Harris criticized the New York coaching staff for its handling of the backfield touch distribution. “It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays...if you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do,” Harris said after the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints. “I’ve never been through none of this before.” Harris had 31 rushes for 99 scoreless yards before getting the boot. With Harris gone, Cam Skattebo could get another chance to see increased playing time after being all but benched last week. Tyrone Tracy, who led the team in rushing attempts against New Orleans, could be the de facto lead back for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed four times for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints, adding one reception for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary saw 31 snaps on the day, leading Giants running backs in a pass-happy game script. It’s unclear what the Giants backfield will look like moving forward, but it’s a messy committee for now. Singletary and Tyrone Tracy seem to be the preferred options for passing down snaps, though Tracy is the preferred choice for more high leverage situations. Singletary is worth a waiver claim but fantasy managers should stay tuned to wade through the coach-speak and see what this Giants backfield looks like for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared S Jason Pinnock, RB Devin Singletary, CB Nikko Reed, DT Bobby Jamison-Travis, OT J.C. Davis, and QB Jake Haener inactive for Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary is once again a healthy scratch as the Giants will roll with Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris, and Tyrone Tracy as their top three backs. J.J. McCarthy will serve as the QB2 behind Jameis Winston in what figures to be a messy game in the elements in Washington this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, S Ar’Darius Washington, CB Nikko Reed, DL Jihad Ward, OL J.C. Davis, TE Thomas Fidone, and DT Bobby Jamison-Travis as inactive for Week 4 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: This is the second-straight week that Singletary has been made a healthy scratch for the Giants. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as the backups to Cam Skattebo. It’s also worth noting that QB J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired from the Vikings earlier this week, is active for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, TE Thomas Fidone II, OL J.C. Davis, DL Josh Tupou, DL Bobby Jamison-Travis, CB Deonte Banks, and S Tyler Nubin inactive for Week 3 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary is a healthy scratch this week. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy are the backup running backs for New York. Singletary had nine carries and four catches in the first two weeks of the year. His absence could be a slight boost to Cam Skattebo, though Singletary’s touches may just be distributed to the other backups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Although Skattebo was not targeted in the pass game, his 18 carries handily led the team. Furthermore, presumed backup Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble on one of his two carries, resulting in Devin Singletary taking over primary backup duties for the remainder of the game. Those two variables should keep Skattebo’s weekly volume high after showing no ill effects of the devastating ankle injury suffered in 2025. His touchdown now gives him eight total scores in nine professional appearances despite only six of those being starts, a rate that will keep Skattebo in the weekly borderline RB1 discussion moving forward. Tracy managed just two snaps to Singletary’s 25, leaving Singletary as the primary backup for the moment. It’s possible Najee Harris gets into this discussion after being a healthy scratch in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary are all listed as co-No. 2 backs on New York’s unofficial Week 1 depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: We can’t endorse relying on anyone in this backfield as a surefire bellcow in the event that Cam Skattebo gets hurt or is ineffective enough to lose playing time. It seems like it will be hard to rely on Tracy to have a major role this year with Harris in town.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan says Najee Harris “was brought in under the premise that he’s going to be a significant contributor” for the Giants this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: It’s worth noting that Cam Skattebo continues to be the first running back up in practice, but it sounds like the Giants could have a vision for Harris, who signed with the team on a one-year, minimum-salary deal, per Raanan. Harris is returning from a torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season in Week 3, but there’s plenty of room for him to earn snaps behind Skattebo once he gets up to speed. A blown pass-blocking assignment by Tyrone Tracy in the team’s first preseason game against the Vikings raised immediate questions about whether or not the Giants will trust Tracy in pass-blocking situations this season, and Harris has proven to be a capable pass-blocker in the past. At this point, it’s hard to imagine Harris having any standalone fantasy value in a healthy Giants backfield, but he could be worth a handcuff to Skattebo in deeper leagues based on these latest reports.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 11 times for 39 yards in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens, adding four receptions for 19 additional yards.
Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 3 receptions for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown took a surprising backseat to Samaje Perine in the Bengals’ win over the Dolphins. He still out-snapped Perine 38-to-33, but a red zone fumble hurt his fantasy production while splitting backfield touches 50/50. There were a few snaps where Brown lined up as a receiver with Perine in the backfield; the Bengals used both backs heavily. Brown previously dominated all sorts of touches for the Bengals backfield, so this is a new development. Game script certainly played a factor but Brown’s ceiling as an RB1 may be considerably lessened if Perine’s usage sticks. He is a fantasy RB2 with a Week 7 matchup against the Ravens on the horizon after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars, adding 11 receptions for 71 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: It was a big pass-catching day for Brown, who saw 11-of-54 total Bengals targets on the day. After Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited, Brown and Tee Higgins saw massive upticks in usage. Brown saw 57 backfield snaps, catching a series of checkdowns and wheel routes despite just 10 rushing yards on the day. He worked ahead of Samaje Perine on passing downs, a good sign for his fantasy production moving forward. We don’t expect Brown to consistently see this many targets but a high backfield share gives him a consistent fantasy floor. Brown is a fringe RB1 for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 61 yards in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers, and two receptions for eight additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown was effective with the opportunities he received, but the Bengals did all of their damage through the air in this one, as Joe Burrow and the company aimed to keep pace with a surprisingly explosive Steelers offense. As far as the Bengals’ backfield is concerned, Brown continues to be the only game in town. He handled 71.4 percent of the Bengals’ running back opportunities in this one but has only one touchdown to show for his efforts this season. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 20 times for 80 yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: He “added” three catches for two yards on five targets, getting absolutely exploded by Kamari Lassiter on one of them. He also had a 20-ish yard run called back for holding. Brown looked quick and able, but the Bengals ran just two plays inside the Texans red zone all game. He played on 42-of-60 snaps per PFF. Brown will be in the low-end RB1 ranks against the Steelers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs, adding five receptions for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: It was neither an efficient nor prolific outing for the Bengals’ lead back, but he found the end zone and out-touched No. 2 Samaje Perine 21-8. It was a full “as expected” day in the Bengals’ backfield. Brown will remain in the RB10-14 range for Week 2 against the Texans. That’s a tough defensive matchup, albeit one the similarly offensive-minded Bills just handled with ease.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. said he “wouldn’t be surprised if the Bengals double last year’s” number of runs from under center on early downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Dehner has been covering the Bengals’ intent to increase the number of plays run from under center all summer. Last season, “the Bengals ran from under center 120 times on early downs. The league average was 210.” Per Dehner, it has become clear “over the weeks that the under-center offense would not be going away.” The Bengals are committed to changing their ways in pursuit of more explosive gains. Starting RB Chase Brown is a locked-in RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Bengals RB Chase Brown said coach Zac Taylor is calling “a lot” of play action and run plays from under center at training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Late in June, The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reported that QB Joe Burrow had agreed to try out more under-center concepts in spring practices. The Bengals’ quarterback prefers to operate from shotgun, but the offense has struggled to generate explosive pass and run plays in recent seasons. Meanwhile, 2025 playoff teams notably thrived under center, prompting a potential schematic switch in Cincinnati this year. Dehner previously reported on Brown’s efficiency leaps when switching from shotgun to under center. Burrow and his wide receiver should, theoretically, receive an efficiency bump from the intended changes as well. This is exciting for fantasy football purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner, Jr. reports Chase Brown has been “at the center of unique twists” in the Bengals offense during training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown, according to Dehner, is “being used all over the formation,” similar to the way Ja’Marr Chase has been deployed in recent years. Brown lines up in the slot and runs a slant one play, then takes a jet sweep the next. He’s part of 20 personnel with two running backs, motions into the backfield, behind a fullback and almost any other spot imaginable.” The Bengals are preparing to use motion at a much higher rate than they have during the Joe Burrow era, especially when Burrow is under center. It’s led to some early camp struggles, per Dehner. “We all got to prepare a little bit more, at least I do, a lot for the motions and playing F and wherever they are putting me takes a little extra study time because I haven’t really done that before,” Brown said. “It’s cool they trust me doing that and believe in my skill set enough. It’s been fun.” Dehner said the team’s “pre-snap eye candy and under-center emphasis have helped establish a refreshed run game” ahead of the 2026 season. Brown’s pass game involvement should give him every chance to be a top-5 back in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson was also targeted on three different deep passes that resulted in San Francisco penalties. That doesn’t help your fantasy team, but it is indicative of his role in this offense. Dotson did run the second-most routes of any receiver on the Falcons; however, he is really only targeted on deep shots down the field, which will make his production inconsistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-5 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson, whose season-high yardage coming into the week was 54 — his total in both of the past two weeks — got loose a couple times in this one, mostly when the Falcons ditched their usual run-heavy offense in favor of a fast-pace pass-heavy approach while facing a multiple touchdown second half deficit. Running a route on 32 of the Falcons’ 38 drop backs, Dotson led the team in receiving yards thanks largely to a 41-yard grab. Dotson could be a deep league play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson continues to operate as the team’s WR2 opposite Drake London but remains unlikely to return consistent fantasy production in an offense heavily concentrated on its top two options in London and Bijan Robinson. Dotson’s touchdown came in the fourth quarter with the team cruising, pushing the lead to 21 points with under 10 minutes to play. Fantasy managers can safely keep Dotson on the bench ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson saw four targets for the second week in a row. He went for 19 yards on one catch last week and didn’t look any different this time around. Dotson is the team’s No. 2 receiver by routes, but there aren’t enough targets to go around after Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson all get theirs. Dotson is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for 19 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson actually operated as the second receiver for the Falcons in this one, running a route on 20 of the team’s 29 dropbacks. He also played 38 snaps, while Olamide Zaccheaus played just 18. That didn’t amount to much, but it’s something for fantasy managers in deeper leagues to keep in mind when Michael Penix eventually gets back onto the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare.
