Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes that if the Falcons make a “random offseason move,” it might come at wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Atlanta depth chart at wideout is sparse even after we account for third-round pick Zachariah Branch in the draft. The No. 2 receiver right now might be Jahan Dotson. Olamide Zaccheaus is also in the picture. The Falcons still have $27 million in cap space but we’ve rarely heard them mentioned by national reporters as interested in the Stefon Diggs/Deebo Samuel/Keenan Allen best veteran free agent wideout tier. Those guys aren’t mentioned in this report either, but they do make plenty of sense from a roster standpoint.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes Jahan Dotson “may be” Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Falcons released Darnell Mooney and KhaDarel Hodge, leaving them with a depth chart behind Mooney of Olamide Zaccheaus, Casey Washington and Deven Thompkins. The Falcons, who lost their first-round pick in the ill-fated James Pearce trade, also don’t have many draft picks this year and could be less likely than most teams to draft a wideout that could challenge Dotson for a role. We’re not quite at “sleeper” status here, but we’re at least late-round Best Ball curious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Falcons signed WR Jahan Dotson, formerly of the Eagles, to a two-year contract worth $15 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson could see starter’s snaps in Atlanta after the Falcons parted ways with Darnell Mooney. Dotson was stuck behind DeVonta Smith and A.J. Brown over the past couple seasons in Philadelphia with no real way to see consistent routes or targets in the Eagles’ ultra run-heavy offense. Dotson managed just 37 catches and one touchdown over 34 regular season games with the Eagles. In Atlanta he will be a distant WR2 at best in Kevin Stefanski’s offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor has shown signs of life of late in a Titans offense operating quickly in recent weeks. Against the Browns he tied Carnell Tate for the team lead in targets while running a route on nearly 90 percent of the team’s drop backs. Even with more involvement in the Tennessee offense, Ayomanor should remain on the waiver wire in most fantasy formats ahead of the Titans’ Week 8 matchup against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: It goes down as his second one-catch, three-target, 11-yard game of the season. He posted those exact numbers in Week 1, though with a touchdown for good measure. Ayomanor popped for 69 yards in Week 2 but failed to find the big play in this game, cratering his numbers. As the WR3 on one of the worst offenses in football, he is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 2-of-3 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: One week after finding the end zone, Ayomanor led the Titans in receiving as they nearly upset the Birds. 41 of his yards came on an impressive leaping grab over Marcus Epps. Good stuff, but there’s not going to be much “good stuff” in this limited attack. Ayomanor should also routinely be out-targeted and out-gained by both Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson. Even in 14-team leagues, Ayomanor is probably off the re-draft radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for an 11-yard touchdown in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor’s score came deep into garbage time with the Titans trailing 23-3. 23-year-old Ayomanor had an impressive rookie year for a fourth-round pick in 2025, but he’s now buried behind Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson in the Titans’ receiver corps. This is not an offense that is going to be producing consistent production out of the No. 3 receiver spot. We’ll let you know if Ayomanor becomes 12-team league relevant, but don’t count on it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Titans WR Elic Ayomanor (shoulder) resumed practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Per ESPN’s Turron Davenport, Ayomanor was in the huddle early at today’s practice, which is a good sign. The second-year wide receiver left practice early yesterday after seemingly injuring his left shoulder. He appears to be good to go and will now resume competing for a starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 4-of-7 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 17 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor secured touchdown No. 4 of his rookie season by leaving his defender in the dust for a seven-yard score. His seven targets tied Chig Okonkwo for a team-high in pass-game opportunities. Ayomanor hasn’t caught more than four passes in a game this year and that’s unlikely to change versus the Jags next week. He will be a splash-play WR5 for the season finale.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-4 targets for 58 yards in the Titans’ Week 16 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Today was the first time since November 2 Ayomanor caught more than two passes, while those receiving yards were actually a new season high. Not bad, if not terribly notable. Chimere Dike remained the more impressive young wideout against the Chiefs. Ayomanor is a young player who has shown something in an offense displaying subtle signs of progress, but he’s not on the radar for fantasy finals week, while his 2026 rank remains very much to be determined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught his only target for 17 yards in the Titans’ Week 15 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor had only one target on the day, but he hauled it in, so that’s something. The Titans don’t seem to want Cam Ward to throw the ball downfield much, which means it’s really hard for anybody to roster Ayomanor in re-draft leagues for the remainder of this season. However, Ayomanor and Ward also appeared to have a miscommunication on a fourth-quarter pass that almost led to an interception, so maybe that hesitancy makes some sense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for a 14-yard touchdown in the Titans’ Week 14 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor’s first quarter score came after a play fake helped him a get a step on the DB in man coverage. It was a great start, but unfortunately his only action on a day where the Titans surprisingly road paved Cleveland on the ground. Ayomanor now has only four grabs for 30 yards over the past three weeks, which is especially disappointing since it has coincided with Calvin Ridley’s season-ending absence. Ayomanor still has end-of-bench dynasty league appeal, but he is miles from 12-team league relevance as we begin the fantasy playoffs, which we might not have guessed during his relatively hot start to the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-5 targets for five yards in the Titans’ Week 13 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor returned from a one-game absence due to his hamstring injury and led all Titans receivers in snaps. He and Cam Ward had very little chemistry this game as Ayomanor caught just one of his five targets. Chimere Dike and Van Jefferson were the only other wideouts to get over three targets; Jefferson caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards. No Titans receivers should be in fantasy lineups for Week 14 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas was active for the first time since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2. Though he logged a measly 14 percent target share, Douglas was involved early, turning a first-quarter red zone target into his first NFL touchdown. Douglas turned his second catch of the day, a short out route, into a 63-yard touchdown by toe-tapping his way along the sideline for a game-sealing score. His role is only going in one direction after the breakout performance. He will be in the WR3 mix when the Dolphins take on the Pats next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas hasn’t played since Week 2 against the 49ers, but the rookie caught five passes for 94 yards in his pro debut against the Raiders and has been targeted on 16.4 percent of his routes. Stuck in a Dolphins offense that currently ranks 31st in scoring and passing yards, Douglas will be hard to trust as anything more than a fringe WR3/WR4 this week against a top-five Jets pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: That’s back-to-back limited sessions from Douglas as he attempts to come back from an injury suffered in Week 2. We’d bet on him getting to the questionable line at this point given the significant layoff, but he does have a real chance to play against the Jets in Week 7 and be a WR4/FLEX candidate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas told reporters that he has finally progressed to being “day-to-day,” giving him a real chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas should be added in 12-team formats. He played very well early on and will likely warrant FLEX consideration upon his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) won’t play in Miami’s Week 5 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas has not practiced or played since Week 2. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve list” he could be placed on. Ah well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Dolphins coach Jeff Halfey said Douglas is “doing better” but is not ready to practice yet. It sounds like the rookie will miss another week. Malik Washington will continue to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 receiver, putting him in the WR3 mix for Week 5. Fellow rookie Chris Bell has seen his role grow every week, but the fantasy numbers aren’t there to match. He was held without a catch on three targets in Week 4. Bell is a solid long-term stash but barely cracks the WR5 ranks for Miami’s matchup with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team is taking it “one day at a time” with Caleb Douglas’ ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: It’s hard to know what to make of this, but Douglas has missed back-to-back games with his injury and could be at risk of missing a third straight game if he can’t get on the practice field ahead of Week 5’s game against the Bengals. Douglas did not practice at all last week, so even getting on the field in a limited capacity would be an improvement. His name will be one to keep an eye on when the Dolphins release their first injury report on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas, QB Brady Cook, CB Marcellas Dial, EDGE Rob Beal, OG DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: The Dolphins will be without Douglas, one of their two talented rookie wide receivers, against the Vikings’ top-tier defense today. He is sidelined by an ankle injury. Joly, the Dolphins’ rookie tight end, is inactive after making his debut last week. Cook wil serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) will not play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury, paving the way for fellow rookie Chris Bell to build on his Week 3 performance in which he went for 4-67-0 on eight targets. Bell and all Dolphins pass-catchers will be tough for fantasy managers to trust as anything more than WR4s on the road against a Vikings defense that could give them fits all afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: We expect to see Douglas listed with a second DNP next to his name today, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4 against the Vikings. Were he indeed to miss this week’s game, WRs Chris Bell (knee) and Malik Washington would benefit. Washington’s target volume is somewhat intriguing, but Bell looks like the far more talented player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 20-of-28 passes for 252 yards in New York’s 27-21, Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Nine threatened a really good box score, crossing 200 yards by the third quarter, but both the Texans (playing more aggressive coverage) and the Giants (using Jameis Winston in short-yardage situations) conspired to keep McCarthy scoreless. Still, it was a nice debut start. McCarthy took three sacks but had zero turnovers while managing a handful of nice throws. The Giants head on bye in Week 8, but McCarthy has played like a reasonable superflex QB2 against the Eagles in a few weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Giants are expected to start J.J. McCarthy “beyond their Week 8 bye.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: The Giants pivoted to “NINE” after he lit up the Saints for 243 yards in the fourth quarter of Week 6. Having already spent some draft capital to acquire McCarthy, the team is going to give him an extended tryout as the starter. If he does well, the Giants will likely hang on to him as Jaxson Dart’s backup next year. They could also trade him in the offseason if he plays well to garner interest from other teams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports J.J. McCarthy will start in Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: John Harbaugh is making the switch after a historic fourth quarter from “NINE”. McCarthy threw for 243 yards and a score in 11 minutes of action as the Giants mounted a frantic comeback against the Saints. Though he came up short in the end, McCarthy gave the Giants’ offense life after three dreadful quarters from James Winston. Now he’ll get the first snap versus a Houston defense that has been surprisingly ineffective this year. McCarthy is a high-risk QB2 for his first start as a Giant. He should at least be added in all Superflex formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said they’re “working through that now” when asked which quarterback would start against the Texans in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: The fact that he has to think about it probably tips the hand that it will be J.J. McCarthy sooner or later — if not outright now. Jameis Winston was replaced by McCarthy in the fourth quarter yesterday and McCarthy showcased his deep arm and almost erased a large deficit by throwing for 243 yards on 21 attempts. If McCarthy did start against the Texans, he would likely be a bottom five superflex option on the Week 7 slate because of his established history as a starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said he “can’t answer that now” when asked about who his starting quarterback would be heading into Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: It’s the exact kind of answer we would expect from a coach who is just minutes removed from his team nearly completing a comeback victory. J.J. McCarthy stepped in for Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter and lit up the Saints for 243 yards and one touchdown in the fourth quarter, leading the Giants on three scoring drives and 17 unanswered points in a game that the Saints won 34-27. Whether it’s in Week 7 or a point later in the season, McCarthy feels like a lock to start multiple games for the Giants, who now sit at 3-2-1 on the season. The Jameis Winston Experience, while fun, is often short-lived, and his underwhelming performance on Sunday against the Saints (152-1-2) comes a week after Winston struggled for the entire first half against the Commanders before he turned it on in the second half. Harbaugh will likely announce his Week 7 starter in the coming days, but it wouldn’t be surprising to learn the team is handing McCarthy the keys for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 11-of-21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Giants’ 34-27, Week 6 loss to the Saints, adding two carries for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: McCarthy’s first play of the game was a read-option where he kept the ball and rushed for a loss of two yards in the red zone. With the Giants down 24 points in the fourth quarter, McCarthy replaced a struggling Jameis Winston and started throwing several deep targets downfield. He threw an interception his first drive but led multiple successful drives late in the fourth quarter. Charlie Jones corralled a 49-yard pass away from a defender, making a near-interception into a long completion for McCarthy. Martin Emerson dropped an interception later in the drive before McCarthy connected with Isaiah Likely for a touchdown. He wound up leading the Giants in passing and rushing through just one quarter of play. Averaging 11.6 yards per attempt, McCarthy was one play away from leading a comeback against the Saints. Instead, we will wait to see if John Harbaugh will name the 23-year-old the starter for Week 7 against the Texans; he would be a fantasy QB2 if he starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: According to ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, Giants coach John Harbaugh hinted that the Giants have “more in store for the J.J. McCarthy package.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Who is asking for this? McCarthy was on the field for three plays in Week 5. They gained three yards, two of which came from McCarthy on a pair of rush attempts. After flaming out as a traditional quarterback in Minnesota, McCarthy is working his way toward becoming the next Taysom Hill. Jameis Winston remains the starter, but Harbaugh will use McCarthy as a change-of-pace option a few times each week. He could also take over as the starter if Winston struggles for an extended period of time, though we appear to be at least a few weeks away from that being a consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, S Ar’Darius Washington, CB Nikko Reed, DL Jihad Ward, OL J.C. Davis, TE Thomas Fidone, and DT Bobby Jamison-Travis as inactive for Week 4 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: This is the second-straight week that Singletary has been made a healthy scratch for the Giants. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as the backups to Cam Skattebo. It’s also worth noting that QB J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired from the Vikings earlier this week, is active for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said the possibility of Jaxson Dart (knee) returning during the playoffs “may be a bit ambitious.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Everyone but Harbaugh knew Dart wasn’t returning for the playoffs the moment his meniscus repair procedure was announced. Harbaugh, meanwhile, held out hope that his starting quarterback could return in time for a deep playoff run. Even he isn’t keeping that facade up anymore, though he noted that Dart’s surgery “went well.” Coming off an ugly win, Jameis Winston will make his second start of the year in Week 4. J.J. McCarthy will get a crack at the job when the Giants inevitably start losing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Khalil Herbert rushed two times for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: Herbert was filling in for Brian Robinson in Week 7, but he did not have anything close to Brian Robinson’s workload. Hebert also caught one pass for 19 yards and was a couple of inches from taking that into the end zone for a score. The 28-year-old will likely be back on the practice squad next weekend if/when Brian Robinson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Falcons signed RB Khalil Herbert, formerly of the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: Herbert could get elevated on game day, but he will not have a fantasy-relevant role. The Falcons also signed EDGE Drake Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: 49ers released Khalil Herbert.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: Herbert was a camp body for the 49ers when several of their running backs were banged up, but the room is fairly healthy now. He could wind up on San Francisco’s practice squad. Also waived/released were OL Isaac Alarcon, DL Evan Anderson, TE Khalil Dinkins, DL Bryson Eason, DL Viliami Fehoko Jr., LB Jalen Graham, WR Wesley Grimes, DL Jah Joyner, CB Darrell Luter Jr., QB Adrian Martinez, RB Sincere McCormick, S Patrick McMorris, OL Drake Nugent, WR Will Pauling, CB Jakob Robinson, CB Eli Apple, DL Quinton Bell, S Ashtyn Davis, WR KhaDarel Hodge, WR Trenton Irwin, LB Deion Jones, OL Robert Jones, OL Doug Kramer Jr., DL Ogbo Okoronkwo, OL Brandon Parker, WR Malik Turner, P Corliss Waitman, and LS Jon Weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: 49ers signed RB Khalil Herbert, formerly of the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: The 49ers have had poor injury luck at the running back position this summer. Herbert, 28, provides a steady veteran presence. The team correspondingly placed RB Patrick Taylor on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Free agent RB Khalil Herbert attended Eagles rookie minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: Free agent RB Elijah Mitchell attended as well. Herbert appeared in three games with the Jets last year, rushing 16 times for 52 yards and earned three targets. Mitchell logged zero touches and earned one target, playing for the Patriots. The Eagles already have five running backs on the roster, so both players face uphill battles to snag a roster spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Khalil Herbert rushed 12 times for 42 yards in the Jets’ Week 18 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: Herbert was released by the Colts in March and then later signed with the Jets in October. He was firmly behind Breece Hall and Isaiah Davis during the season, but was called upon today with both of them ruled out for the final week of the season. Herbert finishes the season with 16 carries for 52 yards and only three targets in the passing game. A free agent in 2026, Herbert will continue to bounce around the league looking for an opportunistic depth chart opening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Jets RB Breece Hall (knee) is questionable to play in Week 18 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: When asked if Hall will play, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said, “we’ll see.” Glenn has played coy with most start-sit decisions in the Jets’ 3-13 season. No reason to stop now. Hall logged just two limited sessions to close the week. He is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the season. Preserving his health for free agency could be the smart move. He may wish to put his stamp on the season with a strong showing, though. It would be difficult to project his playing time if he is active. Treat him as a volatile RB2 if he suits up. His backup, RB Isaiah Davis (concussion), has been ruled out, leaving Kene Nwangwu (quad) and Khalil Herbert behind Hall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Jets RB Isaiah Davis (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: It’s looking unlikely that Davis will be cleared for Week 18 given the lack of practice — it suggests he’s still in the beginning stages of the protocol. If he rests, Khalil Herbert will likely see backup reps behind Breece Hall against the Bills on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Jets RB Isaiah Davis (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: Starting RB Breece Hall (knee) was also sidelined by a knee injury, though he told reporters post-game that his knee is fine. Whether he can play on Sunday remains to be seen. Jets RB Kene Nwangwu (quad) is listed as the next man up, with RB Khalil Herbert seated behind him on the depth chart. Nwangwu is practicing fully.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.headline: Jets RB Breece Hall (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-her.analysis: Hall told reporters that his knee was fine post-game. Hopefully, this is just a maintenance day, but his practice participation is worth following. His backup, RB Isaiah Davis (concussion), was also sidelined on Wednesday. The Jets list RBs Kene Nwangwu (quad) and Khalil Herbert in the Nos. 3 and 4 spots, respectively. Nwangwu is practicing fully.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 15 times for 68 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason did not start for the Vikings, but out-touched and out-snapped Aaron Jones. He was the primary early-down back and saw two targets as well, though he did not catch either of them. Jones (knee) exited the game in the fourth quarter, leading to Mason finishing out the game for the Vikings. Even before the Jones injury, Mason was the the back with the highest utilization. Mason is a low-end fantasy RB2 heading into a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions; he could emerge as a top-15 option if Jones misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings activated Mason off injured reserve and he is officially active for the first time since suffering a thumb injury in Week 1. He will split backfield touches with Aaron Jones, with Jones likely getting more of the passing-down work and Mason more the early-down work. Mason is a fantasy RB3 in his return. The Vikings declared S Jakobe Thomas, QB Max Brosmer, CB Chuck Demmings, RB Demond Claiborne, DL Elijah Willliams and OT Caleb Tiernan inactive for Week 7 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Vikings plan to activate Jordan Mason (thumb) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason came into the season as the presumed lead back in a timeshare with Aaron Jones, the latter of whom has performed as a true workhorse in Mason’s absence. Although it could take a week or two for Mason to fully regain the lead back role, his presence significantly mutes the potential of Jones. Expect a near-even split when the Vikings take on the Colts in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason practiced in full all week. He seemingly has good odds of suiting up, but sometimes NFL teams will give players extra time off when they are returning from injured reserve. If Mason plays this weekend, he should be able to handle his normal lead-rushing role. In that case, he can be started as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason is firmly on track to play in Week 7 against the Colts. He should tentatively be expected to lead the backfield in carries right away, with Aaron Jones potentially settling into a 1B role. The Colts’ defense is not an imposing unit, so both running backs are FLEX-viable this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings designated Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: His 21-day practice window will open; most of the reporting is that the Vikings expect him to play in Week 7. Assuming that’s the case, we expect to see him hit the ground running on the Wednesday practice report with at least a limited session and perhaps a full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes the Vikings could target a running back with ‘home-run burst’ in a move for the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Lewis connects the Vikings to Chargers backs Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as well as Tennessee’s Tony Pollard, Tampa Bay’s Kenneth Gainwell, and Arizona’s Tyler Allgeier. These are just whispers at the moment, but any kind of costly trade acquisition would cut into the playing time and fantasy value of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. The Vikings have clearly already been shuffling depth pieces around so we believe there could be more urgency there as the trade deadline gets closer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Vikings “hope” to get Jordan Mason (thumb) back from injured reserve for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Late last week, Fowler’s colleague, Kevin Seifert, reported that Mason is expected to return in Week 7 as well. Add him if he is available. Mason is not involved much as a receiver, but his expected rushing workload makes him a reliable FLEX with RB2 upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Kevin Seifert reports Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) is expected to return for Minnesota’s Week 7 game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings play the Saints this week, then go on bye in Week 6, so Aaron Jones has one more massive workload week ahead of him against New Orleans before the backfield heads back to a split. Mason looked good in the early going and, if he was cut loose in a shallow league, makes a worthwhile pickup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings placed RB Jordan Mason on injured reserve with a thumb injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: That escalated quickly. On Monday, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Mason’s “sore thumb” was being evaluated. Apparently, it had sustained a small fracture, which has now been “fixed,” ostensibly surgically, given O’Connell’s phrasing. Short-term injured reserve placement requires players to miss four games, but the Vikings are on bye in Week 6, so Mason will be eligible to return in Week 7. Mason led the backfield with 15 carries in Week 1, so his absence provides RB Aaron Jones with a touch-count boost. Veteran RB DeeJay Dallas operated as the RB3. Rookie RB Demond Claiborne was inactive last week, but should be active in Week 2 against the Lions. Speculatively stashing him could be worthwhile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 137 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
Zay Flowers caught 6-of-11 targets for 66 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers has yet to find the end zone in back-to-back games with Tyler Huntley under center, but the 10 targets per game he has averaged over that span is still encouraging. Flowers led the Ravens in targets by a wide margin in this week’s loss, with his biggest play coming on a 31-yard reception in the third quarter. Scoring opportunities were scarce in this one, as the Ravens managed just 10 points on their first two drives and were shut out for the rest of the game. Flowers will be in the WR1 conversation next week against the Bengals if Lamar Jackson (ankle) makes the start, but would be more of a WR2 if Huntley gets the nod for a third straight week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Perhaps feeling a bit wistful after spending a little of every week of the season on the injury report, Flowers got re-added Thursday with a limited session. He was limited again on Friday but is expected to play. There’s no further word on how serious this toe injury was, but he’s doing enough on the field in his limited time so far this year that nobody is seriously benching Flowers anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers played through a foot injury last week, catching 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards and rushing once for 13 yards. This injury could be related, but we really don’t know. Flowers’ productivity took a hit with Tyler Huntley running the offense last week. Huntley is currently in line to start again, though Lamar Jackson’s (ankle) status is still up in the air. If the toe injury limits Flowers, that further complicates things, but he still must be started if active. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 13 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was largely confined to short area work with Tyler Huntley under center and also saw a 26-yard reception erased from his ledger due to a 29-yard pass interference penalty on the play. It was a weird situation in which the penalty yardage was greater than his reception. Fantasy managers might be forced to continue waiting on the return of Lamar Jackson after it was reported this week that the All Pro starter could be forced to miss another week. Flowers is a locked-in WR2 against the Browns in Week 6 with Huntley under center and an elite WR1 should Jackson return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, OLB Trey Hendrickson, C Cam Jurgens, G Andrew Vorhees, WR Elijah Sarratt, and DT Aeneas Peebles inactive for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Jackson had already been ruled out earlier in the week and reportedly could be looking at a multi-game absence due to an ankle injury suffered before halftime in Week 4. Tyler Huntley will start under center for the Ravens as they look to subdue the momentum of the Falcons, who have won both games started by Michael Penix. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is officially active for Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Zay Flowers (foot) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was limited in practice throughout the week but never appeared at risk of missing Sunday night’s game. The bigger issue for him will be the absence of Lamar Jackson. Flowers has been the most efficient receiver in the league on a per-route basis this year. That will come back to Earth sans Jackson, but he remains on the WR1/2 border, even with Tyler Huntley under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (foot) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 5 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers got in three limited sessions while dealing with the foot injury. He loses ceiling with Tyler Huntley under center, but remains a rock solid low-end WR1 in terms of how much volume he amasses in this passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers appears well on track to play this week after two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday. His ceiling will probably take a small hit with Lamar Jackson out, but he remains the only game in town in Baltimore and should still have WR1 viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was not present during the portion of practice open to the media earlier today, though it was assumed that this was a maintenance issue relating to his multi-week hamstring strain. It turns out Flowers is dealing with a new injury. It is unclear when the injury occurred. If it was an in-game issue last week, then beginning Week 5 with a limited practice is a great sign for his availability. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 20 times for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson did add 59 yards receiving on five catches to help salvage his fantasy day, but this is the third straight week he has delivered a modest fantasy return after explosive performances in Weeks 3 and 4. In fact, this is now five of seven games this season that Robinson has been held under 90 yards rushing. He’s contributing as a pass-catcher, and he looks elusive when he can get beyond the line of scrimmage, but the Falcons may need to make an adjustment on offense with defenses clearly keying on stopping Robinson. We’d expect them to focus on getting him going next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson had nine rushes for 61 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for -8 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson couldn’t get anything going against a Chicago defense allowing the fifth highest rate of yards before contact. The Bears were intent on snuffing out the Atlanta rushing attack and forcing Michael Penix to move the ball through the air. It worked for much of the game. Robinson, who had 425 rushing yards in his previous three games, remains the engine of the run-heavy Falcons offense and should get back on track in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 17 times for 86 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens, adding 32 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson suffered through poor offensive efficiency in the first half, finally breaking loose for a 38-yard carry on the team’s first possession of the third quarter. Although the receiving production and yardage total were enough to salvage a usable fantasy week, it was only the second time in five games in which Robinson failed to find the end zone. Robinson remains an elite fantasy RB1 ahead of a Week 6 showdown against the Bears in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints, adding two yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Week 4 marked Robinson’s second consecutive game going over 100 yards with two touchdowns on the ground, this time aided by a 59-yard touchdown run on his first touch of the game. The Falcons tied a franchise record with five rushing scores, with backfield mate Brian Robinson adding three to the two of Bijan. The return of quarterback Michael Penix has given the Falcons the threat of passing after dropping their first two games of the season behind suboptimal play from the position, and nobody has benefited more from reduced numbers in the box than Robinson. He’ll look to keep the momentum going as a top-tier RB1 when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson single-handedly out-gained the Packers in the first half after clearing the century mark on the ground early in the second quarter. His patience and burst through the gap were on full display, routinely gaining chunk yardage on first down while making the Green Bay defensive front look like Swiss cheese. A 55-yard scamper on a wide zone carry in the first quarter got the All Pro back off to a blazing start, adding his first of two touchdowns to cap the drive. He would take on a second score late in the fourth quarter to send the Packers to their first home opener loss in 14 years. Robinson remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the division rival Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 16 times for 72 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson did what he could in the midst of a Cooper Rush meltdown, but it’s hard to expect much when his team puts up a grand total of three points. Atlanta also pulled their starters early, allowing Brian Robinson Jr. to rack up 13 touches of his own. Robinson is a volume-based RB1 even when Rush is under center, and he’ll move back into the top three once Michael Penix takes over. That could happen next week versus the Packers on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 21 times for 83 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers, adding 90 yards receiving and one touchdown on eight catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: To say Bijan Robinson was the majority of the team’s offense would be an understatement. He had 173 of the team’s 238 total yards and 29 of the 43 touches by any skill player. He played on 47 of the team’s 61 total snaps and only lost carries to Brian Robinson because the team couldn’t possibly continue to ride Bijan Robinson any more than they were. His involvement in the short passing game, especially given who will be at quarterback, makes Bijan Robinson seemingly matchup-proof for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Team reporter Will McFadden reports the Falcons could increase their number of gap- and power-style run plays, while also using RB Bijan Robinson more in the screen game this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: McFadden notes that Robinson had more outside runs than any other player last season. He believes new Falcons OC Tommy Rees and new OL coach Bill Callahan are focused on diversifying the run game tactics by adding a north-south approach. He thinks Falcons running backs “should benefit from a penetrating approach oriented around getting them into second-level space quickly.” McFadden also checked in with Robinson, who said Rees is implementing new screen game concepts, derived from his time with the Browns. Last year in Cleveland, Rees’ offense racked up 413 yards via the screen game, ranking second in the NFL. Adding more ways to get Robinson the ball in space only solidifies his status as the overall RB2 in fantasy drafts this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Falcons signed Bijan Robinson to a three-year contract extension worth up to $75 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: The deal includes a whopping $51 million in guarantees. Robinson becomes the highest-paid running back in NFL history, surpassing Saquon Barkely. Under the new deal, Robinson, 24, will make $22.25 million per year, according to ESPN. This ends Robinson’s brief hold-in at Falcons training camp. Robinson over his first three NFL seasons has totaled 5,648 yards and 34 touchdowns as the centerpiece of the Atlanta offense. That won’t change under new head coach Kevin Stefanski, who has talked up Robinson’s pass-catching ability this offseason. Robinson should be among the first two picks in every fantasy format this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 148 yards and one touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
Tee Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins saw just four targets against the Dolphins after seeing 16 targets in Week 4. The adductor/neck injuries didn’t limit his playing time as much, seeing 45 snaps on the day, No. 2 among Bengals receivers. With Ja’Marr Chase back on the field, Higgins’ target volume decreased considerably and he totaled just 22 yards in a more run-favorable game script. Despite the dud, Higgins still belongs in the WR2 ranks and gets a mediocre Ravens defense in Week 7 after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins is active for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins suffered an adductor injury in Week 4 against the Jaguars and was a full practice participant Friday after DNPs the two days before. Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) both declared active. Though NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports he will play mostly “meaningful plays”, Higgins is in the WR2 ranks while Chase is back in the WR1 ranks this week. The Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries, WR Colbie Young, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will also play. Higgins is likely suiting up at less than full strength, but fantasy managers have to keep him in their lineups versus a Miami defense that is giving up explosive passing plays at the second-highest rate in the league this year. He will be a boom/bust WR2 for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is questionable for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins missed the first two practices of the week but practiced in full on Friday. We would consider him to be truly questionable given his one day of practice, meaning fantasy managers will want to check his official game status when the team announces inactives 90 minutes before kickoff. If he can’t go, Dohnte Meyers, who saw nine targets last week, could be on the fantasy radar as a WR4 in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Chase still needs to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to suit up for Week 5’s game against the Dolphins. That said, he appears to be trending toward being able to play after logging back-to-back practices to close out the week. Tee Higgins (groin/neck), who was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday was also seen sprinting and running routes on Friday, which suggests he could also be good to go for Sunday’s game. We will check back in with official game day statuses in the coming hours when the team releases its final injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins is sporting a T-shirt and shorts at today’s practice. We expect to see him listed as a non-participant at the end of the day. Consecutive absences put him on the wrong side of questionable for the Bengals’ Week 5 game against the Dolphins, though he still has at least a small chance of turning things around tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor told reporters before practice that Higgins would be listed as limited. Not only did he not practice, but the team listed him with a neck injury on top of his adductor issue. He went down with the adductor injury late in Cincy’s Week 4 loss to the Jags. It’s unclear when the neck issue cropped up. With multiple injuries holding him out of practice, Higgins looks unlikely to play in Week 5. With Ja’Marr Chase potentially out as well, Dohnte Meyers could be Joe Burrow No. 1 receiver this week. He should be added in all fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins went down with the injury in the fourth quarter of Week 4. He tried to play through it but ultimately ended the game on the sidelines. A limited practice today is a good sign for his Week 5 availability. That will be doubly important with Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) also questionable for Sunday’s game. If Chase can’t clear protocol in time, Higgins will operate as the Bengals’ No. 1 receiver. Even at less than full strength, he would be a fringe WR1 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Tee Higgins (adductor) is day-to-day and that the team is not ruling him out for Cincinnati’s Week 5 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Taylor said that the team would see where he is at this week. It sounds like the practice reports will loom large for Higgins ahead of next Sunday’s game. Dohnte Meyers took on a big role in the absence of Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) Sunday and could have even more of a runway if both Higgins and Chase are sidelined this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-8 targets for 25 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston was third in targets among Browns pass catchers and saw lots and lots of air yards from Deshaun Watson, who nearly connected with Boston for two long touchdowns on the day. So it goes with a high-variance downfield option like Boston, who now has three straight quiet outings. With a 45 percent air yards share headed into Week 7, Boston will certainly have his big box scores in the coming weeks. Predicting when that might happen will be tough for fantasy managers. He should be a flex play in Week 8 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be on the WR3 line in a good matchup against the Titans. Boston finally had a clunker last week against Baltimore, but he’s been remarkably consistent otherwise and should find easier footing against Tennessee’s rough back seven.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: The Browns’ rookie field-stretcher played through his foot injury last week against the Ravens, posting just a 1/15 receiving line. Ostensibly, the foot is bothering him, but he still has a chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Titans. Hopefully, Boston upgrades to full participation tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston played through the injury last week, catching just 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards. The foot injury could be bugging him. Fortunately, he did not appear to suffer any setbacks. Boston is a WR3/FLEX against the Titans in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: This was the worst game of Boston’s young career. After going for 40-plus yards in his first five games to start the season, the promising rookie was blanketed in coverage all afternoon and managed just one reception as a result. Boston may have had a chance at scoring were it not for a pass near the right side of the end zone sailing too far out of bounds for him to bring both feet down, but scoring opportunities were hard to come by in this one. Boston will be back on the fantasy radar as a WR3 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be a usable WR3 against the Ravens this week. Boston has returned at least 41 yards in every start this year while hitting a deep gain seemingly weekly. The 22-year-old should be Cleveland’s No. 1 target again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Of the (many) Browns in real danger of missing this week’s game against the Ravens, Boston seems to be in the best shape of actually playing. Still, it is two limited sessions in two tries and we wouldn’t be surprised if he wound up with a questionable tag on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: A limited practice to start the week is usually nothing more than maintenance. Boston should still be a safe bet to suit up on Sunday. The second-round rookie has already cemented himself as an impressive downfield threat with three touchdowns and three catches of 40+ yards. He’s managed several spike weeks despite the Browns’ up-and-down performances on offense. Health permitting, Boston will be a low-end WR3 for Week 6 versus Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-7 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston’s score was his third in five games as a pro. This one was a 29-yard strike down the left sideline where Boston won a 1-on-1 matchup with CB Brandon Stephens. Boston’s yardage totals are not popping off the page in this limited offense, but his play-making ability has been. He has also reached at least 40 yards all five times out, giving him a non-zero floor. The rookie second-rounder continues to press his WR3 case heading into Week 6 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 4-of-7 targets for 89 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston has now led the Browns in receiving in three of the team’s first four games, made more impressive by the fact that those were the first four contests of the youngster’s professional career. The second-round rookie continues to flash big play potential after catching his third pass of 46 yards or longer, this time unable to find the end zone after scoring twice in his first two games. Boston still has room to grow considering he has seen just 22 targets in the first month of the season, and could reward fantasy managers that invested late-round picks in his services handsomely in the second half of his rookie year. He’ll be an upside FLEX option against the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix Jr. completed 25-of-34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ 29-20, Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The stats may make it seem like Penix had his way with the 49ers, but it didn’t seem like a seamless performance in reality. He missed some deep passes and overthrew Drake London on a clear touchdown in the second half. He really wasn’t able to get much going down the field, but the Falcons’ defense forced four turnovers, which set up some short fields that Penix was able to take advantage of. He gets a good matchup against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 19-of-33 for 225 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix was a mess in the first half, missing Drake London on what should have been an walk-in 30-yard touchdown. The Falcons abandoned the run game in the second half, facing a three touchdown deficit, and Penix threw three touchdowns in hurry-up mode. Taking five sacks on the day, Penix targeted London and Jahan Dotson heavily, connecting with Dotson on a nicely thrown 41-yard gain in the second half. This was the first multiple-TD game of Penix’s season. He’ll be a low-ceiling superflex play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is active for Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix was able to practice this week and will start for Atlanta in a potentially high scoring game against the Bears. Penix should be considered a streaming option in most formats. Falcons declared QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB C.J. Henderson, DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, LB Christian Harris, OL Ethan Onianwa, and DE Drake Jackson inactive against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix has been removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was reported the day after the Falcons’ overtime loss to the Ravens that there was “optimism” that Penix would start in Week 6. After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice, he seemed like a lock to be ready to go by Sunday, so Friday’s news isn’t all that unexpected. Penix has thrown for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception this season, throwing one touchdown in each of his first three games. He’ll be on the fantasy radar in 2QB/Superflex leagues against a Bears defense that has allowed just two top-12 fantasy finishes to opposing QBs this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is great news for the Falcons’ offense, which can barely function with Tua Tagovailoa at the helm. Penix is firmly on track to play in Week 6 against the Bears, as long as he gets through the week setback-free. Penix can be viewed as a high-end QB2 with four teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “We’ll see how he’s feeling,” head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters Wednesday morning, adding that Penix should be able to play through the injury. Even if it’s a limited practice session for Penix, it’s good news for his Week 6 availability following his Sunday night rib injury against the Ravens. Penix, operating under center at a much higher rate than last season, is among the most efficient quarterbacks in the league through Week 5. If Penix is out, Tua Tagovailoa would represent a major downgrade for all Atlanta pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports there’s “optimism” that Michael Penix (ribs) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix said after Sunday’s loss that he didn’t believe his injury would be long-term. He was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa in overtime because of his injury, but he also added that he likely would have gone back on the field had the Falcons received the ball to start the extra quarter. Instead, Penix said his pain worsened the longer he sat, which was why he ultimately didn’t go back in. Penix’s status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he can’t start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would be in line to start his first game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) said he doesn’t believe his injury will be a long-term issue.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix will undergo an MRI on Monday to confirm the severity of his injury, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing much time. Penix exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday night’s game against the Ravens and was forced to stay on the sideline in overtime to watch Tua Tagovailoa throw the game-losing interception shortly after the Ravens scored the go-ahead touchdown. Penix threw for 240 yards and a touchdown and has been solid in his three games since returning from injury. If he’s not able to start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would presumably draw the start at home against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Falcons QB Michael Penix (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix took the full brunt of a brutal hit to the midsection late in the fourth quarter of Week 5 against the Ravens. He would leave for one play due to the medical timeout, return for one play, and then retreat to the sideline. Tua Tagovailoa came on in relief in overtime, with the team designating Penix questionable to return with an injury to his ribs. Penix completed 19-of-32 passes for 240 yards and one touchdown prior to departing, adding eight yards on two carries. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his practice status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 15-of-20 passes for 223 yards and one touchdown in the Falcons’ 45-24, Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix wasn’t asked to do much with his arm as the Falcons tied a franchise record with five rushing scores, but the threat of consistent and reliable passing has done wonders for a Falcons offense that looked lost through two games behind poor quarterback play. It also doesn’t hurt when your All Pro running back goes for a 59-yard touchdown on his first touch of the game. The Falcons were never threatened by an underperforming Saints team after jumping out to a 14-point lead in the first quarter. Penix has yet to be called on for increased passing volume through two starts, something that could change, pending the health of Lamar Jackson, in Week 5 when they host the Ravens. Penix remains a middling QB2 and does not warrant starting in all formats outside of two-quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 8-of-10 targets for 129 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding three rushes for 23 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: The Browns slot man shredded the Tennessee secondary from start to finish. Coming into the game with a season-high of 64 receiving yards, Concepcion eclipsed that mark in the second quarter and didn’t look back. He continually shed tacklers against a low-effort Titans defense and functioned as the centerpiece of the Cleveland passing game. He led the Browns in targets, mostly seeing designed short-area throws from Deshaun Watson. In a Browns offense with a top-10 neutral pass rate, Concepcion should be a weekly top-36 option in PPR formats. He’ll get the Steelers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion should be treated as a PPR WR3/WR4 tweener this week in a good matchup against the Titans. With Denzel Boston also active, we likely won’t be seeing any major explosions here. Concepcion-reliant managers would accept any explosion at this point as he’s found it hard to crack 50 receiving yards so far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: The Browns’ short-area target earner is banged up, but he still has a chance to play in Week 7 against the Titans. Ideally, Concepcion will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If he remains limited, he may end up being listed with a questionable tag. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: The rookie wide receiver has been awfully banged up over the past two weeks. He suffered a concussion in Week 5, yet managed to play in Week 6. Unfortunately, he did not leave the contest unscathed, picking up two lower-body injuries. Hopefully, he resumes practicing fully tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 4-of-6 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens, adding two carries for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion’s six targets led all Browns players, while his 37 receiving yards were good for second-most behind Jerry Jeudy. Concepcion’s biggest play of the game came on a 17-yard reception in the third quarter that helped set up the Browns’ first scoring drive of the afternoon. Concepcion had a red zone carry inside the Ravens’ 10-yard line that resulted in only a one-yard gain, but it’s always good to see his coaches trusting him in the valuable areas of the field. We are still waiting on his first breakout game, but the volume continues to be encouraging. Concepcion will be a fringe WR3/WR4 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: Browns coach Todd Monken said KC Concepcion (concussion) has cleared protocol and will play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion will have some low-end WR3/FLEX appeal with four teams on bye in PPR leagues. He simply hasn’t been able to find much space with his opportunities so far, with two 25-yard catches and 16 other catches that went for just 99 yards in his first five weeks of action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: He’s still in concussion protocol, but it looks like he’ll have at least some chance of clearing before Sunday’s game against the Ravens. Concepcion would struggle to be more than a FLEX option here even if healthy, so fantasy managers should probably look at alternatives this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (concussion) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: It’s a remarkable turn after Concepcion was knocked out cold on the field in Week 5 against the Jets. If Concepcion is able to practice in the coming days he should be active for Week 6 against the Ravens. The rookie leads the Cleveland offense with a 23 percent target per route rate, used primarily as a gadget player near the line of scrimmage. He would be a flex option in PPR formats if he suits up against Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion suffered a concussion in the first quarter of the Browns’ Week 5 game against the Jets and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Making a spinning first quarter grab, Concepcion took a high hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick, who was flagged for a personal foul. It was the kind of hit the NFL is trying to legislate out of the game, but it wasn’t necessarily dirty. It was extremely unfortunate, as Concepcion did appear to be briefly out cold. He thankfully made his way to his feet and to the locker room unassisted, but he was ruled out before even undergoing a formal evaluation. He will now be highly questionable for Week 6 against the Ravens. Concepcion’s loss will mean more routes for beleaguered Jerry Jeudy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion continues to operate as the primary slot receiver for a Browns team clearly looking to their youth while phasing out veteran Jerry Jeudy, the latter of whom managed three receptions on three targets for 36 yards. Concepcion has yet to lead the team in receiving while working in a short area role, with this the first game thus far which he has gained more then 43 yards. He’ll be a difficult start in fantasy circles when the Browns take on the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 5-of-6 targets for 115 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper was an electric deep threat once again, bringing down catches for 60 and 52 yards, neither of which was his touchdown. He scored shortly after the 52-yard grab by lining up as a running back and cruising past his defender for an easy three-yard touchdown reception. Cooper Jr. is the first rookie in franchise history with back-to-back games with 100+ receiving yards and a touchdown. While we can’t say he has overtaken Garrett Wilson already, this is looking like, at worst, a co-WR1 situation. Cooper will flirt with a WR2 ranking when he takes on the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 6-of-7 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 1, the No. 30 overall pick shook off his ankle issue by recording the first 100-yard outing of his now two-game career. It was a much needed effort with No. 1 Garrett Wilson getting tangled up in Christian Gonzalez’s coverage. The highlight was a 48-yard touchdown where Cooper got behind the entire defense then came back to an underthrown deep ball for six. This was after he had a shorter touchdown called back by a dubious Tim Patrick OPI penalty. Now firmly in the mix for No. 2 status even when Adonai Mitchell comes back from his seemingly never-ending finger injury, Cooper is worth rostering in a majority of fantasy leagues with injuries mounting and bye weeks raging. The Jets have a plus Week 7 matchup in the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Up for the first time since Week 1, Cooper should immediately slide in as the Jets’ No. 2 wideout with Adonai Mitchell (finger) still somehow on the shelf. He’s a dart throw WR4 for a contest where the Jets should be playing from behind. Joining Mitchell on the shelf for Gang Green are RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LG Dylan Parham, DT Jack Heflin and EDGE Joseph Ossai.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week, but is officially set to return after logging a full practice on Friday. The rookie receiver could step into an immediate role for the Jets with Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for at least one more week, but he could still be a few weeks away from fantasy relevance. Cooper played on just five snaps in Week 1 before his injury, but did catch one pass for 30 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets opened the 21-day practice window for Omar Cooper (ankle).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper has been on injured reserve since sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 1. He could return as soon as this week against the Patriots, though he could see his snaps and routes limited. Cooper can be rostered in deeper 12-team formats. Garrett Wilson’s domination of the New York passing offense makes it tough for anyone else to post fantasy-relevant numbers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets placed WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Cooper is going on injured reserve for an ankle sprain. He’ll be sidelined for at least four games with a designation to return. Rapoport mentions that Cooper should be back “shortly.” Cooper could still make an impact in the second half of his rookie season, but he isn’t worth holding in most fantasy formats at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: This was always expected to be the case, but head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday, while speaking with the media, that Cooper, RB/KR Kene Nwangwu (back), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), and EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) will all miss Sunday’s game against the Packers. It was reported earlier this week that the Jets are hoping to have Cooper back “within the next four weeks,” so it wouldn’t be surprising if he also missed Week 3’s game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is “week to week, with the hope that he returns within the next four weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The phrasing at the end of that sentence makes it clear the Jets are pondering not sending him to injured reserve. Fantasy managers who took the plunge in non-dynasty leagues do not necessarily have to hold on to Cooper through the early weeks if something catches their eye on the wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that Jets WR Omar Cooper is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Pelissero also reported that Cooper will undergo an MRI to further assess the injury on Monday, confirming NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport’s report from earlier this evening. Cooper could be looking at a multi-week absence, but only time will tell. Hopefully, it is just a mild injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 27-of-40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the 49ers’ 29-20, Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: After losing seemingly every wide receiver to injury, it was only a matter of time before we finally had a down Purdy game. The truth is, he didn’t even play poorly. His first interception was on a pass that he was trying to throw away when safety Jesse Bates made an incredible toe-drag interception. The second pick was on a really nice play by linebacker Kendal Daniels over the middle. Purdy looked good and gave his team a chance to win despite a depleted offense. The 49ers will have a bye next week and then hopefully get back at least one of their primary receivers before a Week 9 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-29 passes for 264 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ 23-17, Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 28 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers absolutely dominated the first two quarters, gaining 303 yards of total offense on 41 plays before the break.
