The situation would alter course in a hurry after Purdy lost his top option through the air in the final minute of the second quarter as Mike Evans departed with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable entering the game. The team would go on to gain only 72 additional yards after the intermission, allowing the Commanders the ability to claw their way back into the game in the fourth quarter. Even so, Purdy now holds the NFL record for highest career passer rating after qualifying for the statistic with his 1,500th pass attempt in the win, which pushes the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 record ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Falcons before their bye the following week. Purdy remains a surefire QB1 against the pass-funnel Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the 49ers’ 32-29, Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers made the most of several short fields in this one. After an interception by Sam Darnold on the Seahawks’ first drive of the game, Purdy led a short 18-yard drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans to give the Niners an early lead. Purdy would orchestrate a long scoring drive in the fourth quarter, completing seven passes for 89 yards, with his final completion resulting in a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. The Seahawks became the first team to sack Purdy this season, bringing him down three times in the backfield in the second half, but Purdy was able to evade pressure for the entire second half. Purdy and the Niners get a juicy Week 6 matchup next Monday against the Commanders, where he will profile as a solid QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-30 attempts for 218 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos, adding ten rushes for 29 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy’s ten rushing attempts were a season high, and the product of Denver’s secondary blanketing Niners pass catchers for much of the game. Injuries to both starting Broncos corners eventually loosened things up for Purdy and the 49ers. He connected with George Kittle on a fourth quarter screen pass that went for a 58-yard score — the biggest play of the game. Purdy, who now has 11 touchdown passes through four games, is a weekly top-10 fantasy play even on his less-than-efficient days. He gets a tough matchup against Seattle in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 15-of-27 passes for 297 yards and four touchdowns in the 49ers’ 36-30, Week 3 win over the Cardinals, adding two carries for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers offense had another fruitful fantasy day despite injuries haunting the team once again. Purdy showcased his mobility and athleticism, often making throws on the run and scrambling out of pressure. His first score was a completion to Mike Evans, who lateraled it to Deebo Samuel for the score. Purdy then threw a more traditional touchdown to Evans later in the first half, then threw two scores to George Kittle to seal the game in the second half. Despite losing Evans and LT Trent Williams by the third quarter, Purdy was still able to gash the Cardinals defense and surpass 300 total yards. Though the offense keeps losing pieces, Purdy in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme is a fantasy QB1 until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 20-of-22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns in a 35-13, Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding 30 yards rushing and a touchdown on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The Dolphins’ defense didn’t put up much of a fight, but Purdy was tremendous in this one. He bought extra time in the pocket when he needed to, made plays with his legs if the opportunities were there, and found open receivers over the middle of the field all game long. He may find the going a little bit tougher next week against the Cardinals, but probably not much. The bigger question will be who else can step up in the receiver room with Demarcus Robinson leaving this game with an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 25-of-34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception in the 49ers’ 27-7, Week 1 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy also added 29 yards on his five attempts. The veteran signal-caller did throw a terrible interception, but outside of that pick he played exceptionally well; even if most of his completions were for short yardage. All three passing scores came to different players, with his best throw being a perfectly placed touchdown to Deebo Samuel between two Rams’ defenders to cement the blowout. Purdy will look to keep it going in Week 2, and gets a friendly matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that 49ers QB Brock Purdy said he is “prepared to use his mobility more this year if needed.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers’ quarterback is not a straight-line burner, but he is more agile than he is given credit for. Purdy adds that he won’t constantly be looking for opportunities to run, however, he believes he can help the offense by scrambling for 10-12 yards from time to time. Purdy has racked up 113 carries over the past two NFL seasons, including the playoffs, proving himself an efficient scrambler with a 47.8 percent conversion rate that ranks first among quarterbacks with at least 50 attempts. He’s a borderline QB1/2. Scrambling more often could get him into the weekly low-end QB1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: 49ers added $300,000 in incentives to Mac Jones’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Jones, who could have started elsewhere this season if the Niners had found a trading partner, will now make $3.55 million in 2026, with another $2.25 million available in incentives. Jones will be a free agent after the 2026 season. The Niners reportedly wanted a first-round draft pick in exchange for Jones. The veteran threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions last season over eight games as the Niners’ starter. Jones in 2025 was tenth in EPA per drop back, just behind Sam Darnold and Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Vikings will face the 49ers in Mexico City on November 22.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The Kyler Murray experiment should be well underway by late November as Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings look to recover from their failed dalliance with J.J. McCarthy as the team’s starting quarterback. Murray will lead a quietly loaded Minnesota offense against Kyle Shanahan’s EPA-maximizing Niners offense. The last time Brock Purdy faced the Vikings defense he threw for 319 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in a Week 2 2024 loss. Purdy took a season-high six sacks in that game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard had 25 rushes for 129 yards and three touchdowns in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard, whose last big game before Sunday was against these same Browns in 2025, scored two first quarter touchdowns against a Cleveland rush defense that seemed uninterested in tackling Pollard. He scored a third rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter, and could have had a fourth score if not for a Browns goal line stand. Pollard has seen big workloads with Tyjae Spears (knee) sidelined but hadn’t done much with the opportunity before Sunday. The Titans offense operated quickly, using no-huddle through much of the game. That created more play volume that benefited Pollard and the rest of the Titans offense. As long as Spears remains sidelined, Pollard should remain in 12-team lineups next week against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was targeted only once, finishing without a reception. Pollard has somewhat surprisingly banished No. 2 Tyjae Spears to pure breather back status, but the Titans’ overall play volume and touchdown opportunities are so limited that he is still struggling to achieve weekly RB2 status. He has nevertheless shored up his RB3/FLEX floor. That is where you will find him in the Week 7 ranks against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 14 times for 52 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard looks like he could be a legitimate NFL running back somewhere, but it sure can’t happen on this offense. He’s cleared 14 carries and 48 yards in each of his last four games and has just one touchdown to show for it. It’s fringe low-end RB2 land for Pollard, as usual, against the Colts next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard will take on the 0-4 Texans, who have had some trouble handling the run, and should be a viable low-end RB2 this week. He continues to get Wednesday vet days while dealing with this foot injury, but doesn’t seem to be in any real danger of missing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: During Weeks 3-4, Pollard took Wednesdays off, rehabbing an ankle injury. He would resume practicing on Thursday and suit up on Sunday. Now, with his new foot issue, he appears to be on the same practice plan. Expect him to play in Week 5 against the Texans. Pollard was a full participant on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: The Titans have given Pollard Wednesday off in back-to-back weeks. He was removed from the injury report entirely on Friday both times. This week should be no different. Pollard has 39 touches over the past two weeks. Even on a struggling Titans offense, that’s enough work to put him on the RB2/3 border for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 16 times for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens, adding two catches for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was wildly inefficient in this one, but saved his fantasy day when he scored a three-yard touchdown in the first quarter to give the Titans their first points of the day. It was the first touchdown of the season for Pollard, who continues to serve as the Titans’ primary back, but there’s not much fantasy upside to be had here. Pollard will be a boom-or-bust RB3 next week against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Tony Pollard “fits the profile” of a player who could be traded ahead of the deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Schefter didn’t cite any sources telling him that Pollard could be on the move, but he did connect a few key dots. Pollard is in the final year of his contract and the Titans are going nowhere fast. If they don’t plan on re-signing him next offseason, they might as well get something in return for him in the middle of another lost season. His departure would also clear the way for rookie Nick Singleton to see more work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: With Titans RB2 Tyjae Spears (ankle) questionable to play, Pollard could end up handling a big workload. Unfortunately, the Titans field an unproductive offense and face the Ravens this week. He can only be viewed as a moderate FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 23-of-34 passes for 298 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens’ 35-13, Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: This makes it two-straight games where Huntley and the Ravens failed to score in the second half. Huntley was solid in the first half, throwing for 227-1-0 on 21 passes, with his lone touchdown pass coming on a 48-yard screen pass to Zay Flowers on the Ravens’ opening drive. He would lead the Ravens on two drives that ended in field goals in the second quarter, but the Ravens struggled mightily in the second half as the Bengals rallied for 35 unanswered points. At one point, Huntley had the Ravens in position for a short field goal to go up 16-14, but passed on the points and opted to go for it on fourth-and-two, which resulted in an incomplete pass to tight end Josh Cuevas. It was reported during the game that Lamar Jackson (ankle) would be back for Week 8’s game against the Ravens. Now sitting at 4-3 on the year, it goes without saying that the Ravens are in desperate need of Jackson in what is shaping up to be a highly competitive AFC North division.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 19-of-31 passes for 165 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens’ 13-10, Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley led the Ravens on a 10-play drive that ended with a two-yard touchdown pass to tight end Josh Cuevas to start the game. On the Ravens’ second drive, Huntley and Cuevas would connect on a 29-yard pass, only for that drive to end in a field goal to put the Ravens up 10-0 early. Unfortunately for Huntley and the Ravens, that would be all the scoring they would manage, as they were kept off the board for the remainder of the game thanks to a stout Browns defense that managed to sack Huntley three times and force a turnover from Derrick Henry. This was far different than last week’s start against the Falcons, when Huntley was responsible for three total touchdowns, and a reminder of the high-variance play we have come to expect from him. With the Ravens now sitting at 4-2 on the season, they will hopefully have Lamar Jackson (ankle) back under center next week when they play host to the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Jackson will miss a second straight game with his ankle injury despite reports at the beginning of the week that said he had a “realistic” chance to play in Week 6. It was also reported after the team’s overtime win against the Falcons that Lamar was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5. Jackson and the Ravens will now set their sights on having him ready to go in Week 7 at home against the Bengals, while Tyler Huntley will draw the start this week against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: All signs are pointing to Tyler Huntley making his second straight start. Jackson was a DNP for all three practices this week and will likely be ruled out in the next few hours, meaning Huntley will have a chance at a “revenge game” against a Browns team that he spent part of the 2024 and 2025 seasons with. Huntley threw for 201-2-0 in last week’s win over the Falcons and rushed for another 20 yards and one touchdown. He’ll have some appeal in 2QB and Superflex leagues on the road against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Jackson still has a chance to face the Browns this week, albeit a very small one. Backup Tyler Huntley will likely be under center for the second week in a row, although coach Jesse Minter said last week that Jackson doesn’t have to practice “much” before being cleared to play. Huntley is a viable QB2 if he gets the start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) has a “realistic” shot to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Jackson’s ankle injury, which has been described as neither high nor low, kept him sidelined in the Ravens’ win over the Falcons. It’s possible the Ravens will be cautious with Jackson and have Tyler Huntley start one more game in Week 6 against the Browns. Huntley against the Falcons threw for 201 yards and two scores. He was the seventh most accurate QB of the week. Jackson’s practice participation will be closely monitored over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports there is “some hope” Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: According to Rapoport, Jackson was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5 against the Falcons, which is an encouraging sign as the Ravens enter a pivotal matchup against the Browns. Jackson’s injury didn’t appear too severe when it initially happened in the second quarter of Week 4’s win over the Titans, so it’s not too surprising to hear that he nearly suited up for Sunday night’s game. That said, Jackson’s injuries have lingered in the past, so we’ll be monitoring his status throughout the week. If he’s not able to go, Tyler Huntley would make a second straight start for the Ravens, who currently lead the AFC North with a 4-1 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ 30-23, Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 20 yards and a touchdown on six carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley was in command of the offense throughout, showing poise and pocket presence in the face of one of the most stout defensive fronts in the league. The Ravens marched the field on the opening possession but a dropped touchdown from tight end Mark Andrews forced them to settle for a field goal. Their next possession resulted in an Andrews fumble that was returned for a touchdown, forcing the Ravens to play from behind for the remainder of the game. Down by eight with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, Huntley took the ball and led the team to a touchdown and successful two-point conversion to force overtime. He would then lead an opening possession touchdown drive in the extra frame, with the team escaping with an unlikely comeback victory on a game-sealing interception. Huntley could be tasked with another start in Week 6 against the Browns after late-week reports indicated that Lamar Jackson could be headed for another absence. Huntley will be a middling QB2, should he start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Tyler Huntley will start in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley figures to be a low-end superflex QB2 in Week 5, probably a bottom-five option for the week given how well the Falcons defense has played and how weak the Ravens skill position room looks. He led the team to zero points in the second half last week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will not play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Many thanks to Minter for ruling Jackson out now rather than forcing fantasy managers to navigate a questionable designation all weekend. Jackson did not practice at all this week for the Ravens and felt like a near lock to miss this week’s game after it was reported on Tuesday that he had an “outside chance” to play on Sunday night against the Falcons. Minter said earlier in the week that he did not think Jackson’s injury would result in a “crazy long-term” absence, so we’ll see how things go for him next week when the Ravens prepare to face the AFC North-leading Browns in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 22-of-30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 35-13, Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: After throwing for just 55 scoreless yards in the first half, Burrow and the Bengals came out firing on all cylinders in the second half. Trailing 13-0 at halftime, Burrow immediately orchestrated a nine-play, 66-yard drive that ended with a six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and followed that up with four more touchdown drives on his team’s next four possessions to jump out to a 35-13 lead. Burrow was as sharp as could be in the second half, completing 16-of-18 attempts while also completing two passes of 20-plus air yards. Burrow has now thrown four touchdowns in back-to-back games and has four multi-touchdown games this season. He’ll be on the QB1 radar next week when the Bengals play host to the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 31-24, Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense mostly had a smooth-sailing day against the lackadaisical Dolphins defense. After a high-volume Week 4, Burrow threw 32 passes, tossing touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, and Tanner Hudson in the first half. He just missed Ja’Marr Chase for a 70-yard score in the second half, but later connected with Chase for a 45-yard score in the third quarter. Burrow was hardly under pressure and had plenty of time to make accurate throws and take deep shots against Miami. He is a fantasy QB1 heading into the Bengals’ bye and gets a middling defense in the Ravens for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passes for 428 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Bengals’ 22-17, Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense struggled to finish drives for much of this game, with Burrow throwing his first touchdown to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter. He also added a rushing touchdown on a fourth-quarter quarterback sneak. Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) leaving early didn’t help as Burrow threw two interceptions and nearly had a third. He threw one to Travis Hunter in the first quarter, though it was nullified by a roughing the passer penalty. He later threw one with under two minutes left in the first half, leading to a Jaguars score the other way. The final interception came in the fourth quarter in the red zone, ending a promising drive. Burrow made great plays under pressure, often finding Tee Higgins downfield. However, the interceptions proved to be back-breaking and the Bengals’ comeback attempt ultimately fell short. Burrow is a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 5 against a soft Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 281 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 30-27, Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow came out hot in this one, completing his first 14 passes while throwing a three-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase on the Bengals’ opening drive. Burrow would throw his second touchdown of the day late in the second half when he connected with Tee Higgins for a 28-yard score and found Mike Gesicki 25 yards downfield on a fourth-and-two for his third touchdown of the day. Burrow led his offense on multiple long drives in this one, but with his team trailing 30-27 and driving late in the fourth quarter, he would cough up the ball on a strip-sack, which was recovered by Pittsburgh to seal the win for the Steelers. Burrow has attempted 30-plus passes in every game this season while throwing for six touchdowns to just one interception. He’ll be on the QB1 radar for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 20-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns in Cincinnati’s 20-6, Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow was under pressure quite a bit in this one, as he took five sacks, but the Bengals were able to establish enough of a lead on a few incredible out-of-structure plays by Burrow that they took the air out of the ball in the middle of the third quarter. Both touchdown passes were to Ja’Marr Chase, the second as Burrow drifted out of his pocket to the right. It’s full-steam ahead in the QB1 tiers as Burrow heads to Pittsburgh in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (back) is active for Cincinnati’s Week 2 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: It never seemed like there was a real chance Burrow would miss this game, even after Josh Johnson was elevated from the practice squad yesterday. Burrow will be on the QB1 line against a Texans defense looking to rebound. Inactive for the Bengals are: Johnson, WR Ke’Shawn Williams, CB Josh Newton, C Connor Lew, OL Myles Hinton, DT B.J. Hill (Achilles), and DT Landon Robinson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Joe Burrow (back) will play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals called up Josh Johnson from the practice squad over the weekend, raising some eyebrows regarding Burrow’s health. The move, however, was purely a precaution. Burrow has already said he is playing this week. He remains near the top of the QB1 ranks despite a tough matchup with the Houston defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: This listing is effectively a formality. Burrow laughed off the idea of missing the Bengals’ game against the Texans earlier this week, and today, coach Zac Taylor said Burrow is “good to go” after practicing in full. Burrow’s status is, of course, worth following, but we do expect him to play. Treat him as a QB1, per usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (back tightness) will play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow was upgraded to a full participant in Friday’s practice and is good to go for Sunday’s game, per head coach Zac Taylor. Burrow was limited in the first two practices of the week due to back tightness, but that was likely more out of precaution than it was due to anything serious. Burrow profiles as a high-end QB1 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Bengals expect Joe Burrow (back tightness) to play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow has been limited in each of the team’s first two practices, likely because the Bengals are exercising caution with their QB1. With one more practice to go before the Bengals release their final injury report, it sounds like there is no real concern about Burrow’s availability for Week 2 against a Texans defense looking to rebound from a tough season opener in which they allowed 36 points to the Bills. We will be sure to provide a final status for Burrow once the team announces it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is active for Week 7 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Lions declared TE Jackson Meeks, S Bishop Fitzgerald, C Seth McLaughlin, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DE Ahmed Hassanein inactive against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions C Cade Mays (wrist) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays seems likely to be activated off injured reserve ahead of the game given Dan Campbell’s public statements on the matter, him giving a presser today, and the trend to full sessions following the team’s Week 6 bye. It should be an upgrade for Detroit’s offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated C Cade Mays’ (wrist) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: This is a big deal for fantasy purposes. The Lions signed Mays to a three-year, $25 million contract this offseason, shoring up their center position with a reliable prime-age starter. Mays injured his wrist early in August, so he has not yet taken the field on game day with his new team. The Lions’ permissive defense continues to put the offense into pass-heavy game scripts. Getting Mays back on the field will fortify Jared Goff’s protection. He was limited on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions place S Brian Branch on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with an Achilles injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Branch ruptured an Achilles tendon in Week 14 last year. He is still recovering. The Lions also placed C Cade Mays (wrist) on the injured reserve/designated for return list due to his summer injury. Both players will be eligible to return after missing four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said C Cade Mays (wrist) will miss a “significant amount of time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The Lions sought to upgrade at center this offseason and went out and signed Mays to a three-year, $25 million contract. Now, the 27-year-old lineman is expected to be sidelined for the next 8-10 weeks after fracturing a small bone in his wrist , per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Campbell said that the injury is not believed to be season-ending, but it’s still a major blow to the offensive line. Former second-round pick Juice Scruggs came over in the David Montgomery trade and has played center before, so he will presumably get the first crack at taking over in Mays’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions agreed to terms with C Cade Mays, formerly of the Panthers, on a three-year, $25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: A boost for Jahmyr Gibbs! Mays is a huge power-blocking 6-foot-6, 325-pound center and should help solidify a troubled interior line for the Lions. It allows them to leave Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge at guard and makes Juice Scruggs a depth piece.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Panthers OG Chandler Zavala (calf) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Zavala suffered the calf injury in Panthers’ Week 12 loss to the 49ers and starts out the week not practicing. Also out was C Cade Mays (ankle). Jake Curhan and Austin Corbett are in line to start for Zavala and Mays, respectively, if neither can play in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Aaron Banks (knee/toe) is active for Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Banks was questionable headed into the weekend. He’ll miss at least one game with toe and knee injuries, a potential blow to Jordan Love, Josh Jacobs, and the Green Bay offense. With Jacobs active for the first time this year, the Packers will keep Kaleb Johnson inactive. Packers declared CB Benjamin St-Juste, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, OL Jager Burton, OL Donovan Jennings, and G Kevin Zeitler inactive against Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared OL Aaron Banks, CB Benjamin St-Juste, OL Jager Burton, and OL Donovan Jennings inactive for Week 6 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: No real surprises from the Packers as they look to continue their recent momentum forward as they chase the Vikings and Bears in the competitive NFC North. The team also appears set to get back franchise running back Josh Jacobs for Week 7 after it was reported the veteran back will be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared OG Aaron Banks, OL Jacon Monk, DL Anthony Campbell, and RG Kevin Zeitler inactive for Week 4 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Banks missed Week 1 with the knee issue. He suited up in Week 2 but aggravated the injury and has been out ever since. He is also dealing with a toe injury, per the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared CB Benjamin St-Juste, OL John Williams, OL Travis Glover, DT Warren Brinson, and DT Javon Hargrave inactive for Week 2 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: That means that starting left guard Aaron Banks (knee) will be back on the field after missing Week 1 against the Vikings. In a game that figures to be played in constant rain, having a fully healthy offensive line will be a nice boost for Marshawn Lloyd and the Packers’ offense. Javon Hargrave (concussion) remains out for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared OG Aaron Banks, LB Ty’Ron Hopper, OL Travis Glover, WR J. Michael Sturdivant, DT Warren Brinson, and DT Anthony Campbell inactive for Week 1 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Banks is dealing with knee tendinitis. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. Rookie Jager Burton is expected to start at left guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers restructured OG Aaron Banks’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, this “simple restructure” will reduce Banks’ 2026 cap hit down to $24.8 million. Banks, who was drafted in the second round by the 49ers back in 2021, signed a four-year contract with the Packers last offseason and is under contract through 2028. The five-year vet started 14 of the 15 games he appeared in for the Packers in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared K Brandon McManus, DL Devonte Wyatt, OT Anthony Belton and CB Kamal Hadden inactive for Week 6 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: The Packers signed K Lucas Havrisik on Saturday, with McManus nursing a quad injury. Havrisik will kick in McManus’ stead. Green Bay received great news regarding the offensive line’s health. LT Rasheed Walker (quad), LG Aaron Banks (groin/knee), RT Zach Tom (oblique/back) and backup OG/C Jacob Monk are all active this week. The talented unit should keep QB Jordan Love upright against the Bengals. Starting CB Nate Hobbs (concussion) is not on the inactives list, indicating he successfully passed the NFL’s concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers LT Rasheed Walker (quad) is questionable for Week 6 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Packers LG Aaron Banks (groin/knee), RT Zach Tom (oblique/back), backup OG/C Jacob Monk (hamstring) and CB Nate Hobbs (concussion) are questionable. On the plus side, backup LT Jordan Morgan (knee) will be active. Packers backup OT Anthony Belton (ankle) is out. The Packers are 2-1-1 despite the lengthy offensive line injury list. If the unit can get healthy later this year, this team will be a force to be reckoned with.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers RB Josh Jacobs (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Jacobs should handle another high-end RB1 workload against the Cowboys this week. The Packers will be without both RT Zach Tom (oblique) and his direct backup, RT Anthony Belton, who is on the injury report with an ankle injury. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Tom injured his knee on Wednesday. It is worth noting that high-ankle sprains and MCL sprains often share the same injury mechanism. Packers LG Aaron Banks (groin) is doubtful to play. On the plus side, TE Tucker Kraft (knee/elbow) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers LG Aaron Banks (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Jordan Morgan looks like a candidate to get a full game at guard with Banks injuring himself in Week 3 and not practicing in either of the first two sessions of the week. It won’t keep you away from any Packers — this is the Cowboys defense we’re talking about — but it might make their rushing effectiveness go down a bit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is active for Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was reportedly good to go as of this morning, so this doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Even in his 10th NFL season, Baker is still wreaking havoc on opposing offenses. He has four pass breakups, one pick, and 3.5 sacks this year. Inactive for the Cardinals are RB Jeremiyah Love, QB Carson Beck, DT Walter Nolen III, S Andrew Wingard, OL Jon Gaines, CB Max Melton, and OL Albert Reese.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Budda Baker (groin/illness) is expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was listed as questionable for Week 7 after getting in a limited practice on Friday. He is good to go after making it through the weekend unscathed. Baker has one interception, four pass breakups, and a stunning 3.5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker practiced in a limited capacity on Friday, and the veteran safety is no stranger to playing through injuries. The Cardinals ruled out DL Walter Nolen (ankle) and S Andrew Wingard (knee). Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (knee) has been cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker played through the groin injury in Week 6 but starts out this week not practicing due to both the groin injury and an illness. Also not practicing for the Cardinals defense were DL Walter Nolen (ankle), S Andrew Wingard (knee), and CB Garrett Williams (knee). Each player will likely need to practice in some capacity in order to play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin) is active in Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker and EDGE Zaven Collins (hip) were both added to the Cardinals’ injury report on Friday. Neither player practiced that day, but both are evidently good to go for this divisional showdown against the Rams (2-3). The Cardinals (1-4) are road underdogs, but this game should be a fantasy-friendly environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin) is questionable for Arizona’s Week 6 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: It was a pop-up DNP for Baker on Friday after he had initially been listed as NIR-Rest on Wednesday. Ominous. Baker stands a real chance at missing Sunday’s game and throwing the Cardinals defense into (checking notes) further chaos against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals HC Jonathan Gannon said Budda Baker (concussion) will not play in Week 17 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker entered the league’s concussion protocol earlier this week after going down in Week 16’s game against the Falcons. The star safety will miss at least one game due to his brain injury, with backup safety Kitan Crawford looking like the next man up to fill his role. In addition to Baker, the Cardinals also ruled out LT Paris Johnson (knee), and CB Kei’Tre Clark (knee) for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker entered the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was evaluated for a brain injury in Week 16 against the Falcons but re-entered the game, only to report concussion-like symptoms on Wednesday. Baker is likely to sit out this week against the Bengals, creating an even better matchup for Joe Burrow and the Bengals pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker returned to Week 16 against the Falcons after being evaluated for a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker remained down after making a tackle and took a minute to make his way to the sideline. After meeting with the training staff on the sideline, he jogged to the locker room for the concussion evaluation. After a short time, he was able to return to the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker (hamstring) is active for Week 10 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was limited through most of the week in practice but will suit up against Seattle after practicing in full on Friday. Cardinals declared OT Josh Fryar, OT Demontrey Jacobs, CB Will Johnson, CB Max Melton, DT Bilal Nichols, WR Xavier Weaver, and LB Mack Wilson inactive against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was solid over the first four weeks of the season, but this was another clunker for the 30-year-old tight end. After going over 50 yards in his first four games and bringing in three touchdowns, Johnson has just 23 total yards without a score in the next three. Because of positional value Johnson can’t be completely ignored, but the Saints haven’t paid much attention to him lately, so it’s time to look for alternatives, at least.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch either of his two targets in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was silent in a low-efficiency passing day for the Saints offense. The tight end position in general was a non-factor as a pass-catching group on the day. As Tyler Shough deals with broken bones in his non-throwing hand, the Saints’ passing game is tightening up and has less room for Johnson. He is a fantasy TE2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson had hovered around 50 yards in every game before today’s loss, but a shutdown Minnesota defense was more than enough to mute the production of every New Orleans pass-catcher. Things should improve for everyone when the Saints take on the Giants next week. Johnson will be a volume-based TE2 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 6-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson saw a slight uptick in snaps and routes after Noah Fant was inactive with an abdominal injury but returned a modest receiving line while being kept out of the end zone. The towering veteran finished third on the team in targets behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, the latter of whom scored the only receiving touchdown in a game that saw the two teams combine for seven rushing scores. Johnson remains a back-end TE1 for as long as rookie Jordyn Tyson remains sidelined, which appears likely to persist for another few weeks, at minimum. That holds true ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the vaunted Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 8-of-8 targets for 53 yards, two touchdowns and one lost fumble in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was getting open at will on out routes and shallow crossers. He and Noah Fant, along with the two Raiders tight ends, combined for six touchdowns, tying an NFL positional record. Johnson fumbled while trying to make a big play for his team late in the game. He attempted to stiff-arm Nakobe Dean, who cleanly punched the ball out for Eric Stokes to recover. Tyler Shough threw a bad pass to Johnson earlier on, which CB Hezekiah Masses easily picked off and returned downfield. Johnson raced after him and successfully punched the ball out with a diving hammer-fist, but the Raiders ultimately recovered that fumble, leading to a turnover for the Saints. Johnson remains a reliable TE1 against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 targets for 66 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was on the receiving end of two big plays in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. Johnson hauled in a short pass on a third-and-13 in the third quarter and turned it upfield for a 25-yard gain. In the fourth quarter, Johnson again picked up 25 yards on a short pass on third-and-eight, taking it to the Ravens’ five-yard line and setting the Saints up for a touchdown a few plays later. Johnson has caught seven passes in his first two games and is averaging an impressive 17.1 YPR on said catches. He’ll be on the TE2 radar for next week’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson posted a 3/54/1 receiving line last week and can be treated as a TE1 again in Week 2. Saints WR1 Chris Olave is nursing a hamstring strain, though the team is telling reporters that the injury is not concerning. Johnson could take on a slightly larger workload if Olave is at all limited, though we won’t know if that is the case until the dust settles and the game ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson is firmly on track to play. Illness-related absences are very rare, and the Saints’ No. 1 tight end is already back at it. The Saints face the Ravens this weekend, in what should be a high-scoring game environment. Johnson is a locked-in TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Players rarely miss games because of illnesses, especially when it crops up four days before kickoff. Johnson should be fine, but fantasy managers counting on him as a high-end TE2 will want to check in on Friday. Fellow tight end Oscar Delp was limited with a hamstring issue. He missed Week 1 because of the injury but has a shot at making his NFL debut versus the Ravens this Sunday. He will not be on the fantasy radar if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 3-of-7 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 1 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson didn’t catch his first pass of the game until the final minute, when Tyler Shough found him in the end zone for a game-tying score. He then racked up another 45 yards on a catch at the end of the fourth quarter and another in overtime. Johnson only finished fourth on the team in targets, which could be an issue when the team’s passing volume inevitably dips. He will be a mid-range TE2 for another potential shootout with the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Barion Brown caught all three of his targets for 57 yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: Brown did virtually all of his damage on a 49-yard connection that helped set up the only touchdown of the day for the Saints. The 22-year-old also had 97 yards in return yardage, and the athleticism of Brown was apparent even on a limited amount of touches. The sixth-round selection is worth keeping an eye on in in dynasty leagues, but isn’t someone fantasy managers can trust in redraft formats as of yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Saints TE Noah Fant (abdomen) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 5 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: Fant sat out in Week 4 after scoring two touchdowns in Week 3. He is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but he can serve as a checkdown option for Tyler Shough. The Saints labeled WR Barion Brown (thigh) questionable to play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: Both Brown and TE Noah Fant (abdomen) were limited today, putting them tentatively on track to play on Monday night against the Falcons. Neither player belongs in fantasy lineups, but their presence is helpful for QB Tyler Shough.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Saints declared WR Barion Brown, QB Zach Wilson, CB Martin Emerson Jr., DL Christen Miller, TE Treyton Welch, DT John Ridgeway and EDGE Tyree Wilson inactive for Week 3 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: The Saints will be without their gadget player and return specialist, teeing up WR Bryce Lance for the full-time No. 3 wide receiver role. Brown is not relevant in 12-team leagues, though he may be missed by the Saints. Emerson, the Saints’ No. 3 cornerback, is sidelined by a shoulder injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Saints ruled out WR Barion Brown (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: The Saints will be without their gadget wide receiver and return specialist. His absence should allow WR Bryce Lance to consolidate routes in the No. 3 wide receiver role, but Lance is only a 14-team dart throw. Hopefully, Brown is back at it next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: It seems like Brown is very unlikely to play at this point. His agility and long speed define his game as a gadget player and return specialist. His absence could benefit WR2 Devaughn Vele and WR Bryce Lance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: Brown generally contributes as a gadget receiver and in the return game. Were he to sit out in Week 3, his absence would likely be a bigger deal for the Saints than it would be for fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: Saints WR Bryce Lance caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: Lance could have the inside track for the Saints’ short-term No. 3 wide receiver job with WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) sidelined, though WR Barion Brown will almost assuredly make the roster as a receiver and returner. Lance nearly added a decent, leaping downfield gain to his box score, but QB Spencer Rattler’s pass grazed off his fingertips along the sideline. Brown was not involved as a receiver today, but rushed twice for 19 yards and one touchdown, including an eight-yard jet sweep that got him into the end zone. He also returned one punt for four yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett believes the Saints might not need to sign a short-term replacement for WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: Triplett was apparently surprised to see reporters wondering whether the Saints should bring a veteran receiver aboard. According to him, the Saints had nine legitimate wide receiver candidates to make the final roster, with rookie WRs Bryce Lance and Barion Brown leading the charge. Per Triplett, Lance “is coming on faster than anyone else,” though Brown notably surged early in camp. Lance does not play on special teams, which could make him an ideal No. 3 wide receiver. Triplett also believes the Saints should design a package of plays for the speedy Brown, who WR Chris Olave said is “basically the same player” as former Saints WR Rashid Shaheed. For deep league fantasy managers, Lance could be worth a late-round dart throw. Both players should be rostered in dynasty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.headline: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reports that Saints WR Barion Brown looks like “the real deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/barion-bro.analysis: Per Underhill, Brown’s “momentum is undeniable,” and “it would be a surprise if Brown doesn’t play himself into a role on offense.” It sounds like making the final roster is a box that’s already been checked for the sixth-round rookie. He notably took reps with QB Tyler Shough on Thursday. Although Brown could have a very tough time becoming fantasy-relevant in re-draft formats, he is a player to know for dynasty purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-5 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele brought in a one-yard touchdown on fourth-and-goal late in the second quarter to tie the game at 10-10. It would be the last points the Saints would score. Vale has hovered around these numbers through the first half of 2026, and while it provides Shough with a nice safety valve, it’s not exactly what fantasy managers should be chasing. He’ll be a WR4 in Week 9 against the Browns after the Saints “enjoy” their bye in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: The Saints offense has not pushed the ball downfield over the past two weeks, leading to low-scoring outputs for Vele. He caught three passes on the day, and nearly reeled in a fourth catch on a Tyler Shough sideline overthrow in the second quarter. When the Saints aren’t in a pass-happy game script, Vele is relegated to touchdown-dependent FLEX value. He will be in the WR4 ranks against the Steelers for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 4-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Tyler Shough managed a dismal 96 passing yards in this game, so there simply wasn’t enough production for any New Orleans wideout to post usable fantasy numbers. Vele still tied Chris Olave for a team-high in targets. He has at least four catches and six targets in every game this year. Even after a quiet Week 5, Vele remains a solid WR4 option headed into a Week 6 date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele’s nine targets ranked behind only alpha Chris Olave, although he was headed for another modest fantasy outing before a garbage time touchdown with less than two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter of the blowout loss. Vele has yet to eclipse 69 yards through the first month of play as he continues to operate in an intermediate role for a Saints team struggling to attack downfield. Fantasy managers could consider sitting Vele against the ferocious Vikings defense in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards in the Saints’ loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele nearly added a decent first-down pickup to his box score, but he was unable to secure the pass as he was diving to the ground. Aside from that, he had a nice 17-yard gain in which he ripped his leg away from a would-be tackler and scampered away for a few extra yards. Vele is a boom-bust FLEX against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: It seems like Brown is very unlikely to play at this point. His agility and long speed define his game as a gadget player and return specialist. His absence could benefit WR2 Devaughn Vele and WR Bryce Lance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: It was another solid outing for Vele, who has now caught 12 passes for 133 yards and one touchdown in his first two games this season. Vele’s biggest play came on a third-and-eight when he hauled in a 29-yard reception to extend a drive that ended with a Daniel Carlson field goal. Vele is the clear-cut WR2 for the Saints at this point and could be worth a dart throw in deeper leagues next week as a WR3/WR4 in Week 3 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reports that Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) “left practice as a precautionary measure” on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Underhill adds that Olave’s hamstring issue is not expected to be a “problem.” If this really is a non-issue, perhaps Olave just experienced cramping today and will be back out there on Friday, practicing in full. That said, soft tissue issues that pop up mid-week are typically not good. Saints No. 2 WR Devaughn Vele is worth adding if he is a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 7-of-9 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 1 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele stepped in as the Saints’ No. 2 receiver with Jordyn Tyson on injured reserve. He did a flawless impression of a top-10 pick, making multiple diving grabs to keep the Saints alive in the second half. The Saints acquired Vele via trade last offseason but couldn’t get him going until late in the season. He then missed the final month of the year with a shoulder issue. A healthy offseason seems to have done him well, and he’s now poised to be the No. 2 receiver on a fast, pass-heavy offense until Tyson returns. Vele will be a WR4 for his Week 2 matchup with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is expected to miss roughly two months, reports NFL Insider Ian Rapoport.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Tyson left practice last Thursday with a hamstring injury and sought opinions from multiple doctors over the weekend. Now he’s slated to miss roughly two months, according to Rapoport. It’s a tough blow for the 22-year-old receiver who also battled hamstring injuries during his college career. The Saints also drafted receivers Bryce Lance and Barion Brown, though Devaughn Vele could be first in line for additional targets while Tyson is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 6-of-10 targets for 57 yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was once again a shorter-yardage target with a long gain of just 14 yards in the contest. Tyler Shough missed the 26-year-old on what would have been a walk-in touchdown from deep on a disappointing day for the top target in the Saints’ passing attack, at least based on expectations. He’ll remain one of the top fantasy receiving options in his next game, but that won’t come for two weeks as the Saints get a bye before facing the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Loomis said Tyson is “improving” in his long rehab from a major preseason hamstring injury. Tyson, who traveled with the Saints to France for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, could still be a couple weeks away as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery. In the meantime, Bryce Lance will operate as the Saints’ No. 2 wideout behind Chris Olave. Lance over the past two weeks has a 13 percent target share and a 20 percent air yards share in the pass-first New Orleans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-7 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave finished as the Saints’ leading receiver after coming into the weekend questionable with an illness. He was able to salvage his fantasy day with an 18-yard score at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Despite a season-low 43 yards receiving, Olave is still averaging just under 100 yards receiving per game this season. There is no question he belongs in the fantasy WR1 ranks heading into a Week 7 showdown against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Olave (illness) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: There was reportedly a bug going around the Saints’ locker room last weekend, and Olave seems to have caught the tail end of it. He missed the first two practices of the week but was back on the field for Friday’s session. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. Barring any further updates, we’re expecting business as usual for the star wideout. He remains entrenched in the WR1 mix for his date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave missed the first two days of practice this week with the illness, but we’d ultimately still expect him to play. He should be regarded as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’ll be an easy WR1, assuming he plays, against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Unless we get word that it’s an exceptionally rough illness, we’d expect no worse than a questionable listing on Friday despite the two missed practices. Olave should remain a smash WR1 against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: We expect Olave to be fine for the Saints’ Week 6 game against the Giants. There is currently no cause for concern, but this is worth keeping an eye on. Olave experienced blood clots in his lung last season, and spent much of the offseason recovering. We are not doctors and cannot opine on the matter. For now, expect him to play, but keep an eye out for his hopeful return to practice tomorrow or Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-6 targets for 46 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was averaging over 120 yards per game before today’s contest. The Saints’ extreme play volume and tilt to toward passing the ball turned his great role into elite fantasy production. That finally came to a halt with Brian Flore’s defense shutting down Tyler Shough. The second-year passer completed just 16 throws for 96 yards. Shough and the entire passing attack should improve drastically versus the Giants next week. Fantasy managers can keep treating Olave as a WR1 despite this speed bump.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (foot) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: The Saints gave Olave a rest day on Wednesday. He then logged a limited practice on Thursday, listed with a new foot injury, and was reportedly seen sporting a walking boot after practice. ESPN’s Kat Terrell notes, however, that “walking boots are often a precautionary measure.” The fact that the team cleared him right away is reassuring. He can be treated as a low-end WR1, as usual. Olave later told Terrell that his “foot got a little bruised in Thursday’s practice, but he’s good.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (foot) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: It is tough to say when exactly the injury happened. This is bizarre. Olave took a hard hit to the lower body late in Week 4 and subbed himself out for the team’s final possession. He did not practice on Wednesday. The team listed it as a rest day, and New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reported that coach Kellen Moore clarified three times that Olave’s Wednesday absence was not injury-related. Olave resumed practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday with a foot injury. If this injury occurred in-game, he should be considered likely to play. If it occurred in practice today, he would be firmly in the questionable column. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth didn’t appear to be bothered by his calf injury, and he quadrupled the targets of Darnell Washington (4-to-1) in this game. Washington was able to convert his only target for a touchdown, however, and Freirmuth dropped what would have been a 20-yard gain in the third quarter. Freiermuth will likely get a similar amount of targets in Week 8 against the Browns, for better or worse.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: The Muth was clearly limited by his nagging calf injury in this game. He was added to the injury report over the weekend and played through the issue despite being hit with a late questionable tag. He was spotted hobbling to the sidelines at least once during this game, though he ultimately gutted it out and played through the issue. He and Darnell Washington each played 54 of 76 offensive snaps. Better days should be ahead for Freiermuth once he’s healthy, but it will be hard to trust him as anything other than a TE2 flyer for his Week 7 game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Muth was a late addition to the injury report, with the Steelers adding him on Saturday and listing him as questionable. With multiple starting receivers out this week, Muth will be asked to take on more work as a pass-catcher, moving him up the TE2 ranks. Inactive for the Steelers are WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DL Kevin Jobity Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Steelers are “optimistic” Pat Freiermuth (calf) will play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report on Saturday. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. A last-minute addition to the injury report is never a good sign, so we wouldn’t be surprised if his snaps are limited even if he is active. On the other hand, with Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman out, the Steelers may have no choice but to play a banged-up Muth more than expected. He will be a high-risk TE2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth popped up on the injury report Saturday afternoon with a calf injury. He’s questionable for this weekend against the Buccaneers. Freiermuth would’ve been in line for a sizable workload with the Steelers down multiple wide receivers. Coming off a two touchdown performance in Week 5, fantasy managers need a backup plan in case Freiermuth is ultimately ruled out against Tampa Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards and two touchdowns in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth ran 27 routes on 38 dropbacks, which was a distant third behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard; however, Aaron Rodgers is far more effective when targeting the intermediate and middle areas of the field, which makes Freiermuth a more consistent target than either of the wide receivers. With Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) both hurt, Freiermuth could be a fringe TE1 next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth found the end zone late in the fourth quarter for his second touchdown of the season, tying fellow tight end Darnell Washington for fourth on the team with five targets. Washington managed to corral just two of his five targets but eclipsed the yardage total of Freiermuth with 27 yards while also adding a touchdown of his own. Both tight ends appear unlikely to contribute viable counting stats considering neither has seen more than five targets in a game during the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Aaron Rodgers narrowly missed Freiermuth on a 20-plus-yard throw in the third quarter that could have been a touchdown if they had connected. Freiermuth has been targeted 14 times through the first three weeks but has just one meaningful fantasy line (5-45-1) thus far. Fantasy managers can find better options than Muth in Week 4’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth has a hold on the Steelers’ TE1 role, getting much of Aaron Rodgers’ short-yardage looks in the flat and middle of the field. The Steelers were not in the red zone all that much, so we have yet to see the 27-year-old’s utilization there. Regardless, he is consistently a top-four pass-catching option for the team, he’s just stuck in the low-ceiling Pittsburgh offense. Freiermuth is a touchdown-dependent fantasy play and will be in the low-end TE2 ranks for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington caught his only target for a four-yard touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington used his massive — massive seems like a huge understatement — size to haul in a touchdown near the sideline. That’s his third touchdown in four games, and it’s pretty clear that he’s become a focal point once the Steelers get inside of the red zone. He just isn’t much of one outside of those opportunities, and that makes him the most touchdown dependent tight end to ever exist. Maybe a little bit of hyperbole there. Washington will try and score again in Week 8 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darenll Washington caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington got in the end zone for the third time this year via an RPO toss from Rodgers near the goal line. His six targets were double the total of Pat Freiermuth, who was laboring through a calf injury in this contest. Muth should be healthier and earn more looks next week, making this minor spike game from Washington rather unsustainable. Washington will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for his Week 7 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Freiermuth found the end zone late in the fourth quarter for his second touchdown of the season, tying fellow tight end Darnell Washington for fourth on the team with five targets. Washington managed to corral just two of his five targets but eclipsed the yardage total of Freiermuth with 27 yards while also adding a touchdown of his own. Both tight ends appear unlikely to contribute viable counting stats considering neither has seen more than five targets in a game during the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington caught 3-of-4 targets for 67 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: No, Washington can’t be trusted in fantasy, but he sure is fun when he gets a full head of steam. Washington caught a season-high three passes in Sunday’s win over the Bengals and led the Steelers in receiving yards, thanks largely to the 47-yard play he made in the fourth quarter. A true man among boys with the ball in his hands, Washington rumbled through and past multiple defenders on his way to the big gain. While he’s always good for an exciting play or two, Washington can be left on waivers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes TE Pat Freiermuth will be the Steelers’ “go-to pass-catching tight end” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: The Steelers notably signed TE Darnell Washington to a four-year, $42 million contract extension this offseason, but DeFabo believes Freiermuth is still the team’s TE1. He expects Washington to continue operating as a receiving threat, “especially in the red zone,” but he is apparently stuck in the TE2 role. Washington’s profile is certainly more intriguing, but he may be best viewed as a boom-bust backup option in best ball for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers signed TE Darnell Washington to a four-year, $42 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington’s contract includes $21 million in guaranteed money. A third-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft from Georgia, he’s been as advertised so far in his pro career. Washington has only 57 catches, 625 yards and two touchdowns in three seasons, but is a tremendous blocker and extremely difficult to tackle when he has the ball. Listed at 6-foot-7 and 264 pounds, he’s one of the most physically imposing players in the NFL. With a $10.5 million average annual value, Washington is 12th in AAV among tight ends. That level of commitment could be a sign the Steelers plan to use a good amount of two tight end sets with Washington and Pat Freiermuth in head coach Mike McCarthy’s first season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers TE Darnell Washington had surgery to repair his broken arm.
