https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington underwent surgery Monday and won’t return to the Steelers this season, even if they manage to beat the Ravens in Week 18 and make the playoffs. Washington ends the 2025 season with 31 receptions on 43 targets for 364 yards and one touchdown. He was third among Pittsburgh tight ends in catches, as Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth remains involved in Arthur Smith’s tight end-heavy offensive scheme. With Washington sidelined, Freiermuth would seem to be the main beneficiary. Both Smith and Freiermuth have a 48 percent route participation rate through Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers HC Mike Tomlin said Darnell Washington suffered a broken arm in Week 17’s loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington was ruled out shortly after leaving the field in the second quarter of Sunday’s game. The hulking tight end won’t be available for Week 18’s must-win game against the Ravens that will decide the winner of the AFC North, which further hurts a passing game that will already be without DK Metcalf. Both Pat Freiermuth and Jonnu Smith could benefit from an uptick in targets with Washington sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington (forearm) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 17’s game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington went down in the second quarter and attempted to come back in for a play. After his lone attempt to gut it out, he left for the sidelines and was ruled out shortly after leaving the field. Washington’s day ends with two receptions for 15 yards on two targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Aaron Rodgers was focused on hitting his halfbacks out of the backfield much more than his wideouts, and Bernard was unable to get much done outside of a 20-yard reception. The rookie wideout had gone over 80 yards in his last two games, but this shows the volatility in Bernard’s fantasy profile as a rookie. He’ll look to bounce back against the Browns in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 11-of-12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard began the game with a potentially catastrophic blunder by moving the chains on first down, only to run back behind the sticks in search of more yards. He was taken down behind the line to gain for a turnover on downs. Instead of banishing him to the bench, Aaron Rodgers continued to lean on the rookie throughout the contest for easy completions underneath. He tied DK Metcalf for a team-high in catches. Per the broadcast, it was the most catches by a rookie receiver of Rodgers since the grizzled veteran entered the league. Bernard went from a PPR scam to a full-blown breakout in overtime by extending the ball for a game-winning touchdown with two defenders draped over him. Bernard has 21 targets over the past two weeks. He also has at least 80 yards in back-to-back games. He is looking at a WR3 ranking for his Week 7 matchup with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-9 targets for 80 yards in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Michael Pittman (foot) was ruled out earlier in the week, and then Roman Wilson dislocated his finger during the game, so there wasn’t a lot of competition for Bernard and DK Metcalf. The rookie from Alabama played the same number of snaps as Metcalf and ran a route on 35 of the team’s 38 dropbacks. This isn’t an explosive passing attack, but Bernard looks like the WR2 in Pittsburgh now and is more of an intermediate and short-area target than DK Metcalf, which could lead to decent fantasy value over the next few weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Roman Wilson has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 5 against the Colts with a dislocated finger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Wilson had just one target in the first half. He pinned the reception to his hip, but the ball was ripped loose by a defender, which not only made the pass incomplete but also seemed to dislocate Wilson’s finger. With Michael Pittman Jr. also hurt, we should continue to see a lot of Germie Bernard in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Michael Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury and will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: McCarthy told reporters the team is evaluating Pittman’s roster spot, meaning they could place him on injured reserve. He would miss at least four weeks while on IR. Pittman tried to play through the foot injury but only made it two weeks before aggravating the issue. He was spotted using a scooter to support his foot in the locker room on Wednesday. We suspect the Steelers will place him on IR to give Pittman enough time to fully recover. Germie Bernard will now operate as the team’s permanent WR3, with Roman Wilson taking on more work as the clear No. 2 receiver. Both players will be decent FLEX options for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: He was limited in practice all three days this week with a foot injury that kept him out of Week 2. We’d say Pittman is on the optimistic side of questionable based on his participation status. If he’s out again, it would likely be Germie Bernard picking up the slack, as he did in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Pittman didn’t practice once last week, so a limited session today is a big step in the right direction. Germie Bernard took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and caught four passes for 35 yards, but he also coughed up a drop that was then intercepted by New England. The mistake all but guarantees his return to the bench once Pittman is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard saw increased opportunity with Michael Pittman ruled out for Week 2. He caught all four of his receptions on one drive in the second quarter but ended as the second-most targeted receiver on the team. Bernard seemed to lose much of the trust he earned with a rough bobble on an Aaron Rodgers screen pass that led to an interception in the fourth quarter. The rookie second-round pick will find fantasy relevance while Pittman is out, but is no more than a fantasy WR5 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers WR Germie Bernard caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard started alongside other Steelers backups this evening, indicating he has not yet earned a starting role in three-wide receiver sets. That said, he looked good. Bernard found the end zone via a screen pass on the Steelers’ second drive, shaking a defender immediately after the catch before muscling past another as he crossed the plane. He nearly scored again on the following drive, but QB Will Howard overthrew him in the end zone. The Steelers’ top-two WRs, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, are just getting over injuries, and No. 3 WR Roman Wilson should not be considered insurmountable in-house competition. Bernard could work his way into the lineup early in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for five yards in the Saints’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers, adding seven receptions for 57 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Tyler Shough ended up leading the Saints with seven rushing yards. Yikes. Kamara was effective as a receiver out of the backfield, but to say that New Orleans struggled to run the ball is quite the understatement; finishing with 18 yards on 17 attempts. The good news for fantasy managers that used Kamara is that he was effective out of the backfield as a receiver, but it’s a modest day for the 31-year-old. Kamara and the Saints will try and get something going after a bye against the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was removed from the injury report for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was still listed as limited in Friday’s practice, but the Saints feel confident enough in his health to clear him for Week 7. Kamara found the end zone last week on a 31-yard reception, but has largely been inefficient with his touches this season. He seen 14 opportunities to Kendre Miller’s 30 over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a touchdown-dependent RB3 against the Steelers. The only players on the Saints carrying injury designations into the weekend are guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DL Nathan Sheperd (illness). Both are listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: He’s played through this listing for a few weeks now, and though he’ll sometimes get dinged up in game, appears no worse for the wear. Kendre Miller feels like the more viable back in a normal game script right now, with Kamara playing more on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara has been playing through the back issue for several weeks. He is expected to do so again this week. Kamara is part of a three-back committee, and he isn’t the leader of the trio, but that didn’t stop him from finding the end zone on nine touches last week. With a limited receiving role to go along with his shrinking rushing workload, he’s barely in the RB3 mix for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed seven times for 34 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants, adding two receptions for 35 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints deployed a committee backfield once again for Week 6. Kamara was the third running back into the game for the Saints, but was the only one to score a touchdown. He briefly went to the medical tent after falling on his hip in the first half but re-entered the game soon after. Kamara caught a swing pass from Tyler Shough and tip-toed away from the sideline to score from 17 yards out in the third quarter. With that catch, he became the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000 yards receiving and 5,000 yards rushing in his career. Despite the touchdown and milestone, Kamara was still third in running back snaps and is a touchdown-dependent FLEX play for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Saints declared RB Alvin Kamara (back) active for Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara is active after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported he would be expected to play in Week 6. He played through the back injury last week and is part of a rough running back committee in the Saints backfield. Kamara is in the RB4 ranks for fantasy purposes. Also active is Chris Olave (illness). The Saints declared QB Zach Wilson, EDGE Anfernee Jennings, S Mike Reid, LB Kaden Elliss, DT Nathan Shepherd, and DT John Ridgeway inactive for Week 6 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Alvin Kamara (back) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through the back issue last week, though he only saw five touches. He has fallen behind Kendre Miller in the pecking order for carries, and even CJ Donaldson is pushing him for work on passing downs. Kamara is barely an RB4 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara practiced each day this week, so it’s a bit surprising to see him here. Assuming no rough quotes or reports come out, we’d regard him as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’s a reasonable FLEX play against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through this injury in Week 5, and it doesn’t seem like he’s in any real danger of missing this one. It would be nice to see a full practice on Friday, but even if we don’t get that, Kamara should be a FLEX consideration for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through the back injury last week but only touched the ball five times. Kendre Miller rushed 10 times and CJ Donaldson led the team in snaps. The Saints are likely managing Kamara’s workload as he deals with this back issue. Kamara is not on the fantasy radar for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 2-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: After having a whopping 15 targets in the Week 6 win over the Bucs, Metcalf was essentially a non-factor in this one. He was able to haul in a 51-yard connection that set up the lone touchdown for the Steelers, but for the second time in three weeks, Metcalf was held under four catches. He’ll be a volatile WR2/3 for Week 8 in a matchup with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 11-of-15 targets for 93 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Aaron Rodgers couldn’t get much going outside of check-downs for the better part of three quarters. Then, in desperation mode, Rodgers started forcing targets to his No. 1 receiver. Metcalf saw 12 targets in the fourth quarter and overtime. He turned that into 81 yards, otherwise known as nearly all of his production for the day. Metcalf’s ability to win downfield and on the boundary isn’t being maximized by Rodgers, but the team is throwing so often that Metcalf can still rack up fantasy points with ease. With a vulnerable Saints defense on deck for Week 7, Metcalf is on the WR2/3 border as we approach the midpoint of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf (illness) was removed from the injury report and is expected to play against the Buccaneers in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Good news. Metcalf missed practice Friday and was listed as questionable, but has since been removed from the injury report and is expected to play this week. With the Steelers missing Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek, Metcalf could see even more targets than usual against Tampa Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf (illness) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: This is unfortunate. The Steelers placed Michael Pittman on injured reserve recently, and both Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek are out this week. Metcalf has a chance to play this week, but fantasy managers must, unfortunately, keep an eye on the news over the next 48 hours. Rookie Germie Bernard could lead the team in targets again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: This was not the game many expected against a beleaguered Colts defense. Two of Metcalf’s three catches were on screens behind the line of scrimmage, and he was only targeted 10 yards down the field once. Aaron Rodgers is not having much success throwing the ball deep down the field, which means Metcalf is likely going to be a touchdown-dependent WR3 in fantasy next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 5-of-9 targets for 115 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf managed just three receptions through the first three-plus quarters of play before making two grabs for 50 yards on the team’s penultimate possession, eventually resulting in a tie game with under two minutes to play following a successful two-point conversion. Even though this marks the third game in four tries with nine or more targets, Week 4 was the first game with more than 40 yards for Metcalf as he works to strengthen his connection with Rodgers in a downfield role. In fact, Metcalf more than doubled his year-to-date yardage total from the previous three games against two of the better coverage corners in the league. The individual matchup doesn’t get much easier ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Colts, who boast another top corner duo in Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward. Metcalf remains a wide range of outcomes weekly WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-5 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf has yet to crack 40 yards in a game this season, but he did manage to find the end zone for a six-yard touchdown late in the third quarter. The big plays have not been there for Metcalf thus far, who has a long catch of 16 yards. Metcalf will be on the WR3/WR4 radar for next week’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 4-of-9 targets for 27 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf had an inefficient day, finishing fifth on the Steelers in yards despite leading the team in targets. He was unable to get open downfield and Aaron Rodgers’ struggles made many intermediate targets fell incomplete. Metcalf dropped a critical third-down pass in the third quarter, continuing his drop issues from last week. A second straight inefficient week despite a high volume of targets makes Metcalf a rough fantasy play moving forward. Despite Michael Pittman’s absence, the fantasy points are just not consistent for Metcalf in the Steelers passing game. He will be a low-end fantasy WR3 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: Steelers WR Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Pittman did not practice at all this week. If he plays, he could be fairly limited. We tentatively expect him to be inactive on game day, though. Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth had a solid role last week and could take on No. 2 pass-catcher duties if Pittman indeed cannot play. Steelers WR DK Metcalf will almost assuredly take on a larger role, operating as the team’s receiving focal point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: Aaron Rodgers said he’s “going to keep feeding” DK Metcalf.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf caught just 4-of-10 targets in Week 1 and was flagged twice for offensive pass interference while struggling to make contested catches. It wasn’t ideal. But Rodgers’ words should sooth any thought of bumping Metcalf down the ranks just yet. “I’m not worried about DK at all, man,” Rodgers said.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed nine times for 48 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding six catches for 45 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was the clear backup to Jaylen Warren, but he was able to have a solid day thanks in large part to checkdowns from Aaron Rodgers. The 28-year-old had a long rush of 16 yards, and the toe injury that sidelined him earlier in the campaign doesn’t appear to be bothering him. Dowdle is a FLEX option for Week 8 against the Browns, at best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is active for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: The knee issue was new for Dowdle and limited him to three partial practices this week. He was listed as questionable for Week 7 on Friday. Dowdle will once again form the 1B portion of Pittsburgh’s backfield committee. He’s a low-end RB3 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is questionable for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was listed as limited throughout the week and will officially be questionable entering this week’s game with the Saints. This is a new injury he is dealing with but it doesn’t sound like he’s at serious risk of missing the game at this time. Dowdle played on just 17 percent of snaps in his return to action last week and saw 11 opportunities. He’ll profile as a low-end RB3 this week if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: It’s a new injury that popped up on Wednesday, but with two limited sessions we’re not overly concerned about Dowdle missing Sunday morning’s Civil Unrest Bowl in Paris. He’ll be in the RB3/FLEX discussion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: The Steelers will likely limit Dowdle’s reps for a few weeks as he manages the toe injury that cost him three games. He should be good to go for Sunday’s game by Friday. Dowdle saw 10 touches in his first game back and looked relatively explosive, running for 40 yards on seven attempts. He is in the RB3 mix for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed seven times for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding three catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was active for the first time since injuring his toe in Week 2. He initially formed a near 50-50 committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter pulled away in the fourth quarter and overtime. Warren racked up four carries and one catch in overtime alone, bringing his touch total from 11 to 16. Dowdle saw a single carry in the extra frame. Dowdle’s role should grow in the coming weeks, but it’s clear that Warren is the top option in the backfield, leaving Dowdle as a low-end RB3 for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle is back after missing three games with the toe issue. He will form a committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter’s elite play last week likely earned him a larger split of the backfield in Week 6. Dowdle will primarily operate between the tackles, pushing him to the back of the RB3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle seemingly has a good chance to play. He was limited on Wednesday, but practiced in full on Thursday and Friday. However, Jaylen Warren has played extremely well with Dowdle sidelined and coach Mike McCarthy has said that Warren will remain a high-volume player. If active, Dowdle is a FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: It’s his first full practice since suffering the toe injury. Dowdle looks to be headed for hard-to-trust FLEX territory with Jaylen Warren crushing in his absence and Mike McCarthy (rightfully) saying that Warren deserves the lion’s share of the workload at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 18 times for 101 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding three catches for 36 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren got off to a hot start with 43 yards on the first drive, with 29 of those coming on a play that set up a short field goal. He totaled 78 yards in the first half, but found the sledding a little tougher in the final two periods with the Saints focused on stuffing the run. He outcarried Rico Dowdle 18-9, although Dowdle did add six catches to make the touches a little more even. Warren will look to impress again in Week 8 against the Browns’ front seven.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 14 times for 50 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding two catches for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren and Rico Dowdle, who was active after missing three games with a toe injury, split the backfield carries for the majority of this game. Warren finally pulled away from Dowdle late in the fourth quarter and overtime. Over the final 20 minutes of the contest, Warren out-carried Dowdle 7-2. He held a modest 7-5 carries advantage through three quarters. Dowdle was more efficient on the ground, but the Steelers clearly trust Warren more in all situations when push comes to shove. Warren will be in the RB2 mix when he takes on the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said “there’s a number you’d like to continue to give [Jaylen Warren],” even after Rico Dowdle (toe) returns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: “He’s produced, so it’s been heavy. It’d be great to get Rico back this week, too. ... Having him as a one-two punch was the vision of this offense, but Jaylen’s crushing it right now. He’s been awesome for us,” McCarthy continued. That’s a very telling “but.” Warren has to be regarded as the chair of a committee at this point rather than in a backfield split, and Dowdle probably doesn’t belong in the FLEX conversation coming off his injury until we see a good workload for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts, adding six catches for 87 yards and another touchdown through the air.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren got the Steelers on the board with an 80-yard catch-and-run, where he simply beat the Colts defenders down the sideline. He also ripped off a 50-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. The Steelers only had one other play go for longer than 17 yards on the day. Since Rico Dowdle has been out with a toe injury, Warren has emerged as a true RB1 in fantasy football. Even when Dowdle returns, you have to think that the Steelers have seen enough that they need to give Warren the lion’s share of the work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar, CB Jamel Dean, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DT Kevin Jobity Jr. inactive for Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Dowdle was unlikely to suit up due to his ongoing foot injury, so this doesn’t come as a major surprise. We could be looking at a big game for Jaylen Warren against an underperforming Colts defense. With Keenan Allen back for the Colts, the injury to Jamel Dean is a bit of a blow to this Pittsburgh secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Rico Dowdle is making progress in his attempt to return from a toe injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: McCarthy said he expects Dowdle and Jaylen Warren to be a “one-two punch” once Dowdle returns to the field. Warren has totaled 34 rushes over the last two weeks while rushing for 220 scoreless yards, but had a 21-89-0 line during the first two weeks of the season when Dowdle was active. Both backs will likely fall in the RB3/FLEX range if Dowdle suits up for Week 5’s game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 17 times for 93 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns, adding 33 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren’s six targets combine with his 17 carries to give him his second consecutive game with more than 20 opportunities in the absence of Rico Dowdle, seeing all but two running back opportunities in the process. More impressive was the fact that he once again maintained elite efficiency on the ground through the additional touches, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt against a solid Browns run defense. The veteran back appears likely to revert to a strict timeshare with Dowdle expected back for Week 5 after the long week, bringing him back to the RB3 range for a meeting with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports there is a “pretty good chance” Rico Dowdle (toe) returns in Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle did not practice this week and was ruled out for Thursday’s game against the Browns. Rapoport called him day-to-day. The mini-bye between today’s game and Pittsburgh’s Week 5 date with Indy at home should be enough rest to get Dowdle back on the field. Jaylen Warren will see almost the entirety of the backfield tonight before returning to committee duties once Dowdle is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-38 passes for 273 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Saints’ 16-10, Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough’s seven rushing yards led the team, which isn’t ideal. The 27-year-old was mostly accurate and on-time with his throws, but he should have had three turnovers on the first half — one dropped interception, one strip-sack that was overturned and one fumble that luckily went out of bounds — and he threw a costly red-zone interception. It wasn’t Shough at his best, but there were some flashes of brilliance in the loss. Shough will get a bye week before he faces the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in the Saints’ 34-27, Week 6 win over the Giants, adding five carries for 32 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints had their usual slow start on offense, going scoreless in the first quarter. Shough then did what he does best and led an effective offensive effort the rest of the way. He is dealing with broken bones in his non-throwing hand and it arguably impacted some of his throws, missing open receivers and struggling to push the ball downfield. Though he averaged 4.8 yards per attempt, he totaled three touchdowns on the day. Shough was also impactful as a runner, totaling 32 yards and a tush push touchdown on the day while also getting tackled inside the five-yard line on another rush. Two straight games have been impacted by Shough’s hand injury but the post-first quarter volume continues to elevate his fantasy floor. Shough is a high-end QB2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tyler Shough has two broken bones in his non-throwing hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Both Shough and Kellen Moore have given non-answers when asked about the quarterback’s left hand. Per Schefter, the injury could take a couple of months to heal, but it will not cost him any playing time. Shough injured his hand versus the Falcons in Week 4 and wore a protective glove in Week 5. He is coming off his two worst games of the year, though we don’t suspect the hand is to blame. Things get much easier this week with the Giants on tap. Shough will get another shot at a QB1 finish in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore, asked directly if Tyler Shough’s non-throwing hand is broken, said “it got banged two weeks ago and he’s just wearing some protective layers there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: So, probably, then. The hand hasn’t really been a contributing factor to New Orleans’ decline so much as the Saints offensive line has just been in the blender for two weeks against Atlanta and Minnesota’s fronts, but it sure looks like Shough is managing through something and we should probably break ties against him in the rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-25 passes for 96 yards and two interceptions in the Saints’ 23-13, Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough had been coasting on extreme play volume over the first month of the fantasy season. Brian Flores and the Vikings’ hyper-aggressive defense had no issues shutting down that approach. The Saints had five drives in the first half. Only one lasted longer than three plays. Of their four second-half drives, two ended with interceptions. A fumbled kickoff coming out of the break didn’t help the team’s play volume either. Shough has ultimately been a better fantasy quarterback than a real-life passer this year and the Vikings’ defense exposed that truth for the better part of four quarters. He will look to rebound against a far worse Giants unit in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As expected, he’ll start and be on the QB1/QB2 borderline against an extremely pesky and attacking Vikings defense that has held down quarterback scoring quite well so far this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As a right-handed quarterback, Shough should be fine despite his surprise appearance on the injury report. Even in a blowout loss on Monday, the second-year passer racked up 286 yards and a touchdown on 48 attempts. As long as the volume is there, Shough is good for low-end QB1 numbers. He will remain inside the top 12 at his position for Week 5 against Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-48 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 45-24, Week 4 loss to the Falcons, adding five yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough and the Saints stayed true to recent form as they quickly fell into a 14-point hole in the first quarter, with the team now averaging an almost eight point deficit at the half since head coach Kellen Moore took over to start the 2025 season. The team was unable to reproduce the second half magic they so frequently muster behind an overmatched offensive line. Shough needed a late touchdown toss to Devaughn Vele with less than two minutes to play to give fantasy managers something of value. Moore and Shough have their work cut out for them with Brian Flores’ relentless defense coming to town in Week 5, where Shough will be on the QB1/2 border in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints’ 27-35, Week 3 loss to the Raiders, adding one rush for 36 yards and two lost fumbles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough funneled four touchdown passes to Saints TEs Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, bringing the game’s total to six tight end touchdowns, which tied a league record. The Saints’ quarterback played well overall, though his interception was due to a poor throw. Both fumbles were caused by Raiders pass rushers, and Shough had a third fumble reversed by an illegal contact penalty on the Raiders. Regardless, he can be trusted to throw the ball voluminously while adding a little extra with his legs. He warrants low-end QB1 treatment against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 27-of-34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 24-17, Week 2 win over the Ravens, adding nine carries for 23 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough played mistake-free football all afternoon, chipping away at the Ravens’ defense before leading his team to 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Shough repeatedly connected with Chris Olave all afternoon, and he found the star receiver uncontested in the end zone for his lone touchdown. Shough punched in a one-yard score on a QB sneak with 1:21 left to put the Saints up 24-17 and complete the upset of the Ravens on the road. It wasn’t an overly flashy outing by Shough, but he was efficient against a stout Ravens defense, which still managed three sacks on the day. He’s now strung together two strong fantasy performances and will be on the radar as a high-end QB2 next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 19-of-30 passes for 219 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ 16-10, Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers dinked and dunked for the overwhelming majority of the game with over half of his completions coming to his running backs. He did connect with DK Metcalf for a 51-yard connection on a beautiful deep ball, and he found Darnell Washington for his lone scoring play. Outside of that passing touchdown, the biggest play for Rodgers was a scramble on third-and-six just before the two-minute warning that essentially cemented the game. Rodgers and the Steelers move to 5-2 with the win in Paris, and they’ll face the Browns in Week 8. He’ll be a QB2 for that contest, on paper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 33-of-49 passes for 253 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Steelers’ 26-19, Week 6 overtime win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers and the Steelers couldn’t get anything going through three quarters. They had just three points on the board and Germie Bernard check-downs were their only method of moving the ball. Even that was barely working. Running out of options, Rodgers simply started forcing the ball to DK Metcalf. He targeted Metcalf 12 times in the fourth quarter and overtime. The Steelers scored 16 points in the fourth quarter and another seven in the extra frame. Rodgers now has at least 230 yards and multiple touchdowns in four straight games. The Steelers’ pass-crazed approach under Mike McCarthy has kept him in the QB2 mix so far, and it will do so again when he faces the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 22-of-31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Steelers’ 34-22, Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The Steelers seemed worried about the Colts’ pass rush today, so there were a lot of quick-hit passes from Rodgers. The vast majority of them went to running backs or tight ends. Only nine of Rodgers’ 22 completions went to wide receivers, and 80 of his 235 passing yards came on a short pass to Jaylen Warren that the running back took up the sideline for a long touchdown. That’s not to say Rodgers didn’t play well. He did a good job avoiding sacks and not taking negative plays, but the Steelers’ offense didn’t look very potent outside of two explosive plays from Jaylen Warren. They may find things a little bit tougher against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 22-of-40 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Steelers’ 27-24, Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers was under constant pressure from an unrelenting Cleveland pass rush, taking five sacks while throwing two interceptions in the loss. The offense struggled to maintain consistent efficiency as the Steelers fell into a 21-7 hole in the second quarter, eventually requiring more Rodgers fourth quarter heroics to knot the game at 24 with under two minutes to play. That would be enough time for Deshaun Watson to get the Browns into field goal range for the go-ahead kick with 10 seconds remaining. With just one timeout in hand, the Steelers were forced into downfield aggression on the final play of the game, which resulted in the second of two Rodgers interceptions. The Steelers have now been involved in three one-score games through four weeks, something both Steelers fans and those familiar with head coach Mike McCarthy are all too familiar with - two of those games resulted in wins. Up next for Rodgers and the Steelers are the reeling Colts in Week 5, against whom Rodgers will remain a middling QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 19-of-34 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Steelers’ 30-27, Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers’ first throw of the game came on a 30-yard dump-off to Jaylen Warren, but three plays later, Rodgers would connect with a wide-open Roman Wilson down the left sideline for a 38-yard touchdown. That would be the first of two touchdowns Rodgers would throw in the first quarter, with his second coming on a play-action pass to Ben Skowronek for a 23-yard score. Rodgers and the offense would stall a bit in the second quarter, with an interception on a dropped pass by Roman Wilson highlighting their struggles, but in the second half, the Steelers would rip off four plays for 20-plus yards to keep the pressure on the Bengals’ defense. Rodgers threw a six-yard touchdown pass to DK Metcalf in the third quarter to put the Steelers up 24-20, and benefited from a long catch-and-run by Darnell Washington on a 47-yard play that helped set up an eventual field goal by Chris Boswell. This was easily the best game of the season for Rodgers, who averaged a solid 7.1 ADOT on his completed passes against a Bengals defense that was solid through the first two weeks. Despite the strong outing, Rodgers shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a QB2 in Thursday’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy “plans to pare down the game plan with the goal of executing the staple plays more consistently.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo penned a rather pessimistic assessment of the Steelers’ current state on Sunday night. We can’t necessarily blame him. The results have been disappointing. Perhaps thinning out the playbook will pay off. McCarthy believes QB Aaron Rodgers “could play with any volume of game plan, but at the end of the day, it’s a team game.” DeFabo notes that the Steelers moved WR DK Metcalf into the slot at times, attempting to avoid Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez’s coverage, but Gonzalez surprisingly trailed him, and Metcalf turned in an inefficient outing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 23-of-39 passes for 189 yards, an interception and a fumble in the Steelers’ 20-3, Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers led an anemic offense in a defense-heavy matchup with the Patriots for Week 2. The Steelers began the day with a couple of three-and-outs and were unable to find chunk plays the whole game. Rodgers fumbled in the second quarter on a play that pushed the Steelers back 37 yards due to a game of pinball in an effort to scoop up the ball; the play kicked the Steelers out of field goal territory. He later fumbled for a Pats scoop-and-score in the fourth quarter. Rodgers’ second turnover was an interception coming off a Germie Bernard bobble in the fourth quarter. A 4.8 yards per attempt mark indicates an offense that cannot push the ball downfield. Fantasy managers will not see chunk gains from Rodgers, who should be a fantasy QB3 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 24-of-40 passes for 221 yards and one touchdown in the Steelers’ 20-13, Week 1 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers averaged just 5.5 yards per completion and didn’t complete a single pass over 20 yards downfield, going 0-for-6. He was also just 4-for-14 for 64 yards when he was under pressure. That being said, he also didn’t make many bad decisions and threw a couple of beautiful passes in tight windows over the middle of the field. It’s a new season, but this doesn’t really feel much like a new Steelers’ offense, which means the ceiling might be low when it comes to fantasy production. Rodgers remains just a QB2 option next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Steelers kept all four quarterbacks for the team’s initial 53-man roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The Steelers will head into the regular season with Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar, who shined in training camp and during preseason outings in Mike McCarthy’s offense. If the 2026 season goes south for Pittsburgh, look for McCarthy to see what he has in Allar and perhaps Howard. Rudolph will likely back up Rodgers to start the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports that Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers could play one or two series in the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers may not play at all, and reports indicate that he, personally, could go either way on the matter. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy plans to play quarterbacks in three groups. The first two will split first-half reps, while the third plays for the entire second half. Shortly after this report, during pre-game warmups, Pryor said that “all signs are pointing to Rodgers being on the bench tonight.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Za’Darius Smith (neck) and Gervon Dexter Sr. (hamstring) will both play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: Both defenders were both listed as questionable for the Falcons, but both of them will be able to suit up, which is great news for the Falcons against a really banged-up 49ers offense. It remains to be seen if either player will play a full complement of snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Za’Darius Smith (neck) is expected to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: The same is true of Gervon Dexter, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Rapoport added that there is “much less optimism” for Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). That could mean an uptick in snaps for rookie wideout Zachariah Branch. He’s worth an add in deep leagues, but this offense isn’t likely to support another fantasy-relevant pass-catcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Falcons declared DE Za’Darius Smith, LB Christian Harris, QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, OL Ethan Onianwa, DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, and DB Robert Longerbeam inactive for Week 5 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: The Falcons remain one of the healthier teams in the league as they enter Week 5 with no major injuries amongst skill position players. They’ll look to maintain the momentum under starting quarterback Michael Penix, who has won his first two starts of the season, against the stingy Ravens on Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Falcons declared QB Tua Tagovailoa, QB Michael Penix, DB Billy Bowman Jr., DB Malcom DeWalt IV, ILB Christian Harris, and OL Ethan Onianwa inactive for Week 1 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: We knew earlier this week that both Penix (knee) and Tagovailoa (back) would be sidelined, and that Cooper Rush would start. EDGE Za’Darius Smith was listed as questionable with a shoulder injury, but he will suit up for this one. Christian Harris, who had been a favorite to start at inside linebacker, is a healthy inactive, which means rookies Kendal Daniels or Harold Perkins Jr. will see extended run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Falcons signed EDGE Za’Darius Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: Smith signed with the Eagles and appeared in five games before abruptly announcing his retirement in October of last year. He worked out for the Browns, one of his many former teams, as recently as last week. Now Jonathan Jones of the Athletic reports the Falcons have signed Smith for pass rush help. It’s unclear how much the 33-year-old EDGE has left in the tank. The last time Smith played a full season was in 2024 when he recorded nine sacks in 17 games with the Browns and Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Free agent EDGE Za’Darius Smith worked out for the Browns on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: Smith, 33, retired in October 2025 as a member of the Eagles. The team released him from the reserve/retired list in June, officially making him a free agent. He is apparently hoping to continue his career. Smith played for the Browns in Weeks 1-9 during the 2024 season before being traded to the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Eagles released Za’Darius Smith from the reserve/retired list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: Smith announced his retirement in the middle of the 2025 season after signing a one-year deal with Philly just ahead of Week 1. His release makes him a free agent and is an indication that he plans to return to football this year. Smith totaled 1.5 sacks in five games with the Eagles last year. He is likely a part-time player at this point in his career, but Smith still has enough left in the tank to contribute on a playoff-caliber roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Eagles EDGE Za’Darius Smith retired from the NFL after 11 seasons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: This one comes as a bit of a surprise after Smith signed a one-year contract with the Eagles shortly before Week 1, and played in the team’s Week 6 loss to the Giants on Thursday night. The former fourth-round pick who first entered the league with the Ravens in 2015 walks away from the game with 70.5 career sacks on his resumé to go with 87 TFLs and 10 forced fumbles. Smith’s most productive seasons came with the Packers, who he signed a four-year contract with during the 2019 offseason. He earned back-to-back Pro Bowl nods during his first two years in Green Bay, racking up 26 sacks over that span and also received Second-Team All-Pro honors in 2020. Smith’s decision to walk away leaves an already banged up Eagles defense another man short. They will likely look to bring on another veteran pass rusher in the coming days to make up for his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: Eagles signed EDGE Za’Darius Smith to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: After sitting out all offseason, Smith hooks on with the Eagles on a ring-chaser contract for the season. Smith had nine sacks as well as 50 hurries per PFF charting in 2025. He’ll give Philadelphia a sure-fire outside rusher on passing downs and possibly could have a bigger role than that depending on how thing shake out in the defensive line rotation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports “multiple contending names” have checked in on FA EDGE Za’Darius Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zadarius-s.analysis: Smith has been linked to the Lions all offseason, with both sides noting that they had mutual interest and Brad Holmes hinting that Smith had no interest in going through training camp at this stage of his career. With Josh Paschal out an extended period of time, the Lions interest likely has only grown in a reunion at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Denzel Ward (hand) is active for Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Ward missed some practice time this week with a right hand injury. He’ll suit up against Cam Ward and the atrocious Titans passing attack. Browns declared QB Taylen Green, LB Justin Jefferson, CB Noah Igbinoghene, RB Audric Estime, DT Mike Hall Jr., and C Parker Brailsford inactive against Tennessee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Grant Delpit (concussion) will play in Week 7 against the
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Delpit cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend and is good to go. Denzel Ward, on the other hand, will go through warmups to see if he can play. Ward is dealing with a hand injury and is listed as questionable for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Denzel Ward (hand) was limited in Friday’s practice and is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Ward popped up on the injury report today. Friday pop-up questionables are always tough to understand from the outside without any major reporting, but it stands to reason that Ward has a real chance to miss the game based on the listing. The Browns cleared Carson Schwesinger (ankle) from the report, so at least their star linebacker will be in there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns signed CB Denzel Ward to a two-year, $62.2 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: $52.3 million of the contract is guaranteed. It’s a huge payday for a 29-year-old cornerback, but Ward has been a stalwart for the Browns defense his entire career and hasn’t shown any real signs of aging just yet. He had two years remaining on his contract, so it’s likely that most of that guaranteed money just ties him to the Browns through 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi believes Browns CB Denzel Ward could be extended this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Browns beat writers have been very careful to say that they don’t know why Ward didn’t participate in mandatory minicamp — Todd Monken said nothing when asked about it — but it does have the whiff of a hold in situation. Ward has no guaranteed salary remaining on his deal entering his age-29 season, so it feels like a no-brainer for him to get some sort of adjustment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns general manager Andrew Berry said the team is not interested in trading CB Denzel Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Berry fielded questions after trading EDGE Myles Garrett to the Rams in exchange for EDGE Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. Understandably, reporters wanted to know if Ward, whom the team drafted via the No. 4 overall pick in 2018, one year after the team drafted Garrett No. 1 overall, was also available for trade. Berry restructured both players’ contracts this offseason and told the media that Garrett was not on the trade block. He could be telling the truth here, but the fact remains that trading away a talented, yet aging, cornerback could net decent draft capital for a team that is seemingly attempting a speedy reset.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns restructured the contract of CB Denzel Ward, saving $2 million against the cap in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: The franchise converted a $2.5 million roster bonus into a signing bonus, saving $2 million against the cap in 2026 while adding $500,000 to his cap hit for each subsequent season. This comes a day after the Browns restructured the contract of quarterback Deshaun Watson. The rebuilding Browns remain unlikely to make major splashes in free agency but at least these moves give them options in the coming months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns OG Wyatt Teller (calf) is inactive for Week 16 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Teller was questionable entering the weekend but has been ruled out. Backup Teven Jenkins will start in his place. In addition to Teller, the Browns have also ruled out CB Denzel Ward, RB Dylan Sampson, DT Mike Hall Jr., WR Jamari Thrash, TE David Njoku, and DT Sam Kamara.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns CB Denzel Ward (calf) will not play in Cleveland’s Week 16 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: He didn’t practice all week for the second-straight week and, again, carries some IR shutdown risk over the weekend ahead of Sunday’s game. If he remains active, Ward starts Week 17 firmly on the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns CB Denzel Ward (calf) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 15 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Ward did not practice at any point this week since suffering the injury in Week 14. He certainly could be a candidate for an IR shut down with the Browns eliminated from the playoffs. Ward has had the worst PFF coverage grade of his career so far in 2025, at 54.4 in 701 defensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and will get San Francisco’s Week 8 bye to recover. The 33-year-old’s absence will leave veterans Christian Kirk and Brandin Cooks along with youngsters Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins on the 49ers receiver depth chart for Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: NBC Sports’ Jennifer Lee Chan reported earlier this week that Evans is expected to “miss a little time,” making his two absences unsurprising. Evans has not been formally ruled out, and he is no stranger to playing through injury, but fantasy managers should expect him to miss the 49ers’ Week 7 game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans is already expected to miss “a little time” because of his Achilles tendinitis, so this isn’t a surprise. It’s safe to assume he’s out for at least Week 7, but the good news is that it’s not expected to be a long-term issue. Evans could be back as soon as Week 9 following the 49ers’ bye week. With Deebo Samuel all but ruled out for this week’s matchup with Atlanta, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins are set for starting roles on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Deebo Samuel (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Neither did Mike Evans, who is dealing with Achilles tendinitis. These absences shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Evans is expected to miss Week 7 after aggravating his Achilles issue on Monday. Samuel is expected to miss “at least a couple of weeks” and has been sidelined for just one game so far. Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks are in line to start for the 49ers this week. What a time to be alive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reports Mike Evans’ Achilles is intact but he is expected to “miss a little time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Chan speculates that the window for his recovery could align with the team’s Week 8 bye week, meaning Evans would miss just one game with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable heading into Monday Night Football against the Commanders. All things considered, it’s solid news for Evans, the 49ers, and his fantasy managers. Expect a more concrete update from the team in the coming days as they limp into a Week 7 game against the Falcons down plentiful impact wide receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) limped to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans came into the game with two injury designations, ribs and Achilles, ultimately suiting up. He limped to the locker room with the help of training staff and was seen in the tunnel pointing to his Achilles. The 33-year-old receiver has been on the injury report for much of the season, with the most recent ailment potentially proving to be too much to play through. Expect an update from the team after the half. Evans caught 3-of-5 targets for 94 yards prior to departing. 49ers beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reported after the game that Evans’ Achilles is intact but will “miss a little time.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is active for Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans will gut it out in Week 6 as fellow wide receiver Deebo Samuel is unable to go. Look for the bulk of the aerial offense to flow through Evans, George Kittle, and Christian McCaffrey, the three of whom handily led the team in route participation a week ago following Samuel’s departure. Inactive for the 49ers are QB Kurtis Rourke, DE Nick Bosa, WR Deebo Samuel, S Marques Sigle, LB Garret Wallow, OT Enrique Cruz Jr., and DT Naquan Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, Adam Schefter said “the 49ers are optimistic” Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) will play in Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans did not log a practice in the days leading up to Monday night’s game against the Commanders, but the team still listed him as questionable on Saturday. Schefter reports the Niners want to see how Evans looks during pregame warmups, but it sounds like they are somewhat hopeful he will be active for Monday’s game. Evans has caught 24 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns this season and went for 7-113-1 on 10 targets in last week’s win over the Seahawks. He would be a must-start on Monday against Washington if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans was unable to practice through Friday but ultimately did enough to land a questionable tag with multiple injury designations. However likely it is that Evans continues to play through various ailments, fantasy managers could look to make alternate plans considering the timing of the 49ers’ game on Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins declared WR Jalen Tolbert, LB Willie Gay, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., CB Reese Taylor, DE Rob Beal Jr., OL DJ Campbell, and OT Chukwuebuka Godrick inactive for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: With Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell both healthy, Tolbert doesn’t have a spot on the game-day roster and is a healthy scratch this week. Douglas is back after missing a month because of an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins declared QB Brady Cook, DE Chop Robinson, WR Jalen Tolbert, OL DJ Campbell, CB Marcellus Dial Jr., TE Justin Joly, and OT Chukwuebuka Godrick inactive for Week 2 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Robinson remains in concussion protocol and was ruled out earlier in the week. Interestingly, Jalen Tolbert remains unable to be active on a Dolphins team that is hurting for weapons on offense. A lot of it has to do with him not having a clear role on special teams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins declared WR Jalen Tolbert, QB Brady Cook, CB Reese Taylor, OG DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 1 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Tolbert is listed as a second-stringer on the Dolphins’ depth, reinforcing coach Jeff Hafley’s confidence in rookie WRs Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas. Those two are listed as starters alongside slot WR Malik Washington. A wait-and-see approach is probably smart for the rookies, but they can be started in the FLEX spot as needed. Cook will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones believes Jalen Tolbert “appeared to be” one of Malik Willis’ top targets in OTAs and minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Furones also lists Greg Dulcich as a player that was a primary receiver for Willis, but we’ve done plenty of offseason hype on Dulcich. Tolbert appears to be a potential “someone has to catch a ball here” deep league pick, as he’s well off the fantasy radar at this point. He’s not off the board among the top-100 wideouts in ADP. The ceiling is likely low, but if he can emerge as the top option amongst Miami’s wideouts, Tolbert could be a viable WR3/WR4 at points this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: The Miami Herald’s Omar Kelly reports that Dolphins WR Jalen Tolbert distanced himself from his peers, but believes the receiver unit “doesn’t have a single player who would start for another NFL team.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Oh, boy. Kelly giveth and taketh away. On the one hand, Kelly believes Tolbert “seems ready to handle the split end, possession receiver role.” On the other hand, Kelly thinks Tolbert is a replacement-level player. Tolbert has cleared 275 receiving yards just once in his four-year career. Kelly is probably right. If Tolbert can become the clear-cut No. 1 target, he might be able to return FLEX value, but he could be an extremely volatile producer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team’s passing offense is “a work in progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Malik Willis, Hafley said during a Tuesday presser, is still building chemistry with the team’s pass catchers in OTAs and working on timing. That presumably includes Malik Washington, who had 46 catches for 317 yards and three scores last season, and Greg Dulcich, who’s expected by Miami beat writers to “figure heavily” into the team’s passing attack in 2026. Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell could also see heavy snaps in the Miami passing game this season. Tolbert, who flashed in Dallas in 2024 with 610 yards and seven touchdowns, could emerge as the Dolphins’ top pass-catching option with a solid training camp. There likely won’t be much target volume to go around, however, considering the team’s plans to operate a run-heavy offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Dolphins signed WR Jalen Tolbert, formerly of the Cowboys, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schlutz reports Tolbert is “close with Malik Willis,” who was signed by the Dolphins earlier this week. A former third-round pick of the 2022 NFL Draft, Tolbert never emerged as a top option in the Cowboys’ passing game. Last season, the 27-year-old had his least productive season since his rookie year, catching 18 passes for 203 yards and one touchdown despite appearing on 464 offensive snaps. With Jaylen Waddle being the only starter of note in Miami’s receiver room, it’s possible Tolbert carves out a more meaningful role this season, but we wouldn’t bet on there being much fantasy value here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Jalen Tolbert failed to catch his only target in a Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: We’re just a couple of years away from Tolbert being thought of as a potential fantasy sleeper. Instead, the 26-year-old will finish with 18 catches on 34 targets for 203 yards and one touchdown. He’ll enter free agency this offseason, but doesn’t figure to command a lot of interest as anything other than a depth option to round out a team’s wide receiver corps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Cowboys declared DE Jadeveon Clowney, WR Jalen Tolbert, RB Jaydon Blue, DT Jay Toia, DT Perrion Winfrey and OT Tyler Guyton inactive for Week 14 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: Clowney (hamstring) attempted to give it a go in warmups after practicing once, a limited session on Wednesday, this week. He will be missed against the Lions’ top-notch offense. The Cowboys have once again declared Blue, the once-exciting rookie, inactive this week. He does not need to be stashed at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.headline: Jalen Tolbert caught 2-of-2 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-tolb.analysis: A 35-yard bomb from Joe Milton hit Tolbert square in the hands — a thing of beauty — as the Cowboys were down 27 in the fourth quarter. Tolbert playing at that point tells you all you need to know about how his season is going, as he fell behind Ryan Flournoy with eight snaps to Flournoy’s 28. Neither player is fantasy-interesting with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens vacuuming up the targets in this offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Bengals declared S Russ Yeas, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, DE Shemar Stewart, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 7 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: The Bengals are coming off their bye at near-full strength, with all five inactives healthy scratches. Stewart, who was the No. 17 overall pick in last year’s draft, has appeared in just three games this season, totaling three tackles and one sack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Bears ruled out CB Kyler Gordon (calf) for Week 4 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: Gordon, LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) are all in the process of returning from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. None of them will play this week. Fill-in starting DB Cam Lewis (hip) is doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Bengals declared EDGE Shemar Stewart, WR Ke’Shawn Williams, CB Josh Newton, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries and DL Landon Robinson inactive for Week 1 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: The Bengals would obviously prefer Stewart to be out there vs. the Bucs, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Bengals CB DJ Turner (hamstring) will play in Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: Turner popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the hamstring issue, but head coach Zac Taylor said the fourth-year corner will be good to go for Sunday’s game. Turner posted career highs in pass breakups (18) and interceptions (2) last season while earning a PFF coverage grade of 78.1. The Bengals will rely heavily on him in Week 1 to slow down Baker Mayfield and a revamped Buccaneers passing game. While Turner is healthy and good to go, Taylor said DE Shemar Stewart (knee) is doubtful, making him unlikely to play in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Shemar Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: Stewart was able to limp off the field but eventually rode the cart to the locker room, causing some concern that he suffered a major injury. He will undergo treatment for the issue but, according to Rapoport, avoided any ligament damage. Bengals coach Zac Taylor said he would miss “several weeks.” That’s not ideal for a second-year player, but it doesn’t sound like he is at risk of missing any time during the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Shemar Stewart suffered a leg injury during Wednesday’s practice and was carted off the field.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: Stewart initially limped off the field and was checked out by trainers before riding the cart into the locker room. The fact that he was able to make his way off the field hopefully means this isn’t a major injury, but it’s too early to be sure. The No. 17 overall pick last year struggled with ankle injuries early in his rookie season and later dealt with a knee issue. He appeared in just eight games and recorded one sack. The Bengals were hoping for a year two breakout from Stewart, but he might be in for another slow start if the latest injury costs him much time in camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Bengals HC Zac Taylor said Shemar Stewart (knee) will play in Week 16 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: Stewart was designated for a return from injured reserve last week and will now take the field against the Dolphins this weekend. The rookie pass-rusher has totaled just six tackles in the five games he’s appeared in this season and is still in search of his first career sack. In addition to Stewart, Taylor also said DT B.J. Hill (ankle) will be available to play in Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Bengals designated EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: Stewart will return to practice this week. The Bengals now have 21 days to activate him from injured reserve. The first-round rookie hasn’t played much this year because of ankle and knee injuries. He has six combined tackles and eight pressures in five appearances so far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Bengals EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) will be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: Stewart missed multiple games with an ankle injury and is now set to miss at least the next four games due to a knee injury. The 22-year-old defensive end will miss most of his rookie season due to injury and his play wasn’t anything to write home about when he was actually on the field. His 36.9 overall PFF grade was dead last among 114 defensive ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.headline: Bengals EDGE Trey Hendrickson (hip) won’t play in Cincinnati’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shemar-ste.analysis: It remains to be seen when Hendrickson will play again, as he did not practice all week. Shemar Stewart (knee) also remains out with a long-term injury. Pittsburgh’s offense should be able to get back on track against one of the NFL’s weakest defenses this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) is inactive for New York’s Week 7 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson was doubtful before being ruled out. He’ll have a chance to come back after New York’s Week 8 bye. Also inactive for the Giants are: OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow (knee), CB Greg Newsome II (concussion), S Jevón Holland (concussion), QB Jake Haener (3rd QB) and CB Nikko Reed. OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and Tyler Nubin (neck) are playing despite being tagged as questionable on Friday.
