https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) is doubtful for Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but he can help out the Giants’ offense in real life when he is available. Isaiah Likely is the Giants’ clear-cut TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (neck) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson looks to be on track to returning to the field after missing Week 6, though he’s not doing anything fantasy-interesting at this point as Isaiah Likely has taken over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Mooney should be good to go this week, but he does not need to be on fantasy football rosters. Giants TE Theo Johnson (neck) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants declared TE Theo Johnson, CB Colton Hood, QB Jake Haener, S Tyler Nubin, OL Jermaine Eluemunor, and DL C.J. Okoye inactive for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson was declared out heading into the weekend with a neck injury. Also out due to injury are Hood (concussion), Eluemunor (calf), and Nubin (neck). Expect to see more Thomas Fidone behind Isaiah Likely at the tight end position with Johnson out against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) will not play in New York’s Week 6 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: It’s Thomas Fidone hours in New York, marone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (shoulder) is practicing fully for Week 1 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson was seen practicing in a non-contact jersey last week, so today’s full session is positive. Unfortunately, Johnson’s path to fantasy football TE1 status is likely blocked by TE Isaiah Likely, so Johnson is not on the radar for most leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (shoulder) participated in practice Tuesday wearing a non-contact jersey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: John Harbaugh has said that Johnson “will be fine,” but we’re going to cover our bases on this one with the Giants keeping five tight ends. Johnson has a week and change to get healthy for Sunday Night Football in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: North Jersey’s Art Stapleton reports that Giants TE Isaiah Likely and TE Theo Johnson are currently the team’s top-two pass catchers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: This is the third positive report in as many months for Likely, who is set to handle TE1 duties for his new team. Johnson is slated for the TE2 role after posting a 45/528/5 receiving line in his second NFL season last year. Giants WR1 Malik Nabers recently underwent a clean-up procedure on his knee and field-stretching WR Darius Slayton is recovering from core muscle surgery. Nabers will retake the No. 1 pass-catching role when healthy. Slayton, 29, is on the downslope. Likely is in the low-end TE1 tier and could improve his stock through the spring and summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans declared S Jalen Pitre (shoulder), RB David Montgomery (groin), S Reed Blankenship (concussion), T Blake Fisher (thumb), OL Febechi Nwaiwu, OL Nate Thomas and TE Marlin Klein inactive for Houston’s Week 7 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Both Pitre and Montgomery, who are week-to-week, have a chance to come back after Houston’s Week 8 bye. They’ve both missed two weeks now with their respective injuries. The latter three are healthy scratches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans S Jalen Pitre is week-to-week with an AC joint sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre suffered a left shoulder injury in Week 5, now revealed to be an AC joint sprain. The good news is he won’t require surgery or go on injured reserve, but the 27-year-old is considered “week-to-week.” Given the designation, Pitre seems unlikely to play Week 6 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed C.J. Stroud (concussion) cleared protocol and will start against the Colts on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Jalen Pitre, too, cleared protocol and will take on the current AFC South leaders. Stroud will be on the QB2 line after a long layoff, but has done reasonably well against the Colts over his two NFL seasons to date. Indianapolis’ defense, while improved with the return of Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner, isn’t a bad matchup from a fantasy perspective.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said C.J. Stroud’s (concussion) status for Week 12 against the Bills is uncertain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Something similar was reported on Sunday morning, but speaking on Monday, Ryans confirmed that Stroud may not return this week. The Texans’ QB1 remains in the league’s concussion protocol, but the Texans playing on Thursday night only adds to the complications. Stroud has missed two straight games due to his concussion, but the Texans have managed to go 2-0 in his absence with Davis Mills under center. Mills has thrown for 566 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in his two starts this season, but shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a desperation play in 2QB/superflex leads if he draws the start. Ryans said S Jalen Pitre, who is also in the concussion protocol, is uncertain for Thursday night’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans EDGE Will Anderson (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: He will be around to harass Trevor Lawrence on Sunday. Jalen Pitre (concussion) was ruled out, giving some extra space for Parker Washington to move around in the slot against Houston’s backup cornerbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans signed CB/S Jalen Pitre to a three-year, $39 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the deal has $29.156 million in guarantees. Pitre missed the back half of last season with a pectoral tear, but excelled in his new role as Texans nickel corner with a career-best 71.3 PFF coverage grade. This isn’t a needle-moving re-signing, but clearly Houston valued their slot corner highly to get this done ahead of the draft. Pitre was set to enter the final year of his rookie contract in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Texans S Jalen Pitre (pectoral) will undergo season-ending surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre reportedly suffered a partially torn pectoral muscle and will undergo a repair that will sideline him for the remainder of the year. Pitre is technically a safety but primarily functions as the Texans’ slot DB, which is notable for fantasy purposes. Pitre finishes with a team-high 31 coverage tackles and six passes defended.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans DB Jalen Pitre (pectoral) is expected to miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: He partially tore the pec in Week 12’s loss against the Titans. His absence put Eric Murray on to the field as a deep safety and Jimmie Ward moved up to be the main nickel for Houston. Ward caught a pick-six in Pitre’s absence, so perhaps the drop-off won’t be stark, but Murray has never been a great defender. Pitre had been having the best season of his career with a 79.5 PFF run grade in 660 defensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Jalen Pitre (shoulder) left Houston’s Week 12 game against the Titans and was ruled out.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre initially was ruled questionable. He left in the second quarter without his helmet and was not spotted on the sidelines at the beginning of the second half. The Texans moved Jimmie Ward into the nickel safety spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Peyton Manning is not expected to be a candidate for the Colts’ general manager vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Manning was floated as a potential replacement for Chris Ballard after the latter was fired, but it was just baseless speculation. According to Schefter, the Colts have not discussed hiring Manning in any capacity. With no front office experience to his name and loads of media obligations to tend to, it doesn’t make sense for Manning to take a job with an NFL team at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Dan Patrick of The Dan Patrick Show said a source familiar with the Colts’ GM situation told him the team’s “first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Patrick isn’t a reporter we go to often here, but he’s a well-connected veteran in the industry. According to Patrick, his source said the call with Manning will not only be to get the names of potential candidates for the GM vacancy but also to “explore whether or not Peyton would be interested in being a general manager for the Colts as the entry point that would include ownership interest in the Colts.” Mannings’ connection to the Colts doesn’t need to be explained to anyone, but it’s far too early to say whether Manning has any interest in the role. Long-time GM Chris Ballard was recently relieved of his duties, and the Colts will likely speak to several candidates to fill the role in the offseason. Manning has not been involved in any football front office roles since retiring after the 2015 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Peyton Manning has been elected to the Pro Football Hall-of-Fame.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: The absolutely loaded 2021 class also includes Calvin Johnson. Alongside fantasy legends Manning and Megatron, DB Charles Woodson, S John Lynch, OG Alan Faneca, WR Drew Pearson, executive Bill Nunn and coach Tom Flores will also be enshrined. One of the greatest players in league history, Manning also helped fundamentally change the way the game is played his hyper-accurate, precision passing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Bleacher Report’s Kalyn Kahler reports Peyton Manning has had “offers to run teams.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Since retiring in 2016, Manning has bounced from organization to organization informally taking notes on how teams are operated, particularly with scouting. There have been a few reports of Manning having offers to be a general manager, although the future Hall of Fame quarterback denies that a written offer has never been presented. It’s clear that Manning has some degree of interest in an executive role, but it’s unclear if he’ll actually accept a position at any point in the near future. People around Manning believe he’d be better as a general manager than as a television analyst because of how much he likes being hands on. He will likely have offers to go in either direction for the next decade. In the meantime, Manning has commercials to film.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Peyton Manning is 0-5 in Foxboro in his career, with 15 interceptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: If you own Ty Law in IDP leagues, be sure to start him, as he owns seven of those picks. We really don’t expect Manning to continue to struggle this badly against New England, but neither will he have his best game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Coach Tony Dungy wants to see his starting offense get more time together in Saturday’s preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Quarterback Peyton Manning, wide receiver Marvin Harrison, running back Edgerrin James and the No. 1 offense are slated for a heavier workload, perhaps playing a good way into the second quarter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Peyton Manning said Tuesday night on Letterman that he’d be willing to defer money to help the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Consider the place he’s saying it, but Manning was quoted saying, ''I want to be a Colt for life, and so they’ll start doing that probably maybe next year, the year after. . . . You do what you can to help build the team around you, to keep some of the good players and get some new young players.’'

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: When asked about how much his starters will play in week 17, coach Tony Dungy said, “They’ll all play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: We doubt they’ll play much. A scheduling oddity has them facing the Broncos, their most likely playoff opponent, at the end of the season for the second straight year. The Broncos punked the Colts late last season before getting embarrased in the playoffs. It could happen again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Colts owner Jim Irsay reiterated his faith that the Colts will re-sign Peyton Manning, making him the highest paid player in the league.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Manning is an unrestricted free agent, but there doesn’t appear to be any chance of this deal not getting done. The team could also franchise him, but that would cost $18.4 million against the cap this season, so a long-term deal would make more sense. Marvin Harrison and Edgerrin James are both free agents after this season. Keeping all 3 may prove difficult.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: The Colts deadline to get Peyton Manning signed to a long-term deal is today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Colts fans everywhere should be crossing their fingers because their team’s depth will seriously suffer if a deal is not reached. Manning is currently the Colts franchise player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Alontae Taylor is expected to be active for Week 7 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: Taylor, who was signed to a three-year, $60 million contract in the offseason, was a healthy scratch last week. That appears to be a temporary benching as Taylor will be back in the mix against Cleveland. Pro Football Focus currently has Taylor ranked 101st in coverage grade among all corners. His return doesn’t move the needle for Tennessee’s defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Titans agreed to terms with CB Alontae Taylor, formerly of the Saints, on a three-year, $60 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: $42 million is fully guaranteed as the Titans continue to spend heavily on their defense in Day 1 of free agency. They’ve added Cordale Flott and Taylor to the cornerback room. Taylor’s ideal fit is in the slot, but he has worked outside at times for the Saints and his role in Tennessee is probably dependent on what happens with former free-agent bust L’Jarius Sneed. Flott and Taylor will try to repair Tennessee’s pass defense under new head coach Robert Saleh.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (ankle) is active for Week 9 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: Both Kamara and Shaheed remained limited throughout all three practices this week. Kamara is a borderline RB2/3 while Shaheed, who injured his hip on the Saints’ final Week 8 drive, is a WR3. Saints CB Alontae Taylor (shoulder) is also active. The Saints declared DT John Ridgeway, DT Khristian Boyd, CB Rejzohn Wright, DB Ugo Amadi, OG Xavier Truss and TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden inactive for Week 9 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Saints ruled out EDGE Chase Young (calf) for Week 1 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: Young’s absence is a tough loss to stomach for a transitioning Saints’ defense. Veteran EDGE Cameron Jordan will start in Young’s stead. CB Alontae Taylor was cleared to play after successfully rehabbing a groin injury suffered on August 8th. Saints OG Trevor Penning (toe) will also miss the game, weakening the left side of New Orleans’ offensive line. Although the Saints’ first-round rookie LT Kelvin Banks Jr. can be expected to hold his own, the coaching staff would undoubtedly prefer to have a proven veteran on the field next to him. Penning is backed up by former Titans starter, OG Dillon Radunz.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Saints activated CB Alontae Taylor from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: The No. 49 overall pick of the draft, Taylor had missed the past four games with a knee issue. His return comes as the Saints are missing Marshon Lattimore. Taylor could actually see some snaps Thursday evening against the Cardinals. He was on the field for 19 plays in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Saints selected Alabama CB Alontae Taylor with the No. 49 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: Taylor (6’0/199) made 31 starts over the course of his four-year career with the Volunteers. He was an on-again, off-again starter over his first three years. During that time, he posted average PFF grades over 1,623 snaps while recording two interceptions and nine pass breakups. His senior year saw a huge breakout. His PFF grade grew by nearly 30 points from his junior year going from 56.4 to 83.1. He had three games where he graded over 80 in both overall and coverage while also accumulating two interceptions and four pass breakups. Taylor has the size, length, and speed to thrive on the outside. He struggles mightly with change of direction and isn’t the best mover outside of straight-line speed. Taylor projects to play both the slot and on the outside for the Saints in Year 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: PFN’s Tony Pauline reports that Tennessee DB Alontae Taylor has had top-30 visits with the Cincinnati Bengals, Las Vegas Raiders, Houston Texans, and Tennessee Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: Per Pauline, some teams see Taylor as a CB, while others see him as a S. “Right now, he’s getting grades that range from late Round 3 to the early fourth,” Pauline wrote. Taylor ran a 4.36 forty with a 1.50 10-yard split at 6’0/199 at the NFL Combine.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Tennessee freshman CB Alontae Taylor was ejected for what was described as a “flagrant hit” during the first quarter of Saturday’s game against Alabama.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: Taylor didn’t last long in a game Alabama led 21-0 before the first quarter reached the halfway point. With the loss of the freshman starter Tennessee, which was already down two cornerbacks, sees its depth problem at the position get even worse against one of the nation’s most prolific passing attacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Rivals recruiting analysts Woody Wommack and Rob Cassidy called Tennessee four-star 2017 ATH Alontae Taylor an “electric playmaker.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: Taylor was one of the standout performers at the Adidas East Coast Invitational on Saturday. Wrote the Rivals team, “Offensive weapons like Taylor don’t come along very often so the Vols were smart in making him an early priority.” The 5-foot-11, 180-pounder plays quarterback at Coffee County Central (Tennessee), but he will likely transition to wideout with the Volunteers. He ranks as Rivals’ No. 248 overall prospect for the 2018 cycle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.headline: Rivals recruiting analysts Rob Cassidy, Chad Simmons and Woody Wommack tagged Tennessee four-star 2017 verbal ATH commit Alontae Taylor as one of the standouts from the Rivals 3 Stripe Camp in St. Louis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alontae-ta.analysis: “Taylor was so impressive that he almost made getting open look effortless, even when battling the event’s top defensive backs,” noted the trio of analysts. “Taylor’s progression from year to year has been very impressive and the more comfortable he becomes as a wide receiver, the better he seems to perform.” The 5-foot-11, 180-pounder had previously been playing quarterback at Coffee County Central (Tennessee) before shifting over to wideout. Rivals ranks him as the No. 143 overall prospect for the 2018 cycle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Grant Delpit (concussion) will play in Week 7 against the
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend and is good to go. Denzel Ward, on the other hand, will go through warmups to see if he can play. Ward is dealing with a hand injury and is listed as questionable for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns G Teven Jenkins (back) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 3 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: He did not practice at any point this week and looks to be questionable for Week 4. The Browns also listed CB Tyson Campbell (hip, ankle) and Grant Delpit (shoulder) as questionable. Browns coach Todd Monken said he’s “hopeful” Campbell and Delpit will go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns signed Grant Delpit to a three-year, $48 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the deal includes $35 million guaranteed. Delpit was set to play out the final year of his current contract in 2026 before landing this new deal. He totaled four pass breakups, one intercpetion, and a career-high three sacks in 2025. Though the pass-rushing production is unlikely to hold up this year, Delpit is a versatile safety on a defense that traded Myles Garrett in the offseason. Keeping him around beyond 2026 made sense for both sides.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns S Grant Delpit (concussion) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit missed Week 6 with the concussion after missing all three practices. A return on Wednesday gives him a good shot at suiting up on Sunday. The Browns’ starting strong safety has 32 tackles and four TFLs this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns S Grant Delpit (concussion) will not play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit suffered the concussion in Week 5 and did not practice this week before being ruled out. Fellow starting safety Ronnie Hickman Jr. (ankle) was also ruled out. Cleveland’s depleted secondary will be an easy target for a returning duo of A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns S Grant Delpit (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit suffered the concussion in the fourth quarter of Cleveland’s Week 5 loss to the Commanders and did not return. He is now in the league’s concussion protocol. Delpit has 32 tackles, four TFLs, and one fumble recovery this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns S Grant Delpit is being evaluated for a concussion and will not return to Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit was down on the field for a while after a big hit in the fourth quarter. He was able to walk off the field under his own power but will not return to the game with Cleveland trailing by three touchdowns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns ruled out S Grant Delpit (groin) for Saturday’s Wild Card game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit was designated for return earlier this week but won’t be cleared in time for Saturday’s contest. The veteran safety hasn’t played since Week 14’s contest against the Jaguars and will now miss a fifth-consecutive game with the injury. Delpit signed a new deal with the Browns prior to his injury and has totaled 63 tackles, seven TFLs, and one interception in 13 games this season. In addition to Delpit, the Browns also ruled out WR Cedric Tillman (concussion).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns S Grant Delpit was designated to return from injured reserve and practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury in December and now the Browns open his practice window with Wild Card Weekend looming. He got in a limited practice on Wednesday, opening the door for a potential return on Saturday. Fellow defensive backs Juan Thornhill (calf) and Greg Newsome (knee) also practiced in a limited capacity as the secondary prepares for C.J. Stroud and company.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.headline: Browns placed S Grant Delpit on injured reserve with a groin injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grant-delp.analysis: Delpit just signed a three year extension over the weekend, and now his regular season will be finished. It’s a brutal blow for Cleveland just as they get cornerback Denzel Ward back from injury. Delpit is a former 2020 second-round pick who has started 36 of the 45 games he’s appeared in. This season, he’s totaled 80 tackles, seven TFLs, 1.5 sacks, and one interception. The Browns signed S Duron Harmon to the active roster to take Delpit’s place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Nick Emmanwori (hip) is expected to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: Uchenna Nwosu, also dealing with a hip injury, is also expected to suit up. No free lunch for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs this week. The Seahawks will be at full force. Facing the best defense in the league by most measures, Mahomes is on the QB1/2 border for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Drew Lock (right elbow) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: The Seahawks’ backup quarterback is dealing with an injury in his throwing arm, so any calls for Sam Darnold’s benching will have to quiet down. Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip) are questionable. The Seahawks ruled out Chazz Surratt (calf) and LB DrakeThomas (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) is active for Week 2 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: The Seahawks’ star defensive back makes his 2026 debut against the Cardinals this afternoon. Still recovering from his offseason ankle surgery, Emmanwori missed the Seahawks’ Week 1 game against the Patriots. He picked up a hip injury this week, but is evidently good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: Emmanwori picked up a hip injury mid-week. Hopefully, he is good to go by Sunday. The Seahawks ruled out fellow starting S Ty Okada (hamstring) for this one, but the Seahawks D/ST remains formidable overall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: Emmanwori remains limited through two Week 2 practices, and Okada (hamstring) has not yet resumed practicing. Emmanwori seemingly has a chance to play, but Okada appears to be a long shot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: Emmanwori is still unable to get in a full practice as he nurses a pesky ankle injury, also adding a hip issue to his practice designation. He will likely need a full practice before he is set to return for the Seahawks. Fellow safety Ty Okada (hamstring) missed practice on Wednesday; both players missed Week 1 and are in jeopardy of missing Week 2 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is inactive for Week 1 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: Emmanwori underwent surgery to deal with an ankle issue back in July. Despite some limited practice participation, the 22-year-old is not yet ready to return. With S Ty Okada (hamstring) also out, the Seahawks will lack depth in the back of the secondary for Week 1 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is questionable for Seattle’s Week 1 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: One of Seattle’s other projected starters on defense, Ty Okada, was ruled out with a hamstring injury. It would certainly be a boon to Rhamondre Stevenson’s value if Emmanwori can’t go on Wednesday. Emmanwori had surgery on his ankle in July and opened camp on the PUP list. He’s generally been regarded as more doubtful-than-questionable, but there’s a chance he’s able to go based on this listing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Seahawks S Ty Okada (hamstring) did not practice Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: It’s the second straight missed practice for Okada as he tends to a hamstring injury, while fellow starting safety Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is thought to be doubtful to suit up against the Patriots Wednesday, per those close to the team. The team’s final injury report of their Week 1 preparation will be released Tuesday, upon which we’ll receive final game designations. Keep a close eye on the transaction reports from Seattle to gauge the expected level of health of both players. Considering the Seahawks carried only three safeties on their initial 53-man roster, any practice squad elevations from the secondary could signal expected absences from one, or both, players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.headline: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) was limited on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-emman.analysis: Emmanwori’s participation is somewhat surprising. That said, The News Tribune’s Gregg Bell echoed ESPN’s Brady Henderson in a report issued at the end of practice, writing that Seahawks teammates seem to suggest that Emmanwori is doubtful to play this week. The team is still working through backup options at this time, though coach Mike Macdonald wants CB Devon Witherspoon to contribute as a nickel defender, both in coverage and via blitz packages, if Emmanwori cannot play. Fellow starting safety Ty Okada (hamstring) did not practice on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chiefs coach Andy Reid told Josh Simmons to leave a team meeting on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: According to Rapoport, Simmons was sitting with his feet up during a meeting and Reid told him to put his feet down. Simmons then “pushed back” by saying he had to sit that way because of his back injury. Reid then sent him to get treatment from the training staff. Even Patrick Mahomes chimed in and told Simmons to leave. Simmons was placed on injured reserve the next day. The former first-round pick appeared in just eight games as a rookie and hasn’t taken the field yet this year. Now he’s becoming a problem in the locker room on top of his never-ending health issues. We wouldn’t expect to see him play in a Chiefs uniform again anytime soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs placed Josh Simmons on injured reserve with a back injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs made head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder available to the media to explain the 2026 Simmons Saga today. On August 17th, the young left tackle reported calf discomfort in the same leg that he underwent a patellar tendon repair in 2024. Chiefs trainers discovered that a bulging, herniated disc in his lumbar spine was causing the lower-leg issue. According to Burkholder, offensive linemen occasionally deal with this type of disc issue, but Simmons’ issue was complicated because it was abnormally high up in the lumbar spine. Simmons consulted with a well-regarded spine specialist, who recommended rehabilitation instead of surgery. Imaging taken early in the rehab process showed improvement, so they stayed the course, but unfortunately, Simmons’ recovery has recently plateaued, leading to the injured reserve placement. Simmons will be eligible to return for the Chiefs’ Week 11 game against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons did actually practice this week, so he’s trending in the right direction, but Khalil Benson gets another start while Simmons tries to get past a bulging disc in his back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs’ starting left tackle might need more time off, but his continued practice participation is good to see. The Chiefs take on the struggling Chargers this week, and may be able to get by alright without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons has been held out of practice for roughly two months while dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. Kansas City’s starting left tackle has yet to play a snap this year while dealing with the back injury. Head coach Andy Reid said the team will “ease him back in, but on a limited basis.” There is currently no timetable for when Simmons will return. Undrafted Khalil Benson has been serviceable as the team’s starting left tackle, but Simmons will ultimately be a notable upgrade whenever he returns to action. Benson is still expected to start this week versus the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Earlier this week, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Simmons is dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. Brutal. On the plus side, CB Chamarri Conner (knee) will make his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Josh Simmons is dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons hasn’t played or practiced this year. Reid told reporters that he was making progress but will remain out of practice today. Kahlil Benson will presumably draw another start at left tackle in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs LT Josh Simmons (back) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 3 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Kahlil Benson draws another start. Simmons has not been spotted at practice since the regular season started.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs declared OT Josh Simmons, S Chamarri Conner, TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DT Bryson Eason, OT Diego Pounds, and DE Jack Pyburn inactive for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs enter Week 2 relatively healthy as they look to start the season with consecutive victories. It will be interesting to see if the Chiefs carry forward a run-heavy attack after pounding the football on the ground in a Week 1 win over the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Backup OT Kahlil Benson will start in Simmons’ stead. He did so last week and avoided major mistakes. The Chiefs also ruled out CB Chamarri Conner (knee).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Brian Branch (Achilles) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: After three full sessions this week, Branch is expected to be activated off reserve/PUP and should have no snap count per DC Kelvin Sheppard. He can be welcomed back to IDP lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Brian Branch (Achilles) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: He seems likely to be activated off injured reserve after getting the Week 6 bye to get acclimated. Lions DC Kelvin Sheppard has said that Branch will not be on a snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said it will take a few weeks for S Brian Branch (Achilles) to ramp up before playing on game day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch has officially resumed practicing, but he has a 21-day practice window to bring himself up to speed. The team has handled Branch’s recovery responsibly thus far. He is unlikely to be rushed out there, no matter how poorly the Lions’ defense is playing. We do not expect him to face the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions S Brian Branch (Achilles) has a “really good chance” to return to practice next week, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch is still on the PUP list after tearing his Achilles last season. Lions HC Dan Campbell said Branch was close to returning to practice on Friday, though he wouldn’t disclose when exactly the Lions will open the 21-day practice window for the 24-year-old safety. According to Pelissero, there’s a really good chance Branch returns to practice next week. He’ll undoubtedly help a Lions pass defense that has been torn to shreds in the first three weeks of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Brian Branch (Achilles) is “close” to returning to the field.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Campbell didn’t say when he expects Branch to return, but said the fourth-year safety “looks really good” as he continues to recover from a torn Achilles he suffered in Week 14 last season. The Lions haven’t opened Branch’s 21-day window for return, which will be the first sign that he’s nearing a comeback. Branch totaled 75 tackles, five TFLs, and 2.5 sacks for the Lions in 12 games last season and will be a welcome addition to a secondary that has allowed the most passing yards in the league through the first three weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said S Brian Branch (Achilles) “has a chance” to resume practicing sooner than S Kerby Joseph (knee), “but it won’t be this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Campbell spoke in a dejected tone when asked about the Lions’ safety duo returning to practice, particularly when discussing Joseph’s outlook. Campbell said Joseph did not suffer a setback, but stopped short of fully explaining the situation. It sounds like Joseph’s recovery stalled. The training staff was focused on strengthening Joseph’s knee, “but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do.” The Lions will not ask Joseph to play until he gets his knee as strong as it can possibly be, “and he feels comfortable.” Branch could return to practice in the coming weeks, but at this point, Joseph’s career status seems like it might be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions place S Brian Branch on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with an Achilles injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch ruptured an Achilles tendon in Week 14 last year. He is still recovering. The Lions also placed C Cade Mays (wrist) on the injured reserve/designated for return list due to his summer injury. Both players will be eligible to return after missing four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions placed S Kerby Joseph on the active/PUP list with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Just yesterday, Joseph implied via social media that he would avoid the physically unable to perform list. So much for that. Joseph dealt with a recurring knee issue for the entire 2025 season, which was first reported on at the end of July 2025, roughly three months after the Lions made him the NFL’s highest-paid safety. Given Joseph’s post, one imagines he has a chance to resume practicing relatively soon, but only time will tell. Branch suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 14 last year. As of June 13th, Lions coach Dan Campbell said there was no timetable for his return. The Lions also placed TE Tyler Conklin on the physically unable to perform list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.headline: Steelers declared CB Brandin Echols, WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, RB Eli Heidenreich, and CB Terell Smith inactive for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.analysis: Echols and Skowronek are the only players on Pittsburgh’s active roster who will miss today’s game because of injuries, though they have several key players on IR. Both players have more snaps on special teams than offense or defense this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.headline: Steelers CB Brandin Echols has entered the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.analysis: Echols was injured in Week 3’s win over the Bengals and did not return to the field. Given the short turnaround time for the Steelers to prepare for Thursday’s game against the Browns, Echols is a virtual lock to miss Week 4, but could return in time for Week 5’s game when the Steelers play host to the Colts. Echols has played primarily on special teams this season and has logged only 13 snaps on defense, per PFF.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.headline: Jets CB Brandin Echols exited Week 10 against the Cardinals with a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.analysis: The Jets’ secondary has underperformed while dealing with injuries this season. Echols will be missed in sub-packages. He is a capable rotational player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.headline: NFL suspended Jets CB Brandin Echols one game for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.analysis: Echols was involved in a two-car crash in April 2022 that left the other driver with a spinal-cord injury that required multiple surgeries. Echols was driving 84 in a 50 mph zone according to ESPN’s Rich Cimini. Echols fell out of New York’s defensive plans in 2022 and was used on just 69 defensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.headline: Jets selected Kentucky CB Brandin Echols with the No. 200 overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.analysis: Echols (5'10/179) is a former JUCO product who became a two-year starter for Kentucky, turning out 11 passes defended over that span. Echols never did grab an interception, though he came close in one instance against Alabama in 2020. Echols shines most in off-man coverage, where he can use his high-end speed (4.30 40-yard dash) and adequate agility without getting outmuscled at the line of scrimmage. Echols can also drive back to the ball with great explosion, as evidenced by his 98th- and 99th-percentile vertical and broad jumps, respectively. Given his frame, however, Echols regularly loses the battle of physicality, both at the line and down the field. Echols also struggles to tackle, which brings into question how well he could theoretically survive at nickel in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.headline: Anthony Treash of Pro Football Focus ranks Kentucky senior CB Brandin Echols as the top returning player for the Wildcats.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-ec.analysis: Echols transferred to Kentucky without much fanfare who moved from wide receiver to corner, but he started 11-of-13 games for the Wildcats last year, and he led the team with nine pass breakups and was fourth with 52 tackles. “The Wildcat is one of the 10 best press-man corners in college football,” writes Treash, “where he’s allowed just eight catches on his 23 targets for 99 yards.” He also notes Echols was excellent in contested situations, allowing six catches in 12 opportunities. The 6-foot-1, 175-pound corner is one of the best returners in the SEC, and should be following the top wideouts in the conference in 2020.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Browns signed Maliek Collins to a two-year, $30 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the deal includes $23 million in total guarantees. Collins has heated up recently with 3.5 sacks over his past three games. He is coming off a career-high 6.5 sacks in 2025 and now has a chance to top that number this year. Collins’ new deal keeps him under contract with the Browns through 2028.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Mason Graham is expected to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury of his own and Maliek Collins missed today’s practice with a foot injury. That’s three front-seven starters potentially out for Week 6. With Lamar Jackson still banged up, expect the Ravens to give Derrick Henry all the touches he can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Browns HC Todd Monken said Maliek Collins is “good to go” ahead of Week 1’s game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins opened training camp on the PUP list due to a quad injury that ended his 2025 campaign. He was activated from the PUP list two weeks ago and has been practicing with the team and appears to be in position to play in Week 1 against the Jags. Collins totaled 25 tackles, seven TFLs, and 6.5 sacks in the 12 games he appeared in last season for the Browns and has tallied five or more sacks in each of his last three seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Browns placed DT Maliek Collins on physically unable to perform list with a quad injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins suffered a season-ending quad injury in Week 13 and was unable to participate in organized team activities and mandatory minicamp this year. Despite missing so much of the season, Collins ranked fourth on the team in quarterback pressures (36) and second in NFL sacks (6.5). The Browns need the 31-year-old player to remain productive this year. Hopefully, he returns soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi reports it’s “unclear” if Maliek Collins (quad) will be ready for the start of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins was carted off in Week 13 and spent the rest of the season on injured reserve. He did not participate in OTAs or minicamp. The 31-year-old veteran had 6.5 sacks last year and will be asked to do more in the absence of Myles Garrett this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Browns HC Kevin Stefanski said Maliek Collins will miss the remainder of the season due to a quad injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins was carted from the field in the third quarter of the Browns’ Week 13 loss to the 49ers and will now miss the remainder of the season. Collins is expected to undergo surgery in the coming days. The 10-year vet has been playing at a high level in his first year with the Browns, notching a career-high 6.5 sacks in the 12 games he’s appeared in while also totaling 25 tackles, seven TFLs, and 13 QB hits. Collins joined the Browns on a two-year, $20 million contract this offseason and should be ready in time for the start of training camp next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Browns DT Maliek Collins (oblique) is active for Week 11 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins suffered an oblique injury on Friday, but the 30-year-old defensive tackle is good to go. His 21 quarterback pressures and five sacks both rank second on the team. The Browns declared WR Jamari Thrash, OG Zak Zinter, OT Cornelius Lucas, RB Raheim Sanders, DT Sam Kamara, LB Easton Mascarenas-Arnold and DE Alex Wright inactive for Week 11 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Browns DT Maliek Collins (oblique) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins “felt something” during practice on Friday per Kevin Stefanski and left early. Collins has been one of the better players on the Browns defense this year, notching a 90.4 PFF pass rush grade. His absence would be felt if he didn’t suit up on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: Browns agreed to terms with DT Maliek Collins, formerly of the 49ers, on a two-year, $20 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins was a cap casualty for the 49ers this offseason but didn’t take long to land on his feet. Per NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero, his new deal includes $13 million guaranteed. Collins logged five sacks in Houston in 2023 and was then traded to the 49ers for another five-sack season. He started all 17 games and added two fumble recoveries to his stat sheet. Collins will take the place of Dalvin Tomlinson, who was released by Cleveland earlier this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.headline: 49ers released DT Maliek Collins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maliek-col.analysis: Collins was acquired from the Texans last offseason in exchange for a seventh-round draft pick. The veteran defensive tackle was entering the final year of his contract, but will now be a free agent after a year in which he totaled 33 tackles, five sacks, and five TFLs. His five sacks tied a previous career high while his 715 defensive snaps marked his most since 2019. Collins turns 30 next month and can still provide defenses an adequate body to fill rush lanes and get after the quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints declared OG Cesar Ruiz, S Mike Reid, TE Treyton Welch, EDGE Tyree Wilson, DL Nathan Shepherd, DT John Ridgeway III, and QB Zach Wilson inactive for Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Ruiz and Shepard were the only Saints listed as questionable for Week 7. Jeremiah Wright will take his spot at right guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was removed from the injury report for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Kamara was still listed as limited in Friday’s practice, but the Saints feel confident enough in his health to clear him for Week 7. Kamara found the end zone last week on a 31-yard reception, but has largely been inefficient with his touches this season. He seen 14 opportunities to Kendre Miller’s 30 over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a touchdown-dependent RB3 against the Steelers. The only players on the Saints carrying injury designations into the weekend are guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DL Nathan Sheperd (illness). Both are listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Cesar Ruiz (ankle) is out for Week 5 and is “week to week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Torricelli Simpkins III took Ruiz’s place after he left Week 4’s game against the Bills and played 39 snaps. If Dillon Radunz is unable to get off the injury report this week, Simpkins will likely play guard for the Saints in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints OG Cesar Ruiz is questionable to return to Week 4 against the Bills with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: The Saints finally had their starting offensive line healthy, but that didn’t last two quarters as Ruiz got injured in the second. He was able to limp off the field, but then was taken into the locker room on a cart. It appears unlikely that he’ll return this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints RG Cesar Ruiz (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 14 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Ruiz left Week 13 with a concussion and missed Wednesday’s practice. He was back for a limited session on Thursday before getting fully cleared today. Fellow interior offensive lineman Lucas Patrick was also cleared for action this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints RG Cesar Ruiz (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Ruiz left Week 13 with concussion symptoms and did not return. Per head coach Darren Rizzi, Ruiz has made some progress through the league’s concussion protocols. That gives him a shot at suiting up on Sunday. His practice statuses over the next two days will be telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints RG Cesar Ruiz (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Ruiz missed four games with the knee issue but is one of many Saints players returning to the lineup this week. They are getting healthy at several spots but are still going to be without Derek Carr this week. Even with an improved offensive line, Spencer Rattler will be an easy target for LA’s defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints RG Cesar Ruiz (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Ruiz has missed the past four weeks with a knee injury. He is one of several Saints offensive linemen to go down with a multi-week injury this season. Not much will change for the New Orleans as long as Spencer Rattler is under center, but getting Ruiz back will help the offense when Derek Carr returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Saints are expected to restructure RG Cesar Ruiz’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Ruiz signed a four-year, $44 million contract extension just before Week 1 last year. He is one of many Saints players who will have their contract restructured this offseason as they work their way from $75 million over the cap down to zero. This move will net the Saints $6.6 million in cap space.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.headline: Saints RG Cesar Ruiz (concussion) will not play in Week 4 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cesar-ruiz.analysis: Also out for the Saints are cornerback Paulson Adebo and safety Jordan Howden. Even down multiple starting members of their secondary, the Saints will still be a tough matchup for Baker Mayfield.
